\section{The Insertion at a Fixed Cutoff}

This paper follows a Wilson loop through the first renormalisation-group step of Ba{\l}aban's construction of four-dimensional lattice Yang--Mills theory \cite{BalabanCRE,BalabanRG1}. That step is the block-spin transformation $T$ of \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator}: the bond variables of a periodic fine lattice of spacing $\varepsilon$ are averaged over blocks of side $L$, and the bare measure is mapped to the induced measure of the bond variables of the coarse lattice of spacing $L\varepsilon$. The loop is inserted in the bare measure and carried through $T$; the result (Section~\ref{sec:main-result}) writes its bare expectation as a perimeter factor times a corner factor times an average, over the coarse ensemble, of the loop at the background field reconstructed from the coarse field, plus two error terms that it bounds.

The gauge group $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group, $g_0$ is the bare coupling, and $\chi \colon G \to \mathbb C$ is a normalised irreducible character, so that $\chi(\id)=1$. Let $\varepsilon>0$ be the fine lattice spacing and $L>1$ the blocking factor. The fine and coarse bond fields are $U$ and $V$, respectively.

$C$ is an oriented square contour on the fine lattice and $\bar C$ an oriented square on the lattice of spacing $L\varepsilon$, each side of $\bar C$ being represented by the corresponding straight fine path in $C$; the two contours describe the same square in the underlying torus.

For a field $U$ and an ordered contour $C=(b_1,\ldots,b_n)$, holonomy and the Wilson loop are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:wilson-definition}
    \Hol_U C\coloneqq U(b_1)\cdots U(b_n),
    \qquad W_{\chi}(C;U)\coloneqq\chi(\Hol_U C)\;.
\end{equation}
The bond field satisfies $U(b^{-1})= U(b)^{-1}$ when a contour traverses a bond backwards. The character makes $W_{\chi}$ gauge invariant.

Let $E$ and $E_1$ be the positive fine and coarse bonds of the four-dimensional periodic lattices, and let $\mathcal P_T$ be the unoriented fine plaquettes. The action uses a fixed unitary realisation $G\subset U(N)$ and $\tr_N= N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}$. With $\partial p$ denoting the oriented boundary of $p$, the bare action and density are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bare-action}
    S(U)\coloneqq\sum_{p\in \mathcal P_T}
        (1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N U(\partial p)),
    \qquad \rho_0(U)\coloneqq\exp(-g_0^{-2}S(U)-E_{\varepsilon})\;.
\end{equation}
Here $E_{\varepsilon}$ is a field-independent vacuum scalar. Product normalised Haar measures on $G^E$ and $G^{E_1}$ are denoted by $\dd U$ and $\dd V$.

The full first-step operator, before the small-field/large-field decomposition, is \cite[(0.1)]{BalabanCRE}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bare-blocking-operator}
    (T\rho)(V)=\int
        \left(\prod_{c\in E_1}\delta_G(M(U,c)V(c)^{-1})\right)
        \rho(U)\,\dd U\;.
\end{equation}
Here $\delta_G$ is the group Dirac measure normalised against Haar measure, $\int\delta_G(WV^{-1})\,\dd V=1$ for every $W\in G$, and $M$ is the averaging operation, defined as follows. For a positive coarse bond $c$ let $P_c(U)$ be the transport along the straight fine path from $c_-$ to $c_+$, let $\beta_c(U)$ be the logarithmic average of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, displayed in \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} below, and let $\mathcal O_c$ be the set of fine configurations $U$ at which every logarithm in $\beta_c(U)$ has its argument in the chart domain (the chart is the inverse of $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ on the Hilbert ball $h(A)<\varrho_G$, fixed in the conventions paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}). The averaging operation is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:global-average}
    M(U,c)\coloneqq
    \begin{cases}
        e^{i\beta_c(U)}P_c(U), & U\in\mathcal O_c,\\
        P_c(U), & U\notin\mathcal O_c.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
\cite[(0.1)]{BalabanCRE} integrates over every fine configuration, so it needs an averaging operation on all of $G^E$; Ba{\l}aban's own formula is \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, defined where its logarithms are, and Ba{\l}aban states in \cite[p.~243]{BalabanCRE} that any averaging operation satisfying general properties analogous to \cite[(0.5)--(0.9)]{BalabanRG1} may be taken.

The properties of \eqref{eq:global-average} used in this paper are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}; (ii) is the analogue of the gauge covariance \cite[(0.6)]{BalabanRG1}. On the branches the averaging operation is evaluated on $\mathcal O_c$ only, where it is \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} ((B1), Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}); its value off $\mathcal O_c$ enters only through the constraint on the rows of $\Omega_1^c$.

\begin{lemma}[The Averaging Operation]\label{lem:global-average}
(i) $\mathcal O_c$ is open, and $M(\bigcdot ,c)\colon G^E\to G$ is Borel, analytic on $\mathcal O_c$, where it is \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, and a function of the bonds with both endpoints in the two blocks of $c$ alone.

(ii) For every fine gauge transformation $g\colon T\to G$, $U^g(b)= g(b_-)U(b)g(b_+)^{-1}$, one has $U^g\in\mathcal O_c$ if and only if $U\in\mathcal O_c$, and $M(U^g,c)= g(c_-)M(U,c)g(c_+)^{-1}$; in particular $M(U^g)= M(U)$ when $g$ is the identity at the block centres.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) The chart domain is open, being the image of the open ball under $A\mapsto e^{iA}$, which is injective with invertible differential there (the conventions paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}). Each loop $U(\gamma)U([x,x'])U(\gamma')^{-1}P_c(U)^{-1}$ of \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} is a product of bond variables and their inverses, continuous in $U$, so $\mathcal O_c$, the set where finitely many such loops lie in the chart domain, is open; the chart is analytic on the chart domain (inverse of an analytic map with invertible differential), so $\beta_c$ and $e^{i\beta_c}P_c$ are analytic on $\mathcal O_c$, and $P_c$ is analytic on $G^E$. A map that is continuous on an open set and continuous on its complement is Borel. The paths $\gamma$, $[x,x']$, $\gamma'$ and the straight path of $c$ have all their bonds with both endpoints in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$: $\gamma\subset\mathcal B_{c_-}$, $\gamma'\subset\mathcal B_{c_+}$, and the straight path from $x\in\mathcal B_{c_-}$ to $x+Le_{\mu}\in\mathcal B_{c_+}$ leaves $\mathcal B_{c_-}$ at the bond at which it enters $\mathcal B_{c_+}$.

(ii) Every loop is based at $c_-$, so under $g$ it is conjugated by $g(c_-)$. The Hilbert ball is $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant, $h$ being $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant, and $e^{i\,gAg^{-1}}= ge^{iA}g^{-1}$; so the chart domain is invariant under conjugation, and for $W$ in it $\frac1i\log(gWg^{-1})= g(\frac1i\log W)g^{-1}$, by the injectivity of $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ on the ball. Hence $U^g\in\mathcal O_c$ if and only if $U\in\mathcal O_c$, $\beta_c(U^g)= g(c_-)\beta_c(U)g(c_-)^{-1}$ and $e^{i\beta_c(U^g)}= g(c_-)e^{i\beta_c(U)}g(c_-)^{-1}$ there, while $P_c(U^g)= g(c_-)P_c(U)g(c_+)^{-1}$ everywhere. The product gives the covariance on $\mathcal O_c$, and off $\mathcal O_c$ it is the covariance of $P_c$.
\end{proof}

The right side of \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator} is read as follows. For bounded Borel $h$ on $G^{E_1}$ and $W\in G^{E_1}$, $\int\dd V\,h(V)\prod_{c\in E_1}\delta_G(W(c)V(c)^{-1})= h(W)$; so for a nonnegative or integrable Borel function $\rho$ on $G^E$, $T\rho$ is the image measure of $\rho\,\dd U$ under the Borel map $M\colon G^E\to G^{E_1}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}, $(T\rho)(A)=\int_{M^{-1}(A)}\rho\,\dd U$ for Borel $A\subseteq G^{E_1}$, that is $\int h\,\dd(T\rho)=\int h(M(U))\rho(U)\,\dd U$. This is the meaning of \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator} and of every group $\delta$-function of a coarse variable in this paper: it is integrated against that variable first.

Ba{\l}aban writes \cite[(0.1)]{BalabanCRE} as a Haar density; for integrable $\rho$ the finite measure $T\rho$ has a Haar density exactly when it is absolutely continuous with respect to $\dd V$, and then $(T\rho)(V)$ denotes a version of that density. Every identity below in which $\rho_1(V)$ or $N_1(V)$ appears is an identity of measures, in which $\rho_1(V)\,\dd V$ and $N_1(V)\,\dd V$ stand for the measures $\rho_1$ and $N_1$ of \eqref{eq:first-step}, and Ba{\l}aban's transformations of (0.1) into (1.11)--(1.15) \cite{BalabanCRE} are identities for the integrals of bounded Borel functions of $V$ against these measures under the branch hypotheses (B1)--(B4) of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}, which record the facts about Ba{\l}aban's construction that these identities use.

The first-step objects are those of $T$ alone, without Ba{\l}aban's additional operation $\mathbf R$ \cite[p.~243]{BalabanCRE}, which changes the densities on the large-field regions.

The bare expectation is $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[F]\coloneqq \int F\rho_0\,\dd U/\int\rho_0\,\dd U$ for bounded Borel $F$ on $G^E$. Ba{\l}aban's cutoffs, gauge insertions and changes of variables give alternative representations of this same integral: the partitions of unity \cite[(1.1), (1.4)]{BalabanCRE} sum to one pointwise, so the sum over histories of the branch integrals is the full integral $\int\rho_0\,\dd U$ whatever the value of $M$ off $\bigcup_c\mathcal O_c$, the branch integrals using $M$ on $\mathcal O_c$ only (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}).

For a finite or complex measure $\mu$ on $G^E$, $T\mu\coloneqq M_*\mu$ is the same pushforward, so that $T$ acts on the measures defined next. The outgoing measure and the measure with the insertion are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:first-step}
    \rho_1\coloneqq T[\rho_0],
    \qquad N_1\coloneqq T[\rho_0 W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )]\;.
\end{equation}
Here $\rho_1$ is a finite positive measure on $G^{E_1}$ with $\rho_1(G^{E_1})=\int\rho_0\,\dd U$, and $N_1$ is a complex measure with $| N_1(A)|\leqslant \int_{M^{-1}(A)}\rho_0| W_{\chi}|\,\dd U\leqslant \rho_1(A)$ for every Borel $A$, so that $| N_1|\leqslant \rho_1$ for the total variation and $N_1\ll\rho_1$. The outgoing Wilson function is the Radon--Nikodym derivative
\begin{equation}\label{eq:outgoing-loop}
    W_1(C;V)=\frac{\dd N_1}{\dd\rho_1}(V)\;,
\end{equation}
defined for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$, with $| W_1|\leqslant 1$ $\rho_1$-almost everywhere; a Borel version with $| W_1|\leqslant 1$ everywhere is fixed. Where $\rho_1$ and $N_1$ have Haar densities, $W_1(C;V)= N_1(V)/\rho_1(V)$ for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$, the density-ratio form in which \cite{BalabanCRE} writes such quantities.

The intermediate integration over regular fluctuations is a function of the exterior fine field and the unintegrated fluctuations; these are integrated by the outer operation \cite[(1.29)]{BalabanCRE}, which without the insertion gives $\rho_1$ (the vacuum construction is \cite[(1.11)--(1.30)]{BalabanCRE}).

\subsection{Normalisation}
The physical partition function and the expectation after the transformation are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:one-step-physical-partition}
    \mathcal Z_0\coloneqq\int\rho_0(U)\,\dd U
        =\rho_1(G^{E_1})>0\;,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
    \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C)]
        =\frac{1}{\mathcal Z_0}N_1(G^{E_1})
        =\frac{1}{\mathcal Z_0}\int W_1(C;V)\,\dd\rho_1(V)\;.
\end{equation}
Both integrals include the small-field and the large-field regions; the normalising factors of the conditional fluctuation integrals used below are part of the construction of $N_1$ and $\rho_1$.

\subsection{The Main Result}\label{sec:main-result}

The main statement of the paper concerns $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C)]$ for a square contour: after the first step the expectation is a perimeter factor times a corner factor, times the expectation, in the coarse ensemble enriched by the large-field branch data, of $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)$: the fine loop at the background $U_1$ reconstructed from the coarse field and the exterior fine field, with a finite-geometry exponent and the indicator of the covered event, plus two error terms.

The objects are defined in Sections~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}--\ref{sec:remaining-physical-comparison} and the appendices, and are listed here.

Theorem~\ref{thm:two-loop-theorem} gives the same form for the product of the Wilson functions of two vertex-disjoint squares in planes parallel to that of $e_1,e_2$, with the product of the two coefficients, the two finite-geometry exponents and a cross exponent bounded in terms of the distance between the squares; its objects specific to the pair are defined in Section~\ref{sec:two-loops} and referenced from its statement.

\emph{Notation.} $C_n$ is a coarse translate of the counterclockwise square with vertices $0$, $nLe_1$, $nL(e_1+e_2)$, $nLe_2$ in fine-lattice units (Section~\ref{sec:regional-square-scalar}), $n\geqslant 1$; it has $n_C=4nL$ contour bonds, $4n$ coarse segments indexed cyclically by $j\in\{0,\ldots,4n-1\}$, and $P(C_n)$ is its perimeter as it enters \eqref{eq:extracted-loop-scalar} (Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1}).

$W_{\chi}(C;U)$ is the normalised character $\chi$ of the holonomy of the fine field $U$ around $C$, $\varepsilon$ the fine lattice spacing, and $\sigma$ names the cutoff norm of \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}, the operator or the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm (conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}).

$T$ is the operator \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator} with the averaging operation \eqref{eq:global-average}; $\rho_1$, $N_1$, $W_1$ and $\mathcal Z_0$ are \eqref{eq:first-step}, \eqref{eq:outgoing-loop} and \eqref{eq:one-step-physical-partition}, and $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}$ is the bare expectation defined after \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator}.

$\xi=(\Omega_1,R_1,V,V_0,A_{\mathrm e})$ is the branch data of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} (the small-field region $\Omega_1$, the large-fluctuation region $R_1$, which with $\Omega_1$ determines the filled region $\Lambda_1$, the coarse field, the exterior fine field and the exterior free fluctuation; at the original carrier there are no labels), $U_1= U_1(V,V_0)$ the background of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}, $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ the history expectation \eqref{eq:c3-6-1} (weight $\mathsf w_{\xi}= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}$, normalisation $\mathcal Z_0$; positive, with $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$), and $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ the covered event of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}.

$\kappa_{C_n}\coloneqq e^{-\delta m^{\sigma}(g_0,\varepsilon)P(C_n)}(z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}(g_0,\pi/2))^4$ is the scalar \eqref{eq:extracted-loop-scalar}, with the perimeter coefficient $\delta m^{\sigma}$ of \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass} and the corner factor $z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}$ of \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor}, in the cutoff prescription $\sigma$ fixed throughout.

The setting consists of $\sigma$, the averaging and mean prescriptions of \cite[(0.4) and (0.10)--(0.11)]{BalabanRG1}, the gauge-fixing functional of \cite[(1.5)--(1.7)]{BalabanCRE}, the designated-bond convention (Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1}), and the cutoff test (1.18) at the radius $r= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ (the constants $A_1$, $p_0$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, with its $\delta_0$ as corrected in Section~\ref{app:thresholds} and (H4)).

$E_{\mathrm{def}}$ is the signed-defect term \eqref{eq:c4-1-1}, $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ the exterior-response and uncovered term \eqref{eq:c3-6-2}, and $E^{\circ}_{\xi}= E^{\circ}_{I,C_n,T}$ the finite-geometry exponent \eqref{eq:c4c-5-2} of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, a function of the history through the carrier $I=\Lambda_1^*$ alone.

$d_j\coloneqq\max(0,d_T(K_j,I^c)-R_0)$ and $\iota_T\coloneqq\max(0,N_{\min}/4-R_0)$ are the distances \eqref{eq:c4c-1-1}: $K_j$ the union of the free-input stencils of the fine traversals of segment $j$, $I^c$ the complement of the carrier in the torus free carrier, $d_T$ the periodic fine-bond metric, $N_{\min}$ the shortest fine period, and $R_0\coloneqq 4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$ the fixed range of Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} ($R_*$ the perimeter range, not the walk range $n_*R$ of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}; this $R_0$ is not the scale $R_0$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}).

The scales of the statement are $\tau$, the marked-forest parameter of \eqref{eq:marginal-fixed-forest-bound}, $\tau\coloneqq C[g_0(1+r)^3+e^{-cr^2}]$ with the cutoff radius $r= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ of \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}; $\pi_*\coloneqq\min(p_0(g_0),p_0(g_1))$ with $p_0(g)\coloneqq A_0(\log g^{-2})^{p_0}$ and $g_1= g_1(g_0)$ the first-step coupling of \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE}; $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$; $\rho$ of \eqref{eq:c4-4-8}, $\rho= O(g_0^2(1+r)^4)$; and $b\coloneqq\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor$ with the scale $R_1= R_1(g_0)$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} (Section~\ref{app:thresholds}).

The constants $C$, $c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, $C'_L$, $c_*$ of \eqref{eq:c4-2-2} and Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}, $C_{\chi}$, $c$ of \eqref{eq:c4-6-8}, $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-14} are fixed before the coupling and depend on $L$, the group, the character, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$, the fixed expansion and chart choices and the constants $A_0$, $A_1$, $p_0$, $B_3$, $\beta_0$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} only (the last through $c_{\theta}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-4}, hence $c_*$, which involve $\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$, $B_3$ and the bound \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} on $g_1/g_0$), not on $g_0$, $n$, the torus or the history; the constants $C$, $c$ of different statements are distinct and are named by their statement.

$K\coloneqq 256$ is the fixed constant bounding, in units of $\ell\coloneqq LMR_1$, the distance of a witness from its tested bond (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}; distinct from the periods $K_{\mu}$ and the stencils $K_j$), and $C_K\coloneqq 4(4K\ell+9)^4$ depends on $g_0$ through the $R_1= R_1(g_0)$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, a power of $L$ with $R_1\geqslant (\log g_1^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$; $\delta^I_q$ of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expbound-I} depends on $g_0$ (through $\tau$, $C_K$ and the one-point rate $q$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}), not on $n$, the torus or the history, and is smaller than every power of $g_0$ (Remark~\ref{rem:main-regime}(1)).

\emph{Hypotheses.} (H1) $G$ is a compact connected simple Lie group in its fixed unitary realisation $G\subset U(N)$ and $\chi$ a normalised irreducible character (the opening of this section and the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}).

(H2) The parameters satisfy the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}, the constants are fixed in the order of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, and $g_0$ lies below the threshold of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}: its items 1--6 and the further conditions listed there, among them the threshold $g_*$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5} (which contains that of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}), the thresholds of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3} (those of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}, \ref{lem:c4-6-2} and~\ref{lem:c4-6-3}, $R_{\Upsilon}\geqslant 2$, $u\leqslant u_*$, $v\leqslant 1$ and the small-coupling conditions of Sections~\ref{sec:c4-10-1} and~\ref{sec:c4-11-5}), the common small-coupling thresholds of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}, the thresholds of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} and~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} (required already for (ii), through $g_*$) and the further threshold of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expbound-I}; Corollaries~\ref{cor:main-factorisation} and~\ref{cor:main-leading-size} use in addition the further threshold stated in Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation}.

(H3) The torus is one of those of \cite{BalabanRG1} (p.251, where the period is $2L^m$ in physical units with the lattice spacing $\varepsilon= L^{-K}$, so that the exponent of \cite{BalabanRG1} is $m-K$ in terms of the $m$ here; the family of tori is the same): the fine periods are $N_{\mu}=2L^m$ fine-lattice units in every direction, with the integer $m$ so large that $N_{\mu}$ is a multiple of $\ell= LMR_1$ (a power of $L$: $M$ by \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}, $R_1$ by \cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE}; the periods are then compatible and even, Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}), and every coarse period $K_{\mu}= N_{\mu}/L=2L^{m-1}$ satisfies $K_{\mu}\geqslant 3(n+2)$ and exceeds $\max(2,2R_{\mathrm p}+8)$ (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}); for (iii) in addition $N_{\min}\geqslant 4R_0+(4/c)\log(4n)$ with the $c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} (Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split}). These are lower bounds on $m$ in terms of the fixed loop and the coupling. The collar conditions \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes} concern $M$, $M_2$ and $R_1$ and are among the thresholds of (H2) (item 1 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}). The results of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7} and of the later sections are stated for general compatible even periods and are used here for these.

(H4) Ba{\l}aban's results are used as stated and cited, in the readings recorded where \cite{BalabanCRE} fixes no convention: the branch hypotheses (B1)--(B4) of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} with Ba{\l}aban's derivation of \cite[(1.11)--(1.25)]{BalabanCRE} as recorded there, \cite[(0.4) and (0.10)--(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} for the averaging operation and the group means, Ba{\l}aban's transfer statements \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE} (all the results of \cite{BalabanVAR} used for the averaging and determining sets of \cite{BalabanCRE}), \cite{BalabanRG1} after (0.10) and after (0.12), through which Section~\ref{sec:c3-9} takes over the constraint \cite[(3)]{BalabanVAR} and \cite[Proposition~1, (51)]{BalabanAVG} for the averaging \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, the results of \cite{BalabanVAR} for the determining sets $\mathbf B_1(Q_w^{[4]})$ and $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} in place of the spacing condition \cite[(1)]{BalabanVAR} for their fine layers, and the restoring bound \eqref{eq:c3-9-7}, for the local minima and for the function of (1.21) (\cite[p.~269]{BalabanCRE}), \cite[(1.5)--(1.7)]{BalabanCRE} for the gauge-fixing functional, \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE} for $g_1$, p.246 for $R_1$ and $\varepsilon_1$, and \cite[(2.4)--(2.9)]{BalabanCRE} for the relations between the scales $R_j$, $g_j$ and $\varepsilon_j$ (Section~\ref{app:thresholds}), the conditions of \cite{BalabanCRE} on the parameters as taken over in item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, and the validity of Ba{\l}aban's construction \cite{BalabanCRE} for the values $M_1< M_2< M$ fixed there following Ba{\l}aban's prescription (the conventions after \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}).

The constants that Ba{\l}aban does not display are Ba{\l}aban's and are independent of the coupling and of the branch:
\begin{itemize}
\item $B_3$ depends on $d$ and $L$ only \cite[Theorem~1, p.~279]{BalabanVAR};
\item the $O(L^2)$ of p.247 behind the domain statement of (B1) and item 6 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds} is that of the reasoning of \cite[Lemma~1, p.~79]{BalabanREG}, which \cite{BalabanCRE} invokes there and whose bound $|V'-1|<4d^2\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ has absolute constants;
\item the $O(1)$ of (B3)(iii) is obtained in the general step of \cite[p.~268, (3.17)--(3.19)]{BalabanCRE}, from $44d^2B_3$ and \cite[(106)--(108), (159)--(163)]{BalabanAVG}, whose constants are displayed there;
\item the bound on $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of p.251, behind the condition ``$MR_1$ large'' of item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, is derived in Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} from \cite[Proposition~9, (172), and (190)]{BalabanVAR} and the block-local restoration of the axial gauge, with constants fixed before $g_0$;
\item the $O(1)$ of (B1)(iv) is displayed in \cite[p.~25]{BalabanAVG}, $d(2d+1)$;
\item the decay rate $\delta_{\mathrm c}$ of the bound of (B3)(iii) is that of the exponential decay property \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR}, which Ba{\l}aban invokes in \cite[p.~266]{BalabanCRE} for the functions $\mathbf H_{k,\square}$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} uses for $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$: in the Landau gauge it is the rate $\delta_{\mathrm P}/8$ of \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR} in the distance $d(y,y')$ of \cite[(2.46)]{BalabanPRT2}, whose scale weights are fixed powers of $L$ at the first step (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-3}), with $\delta_{\mathrm P}$ the common decay rate defined in \cite[p.~423]{BalabanPBG} after Theorem~3.12, ``a positive, absolute constant depending on $d$ and $L$ only'', for every background satisfying \cite[(3.35)--(3.36)]{BalabanPBG}, a class that contains the minimal configurations by \cite[Theorem~1, (9)--(10)]{BalabanVAR}.
\end{itemize}

The $\widetilde Q$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} is $LQ_{U_1}$, the linear part of the constraint function \cite[(2.4), p.~266]{BalabanRG1} (decomposed as $L\widetilde QB'+\widetilde C(B')$ at p.267), and the $\sigma$ in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} is the normalised Haar density $\sigma/\sigma_0$ of \cite[(18), p.~260]{BalabanUV3} ($\dd U'=\sigma(A')\,\dd A'$, $\sigma_0=\sigma(0)$), the transformation to which Ba{\l}aban refers at the foot of \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} (the step list of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}).

The terms that \cite{BalabanCRE} does not define are taken in the sense Ba{\l}aban gives them:
\begin{itemize}
\item the ``domain of integration in (1.11)'', p.248, is the set to which the characteristic factors of (1.11) restrict the integral, the support of every one of them (as \cite[p.~265]{BalabanRG1} defines its characteristic function ``in such a way that the domain of integration in (2.1) is restricted to'' a set of configurations), under which $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$, (B1)(iii), and Remark~\ref{rem:c3-8-1};
\item in (B1), $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ is the minimal configuration of (2.12) and (2.15) for the determining data named at p.251, as \cite{BalabanCRE} writes the operation it calls similar to (1.21)--(1.23) at the general step, p.269, with data from both scales, so that (1.21) depends on $(V,V_0)$;
\item the rows of $\Omega_1$ and of $\Omega_1^c$ (Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}) are those of \cite[Sect.~A]{BalabanUV3}, which \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} follows: a row with one block off $\Omega_1$ is a row of $\Omega_1$, and its average involves $V_0$ on the outer block as a constant (\cite[(12), p.~258]{BalabanUV3}: $U= V_0$ on $\Omega_1^c$, $\bar U= V$ on $\Omega_1^{(1)}$; the $\delta$-functions of $\Omega_1^c$ are those of the rows $b'\subset\Omega_1^c$, p.259), which is the form of (B2) on such rows;
\item the $X^{\sim}$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} adds every cube meeting $X$, at a face, an edge, or a vertex (\cite[p.~257]{BalabanRG1}: $\tilde\square^n$ is the cube of side $(1+2n)M$ with the centre of $\square$);
\item the $M_1$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} is a lower bound on the cube side (\cite[Theorem~3.1, p.~397]{BalabanPBG} holds ``for $M\geqslant M_1$'', and $M_1$ ``was fixed in'' that paper, \cite[p.~77]{BalabanREG});
\item the ``compatible'' partitions of \cite{BalabanCRE} (p.245, where the partitions introduced there ``have to be compatible'', also with $\pi_0$ and with the partitions introduced later, and p.257, ``compatible with all other partitions'') are nested, the cubes of the coarser of two compatible partitions being unions of cubes of the finer, the sense of \cite[p.~98]{BalabanREG}, ``compatible with the block structure of the lattice $T$, i.e.\ for every $j$ the cube $\square_j$ is a sum of the big blocks'' (Section~\ref{app:regular-covariance});
\item ``regular'' in (2.12) is membership in the class \cite[(6)]{BalabanVAR}, to which Ba{\l}aban refers in \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE} for the precise definitions, with any radius allowed by \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR}, which gives the same minimal orbit for each (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-seed});
\item the $\widetilde D$ in \cite[(1.13)--(1.14)]{BalabanCRE} is the solution of the row equations \cite[(17), pp.~259--260]{BalabanUV3}, the transformation to which Ba{\l}aban refers in \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}, solved ``separately for each function $Q(A',c)$'', with ``a unique solution \dots\ for $A$ sufficiently small'', analytic with a Taylor expansion beginning with second order terms, which is the small solution $\varphi$ of (B4)(i) and the only chart-class family whose fine field lies in $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ (existence, uniqueness, analyticity, and the positivity of the Jacobian (B4)(iii) are proved in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}, from (B1) (with (B3)(i), through (B1)(i)) and (B2) with the readings listed here, the fine periods being at least $8M$, and threshold items 5 and 6).
\end{itemize}

This paper's own readings are the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item the bonds crossing from $\Omega_1$ to $\Omega_1^c$ taken as variables of the integral over $\Omega_1$ (Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}), the rule of \cite[(8), p.~258]{BalabanUV3} for plaquettes, ``plaquettes with at least one corner belonging to $\Omega_1$'', applied to bonds;
\item this paper's convention $\chi_1(\square')=0$, $\chi_1^c(\square')=1$, $\chi_0'(\square')=0$, $\chi_0'^c(\square')=1$ where the configuration $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ does not exist, which keeps (1.4) and (1.8) partitions of unity;
\item three corrections of the printed text of \cite{BalabanCRE}: $v$ read from (1.14) where \cite[p.~249]{BalabanCRE} points to ``(1.15)'' (before \eqref{eq:retained-prechange-density}), the ``$z\neq y$'' in \cite[(1.5)]{BalabanCRE} read as $x\neq y$, as in (1.7) (\eqref{eq:retained-outer-measure-identities}), and the first member of the chain of \cite{BalabanCRE} $\delta_0=g_0A_1p_0(g_0)=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$, p.247, read as $g_0(A_1/A_0)p_0(g_0)$, the value of the last member and of $\delta_k=g_kA_1/A_0\,p_0(g_k)$ at p.265, which fixes the radius $r=\delta_0/g_0$ at which $\kappa_{C_n}$ is identified (Section~\ref{app:thresholds}).
\end{itemize}

The domain of the integral \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} is otherwise Ba{\l}aban's: its averages and means are the principal logarithms of \cite[p.~21, (22)--(25)]{BalabanAVG}; on the whole domain of integration, the designated bonds included, the fluctuation lies in the chart ball of the conventions paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} by \cite[pp.~247--248]{BalabanCRE} (Ba{\l}aban's statements, justified there by the reasoning of Lemma~1 of \cite{BalabanREG}), and the arguments of the averages and means lie there by \cite[pp.~24--25, (44)--(46)]{BalabanAVG} with (B3)(i), p.248, both derived in (B1).

\begin{theorem}[A Wilson Loop after the First Renormalisation Step]\label{thm:main-theorem}
Under (H1)--(H4):
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item (Form.)
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:thm-main-identity}
        \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]=\kappa_{C_n}\,\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\;,
    \end{equation}
    with $\kappa_{C_n}\neq0$, and every term is integrable against the history weight. The coefficients $\delta m^{\sigma}$ and $z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}$ depend on $g_0$, $\varepsilon$, $L$, the group, the character, and the setting only, so $\kappa_{C_n}$ depends on $n$ through $P(C_n)$ alone and not on the torus or the history.
    \item (Bounds.)
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:thm-main-bounds}
        \begin{gathered}
            | E^{\circ}_{\xi}|\leqslant C\tau^2\Bigl[\sum_{j=0}^{4n-1}e^{-cd_j}+4ne^{-c\iota_T}+(n+1)e^{-cn}\Bigr]\leqslant C\tau^2(9n+1)\quad\text{on }A_{\mathrm{cov}}\;,\\
            | E_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}+e^{C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})}-1\;,\\
            | E_{\mathrm{bdry}}|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}\,n_C(1+g_0r)\,e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}\;.
        \end{gathered}
    \end{equation}
    \item (Size of the leading term.) $|\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]|\leqslant e^{C\tau^2(9n+1)}$, and under the additional hypotheses of (H2), (H3) for (iii),
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:thm-main-moment}
        \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}\bigr]\leqslant e^{Y}\;,\qquad Y\coloneqq C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q\;,\qquad\delta^I_q\leqslant \exp\bigl[-c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)\bigr]\;,
    \end{equation}
    so that the leading term of \eqref{eq:thm-main-identity} has modulus at most $|\kappa_{C_n}|e^{Y}$, and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}-1|]\leqslant e^{Y}-1$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
(i) is Corollary~\ref{cor:c4c-5-2}, whose hypotheses are the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1} and those of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} (the square geometry and collar conditions of (H3), the thresholds of (H2)); $\kappa_{C_n}\neq0$ is an exponential by \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass} and \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor}, as stated after \eqref{eq:retained-outgoing-observable}, $\delta m^{\sigma}$ is the absolutely convergent sum \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}, characterised there as a limit, and $z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}$ the exponential \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor} of a convergent corner sum, from both of which $n$ and the torus are absent.

In (ii) the first bound is Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} with the elementary bounds ($e^{-cd_j}\leqslant 1$, $e^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$, $(n+1)e^{-cn}\leqslant n+1$); the second is \eqref{eq:c4-12-8} of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3}, whose hypotheses are those stated at the start of Section~\ref{sec:c4-12} (Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}, Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-2}) and the thresholds named in (H2); the third is \eqref{eq:c3-7-14} of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}, under compatible even periods and \eqref{eq:c3-1-2} (a further condition of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}).

In (iii) the first bound is the positivity of $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ \eqref{eq:c3-6-1}, $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$, $| W_{\chi}|\leqslant 1$ and the crude bound of (ii); \eqref{eq:thm-main-moment} and the two consequences are Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-moment}, from the refined split \eqref{eq:refined-split} of Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split} under $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$ (the torus condition of (H3)), and from \eqref{eq:c5-7-expmoment-I} of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment} at $\lambda= C\tau^2$, whose joint witness bound \eqref{eq:c5-7-joint-I} (Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-joint}) rests on Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}; their hypotheses are those of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, compatible even periods, $g_0< g_*$, and the further threshold of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expbound-I}, all in (H2) and (H3).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Regime of the Statement]\label{rem:main-regime}
(1) The scales: as $g_0\to0$, $\tau= C[g_0(1+r)^3+e^{-cr^2}]\to0$ (with the single radius $r=\delta_0/g_0= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ of the notation paragraph and Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, the radius of the cutoff test $\Theta^{\sigma}$ as well), while $e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$, $e^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}$ and $\delta^I_q$ are smaller than every power of $g_0$ ($\pi_*^2\geqslant A_0^22^{-2p_0}(\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0}$ by \eqref{eq:c5-3-1}, with $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r\geqslant 10$, and for $\delta^I_q$ the last member of \eqref{eq:thm-main-moment} with \eqref{eq:c5-7-delta-small}), and $\rho\varepsilon_1\to0$.

The $n$-dependence of the bounds is explicit: pointwise on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ is at most linear in $n$; under the torus condition $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$ the growth is carried by the $4n$ boundary terms $e^{-cd_j}$, each at most one and exponentially small when the carrier complement is far from segment $j$, while the remaining terms $4ne^{-c\iota_T}+(n+1)e^{-cn}$ of (ii) are at most $2+1/c$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split}); in history average the exponential of $| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|$ carries the perimeter-rate factor $e^{n_C\delta^I_q}$ of (iii), where $\delta^I_q$ is governed by the $C_K$-th root $q^{1/C_K}$ of the one-point rate $q$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}, while Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation} below separates the deterministic torus and corner part of $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ and pays its carrier part at the rate $q^{1/16}$, which gives (iii) with $\delta^{\sharp}_q$ in place of $\delta^I_q$; $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ and the first term of the bound \eqref{eq:thm-main-bounds} on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ are perimeter rates of the same kind; and the second term of that bound is small only when $n_C\rho\varepsilon_1\ll1$ ($e^x-1\geqslant x$).

The bounds \eqref{eq:thm-main-bounds} on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ and $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ are absolute, not relative to $\kappa_{C_n}= e^{-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)}(z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c})^4$; whether they lie below $|\kappa_{C_n}|= e^{-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)}| z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}|^4$ ($\delta m^{\sigma}$ is real, by the argument following \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}) depends on the sizes of $\delta m^{\sigma}$ and $z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}$, for which Sections~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} and~\ref{sec:marginal-corner} give two-sided bounds: $|\kappa^{\sigma}_v|\leqslant C\tau^2$ (the sentence following \eqref{eq:marginal-full-perimeter}, by \eqref{eq:marginal-cluster-tail}, with \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}) and $|\zeta^{\sigma}_{v,w}|\leqslant C\tau^2$ (\eqref{eq:corner-localisation-bound}, Section~\ref{sec:marginal-corner}) give $|\delta m^{\sigma}| P(C_n)= n|\sum_v\kappa^{\sigma}_v|\leqslant 4Cn\tau^2$ and $e^{-4C\tau^2}\leqslant | z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}|^4\leqslant e^{4C\tau^2}$, hence $e^{-4C\tau^2(n+1)}\leqslant |\kappa_{C_n}|\leqslant e^{4C\tau^2(n+1)}$, with $C$ independent of $g_0$, $n$ and the torus (an upper bound is also at hand from the expectation: at any configuration of $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $|\kappa_{C_n}|=| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}| e^{-\Re E^{\circ}_{\xi}}\leqslant e^{C\tau^2(9n+1)}$ by (ii) and $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}|\leqslant 1$, the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3}).

$E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ and the first term of the bound on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ are smaller than every power of $g_0$ at fixed $n$, and the ratios of their bounds to $|\kappa_{C_n}|$ are, respectively, $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}n_C(1+g_0r)e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}/|\kappa_{C_n}|$ and $C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}/|\kappa_{C_n}|$, below one exactly when $\log(C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}n_C(1+g_0r))+\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)+4\log| z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}|^{-1}< c_*\pi_*^2$, respectively $\log(C'_Ln_C)+\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)+4\log| z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}|^{-1}<(c_*/2)\pi_*^2$, conditions that involve the length of the loop through $n_C$ and $P(C_n)$; by the lower bound on $|\kappa_{C_n}|$ they hold whenever $\log(C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}n_C(1+g_0r))+4C\tau^2(n+1)< c_*\pi_*^2$, respectively $\log(C'_Ln_C)+4C\tau^2(n+1)<(c_*/2)\pi_*^2$, that is for $n$ up to a fixed multiple of $\pi_*^2/\tau^2$ at small coupling, and for every fixed $n$ once $g_0$ is small ($\tau\to0$, $\pi_*\to\infty$); when $\delta m^{\sigma}>0$ the exact conditions fail at fixed $g_0$ for all large $n$, which the hypotheses allow on correspondingly large tori.

The second term of the bound on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$, at most $2x$ with $x\coloneqq C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})$ when $x\leqslant 1$ ($e^x-1\leqslant 2x$ for $0\leqslant x\leqslant 1$), is bounded only by a quantity polynomially small in $g_0$ at fixed $n$ ($\rho= O(g_0^2(1+r)^4)$); its comparison with $|\kappa_{C_n}|$ at the original carrier is made by the relative form of \eqref{eq:c4-12-7}: the far-history term there retains $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|=|\kappa_{C_n}|| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}|$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ \eqref{eq:c4c-5-1}, so by \eqref{eq:thm-main-moment} (the far-history term is the $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$-average, with the weight $\mathsf w_{\xi}$ and the normaliser $\mathcal Z_0$ of (iii), of $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}\cap\mathsf N_b^c}| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|(e^x-1)\leqslant \mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}|\kappa_{C_n}| e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}(e^x-1)$) it is at most $|\kappa_{C_n}| e^{C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q}(e^x-1)$, a relative bound, also with $\delta^{\sharp}_q$ in place of $\delta^I_q$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation}); only the near-history term $C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}$ is absolute.

(2) The statements above do not include a bound on the history average of $e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}$ literally independent of $n$ (the proved form is the perimeter rate of (iii)), a lower bound on $|\kappa_{C_n}|$ uniform in $n$ ($|\kappa_{C_n}|= e^{-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)}| z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}|^4$ is bounded below uniformly in $n$ if and only if $\delta m^{\sigma}\leqslant 0$, the sign of $\delta m^{\sigma}$ is not determined here, and the lower bound $e^{-4C\tau^2(n+1)}$ of (1) decays in $n$), a lower bound on the modulus of the leading expectation $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]$ uniform in $n$ (Corollary~\ref{cor:main-leading-size} below gives one at a fixed loop, with an error $\eta_n= a_n+e^{n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q}-1$ whose leading part for $n\leqslant \varepsilon_1^{-1}$ and nontrivial $\chi$ is the area term $2\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi} c_{\mathrm h}n^2\varepsilon_1$, and when $\eta_n<1$ ``below $|\kappa_{C_n}|$'' in (1) compares with the leading term up to the factor $(1-\eta_n)^{-1}e^{C\tau^2(2+1/c)}$), or the second renormalisation step; the output of the step is the pair of the complex measure $\kappa_{C_n}^{-1}N_1$ and the measure $\rho_1$ of Section~\ref{sec:remaining-physical-comparison} (Conjecture~\ref{conj:iteration} of Section~\ref{sec:next-step} states the form expected after $k+1$ steps for $n= L^k$).
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Factorisation of the Leading Term]\label{cor:main-factorisation}
Under (H1)--(H4), including the additional hypotheses of (H2) and (H3) for (iii) of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}, the exponent \eqref{eq:c4c-5-2} on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ is $E^{\circ}_{\xi}= E^{\partial}_{\xi}+E^{\circ}_{T,n}$, with the carrier part and the torus and corner part
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-factorisation-parts}
    E^{\partial}_{\xi}= F_{I,C,T}-F_{C,T}\;,\qquad E^{\circ}_{T,n}=(F_{C,T}-F_{C,\infty}(n))+E^{\sigma}_n
\end{equation}
in the notation of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}. Then $E^{\circ}_{T,n}$ does not depend on the history, $\kappa_{C_n}e^{E^{\circ}_{T,n}}=\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)$ is the flat reference loop \eqref{eq:marginal-literal-ratio} of $C_n$ on the torus, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-factorisation}
    \begin{gathered}
        \kappa_{C_n}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]=\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)\bigl(\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]+R_n\bigr)\;,\\
        | E^{\circ}_{T,n}|\leqslant C\tau^2\bigl[4ne^{-c\iota_T}+(n+1)e^{-cn}\bigr]\leqslant C\tau^2(2+1/c)\;,\\
        | R_n|\leqslant \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}| e^{E^{\partial}_{\xi}}-1|\bigr]\leqslant e^{n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q}-1\;,\qquad
        \delta^{\sharp}_q\coloneqq C\tau^2N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\,e^{C\tau^2L^4C_K\Phi_c}\,q^{1/16}\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
with $C$, $c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, $N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$ and $\Phi_c$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment} (they depend on $L$ and $c$ only, \eqref{eq:c5-7-boundary-marks}), $C_K$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-joint} and the one-point rate $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7} ($g_0< g_*$, as in \eqref{eq:c5-7-expbound-I}).

For $g_0$ below a further threshold, depending on $L$, $M$, $M_1$, $M_2$, the group, the character, the source constants and $c$, $C\tau^2L^4C_K\Phi_c\leqslant 1$ and $\delta^{\sharp}_q\leqslant eC\tau^2N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\,e^{-c_*\pi_*^2/16}$.

Moreover $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}]\leqslant \exp[C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q]$, the bound \eqref{eq:thm-main-moment} of (iii) with $\delta^{\sharp}_q$ in place of $\delta^I_q$. Consequently $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]=\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)(\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]+R_n)+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ by \eqref{eq:thm-main-identity}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The decomposition is \eqref{eq:c4c-5-2}. In the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} at $D= I$, from which Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} is obtained, the three parts are bounded separately: $| E^{\partial}_{\xi}|\leqslant C\tau^2\sum_{j=0}^{4n-1}e^{-cd_j}$ by \eqref{eq:regional-square-boundary-comparison}, $| F_{C,T}-F_{C,\infty}(n)|\leqslant C\tau^2(4n)e^{-c\iota_T}$ by \eqref{eq:regional-square-periodic-comparison}, and $| E^{\sigma}_n|\leqslant C\tau^2(n+1)e^{-cn}$ by \eqref{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound}; the bound of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} is their sum, with the largest of the three constants and the smallest of the three rates; these are the $C$, $c$ of that proposition fixed in the notation paragraph, the $c$ of (H3) and of Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split} is this one, and each of the three bounds holds with them.

$F_{C,T}$ is the logarithm, on the connected source branch, of $\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)= N^{\sigma}_{C_n,T}/D^{\sigma}_T$ \eqref{eq:marginal-literal-ratio}, $F_{C,\infty}(n)$ is the bulk logarithm \eqref{eq:corner-fixed-square-limit} and $E^{\sigma}_n$ the corner-extraction error; none of them involves the carrier $I$ or any other datum of the history, so $E^{\circ}_{T,n}$ is a number fixed by $g_0$, $n$, the torus and the setting. By the identity $F_{I,C,T}=\log\kappa_{C_n}+E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, $\log\kappa_{C_n}+E^{\circ}_{T,n}= F_{I,C,T}-E^{\partial}_{\xi}= F_{C,T}$, whence $\kappa_{C_n}e^{E^{\circ}_{T,n}}=\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)$.

The second form of the bound on $E^{\circ}_{T,n}$ uses $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$, the torus condition of (H3), and $(n+1)e^{-cn}\leqslant 1+1/c$.

Since $E^{\circ}_{T,n}$ is a constant and the integrands are bounded ($| E^{\partial}_{\xi}|\leqslant 4C\tau^2n$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $| W_{\chi}|\leqslant 1$), $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]= e^{E^{\circ}_{T,n}}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\partial}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]$, and the identity holds with $R_n=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}(e^{E^{\partial}_{\xi}}-1)W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]$. By the positivity of $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ \eqref{eq:c3-6-1}, $| W_{\chi}|\leqslant 1$, $e^{| x|}-1\geqslant | e^x-1|$ and the pointwise bound of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expmoment-I}, with $\lambda= C\tau^2$ and the marks $m_b=\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}$, $| R_n|\leqslant \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}| e^{E^{\partial}_{\xi}}-1|]\leqslant \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\exp(\lambda\sum_b\varphi_c(b)m_b)]-1$, using $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$.

Let $L^p$ be the smallest power of $L$ exceeding $\sigma_K=2K\ell+4$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-joint}), so $L^p\leqslant L\sigma_K$, and let $s_{\mu}\coloneqq\min(L^p,N_{\mu}/2)$; $N_{\mu}/s_{\mu}$ is even, as $N_{\mu}=2L^m$ by (H3). The sites of the torus are partitioned into the boxes $Q=\prod_{\mu}[k_{\mu} s_{\mu},(k_{\mu}+1)s_{\mu})$, $k_{\mu}\in\mathbb Z/(N_{\mu}/s_{\mu})$, and $Q$ has the colour $(k_{\mu}\bmod2)_{\mu}$, one of sixteen. Two distinct boxes of one colour differ in some direction $\mu$ by a nonzero even index difference modulo $N_{\mu}/s_{\mu}$, which forces $N_{\mu}/s_{\mu}\geqslant 4$ and $s_{\mu}= L^p$, so their sites are at periodic $\ell^{\infty}$ distance at least $L^p>\sigma_K$. For a finite set $\mathsf S$ of bonds let $N(\mathsf S)$ be the number of boxes containing the initial site of a bond of $\mathsf S$; one bond of $\mathsf S$ in each such box of the most frequent colour gives a subset $\mathsf S'$ at pairwise $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $>\sigma_K$ with $|\mathsf S'|\geqslant N(\mathsf S)/16$, so the first inequality of \eqref{eq:c5-7-joint-I} and $q\leqslant 1$ give $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\prod_{b\in\mathsf S}m_b]\leqslant q^{N(\mathsf S)/16}$.

The expansion of $\exp(\lambda\sum_b\varphi_c(b)m_b)=\prod_b(1+y_bm_b)$, $y_b= e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1\geqslant 0$, into the sum over $\mathsf S$ of $\prod_{b\in\mathsf S}y_bm_b$ (finitely many nonnegative terms, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment}) factorises over the boxes, since $N(\mathsf S)=\sum_Q\mathbf 1\{\mathsf S\text{ has a bond with initial site in }Q\}$:
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\Bigl[\prod_b(1+y_bm_b)\Bigr]&\leqslant \sum_{\mathsf S}\prod_{b\in\mathsf S}y_b\,q^{N(\mathsf S)/16}=\prod_Q\Bigl(1+q^{1/16}\Bigl(\prod_{b\in Q}(1+y_b)-1\Bigr)\Bigr)\\
        &\leqslant \exp\Bigl(q^{1/16}\sum_Q\bigl(e^{\lambda\sum_{b\in Q}\varphi_c(b)}-1\bigr)\Bigr)\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
the products and sums over $b\in Q$ running over the bonds with initial site in $Q$. A box has at most $L^{4p}\leqslant L^4\sigma_K^4$ sites, hence at most $4L^4\sigma_K^4\leqslant L^4C_K$ bonds, so $\lambda\sum_{b\in Q}\varphi_c(b)\leqslant \lambda L^4C_K\Phi_c$ by \eqref{eq:c5-7-boundary-marks}; with $e^x-1\leqslant xe^x$ and $\sum_b\varphi_c(b)\leqslant n_CN'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$ (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment}) the exponent is at most $n_C\lambda N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)e^{\lambda L^4C_K\Phi_c}q^{1/16}= n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q$.

The same pointwise bound gives $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\partial}_{\xi}|}]\leqslant \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\exp(\lambda\sum_b\varphi_c(b)m_b)]\leqslant e^{n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q}$, and with $| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|\leqslant | E^{\circ}_{T,n}|+| E^{\partial}_{\xi}|$ the moment bound follows.

For the further threshold: $C_K\leqslant 4(4K+9)^4(L^2M)^42^{4\mathfrak r}(\log g_0^{-2})^{4\mathfrak r}$ and $\tau\leqslant C[g_0(1+r)^3+e^{-cr^2}]$ with $r= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ (by \eqref{eq:c5-3-1}, as in the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-moment}), so $\tau^2C_K\to0$ as $g_0\to0$, and $q^{1/16}\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2/16}$.

The last statement is \eqref{eq:thm-main-identity} with the identity of \eqref{eq:main-factorisation} substituted.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The Lipschitz Constant of the Character]\label{def:character-lipschitz}
$\pi_{\chi}$ is the irreducible unitary representation of $G$ with $\chi=(\dim\pi_{\chi})^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}\pi_{\chi}$, and $\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}$ is a constant, depending on the group and the character only, with
\begin{equation*}
    \|\pi_{\chi}(g)-\pi_{\chi}(h)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}\| g-h\|_{\mathrm{op}}\qquad(g,h\in G)\;;
\end{equation*}
it exists because $\pi_{\chi}$ is smooth and $G\subset U(N)$ is a compact submanifold.
\end{definition}

\begin{corollary}[The Leading Term at a Fixed Loop]\label{cor:main-leading-size}
Under the hypotheses of Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation}, let $\pi_{\chi}$ and $\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:character-lipschitz}, $C_L$ the contour constant with $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_C$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}, the paragraph before Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-1}), depending on $L$ only, and $q$ the one-point rate of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:main-leading-size}
    \begin{gathered}
        \bigl|\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]-1\bigr|\leqslant a_n\coloneqq 2\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi} c_{\mathrm h}n^2\varepsilon_1+\bigl(2(nL+1)^2+C_Ln_C\bigr)q\;,\\
        \kappa_{C_n}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]=\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)\bigl(1+R^{\sharp}_n\bigr)\;,\qquad| R^{\sharp}_n|\leqslant \eta_n\coloneqq a_n+e^{n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q}-1\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
with $c_{\mathrm h}=\sqrt N$, $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ and $\delta^{\sharp}_q$ of \eqref{eq:main-factorisation}.

Hence, when $\eta_n<1$, the leading term of \eqref{eq:thm-main-identity} is nonzero, $(1-\eta_n)|\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)|\leqslant |\kappa_{C_n}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]|\leqslant (1+\eta_n)|\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)|$, and $e^{-C\tau^2(2+1/c)}|\kappa_{C_n}|\leqslant |\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)|\leqslant e^{C\tau^2(2+1/c)}|\kappa_{C_n}|$ with the $C$, $c$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation}.

For every fixed $n$, $\eta_n\to0$ as $g_0\to0$; at small coupling $\eta_n$ is small for $n$ up to a small multiple of $\varepsilon_1^{-1/2}$, and the bound is not uniform in $n$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Let $S_n$ be the set of the $(nL+1)^2$ fine sites of the closed square bounded by $C_n$ in its plane, and $A_{\square}=\{ S_n\subseteq\Lambda_1\}$, an event of the regions. If $A_{\square}$ fails, some $x\in S_n$ lies in $B_{\xi}=\Lambda_1^c$ and the positive bond $z_x=(x,x+e_1)$ lies in $E(B_{\xi})$ (notation of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}); so $\mathbf 1_{A_{\square}^c}\leqslant \sum_{x\in S_n}\mathbf 1\{ z_x\in E(B_{\xi})\}$, and $\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A_{\square}^c)\leqslant (nL+1)^2q$ by $p_z\leqslant q$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}) and the positivity of $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ \eqref{eq:c3-6-1}.

On a branch in $A_{\square}$ every fine plaquette $p$ of the square has its vertices in $\Lambda_1$, a union of blocks: the block of a vertex $x$ lies in $\Lambda_1$, a bond with both endpoints in that block is free (a designated bond crosses between two blocks) and belongs to $I$, and its initial site is within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $L-1$ of $x$, so every bond of $p$ is within distance $L\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} gives $\| U_1(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$.

Lattice Stokes: the $(nL)^2$ plaquettes of the square are ordered by rows, starting at the base corner $x_0$ of $C_n$, the image of the vertex $0$ of the square of the notation paragraph under the coarse translation that gives $C_n$ (bottom row first, left to right in each row), and let $Q_k$ be the union of the first $k$ of them, whose boundary, oriented counterclockwise and based at $x_0$, is a closed lattice path; $Q_1= p_1$ is the plaquette at $x_0$, for $k\geqslant 1$ the shared path $s$ below does not contain $x_0$, and $\partial Q_{(nL)^2}$ is $C_n$ (another base point or orientation replaces the holonomy $h$ below by a conjugate or by $h^{-1}$, which changes neither $\| h-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ nor $|\chi(h)-1|$, since $\chi(h^{-1})=\overline{\chi(h)}$ and $\chi(\id)=1$); adding the next plaquette $p$ replaces the one or two bonds $s$ it shares with $\partial Q_k$ (its lower and left sides that lie in $Q_k$) by the complementary path $s'$ of $\partial p$, and if the based boundary path of $Q_k$ is $\alpha s\beta$, then $\alpha s'\beta$ is that of $Q_{k+1}$ and its holonomy is $vU(\partial p)^{\pm1}v^{-1}$ times the holonomy of $\alpha s\beta$, with $v$ the holonomy of $\alpha s$ and $\partial p$ based at the endpoint of $s$.

For unitaries, $\| vwv^{-1}-\id\|=\| w-\id\|=\| w^{-1}-\id\|$ and $\| w_1w_2-\id\|\leqslant \| w_1-\id\|+\| w_2-\id\|$, so on $A_{\square}$ the holonomy $h$ of $U_1$ around $C_n$ satisfies $\| h-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant (nL)^2\cdot 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}= 2c_{\mathrm h}n^2\varepsilon_1$, and, $\chi$ being a class function with $|\operatorname{Tr}X|\leqslant \dim\pi_{\chi}\,\| X\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, $| W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)-1|=|\chi(h)-\chi(\id)|\leqslant \|\pi_{\chi}(h)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi} c_{\mathrm h}n^2\varepsilon_1$. Since $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ is positive with $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]-1=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}\cap A_{\square}}(W_{\chi}-1)\bigr]+\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}\cap A_{\square}^c}(W_{\chi}-1)\bigr]-\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c)\;,
\end{equation*}
and the three terms are at most $2\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi} c_{\mathrm h}n^2\varepsilon_1$, $2\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A_{\square}^c)\leqslant 2(nL+1)^2q$ ($| W_{\chi}|\leqslant 1$) and $C_Ln_Cq$ \eqref{eq:c3-7-3} in modulus, which is the first bound.

By Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation} the leading term is $\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)(\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]+R_n)=\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)(1+R^{\sharp}_n)$ with $R^{\sharp}_n=(\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]-1)+R_n$ and $| R_n|\leqslant e^{n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q}-1$, which is the second; the modulus bounds follow from $1-\eta_n\leqslant |1+R^{\sharp}_n|\leqslant 1+\eta_n$ and $\mathcal W^{\circ,\sigma}_T(C_n)=\kappa_{C_n}e^{E^{\circ}_{T,n}}$ with $| E^{\circ}_{T,n}|\leqslant C\tau^2(2+1/c)$.

As $g_0\to0$, $\varepsilon_1\to0$ ($g_1\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_0$ and $g_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_1$, \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} as quoted in Section~\ref{app:thresholds}; the second inequality keeps $\varepsilon_1^{-1}$ polynomial in $g_0^{-1}$), $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}) and, below the further threshold of Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation}, $\delta^{\sharp}_q\leqslant eC\tau^2N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)e^{-c_*\pi_*^2/16}$, with $\pi_*\to\infty$; so $\eta_n\to0$ at fixed $n$, and the terms other than $2\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi} c_{\mathrm h}n^2\varepsilon_1$ are smaller than every power of $g_0$ for $n\leqslant \varepsilon_1^{-1}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The Coarse Loop]\label{def:coarse-loop}
Let $c_0,\ldots,c_{4n-1}$ be the coarse bonds of $C_n$ in the order of traversal from the vertex $0$, with $V(c)\coloneqq V(-c)^{-1}$ and $P_c(U)\coloneqq P_{-c}(U)^{-1}$ for a coarse bond $c$ traversed in the negative direction. The holonomy and the Wilson function of the coarse field along $C_n$ are
\begin{equation*}
    \Hol_VC_n\coloneqq V(c_0)V(c_1)\cdots V(c_{4n-1})\;,\qquad W_{\chi}(C_n;V)\coloneqq\chi(\Hol_VC_n)\;,
\end{equation*}
so that $\Hol_{U_1}C_n= P_{c_0}(U_1)\cdots P_{c_{4n-1}}(U_1)$ in the convention of \eqref{eq:wilson-definition}. The transports along $C_n$, the insertions, and the insertion size are
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{gathered}
        H_0\coloneqq\id\;,\qquad H_j\coloneqq P_{c_0}(U_1)\cdots P_{c_{j-1}}(U_1)\;,\qquad\widetilde R_j\coloneqq H_jV(c_j)P_{c_j}(U_1)^{-1}H_j^{-1}\;,\\
        s\coloneqq 6c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1\;,\qquad t\coloneqq e^{s}-1\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation*}
with $c_{\mathrm h}$ and $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation}.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}[The Leading Term and the Coarse Loop]\label{prop:coarse-loop-form}
Let (H1)--(H4) hold, and let $s\leqslant 1/10$ and $t\leqslant r_G$ (conditions on $g_0$), with $s$, $t$ of Definition~\ref{def:coarse-loop} and $r_G$ the group constant of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}. Then on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, at every branch:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item for every $j$, with $c$ the positive coarse bond such that $c_j=\pm c$: $U_1\in\mathcal O_c$, $V(c)= e^{i\beta_c(U_1)}P_c(U_1)$, and
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:coarse-loop-insertions}
        \bigl\|V(c_j)P_{c_j}(U_1)^{-1}-\id\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant t\;,\qquad \|\beta_c(U_1)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2\arcsin(t/2)\leqslant 1.06\,s\;;
    \end{equation}
    \item the coarse holonomy is
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:coarse-loop-identity}
        \Hol_VC_n=\widetilde R_0\widetilde R_1\cdots\widetilde R_{4n-1}\,\Hol_{U_1}C_n\;,\qquad \bigl\|\widetilde R_0\cdots\widetilde R_{4n-1}-\id\bigr\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant e^{4ns}-1\;,
    \end{equation}
    where $V(c_j)P_{c_j}(U_1)^{-1}$ depends on $U_1$ only through the bonds with both endpoints in the two blocks of $c_j$;
    \item with $\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:character-lipschitz},
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:coarse-loop-difference}
        \bigl|W_{\chi}(C_n;V)-W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr|\leqslant \mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}\bigl(e^{6c_{\mathrm h}n_C\varepsilon_1/L}-1\bigr)\;.
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{corollary}[The Leading Term with the Coarse Loop]\label{cor:coarse-loop-expectation}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:coarse-loop-form},
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{gathered}
        \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]=\kappa_{C_n}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;V)\bigr]+E_{\mathrm{coarse}}+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\;,\\
        | E_{\mathrm{coarse}}|\leqslant |\kappa_{C_n}|\,\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}\bigl(e^{6c_{\mathrm h}n_C\varepsilon_1/L}-1\bigr)e^{C\tau^2(9n+1)}\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation*}
and, under the additional hypotheses of (H2) and (H3) for Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}(iii),
\begin{equation*}
    | E_{\mathrm{coarse}}|\leqslant |\kappa_{C_n}|\,\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}\bigl(e^{6c_{\mathrm h}n_C\varepsilon_1/L}-1\bigr)\exp\bigl[C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q\bigr]\;,
\end{equation*}
with $E_{\mathrm{def}}$, $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ and the constants of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:coarse-loop-form} and Corollary~\ref{cor:coarse-loop-expectation}]
\emph{Location.} For each $j$ let $c$ be the positive coarse bond with $c_j=\pm c$, and $\mathcal E_c$ the set of bonds with both endpoints in the two blocks $\mathcal B_{c_-}$, $\mathcal B_{c_+}$ of $c$. Every loop in $\beta_c$, $U(\gamma)U([x,x'])U(\gamma')^{-1}P_c(U)^{-1}$ with $\gamma\in\mathcal G(c_-,x)$, $\gamma'\in\mathcal G(c_+,x')$, uses only bonds of $\mathcal E_c$: $\gamma$ and $\gamma'$ are monotone paths inside the boxes $\mathcal B_{c_-}$, $\mathcal B_{c_+}$, and $[x,x']$ and the straight path of $c$ run from $\mathcal B_{c_-}$ to $\mathcal B_{c_+}$. The plaquettes used below lie in the box $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$, of $\ell^{\infty}$ diameter $2L-1$.

On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $\Lambda_b\subseteq I=\Lambda_1^*$ for every fine contour bond $b$ of $c$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-6}); $\Lambda_b$ is $\{b\}$ or the set of free bonds of $\mathcal E_c$. Each block of $c$ contains $(L-1)/2$ fine bonds of the straight path of $c$ with both endpoints in that block; they are free (a designated bond crosses between two blocks), so they lie in $I$, and each has an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$. Since $\Lambda_1$ is a union of blocks (the proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:main-leading-size}), both blocks of $c$ lie in $\Lambda_1$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i), every site within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $LMR_1-1>2L$ of $\Lambda_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$, so both blocks of $c$ lie in $\Omega_1$, and the constraint $\bar U_1= V$ of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} on $\Omega_1^{(1)}$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}) gives $V(c)= M(U_1,c)$.

Every plaquette of the box has a bond within distance $8L+1<3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ ($R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant 2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1= 4L+5$), so Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} gives $\|U_1(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$ for each of them.

\emph{Area.} Let $\ell$ be one of the loops, with $x= c_-+\sum_{\nu}n_{\nu}e_{\nu}$, $|n_{\nu}|\leqslant(L-1)/2$ ($\mathcal B_{c_-}$ is the block of the odd $L$ of \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} centred at $c_-$), and let $\gamma_+$ be the translate of $\gamma$ by $Le_{\mu}$, $c=(c_-,c_-+Le_{\mu})$; $\gamma_+\in\mathcal G(c_+,x')$. Passing from the order of directions of $\gamma'$ to that of $\gamma_+$ by adjacent transpositions inverts each pair of directions at most once, and exchanging two consecutive straight segments of lengths $|n_{\alpha}|$, $|n_{\beta}|$ moves the path across $|n_{\alpha}||n_{\beta}|$ plaquettes. Moving $[x,x']$ back along $\gamma$ one bond at a time crosses $L$ plaquettes for a bond of direction $\pm e_{\nu}$, $\nu\neq\mu$, and none for a bond of direction $\pm e_{\mu}$, where the two paths coincide after cancellation of backtracks. So $\ell$ is reduced to the empty loop by at most
\begin{equation*}
    A_L= \sum_{\alpha<\beta}|n_{\alpha}||n_{\beta}|+L\sum_{\nu\neq\mu}|n_{\nu}|\leqslant \tfrac32(L-1)^2+\tfrac32L(L-1)\leqslant 3L^2
\end{equation*}
plaquette moves, by $\sum_{\alpha<\beta}a_{\alpha}a_{\beta}\leqslant\frac38(\sum_{\alpha}a_{\alpha})^2$ for four nonnegative numbers and $\sum_{\nu}|n_{\nu}|\leqslant 2(L-1)$ for the first term, and by $|n_{\nu}|\leqslant(L-1)/2$ for each of the three $\nu\neq\mu$ for the second.

\emph{One loop.} A move across a plaquette $p$ multiplies the transport of the loop at its base point by $gU_1(\partial p)^{\pm1}g^{-1}$, with $g\in G$ a transport along the current loop. So $U_1(\ell)$ is a product of at most $A_L$ such conjugates. For unitary $W$ and $g$, $\| gWg^{-1}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\| W-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\| W^{-1}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, and $\|\prod_m(\id+a_m)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant\prod_m(1+\| a_m\|_{\mathrm{op}})-1$; hence
\begin{equation*}
    \| U_1(\ell)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant(1+2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2})^{3L^2}-1\leqslant t\;.
\end{equation*}
The eigenvalues $e^{i\varphi}$ of $U_1(\ell)$, $\varphi\in(-\pi,\pi]$, satisfy $2|\sin(\varphi/2)|=| e^{i\varphi}-1|\leqslant t$, so the Hermitian matrix $A$ with $e^{iA}= U_1(\ell)$ whose eigenvalues are these $\varphi$ has $\| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2\arcsin(t/2)$. The function $\phi(s)= 2\arcsin((e^{s}-1)/2)$ is convex on $[0,1/10]$, its derivative $e^{s}(1-(e^{s}-1)^2/4)^{-1/2}$ being increasing, so $\phi(s)\leqslant 10\phi(1/10)s\leqslant 1.06s$.

Since $U_1(\ell)\in G$ and $\| U_1(\ell)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant t\leqslant r_G$, $U_1(\ell)$ lies in the chart domain (Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}): $U_1(\ell)= e^{iB}$ with $B\in\mathfrak g$ and $h(B)<\varrho_G$, so $\| B\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant\sqrt N h(B)<\pi$. A Hermitian $B$ with $e^{iB}= U_1(\ell)$ and spectrum in $(-\pi,\pi)$ is the function of $U_1(\ell)$ that takes the value $\varphi$ on the eigenspace of $e^{i\varphi}$, $\varphi\in(-\pi,\pi)$, since $\lambda\mapsto e^{i\lambda}$ is injective on $(-\pi,\pi)$; so $B= A$. Hence $A\in\mathfrak g$, $h(A)<\varrho_G$, and $A$ is the chart value $\frac1i\log U_1(\ell)$, the chart being the inverse of $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ on the chart ball. Hence $U_1\in\mathcal O_c$.

\emph{One coarse bond.} $\beta_c(U_1)$ is a convex combination of the matrices $\frac1i\log U_1(\ell)$ (the weights of \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} are nonnegative and sum to one, $|\mathcal B_{c_-}|= L^4$), so $\|\beta_c(U_1)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2\arcsin(t/2)$, and $V(c)P_c(U_1)^{-1}= e^{i\beta_c(U_1)}$ has $\| e^{i\beta_c(U_1)}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2\sin(\arcsin(t/2))= t$. For $c_j=-c$, $V(c_j)P_{c_j}(U_1)^{-1}= P_c(U_1)^{-1}e^{-i\beta_c(U_1)}P_c(U_1)$, a conjugate of $e^{-i\beta_c(U_1)}$, with the same bound. This is (i), and the dependence stated in (ii) is Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}(i).

\emph{The loop.} By induction on $m$, $V(c_0)\cdots V(c_{m-1})=\widetilde R_0\cdots\widetilde R_{m-1}H_m$, the step being
\begin{equation*}
    \widetilde R_0\cdots\widetilde R_{m-1}H_mV(c_m)=\widetilde R_0\cdots\widetilde R_{m-1}\bigl(H_mV(c_m)P_{c_m}(U_1)^{-1}H_m^{-1}\bigr)H_mP_{c_m}(U_1)\;.
\end{equation*}
At $m= 4n$ this is the identity in \eqref{eq:coarse-loop-identity}. Each $\widetilde R_j$ is a conjugate of $V(c_j)P_{c_j}(U_1)^{-1}$, so $\|\widetilde R_j-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant t$ and $\|\widetilde R_0\cdots\widetilde R_{4n-1}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant(1+t)^{4n}-1= e^{4ns}-1$.

For (iii), $\chi$ is $(\dim\pi_{\chi})^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}\pi_{\chi}$ and $|(\dim\pi_{\chi})^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}X|\leqslant\| X\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, so
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
        | W_{\chi}(C_n;V)-W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)|&\leqslant\|\pi_{\chi}(\Hol_VC_n)-\pi_{\chi}(\Hol_{U_1}C_n)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\\
        &\leqslant\mathrm{Lip}_{\chi}\|\Hol_VC_n-\Hol_{U_1}C_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
and $\|\Hol_VC_n-\Hol_{U_1}C_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|(\widetilde R_0\cdots\widetilde R_{4n-1}-\id)\Hol_{U_1}C_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant e^{4ns}-1$, with $4ns= 24c_{\mathrm h}n\varepsilon_1= 6c_{\mathrm h}n_C\varepsilon_1/L$.

\emph{The expectation.} On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)= W_{\chi}(C_n;V)+(W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)-W_{\chi}(C_n;V))$. Inserted into \eqref{eq:thm-main-identity}, it gives the stated identity with $E_{\mathrm{coarse}}=\kappa_{C_n}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}(W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)-W_{\chi}(C_n;V))]$. Since $| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}|\leqslant e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}$, \eqref{eq:coarse-loop-difference} with $| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|\leqslant C\tau^2(9n+1)$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ \eqref{eq:thm-main-bounds} and $|\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[X]|\leqslant\sup| X|$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-6}) gives the first bound on $E_{\mathrm{coarse}}$, and \eqref{eq:coarse-loop-difference} with \eqref{eq:thm-main-moment} the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The Fine and the Coarse Loop]\label{rem:coarse-loop-form}
(1) \eqref{eq:coarse-loop-identity} is exact: after the first step the fine loop at the background is the coarse holonomy with one insertion per coarse bond, $\Hol_{U_1}C_n= V(c_0)Q_0V(c_1)Q_1\cdots V(c_{4n-1})Q_{4n-1}$ with $Q_j\coloneqq V(c_j)^{-1}P_{c_j}(U_1)$. For $c_j=\pm c$, $Q_j$ is $P_c(U_1)^{-1}e^{-i\beta_c(U_1)}P_c(U_1)$ if $c_j= c$ and $e^{i\beta_c(U_1)}$ if $c_j=-c$, a function of $U_1$ on the bonds of $\mathcal E_{c_j}$, with $\| Q_j-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant t$. The $\widetilde R_j$ of (ii) are conjugates of the $V(c_j)P_{c_j}(U_1)^{-1}$ by the transports $H_j$ along the earlier bonds, and are not local. The insertions are of first order in the plaquette deviations of $U_1$, of size $O(\varepsilon_1)$ per coarse bond.

(2) Per fine contour bond the exponent in \eqref{eq:coarse-loop-difference} is $6c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1/L$, of order $L^{-1}g_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$, while that of $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ is $C_{\chi}\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})$, of order $g_0^3$ times a power of $\log g_0^{-2}$. For a square of fixed physical side $\ell_C$, $n_C$ is of order $\ell_C/\varepsilon$, and $E_{\mathrm{coarse}}$ is controlled by Corollary~\ref{cor:coarse-loop-expectation} only while $n_C\varepsilon_1/L$ is small.

(3) Both $W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)$ and $W_{\chi}(C_n;V)$ are functions of the coarse field and the branch data: after the first step no integral over the free variable $a$ remains in which their difference is averaged ($\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ integrates over the branch data, the retained fluctuation $A_{\mathrm e}$ included). Every average of the difference is taken in the coarse ensemble $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$, which Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem} leaves unevaluated, so a bound on $E_{\mathrm{coarse}}$ that uses cancellations of the first-order part of the insertions is a statement about the coarse measure.
\end{remark}

\begin{definition}[The Two-Loop Data]\label{def:two-loop-data}
$C= C_1\sqcup C_2$, $\chi_1$, $\chi_2$, $n_C\coloneqq n_{C_1}+n_{C_2}$, and $W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U)\coloneqq\chi_1(\Hol_UC_1)\chi_2(\Hol_UC_2)$ are as in Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-setting}: $C_i$ is a coarse translate of the counterclockwise square of side $n_iL$ in a plane parallel to that of $e_1,e_2$, $\chi_i$ is a normalised irreducible character, and $V(C_1)\cap V(C_2)=\varnothing$.

$A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ is the covered event of the pair, $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ and $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ are the terms \eqref{eq:c4-1-1} and \eqref{eq:c3-6-2} formed with the observable and the groups of the pair (Section~\ref{sec:two-loops}), $\kappa_{C_i}$ and $E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}$ are the coefficient and the exponent of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem} for $(C_i,\chi_i)$, $E^{\times}_{\xi}$ is the cross exponent of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}(b), $\Delta_{\times}$ and $d$ are as in \eqref{eq:two-loop-cross-sum}, and $J_{C_i}$ is the set of the $4n_i$ coarse segments of $C_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The Two-Loop Constants]\label{def:two-loop-constants}
For the data of Definition~\ref{def:two-loop-data}:
\begin{itemize}
\item $C$ and the $c$ of the bounds on $E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}$ and of the moment bound are the larger, respectively the smaller, of the constants of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} for the two characters, and $d_j$ is the distance \eqref{eq:c4c-1-1} of segment $j$ of $C_i$ at the carrier $I=\Lambda_1^*$ (not the distance $d$ of \eqref{eq:two-loop-cross-sum});
\item $C_{\chi}\coloneqq\max_iC_{\chi_i}$ and the $c$ of the bound on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}, formed from the constants of \eqref{eq:c4-6-8}, and $C_{\times}$, $c_{\times}$ are the constants of that lemma;
\item $\rho$ is \eqref{eq:c4-4-8} with $u= C^{\mathrm{src}}_{\chi_1\chi_2}g_0(1+r)$, the enlarged source constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-source}, which is distinct from this $C_{\chi}$;
\item $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1\chi_2}\coloneqq C_L\max((C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1}+C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_2})S_c,1)$, with the constants $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_i}$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:c3-6-1} for $\chi_i$ (those of \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} as enlarged in Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound}, before the replacement made in \eqref{eq:c3-7-14}) and $C_L$, $S_c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5};
\item $C'_L$, $c_*$, $C_K$, $\tau$, $\pi_*$, $\varepsilon_1$, and $b$ are those of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}, a constant that depends on the character being taken at its larger value for $\chi_1,\chi_2$ when it is a prefactor and at its smaller value when it is a decay rate.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

The constants $C$, $c$, $C_{\chi}$, $C^{\mathrm{src}}_{\chi_1\chi_2}$, $C_{\times}$, $c_{\times}$, $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1\chi_2}$, $C'_L$, and $c_*$ are fixed before the coupling; $C_K$ and the scales $\tau$, $\pi_*$, $\varepsilon_1$, $\rho$, and $b$ depend on $g_0$ as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}; none of them depends on $n_1$, $n_2$, the positions of the squares, the torus, or the history.

\begin{theorem}[Two Disjoint Squares after the First Renormalisation Step]\label{thm:two-loop-theorem}
Let (H1)--(H4) hold for $(C_1,\chi_1)$ and for $(C_2,\chi_2)$ in place of $(C_n,\chi)$, and let $g_0$ lie below the thresholds of Section~\ref{sec:two-loops}: those of Lemmas~\ref{lem:two-loop-source}, \ref{lem:two-loop-pins} and~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}, and for Corollary~\ref{cor:two-loop-size} that of \eqref{eq:two-loop-moment}. Then, with the data of Definition~\ref{def:two-loop-data} and the constants of Definition~\ref{def:two-loop-constants}:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item (Form.)
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:thm-two-identity}
        \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C)]=\kappa_{C_1}\kappa_{C_2}\,\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}+E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}+E^{\times}_{\xi}}W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U_1)\bigr]+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\;,
    \end{equation}
    every term being integrable against the history weight; $\kappa_{C_i}\neq0$ depends on $n_i$ through $P(C_i)$ alone, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}(i).
    \item (Bounds.) On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $| E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}|\leqslant C\tau^2\bigl[\sum_{j\in J_{C_i}}e^{-cd_j}+4n_ie^{-c\iota_T}+(n_i+1)e^{-cn_i}\bigr]\leqslant C\tau^2(9n_i+1)$ for $i=1,2$, and
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:thm-two-bounds}
        \begin{gathered}
            | E^{\times}_{\xi}|\leqslant C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}\leqslant C_{\times}\rho\,n_Ce^{-c_{\times} d/(LM)}\;,\\
            | E_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}\Bigl[C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}+e^{C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}-1\Bigr]\;,\\
            | E_{\mathrm{bdry}}|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1\chi_2}\,n_C(1+g_0r)\,e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}\;.
        \end{gathered}
    \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}[Size of the Two-Loop Leading Term]\label{cor:two-loop-size}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:two-loop-theorem}, with the same data and constants,
\[
    |\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}+E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}+E^{\times}_{\xi}}W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U_1)]|\leqslant e^{C\tau^2(9n_1+9n_2+2)+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}\;,
\]
and under the condition of (H3) for Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}(iii) for each square,
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:thm-two-moment}
    \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}|+| E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}|}\bigr]\leqslant \exp\bigl[2C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^{I,2}_q\bigr]\;,\qquad\delta^{I,2}_q\leqslant \exp\bigl[-c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)\bigr]\;,
\end{equation}
with $\delta^{I,2}_q$ of \eqref{eq:two-loop-moment}, so that the leading term of \eqref{eq:thm-two-identity} has modulus at most $|\kappa_{C_1}\kappa_{C_2}|e^{X}$ and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}+E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}+E^{\times}_{\xi}}-1|]\leqslant e^{X}-1$, with $X\coloneqq 2C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^{I,2}_q+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:two-loop-theorem} and Corollary~\ref{cor:two-loop-size}]
Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-proof}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The Cross Terms]\label{rem:two-loop-regime}
No condition on the distance of the squares is imposed beyond $V(C_1)\cap V(C_2)=\varnothing$. The cross factor $e^{E^{\times}_{\xi}}$ and the factors $e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$ in \eqref{eq:thm-two-bounds} and in Corollary~\ref{cor:two-loop-size} are close to one when $C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}$ is small. Since $\Delta_{\times}\leqslant n_C$ and $\rho= O(g_0^2(1+r)^4)$, this holds at fixed $n_1$, $n_2$ for all positions of the squares once $g_0$ is small; at fixed coupling, $C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}\leqslant \epsilon$ whenever $d/(LM)\geqslant c_{\times}^{-1}(\log(C_{\times}\rho n_C)+\log\epsilon^{-1})$, which the hypotheses allow on tori with correspondingly large periods. As $C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}\to0$ the bound on $E^{\times}_{\xi}$ tends to zero, and those on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ and $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ take the form of \eqref{eq:thm-main-bounds} with $n_C= n_{C_1}+n_{C_2}$ and the constants $C_{\chi}$, $c$, $\rho$, $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1\chi_2}$ of Definition~\ref{def:two-loop-constants}.
\end{remark}

\section{Extraction from the Effective Interaction}
\label{sec:extraction-procedure}

Ba{\l}aban first constructs the effective interaction as a function of the remaining field. He then extracts its relevant coefficients at the identity and subtracts the corresponding local terms from that field-dependent interaction. The convention is that of \cite[(1.6)--(1.7)]{BalabanRG1} and \cite[(1.30)]{BalabanCRE}, in which the Gaussian normalisation is included in the effective interaction. The intermediate definition in \cite[(2.13)]{BalabanRG1} keeps that contribution separate.

In the small-field construction of \cite{BalabanRG1}, with no large-field regions, let $B$ be a small coarse Lie-algebra field, and let $U_1(e^{iB})$ be the constrained critical configuration with coarse field $e^{iB}$. With $\mathbf E^{(1)}$ the first-step effective interaction, including the Gaussian normalisation,
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal E_1(B)=\mathbf E^{(1)}(g_0,U_1(e^{iB}))\;.
\end{equation}
In an orthonormal basis of the Lie algebra for the action's invariant inner product, the index $a$ denotes a basis element, $\mu$ a bond direction and $x$ its initial coarse site. The second derivative is
\begin{equation}
    \Pi_{1,\mu\nu}^{ab}(x,y)
        \coloneqq\left.
            \frac{\partial^2\mathcal E_1(B)}
                {\partial B_{\mu}^a(x)\,\partial B_{\nu}^b(y)}
          \right|_{B=0}\;.
\end{equation}
