After the colour reduction and the translation-invariant infinite-lattice limit, let $\Pi_{1,\mu\nu}(x)$ denote the resulting scalar kernel with its second site fixed at the origin. In Ba{\l}aban's conventions the coupling counterterm is
\begin{equation}
    \beta_1(g_0)\coloneqq\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^4}x_1x_2\Pi_{1,12}(g_0,x)\;.
\end{equation}
The definition and the symmetry argument are given in \cite[(1.20)--(1.22), (5.37)--(5.43)]{BalabanRG1}.

In a proper regular region $\Lambda_1$, the subtraction has the form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:balaban-regular-subtraction}
    \mathbf E^{(1)}(\Lambda_1,g_0,U_1)
        -\mathbf E^{(1)}(\Lambda_1,g_0,\id)
        -\beta_1(g_0)S_{\phi_1}(U_1)\;.
\end{equation}
Here $\phi_1$ is the localisation cutoff in \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE}, supported in $\Lambda_1$ and equal to one on its specified interior. If $x(p)$ is the initial site of an oriented representative of the plaquette $p$, then
\begin{equation}
    S_{\phi_1}(U)=
        \sum_p\phi_1(x(p))
            \bigl(1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N U(\partial p)\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
The boundary interaction and the exterior integrations remain in \cite[(1.29)--(1.30)]{BalabanCRE}. Ba{\l}aban states after (1.30) that the regular interaction is the interaction of \cite{BalabanRG1} restricted to $\Lambda_1$. Within the cube-localised construction of \cite{BalabanRG1}, the changes of reconstruction and summation domain are controlled in \cite[(4.35)--(4.37)]{BalabanRG1}.

For the Wilson loop, the quantities to extract are the scalar density along a straight side and the scalar contribution of a corner. We denote them by $\delta m$ and $z_{\mathrm c}$. Their construction below uses connected terms of the normalised Wilson integral at the identity background.

Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} identifies the straight-side coefficient with the flat projection of the conditional Wilson kernel in the first RG step, and estimates the error caused by its integration boundary. Section~\ref{sec:remaining-physical-comparison} gives the outgoing insertion with the reconstructed closed flux factors and the remaining conditional source terms retained. Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} writes the conditional first-step integral with the insertion, at the actual background and exterior fields, as an exact sum of local closed insertions paired with signed local measures; the estimates it states as lemmas are proved in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}.

\section{The Sourced Effective Interaction at the First Step}
\label{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}

This section carries out the first step of the procedure in Section~\ref{sec:extraction-procedure}: the conditional first-step integral with the Wilson insertion is written as an exact sum of local closed insertions paired with signed local measures, at the actual background and exterior fields. Every displayed identity is exact at fixed volume. The existence of the objects in those identities and one cluster identity are stated here as lemmas and proved in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}: the two-sided bounds on the block $H_{\xi,II}$ of the regional Hessian on the integration carrier (Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}), the analyticity of the reconstruction on the cutoff box (Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}), the finiteness of the selected integrals (Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}) and the absolute convergence of the cluster sums (Lemmas~\ref{lem:activity-bounds} and~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}, the latter including the cluster identity \eqref{eq:part1-joint-vacuum-exponential}, whose proof is Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:kp}).

Each identity below holds under those lemmas, under the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}, and under the branch hypotheses (B1)--(B4), which record what is taken from Ba{\l}aban's construction of the branch density. The other inputs are Ba{\l}aban's derivation of \cite[(1.11)--(1.25)]{BalabanCRE}, as recorded after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}, \cite[(0.4) and (0.10)--(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} for the averaging operation and the axial transports, Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance} for the flat values, and the $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariance \eqref{eq:marginal-cutoff-invariance} of the bond norm. The bounds on the terms of the final identity are Appendices~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard} and~\ref{app:signed-defects} and Section~\ref{sec:leading-moment}.

Conventions. $G$ is the compact connected simple gauge group fixed at the start of the paper, in its fixed unitary realisation, so that group elements near the identity are $U= e^{iA}$ with $A$ in the real vector space $\mathfrak g$ of Hermitian matrices $i^{-1}\times$(Lie algebra); $\langle X,Y\rangle=\tr_N(XY)$ is the fixed $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant real inner product on $\mathfrak g$ of the flat calculation (the opening paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:flat}; it is the inner product for which every constant of Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance}, in particular $\gamma_L$, is derived), $h(X)=\langle X,X\rangle^{1/2}$, $d_G=\dim\mathfrak g$.

Every quadratic form of this section is defined without reference to this choice; the operators representing the forms, the Hilbert norms, the Lebesgue measures $\dd a$, the $\delta$-functions of \cite[(1.14)]{BalabanCRE}, the Haar density $\sigma$ and the determinants all refer to this one inner product, and a constant said to depend on $L$ and the group only is a constant for it. The identity \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} is an identity between the fine integral, which involves no inner product, and an expression whose measures $\dd A$, $\delta$-functions and densities $\sigma$, constants $\sigma_0$, $z^{(0)}$ are taken for one and the same inner product on $\mathfrak g$, whichever it is; it therefore holds for the fixed inner product with the function $\sigma$ and the constants $\sigma_0$, $z^{(0)}$ belonging to it, and these are the values meant below.

$\log$ is the group chart: the inverse of $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ on the $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant Hilbert ball $h(A)<\varrho_G\coloneqq \pi/\sqrt N$, whose range in $G$ is the chart domain. On this ball $\| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt N\,h(A)<\pi$ (for $h$ the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm, $h(A)^2= N^{-1}\sum_j\lambda_j^2\geqslant N^{-1}\| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2$), so the eigenvalues of $A$ lie in $(-\pi,\pi)$: $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ is injective there (an eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $A$ is recovered from the eigenvalue $e^{i\lambda}$ of $e^{iA}$ on the same eigenspace), its differential is invertible (the differential of $\exp$ at $iA$ is singular only when two eigenvalues of $iA$ differ by a nonzero multiple of $2\pi i$), and its inverse is the restriction to the chart domain of the principal logarithm $\frac1i\log$ used in the flat calculation (``the chart domain'' of $\mathcal O_c$, the sentence preceding \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} and \eqref{eq:global-average}; ``the regular chart containing the identity'', the sentence following \eqref{eq:action-primitive}); every logarithm below is taken in this chart.

The chart is Ba{\l}aban's: \cite[p.~21, (22)--(25)]{BalabanAVG} defines $\log U= iA$ for a unitary $U=\sum_je^{i\lambda_j}P_j$ (spectral projections $P_j$, distinct $\lambda_j\in\,]-\pi,\pi]$) by $A=\sum_j\lambda_jP_j$, Hermitian with $| A|\leqslant \pi$, with the bounds $| U-1|\leqslant |\log U|\leqslant \frac\pi2| U-1|$; the chart logarithm is the restriction of this principal logarithm to the chart domain, on which it is analytic, and the bound (25) holds for the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm $h$ as for the operator norm, since $| e^{i\lambda}-1|=2|\sin(\lambda/2)|\geqslant \frac2\pi|\lambda|$ for $\lambda\in\,]-\pi,\pi]$: $h(\frac1i\log W)\leqslant \frac\pi2h(W-\id)$, and a unitary $W\in G$ with $\| W-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant r_G$, in particular one with $h(W-\id)\leqslant r_G/\sqrt N$, lies in the chart domain, $r_G$ being the group constant of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}.

In particular ``$\mathsf M(U)(c)$ is defined'' means throughout that every logarithm in the averaging formula \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} for the row $c$ has its argument in the chart domain, that is $U\in\mathcal O_c$, where the averaging operation \eqref{eq:global-average} is \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} (it is defined for every $U$; off $\mathcal O_c$ it is the straight transport, a value that enters only through the constraint $\bar V_0= V$ on the rows of $\Omega_1^c$, Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), and ``the local group means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ are defined'' that the transports along the path family from $y$ to $x$ lie in the small-diameter domain of the fixed group mean selected after \cite[(0.9)]{BalabanRG1}, with the relative logarithms of (0.10) in the chart domain. The mean is that specified analytic mean, with the left-right covariance of \cite[(0.6) and (0.10)]{BalabanRG1}, and $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ is defined by (0.11); the implicit function theorem identifies the specified mean with its near-diagonal solution on a sufficiently small neighbourhood. The same convention defines the domain $D^{(11)}$ of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}, the set $\mathcal X$ of the measurability paragraph and the objects of Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}.

The chart being Ba{\l}aban's, the domain statement that on the domain of integration in \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} the arguments of these logarithms and the fluctuation lie in the chart domain is the smallness of the fluctuation in \cite[pp.~247--248]{BalabanCRE} (by Lemma~1 of \cite{BalabanREG}) and of the contour variables (\cite[pp.~24--25]{BalabanAVG}), derived in (B1) for $\varepsilon_0$ small; its constants $O(L^2)$ and $O(1)$ are those of \cite[Lemma~1, p.~79]{BalabanREG} and \cite[p.~25]{BalabanAVG}, independent of the coupling, as recorded in (B1) and in the hypothesis (H4) of the main theorem.

Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} uses besides $\varrho_G$ an operator-norm radius $r_G$ and the comparison constants $c_{\mathrm h}=\sqrt N$, $c_{\mathrm n}=1/N$ between $h$, the matrix norm $|\bigcdot |$ of the cutoff and $\|\bigcdot \|_{\mathrm{op}}$ ($h\leqslant |\bigcdot |\leqslant \|\bigcdot \|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt N h$, where $h(Y)\coloneqq(N^{-1}\tr Y^*Y)^{1/2}$ for an arbitrary matrix $Y$, so that $\| Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}| Y|$ for every matrix and either cutoff norm); they are recalled where used. The right inverse $h_U$ and the force $J_U$ of Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils} always carry their background subscript, which distinguishes them from the norm $h$ and the carrier $J$. $| X|$ is the bond norm of \cite{BalabanCRE} used in \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}, \eqref{eq:marginal-two-cutoffs} (the operator or the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm, fixed once; both are $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant by \eqref{eq:marginal-cutoff-invariance}). For $B\in\mathfrak g^S$ the Hilbert norm is $\| B\|^2=\sum_{b\in S}h(B_b)^2$ and the phase norm is $\| B\|_{\infty}=\max_bh(B_b)$.

$E_*$ is the set of free bonds (all positive fine bonds except the designated bonds $b_0(c)$, \cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1}: $b_0(c)$ is the fine bond contained in the coarse bond $c$ whose endpoints lie in the two blocks of $c$, the sentence following \eqref{eq:constraint-primitive}); $\mathcal B_y$ is the block with centre $y$ and $b_{\pm}$ the endpoints of a bond $b$; distances of bonds are periodic $\ell^{\infty}$ distances of initial vertices.

Bonds and rows of a set $X$ of sites follow \cite[(1.8)--(1.9)]{BalabanCRE}: the bonds of $X$ are the positive fine bonds with at least one endpoint in $X$, $X^{(1)}$ is the set of block centres in $X$, the rows of $X$ are the coarse bonds with at least one endpoint in $X^{(1)}$, written $X^{[1]}$, and $X^*$ is the set of bonds of $X$ other than the designated bonds $b_0(c)$, $c\in X^{[1]}$ (so a bond of $X^*$ may have one endpoint outside $X$, and the variables of a row of $X$ include its designated bond).

The complement is treated differently, following this paper's reading of \cite[(1.11)--(1.12)]{BalabanCRE}, which say only that $V_0= U|_{\Omega_1^c}$ are the integration variables localised in $\Omega_1^c$ (p.248), read with the bonds crossing from $\Omega_1$ to $\Omega_1^c$ as variables of the integral over $\Omega_1$ (the rule of \cite[(8), p.~258]{BalabanUV3} for plaquettes, ``plaquettes with at least one corner belonging to $\Omega_1$'', applied to bonds; the rows are those of \cite[(12), p.~258]{BalabanUV3}, which \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} follows, (H4)): the bonds of $\Omega_1^c$, written $b\in\Omega_1^c$, are the positive fine bonds with both endpoints off $\Omega_1$, the restriction $V_0= U|_{\Omega_1^c}$ is the restriction to these bonds, and the rows of $\Omega_1^c$ are the coarse bonds with both block centres off $\Omega_1$; so every positive fine bond is a bond of $\Omega_1$ or a bond of $\Omega_1^c$ and not both, and every coarse bond is a row of $\Omega_1$ or a row of $\Omega_1^c$ and not both.

$X^{\sim}$ is Ba{\l}aban's enlargement \cite{BalabanCRE} of $X$ by all cubes touching $X$ (p.245; including the cubes meeting $X$ only at an edge or a vertex, as in \cite[p.~257]{BalabanRG1}, where $\tilde\square^n$ is the cube of side $(1+2n)M$ with the centre of $\square$, (H4); used for the distance statement at the end of this sentence and in Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i)) of the partition in terms of which $X$ is defined (p.245, where the partition into cubes $\square$ of side $LM_2R_0$ is introduced, $\square^{\sim}$ is $\square$ enlarged by one layer of $M_2R_0$-cubes, and ``usually'' $X^{\sim}$ enlarges by a layer of the cubes of the partition defining $X$; here $LMR_1$-cubes for $\Omega_1$, $R_1'$ and $\Lambda_1$, $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes for $\square'$, $Q_1$ and $R_1$, p.246), $X^{\sim-1}=((X^c)^{\sim})^c$ is the shrinking and $X^{\sim k}$ the $k$-fold iterate; a site of $X^{\sim-1}$ is at $\ell^{\infty}$ distance at least the cube side from $X^c$.

The exponent of \cite{BalabanCRE} in the definition of the scales, $R_j$ the smallest power of $L$ with $R_j\geqslant (\log g_j^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$, $\mathfrak r\geqslant 2$ and $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r$ (p.245, p.246, \cite[(2.5)]{BalabanCRE}), is written $\mathfrak r$ here, because $r$ is the cutoff radius of \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}. The scales of \cite{BalabanCRE} satisfy $R_0\leqslant (L+1)R_1$ by \cite[(2.9), p.~256]{BalabanCRE}, hence $R_0\leqslant LR_1$ as both are powers of $L$; and $M_1$ is the $M_1$ of \cite[p.~245]{BalabanCRE}, the size of cubes for which the theorems of the previous papers, in particular those on the variational problem, are valid (a lower bound on the cube side: \cite[Theorem~3.1, p.~397]{BalabanPBG} holds ``for $M\geqslant M_1$'', and $M_1$ ``was fixed in'' that paper, \cite[p.~77]{BalabanREG}; \cite{BalabanCRE} takes $M_2= L^2M_1$ as an example, which is consistent with the conditions below).

The identity of a matrix space is written $\id$; the action is $S$ (the $A(U)$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}) and the scalar normaliser $E$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} is written $\mathsf E$: it is the vacuum scalar $E_{\varepsilon}$ of \eqref{eq:bare-action}, a constant independent of the configuration and of the branch, which cancels in every ratio of this paper and enters only the absolute identities for $\mathcal Z_0$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}).

The standing conditions on the parameters are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-standing-conditions}
    \begin{gathered}
    L>11\text{ odd (\cite[p.~251]{BalabanRG1})};\quad M_1< M_2< M\text{ odd powers of }L,\ M\geqslant 8LM_2;\\
    \text{\eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-collar-size}};\quad\delta_M\leqslant 1,\ h_+^2\delta_M^2/\gamma\leqslant \tfrac18,\ 4C_{\mathrm d}\delta_M^2(LM+1)^4\leqslant \tfrac12;\\
    \text{every fine period a multiple of }LMR_1\text{ and at least }8M;\\
    \text{every coarse period}>\max(2,2R_{\mathrm p}+8);\\
    g_0\text{ below the threshold of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:thresholds},}\\
    \text{which includes }LMR_1>4R_{\mathrm c}+4L^2M_2R_1+8\\
    \text{and }\widehat\mu= C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}\varepsilon_1<\min\bigl(\tfrac12\tau_L,\ \gamma_L/(4\max(1,c_L))\bigr)\\
    \text{(the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds})},
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
where $R_{\mathrm p}$ and $R_{\mathrm c}$ are the constants of that appendix (\eqref{eq:regular-covariance-radius-replay} and Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}), $\gamma$, $h_+$ those of \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-inputs}, $\delta_M$, $C_{\mathrm d}$ those of Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}, $\tau_L$, $c_L$ those of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality} and $\gamma_L$, $C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}$ those of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, all depending on $L$ and the group only ($\delta_M$ also on $M$), and $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ the quantity of \cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE}, which depends on the coupling; the threshold depends on $L$, the group, the character $\chi$ (through the constant $K_{\chi}$ of Appendix~\ref{app:signed-defects}), $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$, on the constants $A_0$, $A_1$, the exponents $p_0$ and $\mathfrak r$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, on the constants $B_3$, $\delta_{\mathrm c}$ and the $O(1)$ of the comparison after \cite[(1.19)]{BalabanCRE} recorded in (B3)(iii), and on the map $g_0\mapsto g_1$ of \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE}, which are fixed as in \cite{BalabanCRE} with $A_0/A_1$ large enough for (B3)(i); the order of choice of every constant and the list of conditions are those of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, whose closing paragraph also lists the further conditions imposed where the statements about the square and the appendices state them (Sections~\ref{sec:c3-1}, \ref{sec:c3-7}, and~\ref{sec:leading-moment}).

The threshold also takes over the conditions of \cite{BalabanCRE} on the parameters (item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}). Those on the coupling, $\varepsilon_0$ small enough for Theorem 1 of \cite{BalabanVAR} (reference [15] of \cite{BalabanCRE}, whose bracketed numbers are those of the bibliography of \cite{BalabanRG1}; \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}), $MR_1$ large (p.251, Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}), and $M_2R_1$ large enough for (B3)(ii) (p.250), are conditions that $g_0$ lies below a value depending on $L$, the group, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$, and the constants of \cite{BalabanCRE}, met for small $g_0$ at fixed $M_1,M_2,M$ since $R_1\to\infty$.

Those on $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$ are not listed in \cite{BalabanCRE}: $M_1$ is the cube size for which the theorems of the previous papers hold (p.245), $M_2$ is ``not too much larger'' than $M_1$, e.g. $M_2= L^2M_1$, and $M$ is ``much larger than $M_2$'', its choice ``dictated by many conditions involving this constant'' (p.245). They are taken over as the hypothesis that Ba{\l}aban's construction \cite{BalabanCRE} is valid for the values $M_1< M_2< M$ used here, which follow Ba{\l}aban's prescription (Section~\ref{app:thresholds}); this paper adds to them only the conditions displayed above.

The scale integer $R_1$ is the power of $L$ of \cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE} (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}; the same letter denotes the large-fluctuation region of \cite{BalabanCRE}, and in every product $LMR_1$, $L^2M_2R_1$ it is the scale), so the first-step cubes of sides $LMR_1$ and $L^2M_2R_1$, the $LM$-, $M$- and $M_1$-cubes of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} and the blocks form nested partitions of the fine torus (all sides are powers of $L$, and the $LM$-cubes nest in the $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes once $LM_2R_1\geqslant M$, threshold item 1 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, which holds for small $g_0$ since $R_1\to\infty$); the collar inequality holds once the scale satisfies $R_1\geqslant R_{\mathrm c}+3$, since $LMR_1\geqslant 8L^2M_2R_1$.

The condition ``every coarse period $>2$'' is the operative hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} (it makes $b_0(c)$ the only designated bond in $\mathcal E_c$: with a coarse period equal to two, two coarse bonds would join the same pair of blocks).

Every statement of this section is made under \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}. When $I=\varnothing$ below, $\mathfrak g^I$ is a point, $\dd a$ the unit mass, every sum reduces to its empty term and every identity holds trivially.

Some letters carry more than one meaning, each fixed by its context, as follows.
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_*$ is the walk range $n_*R$ in Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} and in the order of choice of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}; from Section~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} on it is the fixed range introduced there, bounding the label-support diameters and the source-to-stencil distances (fixed independently of the coupling), and it is this $R_*$ that enters $R_0=4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$.
\item $R_0$ is the scale of \cite{BalabanCRE} where its scales and partitions are quoted (the sentence on $R_0\leqslant (L+1)R_1$ above, p.245, and Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-seed}); from Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} on it is this paper's range constant $R_0=4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$, as stated there.
\item $R_1$ is the scale integer in every product $LMR_1$, $L^2M_2R_1$ and wherever it is called the scale, and the large-fluctuation region of \cite{BalabanCRE} where it is called a region.
\item $M$ is the cube side; the group mean is the sans-serif $\mathsf M(U)(c)$; $M(W)$ is in Section~\ref{sec:remaining-physical-comparison} the level-wise collection $M^j(W)$ of \cite[(2.11)]{BalabanCRE} at the first step, and in Section~\ref{sec:two-loops} and from Section~\ref{sec:c4-6-2} on the positive group majorant of a group $W$, with $M_v(\mathfrak c)$ the tree majorant of a tuple.
\item $\ell$ is the macro side $LMR_1$ in Section~\ref{sec:leading-moment} and in Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard}, where it is so declared, and a selection label under summation signs ($\sum_{\ell}$, Section~\ref{sec:probe-kernels}); $\ell_i(Y)= d_i(Y)+5$ are the shifted tree lengths of a domain (defined with \eqref{eq:c2-tree-length}).
\item $m_L$ is the Hessian constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}; $m$ alone is the tuple length in $\mathfrak c=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)$ (Section~\ref{sec:selected-integrals}) and the segment length in coarse units in \eqref{eq:regional-mass-identification}; $m(D)=\varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda_*\ell_1(D)}$ is the majorant of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds}; $\delta m^{\sigma}$ is the mass coefficient \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}.
\item $\theta\geqslant 0$ is the Mayer constant of Section~\ref{app:mayer-constants} (Section~\ref{sec:selected-integrals} on); in Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard}, from \eqref{eq:c3-7-4} on, $\theta$ is the witness threshold defined there, and $\theta_{\mathrm h}$, $\theta_{\mathrm x}$ are the constants of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-2}; $\vartheta$ and $\vartheta_*$ are different letters throughout.
\item $C_L$ is the coercivity constant \eqref{eq:covariance-coercivity-constant} of Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance} in Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds} ($\gamma_L= C_L^{-1}$) and that appendix; it is the contour constant $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_C$ in Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}, at the opening of Appendix~\ref{app:signed-defects}, in Section~\ref{sec:c4-2} (with $C'_L\coloneqq 8C_L$), in Corollary~\ref{cor:main-leading-size} and in Remark~\ref{rem:next-step}; elsewhere it is a constant depending on $L$ (in Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1} also on $N$) as stated where it appears.
\item $K=256$ is the fixed integer of $\sigma_K$, $C_K$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-joint}); in (H3) $K$ is the exponent of \cite{BalabanRG1} in $\varepsilon= L^{-K}$; the number of steps in Section~\ref{sec:next-step} is $k+1$.
\item The italic $B_{\xi}=\Lambda_1^c$ is the filled bad region, the calligraphic $\mathcal B_{\xi}$ the exterior response functional, and the fraktur $\mathfrak B$ a compatible family of the expansion; $B_3$ is the constant of \cite{BalabanCRE}; the fraktur $\mathfrak B_Q$ is a determining set (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}), the calligraphic $\mathcal B_y$ the block with centre $y$, and $B$ without the subscript $\xi$ a generic vector of $\mathfrak g^S$, the ball $B_{\delta}$, the bound $B_C$ or the host constants $B_h$, $B_{\mathrm h}$.
\item In Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} the letter $F$ denotes integrands, and the logarithms $F_{I,C,T}$, $F_{C,T}$, $F_{C,\infty}(n)$ and the integrals $F_{\xi}(t)$ are named with their subscripts; elsewhere $F_{\gamma}$ is a set of edges of a polymer and $F(\Gamma)$ a weight in a cluster sum.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Branch Data, the Outer Operation and the Conditional Integral}
\label{sec:branch-data}

One term of the history sum of \cite[(1.11)--(1.30)]{BalabanCRE} is fixed: the regions $\Omega_1,R_1$ (\cite{BalabanCRE} uses $R_1$ both for the large-fluctuation region of (1.18) and for the scale integer of p.246, the smallest power of $L$ with $R_1\geqslant (\log g_1^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$, which grows as $g_0\to0$; both uses are kept, the scale appearing in the products $LMR_1$, $L^2M_2R_1$, $MR_1$, $M_2R_1$ and in its defining inequality $R_1\geqslant (\log g_1^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$; here $g_1= g_1(g_0)$ is the first-step coupling of \cite{BalabanCRE}, the constant value on $\Lambda_1^{\sim-1}$ of the solution of (1.27), $g_0^{-2}= g_1^{-2}+\beta_1(g_0)$ with the $\beta_1$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, a function of $g_0$ alone, and $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ as on p.246), the derived $\Lambda_1,S_1$ of (1.20) with $\Lambda_1$ the filled domain of the modification following (1.20), the new field $V$, the integration variable $V_0$ on $\Omega_1^c$, and the background $U_1= U_1(V,V_0)$ of (1.12) in its axial mean gauge, equal to $V_0$ on $\Omega_1^c$.

The integration carrier is $I=\Lambda_1^*$, the retained free carrier is $J=\Omega_1^*\setminus I$, and $A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^J$ is the retained fluctuation. The integration variable is $a\in\mathfrak g^I$; both are extended by zero to $\Omega_1^*$ where needed. The branch data are $\xi=(\Omega_1,R_1,V,V_0,A_{\mathrm e})$.

The constraint $\delta(\bar UV^{-1})$ of \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} is a product over the coarse bonds, and it is split by rows: on the rows of $\Omega_1$ (coarse bonds with a block centre in $\Omega_1$) the constraint $\bar U= V$ is the critical-point constraint of (1.12), imposed on the integral over the bonds of $\Omega_1$ (which include the bonds crossing from $\Omega_1$ to $\Omega_1^c$; the rows with one block centre off $\Omega_1$ average also over bonds of $\Omega_1^c$, which enter as the constant $V_0$); read, like every group $\delta$-function here, by integrating against the coarse variables it constrains, it is the fibre measure of the pushforward of the fine measure under the map $\Phi(U)=(\bar U|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}},U|_{\Omega_1^c})$, a submersion on the open set $\mathcal O^{\Phi}$ of fine configurations at which the averages and means on the rows of $\Omega_1$ are defined and $D\Phi$ is onto, which contains the set $\mathcal X$ of the measurability paragraph below and, on every branch, $D(V,V_0)$ (shown there).

The fibre measures of a $C^1$ submersion $\mathsf f$ of an open set $\mathcal Y$ of a manifold with a smooth positive density, here $G^E$ with Haar measure or $\mathfrak g^E$ with Lebesgue measure, into such a manifold of dimension $k$, are defined at \emph{every} point $y$ of $\mathsf f(\mathcal Y)$, not only almost everywhere: by the submersion theorem $\mathcal Y$ is covered by open sets $\mathcal Y_j$ with $C^1$ diffeomorphisms $\psi_j$ from open sets of $\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$ onto $\mathcal Y_j$ and $\mathsf f(\psi_j(y,z))= y$; with a continuous partition of unity $(\theta_j)$ subordinate to $(\mathcal Y_j)$, $\mu^{\mathsf f}_y(g)\coloneqq \sum_j\int(\theta_jg)(\psi_j(y,z))\,|\det D\psi_j(y,z)|\,\dd z$ for Borel $g\geqslant 0$ on $\mathcal Y$, the determinants taken with respect to the densities, that of the manifold on $\mathcal Y_j$ and, on $\mathbb R^k\times\mathbb R^{n-k}$, the product of the target density in the variable $y$ and Lebesgue measure $\dd z$, so that $\dd y$ in (i) is the target density.

Then (i) $\int_{\mathcal Y}\varphi(\mathsf f(x))g(x)\,\dd x=\int\varphi(y)\,\mu^{\mathsf f}_y(g)\,\dd y$ for Borel $\varphi\geqslant 0$ (the change of variables formula and Fubini's theorem); (ii) $y\mapsto\mu^{\mathsf f}_y(g)$ is continuous for every continuous $g$ with compact support in $\mathcal Y$ (dominated convergence); (iii) the family does not depend on the choices made, two families with (i) and (ii) agreeing for almost every $y$ by (i) and hence for every $y$ by (ii); (iv) for every $y\in\mathsf f(\mathcal Y)$ and every such $g$, $\mu^{\mathsf f}_y(g)=\lim_{\delta\to0}| E_{\delta}|^{-1}\int_{\mathsf f^{-1}(E_{\delta})}g\,\dd x$ for every family of Borel sets $E_{\delta}$ with $B_{c\delta}(y)\subseteq E_{\delta}\subseteq B_{C\delta}(y)$ for constants $0< c\leqslant C$, by (i) with $\varphi=\mathbf 1_{E_{\delta}}$ and (ii) (the mean of a continuous function over $E_{\delta}$ tends to its value at $y$); so $\mu^{\mathsf f}_y$ is carried by $\mathsf f^{-1}(y)$, and the fibre measures of the restriction of $\mathsf f$ to an open subset of $\mathcal Y$ are the restrictions of the $\mu^{\mathsf f}_y$.

From (iv) follows the transformation rule, at every level: if $\Xi$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of an open set $\mathcal N_0$ onto an open subset of $\mathcal Y$, $\psi$ a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of an open neighbourhood of $\mathsf f(\Xi(\mathcal N_0))$ onto its image, and $\mathsf f'\coloneqq \psi\circ\mathsf f\circ\Xi$ on $\mathcal N_0$ (a submersion), then $\mu^{\mathsf f'}_{\psi(y)}(g\circ\Xi\,|\det D\Xi|)=|\det D\psi(y)|^{-1}\mu^{\mathsf f}_y(g)$ for every $y\in\mathsf f(\Xi(\mathcal N_0))$ and every Borel $g\geqslant 0$ on $\Xi(\mathcal N_0)$: $\int_{\mathcal N_0}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf f'(x')\in B_{\delta}(\psi(y))}\,g(\Xi(x'))\,|\det D\Xi(x')|\,\dd x'=\int_{\Xi(\mathcal N_0)}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf f(x)\in\psi^{-1}(B_{\delta}(\psi(y)))}\,g(x)\,\dd x$ exactly, for every $\delta$ (the change of variables formula for $\Xi$); the sets $E_{\delta}=\psi^{-1}(B_{\delta}(\psi(y)))$ satisfy the condition of (iv) with $| E_{\delta}|/| B_{\delta}|\to|\det D\psi(y)|^{-1}$; dividing by $| B_{\delta}|$ and letting $\delta\to0$ gives the identity for continuous $g$ of compact support, and two Radon measures on the fibre, a $C^1$ submanifold, agreeing on these agree.

For $\Phi$ on $\mathcal O^{\Phi}$: for Borel $F\geqslant 0$ supported in $\mathcal O^{\Phi}$ and Borel $\varphi\geqslant 0$ (hence for bounded Borel $\varphi$ when $F$ is integrable), $\int\varphi(\Phi(U))F(U)\,\dd U=\int\varphi(V,V_0)\int_{\Phi^{-1}(V,V_0)}F\,\dd\mu_{V,V_0}\,\dd V|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}}\dd V_0$ with $\mu_{V,V_0}\coloneqq \mu^{\Phi}_{(V,V_0)}$, defined for every $(V,V_0)\in\Phi(\mathcal O^{\Phi})$, in particular for every admissible pair, and since $\Phi$ preserves the coordinate $U|_{\Omega_1^c}$ its straightening maps may be taken to preserve it, so that for every $(V,V_0)$ the measure $\mu^{\Phi}_{(V,V_0)}$ is the fibre measure over $V$ of the submersion $U|_{\Omega_1}\mapsto\bar U|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}}$ on the slice $U|_{\Omega_1^c}= V_0$, the Jacobians agreeing because the differentials of the straightening maps are block triangular with the identity in the $V_0$ block.

The chart, linearisation, and elimination steps of \cite{BalabanCRE} listed after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} compute $\mu_{V,V_0}$ in the variables of (1.14)--(1.15), in which the constraint is linear, by the transformation rule applied at the level of the pair itself and two facts.

First, if $\Theta$ is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of an open set $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ onto its image and $\mathcal Q\circ\Theta=\Lambda$ on $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ with $\Lambda$ linear and onto, then $\mathcal Q$ is a submersion on $\Theta(\mathcal N_{\Theta})$ and its fibre measures there are $\mu^{\mathcal Q}_y=\Theta_*(|\det D\Theta|\,\mu^{\Lambda}_y)$ for every $y\in\Lambda(\mathcal N_{\Theta})$, the transformation rule with $\Xi=\Theta$ and $\psi=\id$.

Second, the fibre measure over every $y$, in particular over $0$, of a linear surjection $\Lambda$ whose restriction $\Lambda_{\mathrm d}$ to the designated variables is invertible is Lebesgue measure on the free variables $x_{\mathrm f}$ times $|\det\Lambda_{\mathrm d}|^{-1}$, since $(y,x_{\mathrm f})\mapsto(x_{\mathrm f},\Lambda_{\mathrm d}^{-1}(y-\Lambda_{\mathrm f}x_{\mathrm f}))$ is a single straightening map of $\Lambda$ with Jacobian $|\det\Lambda_{\mathrm d}|^{-1}$ (the sifting of $\delta(\Lambda x)$ over the designated variables); here that restriction is $\bigoplus_c\alpha_c(U_1)$ up to the normalisation of the $\delta$-functions, which gives $z^{(0)}(U_1)$.

The transformation rule is applied first on the slice $U|_{\Omega_1^c}= V_0$ with $\Xi$ the composition of the chart $A'\mapsto e^{iA'}$ and the right translation by $U_1$ on the bonds of $\Omega_1$ ($|\det D\Xi|=\prod_b\sigma(A'(b))$, the Haar density, with respect to Lebesgue and Haar measure) and $\psi$ the row chart $W\mapsto\frac1i\log(WV^{-1})$ on a neighbourhood of $V$ in $G^{\Omega_1^{[1]}}$ ($|\det D\psi(V)|=\sigma_0^{-|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}$ with respect to Haar and Lebesgue measure), under which the slice submersion becomes $\mathcal Q_{U_1}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation} and the level $V$ becomes the level $0$: $\mu_{V,V_0}=\sigma_0^{-|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}\Xi_*(\prod_b\sigma(A'(b))\,\mu^{\mathcal Q_{U_1}}_0)$ on $\Xi$ of the chart domain (the rule is applied on $\mathcal N_0\coloneqq \Xi^{-1}(\mathsf f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi))$, $\mathsf f$ the slice submersion, the part of the chart domain whose row averages lie in the domain of the row chart; every point of the fibre over $V$ in $\Xi$ of the chart domain lies in $\Xi(\mathcal N_0)$, since there $\mathsf f= V\in\operatorname{dom}\psi$, and the fibre measure of a restriction is the restriction of the fibre measure), which is the conversion of the row $\delta$-functions in the step list, at the level of the pair itself.

The two facts are then applied to $\mathcal Q=\mathcal Q_{U_1}$ at fixed $(V,V_0)$, at the level $0$, in the chart variable $A'$ of (1.13), with $\Theta(A)\coloneqq A-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(A)$ on the open set $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), on which $\widetilde D=\varphi$ is analytic, solves the row equations and has $\det(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)>0$, on which $\Theta$ takes chart-valued phases (so that $\Theta(\mathcal N_{\Theta})\subseteq\mathcal N_0$, the set on which the transformation rule was applied above: the phases of $\Theta(A)$ are chart-valued, and at every row $c$ the row phase $\Theta(A)|_{\mathcal E_c}$ has norm below $\vartheta_*<2\varrho_*$, where $\mathcal N_{U_1,c}$, and hence $\mathcal Q_{U_1,c}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation}, is defined and analytic (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i), which applies at every row by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i)), so that the row averages lie in the domain of the row chart), and which contains the argument of every $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(ii)) and does not depend on the region $R_1$ (this step precedes the insertion of (1.18), which introduces $R_1$): $\mathcal Q_{U_1}\circ\Theta= LQ_{U_1}=\Lambda$ on $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ (the row equations and $LQ_{U_1}h_{U_1}=\id$), and $\Theta$ is injective on $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$, since $\Theta(A)=\Theta(A'')= q$ gives $\widetilde D(A)=\mathcal N_{U_1}(q)=\widetilde D(A'')$ by the row equations $d_c=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A-h_{U_1}d)$, hence $A= q+h_{U_1}\widetilde D(A)= A''$; so $\Theta$ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ onto the open set $\Theta(\mathcal N_{\Theta})$ by the inverse function theorem.

On the rows of $\Omega_1^c$ (both block centres off $\Omega_1$) the constraint $\delta(\bar UV^{-1})$ of \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} is the constraint $\bar V_0= V$ on $V_0= U|_{\Omega_1^c}$, written $\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})$ below, and the constrained integral $\int\dd V_0|_{\Omega_1^c}\,\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})\cdots$ in the form in which Ba{\l}aban writes it in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} (in (1.11) it is part of $\int\dd U\,\delta(\bar UV^{-1})$) is taken as it stands there and read, like every group $\delta$-function of a coarse variable in this paper (the paragraph following Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}), by integrating it against the coarse variables it constrains: for bounded Borel $h$ on $G^{E_1}$ and nonnegative Borel $F$, $\int\dd V\,h(V)\int\dd V_0\,\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})F(V,V_0)=\int\dd V|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}}\int\dd V_0\,h(V)F(V,V_0)$ with $V(c)= M(V_0,c)$ of \eqref{eq:global-average} on the rows $c$ of $\Omega_1^c$ (a function of the bonds of $\Omega_1^c$ alone, Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}(i)); so $\int\mathcal O[F](V)\,\dd V$ below is the integral of $F$ against the measure in $V$ that the outer operation defines, and $\mathcal O[F](V)$ is a Haar density only where that measure has one.

Let $D^{(11)}\coloneqq D^{(11)}(\Omega_1,V)$ be the domain of integration in \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE}: the fine configurations $U$ with $\chi_1(\Omega_1)\zeta(\Omega_1^c)\chi_0'(\Omega_1)\ne0$ on which the block averages $\mathsf M(U)$ are defined on every row of $\Omega_1$ and the local group means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$, $x\in\mathcal B_y$, $y\in\Omega_1^{(1)}$, of the gauge-fixing functional $\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},U)$ of (1.11) are defined (in the chart of the preamble, Ba{\l}aban's principal logarithm; by \cite[pp.~247 and 248]{BalabanCRE} with Lemma~1 of \cite{BalabanREG} and \cite[pp.~24--25]{BalabanAVG}, derived in (B1), these two conditions are implied by the nonvanishing of the cutoffs and the constraint for $\varepsilon_0$ small, and they give $D^{(11)}\subseteq\mathcal O_c$ on every row of $\Omega_1$), subject to the constraint $\bar U= V$ on the rows of $\Omega_1$ and $\bar V_0= V$ on the rows of $\Omega_1^c$. Its fibre over the restriction is $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)=\{ U\in D^{(11)}:U|_{\Omega_1^c}= V_0\}$. A pair $(V,V_0)$, written $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ where the region is to be displayed and called a pair throughout ($\Omega_1$ is fixed on the branch), is \emph{admissible} when $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)\neq\varnothing$; (B1) provides the background $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ for every admissible pair.

The domain of integration of (1.15) with the cutoff (1.25) is in general smaller than $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ (the small- and large-fluctuation tests of (1.18) in (1.25) are further conditions; on $R_1$ the large-fluctuation tests exclude the configurations near $U_1$); it is described in the variables of (1.15) as follows. For an admissible pair, a free vector $B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}$ and a family $d=(d_c)_{c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}}$ of solutions of the row equations \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} at the argument $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ (that is, $d_c=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A-h_{U_1}d)$ for every row $c$), let $q_d(B)\coloneqq A-h_{U_1}d\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1}$, the phase \eqref{eq:native-source-local-phase} formed with this family (\cite[(1.13)--(1.14)]{BalabanCRE} at the background $U_1$; on the free bonds $q_d(B)(b)= g_0B(b)$), and let $U_d(B)$ be the fine field equal to $e^{iq_d(B)}U_1$ on the bonds of $\Omega_1$ and to $V_0$ on the bonds of $\Omega_1^c$. The family $d$ is \emph{of chart class} when $h(q_d(B)(b))<\varrho_G$ for every bond $b$ of $\Omega_1$, that is, when the whole phase $q_d(B)$ is chart-valued, the class of the variable $A'$ of \cite[(1.13)]{BalabanCRE}. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-free-variable-domain}
    \begin{aligned}
    \mathcal A_{\xi}\coloneqq \{ B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}:\ &\text{there is a family }d\text{ of chart class at }g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B\\
    &\text{with }U_d(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)\text{ and the cutoff (1.25) nonzero at }U_d(B)\}\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
the cutoff (1.25) being a function of the fine field and the branch data (its tests run over the free bonds $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$, at which the scaled variable is $g_0^{-1}\frac1i\log(UU_1^{-1})$, by (1.18)--(1.19), p.250, and (1.25), p.252, in the variables of (1.15), and through $\chi_0'(S_1)$ over the fine field; no test involves a designated value of the linearised variable, so the cutoff does not involve $\widetilde D$).

For $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$ the family $d$ of chart class with $U_d(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ is unique and equals $\varphi(g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii)), and $\widetilde D_{U_1}(g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B)\coloneqq d$, $q_{U_1}(B)\coloneqq q_d(B)$ and $U(B)\coloneqq U_d(B)$ are defined on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ by this uniqueness; the cutoff (1.25) is then a function of $B$, $U_1$ and the branch data. Since $q_{U_1}(B)$ is chart-valued, it is the chart logarithm of the fluctuation $U(B)U_1^{-1}$, so that $B\mapsto U(B)$ is injective on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ ($U(B)$ determines $U(B)U_1^{-1}$, hence its chart logarithm $q_{U_1}(B)$, hence $B$ on the free bonds, where $q_{U_1}(B)(b)\coloneqq g_0B(b)$).

Conversely, every $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ at which the cutoff (1.25) is nonzero is of the form $U(B)$ with $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$: by (B1) the fluctuation $UU_1^{-1}$ lies in the chart domain bond by bond on $\Omega_1$, so $A'\coloneqq \frac1i\log(UU_1^{-1})$ of (1.13) is defined and chart-valued; the constraint $\mathsf M(U)(c)= V(c)=\mathsf M(U_1)(c)$ on the rows of $\Omega_1$ gives $\mathcal Q_{U_1,c}(A')=0$ in \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation}, that is $LQ_{U_1}A'=-\mathcal N_{U_1}(A')$; with $d\coloneqq \mathcal N_{U_1}(A')$ the vector $A'+h_{U_1}d$ lies in the kernel of $Q_{U_1}$ ($LQ_{U_1}h_{U_1}=\id$) and agrees with $A'$ on the free bonds ($h_{U_1}$ has its outputs at the designated bonds), so it equals $g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ with $B\coloneqq g_0^{-1}A'|_{\Omega_1^*}$, the kernel of $Q_{U_1}$ being the graph of $\mathsf C_{U_1}$ over the free bonds by \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-elimination} ($\alpha_c(U_1)$ invertible, (B2) and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}); hence $A'= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B-h_{U_1}d$, $d_c=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A')=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A-h_{U_1}d)$ solves every row equation, $d$ is of chart class because $A'$ is chart-valued, and $U_d(B)= e^{iA'}U_1= U$ on $\Omega_1$ while $U|_{\Omega_1^c}= V_0$; so $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$ and $U(B)= U$.

Thus $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ is the domain of integration of (1.15) with the cutoff (1.25) in the free variable $B$ of (1.15), and $B\mapsto U(B)$ is a bijection of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ onto $D(V,V_0)\coloneqq \{ U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0):\text{the cutoff (1.25) is nonzero at }U\}= U(\mathcal A_{\xi})$, the same domain in the fine variable, and $D(\Omega_1,R_1,V)\coloneqq \bigcup_{V_0}D(V,V_0)$. By (B4)(ii) the differential of $B\mapsto U(B)$ is injective at every point of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, with image the tangent space of the fibre $\Phi^{-1}(V,V_0)$ at $U(B)$.

For an admissible pair and $A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^J$, $a\in\mathfrak g^I$ let $U_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq U(\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e}))$ be the reconstructed fine field \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field} (the inverse of the changes of variables \cite[(1.13), (1.14), (1.22)]{BalabanCRE} at the background $U_1$, defined where those are: where $(a+A_{\mathrm e})(b)\in\mathcal W_b$ for every $b\in S_1^*$, Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}, and every row solution is defined at $g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})$), and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-new-variable-domain}
    \mathcal D_{\xi}\coloneqq \{(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathfrak g^J\times\mathfrak g^I:\ \Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\text{ is defined and }\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\in\mathcal A_{\xi}\}
\end{equation}
be the domain of integration of (1.15) with the cutoff (1.25) in the variables of (1.22); by (B4)(ii) (Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection}) $\Psi_{\xi}$ maps $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ bijectively onto $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, so the reconstruction $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\mapsto U_{\xi}(a)$ is a bijection of $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ onto $D(V,V_0)$. In particular $\mathcal D_{\xi}\neq\varnothing$ exactly when $\mathcal A_{\xi}\neq\varnothing$, that is when $D(V,V_0)\neq\varnothing$.

A \emph{branch} is a value of the data $\xi$ such that $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ is admissible and $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ for some $a$. On a branch the set $\{ a:(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}\}$ is the open box $\{\Theta_{\xi}=1\}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-young-cutoff} (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(iv)), and the large-field factor $\zeta_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ of \eqref{eq:c-large-field-factor} and the retained cutoff $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})$ of \eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition} are defined and nonzero. The branch indicator $\iota_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ is one when $\xi$ is a branch and zero otherwise; as the fibre over a branch value is the open box, which contains $a=0$, $\iota_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})=1$ exactly when $(A_{\mathrm e},0)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$, a Borel condition (a section of the Borel set $\mathcal D_{\xi}$, measurability paragraph). It is a factor of the integrand of \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}, which therefore vanishes off the branches, and every object below is defined on branches only.

The sets $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, $D(V,V_0)$ and $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ depend on $\xi$ only through $(\Omega_1,R_1,V,V_0)$: the cutoff (1.25) in the variable $B$ of (1.15) and the map $\Psi_{\xi}$ do not involve $A_{\mathrm e}$, which is a variable of these sets.

For a branch function $\mathfrak M_{\xi}$, the outer operation is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}
    \mathcal O[\mathfrak M](V)
        \coloneqq\sum_{\Omega_1,R_1}\chi_1(\Omega_1)
            \int\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})
            \left[\int\iota_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\zeta_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})\kappa_{\xi}\mathfrak M_{\xi}\,\dd A_{\mathrm e}|_J\right]
            \dd V_0|_{\Omega_1^c}\;,
\end{equation}
with the prefactor
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-outer-prefactor}
    \kappa_{\xi}
        = z^{(0)}(U_1)\,g_0^{d_G|\Omega_1^*|}\sigma_0^{|\Omega_1^*|}
            z^{-(L^4-1)|\Omega_1^{(1)}|}
        \exp\left(-g_0^{-2}S(U_1)-\mathsf E\right)\;.
\end{equation}
Here $\chi_1(\Omega_1)$ is the background test of \cite[(2.16)--(2.17)]{BalabanCRE} at $k=1$, a function of $V$; $\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})$ is the part of the constraint $\delta(\bar UV^{-1})$ of (1.11) on the rows of $\Omega_1^c$ (both blocks off $\Omega_1$), as in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}, where it stands in front of the $V_0$ integral.

The large-field factor $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ of (1.11) is defined by the characteristic functions and gauge-fixing exponentials of (1.6) and (1.8) whose cubes or blocks lie in $\Omega_1^c$, resummed over the admissible $P_0$, $P_1$, $Q_1$ (p.248). It is a sum over the admissible $(P_0,P_1,Q_1)$ compatible with $\Omega_1$ of products of nonnegative functions of the fine field $U$ on the bonds near their cubes or blocks and of constants; the factors of (1.4), (1.6) and (1.8) not displayed in (1.11), and the bonds involved, are the following.
\begin{itemize}
\item The large-field factors $\chi_0^c(\square)$ of (1.1) for the $LM_2R_0$-cubes $\square\subseteq P_0$, and the factors $\chi_0(\square)$, $\square\subseteq P_0^c$, that survive the removal of (B3)(i), those of the cubes $\square\not\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim}$: every such cube is at $\ell^{\infty}$ distance at least $LMR_1$ from $\Omega_1$ ($\Omega_1^{\sim}$ adds a layer of $LMR_1$-cubes, the partitions are nested, and the large-field regions are at distance at least $2LMR_1$ from $\Omega_1$, p.248), and the factor tests the plaquettes of $\square^{\sim}$, whose bonds are within $M_2R_0\leqslant LM_2R_1\leqslant MR_1/8< LMR_1$ of $\square$ (conventions: $R_0\leqslant LR_1$ by \cite[(2.9)]{BalabanCRE}; $M\geqslant 8LM_2$), so it is a function of $V_0$.
\item The factors $\chi_1^c(\square')$, $\square'\subseteq P_1$, and $\chi_1(\square')$ of (1.4) for the cubes $\square'\subseteq P_1^c$ not in $\Omega_1$ (those in $\Omega_1$ form $\chi_1(\Omega_1)$) are functions of the block field $V$ (through the local minima $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (1.2)).
\item The gauge-fixing factors $\chi_{Ax}$ of the blocks $\mathcal B_y$, $y\in P_1^1$, not in $\Omega_1^{\sim}$ (those in $\Omega_1^{\sim}$ are removed by (B3)(i)), the exponentials $e^{-g_0^{-2}\mathbf G(P_1^1\setminus\Omega_1^{(1)},U)}$ of (1.6)--(1.7) of the blocks of $P_1^1$ off $\Omega_1$, and the constants $z^{-(L^4-1)| P_1^1\setminus\Omega_1^{(1)}|}$ of the normaliser of (1.5)--(1.6) for these blocks (the exponent of (1.11) counts the blocks of $\Omega_1^{(1)}\subseteq P_1^1$ only): a block off $\Omega_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^c$, since $\Omega_1$ is a union of blocks, and the axial transports $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ use the bonds inside the block, which are bonds of $\Omega_1^c$, so these are functions of $V_0$.
\item The factors $\chi_0'^c(\square')$, $\square'\subseteq Q_1$, and $\chi_0'(\square')$ of (1.8) for the $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1^c$ not in $Q_1$ (those in $\Omega_1$ form $\chi_0'(\Omega_1)$) involve the fine field on $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$, the bonds within $2L^2M_2R_1+1$ of $\square'$, together with the local minima $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (1.2): for $\square'\subseteq Q_1$ these are bonds of $\Omega_1^c$ ($Q_1$ is at distance at least $2LMR_1$ from $\Omega_1$ by (1.10)), and for the other cubes they are bonds of $\Omega_1^c$ and bonds of $\Omega_1$ within $2L^2M_2R_1+1$ of $\Omega_1^c$, which lie in the layer $\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\subseteq S_1$ (\cite[(1.20)]{BalabanCRE}), since $LMR_1\geqslant 8L^2M_2R_1$.
\end{itemize}
So $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ is a nonnegative function of $V$, $V_0$ and of the fine field on the bonds of $\Omega_1$ within $2L^2M_2R_1+1$ of $\Omega_1^c$, the last dependence coming from the factors $\chi_0'(\square')$, $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1^c\setminus Q_1$, only. The phrase of \cite{BalabanCRE} ``localized in $\Omega_1^c$'' refers to the cubes and blocks, and $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ is not a function of $V,V_0$ alone. In the variables of (1.22) it is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-large-field-factor}
    \zeta_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})=\zeta(\Omega_1^c)\bigl(U_{\xi}(a)\bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
with $U_{\xi}(a)$ the reconstructed fine field \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field}; the right side does not depend on $a$, because $V$, $V_0$ are branch data and the bonds of $\Omega_1$ on which $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ depends are at distance at least $LMR_1-2L^2M_2R_1-2>2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ from $\Lambda_1$, so their links are the links of far rows, functions of $A_{\mathrm e}$ and the branch data only (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}, (B4)). It is therefore a factor of the $A_{\mathrm e}$ integrand, as written in \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}.

The constants: $\sigma_0$ is the Haar constant of (1.14), $z$ the gauge-fixing normaliser of (1.5) and $\mathsf E$ the $E$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, all independent of the branch; $z^{(0)}= z^{(0)}(U_1)$ is the factor of the $\delta$-function integration over the designated variables (p.249); it is $\prod_{c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}}|\det_{\mathfrak g}\alpha_c(U_1)|^{-1}$ times a constant fixed by the normalisation of the $\delta$-functions in \cite{BalabanCRE} and by $|\Omega_1^{[1]}|$, with $\alpha_c$ of \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-designated-diagonal}, so it depends on the branch through $U_1$ (the linearised constraint $(\widetilde QA')(c)=0$ of p.249 is the row $c$ of $Q_{U_1}A'=0$, whose coefficient at $A'(b_0(c))$ is $\alpha_c(U_1)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} and \cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1}). These constants enter only through the prefactor $\kappa_{\xi}$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}.

The retained cutoff $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition}: it is the product of the retained factors of \cite[(1.25)]{BalabanCRE}, namely the good free-bond tests of (1.18) at the bonds of $J$, the large-fluctuation tests on $R_1$ and $\chi_0'(S_1)$, all composed with the change of variables (1.22), and it depends on $A_{\mathrm e}$ and the branch data only (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(ii)).

The conditional integrand $\mathcal K_{\xi}(a)$, $a\in\mathfrak g^I$, is the integrand of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} in the variables of (1.22) at the actual branch data, divided by the factors already in $\kappa_{\xi}$, $\zeta_{\xi}$ and $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}$ and by the factors $\chi_1(\Omega_1)$, $\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})$ standing outside the $A_{\mathrm e}$ integral; it is written out in \eqref{eq:native-source-actual-functional}, and $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f]=\int f\mathcal K_{\xi}\,\dd a$ is the conditional functional.

\emph{Measurability and integrability.} The integrand of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} with the cutoff (1.25), in the variables $(V,V_0,A_{\mathrm e},a)$ of (1.22), is a finite composition of indicators of sets defined by inequalities between continuous functions (the tests), of the background $U_1(V,V_0)$, of the local minima $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (1.2) entering $\chi_0'$ and of the field $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of (1.21) entering the bondwise maps (1.22), of the analytic objects of \cite{BalabanCRE} in (B4) and of the bondwise maps (1.22).

The background is a Borel function of the admissible pairs; the proof uses (B1), (B2), and the smoothness of the constraint. Let $\mathcal X$ be the open set of fine configurations $U$ on which $\mathsf M(U)$ is defined on every row of $\Omega_1$, the local group means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$, $x\in\mathcal B_y$, $y\in\Omega_1^{(1)}$, are defined (chart convention of the preamble; they are analytic there) and every $\alpha_c(U)$, $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$, is invertible (Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}), and let $\Phi(U)\coloneqq(\bar U|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}},U|_{\Omega_1^c})$ on $\mathcal X$; $D\Phi(U)$ is onto, since $LQ_Uh_U=\id$ with $h_U$ supported on the designated bonds of $\Omega_1$, so each fibre $\Phi^{-1}(V,V_0)\cap\mathcal X$ is a $C^{\infty}$ submanifold and the tangent space of the fibre is the kernel of $Q_U$, the range of $\mathsf C_U$. Let $\mathrm{Crit}=\{ U\in\mathcal X:D(S+\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},\bigcdot ))(U)\circ\mathsf C_U=0\}$ be the set of critical points of the constrained functional of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} on the fibres; it is relatively closed in $\mathcal X$, being defined by the vanishing of a continuous function; the critical points of this functional, the points of the fibre at which the differential of the functional vanishes on the tangent space of the fibre, are the points of $\mathrm{Crit}$ (on $\mathcal X$ the fibres are manifolds with tangent space the range of $\mathsf C_U$, and $U_1\in\mathcal X$ by (B2) and its axial mean gauge).

The set $\{(V,U):U\in D^{(11)}(\Omega_1,V)\}$ is Borel in $(V,U)$: it is a finite union of sets defined by non-strict and strict inequalities between functions of $(V,U)$ that are continuous in $U$ and Borel in $V$ (such functions are jointly Borel: $G^E$ is separable metric, and a function continuous in $U$ and Borel in $V$ is a pointwise limit of jointly Borel functions, the standard argument for Carath\'eodory functions), and by the equalities $\bar U(c)= V(c)$ on the rows $c$ of $\Omega_1$ (continuous in $U$ on the open set where the averages are defined) and $\mathsf M(U|_{\Omega_1^c},c)= V(c)$ on the rows of $\Omega_1^c$ (the global average \eqref{eq:global-average}, defined for every $U$ and Borel in $U$: analytic on the open set $\mathcal O_c$ and, off it, the straight transport of the preamble, a continuous function) (the tests involve $V$, $U$ and the Borel functions $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (B1); each factor $\chi_0'(\square')$ is zero for $V$ outside the Borel set $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}(\square')$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser} for the determining set of $\square'$, where the configuration it compares with does not exist, by the convention of (B1), so that $\{(V,U):\chi_0'(\square')\neq0\}=\{(V,U):V\in\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}(\square'),\ \sup_{b\in(\square'^{\sim2})^*}| U(b)U_{1,\square'}(V)(b)^{-1}-\id|<2\delta_0\}$ is Borel, and $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ is never evaluated off $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}(\square')$; likewise the factors of (1.4), functions of $V$ alone, are Borel: by the convention of (B1), $\chi_1(\square')=\mathbf 1\{ V\in\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}(\square')\}\,\mathbf 1\{\sup_{p\subset\square'^{\sim}}| U_{1,\square'}(V)(\partial p)-\id|<\varepsilon_1L^{-2}\}$ and $\chi_1^c(\square')=1-\chi_1(\square')$), intersected with the open set where the averages and the means are defined; and by (B1) for every admissible pair the fibre $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ contains exactly one point of $\mathrm{Crit}$, namely $U_1(V,V_0)$.

So the graph $\{(V,V_0,U):U\in D^{(11)}(\Omega_1,V)\cap\mathrm{Crit},\ \Phi(U)=(V|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}},V_0)\}$ of $(V,V_0)\mapsto U_1(V,V_0)$ is a Borel set (the intersection of a Borel set with the graph of the continuous map $\Phi$ on the open set $\mathcal X$, a Borel set, relatively closed over $\mathcal X$), and a function whose graph is a Borel subset of a product of Polish spaces is Borel on a Borel domain: the domain is the projection of a Borel set with singleton sections, Borel by the Lusin--Novikov theorem \cite[Theorem 18.10]{Kechris}, and a function on a Borel domain whose graph is Borel is Borel, \cite[Theorem 14.12]{Kechris}. Hence the set of admissible pairs is Borel and $U_1$ is Borel on it.

The set $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain} is Borel, and $q_{U_1}$ is Borel on it. Let $\mathsf P$ be the set of pairs $(B,d)\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}\times\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^{[1]}}$ such that $d$ solves every row equation at $g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$, is of chart class, and $U_d(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ with the cutoff (1.25) nonzero at $U_d(B)$. It is Borel, jointly with $(V,V_0)$ through the Borel background $U_1$: the row equations are equalities between functions continuous on the open set where the relative averages are defined, the chart-class condition is open, $U_d(B)$ is continuous in $(B,d,U_1)$, $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ is a section of the Borel set above, and the cutoff is a finite product of indicators of inequalities between Borel functions. By definition $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ is the projection of $\mathsf P$ to the first factor, and every section $\mathsf P(B)$ has at most one point, by the uniqueness of the chart-class family (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii)); so $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ is Borel by the Lusin--Novikov theorem \cite[Theorem 18.10]{Kechris} (the projection of a Borel set with countable sections), and $B\mapsto d$ is Borel on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ by \cite[Theorem 14.12]{Kechris} (its graph is $\mathsf P$); hence $q_{U_1}$, $U(B)$ and the row solutions $\widetilde D_c$ of (B4)(i) are Borel on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, jointly with the branch data; so is $\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D$ at the arguments $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$, $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, by the following formula.

With $A'= q_{U_1}(B)$, the identity $\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(A))= LQ_{U_1}A$ holds on the open set $\mathcal N_{\Theta}\ni A$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), on which $\widetilde D=\varphi$ solves the row equations and is analytic (by \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation} and $LQ_{U_1}h_{U_1}=\id$), so by the chain rule $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')\circ(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A))= LQ_{U_1}$. Applied to $h_{U_1}w$, $w\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^{[1]}}$, this gives $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')h_{U_1}\circ(\id-\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A)h_{U_1})= LQ_{U_1}h_{U_1}=\id$ on $\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^{[1]}}$, so the square map $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')h_{U_1}$ is invertible, and then $\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A)=(D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')h_{U_1})^{-1}\bigl(D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')-LQ_{U_1}\bigr)$, a continuous function of $(U_1,A')$ on the open set where the averages are defined, composed with the Borel maps $U_1$ and $q_{U_1}$; hence it is Borel. The same identity shows that $\id-\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A)h_{U_1}$ is invertible, hence $\det(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A))=\det(\id-\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A)h_{U_1})\neq0$ (Sylvester's determinant identity), which is the nonvanishing part of (B4)(iii) at every argument of the domain of integration.

Moreover $D(V,V_0)\subseteq\mathcal O^{\Phi}$, the set on which $\Phi$ is a submersion (the paragraph defining $D^{(11)}$): for $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ and $A'= q_{U_1}(B)$, the identity $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')\circ(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D(A))= LQ_{U_1}$ just derived has right side onto by (B2) and second factor invertible; hence $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')$ is onto. Since $\mathcal Q_{U_1,c}(A')=\frac1i\log(\mathsf M(e^{iA'}U_1)(c)V(c)^{-1})$ with $\mathsf M(e^{iA'}U_1)(c)= V(c)$, where the differential of the chart is the identity, and $A'\mapsto e^{iA'}U_1$ has invertible differential ($A'$ is chart-valued), the differential of $U\mapsto\bar U|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}}$ at $U(B)= e^{iA'}U_1$ is onto, that is, $D\Phi(U(B))$ is onto.

Borel as well is $\mathcal D_{\xi}$, the preimage of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ under $\Psi_{\xi}$, which is continuous in its argument on its open domain and depends on the pair through the Borel field $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ below, hence is jointly Borel by the argument just given, and $D(V,V_0)= U(\mathcal A_{\xi})$ is Borel as the image of a Borel set under the injective Borel map $B\mapsto U(B)$ (injective, as shown after \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain}), by the Lusin--Souslin theorem for Borel injections \cite[Corollary 15.2]{Kechris}; the Jacobians and the bondwise maps are continuous in their arguments; the local minima $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (1.2) are Borel functions of $V$, and the configuration $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ of (1.21) is a Borel function of $(V,V_0)$ (\cite{BalabanCRE} states that it depends on $V|_{\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c}$; its defining conditions as recorded in (B1) involve $V_0$ where the rows of $(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c$ cross to $\Omega_1^c$, and the Borel choice is made in the pair): they are the Borel choices of Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser} fixed in (B1); hence $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}= L\,\frac1i\log\bigl(U_1U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)^{-1}\bigr)$ of (1.21) is Borel in $(V,V_0)$ on the bonds of $S_1^*$, where alone it is used (the chart logarithm is continuous on the chart domain, which contains the argument there by Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} and \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs}).

So the integrand is jointly Borel, and nonnegative. By Tonelli's theorem the section integral $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]=\int\mathcal K_{\xi}\,\dd a$ is a $[0,\infty]$-valued Borel function of the branch data, and $\int\mathcal O[\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]](V)\,\dd V$ is the integral of the nonnegative integrand over all variables, equal to the fine integral $\mathcal Z_0$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} below, which is finite (a bounded function on a compact group); hence the outer integrals converge, $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]<\infty$ for almost every value of the branch data, and on every branch $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]<\infty$, since the integrand \eqref{eq:native-source-actual-functional} is bounded on the bounded box $\{\Theta_{\xi}=1\}$ (its exponent is the sum of an analytic function bounded on the closed box, Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}, and of a constant of the branch, Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}). The Wilson function $f_{\xi}(a)= W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a))$ is jointly Borel for the same reason and $| f_{\xi}|\leqslant 1$, so $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]$ is a Borel function of the branch data with $|\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]|\leqslant \mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]$, and Fubini's theorem applies to it. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}
    \mathcal Z_0=\int\mathcal O[\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]](V)\,\dd V,
    \qquad
    \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C)]
        =\frac{1}{\mathcal Z_0}\int\mathcal O[\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]](V)\,\dd V\;,
\end{equation}
with $f_{\xi}(a)= W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a))$ the Wilson function of the reconstructed fine field $U_{\xi}(a)$ of \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field}. The first identity is obtained by Ba{\l}aban's steps from the fine integral to \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} with the cutoff (1.25), performed with $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ kept inside the $V_0$ integral and the cutoff in its exact composed form (the estimate-based removals of \cite{BalabanCRE} are recorded in (B3)); the second is the same derivation with the bounded function $W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )$ of the fine field, invariant under all fine gauge transformations, inserted under the fine integral.

The steps, in the following order, which is that of \cite{BalabanCRE} except at two places (p.248 drops $\chi_0$ and $\chi_{Ax}$ before the resummation (1.11), and p.249--250 integrates the $\delta$-functions over the designated variables before inserting (1.18); the operations concerned are multiplications of the integrand by functions of the fine field equal to one, regroupings of a finite sum and the evaluation of $\delta$-functions, and the resulting integrand, a function of the fine field, is the same in either order):
\begin{itemize}
\item the insertion of the block-average $\delta$-functions and of the partitions of unity (1.1), (1.4) (multiplications by functions equal to one, invariant under the fine gauge transformations of (1.5): the tests of (1.1) are plaquette tests and those of (1.4) are functions of $V$), with the group Dirac measure normalised against Haar measure, $\int\delta(\bar UV^{-1})\,\dd V=1$ for every $U$ (the sentence following \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator}; \cite[(0.1)]{BalabanCRE} is the blocking operator whose $\delta$-functions these are; this is why $\mathcal Z_0=\int\varrho_1\,\dd V$ in the notation of \cite{BalabanCRE});
\item the Faddeev--Popov gauge fixing (1.5)--(1.6), an identity for the integral of any function invariant under the gauge transformations $u$ of (1.5), which introduces the normaliser $z^{-(L^4-1)| P_1^1|}$ of (1.5) for the blocks of the gauge-fixed region;
\item the insertion of the partition of unity (1.8) after the gauge is fixed (its tests compare $U$ with the axial-gauge minima $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ and are not gauge invariant);
\item the resummation (1.11) over $P_0,P_1,Q_1$ at fixed $\Omega_1$ (p.248, a regrouping of a finite sum; $R_1$ is introduced afterwards, in (1.18)), after which the gauge-fixed blocks displayed are those of $\Omega_1^{(1)}$ and the displayed normaliser is $z^{-(L^4-1)|\Omega_1^{(1)}|}$, the gauge-fixing factors and normalisers of the other blocks of $P_1^1$ being part of $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$;
\item the removal of (B3)(i), which replaces factors by one where the retained factors are nonzero;
\item the change of variables $U= U'U_1$ on the bonds of $\Omega_1$ at fixed $(V,V_0)$ (a translation of the Haar measure) and $A'=\frac1i\log U'$ of (1.13), the chart being a bijection of the domain onto its image with the Haar density as Jacobian, $\dd U'=\sigma(A')\,\dd A'$ bond by bond with $\sigma(0)=\sigma_0$ (the domain lies in the chart domain by (B1));
\item the conversion of the group $\delta$-functions on the rows of $\Omega_1$: by \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation} and $\mathsf M(U_1)(c)= V(c)$, $\mathsf M(e^{iA'}U_1)(c)V(c)^{-1}= e^{i\mathcal Q_{U_1,c}(A')}$, and $\delta_G(e^{iX})=\sigma(X)^{-1}\delta(X)=\sigma_0^{-1}\delta(X)$ on the support, so the row $\delta$-functions become $\sigma_0^{-|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}\prod_c\delta(\mathcal Q_{U_1,c}(A'))$ (the transformation rule of the paragraph preceding \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain}, applied at the level of the pair $(V,V_0)$, as is every later change of variables of this list);
\item the linearising substitution $A'= B-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(B)$ of (1.14) (\cite{BalabanCRE} writes both variables as $A$; in this step list $B$ is the unscaled variable of (1.14) and $A$ the scaled one of p.249, whereas Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} writes $B$ for the scaled free vector and $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ for the unscaled kernel vector, and the lemmas follow Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), the change of variables by the diffeomorphism $\Theta$ of the paragraph preceding \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain}, defined there on the set $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), which does not depend on $R_1$, since this step precedes the insertion of (1.18), which introduces $R_1$ ((B4)(i), (iii) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv); $\Theta$ is injective with $\mathcal Q_{U_1}\circ\Theta= LQ_{U_1}$), with the Jacobian $|\det(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)|$ (the first fact of that paragraph, at the level $0$), after which $\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')= LQ_{U_1}B$ (the equation of \cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1}, \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit}) and the constraint is the linear constraint $\delta(\widetilde QB)$ of (1.14), the $\widetilde Q$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} being $LQ_{U_1}$, the linear part of the constraint function $\widetilde Q$ of \cite[(2.4), p.~266]{BalabanRG1} (the $\widetilde Q$ of \cite{BalabanRG1} in the equation quoted at \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} is $Q_U$, so that its $L\widetilde Q$ is this operator; $\delta(LQ_{U_1}B)= L^{-d_G|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}\delta(Q_{U_1}B)$, and the constant $L^{-d_G|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}$ of this rescaling of the $\delta$-functions is part of $z^{(0)}$, p.249), while the Haar factor $\prod_{b\in\Omega_1}\sigma(A'(b))$ is written as $\sigma_0^{\#\{\text{bonds of }\Omega_1\}}$ times the normalised density $\prod_b\sigma(A'(b))/\sigma_0$, the $\sigma(A-h\widetilde D(A))$ in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} (the $\sigma$ there is the normalised density, as in \cite[(18), p.~260]{BalabanUV3}, to which Ba{\l}aban refers at the foot of \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} and where $\sigma/\sigma_0$ appears with the exponent $\log\sigma_0|\Omega_1^*|$ of (1.14)): the $\sigma_0^{|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}$ of this product cancels the $\sigma_0^{-|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}$ of the conversion, and $\sigma_0^{\#\{\text{bonds of }\Omega_1\}-|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}=\sigma_0^{|\Omega_1^*|}$ is the factor in \cite[(1.14) and (1.15)]{BalabanCRE};
\item the scaling $B= g_0A$ of p.249 (in \cite{BalabanCRE}: $A= g_0A'$), with Jacobian $g_0^{d_G\times(\text{number of bonds of }\Omega_1)}$ and $\delta(\widetilde Qg_0A)= g_0^{-d_G|\Omega_1^{[1]}|}\delta(\widetilde QA)$, so that the power of $g_0$ is $g_0^{d_G|\Omega_1^*|}$;
\item the insertion of the partition of unity (1.18) in the scaled variable (p.250) and the removal of (B3)(ii), which together produce the cutoff (1.25);
\item the integration of the $\delta$-functions $\delta(\widetilde QA)$ over the designated variables $A(b_0(c))$, $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$, which is the elimination of (B2) and produces the factor $z^{(0)}(U_1)$, after which the remaining Lebesgue measure is $\dd A|_{\Omega_1^*}$ and the normalised Haar density remains at every bond of $\Omega_1$, at the designated bonds evaluated at the eliminated values (it is the Haar primitive \eqref{eq:native-source-haar-primitive}, part of the $v$ of \cite{BalabanCRE});
\item the bondwise change of variables (1.22) on $S_1^*$, a change of variables by (B4)(ii) with the Jacobian $|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|$.
\end{itemize}
Each step is an identity for the integral of any bounded measurable function of the fine field, and the fine field is expressed through the integration variables by the reconstruction \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field}.

The outer operation is Ba{\l}aban's expansion at the stage of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} with the cutoff (1.25). The conditional integration (1.26) of \cite{BalabanCRE}, its cluster expansion, and the renormalisation (1.27)--(1.28) are not used; the first-step coupling $g_1(g_0)$ defined by (1.27) on $\Lambda_1^{\sim-1}$ enters the scale $R_1$ and the quantity $\varepsilon_1$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds} (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}) as a parameter depending on $g_0$ alone.

The following facts about the branch density are taken from \cite{BalabanCRE} as stated there, except where an item records a reading, a derivation or a proof (among them the Borel choices, the convention and the derivations in (B1), the Remark under (B2), the parts of (B4)(i) and (iii) proved in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}, and the proofs in (B4)(ii)). Together with the lemmas proved in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, the standing conditions, and the further statements of \cite{BalabanCRE} named in this section (the definitions (1.1)--(1.10) and (1.18)--(1.22), the local minima $U_{1,\square'}$ of (1.2) and the field $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of (1.21), the axial mean gauge of $U_1$ of p.248, the scale relations (2.6) and (2.9) of p.255--256, the coupling map (1.27) with its $\beta_1$, (2.16)--(2.17) for $\chi_1(\Omega_1)$, (2.4)--(2.5) and p.246 for $\varepsilon_j$ and $R_j$, (1.17) for the gauge action on phases, and, through (B1), Theorem 1 of \cite{BalabanVAR}, reference [15] of \cite{BalabanCRE}; (26) of \cite{BalabanVAR} is cited in \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} for the expansion of the action), they are the inputs of this section:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(B1)] \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} is taken as it stands, with its domain of integration $D^{(11)}$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}); the local minima $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (1.2) are minimal configurations of the variational problem \cite[(2.12)]{BalabanCRE} for the determining set of (1.2), elements of the unique minimal orbit (p.256) taken in the axial gauge (p.247); the configuration $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ of (1.21) is determined, p.251, by the conditions of (1.12) on the domain $(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c$ (the constraint $\bar U= V$, the rows crossing to $\Omega_1^c$ involving $V_0$ as in (B2), and the minimality of the constrained functional, whose critical point is its minimum, p.248) and on $\Lambda_1^{\sim}\setminus\Lambda_1$ by the determining set $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$ and the configuration $Q_1^{s*}V$, in the axial gauge; \cite{BalabanCRE} names the determining data only at p.251, and the configuration is the minimal configuration in the sense of (2.12) (p.256: the functional $A^{\eta}$ minimised over the regular configurations satisfying the constraints) for the constraints named, as \cite{BalabanCRE} writes the operation it calls similar to (1.21)--(1.23) at the general step, p.269, where the function is $U(\mathbf B(\Lambda_{k+1}^c\cap\Lambda_k)\cup\mathbf B_{k+1},\bigcdot)$ of (2.15) with data from both scales; the phrase of \cite{BalabanCRE} ``depends on $V$ restricted to $\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c$'' is accordingly its statement about the dependence on $V$, the crossing rows involving $V_0$ as for $U_1$, so that the Borel choice below is made in the pair $(V,V_0)$.

The integrals over $V$ in \cite{BalabanCRE} presuppose that these configurations depend measurably on the data. By Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser}, which covers conditions that are equalities between continuous functions and the minimality of a continuous functional over a set so defined, a Borel choice exists for each of the two problems, in $V$ for (1.2) and in $(V,V_0)$ for (1.21); one such choice is fixed for each. Where the data are regular the chosen configuration is Ba{\l}aban's: the minimal configurations for given data form one orbit, in the regularity class \cite[(6)]{BalabanVAR} (\cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE}, ``the minimal orbit, i.e., the set of minima''; \cite[Theorem~1, p.~279]{BalabanVAR}; the class and radius of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7-1}, and of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1} for the configuration of (1.21)), of the gauge transformations equal to the identity on the set $\mathfrak B_k$ of determining points (\cite[(4), p.~278]{BalabanVAR}: every fine site of the scale-zero determining set and the block centres of the scale-one set), and the axial gauge determines a unique element in each such orbit: the axial condition $U(y,x)=\id$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} is posed on the mean contour variables of \cite[(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} (\cite[p.~247]{BalabanCRE}), which a transformation $w$ of the orbit changes to $w(y)U(y,x)w(x)^{-1}$ by \cite[(0.6)]{BalabanRG1}, so that $w(y)=\id$ and the axial condition for both configurations force $w(x)=\id$ (\cite[p.~78]{BalabanREG} for the single-contour axial gauge); so the axial representative is unique, and the statements of \cite{BalabanCRE} about these configurations that are used here (the tests (1.4) and (1.8) and (B3)(iii)) hold for the chosen configurations; \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs} is proved for them in Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}.

The averages and means of (1.11) are the principal logarithms of \cite[p.~21, (22)--(25)]{BalabanAVG}, Ba{\l}aban's own convention, restricted in the preamble to the chart ball. That on the domain of integration every argument of a logarithm of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} on a row of $\Omega_1$ lies in the chart domain, every family of transports entering a mean (0.10)--(0.11) at a block centre of $\Omega_1^{(1)}$ lies in the small-diameter domain of the mean, and the fluctuation $U'= UU_1^{-1}$ lies in the chart domain on every bond of $\Omega_1$, the designated bonds $b_0(c)$ included, so that $A'=\frac1i\log U'$ of (1.13) is defined, is the smallness statement of \cite[pp.~247--248]{BalabanCRE}, which Ba{\l}aban justifies by the reasoning of the proof of Lemma~1 of \cite{BalabanREG}. Since the hypotheses of that lemma (the exact axial condition and \cite[(1.7)]{BalabanREG} on the blocks concerned) are not those of the domain of \cite{BalabanCRE}, the statement is derived as follows, with that proof as the model.

(i) On the domain of integration the cutoffs $\chi_0$ and $\chi_{Ax}$ of (1.5)--(1.6) localised in $\Omega_1^{\sim}$ equal one ((B3)(i), p.248): $| U(\partial p)-1|<\varepsilon_0$ for every plaquette $p\subset\Omega_1^{\sim}$ and $| U(y,x)-1|<\varepsilon_0$ for every mean (0.11) at $y\in\Omega_1^{\sim(1)}$, $x\in B(y)$.

(ii) For such $U$ \cite{BalabanCRE} states $| UU_{1,\square'}^{-1}-1|< O(L^2)\varepsilon_0$ on every bond of $\square'^{\sim2}$ (p.247, ``on $\square'^{\sim2}$'', the designated bonds not excluded, whereas the test (1.8) runs over $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$), ``by the same reasoning as in the proof of Lemma~1 [14]'', that is Lemma~1 of \cite{BalabanREG} (p.~79, (1.24)--(1.25)): if two configurations $V_0$ and $V'V_0$ have plaquette variables within $\alpha_0L^{-2}$ of one on $\Omega_1$ ((1.7) there), the same variables on the axial contours $\Gamma_{y,x}$, $x\in B(y)$, and block averages within $\alpha_1$ of each other on $\Omega_1^{(1)}$, then $| V'-1|<4d^2\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ on every bond of $\Omega_1$; its proof (pp.~79--80) bounds the bonds inside a block from the plaquettes and the axial conditions, the bonds joining two blocks from these, and the designated bond $b_0$ of each coarse bond $c$ from the block-average condition (pp.79--80), and the bound is local (p.80); \cite{BalabanCRE} applies the reasoning with $V_0= U_{1,\square'}$ in the axial gauge, the block averages of both configurations equal to $V$ on the blocks of $\square'^{\sim4}$ ((1.2)--(1.3), p.246, and the constraint of (1.11)) and the axial condition on $U$ holding within $\varepsilon_0$ by (i).
