(iii) $U_1$ lies in the domain of integration (p.248; the ``domain of integration in (1.11)'' of \cite{BalabanCRE} is the support of every characteristic factor of (1.11), the set to which they restrict the integral, as in \cite[p.~265]{BalabanRG1}, (H4) and Remark~\ref{rem:c3-8-1}), so (ii) applies to $U_1$ too, and $U'=(UU_{1,\square'}^{-1})(U_{1,\square'}U_1^{-1})$ is within $2\,O(L^2)\varepsilon_0$ of one on every bond of $\square'^{\sim2}$, for every cube $\square'\subset\Omega_1$ (p.248: ``both fields in the parenthesis \dots\ are small'').

(iv) The arguments of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} on a row of $\Omega_1$ are closed contours in two adjacent blocks of $\Omega_1^{\sim}$, and two transports of a family $\mathbf G(y,x)$ differ by such a contour; by the reasoning of \cite[pp.~24--25]{BalabanAVG} ((44)--(46): in a local axial gauge every bond of the four blocks $\Delta(p')$ is within $dL\alpha_0$ of one and every contour $\Gamma$ in them within $|\Gamma| dL\alpha_0= O(1)L^2\alpha_0$, ``for $L^2\alpha_0$ sufficiently small''), with $\alpha_0=\sqrt N\varepsilon_0$ from (i) (the $|\bigcdot |$ of \cite{BalabanAVG} is the operator norm, which the norm of (i) bounds up to the factor $\sqrt N$), every such closed contour variable, a conjugation-invariant quantity, is within $O(1)L^2\varepsilon_0$ of one, and so is the diameter of each family of transports.

The constant $O(1)$ of (iv) is displayed by \cite{BalabanAVG}, $|\Gamma|\leqslant (2d+1)L$ and the factor $d$, up to the elementary count of the contours of \cite[(0.4) and (0.10)--(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} in the four blocks and the factor $\sqrt N$; the constant $O(L^2)$ of (ii) is not displayed in \cite{BalabanCRE}; it is that of the reasoning of \cite[Lemma~1, p.~79]{BalabanREG}, whose bound $4d^2\alpha_0+\alpha_1$ has absolute constants, and, like the constants of (B3)(iii), it is independent of the coupling and of the branch ((H4)), so that for $\varepsilon_0$ small at fixed $L$ the quantities of (iii) and (iv) lie below $\varrho_G$, $r_G/\sqrt N$, and the small-diameter radius of the mean (``$\varepsilon_0$ sufficiently small'', \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}; item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}). This is the domain $D^{(11)}$ of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}.

A convention of this paper: every factor of (1.4) and (1.8) defined through the configuration $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ of (1.2) is assigned a value for the $V$ for which that configuration does not exist ($V\notin\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}(\square')$, Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser}), namely $\chi_1(\square')=0$, $\chi_1^c(\square')=1$, $\chi_0'(\square')=0$ and $\chi_0'^c(\square')=1$, so that (1.4) and (1.8) remain partitions of unity (\cite[(1.2)--(1.4) and (1.8), pp.~246--247]{BalabanCRE} define these factors through $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ without an existence clause), and $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ enters only where it exists. Under it, where $\chi_1(\Omega_1)\neq0$ the configuration $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ exists for every cube $\square'\subset\Omega_1$, and where a factor $\chi_0'(\square')$ is nonzero it exists for that cube.

For every admissible $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ the background $U_1= U_1(V,V_0)$ of (1.12) exists, is the unique critical point of the constrained functional of \cite{BalabanCRE} in the domain of integration in (1.11), that is in the fibre $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$, and is a minimum with strictly positive second differential (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}: ``there exists exactly one critical point'' of (1.12) in the domain of integration in (1.11), by Theorem 1 of \cite{BalabanVAR} (reference [15] of \cite{BalabanCRE}, the variational problem of the averaging operation) for $\varepsilon_0$ small; ``it is a minimum of (1.12), with a strictly positive second order differential'', stated there without further citation); the fluctuation $U'= UU_1^{-1}$ lies in the chart domain for every $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ (p.248, derived above), so that $A'=\frac1i\log U'$ of (1.13) is defined.

So of (B2) only its form on the rows with one block off $\Omega_1$ (the outer block entering as the constant $V_0$, and $A'(b_0(c))$ the eliminated variable) is an input.

\item[(B4)] For every admissible pair $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ and every region $R_1$ of the history sum, the expressions in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15) and (1.22)--(1.24)]{BalabanCRE} are defined on the domain of integration: the linearising correction $\widetilde D$ of (1.14), p.249 (at the foot of \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} Ba{\l}aban refers to the transformations analysed between (16)--(18) of [16], or between (I.1.8)--(I.1.9) of [I], where [I] is \cite{BalabanRG1} in the reference list of \cite[p.~285]{BalabanCRE}; \cite[(1.8)--(1.9), p.~261]{BalabanRG1} concern the functions $J_j$, and the linearisation of the unit-lattice step of \cite{BalabanRG1} is the one following \cite[(2.10), p.~267]{BalabanRG1}, where Ba{\l}aban states for its correction that its defining equation has exactly one solution, analytic in its argument, with an expansion beginning with quadratic terms; here $\widetilde D$ is the small solution $\varphi$ of (i)); the phase $A-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(A)$; the Haar density $\sigma(A-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(A))$; the logarithm $\operatorname{Tr}\log(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)$ of the Jacobian of (1.14); and the bondwise maps of (1.22) with their Jacobian.

Three further properties of these objects are recorded as part of (B4); they are Ba{\l}aban's statements and facts proved in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}.

(i) The defining equation of $\widetilde D$ is the system \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} over the rows $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$, which decouples row by row (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}), as in \cite[(17), pp.~259--260]{BalabanUV3}, the transformation to which Ba{\l}aban refers in \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}, where the equation is solved ``separately for each function $Q(A',c)$''; the row component $\widetilde D_c(A)$ depends on $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ only.

\cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1} states for the equation $L\widetilde QB'+\widetilde C(B')= L\widetilde QB$, $B'= B-h\widetilde D(B)$, that ``there exists exactly one solution of this equation, and that it is an analytic function of $B$'', in the unit-lattice step of \cite{BalabanRG1}, without naming the class in which the solution is unique, and \cite[p.~260]{BalabanUV3} states for (17) that ``there exists a unique solution $\tilde D$ of this equation for $A$ sufficiently small, and it is an analytic function of $A$ with a Taylor expansion beginning with second order terms''; these statements are used only for the identification at the end of (i).

The row equation \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} involves the eliminated phase only through $e^{iq}$, so its solutions are determined only up to the periods of the exponential; the class used here is the chart class of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} (the whole phase in the chart ball $h(q)<\varrho_G$, the class of the chart-valued variable $A'$ of \cite[(1.13)]{BalabanCRE}) with the fine field in $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$. In this class the row solution is determined by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness} of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, proved from (B1) (with (B3)(i), through (B1)(i)), (B2), the compatible partitions of \cite{BalabanCRE} being nested ((H4)), the fine periods being at least $8M$, Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge}, \ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} and~\ref{lem:two-block}, and threshold items 5 and 6: at every row $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$, near or far, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} applies to $U_1$ and gives the small solution $\varphi_c$, analytic on the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$, real on real phases, with $\varphi_c(0)=0$ and $D\varphi_c(0)=0$, unique among the solutions $d_c$ with $h(d_c)\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm d}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i)); the argument $A$ of every $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ lies in the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*/2$ at every row (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(ii)); and every chart-class family $d$ at $g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ with $U_d(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ is $\varphi(g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B)$, $\varphi=(\varphi_c)_c$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii)).

The row solution of this paper is $\widetilde D_c=\varphi_c$ at every row, and $\widetilde D=\varphi$ is analytic and solves the row equations on the open set $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), which contains all arguments of the domain of integration. Every solution of the row system with chart-valued phase and fine field in $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ is $\varphi$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii); and the $\widetilde D$ in \cite[(1.13)--(1.14), pp.~248--249]{BalabanCRE} is $\varphi$: for $A$ sufficiently small both are small solutions of the row equations ($\varphi(0)=0$), so they agree by the uniqueness stated in \cite{BalabanUV3}, and the $\widetilde D$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, the analytic function so described by \cite{BalabanUV3} and \cite{BalabanRG1}, therefore agrees with $\varphi$ on the connected ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ on which $\varphi$ is analytic, a ball containing the arguments of the domain of integration (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(ii)).

(ii) The substitutions (1.14) and (1.22) are changes of variables: the map $B\mapsto U(B)$ of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}, the composition of (1.13) and (1.14), is a bijection of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ onto $D(V,V_0)$ (shown there from (B1), (B2) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}), and its differential, that of $B\mapsto g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ followed by the substitution $A'= A-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(A)$ and the exponential, is injective at every point of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ with image the tangent space of the fibre $\Phi^{-1}(V,V_0)$ at $U(B)$ (the Jacobian $\det(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)$ of (1.14) is nonzero there, (iii), $\mathsf C_{U_1}$ is injective, and the image of $(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)\mathsf C_{U_1}$ is the kernel of $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')$ by the identity $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')\circ(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)= LQ_{U_1}$ of the measurability paragraph, $LQ_{U_1}\mathsf C_{U_1}=0$, and a count of dimensions, $D\mathcal Q_{U_1}(A')$ being onto); and $\Psi_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map}, acting bond by bond on $S_1^*$, is a $C^{\infty}$ map which maps $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ bijectively onto $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ with invertible differential at every point of $\mathcal D_{\xi}$: this is Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection} of Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}, proved from the bound on $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE}, derived in Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} from \cite[Theorem~1, (172), Proposition~9, and (190)]{BalabanVAR}, the application of \cite{BalabanVAR} to the determining set $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$ in \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE}, and the restoring bound \eqref{eq:c3-9-7}, from the membership $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ of (B1), that is the cutoff $\chi_0'(\Omega_1)$ at $U_1$ (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}), and from the choice of the cutoff $g$ of (1.22) made there. The Jacobian of (1.22) is $|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|$, the exact Jacobian of \eqref{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map}, in place of the expression \cite[(1.24)]{BalabanCRE}.

(iii) The determinant $\det(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)$ is nonzero on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, by (i) and Sylvester's identity (the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}); \cite{BalabanCRE} performs (1.14) as a change of variables and writes its Jacobian as $\exp\operatorname{Tr}\log(I-h(\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)(A))$ (p.249). The determinant is positive there, so that the logarithm of \cite{BalabanCRE} is the real logarithm and equals $\sum_c\log\det_{\mathfrak g}(\id-h_{U_1}(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_c)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum}): this is Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), \eqref{eq:c2-fibre-jacobian}, at every row; the identities of this paper use the absolute Jacobian $|\det(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)|$, for which the nonvanishing suffices.

For the rows within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ and the inputs of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}, the expressions of (B4) coincide with the analytic objects of that lemma, by the uniqueness of the small solution stated there; elsewhere they enter only through $a$-independent factors (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}, \eqref{eq:c-large-field-factor}).
\end{itemize}

The Borel choice fixed in (B1) exists:

\begin{definition}[Constrained Minimisation Data]\label{def:minimisation-data}
Let $E$ be a finite set of fine bonds, $\mathbf B$ a set of blocks, and $\mathcal U\subseteq G^{E}$ a finite intersection of open and closed subsets of the compact metric space $G^E$, contained in the open set on which the group means $U(y,x)$ of \cite[(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} at the block centres $y$ of $\mathbf B$ are defined (chart convention of the preamble). Let $P$ be a Polish space of parameters, $\mathcal W$ a relatively open subset of $\mathcal U\times P$ (the set on which the averages entering the conditions are defined; $\mathcal W=\mathcal U\times P$ is allowed), $\mathfrak c$ and $\mathfrak d$ continuous maps on $\mathcal W$ into metric spaces, and $S$ a continuous real function on $\mathcal W$ (the action, which may involve the parameter through boundary plaquettes). For $p\in P$,
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal W(p)\coloneqq\{ U:(U,p)\in\mathcal W\}\;,\qquad\mathcal K(p)\coloneqq\{ U\in\mathcal W(p):\mathfrak c(U,p)=0\}\;,
\end{equation*}
$\mathcal W(p)$ being an open subset of $\mathcal U$; $\mathcal V$ is the set of $p$ with $\mathcal K(p)\neq\varnothing$ on which $S(\bigcdot ,p)$ attains its infimum $m(p)$ over $\mathcal K(p)$. The set of minimal configurations satisfying the further equalities $\mathfrak d=0$, in the axial gauge (p.248), is
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}\coloneqq\{(p,U):\ &p\in\mathcal V,\ U\in\mathcal K(p),\ S(U,p)= m(p),\ \mathfrak d(U,p)=0,\\
&U(y,x)=\id\text{ for every centre }y\text{ of a block of }\mathbf B\text{ whose bonds lie in }E\\
&\text{and }x\in\mathcal B_y\setminus\{ y\}\}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
with projection $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}$ to the first factor.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Borel Choice of Minimal Configurations]\label{lem:borel-minimiser}
For the data of Definition~\ref{def:minimisation-data}, $\mathcal V$, $m$, $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}$, and $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}$ are Borel, and there is a Borel map $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}\ni p\mapsto U_{\mathbf B}(p)$ with $(p,U_{\mathbf B}(p))\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}$ for every $p\in\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{definition}[Regular Configurations]\label{def:regular-configurations}
For the determining sets $\mathbf B$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, that of (1.2) and that of (1.21), $E= E(\mathbf B)$ is the set of fine bonds of the region determined and $\mathcal U=\mathcal U_{\mathbf B}$ the set of regular configurations, on which the averaging operation $M_{\mathbf B}$ of \cite[(2.11)]{BalabanCRE} is defined: the configurations of the class (2) of \cite[p.~278]{BalabanVAR} (reference [15] of \cite{BalabanCRE}), given by finitely many strict inequalities between continuous functions of $U$ (the plaquette variables $| U(\partial p)-1|$ and the covariant divergences $|(D_U^{\eta*}\partial U)(b)|$, polynomials in the matrix entries of the bond variables and their inverses), with the averages (the logarithmic averages of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}) and the means $U(y,x)$ defined in the chart convention, an open set; the space \cite[(6)]{BalabanVAR} is its intersection with the constraint set (3), which is the constraint $\mathfrak c=0$ of Definition~\ref{def:two-minimisation-problems}; $M_{\mathbf B}$ is continuous on $\mathcal U$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The Two Minimisation Problems of the Step]\label{def:two-minimisation-problems}
With $E$ and $\mathcal U=\mathcal U_{\mathbf B}$ of Definition~\ref{def:regular-configurations}, for the problem (1.2) the parameter is $p= V|_{\square'^{\sim4}}$ (p.246), $\mathcal W=\mathcal U\times P$, $\mathfrak d\equiv0$, and
\begin{equation*}
    \mathfrak c(U,V)\coloneqq M_{\mathbf B}(U)\,(M^{\bigcdot }(Q_1^{s*}V))^{-1}-\id\;,
\end{equation*}
so that $\mathcal K(V)=\{ U\in\mathcal U_{\mathbf B}:M_{\mathbf B}(U)= M^{\bigcdot }(Q_1^{s*}V)\}$ is the constraint set of the variational problem \cite[(2.12)]{BalabanCRE} for the data of (1.2).

For the configuration of (1.21), $p=(V,V_0)$, $E$ the bonds of $\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c$ (the ``function $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$'' of \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE}), $\mathcal W$ the relatively open set of the $(U,p)$ at which the averages of the rows crossing to $\Omega_1^c$, which involve $V_0$ on the outer block, are defined, $\mathfrak c$ collects the constraints $\bar U= V$ on the rows of $(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c$ (with $V_0$ on the blocks off $\Omega_1$) and $M_{\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)}(U)= M^{\bigcdot }(Q_1^{s*}V)$ on the bonds of the determining set in $\Lambda_1^{\sim}\setminus\Lambda_1$ (its fine layer fixed to $Q_1^{s*}V$ and its coarse bonds to the averages of $Q_1^{s*}V$; the form of the constraint of (1.2); \cite{BalabanCRE} names the determining data, ``the set $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$ and the configuration $Q_1^{s*}V$'', p.251), $\mathfrak d\equiv0$, and $S(U,p)$ is the functional $A^{\eta}$ of (2.12) for the determining set $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$, in which the plaquettes meeting $\Omega_1^c$ involve $V_0$, as recorded in (B1) from pp.251 and 269.
\end{definition}

For (1.21), the minimality $S(U)= m(p)$ over $\mathcal K(p)$ is the condition of (1.12) on $(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c$, the critical point of (1.12) being its minimum (p.248), and no critical-point equation is imposed separately.

\begin{lemma}[The Minimal Configurations of the Step]\label{lem:step-minimisers}
For the problem (1.2) of Definition~\ref{def:two-minimisation-problems}, every regular $V$ lies in $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}$, and $U_{1,\square'}(V)= U(\mathbf B_1(\square'^{\sim4}),M^{\bigcdot }(Q_1^{s*}V))$ is the representative of the unique minimal orbit of (2.12) chosen in \cite[p.~247]{BalabanCRE}, ``taken in the axial gauge''. For the problem (1.21), the configuration exists for every admissible pair $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser}]
The set $\mathcal K\coloneqq\{(p,U):(U,p)\in\mathcal W,\ \mathfrak c(U,p)=0\}$ is Borel in $P\times G^{E}$, as the zero set of a continuous function on the Borel set $\mathcal W$ (relatively open in the Borel set $\mathcal U\times P$), and so is $\mathcal K_t=\{(p,U)\in\mathcal K: S(U,p)< t\}$ for every rational $t$. Every section $\mathcal K_t(p)=\{ U\in\mathcal W(p): \mathfrak c(U,p)=0,\ S(U,p)< t\}$ is the intersection of $\mathcal U$, a finite intersection of open and closed subsets of the compact metric space $G^{E}$, with the open set $\mathcal W(p)$, a closed set (the zero set of $\mathfrak c(\bigcdot ,p)$ is relatively closed in $\mathcal W(p)$, the trace of a closed set) and an open set (the trace of $\{ S(\bigcdot ,p)< t\}$, relatively open in $\mathcal W(p)$), hence $K_{\sigma}$: an open subset of a compact metric space is a countable union of compact sets, and the intersection of a $K_{\sigma}$ set with a closed set, or with an open set, is $K_{\sigma}$. By the Arsenin--Kunugui theorem (a Borel subset of a product of Polish spaces whose sections are $K_{\sigma}$ has a Borel projection and a Borel uniformisation, \cite[Theorem 35.46(ii)]{Kechris}), $\operatorname{proj}\mathcal K_t=\{ p: \inf_{\mathcal K(p)}S< t\}$ is Borel for every rational $t$, and so is $\operatorname{proj}\mathcal K=\{ p:\mathcal K(p)\neq\varnothing\}$; hence $\widetilde m(p)=\inf_{\mathcal K(p)}S$ is a Borel function on $\operatorname{proj}\mathcal K$.

The set $\mathcal M\coloneqq\{(p,U)\in\mathcal K: S(U,p)=\widetilde m(p)\}$ is Borel, its sections $\mathcal K(p)\cap\{ S=\widetilde m(p)\}$ are $K_{\sigma}$, so $\mathcal V=\operatorname{proj}\mathcal M$ is Borel by the same theorem, and $m=\widetilde m$ on $\mathcal V$.

The axial gauge conditions $U(y,x)=\id$ are relatively closed conditions on the open set on which the means $U(y,x)$ of \cite[(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} are defined (\cite[p.~253]{BalabanRG1} defines the mean for sets of sufficiently small diameter, and it is continuous there in the chart convention), an open set containing $\mathcal U$ by hypothesis; and $\mathfrak d(U,p)=0$ is a relatively closed condition on $\mathcal W$. So $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}=\mathcal M\cap\{\mathfrak d=0\}\cap\{ U\text{ axial}\}$ is Borel, and its sections are $K_{\sigma}$, being intersections of $K_{\sigma}$ subsets of $\mathcal U$ with closed sets (the trace on $\mathcal U$ of a relatively closed subset of an open set containing $\mathcal U$ is the trace of a closed set); the theorem gives that $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}$ is Borel and that $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}$ has a Borel uniformisation, a Borel map $U_{\mathbf B}$ on $\mathcal V_{\mathrm{ax}}$ with graph in $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:step-minimisers}]
For (1.2), a regular $V$ determines the unique minimal orbit of (2.12), whose elements are the minimal configurations \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE}, so $V\in\mathcal V$, and the configurations $U_{1,\square'}$ are taken in the axial gauge (p.247); a gauge transformation equal to $\id$ at the block centres and to the mean $U(y,x)$ elsewhere brings a minimal configuration to the axial gauge, leaving the block averages of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} at the block centres unchanged (\cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} transforms at the block centres, proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}) and $S(U)$ unchanged when $S$ is gauge invariant, as the action is; the configuration so obtained is regular, satisfies the constraint and is minimal: \cite{BalabanVAR} states that its class (2) is gauge invariant and its constraint set (3) invariant under the gauge transformations equal to one on its set $\mathfrak B_k$ of determining points ((4), p.278), which the transformation used is: it is the identity at the block centres, and on the blocks of the fine determining layer, where the constraint fixes the configuration to the straight extension $Q_1^{s*}V$, whose intrablock contours are the identity (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-2}), the mean $U(y,x)$ is the identity; and that the space (6) and the action (5) are invariant under these (p.278); so $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{ax}}(V)\neq\varnothing$.

For (1.21), the existence for every admissible pair is the existence of the minimal orbit of \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} for these determining data, Ba{\l}aban's application of \cite{BalabanVAR} to the determining sets of \cite[pp.~251 and 256]{BalabanCRE} (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}); the configuration of (1.21) is that of \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Constrained Hessian at a Regular Background and Its Stencils}
\label{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}

Let $\mathsf M$ be Ba{\l}aban's averaging operation \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} (written $M$ there; here $M$ is the cube side), and let $\Omega$ be a region, a union of blocks, and $U$ a configuration of the fine torus for which $\mathsf M(U)(c)$ is defined on every row $c\in\Omega^{[1]}$ of that region and the local group means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$, $x\in\mathcal B_y$, are defined for every centre $y\in\Omega^{(1)}$ (chart convention of the preamble; for $U= U_1$ on $\Omega_1$ both hold, because $U_1\in D^{(11)}$ and $U_1$ is in its axial mean gauge, $\mathcal U_{U_1}(y,x)=\id$); the objects below are then defined for phases $q$ in a neighbourhood of zero depending on $U$, which Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} and Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} quantify for the backgrounds that occur.

The objects of this subsection are defined relative to the region $\Omega$: the rows are the coarse bonds $c\in\Omega^{[1]}$ (at least one block in $\Omega$), the block sums run over the centres $y\in\Omega^{(1)}$, the free carrier is $\Omega^*$, and the links of $U$ on bonds with both endpoints off $\Omega$ enter as fixed constants, with the phase variable equal to zero there. The torus itself ($\Omega= T$) is written without a superscript; the branch uses $\Omega=\Omega_1$ and $U= U_1$. For $c\in\Omega^{[1]}$ the row maps are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation}
    \mathcal Q_{U,c}(q)\coloneqq\frac{1}{i}\log\left(\mathsf M(e^{iq}U)(c)\,\mathsf M(U)(c)^{-1}\right),\quad
    Q_U\coloneqq\frac{1}{L}D\mathcal Q_U(0),\quad
    \mathcal N_U(q)\coloneqq\mathcal Q_U(q)-LQ_Uq\;,
\end{equation}
so that $\mathcal N_U$ is the remainder denoted $\widetilde C$ in the linearisation following \cite[(2.10)]{BalabanRG1}; the logarithm is the group chart of the conventions above, defined when the relative average lies in the chart domain. For a coarse bond $c$ with designated fine bond $b_0(c)$, and a coarse centre $y$, the bond stencils are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-stencil-bonds}
    \mathcal E_c\coloneqq\{ r\, | \,\{ r_-,r_+\}\subset\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}\},
    \qquad
    \mathcal E_y\coloneqq\{ r\, | \,\{ r_-,r_+\}\subset\mathcal B_y\}\;,
\end{equation}
$r$ ranging over the positive fine bonds.

\begin{lemma}[Two-Block Structure]\label{lem:two-block}
Let $L\geqslant 3$ be odd and let every coarse period exceed two. The row components $\mathcal Q_{U,c}$ and $\mathcal N_{U,c}$ depend only on the phases and background bonds in $\mathcal E_c$, and $b_0(c)$ is the only designated bond in $\mathcal E_c$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-stencil-designated-diagonal}
    Q_{0,U}(c,c')\coloneqq\delta_{cc'}\alpha_c(U),\qquad \alpha_c(U)\coloneqq Q_U(c,b_0(c))\;,
\end{equation}
where $Q_{0,U}$ is the restriction of $Q_U$ to the designated bonds, with $\alpha_c(\id)= L^{-4}\id$. There is a phase radius $\tau_L>0$, depending on $L$ and the group only, such that for $U= e^{iA}$ with $\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L$ every $\alpha_c(U)$ is analytic in $A$ with smallest singular value at least $L^{-4}/2$. Under a site gauge transformation $u$, $\alpha_c(U^u)=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(c_-)}\alpha_c(U)\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_0(c)_-)}^{-1}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every path in the row of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} for $c$ lies in the two endpoint blocks, since the row averages parallel transports from the centre of $\mathcal B_{c_-}$ to the centre of $\mathcal B_{c_+}$ along paths inside the two blocks; a designated bond crosses its own coarse interface, and two adjacent blocks share exactly the interface labelled by $c$, so $b_0(c)$ is the only designated bond with both endpoints in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$ (for $L\geqslant 3$ odd the other designated bonds cross other interfaces).

At the flat field, differentiating \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} gives \eqref{eq:covariance-two-averages} of Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance}: the straight-path term $(Q_1a)(c)= L^{-5}\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_{c_-}}a([x,x'])$ contains $b_0(c)$ in exactly $L$ of its $L^4$ translated straight paths of $L$ bonds each (the $L$ starting points on the line through $b_0(c)$), each with coefficient $L^{-5}$, and the mean-path term involves the paths $\Phi$ inside the blocks, which contain no designated bond; this gives $\alpha_c(\id)= L^{-4}\id$, the designated coefficient $Q_{0,\infty}= L^{-4}I$ computed in Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance} (paragraph ``Construction on the infinite lattice'', after \eqref{eq:bulk-operator-definition}; the computation is local and holds on every torus).

For $U= e^{iA}$, $\alpha_c(U)$ is an analytic function of $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ near zero (a composition of exponentials, the averaging and the chart logarithm) with $\alpha_c(\id)= L^{-4}\id$; the smallest singular value is continuous, so for each of the finitely many row types modulo $L\mathbb Z^4$ (translations commute with $\mathsf M$) there is a radius on which $\alpha_c$ is analytic with smallest singular value at least $L^{-4}/2$, and $\tau_L$ is the smallest of these radii; it depends on $L$ and the group only.

The gauge covariance is $\mathsf M(U^u)(c)= u(c_-)\mathsf M(U)(c)u(c_+)^{-1}$ (\cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} transforms at the block centres) together with $(R_uq)(b)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_-)}q(b)$ for the phase (\cite[(1.17)]{BalabanCRE}): $\mathcal Q_{U^u,c}(R_uq)=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(c_-)}\mathcal Q_{U,c}(q)$, hence $Q_{U^u}R_u=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(c_-)}Q_U$ row by row, and the $b_0(c)$ column gives the formula.
\end{proof}

By (B2) and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}, $\alpha_c(U)$ is invertible on every row of the regions used below. With $LQ_Uh_U=\id$ for the supported right inverse $h_U$, whose only nonzero outputs are at the designated bonds, the elimination maps are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-stencil-elimination}
    \begin{gathered}
    (\mathsf C_UB)(b_0(c))
        \coloneqq-\alpha_c(U)^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}Q_U(c,b)B(b),
    \\
    (h_Uv)(b_0(c))\coloneqq h_U(c)v(c),\qquad h_U(c)\coloneqq\frac{1}{L}\alpha_c(U)^{-1}\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
and $(\mathsf C_UB)(r)= B(r)$ on free bonds $r\in E_*$; thus $Q_U\mathsf C_U=0$. The free-input and background stencils of a fine bond are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-stencil-extension-support}
    (\mathcal F_r,\mathcal A_r)\coloneqq
    \begin{cases}
        (\{ r\},\varnothing),&r\in E_*\;,\\
        (\mathcal E_c\cap E_*,\mathcal E_c),&r= b_0(c)\;.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}

The constrained quadratic form is \cite[(1.14)--(1.16)]{BalabanCRE} on the region $\Omega$. With $J_U$ and $\Delta_U$ the first derivative and Hessian at $q=0$ of $q\mapsto S(e^{iq}U)$, $q\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega}$ (the plaquettes with a bond in $\Omega$ contribute; links off $\Omega$ are the fixed constants), and the relative gauge functional
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-gauge}
    \mathscr G^{\Omega}_U(q)\coloneqq\sum_{y\in\Omega}\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y\setminus\{ y\}}
        \left(1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N(\mathcal U_{e^{iq}U}(y,x)\mathcal U_U(y,x)^{-1})\right),
    \qquad G^{(2),\Omega}_U(a)\coloneqq D^2\mathscr G^{\Omega}_U(0)[a,a]\;,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ is the axial transport from the block centre $y$ to $x$ of the gauge-fixing functional $\mathbf G$ in \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} and the sum is over the block centres of $\Omega$, the regional Hessian $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U$ on $\mathfrak g^{\Omega^*}$ is the symmetric operator of the quadratic form ($B$ is extended by zero to the free bonds outside $\Omega^*$, so that $a=\mathsf C_UB$ is defined on every row of $\Omega^{[1]}$)
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-hessian}
    \langle B,\mathsf H^{\Omega}_UB\rangle
        =\langle a,\Delta_Ua\rangle+G^{(2),\Omega}_U(a)
            -\langle J_U,h_UD^2\mathcal N_U(0)[a,a]\rangle,
    \qquad a=\mathsf C_UB\;,
\end{equation}
with the rows of $\mathcal N_U$ and $h_U$ those of $\Omega^{[1]}$. The right side equals $D^2(S+\mathscr G^{\Omega}_U)(0)[a,a]-DS(0)[h_UD^2\mathcal N_U(0)[a,a]]$, which does not involve the inner product; $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U$ is its operator for the fixed one, and its entries $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U(b,b')\in\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak g)$ are those of the polarised bilinear form.

This is \cite[(1.16)]{BalabanCRE}, $\langle A,\Delta_1A\rangle=\langle A,\Delta A\rangle-2\langle hC^{(2)}(A),J_1\rangle+\mathbf G^{(2)}(A)$, with, as in \cite{BalabanCRE}, $C^{(2)}(A)=\frac12D^2\mathcal N_U(0)[A,A]$ (the quadratic term of the linearising transformation, \cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1}, $\widetilde D^{(2)}=\widetilde C^{(2)}$) and $\mathbf G^{(2)}(A)= D^2\mathscr G(0)[A,A]$; at $\Omega=\Omega_1$, $U= U_1$ the relative gauge functional is the absolute one of \cite{BalabanCRE}, $\mathscr G^{\Omega_1}_{U_1}(q)=\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},e^{iq}U_1)$ with $\mathbf G$ of (1.7), (1.11), because $U_1$ is in its axial mean gauge, $\mathcal U_{U_1}(y,x)=\id$ for $x\in\mathcal B_y$, $y\in\Omega_1^{(1)}$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}; \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}), so that $\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},U_1)=0$; and $\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{U_1}$ is the $C^*\Delta_1C$ of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}, the same quadratic form written as an operator for the fixed inner product. The precision of the branch is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-regional-hessian}
    H_{\xi}\coloneqq\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{U_1}\quad\text{on }\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*},\qquad H_{\xi,II}\coloneqq\iota_I^*H_{\xi}\iota_I,\qquad H_{\xi,IJ}\coloneqq\iota_I^*H_{\xi}\iota_J\;,
\end{equation}
with $\iota_I,\iota_J$ the extensions by zero. With $s_{p,U}(q)\coloneqq 1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N((e^{iq}U)(\partial p))$, $\mathscr G_{y,U}$ the $y$-summand of \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-gauge}, and $a=\mathsf C_UB$, the form decomposes into local terms,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition}
    \begin{gathered}
    \langle B,\mathsf H^{\Omega}_UB\rangle=\sum_{p\cap\Omega\ne\varnothing}\mathfrak a_p(B;U)+\sum_{y\in\Omega}\mathfrak g_y(B;U)-\sum_{c\in\Omega^{[1]}}\mathfrak t_c(B;U),\\
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathfrak a_p&\coloneqq D^2s_{p,U}(0)[a,a],\\
        \mathfrak g_y&\coloneqq D^2\mathscr G_{y,U}(0)[a,a],\\
        \mathfrak t_c&\coloneqq\tfrac1L\langle J_U(b_0(c)),\alpha_c(U)^{-1}D^2\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)[a,a]\rangle\;.
    \end{aligned}
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Their free-input and background sets are read off from Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} and \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-elimination}: $a(r)$ depends on $B|_{\mathcal F_r}$ and on the background on $\mathcal A_r$, so $\mathfrak a_p$ has free-input set $\bigcup_{r\subset\partial p}\mathcal F_r$ and background set $\bigcup_{r\subset\partial p}(\{ r\}\cup\mathcal A_r)$; $\mathfrak g_y$ involves the phases on the axial paths inside $\mathcal B_y$, which contain no designated bond (designated bonds cross interfaces), so its free-input and background sets are $\mathcal E_y\cap E_*$ and $\mathcal E_y$; $\mathfrak t_c$ involves $\mathcal N_{U,c}$, $\alpha_c$ and $J_U(b_0(c))$, the latter depending on the plaquettes through $b_0(c)$, which lie in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$ for $L\geqslant 3$, so its sets are $\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$ and $\mathcal E_c$. The entries of $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U$ are the sums of the polarised entries of these terms.

For a pair of positive bonds $(b,b')$ let $\mathcal T_{bb'}$ be the set of terms of \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition} (plaquettes, centres, rows of the torus) whose free-input set contains both $b$ and $b'$, and let the \emph{entry stencil} $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ be the union of the background sets of these terms (one of finitely many types modulo $L\mathbb Z^4$; it is empty unless $d(b,b')\leqslant 4L$, Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}). The entry function is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-entry-function}
    f_{bb'}(U)=\sum_{\mathfrak T\in\mathcal T_{bb'}}(\text{polarised entry of }\mathfrak T\text{ at }(b,b'))\in\operatorname{End}(\mathfrak g),\qquad f_{bb'}(A)\coloneqq f_{bb'}(e^{iA})\;,
\end{equation}
defined for every configuration $U$ on $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ for which $\mathsf M(U)$ is defined and $\alpha_c(U)$ is invertible on the rows of the terms in $\mathcal T_{bb'}$ and the local group means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ are defined for the centres $y$ of the terms in $\mathcal T_{bb'}$ (the terms involve $\mathsf C_U$ on those rows and the means of those centres), whatever the configuration elsewhere.

The regional form is the compression of the torus form: for a background $U$ on which $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U$ is defined (Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}: $\mathsf M(U)$ defined and $\alpha_c(U)$ invertible on the rows of $\Omega^{[1]}$, the means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ defined for $y\in\Omega^{(1)}$) and every pair $(b,b')\in\Omega^*\times\Omega^*$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-regional-compression}
    \mathsf H^{\Omega}_U(b,b')= f_{bb'}(U|_{\mathcal S_{bb'}})\;,
\end{equation}
because a term whose free-input set contains the bond $b$ of $\Omega^*$ has its index in $\Omega$ (a plaquette containing $b$, or containing a bond $r$ with $b\in\mathcal F_r$, meets $\Omega$; a centre $y$ with $b\in\mathcal E_y$ lies in $\Omega$; a row $c$ with $b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$ has an endpoint block containing an endpoint of $b$, so $c\in\Omega^{[1]}$), hence every term of $\mathcal T_{bb'}$ is a term of the regional sum, and the regional form is defined under the weaker requirement on $U$ stated above (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry}).

\begin{lemma}[Gauge Law and Locality of the Hessian]\label{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}
Let $u$ be a site gauge transformation of the torus, acting on the background by $U\mapsto U^u$ and on phases by $(R_uq)(b)=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_-)}q(b)$ (\cite[(1.17)]{BalabanCRE}), and let $R_{u,*}$ be the restriction of $R_u$ to the free carrier $\Omega^*$; it is orthogonal for the invariant inner product. Then, for every region $\Omega$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-gauge-constrained-hessian}
    \mathsf H^{\Omega}_{U^u}= R_{u,*}\mathsf H^{\Omega}_UR_{u,*}^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}
Every entry $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U(b,b')$ is a finite composition of local analytic operations in the background bonds of the entry stencil $\mathcal S_{bb'}$, which lies within the range $\rho_L=4L$ of $b$, including the fibre inverses $\alpha_c^{-1}$, and it vanishes for $d(b,b')>\rho_L$ (the stencils are listed in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}). The entry function $f_{bb'}$ of \eqref{eq:c-entry-function} is entrywise gauge covariant: for a site gauge transformation $u$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-entry-gauge-covariance}
    f_{bb'}(U^u)=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_-)}f_{bb'}(U)\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b'_-)}^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}

The norms are the operator norm for the Hilbert norms induced by $h$ and, for $Df_{bb'}(A)$, the norm $\sup_{\| X\|_{\infty}\leqslant 1}\| Df_{bb'}(A)[X]\|$. Let $\tau_L$ denote the radius of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}, reduced so that these operations are analytic on $\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L$ and reduced once more in \eqref{eq:c2-tau-final} of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}; every statement is made for this final value. The entry constants are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-entry-constants}
    m_L\coloneqq\max_b\sum_{b'}\sup_{\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L}\| f_{bb'}(A)\|,
    \qquad
    c_L\coloneqq\max_b\sum_{b'}\sup_{\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L}\| Df_{bb'}(A)\|\;.
\end{equation}
These depend on $L$, the group and the invariant inner product only.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The intertwinings are $\mathsf M(U^u)(c)= u(c_-)\mathsf M(U)(c)u(c_+)^{-1}$, hence $\mathcal Q_{U^u}\circ R_u= R^{(1)}_u\mathcal Q_U$ with $(R^{(1)}_uv)(c)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ad}_{u(c_-)}v(c)$ (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}), and therefore $Q_{U^u}R_u= R^{(1)}_uQ_U$, $\mathcal N_{U^u}\circ R_u= R^{(1)}_u\mathcal N_U$, $h_{U^u}= R_uh_U(R^{(1)}_u)^{-1}$ (from the covariance of $\alpha_c$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}) and $\mathsf C_{U^u}= R_u\mathsf C_UR_{u,*}^{-1}$. The three terms of \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-hessian} are then each preserved: $S((e^{iR_uq})U^u)= S((e^{iq}U)^u)= S(e^{iq}U)$ gives $\Delta_{U^u}= R_u\Delta_UR_u^{-1}$ and $J_{U^u}= R_uJ_U$; each relative mean $\mathcal U_{e^{iq}U}(y,x)\mathcal U_U(y,x)^{-1}$ is conjugated by $u(y)$, which preserves the trace; and $\langle J_{U^u},h_{U^u}D^2\mathcal N_{U^u}(0)[R_ua,R_ua]\rangle=\langle R_uJ_U,R_uh_UD^2\mathcal N_U(0)[a,a]\rangle$ equals the untransformed force term because $R_u$ is orthogonal for the invariant inner product. The same three identities hold term by term in \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition} (each term is a function of $U$ and $a=\mathsf C_UB$ on its own stencil, and $\mathsf C_{U^u}R_{u,*}B= R_u\mathsf C_UB$), so the polarised entry of each term transforms as $\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_-)}(\bigcdot )\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b'_-)}^{-1}$, which is \eqref{eq:c-entry-gauge-covariance}.

Locality: the index of a term is the lower vertex $x(p)$ of its plaquette, the centre $y$ or the initial vertex of $b_0(c)$, and the distance of a bond to the index is that of its initial vertex. By the two-block structure of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} substituted into \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition}, the free-input and background bonds of a block or row term have initial vertices in the one or two blocks of the index, within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2L-1$ of it (the sites of two adjacent blocks are within $2L-1$ of each other); a bond $r$ of $\partial p$ has initial vertex within $1$ of $x(p)$, and the bonds of $\mathcal F_r\cup\mathcal A_r$ are within $2L-1$ of $r$, so the bonds of a plaquette term are within $2L$ of its index. Hence a term whose free-input set contains $b$ and $b'$ has $d(b,b')\leqslant 4L=\rho_L$, and its background bonds are within $4L$ of $b$. The stencils are listed in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Regular-Background Bounds]\label{lem:regular-bounds}
Let $\gamma_L\coloneqq C_L^{-1}$ be the flat lower bound \eqref{eq:covariance-uniform-gap} of Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance}, $\tau_L$ the final radius of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}, and let $R_{\mathrm c}$ (the collar range, Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}) and $C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}$ be the constants fixed in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:regular-covariance}; they depend on $L$ and the group only. Whenever \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} holds and $\widehat\mu= C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}\varepsilon_1$, $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ (\cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE}, with $g_1$ the first-step coupling), satisfies $\widehat\mu<\tau_L/2$ and $\max(1,c_L)\widehat\mu<\gamma_L/4$, on every branch (where $H_{\xi}$ is defined, by (B1) and (B2), as the operator of a quadratic form at fixed volume)
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-regular-two-sided}
    \frac{\gamma_L}{2}\,\id\leqslant H_{\xi,II}\leqslant m_L\,\id\;,
\end{equation}
and $H_{\xi,II}(b,b')=0$ for $d(b,b')>\rho_L$ (the entry stencil $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ is empty beyond that distance, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}). The same bounds hold for every principal restriction of $H_{\xi,II}$. Moreover, for every row $b\in I$ the row sum over all free bonds, those outside $I$ included, obeys $\sum_{b'\in\Omega_1^*}\|(H_{\xi})_{bb'}\|\leqslant m_L$, with $\|\bigcdot \|$ the operator norm for $h$ and $m_L$ of \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-entry-constants}.
\end{lemma}

The proof is in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:regular-covariance}.

\subsection{The Source Phase and the Local Primitives}
\label{sec:source-phase-primitives}

On the branch $U= U_1$ and $\Omega=\Omega_1$.

For the reference background $U=\id$ of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} only the near rows and the germs occur (the reference inputs vanish off $I$), the row solutions are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} in its reference form (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}), (B4) is not invoked, and $v$, $V$ below are defined by the same formulas. Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum} uses in addition that $U$ is a critical point of $S$ under the block-average constraint and is in the axial mean gauge, which holds for $U_1$ by (B1) and Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} and for $U=\id$ because the flat configuration minimises $S$ and $\mathscr G^{\Omega_1}_{\id}$ outright and has $\mathcal U_{\id}(y,x)=\id$.

For a free vector $B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}$ let $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1}$. The first-step correction $\widetilde D_U$ (for $U= U_1$, the correction of \cite[(1.13)--(1.14)]{BalabanCRE}, as identified in (B4)(i)) is the solution, selected below, of the system
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-local-implicit}
    \widetilde D_{U,c}(A)=\mathcal N_{U,c}\bigl(A-h_U\widetilde D_U(A)\bigr),\qquad c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}\;,
\end{equation}
the form of the equation of \cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1} for Ba{\l}aban's own step ($L\widetilde QB'+\widetilde C(B')= L\widetilde QB$ with $B'= B-h\widetilde D(B)$, $\widetilde C=\mathcal N_U$, $\widetilde Q= Q_U$) written row by row.

Let $\rho_{\mathrm d}>0$ be the radius $2K_*\vartheta_*^2$ of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii); it depends on $L$ and the group only. A solution $d_c$ of the row equation of $c$ with $h(d_c)<\rho_{\mathrm d}$ is called \emph{small}.

The row solution $\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)$ is defined as follows:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $U= U_1$ on the rows not within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ (the far rows; a row is within $\rho$ of a bond set when every bond of its two-block set is, see below) it is the row solution $\widetilde D_c(A)=\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$ of (B4)(i), defined on the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i)); the arguments $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$, $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, of the domain of integration \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain} lie in the ball of radius $\vartheta_*/2$, $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*/2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(ii)), and there its value is the component at $c$ of the chart-class family of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii));
\item on the rows within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ (the near rows), for $U= U_1$ and for the reference background, it is the unique small solution of the row equation of $c$ at the argument $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ given by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} on the row polydisc $\mathcal U_c$;
\item on a fixed neighbourhood $\mathcal N_c$ of $A|_{\mathcal E_c}=0$, for every row, it is the germ of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}, where $\mathcal N_c$ is the neighbourhood given by that lemma, reduced so that it lies in the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ and the germ takes values with $h<\rho_{\mathrm d}$ (both hold near zero, where the germ vanishes, and both conditions are open; the phase $A-h_U(c)d_c$ then has norm below $\vartheta_*+H_*\rho_{\mathrm d}<2\vartheta_*\leqslant \varrho_G$ and is chart-valued).
\end{itemize}
Where two of these definitions apply they agree: each produces a solution $d_c$ of the row equation with $h(d_c)\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm d}$ at an argument in the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ (the far-row values by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i), the near-row values by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}, the germ by the reduction of $\mathcal N_c$), and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii), which applies at every row for $U= U_1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i)) and for the reference background $U=\id$ (zero phases), gives exactly one such solution.

The reconstructed phase is the function of the free vector
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-local-phase}
    q_U(B)= A-h_U\widetilde D_U(A)\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1},\qquad A= g_0\mathsf C_UB\;,
\end{equation}
defined on free and designated bonds of $\Omega_1$ wherever every row solution is defined. The integration variable of the branch is $a+A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}$ in the variables of \cite[(1.22)]{BalabanCRE}; with $\Psi_{\xi}$ the bondwise map \eqref{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map} of Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar} from these variables to those of (1.15), the reconstructed fine field is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-reconstructed-field}
    U_{\xi}(a)(b)\coloneqq e^{iq_U(\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e}))(b)}U_1(b)\quad(b\in\Omega_1),\qquad U_{\xi}(a)(b)\coloneqq V_0(b)\quad(b\in\Omega_1^c)\;,
\end{equation}
the fine field $U= U'U_1$ of \cite[(1.13)]{BalabanCRE} at the actual branch data, $U_{\xi}(a)= U(\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e}))$ in the notation of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}; it is defined for $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ by the definition of $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ and $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} and Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality} its links on the rows within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ are defined for every $a$ in the enlarged box defined there, the other links not depending on $a$.

Let $U^0_{\xi}\coloneqq U_{\xi}(0)$. Since $I\cap S_1^*=\varnothing$ (\eqref{eq:c-collar-distance} below) and $\Psi_{\xi}$ acts bond by bond and is the identity off $S_1^*$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-bondwise-shift}
    \Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})= a+\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\qquad(a\in\mathfrak g^I,\ A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^J)\;.
\end{equation}
A row $c$ is said to lie within $\rho$ of a bond set $S$ when every bond of $\mathcal E_c$ is within distance $\rho$ of $S$; as the bonds of $\mathcal E_c$ have their initial vertices in two adjacent blocks, this holds as soon as one bond of $\mathcal E_c$ is within $\rho-(2L-1)$ of $S$.

\begin{lemma}[Rowwise Locality of the Reconstruction]\label{lem:row-locality}
The equation of row $c$ in \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} involves $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ alone and depends only on $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ and $U|_{\mathcal E_c}$; so the system decouples row by row, and a solution $d_c$ of the row equation at the argument $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ is a function of $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ and $U|_{\mathcal E_c}$.

The row equation has a unique analytic germ of solutions at $(A|_{\mathcal E_c},d_c)=(0,0)$, with $d_c(0)=0$ and $Dd_c(0)=0$; it is the germ at zero of every solution continuous at zero with value zero, in particular, for $U= U_1$, of the row solution $\widetilde D_c=\varphi_c$ of (B4)(i).

Consequently, wherever the row solutions are defined (Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}): on a free bond $r$, $q_U(B)(r)= g_0B(r)$; on $b_0(c)$, $q_U(B)(b_0(c))$ depends only on $B|_{\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}$ and on $U|_{\mathcal E_c}$; and $q_U(B)$ vanishes on all of $\mathcal E_c$ whenever $B=0$ on $\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$ and the row solution is the germ value there. In particular, by \eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}, the link $U_{\xi}(a)(r)$ depends on $a$ only through $a|_{\mathcal F_r\cap I}$ for $r\in\Omega_1$, and not at all for $r\in\Omega_1^c$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\mathcal E_c$ contains no designated bond other than $b_0(c)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}), so $h_U\widetilde D_U(A)$ restricted to $\mathcal E_c$ involves only $\widetilde D_{U,c}$, and $\mathcal N_{U,c}$ depends on its argument restricted to $\mathcal E_c$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}); by \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-elimination}, $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ depends on $B|_{\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}$ only.

At $(0,0)$ the derivative in $d_c$ of $d_c-\mathcal N_{U,c}(A-h_U(c)d_c)$ is the identity, since $D\mathcal N_U(0)= D\mathcal Q_U(0)-LQ_U=0$, and $\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$ (the zero phase reproduces the averages of $U$). The implicit function theorem gives the germ, unique among continuous solutions near $(0,0)$, with $d_c(0)=0$ and $Dd_c(0)= D\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)(\ldots)=0$.

For $U= U_1$ the row solution $\varphi_c$ of (B4)(i) is analytic with $\varphi_c(0)=0$ and solves the row equation (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i)), so its germ at zero is this one. If $B=0$ on $\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$ then $A=0$ on $\mathcal E_c$, so the germ value is $\widetilde D_{U,c}(0)=0$ and $q_U(B)=0$ on $\mathcal E_c$.

The last claim follows from \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field}, \eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift} and $\mathcal F_{b_0(c)}=\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$: the links of $U_{\xi}(a)$ on the bonds of $\mathcal E_c$ involve the row solution of $c$ at the argument $g_0\mathsf C_U\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})|_{\mathcal E_c}$, which involves $a$ only through $a|_{\mathcal E_c\cap E_*\cap I}$.
\end{proof}

The analyticity of the reconstruction on the cutoff box is Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} below, stated on the following sets.

\begin{definition}[Polydiscs and the Enlarged Box]\label{def:polydiscs}
Let $r$ be the cutoff radius of \eqref{eq:native-source-young-cutoff}, $R_{\mathrm c}$ the collar range of Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}, and $\vartheta_*>0$ the phase radius of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} ($\vartheta_*\leqslant \tau_L/2$; it depends on $L$ and the group only). The enlarged box is $\{ a\in\mathfrak g^I\, | \,| a(b)|\leqslant 2r\ \forall b\in I\}$. The row polydisc of a row $c$ and the block polydisc of a centre $y$ are
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal U_c\coloneqq\{ B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}\, | \,| B(b)|<2+4r\ \forall b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*\}\;,\qquad\mathcal U_y\coloneqq\{ B\, | \,| B(b)|<2+4r\ \forall b\in\mathcal E_y\}
\end{equation*}
(every bond of $\mathcal E_y$ is free). A centre $y$ lies within $\rho$ of a bond set $S$ when every bond of $\mathcal E_y$ does.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[The Chart Functions]\label{def:chart-functions}
Let $c$ be a row and $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ the small solution of the row equation of $c$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}(i)). The row determinant of $c$ at a phase $A$ is $\det_{\mathfrak g}(\id-h_U(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c}(A))$. For $B\in\mathcal U_c$ and $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$, the chart functions of $c$ are $\widetilde D_{U,c}$, the phase $q_U$ on $\mathcal E_c$, the normalised Haar logarithms $\log(\sigma(q_U(\bigcdot )(b))/\sigma(0))$ for $b\in\mathcal E_c$, the real logarithm of the row determinant, and, when $c$ is within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, the plaquette terms $s_{p,U}(q_U(\bigcdot ))$ of the plaquettes $p$ with a bond in $\mathcal E_c$ (on the intersection of the polydiscs of the rows of $p$).

Let $y$ be a centre and $B\in\mathcal U_y$. The relative means of $y$ are $\mathcal U_{e^{iq}U}(y,x)\mathcal U_U(y,x)^{-1}$, $x\in\mathcal B_y$, at $q= q_U(B)= g_0B$ on $\mathcal E_y$, and the chart functions of $y$ are these relative means and the gauge term $\mathscr G_{y,U}(q_U(\bigcdot ))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Charts]\label{lem:charts}
On every branch, and for the reference background $U=\id$ of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}, let $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$ be a row and $y\in\Omega_1^{(1)}$ a centre within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item for every real phase $A$ with $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ (Hilbert norm of $\mathfrak g^{\mathcal E_c}$), the row equation of $c$ at $A$ has exactly one small solution, $\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)=\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$, where $\varphi_c$ is analytic on the complex ball $\{\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*\}$, real on real phases, with $\varphi_c(0)=0$, $D\varphi_c(0)=0$;
\item under threshold item 3 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, $g_0\mathsf C_U\mathcal U_c$ lies in the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$; for $B\in\mathcal U_c$ the row determinant of $c$ is positive, and the chart functions of $c$ (Definition~\ref{def:chart-functions}) are analytic functions of $B|_{\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}$ on $\mathcal U_c$; the first four vanish at $B=0$, $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ and $q_U(\bigcdot )(b_0(c))-g_0(\mathsf C_UB)(b_0(c))$ together with their first derivatives;
\item for every $B\in\mathcal U_y$ the relative means of $y$ exist and lie within $r_G$ of $\id$ in operator norm, and the gauge term of $y$ is an analytic function of $B|_{\mathcal E_y}$ on $\mathcal U_y$ vanishing at $B=0$;
\item the derivatives in $B$ up to order five of the chart functions are bounded on the polydiscs by constants depending on $L$ and the group only;
\item every $a+t\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ with $a$ in the enlarged box and $t\in[0,1]$ lies in $\mathcal U_c$ and $\mathcal U_y$, and every near primitive $\mathfrak p$ is an analytic function of $(a,t)$ there, with $|\mathfrak p(a+t\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e}))|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0(1+2r)^3$, $C_{\mathrm p}$ depending on $L$ and the group only, and its derivatives in $a$ up to order four bounded as in \eqref{eq:c2-primitive-sizes}--\eqref{eq:convex-primitive-derivatives};
\item where $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$, these objects coincide with the objects of \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i)--(iii) and (vi) are proved in Section~\ref{app:charts}, after Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}, from Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} and~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}; the relative means lie in the domain of the chart logarithm $\log_G$ of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}. The functions of (ii) and (iii) are the compositions of analytic functions $\varphi$ of the real phase $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ (or $q|_{\mathcal E_y}$) with the linear map $B\mapsto g_0\mathsf C_UB$, where $\varphi$ is analytic on a complex neighbourhood of the closed phase ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ (which contains $g_0\mathsf C_U\mathcal U_c$; for the row solution and the phase, on the complex ball of radius $\vartheta_*$) and has derivatives up to order five bounded on that closed ball by constants depending on $L$ and the group only; this gives (iv).

The inclusion in (v) is Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i),(iii): $\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})= A_{\mathrm e}$ and $| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|< r$ on the bonds of $\mathcal E_c$, $\mathcal E_y$, which are within $2R_{\mathrm c}+4L-1\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$. The bounds of (v) are Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}, \eqref{eq:c2-primitive-sizes}, the prefactor $g_0^{-2}$ of $E_{\xi,\alpha}$ being absorbed by the third-order Taylor remainder; under threshold item 4 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, $g_0s_{\xi}^2\leqslant 4g_0(1+r)^3\leqslant 4\omega_*/C_0$, so these are bounds by constants depending on $L$ and the group only.
\end{proof}

The centred exponent and its primitives are those of \cite[(1.14)--(1.16)]{BalabanCRE}, written as functions of the free vector $B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}$. With $s_{p,U}(q)\coloneqq 1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N((e^{iq}U)(\partial p))$ for a plaquette $p$ meeting $\Omega_1$ (links off $\Omega_1$ fixed at $V_0$),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-energy-primitives}
    E_{\xi,p}(B)\coloneqq-\frac{1}{g_0^2}\bigl[s_{p,U}(q_U(B))-s_{p,U}(0)\bigr]\;,
\end{equation}
and $E_{\xi,y}(B)=-g_0^{-2}\mathscr G_{y,U}(q_U(B))$ from the $y$-summand of \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-gauge}, $y\in\Omega_1$. For either label $\alpha$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-energy-residual}
    p_{\xi,\alpha}(B)\coloneqq E_{\xi,\alpha}(B)-DE_{\xi,\alpha}(0)[B]-\frac{1}{2}D^2E_{\xi,\alpha}(0)[B,B]\;.
\end{equation}
With $\sigma(q)\,\dd q$ the pullback under $q\mapsto e^{iq}$ of the Haar measure $\dd U$ of \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} (the density $\sigma$ of (1.14), for the fixed inner product as explained in the conventions; its normalisation enters only the constants $\kappa_{\xi}$ and $c_{\xi}$), for every bond $b$ of $\Omega_1$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-haar-primitive}
    p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)\coloneqq\log\sigma(q_U(B)(b))-\log\sigma(0)\;,
\end{equation}
and for every row $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-jacobian-primitive}
    p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)
        \coloneqq\log\Bigl|\det_{\mathfrak g}\left(\id-h_U(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c}(g_0\mathsf C_UB)\right)\Bigr|\;,
\end{equation}
where $\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c}$ is the partial derivative of the row solution, regarded as a function of the $|\mathcal E_c|$ independent variables $A(b)$, $b\in\mathcal E_c$, with respect to the variable at $b_0(c)$, evaluated at $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$ (this is the designated block of the $\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum}).

A primitive is defined at $B$ when the row solutions of its rows are defined at $g_0\mathsf C_UB$ (Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}: on the domain of integration, on the polydiscs for the rows near $I$, and near $B|_{\text{inputs}}=0$); for a primitive whose row solutions are not defined at $B=0$ on the domain of integration (which happens when $R_1\ne\varnothing$, since the large-fluctuation tests exclude $A=0$ on $R_1$), the Taylor polynomial at $B=0$ in \eqref{eq:native-source-energy-residual} is formed from the germs of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}; the $V$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} is the sum of the terms of order higher than two of the expansion at $A=0$ (p.249, \cite[p.~267]{BalabanRG1}), and Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum} identifies the two.

The letter $\mathfrak p$ denotes a primitive of any of the three kinds. By Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality} the free-input set of $E_{\xi,p}$ and $p_{\xi,p}$ is $\bigcup_{r\subset\partial p}\mathcal F_r$, that of $E_{\xi,y}$ and $p_{\xi,y}$ is $\mathcal E_y\cap E_*=\mathcal E_y$, that of $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}$ is $\mathcal F_b$ and that of $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}$ is $\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$; the background set of each is the set of bonds whose links enter (bonds of $\Omega_1$ and, for plaquettes and rows at the boundary of $\Omega_1$, bonds of $\Omega_1^c$ carrying $V_0$), as in \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition}; the rows of a primitive are the rows $c$ with $b_0(c)$ in its background set (a gauge primitive $E_{\xi,y}$ has no rows: $\mathcal E_y$ contains no designated bond, and $q_U(B)= g_0B$ on it).

A primitive is \emph{near} if its free-input set meets $I$ and \emph{far} otherwise; a far primitive is a function of $A_{\mathrm e}$ and the branch data alone (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}, on the domain of (B4)). A near primitive has a bond $b_1\in I$ in its free-input set, and every bond of $\mathcal E_c$ for a row $c$ of the primitive, and every bond of $\mathcal E_y$ for a gauge primitive, is within $4L+3\leqslant 2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $b_1$ (two bonds of a two-block set are within $2L-1$ of each other, the bonds of a plaquette within $1$); so the rows of a near primitive, and the centre of a near gauge primitive, lie within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, and by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} every near primitive is defined and analytic in $(a,t)$ at the inputs $a+t\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$, $a$ in the enlarged box, $t\in[0,1]$.

An \emph{arc} $\gamma$ of the contour $C$ is a set of consecutive bonds of $C$ (with their orientations), and $\gamma_+$ is the set of their positive representatives; the free-input and background stencils of an arc are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-arc-stencils}
    F_{\gamma}\coloneqq\bigcup_{r\in\gamma_+}\mathcal F_r,
    \qquad
    D_{\gamma}\coloneqq\gamma_+\cup\bigcup_{c\, | \,b_0(c)\in\gamma_+}\mathcal E_c\;.
\end{equation}

\begin{definition}[The Functions $v$, $V$, and $\mathscr E_{\xi}$]\label{def:v-V-exponent}
$v$ and $V$ are the functions of \cite[(1.15), p.~249]{BalabanCRE}: $v(A)$ is the sum of the logarithms of the Haar densities $\sigma(A-h\widetilde D(A))$ over the bonds of $\Omega_1$ and of $\log|\det(\id-h\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)|$, the logarithm of the absolute Jacobian of (1.14), which is, in the notation of \cite{BalabanCRE}, $\operatorname{Tr}\log(\id-h\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)$ where the determinant is positive (on the near rows, factor by factor, by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}; on all of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ by (B4)(iii), Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv)), the identities below using the absolute value throughout; $V(A)$ is the remainder after the Taylor polynomial of degree two at $A=0$ of the action and the gauge-fixing functional at the phase $A-h\widetilde D(A)$ (the ``terms of order higher than two'' of \cite{BalabanCRE}; the Taylor coefficients at $A=0$ are those of the germs of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}). The exponent of the second factor of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} at the free vector $B$, with the quadratic form written through the regional Hessian \eqref{eq:c-regional-hessian}, is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-collar-full-exponent}
    \mathscr E_{\xi}(B)\coloneqq-\frac{1}{2}\langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle+v(g_0\mathsf C_UB)-g_0^{-2}V(g_0\mathsf C_UB)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Exact Primitive Sum]\label{lem:primitive-sum}
For $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, and more generally for every $B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}$ at which every row solution is defined with the row solutions of the near rows those of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} and those of the far rows the germs at zero argument ($B=0$ on their two-block sets), with $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-primitive-sum}
    v(A)-v(0)-g_0^{-2}V(A)
        =\sum_{\alpha}p_{\xi,\alpha}(B)+\sum_{b}p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)+\sum_{c}p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)\;,
\end{equation}
the first sum over the plaquettes $p$ meeting $\Omega_1$ and the centres $y\in\Omega_1^{(1)}$, the second over the bonds $b$ of $\Omega_1$, the third over the rows $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$ (the same ranges in every sum $\sum_{\alpha}$, $\sum_b$, $\sum_c$ below). The exponent $\mathscr E_{\xi}$ of Definition~\ref{def:v-V-exponent} satisfies $\mathscr E_{\xi}(0)= v(0)$ with $v(0)=\sum_b\log(\sigma(0)/\sigma_0)=0$ (sum over the bonds of $\Omega_1$; the Haar densities in the $v$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} are divided by their value $\sigma_0$ at the identity, as fixed in the step list after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}) and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-centred-exponent}
    \begin{aligned}
    \mathscr E_{\xi}(B)-\mathscr E_{\xi}(0)&=-\frac{1}{2}\langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle+\sum_{\alpha} p_{\xi,\alpha}(B)+\sum_bp^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)+\sum_cp^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)\\
    &=\sum_{\alpha} E_{\xi,\alpha}(B)+\sum_bp^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)+\sum_cp^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The sum $\sum_{\alpha} E_{\xi,\alpha}(B)$ is $-g_0^{-2}$ times the difference of the action plus gauge-fixing functional at the phase $q_U(B)$ and at $q=0$: here the gauge-fixing functional of \cite[(1.11), (1.14)]{BalabanCRE} is $\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},e^{iq}U_1)=\mathscr G^{\Omega_1}_{U_1}(q)$ because $U_1$ is in the axial mean gauge (Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}, after \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-hessian}).

Since $D\widetilde D_U(0)=0$, $Dq_U(0)[B]= g_0\mathsf C_UB$, and the linear term of the Taylor expansion in $B$ at zero is $\sum_{\alpha} DE_{\xi,\alpha}(0)[B]=-g_0^{-1}\bigl(DS(U_1)[\mathsf C_UB]+D\mathscr G^{\Omega_1}_U(0)[\mathsf C_UB]\bigr)=0$: the relative gauge functional is a sum of nonnegative terms vanishing at $q=0$, so its first variation vanishes; by \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} $U_1$ is a critical point of $S+\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},\bigcdot )$ on the configurations with $\mathsf M(U)= V$ on $\Omega_1^{(1)}$ and $U= V_0$ on $\Omega_1^c$, and $\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},\bigcdot )\geqslant 0$ attains its minimum $0$ at $U_1$, so $D\mathbf G(\Omega_1^{(1)},U_1)=0$ and $DS(U_1)[\delta]=0$ for every phase $\delta$ supported on the bonds of $\Omega_1$ with $D\mathcal Q_U(0)\delta= LQ_U\delta=0$ (the tangent space of the constraint $\mathsf M(e^{i\delta}U_1)= V$); and $\mathsf C_UB$ is such a phase by $Q_U\mathsf C_U=0$ \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-elimination}.

The quadratic term is $-\frac12\langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle$ by \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-hessian}, with $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$: the second variation of the action is $\langle A,\Delta_UA\rangle$ plus the force term $-2\langle J_U,h_U\frac12D^2\mathcal N_U(0)[A,A]\rangle$ from the second-order part $-h_U\widetilde D^{(2)}_U(A)$ of the phase, and that of the gauge functional is $G^{(2),\Omega_1}_U(A)$. Subtracting both from $\sum_{\alpha} E_{\xi,\alpha}$ gives $\sum_{\alpha} p_{\xi,\alpha}$, which is therefore $-g_0^{-2}V(A)$.

The Haar part of $v$ is $\sum_b\log\sigma(q_U(B)(b))$ bond by bond, so $v$ minus its Haar part at $B=0$ gives $\sum_bp^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}$.

For the Jacobian, $\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D$ has rows indexed by $\Omega_1^{[1]}$ and columns by the bonds of $\Omega_1$, and $h_U$ maps row $c$ to the bond $b_0(c)$; in the ordering (free bonds, designated bonds) the matrix $\id-h_U\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D_U$ is block triangular with identity block on the free bonds and designated block $\operatorname{diag}_c(\id-h_U(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c})$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} (row $c$ depends on $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$, which contains the single designated bond $b_0(c)$), so its determinant is $\prod_c\det_{\mathfrak g}(\id-h_U(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c})$, positive on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ by (B4)(iii), and at the other points admitted in the statement because each near-row factor is positive by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} and each far-row factor equals one at zero argument ($D\widetilde D_{U,c}(0)=0$); so $\operatorname{Tr}\log$ of the matrix, the term in the $v$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, is the real logarithm of the positive determinant, and since each factor is a nonzero real, the logarithm of the absolute value of the product is the sum of the logarithms of the absolute values of the factors, $\sum_c\log|\det_{\mathfrak g}(\cdots)|=\sum_cp^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)$; this vanishes at $B=0$ since $D\widetilde D_U(0)=0$; hence $v(0)$ is the Haar part at $B=0$.

The quadratic form of (1.15) in the free variable, $\frac12\langle B,C^*\Delta_1CB\rangle$, is $\frac12\langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle$ by the identification $\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{U_1}= C^*\Delta_1C$ of Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils} ($\Delta_1$ of (1.16) already contains $\mathbf G^{(2)}$ and the force term; the $g_0^{-2}$ of the action cancels the $g_0^2$ of $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$).

Subtracting $\mathscr E_{\xi}(0)= v(0)$ from \eqref{eq:native-collar-full-exponent} and inserting \eqref{eq:native-source-primitive-sum} gives the first form of \eqref{eq:c-centred-exponent}; the second form restores the quadratic term to $\sum_{\alpha} p_{\xi,\alpha}$.
\end{proof}

Each primitive is assigned a host $Y_{\alpha}$ in the native localisation family $\mathbf D_0$. Its free-input and background stencil $\widetilde{\mathcal S}_{\alpha}$ is lifted to $\mathbb Z^4$ about its base (plaquette lower vertex, block centre, initial vertex of its bond, or initial vertex of $b_0(c)$ for $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}$; the stencil has $\ell^{\infty}$ diameter at most $4L< M$, below every period, so the lift about the base is well defined); with $Z_{\alpha}$ the set of $M$-cubes $Q_z= Mz+[-M/2,M/2]^4$ meeting the lift, the host is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-potential-host}
    Y_{\alpha}\coloneqq\pi_T\Bigl(\bigcup_{z\in\prod_{\mu}([k^-_{\alpha,\mu}-1,k^+_{\alpha,\mu}+1]\cap\mathbb Z)}Q_z\Bigr),
    \qquad k^-_{\alpha,\mu}\coloneqq\min_{z\in Z_{\alpha}}z_{\mu},\quad k^+_{\alpha,\mu}\coloneqq\max_{z\in Z_{\alpha}}z_{\mu}\;,
\end{equation}
with $\pi_T$ the reduction modulo the periods; since the stencil has diameter at most $4L< M$, it meets at most two consecutive $M$-cubes in each direction, so the rectangle has side at most $4$ cubes, and every period being at least $8M$, $\pi_T$ is injective on it. $Y_{\alpha}$ is connected and contains the stencil in its interior.

The potential is, for $Y\in\mathbf D_0$ and $a\in\mathfrak g^I$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-potential-definition}
    \mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)=\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near},\ Y_{\mathfrak p}= Y}\mathfrak p(a)\quad\text{if }| a(b)|< r\ \forall b\in E(Y),\qquad\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)=0\quad\text{otherwise},
\end{equation}
the sum over the near primitives $\mathfrak p$ of all three kinds assigned to $Y$, with $E(Y)\coloneqq\{ b\in I\, | \,b\cap Y\ne\varnothing\}$ and the primitives at zero retained input ($t=0$). It depends on $a|_{E(Y)}$ only, since the free-input set of a primitive assigned to $Y$ lies in $Y$, hence in $E(Y)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}), and it is bounded on the local box by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} (each summand by $C_{\mathrm p}g_0(1+2r)^3$). On the open box $\{| a(b)|< r\ \forall b\in I\}$, $\sum_Y\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)=\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near}}\mathfrak p(a)$.

\subsection{The Boundary Law, the Exterior Interpolation and the Collar}
\label{sec:boundary-law-collar}

\emph{The change of variables.} Let $S_1\coloneqq(\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1})\cup R_1$ (\cite[(1.20)]{BalabanCRE}) and let $S_1^*$ be its free bonds. \cite[(1.22)]{BalabanCRE} replaces the variable $A$ of (1.15) on each bond $b\in S_1^*$ by a new variable $A'(b)$ and leaves the other bonds unchanged: $A=\Psi_{\xi} A'$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map}
    \begin{gathered}
    (\Psi_{\xi} A')(b)= g_0^{-1}\log\left(e^{ig_0A'(b)}e^{-i\omega_b(A'(b))\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)}\right)\quad(b\in S_1^*),\\
    (\Psi_{\xi} A')(b)= A'(b)\quad(b\in\Omega_1^*\setminus S_1^*)\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
where
\begin{itemize}
\item $\omega_b$ is the $C^{\infty}$ cutoff $g$ of \cite[p.~252]{BalabanCRE} ($0\leqslant g\leqslant 1$, $g=0$ on $| A'|\leqslant \frac43g_0^{-1}\delta_0$, $g=1$ where $| e^{ig_0A'}-1|\geqslant \frac53\delta_0$) for $b$ in the set $(R_1^{\sim2}\cap S_1)^*$ named in the definition preceding (1.22) (p.251); \cite{BalabanCRE} specifies $g$ by these properties only, and one such $g$ with $| Dg(A')|\leqslant 6g_0/\delta_0$ for every $A'$ (operator norm for the cutoff norm $|\bigcdot |$) is fixed once: the function $\ell(A')=\min(1,\max(0,(| g_0A'|-\frac{17}{12}\delta_0)/(\frac16\delta_0)))$ is Lipschitz with constant $6g_0/\delta_0$, vanishes for $| g_0A'|\leqslant \frac{17}{12}\delta_0$ and equals one for $| g_0A'|\geqslant \frac{19}{12}\delta_0$, and its convolution with a $C^{\infty}$ probability density supported in $\{| A'|\leqslant \delta_0/(12g_0)\}$ is $C^{\infty}$ with values in $[0,1]$, has the same Lipschitz constant, vanishes for $| g_0A'|\leqslant \frac43\delta_0$ and equals one for $| g_0A'|\geqslant \frac53\delta_0$, hence wherever $| e^{ig_0A'}-\id|\geqslant \frac53\delta_0$, as $| e^{iX}-\id|\leqslant | X|$; and $\omega_b=1$ for the other bonds of $S_1^*$ (p.252 describes the second set as $S_1^*\setminus(R_1^{\sim2})^*$, which differs from the complement of the first set in $S_1^*$ on the bonds joining $R_1^{\sim2}\setminus S_1$ to $S_1\setminus R_1^{\sim2}$; the definition of p.251 is used, on the bonds of the difference the map is the second form of \cite{BalabanCRE} with $g$ replaced by one, and the cutoff is the exact composition \eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition});
\item $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)\in\mathfrak g$ is the field $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,\bigcdot )$ of \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE} at the actual branch data, as it appears in (1.22), without the prefactor $L^{-1}$ of (1.21) (a function of the pair $(V,V_0)$ through $U_1= U_1(V,V_0)$ and $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$, the latter stated by \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE} to depend on $V|_{\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c}$; Borel in $(V,V_0)$ by the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}; with (1.21) and $\omega_b=1$, $e^{ig_0(\Psi_{\xi} A')(b)}U_1(b)= e^{ig_0A'(b)}e^{-i(1-L^{-1})\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)}U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,b)$, which is not the second factor of \cite[(1.23)]{BalabanCRE}: as printed, (1.22) carries $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ where (1.21) carries $L^{-1}\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$, and (1.24) has $+F$ against the $-F$ of (1.22); this paper uses (1.22) as printed, with the exact Jacobian $|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|$ and the cutoff composed in the variable of (1.15), and does not use (1.23)--(1.24));
\item $\log$ is the group chart, the inverse of $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ on the chart ball (so that $\log$ is the chart logarithm of the fluctuation, written $\frac1i\log$ in the notation of \cite{BalabanCRE} for the matrix logarithm, and $g_0^{-1}\log(\cdots)$ is the variable of (1.15)).
\end{itemize}
$\Psi_{\xi}$ acts bond by bond, and $\psi_b$ denotes its component at $b\in S_1^*$, a $C^{\infty}$ map ($g$ is $C^{\infty}$, not analytic) on the open set $\mathcal W_b\subseteq\mathfrak g$ of those $A'(b)$ for which $g_0A'(b)$ lies in the chart ball and the argument of the chart logarithm lies in the chart domain (on the bonds where (1.22) is the identity, the variable $A'$ of (1.22) is the variable $A$ of (1.15), which on the free bonds is $g_0^{-1}$ times the fluctuation variable of (1.13); on $S_1^*$ the new variable $A'$ is restricted to the values with $g_0A'$ in the chart ball as well, which loses no preimage, every preimage under $\psi_b$ of a point of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ lying in $g_0^{-1}K$ with $K$ the ball of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection}(b),(c)).

By Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection} below, which is the (1.22) part of (B4)(ii), $\Psi_{\xi}$ maps $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ bijectively onto $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, the domain of integration of (1.15) with the cutoff (1.25) (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), and $D\Psi_{\xi}$ is invertible there, so that the change of variables formula applies with the Jacobian $|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|=\prod_{b\in S_1^*}|\det D\psi_b|$; $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})$ below is set to zero when $A_{\mathrm e}(b)\notin\mathcal W_b$ for some $b\in S_1^*$. Thus $\log|\det D\Psi_{\xi}(A')|$ depends on $A'|_{S_1^*}$ only, and it is $C^{\infty}$, finite at $(A_{\mathrm e},0)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ and independent of $a$ (a constant on the branch, by $I\cap S_1^*=\varnothing$ and \eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}).

The integration variable of the branch is $A'= a+A_{\mathrm e}$ with $a\in\mathfrak g^I$ and $A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^J$. A bond of $I$ has an endpoint in $\Lambda_1\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-2}\cap(R_1'^{\sim})^c$, a bond of $S_1^*$ has an endpoint in $S_1$, and $\Omega_1^{\sim-2}$ is separated from $\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$, as $(R_1'^{\sim})^c$ is from $R_1\subseteq R_1'$, by a full layer of $LMR_1$-cubes (the enlargement adjoins every touching cube, Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}); hence, with distances between initial vertices,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-collar-distance}
    I\cap S_1^*=\varnothing,\qquad d(I,S_1^*)\geqslant LMR_1-2\;.
\end{equation}
The filling modification following \cite[(1.20)]{BalabanCRE} only removes cubes from $\Lambda_1$, so \eqref{eq:c-collar-distance} holds for the final $\Lambda_1$. This gives \eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}.

\begin{definition}[Boundary Data]\label{def:boundary-data}
Let $r_G\in(0,1]$ be the group constant of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} (defined there with the chart logarithm $\log_G$): every $U\in G$ with $\| U-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant r_G$ lies in the chart domain $N_G$, the image of the chart ball $\{ h(A)<\varrho_G\}$ under $A\mapsto e^{iA}$. Let $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ be an admissible pair and $R_1$ a large-fluctuation region of the history sum (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), with $U_1$ and the configuration $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ of (1.21) formed with the representatives chosen in Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser}. For $b\in S_1^*$ let $\square'(b)\subseteq S_1$ be an $L^2M_2R_1$-cube with $b\in(\square'(b)^{\sim2})^*$. Then
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{gathered}
        \delta_G\coloneqq \min\bigl(\log(3/2)/(12\sqrt N),\,r_G/(10\sqrt N)\bigr)\;,\qquad Z_b\coloneqq U_1(b)U_{1,\square'(b)}(b)^{-1}\;,\\
        \mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)\coloneqq L\log\bigl(U_1(b)\,U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)(b)^{-1}\bigr)\;,\\
        \mathcal T_b\coloneqq \{ A\in\mathfrak g: h(g_0A)<\varrho_G,\ | e^{ig_0A}Z_b-\id|<2\delta_0\}\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation*}
$\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)$ being defined wherever this chart logarithm is.
\end{definition}

The configurations $U_1$ and $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ exist by (B1) and Lemma~\ref{lem:step-minimisers}. Under \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs}, $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ is the analytic $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE}, since $L^{-1}\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)$ then lies in the chart ball and (1.21) determines it there as this logarithm.
