The cube $\square'(b)$ exists: $S_1$ is a union of such cubes, $\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ being a union of $LMR_1$-cubes, each a union of $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes (the cube partitions of \cite[pp.~245--246]{BalabanCRE} are nested: each cube of a coarser partition is a union of cubes of each finer one, the $L$-blocks included, the side ratios $M/(LM_2)$, a power of $L$ by the standing choice, and $LM_2R_1$ being integers), and $R_1$ a union of them, p.250; $b$ has an endpoint in $S_1$, hence in such a cube, and is not designated for a row outside $S_1^{[1]}$: if $b= b_0(c)$, the block containing its endpoint in $S_1$ lies in $S_1$ by the nesting, so $c\in S_1^{[1]}$, which $b\in S_1^*$ excludes.

The bound on $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE}, proved in Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}, is used at the tolerance
\begin{equation}\label{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs}
|\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)|\leqslant \frac{\delta_0}{40}\qquad(b\in S_1^*)\;.
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[The Boundary Change Is a Bijection]\label{lem:boundary-bijection}
Let $\delta_0\leqslant \delta_G$, a condition on the coupling ($\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0\to0$), and let $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ and $R_1$ be as in Definition~\ref{def:boundary-data}. Then for every $b\in S_1^*$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $B(b)\in\mathcal T_b$ for every $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$;
\item[(b)] $\mathcal T_b\subseteq\psi_b(\mathcal W_b)$;
\item[(c)] $\psi_b$ is injective on $\psi_b^{-1}(\mathcal T_b)$, and $D\psi_b$ is invertible at every point of $\psi_b^{-1}(\mathcal T_b)$.
\end{itemize}
Consequently $\Psi_{\xi}$ maps $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ bijectively onto $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, and $D\Psi_{\xi}$ is invertible at every point of $\mathcal D_{\xi}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Norm facts, for the cutoff norm $|\bigcdot |$ (operator or normalised Hilbert--Schmidt) and Hermitian $X$ with $\| X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \pi$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $| e^{iX}-\id|\leqslant | X|\leqslant \frac\pi2| e^{iX}-\id|$ (eigenvalue by eigenvalue, $2|\sin(\theta/2)|\leqslant |\theta|\leqslant \pi|\sin(\theta/2)|$ for $|\theta|\leqslant \pi$, in both norms);
\item $| UY|=| YU|=| Y|$ for unitary $U$, so $| UU'-\id|\leqslant | U-\id|+| U'-\id|$ for unitary $U,U'$;
\item a unitary $U\in G$ with $| U-\id|< r_G/\sqrt N$ lies in the chart domain, since $\| U-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt N| U-\id|$ for either cutoff norm and by the definition of $r_G$ (the eigenvalue argument alone does not give this for a general compact $G\subset U(N)$: the Hermitian logarithm $Y$ of $U$ with eigenvalues in $(-\pi,\pi]$ need not lie in the Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$, so $r_G$ is a constant of the group);
\item on $\{| X|\leqslant 12\delta_0\}$, writing $e^{iX}=\id+iX+R(X)$, one has $\| DR(X)\|\leqslant e^{\| X\|_{\mathrm{op}}}-1\leqslant e^{12\sqrt N\delta_0}-1\leqslant \frac12$ (the derivative of $X^k$ is a sum of $k$ terms $X^jVX^{k-1-j}$, each of norm at most $\| X\|_{\mathrm{op}}^{k-1}| V|$), so $| e^{iX}-e^{iX'}|\geqslant \frac12| X-X'|$ for $| X|,| X'|\leqslant 12\delta_0$.
\end{itemize}

Let $b\in S_1^*$, $H=\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)$, $\omega=\omega_b$, and let $x= g_0A'$ be the group-scale variable: $\psi_b(A')= g_0^{-1}F(g_0A')$ with $F(x)\coloneqq\log(e^{ix}W(x))$, $W(x)= e^{-i\widetilde\omega(x)H}$, $\widetilde\omega(x)=\omega(x/g_0)$, on $\mathfrak B_b= g_0\mathcal W_b=\{ x: h(x)<\varrho_G,\ e^{ix}W(x)\text{ in the chart domain}\}$; $| D\widetilde\omega|\leqslant 6/\delta_0$, and $| W(x)-\id|\leqslant \widetilde\omega(x)| H|\leqslant | H|\leqslant \delta_0/40$.

Moreover $| Z_b-\id|<2\delta_0$: by (B1) the background $U_1$ lies in $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$, the domain of integration in (1.11) (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}), on which the factor $\chi_0'(\square'(b))$ of $\chi_0'(\Omega_1)$ is nonzero, that is $| U_1(b')U_{1,\square'(b)}(b')^{-1}-\id|<2\delta_0$ for every $b'\in(\square'(b)^{\sim2})^*$ (\cite[(1.8)]{BalabanCRE}), and $b$ is one of these bonds.

(a) For $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, $U(B)(b)= e^{ig_0B(b)}U_1(b)$ ($b$ is free, so $q_{U_1}(B)(b)= g_0B(b)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}), and $g_0B(b)$ is the component at $b$ of the chart logarithm $\frac1i\log U'$ of (1.13) (the variable written $A'$ there, not the new variable $A'$ of (1.22)), so $h(g_0B(b))<\varrho_G$ by the chart-class condition in the definition \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain} of $\mathcal A_{\xi}$; the cutoff (1.25) is nonzero at $U(B)$, in particular its factor $\chi_0'(\square'(b))$, the test $| U(B)(b')U_{1,\square'(b)}(b')^{-1}-\id|<2\delta_0$ for $b'\in(\square'(b)^{\sim2})^*$ (\cite[(1.8) and p.~250]{BalabanCRE}; a function of the fine field, composed with the changes of variables (1.14) and $A= g_0A'$ of p.249, Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), and at $b'= b$ this reads $| e^{ig_0B(b)}Z_b-\id|<2\delta_0$.

(b) Let $y= g_0A$ with $A\in\mathcal T_b$. Then $| e^{iy}-\id|\leqslant | e^{iy}Z_b-\id|+| Z_b-\id|<4\delta_0$, and $\| y\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\pi$ since $h(y)<\varrho_G$, so $| y|\leqslant \frac\pi2\cdot4\delta_0<6.3\,\delta_0$.

Let $K=\{ x\in\mathfrak g: | x|\leqslant 7\delta_0\}$, compact and convex, with $K\subseteq\mathfrak B_b$: $h(x)\leqslant | x|\leqslant 7\delta_0<\varrho_G$ (as $7\delta_0\leqslant 7r_G/(10\sqrt N)<\pi/\sqrt N=\varrho_G$, $r_G\leqslant 1$) and $| e^{ix}W(x)-\id|\leqslant | x|+| H|\leqslant 7\delta_0+\delta_0/40<8\delta_0\leqslant r_G/\sqrt N$, so $e^{ix}W(x)$, an element of $G$, lies in the chart domain. For $x\in K$, $e^{iF(x)}= e^{ix}W(x)$ gives $| e^{iF(x)}-e^{ix}|=| W(x)-\id|\leqslant | H|$ and $| e^{iF(x)}-\id|\leqslant 7\delta_0+| H|$, so $| F(x)|\leqslant \frac\pi2(7\delta_0+\delta_0/40)<11.1\,\delta_0<12\delta_0$ ($\| F(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\pi$, $F(x)$ lying in the chart ball) and $| F(x)-x|\leqslant 2| e^{iF(x)}-e^{ix}|\leqslant 2| H|\leqslant \delta_0/20$, both $F(x)$ and $x$ lying in $\{| X|\leqslant 12\delta_0\}$.

The continuous map $T(x)= x-F(x)+y$ maps $K$ into itself, $| T(x)|\leqslant \delta_0/20+6.3\,\delta_0<7\delta_0$, so by Brouwer's fixed point theorem it has a fixed point $x\in K$, that is $F(x)= y$; then $A'= x/g_0\in\mathcal W_b$ and $\psi_b(A')= A$.

(c) Let $x,x'\in\mathfrak B_b$ with $F(x)= F(x')= y$ and $y/g_0\in\mathcal T_b$. Then $e^{ix}= e^{iy}W(x)^{-1}$ gives $| e^{ix}-\id|\leqslant | e^{iy}-\id|+| H|<4\delta_0+\frac1{40}\delta_0$, so $| x|\leqslant \frac\pi2\cdot\frac{161}{40}\delta_0<6.4\,\delta_0$, and likewise $| x'|<6.4\,\delta_0$; both lie in $K$. From $e^{ix}W(x)= e^{ix'}W(x')$, $e^{ix}-e^{ix'}= e^{ix'}\bigl(W(x')W(x)^{-1}-\id\bigr)$ with $W(x')W(x)^{-1}= e^{i(\widetilde\omega(x)-\widetilde\omega(x'))H}$, so $| e^{ix}-e^{ix'}|\leqslant |\widetilde\omega(x)-\widetilde\omega(x')|\,| H|\leqslant \frac6{\delta_0}| x-x'|\cdot\frac{\delta_0}{40}=\frac3{20}| x-x'|$, while $| e^{ix}-e^{ix'}|\geqslant \frac12| x-x'|$; hence $x= x'$.

For the differential at such an $x\in K$: with $P(x)\coloneqq e^{ix}W(x)$, $F=\log\circ P$, and $D\log$ is invertible on the chart domain, so it suffices that $DP(x)$ is injective; $DP(x)[v]= D(e^{i\bigcdot })(x)[v]\,W(x)+e^{ix}DW(x)[v]$ with $| e^{ix}DW(x)[v]|=| D\widetilde\omega(x)[v]|\,| H|\leqslant \frac3{20}| v|$ and $| D(e^{i\bigcdot })(x)[v]\,W(x)|=| iv+DR(x)[v]|\geqslant \frac12| v|$, so $DP(x)[v]=0$ forces $v=0$.

The consequences: $\Psi_{\xi}$ is bondwise and the identity off $S_1^*$. For $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, (a) and (b) give $A'$ with $A'(b)\in\mathcal W_b$ for $b\in S_1^*$ and $\Psi_{\xi}(A')= B$, and $(A_{\mathrm e},a)=(A'|_J,A'|_I)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ by \eqref{eq:c-new-variable-domain}; so $\Psi_{\xi}(\mathcal D_{\xi})=\mathcal A_{\xi}$, the inclusion $\subseteq$ being the definition. If $\Psi_{\xi}(A')=\Psi_{\xi}(A'')= B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, then bond by bond $\psi_b(A'(b))=\psi_b(A''(b))= B(b)\in\mathcal T_b$ by (a), so $A'(b)= A''(b)$ by (c); and $D\Psi_{\xi}=\bigoplus_{b\in S_1^*}D\psi_b\oplus\id$ is invertible at every point of $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ by (c).

Moreover, by (b), (c) and the inverse function theorem, $\Psi_{\xi}$ restricted to the open set $\prod_{b\in S_1^*}\psi_b^{-1}(\mathcal T_b)\times\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*\setminus S_1^*}$ ($\mathcal T_b$ is open, being defined by strict inequalities between continuous functions) is a $C^{\infty}$ diffeomorphism onto the open set $\prod_{b\in S_1^*}\mathcal T_b\times\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*\setminus S_1^*}$, which contains $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ by (a); so $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ lies in the former open set, on which $\log|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|$ is $C^{\infty}$.
\end{proof}

\emph{The inputs.} The bound \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs} is Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-6}).

Ba{\l}aban states in \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE} the bound $|\mathbf H_{1,Ax}|< O(1)B_3\exp(-\delta MR_1)\varepsilon_1$, ``much smaller than $\delta_0$, for $MR_1$ large enough'', for $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ ``on $\square'$'' for the cubes $\square'\subset S_1$, from the distance between $\square'$ and the support of the argument of $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ (one layer of $M_1$-cubes touching $\partial\Lambda_1$) and the exponential decay property of \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR}, which is stated there for the Landau gauge and which \cite{BalabanCRE} transfers to the axial gauge (``on the unit lattice it holds for any gauge, for which propagators are exponentially decaying, hence for the axial gauge too'').

The lemma derives a bound of this form on every bond of $S_1^*$ from \cite[Proposition~9, (172), and (190)]{BalabanVAR}, integrated in the Landau gauge, and from the block-local restoration of the axial gauge, with constants $C_{\mathrm H}$, $c_{\mathrm H}$ fixed before $g_0$; with $\varepsilon_1/\delta_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)A_0/A_1$ (\cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE} and $\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$), the tolerance $\delta_0/40$ is a condition ``$MR_1$ large'', met for small $g_0$ at fixed $M$ since $R_1\to\infty$ (threshold item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}).

The condition on $MR_1$ at the tolerance $\delta_0/40$ and the condition of \cite{BalabanCRE} on $M_2R_1$ are item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}; the condition $\delta_0\leqslant \delta_G$ is among the further conditions listed after its enumeration.

\emph{The cutoff.} The small-field test of \cite[(1.18)]{BalabanCRE} for a cube $\square'$ of side $L^2M_2R_1$ is the indicator of $\{\sup_{b\in(\square'^{\sim2})^*}| A(b)|< r\}$, $r=\delta_0/g_0$, in the bond norm of \cite{BalabanCRE} with the normalisation \eqref{eq:cre-cutoff-normalisation}, and it is the product of one indicator per bond of $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-good-region}
    \mathcal G_{\xi}\coloneqq\bigcup_{\square'\subset R_1^c}(\square'^{\sim2})^*,\qquad R_1^c\coloneqq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1\;,
\end{equation}
the union over the good cubes of (1.18). Since $\Lambda_1\subseteq R_1^c$ and both are unions of such cubes, the first two factors of \cite[(1.25)]{BalabanCRE} are the product of the tests over all good cubes, which by idempotence of indicators is $\prod_{b\in\mathcal G_{\xi}}\mathbf 1_{\{| A(b)|< r\}}$. The cutoff on the integration carrier is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-young-cutoff}
    \Theta_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq\prod_{b\in I}\mathbf 1_{\{| a(b)|< r\}}\;,
\end{equation}
and the retained cutoff is defined as the remaining factors of (1.25), composed with the change of variables:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-cutoff-composition}
    \chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})=\prod_{b\in\mathcal G_{\xi}\cap J}\mathbf 1_{\{|(\Psi_{\xi} A_{\mathrm e})(b)|< r\}}\cdot\bigl[\chi^{(0)c}(R_1)\chi_0'(S_1)\bigr](\Psi_{\xi} A_{\mathrm e})\;,
\end{equation}
where $\chi^{(0)c}(R_1)$ is the product of the large-fluctuation tests of (1.18) over the cubes of $R_1$ and $\chi_0'(S_1)$ the product of the tests of (1.8) over the cubes of $S_1$, both as functions of the variable $A$ of (1.15) on $\Omega_1^*$ (through the free links $e^{ig_0A(b)}U_1(b)$ in the case of (1.8)) and of the branch data ($V_0$ on $\Omega_1^c$, $U_1$ and the local minima $U_{1,\square'}$).

By Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(ii), \eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition} is the complement of $\Theta_{\xi}$ in the exactly transformed cutoff.

\emph{The conditional integrand.} With $\mathscr E_{\xi}$ the exponent of the second exponential of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}, written out in \eqref{eq:native-collar-full-exponent}, the conditional integrand of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-actual-functional}
    \begin{gathered}
    \mathcal K_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq\begin{cases}\exp\Bigl(\mathscr E_{\xi}\bigl(\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\bigr)+\log|\det D\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})|\Bigr),&\Theta_{\xi}(a)=1,\\[2pt] 0,&\Theta_{\xi}(a)=0,\end{cases}\\
    \mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f]\coloneqq\int f(a)\mathcal K_{\xi}(a)\,\dd a\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
the exponent being defined on the box by (B4) and Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}: by Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(ii) below, the integrand of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} in the variables of (1.22), with the cutoff (1.25) in its exact composed form, is $\kappa_{\xi}\,\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})\,\mathcal K_{\xi}(a)$, as used in \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} ($\mathscr E_{\xi}$ and $\kappa_{\xi}$ are the exponent and prefactor of \cite{BalabanCRE} as printed, with $\sigma$, $\sigma_0$ and $z^{(0)}$ for the fixed inner product as explained in the conventions).

The change-of-variables term, Ba{\l}aban's $V^{(0)}(S_1)$ (\cite[(1.24) and p.~252]{BalabanCRE}), is exact inside $\mathcal K_{\xi}$ and is a constant on the branch (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}).

\emph{The exterior interpolation.} Let $H= H_{\xi,II}$. For $t\in[0,1]$ the interpolated objects are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation}
    \begin{aligned}
        P_{\xi,t}(a)&\coloneqq\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near}}\mathfrak p(a+tA_{\mathrm e})\;,\qquad
        j_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq\langle a,H_{\xi,IJ}A_{\mathrm e}\rangle\;,\\
        K_{\xi;t}(a)&\coloneqq\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_I}(a)\exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\langle a,Ha\rangle-tj_{\xi}(a)+P_{\xi,t}(a)\right)\\
        &\qquad(\mathcal D_I\coloneqq\{ a\, | \,| a(b)|< r\ \forall b\in I\}\text{ the open box, }\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_I}=\Theta_{\xi}),\\
        I_{\xi;t}&\coloneqq\int K_{\xi;t}(a)\,\dd a,\qquad
        \dd\nu_{\xi;t}\coloneqq\frac{K_{\xi;t}}{I_{\xi;t}}\,\dd a\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
the sum running over the near primitives of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} (all three kinds). By Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} and Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}\,(i), each near primitive is defined and analytic in $(a,t)$ on the enlarged box at the inputs $a+tA_{\mathrm e}$, $t\in[0,1]$; $K_{\xi;t}$ (zero off the open box) is therefore bounded and Borel on $\mathfrak g^I$, positive on the open box, and $0< I_{\xi;t}<\infty$. On the open box $P_{\xi,0}(a)=\sum_Y\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)$ is the centred potential \eqref{eq:c-potential-definition}, and $K_{\xi;0}$ is the centred kernel of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}. This is the interpolation of \cite[(3.27)--(3.29)]{BalabanCRE} in the exterior field, restricted to the terms that depend on $a$.

The Wilson function and the centred coefficient are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convex-response-operands}
    f_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a)),\qquad F_{\xi}(t)\coloneqq\int f_{\xi}\,\dd\nu_{\xi;t}\;,
\end{equation}
with $U_{\xi}(a)$ the reconstructed fine field \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field} at the actual retained data, including the change of variables; it is not interpolated. By Lemmas~\ref{lem:charts} and~\ref{lem:row-locality}, $f_{\xi}$ is defined and analytic on the enlarged box: each contour link $U_{\xi}(a)(r)$ depends on $a$ only through $a|_{\mathcal F_r\cap I}$, through a row within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ when $\mathcal F_r$ meets $I$, and is constant in $a$ otherwise. Off the enlarged box $f_{\xi}$ is extended by zero, which affects no integral against $\nu_{\xi;t}$.

\begin{lemma}[The Collar]\label{lem:collar}
On every branch:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})(b)= A_{\mathrm e}(b)$ for every $b\in J$ with $d(b,I)\leqslant 2R_{\mathrm c}$; every near primitive and every entry of $H_{\xi,IJ}$ involves $A_{\mathrm e}$ only on such bonds, so $\mathfrak p(a+t\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e}))=\mathfrak p(a+tA_{\mathrm e})$ for near $\mathfrak p$ and $\langle a,H_{\xi,IJ}\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\rangle= j_{\xi}(a)$. For every row $c$ within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ the source phase on the bonds of $\mathcal E_c$ is, componentwise,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-collar-source-phase}
    \begin{aligned}
    q_U\bigl(\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\bigr)(b)&= q_U(a+A_{\mathrm e})(b)\\
    &=\bigl[g_0\mathsf C_U(a+A_{\mathrm e})-h_U\widetilde D_U\bigl(g_0\mathsf C_U(a+A_{\mathrm e})\bigr)\bigr](b)\qquad(b\in\mathcal E_c)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
\item With the branch constant
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-collar-boundary-constant}
    c_{\xi}=\mathscr E_{\xi}(0)-\frac12\langle\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e}),H_{\xi}\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\rangle+\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{far}}\mathfrak p\bigl(\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\bigr)+\log|\det D\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})|\;,
\end{equation}
where $\mathscr E_{\xi}(0)= v(0)$ and the far primitives are evaluated at the retained field alone,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-collar-identity}
    \mathcal K_{\xi}(a)= e^{c_{\xi}}K_{\xi;1}(a)\quad(a\in\mathfrak g^I),\qquad
    \mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f]= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}\int f\,\dd\nu_{\xi;1},\qquad
    \frac{\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]}{\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]}= F_{\xi}(1)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) By Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i), a bond within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ is not in $S_1^*$, where $\Psi_{\xi}$ is the identity. A near primitive has all its inputs within $4L+3\leqslant 2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ (Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}); an entry $(H_{\xi,IJ})_{bb'}$ with $b\in I$ vanishes unless $d(b,b')\leqslant \rho_L=4L<2R_{\mathrm c}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}), since $R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant 2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1=4L+5$.

The phase on a row $c$ within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ depends on the free vector on $\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}), and every bond of $\mathcal E_c$ is within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ by the definition of the row distance (Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}), so $\Psi_{\xi}$ is the identity on these bonds; on $\mathcal E_c$ only the row $c$ contributes to $h_U\widetilde D_U$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}), which gives \eqref{eq:native-collar-source-phase} as an identity between the $\mathcal E_c$-components.

(ii) Let $A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}\coloneqq\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\in\mathfrak g^J$, so that $\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})= a+A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}$ by \eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}. By Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum},
\begin{equation*}
    \mathscr E_{\xi}(a+A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e})=\mathscr E_{\xi}(0)-\frac12\langle a,Ha\rangle-\langle a,H_{\xi,IJ}A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}\rangle-\frac12\langle A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e},H_{\xi} A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}\rangle+\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near}}\mathfrak p(a+A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e})+\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{far}}\mathfrak p(A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e})\;,
\end{equation*}
where the far primitives do not depend on $a$ because their free-input sets miss $I$. By (i) the third term is $-j_{\xi}(a)$ and the near sum is $P_{\xi,1}(a)$. The Jacobian factor depends on $(a+A_{\mathrm e})|_{S_1^*}= A_{\mathrm e}|_{S_1^*}$ only.

The constant $c_{\xi}$ is finite: $\det D\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\neq0$ by (B4)(ii) (the differential of (1.22) is invertible on $\mathcal D_{\xi}$, and $D\Psi_{\xi}$ at $a+A_{\mathrm e}$ depends on $A_{\mathrm e}|_{S_1^*}$ only), and the far primitives are finite: their free-input sets miss $I$, so their values at $A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}$ are their values at $a_0+A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}=\Psi_{\xi}(a_0+A_{\mathrm e})\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$ for any $a_0$ with $(A_{\mathrm e},a_0)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ (a branch has one), where every row solution is defined and the primitives are finite by (B4).

Collecting the $a$-independent terms gives $\mathcal K_{\xi}= e^{c_{\xi}}K_{\xi;1}$, and the two remaining identities follow by integration, dividing by $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}>0$.
\end{proof}

The constant $c_{\xi}$ depends on the branch data (through $A_{\mathrm e}$, $U_1$, $V_0$, and $\Omega_1$) and enters the outer weight $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}$ of the branch in \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}; the history expectation \eqref{eq:c3-6-1} compares $\mathcal O[\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]\,F_{\xi}(1)]$ with $\mathcal O[\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]]$, the same nonnegative weight on both sides.

\begin{lemma}[Boundary Response]\label{lem:boundary-response}
For bounded Borel $f$ on $\mathfrak g^I$, with $\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu}(f,l)\coloneqq\int fl\,\dd\nu-\int f\,\dd\nu\int l\,\dd\nu$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-probe-boundary-functional}
    \int f\,\dd\nu_{\xi;1}=\int f\,\dd\nu_{\xi;0}+\mathcal B_{\xi}[f],\qquad
    \mathcal B_{\xi}[f]=\int_0^1\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f,-j_{\xi}+\partial_tP_{\xi,t})\,\dd t\;,
\end{equation}
where $\partial_tP_{\xi,t}(a)=\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near}}D\mathfrak p(a+tA_{\mathrm e})[A_{\mathrm e}]$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $a$ in the box the exponent $E_t(a)=-\frac12\langle a,Ha\rangle-tj_{\xi}(a)+P_{\xi,t}(a)$ is jointly analytic in $(a,t)$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline{\mathcal D_I}\times[0,1]$, since each near primitive is analytic in the free vector on its row polydiscs (Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}) and the input $a+tA_{\mathrm e}$ is affine in $(a,t)$ with values in those polydiscs; its $t$-derivative $-j_{\xi}(a)+\partial_tP_{\xi,t}(a)$, with $\partial_tP_{\xi,t}(a)=\sum_{\mathfrak p}D\mathfrak p(a+tA_{\mathrm e})[A_{\mathrm e}]$ the derivative in the direction $A_{\mathrm e}$, is continuous and hence bounded on $\overline{\mathcal D_I}\times[0,1]$.

Hence $t\mapsto\int fK_{\xi;t}\,\dd a$ and $t\mapsto I_{\xi;t}$ are $C^1$ with derivatives $\int f\,\partial_tE_t\,K_{\xi;t}\,\dd a$ and $\int\partial_tE_t\,K_{\xi;t}\,\dd a$ (differentiation under the integral over the bounded box, dominated by a constant times $K_{\xi;t}\leqslant e^{\sup| E_t|}$), so $F(t)=\int f\,\dd\nu_{\xi;t}$ has $F'(t)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f,\partial_tE_t)$, and integration over $[0,1]$ gives \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-boundary-functional}.
\end{proof}

By Lemmas~\ref{lem:collar} and~\ref{lem:boundary-response}, on every branch
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-exterior-response}
    \frac{\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]}{\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]}= F_{\xi}(1)= F_{\xi}(0)+\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]\;,
\end{equation}
the first term being the centred expectation of Section~\ref{sec:probe-kernels} and the second the exterior response, estimated in Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard}.

\begin{lemma}[Collar Coverage]\label{lem:collar-coverage}
Let $R_{\mathrm{loc}}\coloneqq 2L+2$, which exceeds the $\ell^{\infty}$ diameter $2L-1$ of every two-block set $\mathcal E_c$, hence of the sets $\mathcal E_y$, $\mathcal F_r$, $\mathcal A_r$ and of the free-input and background sets of the block, row, Haar and Jacobian primitives (those of a plaquette primitive have diameter at most $4L<2R_{\mathrm{loc}}$, proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}), and let $R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant 2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1$ be the collar range fixed in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} after \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-radius-replay}; it depends on $L$ and the group only.

Under \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}, which include $M\geqslant 8LM_2$ and $LMR_1>4R_{\mathrm c}+4L^2M_2R_1+8$, on every branch:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Every site within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $LMR_1-1$ of $\Lambda_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1'\subseteq R_1^c$; $I\subseteq\mathcal G_{\xi}\subseteq\Omega_1^*$; and every free bond $b$ of $\Omega_1$ with $d(b,I)\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$ lies in $\mathcal G_{\xi}\setminus S_1^*$.
\item The cutoff (1.25) composed with the change of variables, as a function of $A'= a+A_{\mathrm e}$, equals $\Theta_{\xi}(a)\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})$ with $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}$ of \eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition}, and $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}$ depends on $A_{\mathrm e}$ and the branch data only.
\item $| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|< r$ for every $b\in J$ with $d(b,I)\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$; that is,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convex-native-radius}
    r_{\mathrm e,\xi}=\max\bigl(\{| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|\, | \,b\in J,\ d(b,I)\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}\}\cup\{0\}\bigr)< r\;.
\end{equation}
\item For an admissible pair and a branch value of $A_{\mathrm e}$, $\{ a\in\mathfrak g^I:(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}\}=\{ a:\Theta_{\xi}(a)=1\}$, the open box of \eqref{eq:native-source-young-cutoff}.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) $\Omega_1$ and $R_1'$ are unions of $LMR_1$-cubes (\cite[(1.10), p.~251]{BalabanCRE}) and $\Lambda_1\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-2}\cap(R_1'^{\sim})^c$, so every site within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $LMR_1-1$ of $\Lambda_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1'\subseteq R_1^c$.

Let $b$ be a free bond of $\Omega_1$ with $d(b,I)\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$: its initial vertex is within $3R_{\mathrm c}+1$ of a site of $\Lambda_1$, so the cube $\square'$ of side $L^2M_2R_1$ containing it lies within $3R_{\mathrm c}+1+L^2M_2R_1< LMR_1-1$ of $\Lambda_1$ (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}), hence $\square'\subseteq R_1^c$ is a good cube; $b$ has an endpoint in $\square'\subseteq\square'^{\sim2}$ and is not designated, so $b\in(\square'^{\sim2})^*\subseteq\mathcal G_{\xi}$. By \eqref{eq:c-collar-distance}, $d(I,S_1^*)\geqslant LMR_1-2>3R_{\mathrm c}$, so $b\notin S_1^*$.

Taking $d(b,I)=0$ gives $I\subseteq\mathcal G_{\xi}$ (a bond of $\Lambda_1$ is a bond of $\Omega_1$, and a designated bond with an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$ belongs to a row of $\Lambda_1$ because $\Lambda_1$ is a union of blocks, so $I\subseteq\Omega_1^*$).

For $\mathcal G_{\xi}\subseteq\Omega_1^*$: a good cube $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ has $\square'^{\sim2}\subseteq\Omega_1$ since $2L^2M_2R_1< LMR_1$ ($M\geqslant 8LM_2$); a bond of $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$ has an endpoint in $\Omega_1$, and a designated bond with an endpoint in $\square'^{\sim2}$, a union of blocks, belongs to a row with an endpoint in $(\square'^{\sim2})^{(1)}$ and is excluded by the definition of $^*$ in (1.8).

(ii) The first two factors of (1.25) are $\prod_{b\in\mathcal G_{\xi}}\mathbf 1_{\{| A(b)|< r\}}$ at $A=\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})$. For $b\in I\subseteq\mathcal G_{\xi}$, $A(b)= a(b)$ by \eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}, giving $\Theta_{\xi}(a)$; for $b\in\mathcal G_{\xi}\setminus I=\mathcal G_{\xi}\cap J$ (by (i)), $A(b)=(\Psi_{\xi} A_{\mathrm e})(b)$, giving the first factor of \eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition}.

The factor $\chi^{(0)c}(R_1)$ involves $A$ on $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$ for cubes $\square'\subseteq R_1$, and $\chi_0'(S_1)$ involves the free links $e^{ig_0A(b)}U_1(b)$ on bonds $b\in(\square'^{\sim2})^*\cap\Omega_1^*$ for cubes $\square'\subseteq S_1$, together with $V_0$ on the bonds of $(\square'^{\sim2})^*$ with both endpoints off $\Omega_1$, $U_1$ and $U_{1,\square'}$. All these bonds have both endpoints within $2L^2M_2R_1+1$ of $R_1\cup S_1$, while every site of $\Lambda_1$ is at distance at least $LMR_1>2L^2M_2R_1+1$ from $R_1\cup S_1$; so none of them has an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$, none lies in $I$, and on them $A=\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$. Hence the last two factors of (1.25), composed with $\Psi_{\xi}$, are functions of $\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ and the branch data.

(iii) For $b\in J$ with $d(b,I)\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$, (i) gives $b\in\mathcal G_{\xi}\cap J$ and $b\notin S_1^*$, so $\mathbf 1_{\{|(\Psi_{\xi} A_{\mathrm e})(b)|< r\}}=\mathbf 1_{\{| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|< r\}}$ is a factor of $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})$, which is nonzero on a branch (the maximum over the empty set is read as $0$).

(iv) Let $a_0$ be such that $(A_{\mathrm e},a_0)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ (a branch), so $B_0=\Psi_{\xi}(a_0+A_{\mathrm e})\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$ and, by (ii), $\Theta_{\xi}(a_0)\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})\neq0$. Let $a$ be any point of the open box and $B=\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})= a+\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ (\eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}; $\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ is defined, since $B_0$ is).

The three conditions of \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain} hold at $B$. The cutoff (1.25) at $B$ is $\Theta_{\xi}(a)\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})=\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}(A_{\mathrm e})\neq0$, by (ii).

Every row equation has a solution at $g_0\mathsf C_UB$: on the near rows by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}, since $B= a+A_{\mathrm e}$ on their two-block sets by (i) and lies in the row polydiscs by (iii); on the far rows the argument $(g_0\mathsf C_UB)|_{\mathcal E_c}$ equals $(g_0\mathsf C_UB_0)|_{\mathcal E_c}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}: it involves $B$ only through $B|_{\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}$, and $\mathcal E_c$ misses $I$ for a far row, every bond of which is at distance more than $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L-(2L-1)>0$ from $I$), where the solution exists because $B_0\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$. So $U(B)$ is defined, and on the far rows and the bonds of $\Omega_1^c$ its links are those of $U(B_0)$.

Finally $U(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$. The restriction to $\Omega_1^c$ is $V_0$. The block averages are defined on every row of $\Omega_1$ and satisfy the constraint $\bar U= V$ there: $U(B)= e^{iq_U(B)}U_1$ with $q_U(B)= A-h_U\widetilde D_U(A)$, $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$, and on every row $c$ the row equation gives $\mathcal Q_{U,c}(q_U(B))= LQ_Uq_U(B)+\mathcal N_{U,c}(q_U(B))= LQ_U(A-h_U\widetilde D_U(A))+\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)=-\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)+\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)=0$, using $Q_U\mathsf C_U=0$ and $LQ_Uh_U=\id$; so $\mathsf M(U(B))(c)=\mathsf M(U_1)(c)= V(c)$ by \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation} and (B1). The constraint $\bar V_0= V$ on the rows of $\Omega_1^c$ involves $V_0$ and $V$ only and holds because the pair is admissible.

The tests of (1.11): $\chi_1(\Omega_1)$ is a function of $V$, $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ does not depend on $a$ (\eqref{eq:c-large-field-factor}), and both are nonzero at $U(B_0)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$. The factor $\chi_0'(\Omega_1)$ is the product of $\chi_0'(\square')$ over the $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1$ (\cite[(1.8)]{BalabanCRE}); the cubes of $S_1=(\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1})\cup R_1$ (\cite[(1.20)]{BalabanCRE}) give the factor $\chi_0'(S_1)$ of (1.25), nonzero at $B$ by the first condition, and every other cube $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1$, so it is a good cube with $\square'^{\sim4}\subseteq\Omega_1$ (as $4L^2M_2R_1< LMR_1$), and its factor $\chi_0'(\square')$ is the second factor of (1.19), equal to one at $B$ by (B3)(ii), the retained factors being nonzero there. Hence $U(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$, so $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$ and $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$.

Conversely $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ gives $\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, so the cutoff (1.25) is nonzero there, and $\Theta_{\xi}(a)=1$ by (ii).
\end{proof}

The exterior response has Ba{\l}aban's integration-by-parts form (\cite[(3.28)]{BalabanCRE}). Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-collar-mean-direction}
    \ell_{\xi}\coloneqq H_{\xi,IJ}A_{\mathrm e},\qquad m_{\xi}\coloneqq H_{\xi,II}^{-1}\ell_{\xi},\qquad D_{m_{\xi}}f(a)\coloneqq\frac{\dd}{\dd s}f(a+sm_{\xi})\Big|_{s=0}\;,
\end{equation}
let $\mathcal D_I$ be the open box of \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation}, with outward unit normal $n(a)$ and surface measure $\dd S$ for the Euclidean structure of $\langle\bigcdot ,\bigcdot \rangle$ on $\mathfrak g^I$ (for which $\dd a$ is Lebesgue measure), defined almost everywhere on its Lipschitz boundary (a product of balls of the norm $|\bigcdot |$), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-collar-flux}
    \mathsf Q_{\xi,t}(a)=-\frac{1}{2}\langle a,H_{\xi,II}a\rangle-t\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle+P_{\xi,t}(a),\quad
    \mathcal T_{\xi,t}[f]=\frac{1}{I_{\xi;t}}\int_{\partial\mathcal D_I}f(a)e^{\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}(a)}\langle m_{\xi},n(a)\rangle\,\dd S(a)\;,
\end{equation}
so that $K_{\xi;t}=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_I}e^{\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}}$ and $j_{\xi}(a)=\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle$.

\begin{lemma}[Integration by Parts with the Hard Cutoff]\label{lem:ibp}
Under the conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, $H_{\xi,II}$ is invertible and $m_{\xi}$ is defined. If $f$ is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline{\mathcal D_I}$, then for every $t\in[0,1]$, with expectations under $\nu_{\xi;t}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-collar-source-ibp}
    \operatorname{Cov}(f,-j_{\xi}+\partial_tP_{\xi,t})
        =-\mathbb E[D_{m_{\xi}}f]+\operatorname{Cov}(f,\partial_tP_{\xi,t}-D_{m_{\xi}}P_{\xi,t})+\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[f]-\mathbb E[f]\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[1]\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$e^{\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}}$ is $C^1$ on the enlarged box, a neighbourhood of $\overline{\mathcal D_I}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}. The divergence theorem on the bounded Lipschitz domain $\mathcal D_I$ gives $\int_{\mathcal D_I}D_{m_{\xi}}(fe^{\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}})\,\dd a= I_{\xi;t}\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[f]$, and $D_{m_{\xi}}\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}=-j_{\xi}-t\langle m_{\xi},\ell_{\xi}\rangle+D_{m_{\xi}}P_{\xi,t}$ because $\langle m_{\xi},H_{\xi,II}a\rangle=\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle= j_{\xi}(a)$. Dividing by $I_{\xi;t}$, $\mathbb E[D_{m_{\xi}}f]+\mathbb E[f(-j_{\xi}-t\langle m_{\xi},\ell_{\xi}\rangle+D_{m_{\xi}}P_{\xi,t})]=\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[f]$. Subtracting the same identity for $f=1$ multiplied by $\mathbb E[f]$ cancels the constant $-t\langle m_{\xi},\ell_{\xi}\rangle$, and the two covariances combine as stated.
\end{proof}

Since $f_{\xi}$ is analytic on the enlarged box (after \eqref{eq:convex-response-operands}), Lemma~\ref{lem:ibp} applies to $f_{\xi}$. The estimate of the right-hand side is Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} in Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard}.

\subsection{A Fixed Walk Expansion of the Centred Kernel}
\label{sec:fixed-first-kernel}

Let $H= H_{\xi,II}$ and $\mathsf G= H^{-1}$. Notation of Sections~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}--\ref{sec:joint-extraction}:
\begin{itemize}
\item $E_0= E(Z_0)$ denotes the seed bonds (the designated bonds $E_0$ of \eqref{eq:constraint-extension} do not occur here);
\item $N_i(Y)$ is a cube count (the measure $N_1$ of \eqref{eq:first-step} does not occur);
\item $\sigma_{\Delta}$ are weakening variables (the Haar density $\sigma$ does not occur);
\item $B$ is the conditioned variable on $\mathfrak g^{E_0}$ (the free vector $B$ of Sections~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}--\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar} does not occur);
\item $D$ without argument is a component;
\item $J_D$, $J_Z$ are sets of bonds of the integration carrier (the retained carrier $J$ does not occur);
\item $\delta_M$ is a decay constant (the Mayer constant $\delta$ of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} does not occur);
\item $\gamma=\gamma_L/2$ is a spectral bound (arcs $\gamma$ of the contour do not occur);
\item a connected final domain is any nonempty wall-connected union of $LM$-cubes;
\item $a_j$, $a_*$, $a_W$ are coefficients and weights, distinct from the integration variable $a$.
\end{itemize}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, on every branch
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-inputs}
    \gamma\id\leqslant H\leqslant h_+\id,\qquad\gamma=\frac{\gamma_L}{2},\quad h_+= m_L\;,
\end{equation}
and by Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}, whose entries $\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{U_1}(b,c)$ at $b,c\in I$ are those of $H$, $H(b,c)=0$ when $d_{\infty,T}(b_-,c_-)> R$, where $R\geqslant \max(\rho_L,2)$ is fixed so that $H(b,c)$ is determined by the background, by the region $\Omega_1$ and by membership in $I$ within distance $R$ of $b_-$.

Norms on $\mathfrak g^I$ are those of the invariant real inner product, with Hermitian extension on the complexification.

The constants $\gamma,h_+,R$ depend on $L$ and the group only (with the invariant inner product fixed in the conventions), and every choice below is made before the branch fields and the coupling, in the order $\gamma,h_+,R$; then $\kappa_1$; then $n_*,R_*,C_{\mathrm w}$; then $M_1$, $\rho_{\mathrm w}= R_*+R+1+2M_1$ and $M$; then $g_0$. None of $\gamma,h_+,R,\kappa_1,C_{\mathrm d}$ depends on $M_1$, $M$ or the coupling ($C_{\mathrm d}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment} is a function of $\gamma,h_+,d_G$).

An aligned auxiliary cubical partition of side $M_1$ in fine units is fixed, with cubes $M_1z+[-M_1/2,M_1/2]^4$; the $M$-cube partition $\pi_0$ and the $LM$-cube partition $\pi_1$ are nested over it, $M/M_1$ and $L$ are odd integers, every fine period is a multiple of $LMR_1$ and at least $8M$, and $M_1$ and $M$ are odd (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}: $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$ are powers of the odd number $L$), so that cube faces lie at half-integer coordinates and no lattice site lies on a face. Cubes and neighbourhoods are periodic images; all radii used below are smaller than $M$, so the periods $\geqslant 8M$ make every neighbourhood a lifted copy of its $\mathbb Z^4$ model.

Let $s_H\coloneqq 2h_+$, $\mathsf A_H=\id-H/s_H$, $q_H=1-\gamma/s_H<1$, and $V_n=4(2nR+3)^4$. A block of $\mathsf A_H^n$ vanishes beyond distance $nR$, has operator norm at most $q_H^n$ and depends only on coefficients within distance $(n+1)R$ of its first bond, so its block-norm row and column sums are at most $V_nq_H^n$.

Let $\kappa_1\geqslant 1$ be the constant fixed in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:mayer-constants} (\eqref{eq:c2-mayer-constants}; it depends on $L$ and the group only), the spatial Cauchy radius being $e^{\kappa_1}$; let $a_*\coloneqq e^{81\kappa_1}$, and let $n_*$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-grouping}
    \beta= V_{n_*}q_H^{n_*},\qquad a_*\beta\leqslant \frac{1}{4}\;.
\end{equation}
Let $R_*\coloneqq n_*R$, $\mathsf P_H=\mathsf A_H^{n_*}$, $V_*= V_{n_*}$, and $a_j=4^{-j}\binom{2j}{j}\in(0,1]$. The binomial series gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-square-root-series}
    \mathsf G^{1/2}= s_H^{-1/2}\sum_{r=0}^{n_*-1}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} a_{n_*m+r}\mathsf A_H^r\mathsf P_H^m\;.
\end{equation}
For a free bond $b$ let $D_b$ be the union of the $M_1$-cubes meeting the closed ball of radius $R_*+R+1$ about $b_-$, with one further $M_1$-layer; it is connected, lies in the ball of radius $\rho_{\mathrm w}= R_*+R+1+2M_1$ about $b_-$, and contains the bonds and coefficient stencils of every block starting at $b$ in \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-square-root-series} with an interior margin. The cube side satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-collar-size}
    M\geqslant 4(\rho_{\mathrm w}+R+R_*+2)\;.
\end{equation}
Then $2\rho_{\mathrm w}< M\leqslant LM$, so $D_b$ meets at most $2^4=16\leqslant 81$ cubes of $\pi_1$.

A walk is a tuple $\omega=(r;b_0,\ldots,b_{m+1})$ with nonzero block product
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-walk-block}
    (\mathsf A_H^r)_{b_0b_1}\prod_{j=1}^m(\mathsf P_H)_{b_jb_{j+1}}\;,
\end{equation}
and localisation domain $D(\omega)=\bigcup_{j\leqslant m}D_{b_j}$, which is connected and contains both endpoint bonds in its interior.

For an $M$-cube $Q$ let $Q^{\sim}$ be the union of the $3^4$ cubes of $\pi_0$ meeting $Q$, so that $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ is the open $\ell^{\infty}$ neighbourhood of radius $M$ of $Q$. For a union $Z_0$ of $M$-cubes (the seed, selected in Section~\ref{sec:selected-integrals}) let $\widetilde Z_0\coloneqq\bigcup_{Q\subseteq Z_0}Q^{\sim}$ be its one-$M$-layer enlargement and $Z_0'$ the union of the $LM$-cubes meeting $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ for some cube $Q$ of $Z_0$. Both are unions over the cubes of $Z_0$, so both commute with unions of seeds, and $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}\subseteq\operatorname{int}Z_0'$ for every cube $Q$ of $Z_0$, since every $LM$-cube incident to a point of the open set $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ meets it.

The cubes $\Delta\in\pi_1$ inside $Z_0'$ carry $\sigma_{\Delta}=1$, the others carry complex variables $\sigma_{\Delta}$, and the weight of a walk is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-walk-weakening}
    w_{\omega}(\sigma)\coloneqq\prod_{\Delta\in\pi_1,\ \Delta\not\subseteq Z_0',\ \Delta\cap D(\omega)\ne\varnothing}\sigma_{\Delta}\;.
\end{equation}
The weighted series is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-weighted-walk-series}
    \begin{gathered}
    S_{Z_0}(\sigma)_{b_0b_{m+1}}\coloneqq s_H^{-1/2}\sum_{r=0}^{n_*-1}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty} a_{n_*m+r}\sum_{b_1,\ldots,b_m}w_{\omega}(\sigma)\,(\mathsf A_H^r)_{b_0b_1}\prod_{j=1}^m(\mathsf P_H)_{b_jb_{j+1}},\\
    \omega\coloneqq(r;b_0,\ldots,b_{m+1})\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
the inner sum running over the intermediate bonds; $S_{Z_0}(1)=\mathsf G^{1/2}$ by \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-square-root-series}.

\begin{lemma}[The Walk Series]\label{lem:walk-series}
On $|\sigma_{\Delta}|\leqslant e^{\kappa_1}$, $| w_{\omega}(\sigma)|\leqslant a_*^{m+1}$, and the series $S_{Z_0}(\sigma)$ converges absolutely in both Schur norms, uniformly on the polydisc, with operator norm and absolute block row and column sums at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-schur-bound}
    C_{\mathrm w}= s_H^{-1/2}\frac{n_*V_*a_*}{1-a_*\beta}\;.
\end{equation}
It is holomorphic on the polydisc of radii $e^{\kappa_1+(\log2)/81}$. The bound is independent of $Z_0$, the volume and the number of its components.

Under a site gauge transformation $u$ of the background, $S_{Z_0}(\sigma)$ formed from $\iota_I^*\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{U_1^u}\iota_I$ in place of $H$ equals $R_{u,*}S_{Z_0}(\sigma)R_{u,*}^{-1}$, with $R_{u,*}$ restricted to $I$ and the same domains and weights.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$D(\omega)$ meets at most $81(m+1)$ cubes of $\pi_1$, which gives the weight bound. The unweakened grouped products have absolute block row and column sums at most $V_*\beta^m$ after summing the intermediate bonds, so the weighted series is dominated by $s_H^{-1/2}n_*V_*\sum_m(a_*\beta)^ma_*$. Increasing each radius by the factor $e^{(\log2)/81}$ multiplies $a_*$ by $2$ and keeps $a_*\beta\leqslant 1/2$. The gauge law is \eqref{eq:regular-gauge-constrained-hessian} restricted to $I$ (so $\mathsf A_H$ is conjugated by $R_{u,*}$) applied to each block; the weights and domains do not involve the background.
\end{proof}

Let $E_0\coloneqq E(Z_0)=\{ b\in I\, | \,b\cap Z_0\ne\varnothing\}$, let $\iota_{E_0}$ be extension by zero and $\Pi_{I\setminus E_0}$ the complementary orthogonal projection, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-C-Gamma}
    C_{E_0}\coloneqq(\iota_{E_0}^*H\iota_{E_0})^{-1},\qquad\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)\coloneqq\iota_{E_0}^*H\Pi_{I\setminus E_0}S_{Z_0}(\sigma)\;.
\end{equation}
Pairings $\langle\bigcdot ,\bigcdot \rangle$ involving complex vectors are the complex-bilinear extensions of the real pairing throughout.

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Conditioning]\label{lem:conditioning}
Let $\mu_0$ be the standard Gaussian measure on $\mathfrak g^I$ and $\mu_{C_{E_0}}$ the centred Gaussian measure on $\mathfrak g^{E_0}$ of covariance $C_{E_0}$. For bounded Borel $F$ on $\mathfrak g^{E_0}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-conditioning}
    \int F(a|_{E_0})\,\dd\mu_{\mathsf G}(a)=\int\left[\int F(B)\,e^{-\frac12\langle\Gamma_{E_0}(1)X,C_{E_0}\Gamma_{E_0}(1)X\rangle}e^{-\langle B,\Gamma_{E_0}(1)X\rangle}\,\dd\mu_{C_{E_0}}(B)\right]\dd\mu_0(X)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
With $a=\mathsf G^{1/2}X$, $a$ has law $\mu_{\mathsf G}$ when $X$ has law $\mu_0$. Given $a|_{I\setminus E_0}$, the conditional law of $a|_{E_0}$ under $\mu_{\mathsf G}$ is Gaussian with covariance $C_{E_0}$ and mean $-C_{E_0}\iota_{E_0}^*H\Pi_{I\setminus E_0}a=-C_{E_0}\Gamma_{E_0}(1)X$ (by completing the square in $\frac12\langle a,Ha\rangle$), and its density with respect to $\mu_{C_{E_0}}$ is the displayed factor. This is \cite[(2.5)--(2.6)]{BalabanRG2}.
\end{proof}

The weakened density is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-density}
    e^{-\frac{1}{2}\langle\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)X,C_{E_0}\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)X\rangle}e^{-\langle B,\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)X\rangle}\,\dd\mu_{C_{E_0}}(B)\,\dd\mu_0(X)\;.
\end{equation}
$C_{E_0}$ is real, positive and independent of $\sigma$; its determinant is one fixed positive number on the whole polydisc.

\begin{lemma}[Component Blocks]\label{lem:component-blocks}
Let $Z\supseteq Z_0'$ be a union of $LM$-cubes, with $\sigma_{\Delta}=0$ for $\Delta\not\subseteq Z$. For each wall-component $D$ of $Z$ let $J_D\coloneqq\{ b\in I\, | \,b\subset\operatorname{int}D\}$ and $E_D= E_0\cap J_D$. Then $E_0\subseteq\bigsqcup_DJ_D$, $E_D= E(Z_0\cap D)$, initial vertices in different $E_D$ have distance at least $2M-2> R$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-exact-blocks}
    C_{E_0}=\bigoplus_D(\iota_{E_D}^*H\iota_{E_D})^{-1},\qquad\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)=\bigoplus_D\Gamma_{E_D}(\sigma|_D)\;,
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma_{E_D}(\sigma|_D)$ is constructed from the seed $Z_0\cap D$ alone, with final domain $D$ (so $\sigma_{\Delta}=0$ for every cube $\Delta$ of $\pi_1$ not in $D$) and the same $I$, $H$ and background. Columns of $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)$ outside $\bigsqcup_DJ_D$ vanish, and $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)$ does not depend on $\sigma_{\Delta}$ for cubes $\Delta$ in a component containing no seed cube.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
A point is interior to a union of closed grid cubes exactly when all its incident cubes belong to it, and the incident family is wall connected (any two cubes containing a point are joined by a chain of cubes containing that point, consecutive ones sharing a wall); hence $\operatorname{int}Z=\bigsqcup_D\operatorname{int}D$, a disjoint union of open sets. For an $M$-cube $Q$ of $Z_0$ the open neighbourhood $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ is connected and lies in $\operatorname{int}Z_0'\subseteq\operatorname{int}Z$, so it lies in one component interior; neighbourhoods in different components are disjoint, so their seed cubes have distance at least $2M$, and a bond meeting a seed cube lies in the same component interior. This gives $E_0\subseteq\bigsqcup J_D$, $E_D= E(Z_0\cap D)$ and the separation, which by finite range makes $\iota_{E_0}^*H\iota_{E_0}$ block diagonal.

Let $(\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma))_{eb}=\sum_{b'}H_{eb'}(\Pi_{I\setminus E_0})_{b'b'}S_{Z_0}(\sigma)_{b'b}$ with $e\in E_D$ be an entry. A nonzero term has $d(e_-,b'_-)\leqslant R$; $e$ meets a seed cube $Q$, so $e_-$ is within $1$ of $Q$ and the open ball of radius $R+2$ about $e_-$ lies in the open $M$-neighbourhood $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ of $Q$, because $R+3\leqslant M$ by \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-collar-size}, hence in $\operatorname{int}D$; so $b'\subset\operatorname{int}D$.

A walk from $b'$ to $b$ with $w_{\omega}\ne0$ has every cube of $\pi_1$ meeting $D(\omega)$ inside $Z$, so $D(\omega)\subset\operatorname{int}Z$; $D(\omega)$ is connected and contains $b'$, so $D(\omega)\subset\operatorname{int}D$ and $b\in J_D$. Its coefficients, domains and weakening variables are independent of the seed; the cubes with $\sigma_{\Delta}=1$ inside $D$ are those of $Z_0'\cap D=(Z_0\cap D)'$ ($Z_0'$ is the union over the seed cubes $Q$ of the $LM$-cubes meeting $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$; such a cube meets $\operatorname{int}Z$ at a point whose incident $LM$-cubes all lie in $Z$ and form a wall-connected family, so it lies in the component containing $Q$); and $\Pi_{I\setminus E_0}$ agrees with $\Pi_{I\setminus E_D}$ on $J_D$. This gives the block decomposition and the vanishing of the columns outside $\bigsqcup J_D$.

Finally, a walk contributing to a row $e\in E_D$ has $D(\omega)\subset\operatorname{int}D$, so its weight involves only $\sigma_{\Delta}$ with $\Delta\subseteq D$; a component without seed cube has no row at all.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian Payment]\label{lem:gaussian-payment}
Let $N_M\coloneqq\lfloor M/(2R_*)\rfloor$, $\delta_M=2C_{\mathrm w}4^{-N_M}$ and $A_*= h_+(\gamma^{-1/2}+1)$; by \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}, $\delta_M\leqslant 1$ and $h_+^2\delta_M^2/\gamma\leqslant 1/8$. $\pi_i(X)$ denotes the set of $\pi_i$-cubes of a union $X$ of such cubes. On every branch, for every seed $Z_0$, every union $Z\supseteq Z_0'$ of $LM$-cubes with $\sigma_{\Delta}=0$ for $\Delta\not\subseteq Z$, and every $\sigma$ in the closed polydisc $\{|\sigma_{\Delta}|\leqslant e^{\kappa_1}\ \forall\Delta\in\pi_1(Z)\setminus\pi_1(Z_0')\}$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\|\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)-\Gamma_{E_0}(1)\|\leqslant h_+\delta_M$ and $\| C_{E_0}^{1/2}(\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)-\Gamma_{E_0}(1))\|\leqslant h_+\gamma^{-1/2}\delta_M$, in the operator norms for the Hilbert norms on $\mathfrak g^I_{\mathbb C}$ and $\mathfrak g^{E_0}_{\mathbb C}$.
\item For $0\leqslant \alpha_G\leqslant \min(\gamma/2,\gamma^2/(16A_*^2))$ and $J_Z=\bigsqcup_DJ_D$, the integral of the absolute value of \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-density} against $e^{\alpha_G\| B\|^2/2}$ is at most $\exp(C_{\mathrm d}(\alpha_G+\delta_M^2)| J_Z|)$, $C_{\mathrm d}= C_{\mathrm d}(\gamma,h_+,d_G)$; with $4C_{\mathrm d}\delta_M^2(LM+1)^4\leqslant 1/2$ (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}) and $\alpha_G\leqslant (8C_{\mathrm d}(LM+1)^4)^{-1}$ this is at most $e^{N_1(Z)}$, and the integral of the absolute value factors over the components $D$ of $Z$ (the signed density factors by Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks}).
\item For $0<\gamma_2$ and the constant $c_{\mathrm n}>0$ of the group with $h(X)^2\geqslant c_{\mathrm n}| X|^2$ on $\mathfrak g$, $\prod_{b\in\mathsf P}\mathbf 1_{\{| B_b|\geqslant r\}}\leqslant e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}|\mathsf P|}\exp(\frac{\gamma_2}{2}\sum_{b\in\mathsf P}h(B_b)^2)$ with $a_{\mathrm{bad}}\coloneqq c_{\mathrm n}\gamma_2r^2/2$, for every $\mathsf P\subseteq E_0$ (a pointwise inequality, used in the appendix with $\gamma_2\leqslant \alpha_G$).
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

The proof is in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:fixed-kernel-payment}.

\subsection{The Selected Integrals and the Polymer Representation}
\label{sec:selected-integrals}

Connectivity of cubes is wall connectivity (\cite{BalabanRG1}, before (0.24)); two domains are compatible when they share neither a cube nor a wall (\cite[(2.11)]{BalabanRG2}); $N_i(Y)$ is the number of $\pi_i$-cubes of $Y$, $d_i(Y)$ its tree length (\cite[p.~257]{BalabanRG1}, written out in \eqref{eq:c2-tree-length}) and $\ell_i(Y)= d_i(Y)+5$.

The localisation family $\mathbf D_0$ consists of the potential hosts \eqref{eq:part1-potential-host} and the probe hosts \eqref{eq:c-probe-host} below; all are connected unions of $M$-cubes.

A potential family indexed by $\mathbf D_0$ is a collection $\{\mathbf W(Y,\bigcdot )\}_{Y\in\mathbf D_0}$ of Borel functions $\mathfrak g^I\to\mathbb C$, each depending on $a$ only through $a|_{E(Y)}$, $E(Y)=\{ b\in I\, | \,b\cap Y\ne\varnothing\}$, and bounded on the local box $\{| a_b|< r\ \forall b\in E(Y)\}$; only the values on the local boxes enter below, because every selected host $Y$ comes with the factors $\chi_b$, $b\in E(Y)\subseteq E(Y_0)$. The potential $\mathbf V_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:c-potential-definition} is such a family; $\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,\bigcdot )=0$ on hosts carrying no near primitive.

\begin{definition}[Selections and Selected Integrals]\label{def:selection}
A selection is a triple $\mathfrak s=(\mathcal D,\mathsf P,Z)$: a finite $\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbf D_0$, a finite $\mathsf P\subseteq I\setminus E(Y_0)$ where $Y_0\coloneqq\bigcup_{Y\in\mathcal D}Y$, and a final domain $Z$. Its seed is $Z_0= Y_0\cup\bigcup\{ Q\in\pi_0\, | \,Q\cap b\ne\varnothing\text{ for some }b\in\mathsf P\}$, with $E_0= E(Z_0)$ and $Z_0'$ as in Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}, and a final domain is a union $Z\supseteq Z_0'$ of $LM$-cubes.

The selected integral of a bounded Borel $F$ on $\mathfrak g^{E_0}$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-selected-integral}
    \begin{aligned}
    \mathcal A^{\mathrm f}_{\mathfrak s}[F]
        &\coloneqq\prod_{\Delta\in\pi_1(Z)\setminus\pi_1(Z_0')}\int_0^1\dd s_{\Delta}\oint_{|\sigma_{\Delta}|= e^{\kappa_1}}\frac{\dd\sigma_{\Delta}}{2\pi i(\sigma_{\Delta}-s_{\Delta})^2}\\
        &\quad\cdot\prod_{Y\in\mathcal D}\int_0^1\dd t_Y\int\dd\mu_0(X)\int\dd\mu_{C_{E_0}}(B)\\
        &\quad\cdot e^{-\frac12\langle\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)X,C_{E_0}\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)X\rangle}e^{-\langle B,\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)X\rangle}
          (-1)^{|\mathsf P|}\\
        &\quad\cdot\prod_{b\in E(Y_0)}\chi_b(B)\prod_{b\in\mathsf P}(1-\chi_b(B))
          \prod_{Y\in\mathcal D}\mathbf W(Y,B)e^{t_Y\mathbf W(Y,B)}\,F(B)\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
with $\chi_b(B)\coloneqq\mathbf 1_{\{| B_b|< r\}}$ in the bond norm of \cite{BalabanCRE} (the indicator of \eqref{eq:native-source-young-cutoff}) and $\sigma_{\Delta}\coloneqq 0$ for $\Delta\not\subseteq Z$.

The vacuum activity of a connected final domain $Z$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-vacuum-activity}
    k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(Z)\coloneqq\sum_{(\mathcal D,\mathsf P)\, | \,Z_0\ne\varnothing,\ Z_0'\subseteq Z}\mathcal A^{\mathrm f}_{(\mathcal D,\mathsf P,Z)}[1]\;,
\end{equation}
and $\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}\coloneqq\sum_{\mathcal P\text{ compatible}}\prod_{Z\in\mathcal P}k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(Z)$ (empty family included), $(\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})^{[Y]}$ the same sum over families compatible with $Y$.
\end{definition}

The selected integral is finite: the integrand is holomorphic in $\sigma$ on the polydisc of Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-series} for fixed $(X,B,t)$, its absolute value is integrable in $(X,B)$ uniformly on the closed polydisc by Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii) together with the boundedness of $F$ and of each $\mathbf W(Y,\bigcdot )$ on its local box (enforced by the factors $\chi_b$, $b\in E(Y_0)$), and the contours have positive distance from $[0,1]$.

Every selected datum depends only on $B$, since $E(Y)\subseteq E_0$ for $Y\in\mathcal D$ and $\mathsf P\subseteq E_0$. A fine bond meets at most two $M$-cubes (no site lies on a face), so at most $2|\mathsf P|$ cubes of the seed are not cubes of $Y_0$.

The seed of a union of selections (disjoint host families and bad-bond sets) is the union of the seeds, and $\widetilde Z_0$, $Z_0'$ are unions over the seed cubes (Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}), so all three commute with unions.

\begin{lemma}[Polymer Representation]\label{lem:polymer}
Let $\mathbf W$ be a potential family indexed by $\mathbf D_0$ and $\mathfrak n_{\xi}=(2\pi)^{d_G| I|/2}\det(H)^{-1/2}$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-polymer}
    \int\Theta_{\xi}(a)\exp\Bigl(-\frac12\langle a,Ha\rangle+\sum_{Y\in\mathbf D_0}\mathbf W(Y,a)\Bigr)\dd a=\mathfrak n_{\xi}\,\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}[\mathbf W]\;,
\end{equation}
with the activities of Definition~\ref{def:selection} formed from $\mathbf W$, and the sum $\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}[\mathbf W]$ is finite (finitely many selections at fixed volume). In particular, for $\mathbf W=\mathbf V_{\xi}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-source-numerator}
    I_{\xi;0}=\mathfrak n_{\xi}\,\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}\;,\qquad\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}=\frac{I_{\xi;0}}{\mathfrak n_{\xi}}>0\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The left side is $\mathfrak n_{\xi}\int\Theta_{\xi} e^{\sum_Y\mathbf W(Y,\bigcdot )}\dd\mu_{\mathsf G}$. The expansion of each $e^{\mathbf W(Y)}=1+\int_0^1\mathbf W(Y)e^{t_Y\mathbf W(Y)}\dd t_Y$ gives the sum over $\mathcal D$. With $\Theta_{\xi}=\prod_{E(Y_0)}\chi_b\prod_{I\setminus E(Y_0)}(1-(1-\chi_b))$, the expansion of the second product gives the sum over $\mathsf P$ with the sign $(-1)^{|\mathsf P|}$. The remaining integrand depends on $a|_{E_0}$ only (each $\mathbf W(Y,\bigcdot )$, $Y\in\mathcal D$, through $a|_{E(Y)}$ with $E(Y)\subseteq E_0$, and it is evaluated on the local box of $Y$ because of the factors $\chi_b$, $b\in E(Y_0)$), so Lemma~\ref{lem:conditioning} applies and produces \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-density} at $\sigma=1$.

For fixed $(X,B,t)$ the density \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-density} is holomorphic in $\sigma$ on the polydisc (Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-series}); for each $\Delta\in\pi_1$ not in $Z_0'$ its value at $\sigma_{\Delta}=1$ is the value at $\sigma_{\Delta}=0$ plus $\int_0^1\partial_{s_{\Delta}}\dd s_{\Delta}$. Expanding the product over these cubes, labelling each term by $Z= Z_0'\cup\{\text{differentiated cubes}\}$, and representing each derivative by its Cauchy integral along $|\sigma_{\Delta}|= e^{\kappa_1}$ gives pointwise identities in $(X,B,t)$; the resulting parameter integrals may be taken outside the Gaussian integrals by Fubini, since the absolute value of the density is integrable uniformly on the polydisc (Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii)) and the other factors are bounded. This is \eqref{eq:c-selected-integral}.

Every cube of $Z_0'$ is wall-connected inside $Z_0'$ to a cube containing a seed cube: a cube $\Delta$ of $Z_0'$ meets $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ for a seed cube $Q$ at a point $x$; since $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ is open, $x$ may be taken in the interior of $\Delta$, so $x$ lies in an $M$-cube $Q'\subseteq Q^{\sim}\cap\Delta$, and $Q'$ is joined to $Q$ by a chain of face-adjacent $M$-cubes of $Q^{\sim}$, whose $LM$-cubes start with $\Delta$, are consecutively equal or wall adjacent, and all belong to $Z_0'$ (each contains an $M$-cube of $Q^{\sim}$, whose interior lies in $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$). Hence a wall-component of $Z$ either contains a seed cube or consists of differentiated cubes only; in the second case $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)$ does not depend on its $\sigma$-variables (Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks}), the Cauchy integral of a function constant in $\sigma_{\Delta}$ vanishes, and the term is zero. So only final domains all of whose components contain a seed cube contribute.

For these, Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks} factors the density and the Gaussian measures over the components $D$ of $Z$ ($\mu_{C_{E_0}}=\bigotimes_D\mu_{C_{E_D}}$ and the density is a product by the block decomposition; the $X$-integral factors because each block of $\Gamma_{E_0}$ reads $X$ on $J_D$ only, and the remaining Gaussian factor of $\mu_0$ integrates to one), and the parameter integrals are indexed by cubes and hosts, each inside one component. The cutoff, potential and sign factors factor because each selected host is a connected union of $M$-cubes inside $Z_0$, hence inside one component, and each bad bond lies in the component containing its (at most two, face-adjacent) incident cubes.

Given $Z$ with components $D_1,\ldots,D_m$, the map $(\mathcal D,\mathsf P)\mapsto((\mathcal D_j,\mathsf P_j))_j$, with $\mathcal D_j$ the hosts inside $D_j$ and $\mathsf P_j$ the bad bonds inside $D_j$, is a bijection from the selections with final domain $Z$ (all $Z_0'\subseteq Z$, every component seeded) onto the tuples of selections $(\mathcal D_j,\mathsf P_j,D_j)$ with nonempty seeds and final domains $D_j$: the inverse is the union, because the seed rule, the enlargement and the coarse cover commute with unions and $(Z_0\cap D_j)'\subseteq D_j$ (it is wall-connected to its seed inside $Z_0'\subseteq Z$). Summing over $Z$ gives the compatible-family sum, in which the empty selection contributes $\int\dd\mu_{\mathsf G}=1$.

Equation \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-source-numerator} is the case $\mathbf W=\mathbf V_{\xi}$: $K_{\xi;0}=\Theta_{\xi}\exp(-\frac12\langle a,Ha\rangle+\sum_Y\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a))$ by \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation} and \eqref{eq:c-potential-definition} (on the open box $\sum_Y\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)= P_{\xi,0}(a)$), and positivity holds because $K_{\xi;0}>0$ on the open box.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Activity Bounds]\label{lem:activity-bounds}
With the constants $\lambda_*,\varepsilon_*>0$ and $\theta\geqslant 0$ of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:mayer-constants} (fixed there before the coupling together with its auxiliary constants $\kappa,\delta,\alpha_6,\omega_*$, independently of $M_1$ and $M$), and $g_0$ below its threshold, for $\mathbf W=\mathbf V_{\xi}$ on every branch and every connected final domain $Z$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-raw-activity-payment}
    | k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(Z)|\leqslant \varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda_*\ell_1(Z)},\qquad
    \sum_{Z'\not\sim Z}| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(Z')| e^{(1+6\theta)N_1(Z')}\leqslant \frac{1}{8}N_1(Z)\;,
\end{equation}
where $Z'$ ranges over the connected final domains and $Z'\not\sim Z$ means incompatible (a domain is incompatible with itself). The same holds for the reference data of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}).
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Vacuum Clusters]\label{lem:vacuum-clusters}
Under Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds}, for an ordered tuple $\mathfrak c=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)$, $m\geqslant 1$, of connected final domains with Ursell coefficient $\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)=\sum_{\mathcal G}(-1)^{|\mathcal G|}$, the sum over the connected spanning subgraphs $\mathcal G$ of the incompatibility graph on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ ($j\ne j'$ joined when $D_j\not\sim D_{j'}$; a domain is incompatible with itself, so repeated domains are joined; $\varphi^T=1$ for $m=1$), let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-vacuum-cluster}
    \Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)\coloneqq\frac{\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)}{m!}\prod_{j=1}^mk^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D_j)\;.
\end{equation}
For every finite set $\mathcal A$ of connected final domains,
\[
    \sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}|\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)| e^{2\theta\sum_jN_1(D_j)}\leqslant \frac18\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\;,
\]
where $\mathfrak c$ hits $\mathcal A$ when some $D_j$ is incompatible with a member of $\mathcal A$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-joint-vacuum-exponential}
    \frac{(\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})^{[\cup\mathcal A]}}{\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}}=\exp\Bigl(-\sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)\Bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

The proof, including the identity \eqref{eq:part1-joint-vacuum-exponential}, is in Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, Section~\ref{app:kp}, by the Kotecký--Preiss criterion with the pinned-tree bound.

\subsection{Probe Kernels and the Centred Expectation}
\label{sec:probe-kernels}

For each $b\in I$ let $\mathcal R_b=\{ r\text{ a bond of }\Omega_1\, | \,b\in\mathcal F_r\}$ be its forward influence set (the bonds whose reconstructed link depends on $a(b)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}); it lies within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2L+1$ of $b$. The set $\{ b\}\cup\mathcal R_b$ is lifted to $\mathbb Z^4$ about $b_-$ (its diameter is below every period), and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-probe-host}
    \begin{aligned}
    Y_b=\pi_T\bigl(&\text{the smallest rectangle of $M$-cubes containing the one-fine-layer}\\
    &\text{neighbourhood of the lift, with one $M$-layer adjoined}\bigr)\;;
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
the lift together with its one-fine-layer neighbourhood has $\ell^{\infty}$ extent at most $2(2L+1)+3=4L+5< M$ in every direction ($M\geqslant 8LM_2\geqslant 8L^2$), so it meets at most two $M$-cubes per direction and the rectangle has side at most $4$ cubes, of length $4M<8M$, so $\pi_T$ is injective on it. $Y_b$ is a connected member of $\mathbf D_0$, contains $b$ and $\mathcal R_b$ in its interior, and $N_0(Y_b)\leqslant 4^4\leqslant s_{\mathrm p}=5^4$.

For a union $R$ of $LM$-cubes its eligible labels are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:probe-eligible-carrier}
    \mathsf L_R\coloneqq\{ b\in I\, | \,Y_b\subseteq R\}\;,
\end{equation}
and $\overline{\mathcal D}_{\mathsf L}$ is the closed box $| a_b|\leqslant r$, $b\in\mathsf L$, in $\mathfrak g^{\mathsf L}$. Each $Y_b$ is a nonempty wall-connected union of $M$-cubes, so $Y_b\subseteq R$ places it inside exactly one wall-component of $R$; hence $\mathsf L_R$ is the disjoint union of the $\mathsf L_D$ over the components $D$ of $R$.

For $\lambda\in\mathfrak g^I_{\mathbb C}$, with the complex bilinear extension of the real pairing, the probe family is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:probe-combined-potential}
    L_Y(\lambda,a)\coloneqq\sum_{b\, | \,Y_b= Y}\langle\lambda_b,a_b\rangle,\qquad\widetilde{\mathbf V}_{\xi,\lambda}(Y,a)\coloneqq\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)+L_Y(\lambda,a)\;,
\end{equation}
a potential family indexed by $\mathbf D_0$ for each $\lambda$ (both terms depend on $a|_{E(Y)}$ only, since $Y_b= Y$ gives $b\in E(Y)$, and both are bounded on the local box of $Y$), entire in $\lambda$. Its partition function is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:probe-partition}
    \mathscr Z^{\mathrm c}_{\xi}(\lambda)\coloneqq\int e^{\sum_{b\in I}\langle\lambda_b,a_b\rangle}K_{\xi;0}(a)\,\dd a=\mathfrak n_{\xi}\sum_{\mathcal P\text{ compatible}}\prod_{D\in\mathcal P}k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(\lambda)\;,
\end{equation}
by Lemma~\ref{lem:polymer} applied to $\widetilde{\mathbf V}_{\xi,\lambda}$, where $k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(\lambda)$ denotes the activity formed from that family; it is entire in $\lambda$ (a finite sum of integrals of entire functions of $\lambda$ with integrable majorants on compact sets of $\lambda$) and $k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(0)= k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)$.

\begin{lemma}[Probe Measures]\label{lem:probe-measures}
On every branch, for every connected final domain $D$ there is a finite complex Borel measure $\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}$ on $\overline{\mathcal D}_{\mathsf L_D}$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:probe-Laplace-identity}
    k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(\lambda)=\int e^{\sum_{b\in\mathsf L_D}\langle\lambda_b,a_b\rangle}\,\dd\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(a)\quad(\lambda\in\mathfrak g^{I}_{\mathbb C}),\qquad
    \nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(\overline{\mathcal D}_{\mathsf L_D})= k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)\;;
\end{equation}
in particular $k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(\lambda)$ depends on $\lambda$ only through $\lambda|_{\mathsf L_D}$.

Explicitly, splitting each probe label from its host's ordinary label, a selection becomes $\ell=(\mathcal D,\mathsf J,\mathsf P,Z)$ with $\mathsf J\subseteq\mathsf L_Z$ the selected probes, $Y_0=\bigcup_{Y\in\mathcal D}Y\cup\bigcup_{b\in\mathsf J}Y_b$, and seed, $E_0$ and $Z_0'$ formed from this $Y_0$ and $\mathsf P$; the Mayer variable of a probe integrates exactly,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:probe-selected-factor}
    \int_0^1\langle\lambda_b,B_b\rangle e^{t_b\langle\lambda_b,B_b\rangle}\,\dd t_b= e^{\langle\lambda_b,B_b\rangle}-1\;,
\end{equation}
and with $\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell}$ the complex measure on $\mathfrak g^{E_0}$ defined by the right side of \eqref{eq:c-selected-integral} for $\mathbf W=\mathbf V_{\xi}$, with $Y_0$, $Z_0$, $E_0$, $Z_0'$ the enlarged data of $\ell$ throughout (the factors $\chi_b$ over $E(Y_0)$, the conditional law and the weakening over this seed), with the Mayer factors $\int_0^1\dd t_Y\,\mathbf W(Y,B)e^{t_Y\mathbf W(Y,B)}$ for $Y\in\mathcal D$ only and no probe factor,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:probe-selection-measure}
    \nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}=\sum_{\ell\, | \,Z= D,\ Z_0\ne\varnothing}\int\Bigl[\bigotimes_{b\in\mathsf J}(\delta_{B_b}-\delta_0)\otimes\bigotimes_{b\in\mathsf L_D\setminus\mathsf J}\delta_0\Bigr]\,\dd\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell}(B)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At a host $Y$ carrying the ordinary potential $\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)$ and the probe terms $F_b=\langle\lambda_b,\bigcdot \rangle$, $b$ with $Y_b= Y$, $e^{\widetilde{\mathbf V}_{\xi,\lambda}(Y)}= e^{\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)}\prod_be^{F_b}=\prod_{\ell'}(1+(e^{F_{\ell'}}-1))$ over the labels $\ell'$ of $Y$ (the ordinary label with $F_{\ell'}=\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)$ and one label per probe); the sum over nonempty label subsets $A$ of $\prod_{\ell'\in A}(e^{F_{\ell'}}-1)$ equals $e^{\widetilde{\mathbf V}_{\xi,\lambda}(Y)}-1$. Every term with $A\ne\varnothing$ has the same active host $Y$, so the split-label expansion has the same $Y_0$, $\mathsf P$, seed, cover and kernel as the one-potential-per-host expansion of Lemma~\ref{lem:polymer}, and the two activities agree term by term after the Mayer variables $t_b$ of the probes are integrated by \eqref{eq:probe-selected-factor}.

The Laplace transform of $\delta_{B_b}-\delta_0$ in the variable $\lambda_b$ is $e^{\langle\lambda_b,B_b\rangle}-1$, and an unselected label contributes the factor one, the transform of $\delta_0$; this proves \eqref{eq:probe-Laplace-identity} for the measure \eqref{eq:probe-selection-measure}.

Each $\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell}$ is a finite complex measure: it is the image under $(X,B,s,\sigma,t)\mapsto B$ of a complex density whose absolute value is integrable by Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii) and the boundedness of each $\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,\bigcdot )$ on its local box, the Cauchy kernels and the cutoff factors; the Dirac tensor has total variation at most $2^{|\mathsf J|}$, and there are finitely many $\ell$ at fixed volume. The support lies in the closed box because $\chi_b(B)$, $b\in E(Y_0)\supseteq\mathsf J$, forces $| B_b|< r$ on the selected probes.

At $\lambda=0$ every term with $\mathsf J\ne\varnothing$ has zero mass, so $\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(\overline{\mathcal D}_{\mathsf L_D})= k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(0)= k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)$.
\end{proof}

For a compatible family $\mathcal P$ let $\mathsf e_{\mathcal P}$ embed $\prod_{D\in\mathcal P}\mathfrak g^{\mathsf L_D}$ into $\mathfrak g^I$ by zero on the remaining labels (the $\mathsf L_D$ are pairwise disjoint).

\begin{lemma}[Measure Identity]\label{lem:measure-identity}
On every branch,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-probe-measure}
    \frac{K_{\xi;0}(a)\,\dd a}{\mathfrak n_{\xi}}=\sum_{\mathcal P\text{ compatible}}(\mathsf e_{\mathcal P})_*\bigotimes_{D\in\mathcal P}\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Both sides are finite complex measures with compact support (finitely many families at fixed volume), and by \eqref{eq:probe-partition} and \eqref{eq:probe-Laplace-identity} they have the same Laplace transform on $\mathfrak g^I_{\mathbb C}$; restricted to imaginary $\lambda$ this is the Fourier transform, which determines a finite measure.
\end{proof}

Let $\delta_{0,\mathsf L_D}$ be the Dirac mass at $0\in\mathfrak g^{\mathsf L_D}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-probe-zero-mass}
    \widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}=\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}-k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)\delta_{0,\mathsf L_D}\;,
\end{equation}
a measure of zero mass (the subtracted term is the sum of the selections with $\mathsf J=\varnothing$). For a nonempty compatible family $\mathcal A$ and bounded Borel $f$ on $\mathfrak g^I$ let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-probe-active-pairing}
    \mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)\coloneqq\int f(\mathsf e_{\mathcal A}a)\,\dd\Bigl(\bigotimes_{D\in\mathcal A}\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}\Bigr)(a),\qquad
    q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)\coloneqq\frac{(\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})^{[\cup\mathcal A]}}{\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}}\;.
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}[Centred Expectation]\label{prop:centred-expectation}
On every branch, for bounded Borel $f$ on $\mathfrak g^I$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-probe-centred-source}
    \int f\,\dd\nu_{\xi;0}=\frac{\int f(a)K_{\xi;0}(a)\,\dd a}{I_{\xi;0}}= f(0)+\sum_{\varnothing\ne\mathcal A\text{ compatible}}q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)\;,
\end{equation}
and, with Lemmas~\ref{lem:collar} and~\ref{lem:boundary-response},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-physical-numerator}
    \mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f]= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}\Bigl[f(0)+\sum_{\varnothing\ne\mathcal A\text{ compatible}}q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)+\mathcal B_{\xi}[f]\Bigr]\;.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$f$ is integrated against \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-measure}, with each $\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}$ expanded as $\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}+k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)\delta_{0,\mathsf L_D}$. A term is indexed by $\mathcal P$ and the subfamily $\mathcal A\subseteq\mathcal P$ carrying the zero-mass factors; $f(\mathsf e_{\mathcal P}a)$ with $a=0$ on the labels of $\mathcal P\setminus\mathcal A$ is $f(\mathsf e_{\mathcal A}a)$. Summing over $\mathcal P\supseteq\mathcal A$ gives $(\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})^{[\cup\mathcal A]}\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)$, and $\mathcal A=\varnothing$ gives $\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi} f(0)$; division by $I_{\xi;0}=\mathfrak n_{\xi}\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}$ gives \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-centred-source}. The second display is $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f]= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}\int f\,\dd\nu_{\xi;1}$ \eqref{eq:c-collar-identity} with \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-boundary-functional}.
\end{proof}

With $f= f_{\xi}$ (extended by zero off the enlarged box; the measures live on the closed box, inside the enlarged box, where $f_{\xi}$ is the Wilson function \eqref{eq:convex-response-operands}), the first display is $F_{\xi}(0)$, and \eqref{eq:c-physical-numerator} is the exact decomposition of the conditional Wilson numerator on every branch: the loop at $a=0$, the sum of closed insertions paired with the signed probe measures, and the exterior response.

\subsection{Joint Extraction of the Scalar Reference}
\label{sec:joint-extraction}

Let $r_n$ be the positive representative of traversal $n\in\{1,\ldots,n_C\}$ of $C$, the traversals numbered cyclically from a fixed base point. For a contour bond $r$ that is not a bond of $\Omega_1$ let $\mathcal F_r\coloneqq\varnothing$: its link is $V_0(r)$ by \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field}, independent of $a$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality} and this convention, the link $U_{\xi}(a)(r_n)$ depends on $a$ only through $a|_{\mathcal F_{r_n}\cap I}$.

For a connected final domain $D$ the contact set is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-contact-set}
    \mathsf T_D\coloneqq\{ n\, | \,\mathcal F_{r_n}\cap\mathsf L_D\ne\varnothing\}\;,
\end{equation}
and $D$ is marked when $\mathsf T_D\ne\varnothing$.

If a family $\mathcal A$ contains an unmarked domain $D$, then for $a$ in the closed box $f_{\xi}(\mathsf e_{\mathcal A}a)= W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(\mathsf e_{\mathcal A}a))$ does not depend on $a|_{\mathsf L_D}$ (every contour link depends on $a|_{\mathcal F_{r_n}\cap I}$, and $\mathcal F_{r_n}\cap\mathsf L_D=\varnothing$ for every $n$), and $\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f_{\xi})=0$ because $\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}$ has zero mass and the measures are supported in the closed box; so only families of marked domains contribute to \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-centred-source} for $f= f_{\xi}$.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c-cluster-expansion}
    q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)=\sum_{k\geqslant 0}\frac{(-1)^k}{k!}\sum_{\mathfrak c_1,\ldots,\mathfrak c_k\text{ each hits }\mathcal A}\prod_{j=1}^k\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c_j)\;,
\end{equation}
the sum being absolutely convergent: $\sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}|\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)|\leqslant \frac18\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}, so the $k$-fold sums are dominated by the exponential series.

A tuple whose incompatibility graph is disconnected has $\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)=0$ (it has no connected spanning subgraph), so the terms containing such a tuple vanish, and every cluster occurrence $\mathfrak c_j$ below has a connected incompatibility graph.

The graph of a term has as vertices the marked domains of $\mathcal A$ and the $k$ cluster occurrences: a marked vertex is joined to each cluster that hits it, two clusters are joined when some constituent domains are incompatible. Every component has a marked root; its contacts are the union of the contact sets of its roots.

The hull of a nonempty set of traversals is its shortest cyclic interval when that interval has fewer than $n_C/2$ positions, and the whole contour otherwise; a shortest interval of fewer than $n_C/2$ positions is unique (two such intervals containing the set have together fewer than $n_C$ positions, so they intersect in a cyclic interval, which contains the set and is shorter than one of them unless they coincide), and if $S\subseteq S'$ and the hull of $S'$ is short then the hull of $S$ is contained in it (the hull of $S'$ is a short interval containing $S$, so the hull of $S$ is short and, by the uniqueness just proved, is the shortest interval containing $S$; the intersection of the two short hulls is again an interval, their union having fewer than $n_C$ positions, and it contains $S$, so it is the hull of $S$).

Let $\approx$ be the transitive closure of the relation ``the hulls of the contacts intersect'' on the components, and for a class $K$ let $\mathcal H(K)$ be the hull of the union of the contacts of its members.

If the union of the members' hulls has fewer than $n_C/2$ positions, $\mathcal H(K)$ equals that union: the union is a cyclic interval (the members' hulls are chained by intersections, and two intersecting intervals with together fewer than $n_C$ positions have an interval union), it contains the union of the contacts, so it contains the hull $\mathcal H(K)$ by minimality; conversely each member's contacts lie in the union of the contacts, whose hull is short, so by monotonicity each member's hull lies in $\mathcal H(K)$. If the union of the members' hulls has at least $n_C/2$ positions, $\mathcal H(K)$ is the whole contour: a short $\mathcal H(K)$ would contain every member's hull by monotonicity.

The groups are the classes if every $\mathcal H(K)$ is short, and the single class of all components otherwise; the intervals of distinct groups are disjoint, since intersecting intervals would relate their classes.

\begin{definition}[Groups]\label{def:groups}
A group $W$ consists of its nonempty compatible marked-root set $\mathcal A(W)$, its ordered list of cluster occurrences $(\mathfrak c_1,\ldots,\mathfrak c_{k(W)})$, $k(W)\geqslant 0$, each hitting a root of $W$, and its interval $\mathcal H(W)$, either a cyclic interval of fewer than $n_C/2$ traversals or the whole contour read from the base point; the data arise from a term of \eqref{eq:c-cluster-expansion} as above; conversely, the term of \eqref{eq:c-cluster-expansion} with root family $\mathcal A(W)$ and cluster list $(\mathfrak c_1,\ldots,\mathfrak c_{k(W)})$ has $W$ as its only group (its graph has the components of $W$, which form one class with the interval $\mathcal H(W)$).

Its weight is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-group-weight}
    w_{\xi}(W)\coloneqq\frac{(-1)^{k(W)}}{k(W)!}\prod_{j=1}^{k(W)}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c_j)\;.
\end{equation}

Two groups are compatible when all their constituent domains (roots and cluster members) are mutually compatible and their intervals are disjoint; a family containing a whole-contour group is a singleton. For a compatible group family $\mathfrak B$ and $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathfrak B$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-closed-family-pairing}
    \mathcal A(\mathcal S)\coloneqq\bigcup_{W\in\mathcal S}\mathcal A(W),\qquad
    A_{\xi}(\mathcal S)\coloneqq\Bigl(\prod_{W\in\mathcal S}w_{\xi}(W)\Bigr)\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A(\mathcal S);f_{\xi}),\qquad A_{\xi}(\varnothing)\coloneqq f_{\xi}(0)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Grouped Source]\label{lem:grouped-source}
On every branch,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-grouped-source}
    F_{\xi}(0)=\sum_{\mathfrak B\text{ compatible}}A_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)\;,
\end{equation}
an absolutely convergent sum over compatible group families (including the empty family; there are finitely many root families at fixed volume but infinitely many cluster lists).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
