Thus the Cauchy factors multiplying \eqref{eq:marginal-density-majorant} are uniformly bounded for that shape. The differentiated density is analytic, and hence continuous, in its covariance entries on a common accretive neighbourhood. This gives pointwise convergence as well as the stated integrable majorant, including when a covariance edge tends to zero. It follows that $\epsilon_{n,R}(T)\to 0$ at fixed $n,R$.

The omitted clusters, including any winding clusters, have total allocated weight at most $Cn\tau^2e^{-\eta R}$ in each sum. Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-fixed-square-limit-bound}
    \left|\log\frac{N_{C_n,T}}{D_T}
        -\widehat F_{\square}(n)\right|
        \leqslant Cn\tau^2e^{-\eta R}+\epsilon_{n,R}(T)\;.
\end{equation}
Here the finite-torus logarithm is the connected expansion of the ratio, on its branch continued from zero source; the vacuum subtraction and original denominator are unchanged. First taking $T\to\infty$ at fixed $n,R$ and then $R\to\infty$ proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-fixed-square-limit}
    F_{\square,\infty}(n)
        =\widehat F_{\square}(n)
        =\lim_{T\to\infty}\log\frac{N_{C_n,T}}{D_T}\;.
\end{equation}
Thus the infinite connected sum and the bulk-limit logarithm used below are the same object.

The four incoming/outgoing pairs of the counterclockwise square are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-square-pairs}
    \mathscr C_{\square}\coloneqq
        \{(e_1,e_2),(e_2,-e_1),(-e_1,-e_2),(-e_2,e_1)\}\;.
\end{equation}
On the branch of $F_{\square,\infty}(n)$ continued from zero source, the same closed-cluster allocation now gives positive constants $C,c$, independent of $n$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound}
    \left| F_{\square,\infty}(n)
        -n\sum_{v\in \mathscr V_{\square}}\kappa_v
        -\sum_{(v,w)\in \mathscr C_{\square}}\zeta_{v,w}\right|
        \leqslant C\tau^2(n+1)e^{-cn}\;.
\end{equation}
In the proof of this estimate every square cluster is allocated over its source segments by $| J_{\Gamma}|^{-1}$, and each side is divided into the segments nearest its initial corner and those nearest its terminal corner, a midpoint tie being broken consistently. A corner then receives the last $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ incoming segments and the first $n-\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ outgoing segments, and it is translated to the coarse origin. At the base corner $(-e_2,e_1)$, trace cyclicity first puts the incoming factors before the outgoing factors, as in the cyclic reassembly after \eqref{eq:marginal-exact-gases}.

For a root in its assigned half-sides, every cluster of extent less than $c_1n-C_1$ is identical to the corresponding bent-path cluster: all marked traversals and their stencils stay away from the other three corners, cyclic intervals become the ordinary local intervals, and the same global Gaussian principal marginals and vacuum labels occur. Any failure of this identification costs extent at least $c_1n-C_1$ and hence at most $C\tau^2e^{-c_2n}$ per root by \eqref{eq:marginal-cluster-tail} and \eqref{eq:corner-bent-tail}. There are $4n$ roots. Extending the four truncated rooted differences to all $j\in\mathbb Z$ costs another $C\tau^2e^{-c_3n}$ by \eqref{eq:corner-localisation-bound}. This proves \eqref{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound}, after enlarging constants for the finitely many short squares.

Here $c_1= L/(4C_{\mathrm{net}})$ and $C_1=2R_*/C_{\mathrm{net}}$ (a cluster rooted in its assigned half-sides and reaching within $R_*$ of another corner has network length at least $nL/2-2R_*$, and the bent-path network constant is at most $2C_{\mathrm{net}}$), $c_2=\eta'c_1$ and $c_3= c/2$ with the $c$ of \eqref{eq:corner-localisation-bound} (the extension runs over $| j|\geqslant n/2$), the factors $e^{\eta'C_1}$ and the like being absorbed in $C$.

With the cutoff index restored, the square corner matching factor is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-square-factor}
    \boxed{\displaystyle
        z_{\mathrm c}^{\sigma}\!\left(g_0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
            \coloneqq\exp\left(\frac{1}{4}
                \sum_{(v,w)\in \mathscr C_{\square}}
                    \zeta_{v,w}^{\sigma}(g_0)\right)}\;.
\end{equation}
This definition fixes the fourth-root branch by the exponential of the convergent corner logarithm. It is the geometric mean of the four oriented corner factors; if the reference construction preserves the corresponding rotations, they agree and \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor} is their common value.

For a real-valued character all the real Gaussian integrals, cluster weights and corner logarithms above are real, so these factors are positive.

For each fixed $n$, the inner limit in the following expression is the limit over compatible tori with their shortest period tending to infinity. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-ratio-limit}
    \boxed{\displaystyle
        \log z_{\mathrm c}^{\sigma}\!\left(g_0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
            =\frac{1}{4}\lim_{n\to\infty}
                \left(\lim_{T\to\infty}
                    \log\frac{N_{C_n,T}^{\sigma}}{D_T^{\sigma}}
                    +4nL\varepsilon\delta m^{\sigma}\right)}\;.
\end{equation}
The denominator is the original vacuum integral throughout the inner limit, whose existence is \eqref{eq:corner-fixed-square-limit}. The outer limit follows from \eqref{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound} and \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}. The order of limits is part of this reference prescription.

Equivalently, with $\mathcal W_{\infty}^{\circ,\sigma}(C_n)=\lim_{T\to\infty}N_{C_n,T}^{\sigma}/D_T^{\sigma}$, there is an error $E_n^{\sigma}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:corner-reference-matching}
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathcal W_{\infty}^{\circ,\sigma}(C_n)
            &= e^{-4nL\varepsilon\delta m^{\sigma}}
                \left(z_{\mathrm c}^{\sigma}
                    \!\left(g_0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)^4
                e^{E_n^{\sigma}}\;,\\
        | E_n^{\sigma}|&\leqslant C\tau^2(n+1)e^{-cn}\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The corner coefficient uses the same flat integral and cutoff prescription as the perimeter coefficient. Its identification in a conditional regular region, with boundary and periodic errors, is Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}.


\section{Identification in a Regular Integration Region}
\label{sec:regional-identification}

The coefficient in \eqref{eq:marginal-full-perimeter} was computed with the translation-invariant flat covariance. A conditional integration in the first RG step instead uses the inverse of a restricted Hessian. The two connected expansions are compared with the action terms that cross the integration boundary retained; this identifies their straight-side coefficients quantitatively.

\subsection{The Wilson Source before the Flat Evaluation}

Let $\mathcal I_C$ be the ordered set of traversals of $C$. For $R\subseteq\mathcal I_C$, the mixed field $U^R$ uses the integration link $U(b)= U'(b)U_1(b)$ on a traversal in $R$ and the background link $U_1(b)$ on every other traversal. Here $U_1= U_1(\Omega_1,V)$ is the reconstruction before the boundary split (with the exterior determining field retained). Reversed traversals use inverse links. Define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-wilson-polynomial}
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathcal G_S(U,U_1)
            &=\sum_{R\subseteq S}(-1)^{| S|-| R|}
                \chi(\Hol_{U^R}C)\;,\\
        \mathcal W(t;U,U_1)
            &=\sum_{S\subseteq\mathcal I_C}
                \left(\prod_{a\in S}t_a\right)\mathcal G_S(U,U_1)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $t=(t_a)_{a\in\mathcal I_C}$ is a family of scalar parameters. Boolean inversion gives
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal W(1;U,U_1)= W_{\chi}(C;U),
    \qquad \mathcal W(0;U,U_1)= W_{\chi}(C;U_1)\;.
\end{equation}
Every term is a closed contraction, invariant under simultaneous gauge transformations of $U$ and $U_1$.

The Wilson insertion starts in \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator}. Its gauge invariance preserves it under the Faddeev--Popov insertion in \cite[(1.5)--(1.6)]{BalabanCRE}. It is then pulled back under $U= U'U_1$ and the constraint linearisation leading to (1.14). At that stage the polynomial \eqref{eq:regional-wilson-polynomial} is introduced; its value at $t=1$ is the pulled-back Wilson insertion. All subsequent changes of variables are applied to every fluctuating link in this polynomial, including the boundary change (1.22).

Let $\xi$ denote the domain labels, the coarse field, the exterior fine field, and the exterior free fluctuation field in this construction. $K_{\xi}(t)$ is the conditional fluctuation integral in \cite[(1.26)]{BalabanCRE}, with the pulled-back polynomial inserted and the change-of-variables density from (1.22)--(1.24) retained once. The same integral with insertion $1$ is $K_{\xi,\mathrm{vac}}$. These definitions precede the separation of the effective interaction into its regular and boundary terms. The exterior integrations and their prefactors are those of (1.15), (1.25) and (1.29).

The flat projection of this conditional kernel sets its coarse and exterior determining fields to the identity and its exterior free fluctuation field to zero. The domain labels are held fixed. This evaluation is applied to $K_{\xi}$, not to the exterior indicators or history weights.

At the projection point $\mathcal W(0)=1$, so the source logarithm is continued from $K_{\xi}(0)= K_{\xi,\mathrm{vac}}$.

\subsection{Regional Integrals and Their Connected Densities}

Fine-lattice units are used; $H=\mathsf H_{\infty}$ is \eqref{eq:bulk-operator-definition}, and $C_{\infty}= H^{-1}$. For a finite set $D\subset E_{*,\infty}$, let $i_D$ extend a free field by zero, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-precision}
    H_D\coloneqq i_D^*Hi_D,
    \qquad C_D\coloneqq H_D^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}
The inverse exists by \eqref{eq:bulk-uniform-gap}.

Let $\mathcal V_D$ consist of the primitive labels from \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} whose supports meet $D$. They keep their original labels, and $v_D(B)= v(i_DB)$. Every primitive missing $D$ vanishes at this field. The cutoff and interaction are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-weight}
    \Theta_D^{\sigma}(B)\coloneqq\prod_{b\in D}\mathbf1_{\{| B_b|_{\sigma}< r\}},
    \qquad P_D(B)\coloneqq\sum_{v\in\mathcal V_D}v(i_DB)\;.
\end{equation}
The threshold is the same $r= r_0(g_0)$ as in \eqref{eq:marginal-two-cutoffs}.

Let $I$ be an interval of $m$ coarse segments on a coarse translate of the oriented line $v\in\mathscr V_{\square}$. Let $P_U(I)$ denote the ordered transport along its fine traversals. Its closed relative source uses the inverse reference transport, as in \eqref{eq:marginal-line-source}. The regional numerator and denominator are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-integrals}
    \begin{aligned}
        N_{D,I}^{\sigma}
            &\coloneqq\int\Theta_D^{\sigma}(B)e^{P_D(B)}
                \chi\bigl(P_{U_{g_0}(i_DB)}(I)P_{U_0}(I)^{-1}\bigr)
                    \,\dd\mu_{C_D}(B)\;,\\
        D_D^{\sigma}
            &\coloneqq\int\Theta_D^{\sigma}(B)e^{P_D(B)}
                    \,\dd\mu_{C_D}(B)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $U_0=\id$ in the chosen frame; retaining its reverse transport specifies the gauge-invariant closed contraction.

The protected-label forest expansion and the web construction of Section~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} apply with every free-input support $\Lambda$ replaced by $\Lambda\cap D$. A source mark with empty restricted stencil is zero. The other labels keep their original identities. The connected weights are $\Phi_{D,I}(\Gamma)$, with marked coarse-segment set $J_{\Gamma}$. The density assigned to segment $j$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-density}
    \kappa_{D,I}(j)\coloneqq
        \sum_{\Gamma\, | \,j\in J_{\Gamma}}
            \frac{\Phi_{D,I}(\Gamma)}{| J_{\Gamma}|}\;.
\end{equation}
The prescription $\sigma$, fixed throughout each comparison, is suppressed in these weights and densities.

For positive bonds $b=(x,i)$ and $c=(y,k)$, the distance is $d(b,c)=\| x-y\|_{\infty}+\mathbf1_{\{ i\ne k\}}$. Let $R_*$ bound the label diameters and source-to-stencil distances, and let $R_H$ be the range of $H$ in this metric. With the interval constant $c_h$ of \eqref{eq:marginal-hull-extent}, let
\begin{equation}
    R_0\coloneqq 4(1+R_*+R_H+L),
    \qquad c_{\mathrm{reg}}\coloneqq 16(1+R_*+c_h+L)\;.
\end{equation}
The coarse segments of $I$ are numbered $0,\ldots,m-1$. Let $K_j$ be the union of their fine-traversal input stencils on segment $j$, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-distance}
    d_j\coloneqq\max\bigl(0,
        \min\bigl(d(K_j,D^c),L\min(j,m-1-j)\bigr)-R_0\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:regional-coefficient}
For either fixed cutoff prescription $\sigma$, and for sufficiently small $g_0$ after the constants in the comparison have been chosen, there are constants $C,c>0$, independent of $D$, $I$ and $j$, such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-coefficient-bound}
    |\kappa_{D,I}(j)-\kappa_v|
        \leqslant C\tau^2e^{-cd_j}\;.
\end{equation}
Here $\tau$ is defined in \eqref{eq:marginal-fixed-forest-bound} and $\kappa_v$ in \eqref{eq:marginal-full-perimeter}. If every $K_j$ is at distance at least $b$ from $D^c$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-summed-bound}
    \left|\log\frac{N_{D,I}^{\sigma}}{D_D^{\sigma}}-m\kappa_v^{\sigma}\right|
        \leqslant C\tau^2(1+me^{-cb})\;.
\end{equation}
The logarithm is continued from zero source.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Principal restriction preserves $\gamma_L I\leqslant H_D\leqslant h_L I$. The finite-range Neumann series in \eqref{eq:bulk-neumann-inverse} therefore gives exponential decay for $C_D$, uniformly in the shape of $D$. Projecting $HC_{\infty}= I$ onto the $D$ rows gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-resolvent}
    C_D-(C_{\infty})_{D,D}
        = C_DH_{D,D^c}(C_{\infty})_{D^c,D}\;.
\end{equation}
Let $\mu>0$ be a common inverse-decay exponent in the fine-bond metric. A term on the right joins $u\in D$ and $w\in D^c$ with $d(u,w)\leqslant R_H$. For $s= d(b,u)+d(w,c)$,
\begin{equation}
    d(b,D^c)+d(c,D^c)+d(b,c)\leqslant 2s+2R_H\;.
\end{equation}
Half of $e^{-\mu s}$ pays this distance with exponent $a=\mu/4$; the remaining half is summable over $u$ and its bounded number of neighbours $w$. Polynomial volume growth gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-covariance-difference}
    \| C_D(b,c)-C_{\infty}(b,c)\|
        \leqslant C e^{-a(d(b,D^c)+d(c,D^c)+d(b,c))}\;.
\end{equation}
On $D$, let $C_t$ interpolate between $(C_{\infty})_{D,D}$ and $C_D$, and let $\mathcal D$ be their difference. Every interpolated covariance and each of its principal marginals has spectrum in $[h_L^{-1},\gamma_L^{-1}]$, uniform exponential decay and scalar colour blocks. Thus the protected-source bounds and the Schur cancellation used in \eqref{eq:marginal-fixed-forest-bound} hold throughout the interpolation.

For a forest term on carrier $A$ with interpolated covariance $M_t= C_t\circ w^F$, and with $E_e(C_t)$ the off-diagonal direction associated with edge $e$, the density derivative has the product-rule decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-density-derivative}
    \begin{aligned}
        \partial_t D^{| F|}p_{M_t}[(E_e(C_t))_{e\in F}]
            &= D^{| F|+1}p_{M_t}
                [\mathcal D_A\circ w^F,(E_e(C_t))_{e\in F}]\\
            &\quad+\sum_{e\in F}D^{| F|}p_{M_t}
                [E_e(\mathcal D),(E_f(C_t))_{f\in F\setminus\{ e\}}]\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Each tuple lists the directions of the symmetric multilinear derivative of the density with respect to its covariance.

The two kinds of terms use separate Cauchy estimates. In the first, the direction $s(\mathcal D_A\circ w^F)$ is added to the covariance centre and every forest direction is fixed. The positive Schur mask contracts operator norm. With $\lambda= h_L^{-1}$, the radius $\lambda/(32\|\mathcal D_A\|)$ uses at most $\lambda/32$ of the accretivity margin; a zero direction gives zero derivative. The forest radii are reduced by a fixed factor so that the total stays below $\lambda/8$.

In the second kind of term, one forest direction is replaced by $E_e(\mathcal D)$, which is bounded by \eqref{eq:regional-covariance-difference}. Its radius is chosen from the exponential entry majorant, without dividing by an entry of $C_t$. The normalised density, including its determinant, is bounded by \eqref{eq:marginal-density-majorant}.

Since $\|\mathcal D_A\|\leqslant C| A| e^{-a d(A,D^c)}$, the integrated differentiated term is bounded by the positive forest majorant, with enlarged constants and reduced edge decay, times
\begin{equation}
    C| A|^2e^{-a d(A,D^c)}\;.
\end{equation}
The exponent of $\tau$ is unchanged. In particular the differentiated functional is still equivariant under constant conjugation, so a component with one source mark retains its quadratic character gain.

For each component $\gamma$, let $u_{\gamma}$ be its positive fixed-forest bound with the uniform exponential entry majorants. This definition applies to vacuum and source components. For a web $W$, let $u_W\coloneqq\prod_{\gamma\in W}u_{\gamma}$; summing these numbers over webs gives the web load.

The positive majorants themselves satisfy the polymer loads. Restricting a support to $D$ preserves its size bound $s_*$, overlap bound $q_*$ and range $R_*$. On $n$ bonds, label choices cost at most $2^{q_*n}$, the forest-to-graph multiplicity costs at most $2^{q_*(s_*-1)n/2}$, unused graph edges at most $e^{V_1n/2}$, and the rooted spatial tree sum at most $n^{n-2}V_1^{n-1}/(n-1)!$, where $V_1$ is the finite row sum of the reduced-decay graph weights. Thus a constant $K_2\geqslant 1$ bounds the vacuum and source root loads by
\begin{equation}
    \sum_{n\geqslant 1}K_2^n\tau^{\lceil n/s_*\rceil},
    \qquad
    \sum_{n\geqslant 1}K_2^n\tau^{\max(2,\lceil n/s_*\rceil)}\;.
\end{equation}
Grouping $n$ into intervals of $s_*$ gives bounds $C\tau/(1-K_2^{s_*}\tau)$ and $C\tau^2/(1-K_2^{s_*}\tau)$, respectively. These sums bound the positive forest majorants before any signed activity is used. The interval-tree recursion then bounds the web loads.

Let $\mu_1>0$ be an exponent remaining after the degree payment, no greater than $\min(\mu,a)/8$, and let
\begin{equation}
    \alpha_*\coloneqq\frac{\mu_1}{1024(1+c_h)},
    \qquad \eta_1\coloneqq\frac{\mu_1}{1024}\;.
\end{equation}
The same sums allow the reserve $e^{4| A|+8\alpha_*H+8\eta_1\ell}$. Let $C_{\mathrm{load}}$ bound their weighted spatial and interval root loads after division by $\tau$ and $\tau^2$, respectively. The coupling $g_0$ satisfies $C_{\mathrm{load}}\tau\leqslant 1/4$ and $C_{\mathrm{load}}\tau^2\leqslant \alpha_*/4$. The incompatibility sum is then bounded by one quarter of $| A_p|+\alpha_*H_p$, so the pinned tree bound applies to the positive majorants $u_p$.

For a cluster $\Gamma$, let $U(\Gamma)$ be its absolute Ursell coefficient, including its factorial, multiplied by the product of these majorants. The product rule, counting repeated activity occurrences, yields
\begin{equation}
    |\partial_t\Phi_t(\Gamma)|
        \leqslant C\ell(\Gamma)^2
            e^{-a d(A_{\Gamma},D^c)}U(\Gamma),
    \qquad
    \sum_{\Gamma\, | \,j\in J_{\Gamma}}
        U(\Gamma)e^{\eta_1\ell(\Gamma)}\leqslant C\tau^2\;.
\end{equation}
The union of carriers is $A_{\Gamma}$. The inequality follows from $\sum_p\ell(p)^2\leqslant \ell(\Gamma)^2$ and the positive-majorant KP bound. Half the extent weight absorbs the polynomial factor.

A component's carrier is connected by its forest and at most $| A| -1$ stencil edges, each of length at most $R_*$, and its contour interval is attached at one selected mark by a path of length at most $R_*$. The interval costs at most $c_h\ell$. Carrier or interval incompatibility joins these networks for a connected cluster. Their total length is at most $(1+2R_*+c_h)\ell(\Gamma)$; adding the root segment costs at most $L$. The chosen $c_{\mathrm{reg}}$ bounds the result.

For $d_j\leqslant 2(R_0+R_*+c_{\mathrm{reg}})$, the rooted bounds prove the comparison after enlarging $C$.

For larger $d_j$, clusters with $\ell(\Gamma)\geqslant d_j/(2c_{\mathrm{reg}})$ are bounded by the extent tail in each gas. Every shorter cluster rooted at $j$ lies away from both the integration boundary and the ends of $I$. Its original stencils lie inside $D$, so its labels, closed sources, local functions and incompatibilities coincide in the two expansions. Only its covariance changes, and every carrier is at distance at least $d_j/2-R_0$ from $D^c$. The fixed loss is absorbed in the comparison constant. Integrating the differentiated bound gives \eqref{eq:regional-coefficient-bound}. Division by $| J_{\Gamma}|$ cannot enlarge it.

Finally, allocation and the endpoint geometric series give
\begin{equation}
    \log\frac{N_{D,I}^{\sigma}}{D_D^{\sigma}}
        =\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\kappa_{D,I}(j),
    \qquad
    \sum_{j=0}^{m-1}e^{-cd_j}\leqslant C(1+me^{-cb})\;,
\end{equation}
which proves \eqref{eq:regional-summed-bound}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Periodic Regions and Ba{\l}aban's Kernel}

Let $E_{*,T}$ be the periodic free carrier, $H_T$ the Hessian in \eqref{eq:flat-covariance}, and $i_{D,T}$ zero extension from $D\subseteq E_{*,T}$. The periodic primitives, written $v_T$ collectively (the terms $v_{\alpha}$, $j_b$ and $d_c$ of \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} on $T$, all three kinds), and the reconstructed links $U_{g_0,T}$ of \eqref{eq:flat-phase} on $T$ are those of Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-periodic-weight}
    H_{D,T}\coloneqq i_{D,T}^*H_Ti_{D,T},
    \qquad C_{D,T}\coloneqq H_{D,T}^{-1},
    \qquad P_{D,T}(B)\coloneqq
        \sum_{v_T\, | \,\operatorname{supp}v_T\cap D\ne\varnothing}
            v_T(i_{D,T}B)\;.
\end{equation}
The primitives of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} at the reference background $U=\id$ (written $p_{\xi,\alpha}$, $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}$, $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}$ as there, with the reference background in place of the branch data) and the local terms of \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} are the same functions, label by label.

\begin{definition}[The Identity Background]\label{def:identity-background}
The identity background is $U=\id$ on the torus $T$ with region $\Omega= T$ (Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}), so that every row $c\in T^{[1]}$ and every centre $y\in T^{(1)}$ occurs. $|\bigcdot |$ is the cutoff norm (so $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |$, the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}), $\|\bigcdot \|$ the Hilbert norm of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}, and $\| A\|_{\infty}\coloneqq\max_bh(A_b)$ the phase norm, in which $a_{\mathrm{ph}}$ and the chart radius $a_L$ of Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt} are measured. The row solutions, the phase $q_{\id}$, and the primitives $p_{\xi,\alpha}$, $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}$, $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}$ at the background $\id$ are those given by the formulas of Sections~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils} and~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} with $\Omega= T$ and $U=\id$, the row solution of every row $c$ being the unique small solution $\varphi_c$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii), which applies to every row of the identity background (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:identity-primitives}(i)).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Primitives at the Identity Background]\label{lem:identity-primitives}
At the identity background, let $B\in\mathfrak g^{E_*}$ be real with $g_0C_{\mathsf C}\max_b| B(b)|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ and $g_0\max_b| B(b)|< a_L$, with $C_{\mathsf C}$, $\vartheta_*$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal Q_{\id}=\mathcal Q$, $Q_{\id}= Q$, $\mathcal N_{\id}=\mathcal N$ \eqref{eq:constraint-primitive}, $\mathsf C_{\id}=\mathsf C$ and $h_{\id}(c)= L^3\id$ for every row \eqref{eq:constraint-extension}; every row solution $\widetilde D_{\id,c}(g_0\mathsf CB)$ is defined, is the unique small solution of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii), and equals the row $c$ of $\widetilde D(g_0\mathsf CB)$ of \eqref{eq:flat-phase}; hence $q_{\id}(B)= q_{g_0}(B)$.
\item $p_{\xi,p}(B)= v_p(B)$ for every plaquette $p$, and $p_{\xi,y}(B)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y\setminus\{ y\}}v_{(y,x)}(B)$ for every centre $y$.
\item $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)= j_b(B)$ for every bond $b$.
\item $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)= d_c(B)$ for every row $c$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently $\sum_{\alpha} p_{\xi,\alpha}(B)+\sum_bp^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)+\sum_cp^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)=\mathcal P_{g_0}(B)$ \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-sum}; and for every bond set $D\subseteq E_*$ and every real $B\in\mathfrak g^D$ with $g_0C_{\mathsf C}\max_b| B(b)|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ and $g_0\max_b| B(b)|< a_L$, the sum of the primitives whose free-input sets meet $D$, evaluated at $i_{D,T}B$, equals $P_{D,T}(B)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) At $U=\id$ every transport is $\id$, so $\beta_c(\id)=0$ and $\mathsf M(\id)(c)= P_c(\id)=\id$ in \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average}; hence $\mathcal Q_{\id,c}(q)=\frac1i\log\mathsf M(e^{iq})(c)$ is the row $c$ of $\mathcal Q(q)$ in \eqref{eq:constraint-primitive}, and $Q_{\id}= Q$, $\mathcal N_{\id}=\mathcal N$ follow from the definitions \eqref{eq:native-source-constraint-normalisation}.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}, $Q_0= Q\iota_0$ is diagonal with entries $\alpha_c(\id)= L^{-4}\id$, so $h_{\id}(c)= L^{-1}\alpha_c(\id)^{-1}= L^3\id$ is the row $c$ of $h= L^{-1}\iota_0Q_0^{-1}$; and since row $c$ of $Q$ is supported on $\mathcal E_c$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}), $(\mathsf C_{\id}B)(b_0(c))=-\alpha_c(\id)^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}Q(c,b)B(b)=-(Q_0^{-1}Q\iota_*B)(c)=(\mathsf CB)(b_0(c))$, while both maps are the identity on free bonds; so $\mathsf C_{\id}=\mathsf C$.

The row equation \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} at $U=\id$ is the row $c$ of the equation defining $\widetilde D$ after \eqref{eq:flat-phase}. Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} applies to the identity background on every row (its gauge hypothesis holds with $u=\id$, $\phi=0$), and by its part (i) the hypothesis on $B$ gives $\| g_0\mathsf CB|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant g_0C_{\mathsf C}\max_b| B(b)|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ for every row, so its part (ii) provides the unique small solution $\varphi_c(g_0\mathsf CB|_{\mathcal E_c})$, which is the row solution of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} for the reference background, analytic on the real ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ and agreeing with the germ of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality} at $A=0$.

The row $c$ of $\widetilde D$ of Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt} is real analytic on $\{\| A\|_{\infty}< a_{\mathrm{ph}}\}$, a function of $A|_{\mathcal S_c}$, hence of $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ ($\mathcal S_c$, the positive fine bonds with both endpoints in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$, is contained in $\mathcal E_c$, Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}), and agrees with the same germ at $A=0$ (the paragraph ``Locality of the first-step interaction'' there). The set of real $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ with $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ and $\| A\|_{\infty}< a_{\mathrm{ph}}$ is convex, hence connected, open, and contains $g_0\mathsf CB|_{\mathcal E_c}$ by the hypothesis on $B$ ($\| g_0\mathsf CB\|_{\infty}\leqslant \|\mathsf C\|_{\infty\to\infty}g_0\max_b| B(b)|< a_{\mathrm{ph}}$ by the definition of $a_L$ and $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |$); the identity theorem identifies the two analytic functions on it.

With $h_{\id}= h$ and $\mathsf C_{\id}=\mathsf C$, \eqref{eq:native-source-local-phase} becomes \eqref{eq:flat-phase}: $q_{\id}(B)= g_0\mathsf CB-h\widetilde D(g_0\mathsf CB)= q_{g_0}(B)$.

(ii) Let $\psi(A)\coloneqq A-h\widetilde D(A)$ as in Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}, so that $q_{g_0}(B)=\psi(g_0\mathsf CB)$, $\psi(0)=0$ and $D\psi(0)=\id$ because $D\widetilde D(0)=0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii)). For a plaquette $p$, $s_{p,\id}(q)=1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N(e^{iq}(\partial p))= f_p(q)$ is the $p$-summand of $S(e^{iq})$, the function $f_p$ of Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}, and $s_{p,\id}(0)=0$ since $\tr_N(\id)=1$; so $E_{\xi,p}(B)=-g_0^{-2}f_p(\psi(g_0\mathsf CB))$ by (i). Each $f_p\geqslant 0$ vanishes at $q=0$, so $Df_p(0)=0$. The chain rule then gives $DE_{\xi,p}(0)[B]=-g_0^{-2}Df_p(0)[D\psi(0)g_0\mathsf CB]=0$ and 
\[
\begin{aligned}
D^2E_{\xi,p}(0)[B,B]&=-g_0^{-2}\bigl(D^2f_p(0)[D\psi(0)g_0\mathsf CB,D\psi(0)g_0\mathsf CB]\\
&\qquad+Df_p(0)[D^2\psi(0)[g_0\mathsf CB,g_0\mathsf CB]]\bigr)\\
&=-D^2f_p(0)[\mathsf CB,\mathsf CB]\;,
\end{aligned}
\]
so by \eqref{eq:native-source-energy-residual}
\begin{equation}
p_{\xi,p}(B)=-\frac1{g_0^2}f_p(\psi(g_0\mathsf CB))+\frac12D^2f_p(0)[\mathsf CB,\mathsf CB]= v_p(B)\;.
\end{equation}

For a centre $y$: at $U=\id$ every path transport is $\id$, so the local group mean $\mathcal U_{\id}(y,x)$, the unique solution near the diagonal value of the equation after \eqref{eq:constraint-extension}, is $\id$; at $q= q_{g_0}(B)$ the mean $\mathcal U_{e^{iq}}(y,x)$ exists by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means} at the identity background, since for a row $c$ with endpoint block $\mathcal B_y$ one has $\mathcal E_y\subseteq\mathcal E_c$ and $\| q_{g_0}(B)|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \| A\|+2H_*K_*\| A\|^2\leqslant \vartheta_*$ for $A= g_0\mathsf CB|_{\mathcal E_c}$, $\| A\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$, by (ii) of that lemma, $\| h_{\id}(c)\|\leqslant H_*$ and $4K_*H_*\vartheta_*<1$; and the $y$-summand of \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-gauge} is $\mathscr G_{y,\id}(q)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y\setminus\{ y\}}(1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N\mathcal U_{e^{iq}}(y,x))=\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y\setminus\{ y\}}f_{(y,x)}(q)$, the sum of the $(y,x)$-summands of $\mathscr G(e^{iq})$ in \eqref{eq:action-primitive}. So $E_{\xi,y}(B)=-g_0^{-2}\mathscr G_{y,\id}(q_{g_0}(B))=\sum_x\bigl(-g_0^{-2}f_{(y,x)}(\psi(g_0\mathsf CB))\bigr)$. Each $f_{(y,x)}\geqslant 0$ vanishes at $q=0$, so $Df_{(y,x)}(0)=0$, and the computation just made for $f_p$ applies to each $f_{(y,x)}$; since the passage from a function to its degree-two Taylor residual at $B=0$ in \eqref{eq:native-source-energy-residual} is linear, $p_{\xi,y}(B)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y\setminus\{ y\}}v_{(y,x)}(B)$.

(iii) In \eqref{eq:native-source-haar-primitive}, $\sigma(q)\,\dd q$ is the pullback under $q\mapsto e^{iq}$ of the Haar measure of \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE}, and in \eqref{eq:literal-residual} $\sigma_H$ is the density of normalised Haar measure in the same coordinates relative to the same Lebesgue measure; the Haar measure of the compact group being unique up to a positive constant, $\sigma=\kappa\sigma_H$ with $\kappa>0$, both are positive on the chart ball (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii) takes the real logarithm of $\sigma(q)/\sigma(0)$ there), and $\sigma(q)/\sigma(0)=\sigma_H(q)/\sigma_H(0)= j_H(q)$. With $q_{\id}(B)= q_{g_0}(B)$ from (i), $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(B)=\log j_H(q_{g_0}(B)(b))= j_b(B)$, both sides being real logarithms of positive numbers: the branch of $j_b$ in \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} is the real logarithm on the convex domain of (i), on which the argument stays positive.

(iv) By (i) (the row solution being $\varphi_c$, which agrees with the row of $\widetilde D$ on an open set containing $g_0\mathsf CB|_{\mathcal E_c}$, so that their derivatives agree there, and $h_{\id}(c)= L^3\id$), $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(B)=\log|\det_{\mathfrak g}(\id-L^3\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_c(g_0\mathsf CB))|$. The determinant is positive on $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii)), so the absolute value is redundant and the expression is $d_c(B)$, whose branch in \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} is the real logarithm of the positive determinant (the sentence after that display).

The first consequence is (ii)--(iv) summed over all labels, with \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-sum}.

For the second, every primitive and every term vanishes at zero input: $p_{\xi,\alpha}(0)= E_{\xi,\alpha}(0)=0$ ($s_{p,\id}(0)=0$, $\mathscr G_{y,\id}(0)=0$), $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(0)=0$, $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(0)=0$ ($\widetilde D(0)=0$, $D\widetilde D(0)=0$), and $v_{\alpha}(0)= j_b(0)= d_c(0)=0$ likewise. A primitive depends on $B$ only through its free-input set (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}, the list after \eqref{eq:native-source-jacobian-primitive}), a term of \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} only through its support. For $B\in\mathfrak g^D$ as in the statement, $i_{D,T}B$ satisfies the hypothesis of the lemma (the maximum norm does not increase), a primitive whose free-input set misses $D$ has zero input at $i_{D,T}B$ and vanishes, and a term whose support misses $D$ vanishes there as well; so the sum of the primitives whose free-input sets meet $D$ and $P_{D,T}(B)$ are both the full sums at $i_{D,T}B$, which agree by the first consequence.
\end{proof}

$N_{D,I,T}^{\sigma}$ and $D_{D,T}^{\sigma}$ are \eqref{eq:regional-integrals} with $C_D,P_D,i_D,U_{g_0}$ replaced by $C_{D,T},P_{D,T},i_{D,T},U_{g_0,T}$; their cutoff is still the product over $D$. The same forest, web, and connected-weight definitions applied to these periodic integrals give weights $\Phi_{D,I,T}(\Gamma)$, and
\begin{equation}
    \kappa_{D,I,T}(j)=
        \sum_{\Gamma\, | \,j\in J_{\Gamma}}
            \frac{\Phi_{D,I,T}(\Gamma)}{| J_{\Gamma}|}\;.
\end{equation}

Let $I$ have a lift with $mL< N_{\min}/3$, where $N_{\min}$ is the smallest fine period. For both periodic open-segment gases the positive cluster majorants obey a uniform rooted tail. Let $U_{D,I,T}(\Gamma)$ be the absolute Ursell coefficient, including its factorial, times the positive object majorants, and let $U_{I,T}$ be its value for $D= E_{*,T}$. There is $\eta_0>0$, independent of the region and periods, such that for every marked segment $j$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-periodic-line-tail}
    \sum_{\Gamma\, | \,j\in J_{\Gamma}}
        U_{D,I,T}(\Gamma)e^{\eta_0\ell(\Gamma)}
        \leqslant C\tau^2\;.
\end{equation}
The majorants dominate the absolute connected weights. The proof is the positive-majorant argument of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-coefficient}: restricting supports preserves the label overlap bounds, and the periodic shell sum is bounded by the infinite-lattice shell sum. Under this lift hypothesis, index separation along the segment is its periodic separation. Thus \eqref{eq:marginal-hull-extent} holds on the lifted segment. Its ordinary intervals have the straight-line interval tree sum. Hence the same load inequalities and extent reserve prove \eqref{eq:regional-periodic-line-tail} for the full and restricted periodic gases, including the covariance interpolations used below.

On a compatible torus with fine periods $N_{\mu}$, $N_{\min}=\min_{\mu} N_{\mu}$, and $I$ has a lift with $mL< N_{\min}/3$. The set $D$ may wrap around the torus. $\kappa_{I,T}(j)$ is the same allocation with $D= E_{*,T}$. In this paragraph $d_j$ is \eqref{eq:regional-distance} with $d_T$ in place of $d$, including its endpoint term $L\min(j,m-1-j)$.

For bounded $d_j\leqslant 2(R_0+R_*+c_{\mathrm{reg}})$, \eqref{eq:regional-periodic-line-tail} and $|\kappa_v|\leqslant C\tau^2$ give \eqref{eq:regional-torus-bound} directly after enlarging $C$.

For larger $d_j$, the periodic version of \eqref{eq:regional-resolvent} and its differentiated cluster estimate compare $\kappa_{D,I,T}(j)$ with $\kappa_{I,T}(j)$. Clusters of extent at least $d_j/(2c_{\mathrm{reg}})$ have total rooted weight at most $C\tau^2e^{-cd_j}$. For smaller clusters the labels agree, and their carriers are at distance at least $d_j/2-R_0$ from $D^c$. The covariance derivative therefore has the same bound, after absorbing the fixed factor $e^{aR_0}$. This proves
\begin{equation}
    |\kappa_{D,I,T}(j)-\kappa_{I,T}(j)|
        \leqslant C\tau^2e^{-cd_j}\;.
\end{equation}

For the comparison of the second density with the infinite straight-line density, the root segment is lifted to the chosen copy of $I$. A cluster network of length $c_{\mathrm{reg}}\ell+R_0< N_{\min}/4$ lifts uniquely and preserves carrier intersections. The distinct translates of $I$ are separated by more than $2N_{\min}/3$ because $mL< N_{\min}/3$, so all its source marks lie on that copy. If also $c_{\mathrm{reg}}\ell+R_0< L\min(j,m-1-j)$, the network avoids the two ends and has the same labels and ordered source factors as the infinite straight-line expansion. Clusters failing either restriction are bounded by the rooted extent tail. For the remaining clusters only the covariance marginals change. Periodisation and lifted separation $d(b,c)\leqslant N_{\min}/4$ give
\begin{equation}
    \| C_T(b,c)-C_{\infty}(b,c)\|
        \leqslant C e^{-\mu(N_{\min}-d(b,c))}
        \leqslant C e^{-\mu N_{\min}/2}e^{-\mu d(b,c)}\;,
\end{equation}
after expressing the decay exponent in fine-bond units. The free-inverse periodisation follows by applying $H_T$ to the absolutely convergent periodised kernel of $H^{-1}$, as in the proof of \eqref{eq:bulk-periodisation}. The covariance interpolation and the density-direction estimates in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} apply with $h_A\coloneqq e^{-\mu N_{\min}/2}$. They retain edge decay and the quadratic source gain; their polynomial carrier factors are absorbed by the reserved extent weight. With $\iota_T=\max(0,N_{\min}/4-R_0)$, summing the short-cluster derivatives and the two tails gives
\begin{equation}
    |\kappa_{I,T}(j)-\kappa_v|
        \leqslant C\tau^2\left[
            e^{-c(L\min(j,m-1-j)-R_0)_+}+e^{-c\iota_T}\right]\;.
\end{equation}
Here $x_+=\max(x,0)$.

Absolute convergence also gives $\log(N_{D,I,T}^{\sigma}/D_{D,T}^{\sigma})=\sum_{j=0}^{m-1}\kappa_{D,I,T}(j)$, since summing the allocation weights $| J_{\Gamma}|^{-1}$ over the marked segments gives one for each source cluster. Adding the two comparisons proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-torus-bound}
    |\kappa_{D,I,T}(j)-\kappa_v|
        \leqslant C\tau^2(e^{-cd_j}+e^{-c\iota_T})\;.
\end{equation}

The identification with $K_{\xi}$ uses the averaging prescription \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, the bond cutoff $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$, and the threshold $\delta_0= g_0r_0(g_0)$ on both sides. The comparison applies separately to either specified $\sigma$.

Let $I$ consist of consecutive traversals of one straight side of $C$. Let $E_{\Omega,*}$ be the free carrier after the designated-bond elimination in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}. Let $D_-$ consist of these bonds with both endpoints in $\Lambda_1$, and $D_+$ of those with at least one endpoint there. The comparison holds for every $D_-\subseteq D\subseteq D_+$, assigning the complementary free variables to the exterior integral. It therefore covers either endpoint convention for the integration boundary.

In the notation of \cite{BalabanCRE} let $M_2,M,R_1$ be the cube-scale integers, so the test cubes have fine side $L^2M_2R_1$ and the macro cubes have fine side $LMR_1$; here $R_1$ denotes the scale integer, not the large-fluctuation region also denoted by $R_1$ in \cite{BalabanCRE}. The partitions are aligned and nested, all periods are divisible by $LMR_1$, and the powers of $L$ satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-collar-sizes}
    M\geqslant 8LM_2,
    \qquad LMR_1>4R_0+4L^2M_2R_1+8\;.
\end{equation}
Here $R_0=4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$ is the fixed range constant above, distinct from the scale integer in \cite{BalabanCRE}. These choices lie within the compatible-partition and large-$M$ prescription of \cite[Section~1]{BalabanCRE}. The collar inequality is among the common parameter conditions; it holds for every scale integer $R_1\geqslant 1$ once $LM-4L^2M_2>4R_0+8$.

For macro regions the collar-distance statement following \cite[(1.10)]{BalabanCRE} supplies the metric separation, including near cube corners. For test-cube enlargements a conservative reach bound suffices: each added layer has width at most $L^2M_2R_1$. This bound also covers a layer of the $L$-fold finer cubes in the enlargement convention of \cite[Section~1]{BalabanCRE}. The parallelepiped modification after (1.20) removes macro cubes from $\Lambda_1$; the remaining region is still a union of macro cubes and hence of test cubes.

Using (1.20) and that collar-distance statement, a site within distance $LMR_1-1$ of $\Lambda_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1'$. Every stencil meeting $D\subseteq D_+$ therefore remains in the regular region. A bond with an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$ is tested by the test cube containing that endpoint, which is contained in $\Lambda_1$ and is good. A bad test or a test in $S_1$ uses only bonds within $2L^2M_2R_1+1$ of its cube. The collar and \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes} keep those bonds outside $D_+$, including the fixed stencil enlargement.

At identity determining data the critical field is the identity: it satisfies the constraints, has zero action and gauge-fixing functional, and is unique in the regular chart by \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE}. Its force is zero. The Hessian on $D$ is consequently $H_{D,T}$, including the diagonal contributions of plaquettes crossing its boundary.

The nonlinear constraint in \cite[(2.4)]{BalabanRG1} becomes $M(e^{iB'})$ at identity background. Its principal logarithm is $\mathcal Q(B')$ from \eqref{eq:constraint-primitive}. The linearisation following (2.10) has linear part $L\widetilde Q B'$, hence $\widetilde Q= Q$ there. Its designated-row right inverse satisfies $LQh= I$. Uniqueness of the small solution for $\widetilde D$ gives exactly \eqref{eq:flat-phase}. Thus the action, Haar and Jacobian terms become $v_T(i_{D,T}B)$ with all primitive labels meeting $D$ retained.

The split reconstruction in \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE} also equals the identity at identity data, and $Q_1^{s*}\id=\id$ by (1.3). Its logarithmic argument is zero. Equation (1.21) then gives $e^{iL^{-1}\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(0)}=1$; the small principal chart implies $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(0)=0$. Since the BCH remainder satisfies $\mathbf F(X,0)=0$, the boundary change (1.22) is the identity, its Jacobian is one and its additional exponent is zero at this projection.

For the cutoff, every free bond in $D$ has an endpoint in a compatible good cube contained in $\Lambda_1$. The twice-enlarged starred test in \cite[(1.18)]{BalabanCRE} covers it. The designated-bond exclusion is the verbal convention following (1.8). A good cube outside $\Lambda_1$ can also test bonds in $D$; its product of bond indicators splits into its $D$ and exterior factors. The $D$ factors are redundant with the covered interior cutoff by idempotence; all exterior factors stay in the outer integral. Bad tests and changed background tests are separated from $D$ by the collar. At zero exterior free field the conditional cutoff is therefore $\Theta_D^{\sigma}$.

The same norm is used on both sides. The threshold is $r=\delta_0/g_0$ by the normalisation convention \eqref{eq:cre-cutoff-normalisation}. The exterior quadratic cross term and its completion-of-square compensator vanish at the projection. Gaussian and constraint normalisations cancel between the two conditional kernels and remain in the exterior integration.

Finally let $t_a\coloneqq 1$ on $I$ and $t_a\coloneqq 0$ elsewhere. At the flat projection, \eqref{eq:regional-wilson-polynomial} is the closed relative source in \eqref{eq:regional-integrals}. With $K_{\xi}^{\mathrm{flat}}$ the projected conditional kernels,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-kernel-identification}
    \frac{K_{\xi}^{\mathrm{flat}}(1_I)}{K_{\xi,\mathrm{vac}}^{\mathrm{flat}}}
        =\frac{N_{D,I,T}^{\sigma}}{D_{D,T}^{\sigma}}\;.
\end{equation}
If $d_T(K_j,D^c)\geqslant b$ for every source segment $j$, then \eqref{eq:regional-torus-bound} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-mass-identification}
    \left|-\frac{1}{mL\varepsilon}
        \log\frac{K_{\xi}^{\mathrm{flat}}(1_I)}
                    {K_{\xi,\mathrm{vac}}^{\mathrm{flat}}}
            -\delta m_v^{\sigma}\right|
        \leqslant \frac{C\tau^2}{L\varepsilon}
            \left(\frac{1}{m}+e^{-cb}+e^{-c\iota_T}\right)\;.
\end{equation}
For every domain label $\xi$ for which the buffer fits inside the torus and $mL< N_{\min}/3$, \eqref{eq:regional-mass-identification} bounds the distance between the per-length scalar and $\delta m_v^{\sigma}$ by $C\tau^2(1/m+e^{-cb}+e^{-c\iota_T})/(L\varepsilon)$ on the fixed torus; along any family of such labels with $m$, $b$ and $\iota_T$ tending to infinity this bound tends to zero, so the per-length scalar converges to $\delta m_v^{\sigma}$, which identifies it with \eqref{eq:marginal-full-perimeter}. The limit is the one defining the coefficient, as in \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}; the estimate \eqref{eq:regional-mass-identification} itself is a statement on each fixed torus.

The four oriented straight-side coefficients give the square coefficient by the average in \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}. This comparison is made inside the conditional kernels.

\subsection{The Regional Square Scalar}\label{sec:regional-square-scalar}

Let $\sigma$ be either cutoff prescription. Let $C_n$ be a coarse translate of the counterclockwise square with vertices $0,nLe_1,nL(e_1+e_2),nLe_2$ in fine-lattice units, with $K_{\mu}\geqslant 3(n+2)$ for every coarse period. Let $D$ be the free bonds integrated in a covered conditional kernel: every free-input stencil of the contour lies in $D$. With the original primitive labels retained, including those crossing the boundary of $D$, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-scalar}
    S^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}\coloneqq
    \frac{\displaystyle\int\Theta_D^{\sigma}(B)e^{P_{D,T}(B)}
        \chi\bigl(\Hol_{U_{g_0,T}(i_{D,T}B)}C_n\bigr)\,\dd\mu_{C_{D,T}}(B)}
    {\displaystyle\int\Theta_D^{\sigma}(B)e^{P_{D,T}(B)}\,\dd\mu_{C_{D,T}}(B)}\;,
    \quad C_{D,T}\coloneqq(i_{D,T}^*H_Ti_{D,T})^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}
Here $H_T$ is the full flat free-field precision on the torus, and $P_{D,T}$ is \eqref{eq:regional-periodic-weight}; $\Theta_D^{\sigma}$ is the bond cutoff of \eqref{eq:regional-weight}. For a conditional history $\xi$, let $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}\coloneqq S^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}$, with $D$ its integration carrier. This is a ratio of conditional reference integrals.

The square's $4n$ coarse segments are indexed cyclically by $j$. Let $K_j$ be the union of the free-input stencils of its fine traversals. With complements taken in the torus free carrier and with the periodic fine-bond metric of \eqref{eq:regional-distance}, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-distances}
    d_j\coloneqq\max\bigl(0,d_T(K_j,D^c)-R_0\bigr),
    \qquad \iota_T\coloneqq\max\bigl(0,N_{\min}/4-R_0\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
The fixed $R_0$ includes the label, reconstruction and precision ranges. Distance to the empty set is infinite, with $e^{-\infty}=0$. There is no distance to a side endpoint in $d_j$.

\begin{proposition}\label{prop:regional-square-extraction}
Under these hypotheses, the collar conditions of the conditional kernel, and the common small-coupling thresholds of the flat and regional expansions, the scalar \eqref{eq:regional-square-scalar} is nonzero. Its logarithm is continued from zero in the traversal-source polynomial \eqref{eq:regional-wilson-polynomial}. There are $C,c>0$, independent of $D,n$ and the compatible periods, and an error $E^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-extraction}
    S^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}
        = e^{-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)}
          \bigl(z_{\mathrm c}^{\sigma}(g_0,\pi/2)\bigr)^4
          e^{E^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}}\;,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-error}
    | E^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}|
        \leqslant C\tau^2\left[
            \sum_{j=0}^{4n-1}e^{-cd_j}
            +4ne^{-c\iota_T}+(n+1)e^{-cn}\right]\;.
\end{equation}
The coefficients are exactly \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass} and \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor}, with the same cutoff prescription. The parameter $\tau$ is \eqref{eq:marginal-fixed-forest-bound}; fixed enlargements of its majorant constants are absorbed in $C$ and the coupling threshold.

The collar hypotheses identify this integral with the conditional scalar of \cite{BalabanCRE}.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Let $F_{D,C,T}\coloneqq\log S^{\circ}_{D,C,T}$, with its branch specified below, $F_{C,T}=\log(N_{C_n,T}^{\sigma}/D_T^{\sigma})$, and $F_{C,\infty}(n)= F_{\square,\infty}(n)$. The first two quantities are compared, then the latter two, and the bulk corner extraction is applied; the errors from changing the kernel and summation domain are retained, as in \cite[(4.35)--(4.37)]{BalabanRG1}.

At the conditional reference data the background and exterior determining fields are the identity and the retained free field is zero. The row precision entries are the flat torus entries on $D$, including the diagonal terms from crossing plaquettes. The collar contains every stencil touching $D$, so the precision is $i_{D,T}^*H_Ti_{D,T}$. The primitives agree with the terms of \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms} label by label, with the designated inverse $L^3$ at the identity and the gauge terms of a centre summed over its pairs $(y,x)$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:identity-primitives}, whose hypothesis on $B$ is the pair of small-coupling conditions fixed in the next paragraph; by its second consequence the sum of the primitives whose free-input sets meet $D$, at $i_{D,T}B$, is $P_{D,T}(B)$, terms whose support misses $D$ vanishing at $i_{D,T}B$. The cutoff is the same product of bond tests. Thus the numerator and denominator in \eqref{eq:regional-square-scalar} are those of the conditional reference scalar, with their normalisers retained in the ratio.

The local implicit solutions used in the two representations have the same analytic germ. To fix their common domain, let $C_{\mathsf C}$ and $\vartheta_*$ be the constants of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} ($C_{\mathsf C}$ bounds the fixed row map from the maximum free-bond norm to the row Hilbert norm, $\vartheta_*$ is its implicit-solution phase radius), and let $a_L$ be the flat chart radius in Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}. The row map is finite dimensional with finitely many translated types, so $C_{\mathsf C}<\infty$; the analytic implicit-function theorem gives a uniform positive phase radius. The radius $a_L$ is reduced if necessary to lie within those row charts and their nonvanishing Jacobian domains, and the coupling satisfies
\begin{equation}
    g_0C_{\mathsf C}(2+4r)<\frac{\vartheta_*}{2},
    \qquad g_0(2+4r)< a_L\;.
\end{equation}
The factor $2+4r$ specifies a larger free-variable polydisc containing the integration box $\| B\|_{\infty}\leqslant r$ with a positive margin. The convex intersection of this polydisc with the phase balls lies in the common analytic charts. The identity theorem therefore identifies the solutions throughout the integration box.

The common chart radius is fixed before the coupling; reducing it preserves all previous estimates by restriction to a smaller domain. These small-coupling requirements and all polymer-load inequalities are imposed together, which is possible because $g_0(1+r)^3\to0$ and $\tau\to0$.

The protected-label expansion applies with supports intersected with $D$ and every original label kept. Zero extension commutes with constant conjugation, so the restricted primitives, cutoffs and closed source differences are invariant. The restricted support graph and forest partition the labels into components. Source components are merged using the shortest cyclic intervals of the flat expansion, with its fixed tie-breaking base; a web interval is their union, possibly the whole circle. Compatible components and webs have disjoint carriers and disjoint web intervals, so their union reverses this decomposition without losing or duplicating labels. If a web crosses the base, cyclicity of the trace moves the base between web intervals before Schur factorisation. This proves the regional counterpart of \eqref{eq:marginal-exact-gases}.

The required quantitative bounds hold uniformly for these restricted labels. Principal restriction and inversion preserve the spectral bounds, and the finite-range Neumann series gives uniform exponential covariance decay in the periodic metric. Let $\mu_1>0$ be a remaining edge-decay exponent after the degree payment, no larger than one eighth of the covariance and comparison exponents, and let
\begin{equation}
    \alpha'\coloneqq\frac{\mu_1}{1024(1+c_h)},
    \qquad \eta'\coloneqq\frac{\mu_1}{1024},
    \qquad a'(p)\coloneqq| A_p|+\alpha'H_p\;.
\end{equation}
Restriction preserves the support-size, overlap and range bounds $s_*,q_*,R_*$. The same labelled-tree count as in \eqref{eq:marginal-load-series}, with a fixed enlarged $K_2$, bounds vacuum and source loads by
\begin{equation}
    \sum_{k\geqslant 1}K_2^k\tau^{\lceil k/s_*\rceil},
    \qquad
    \sum_{k\geqslant 1}K_2^k\tau^{\max(2,\lceil k/s_*\rceil)}\;.
\end{equation}
The bounds remain valid with the reserve $e^{4| A_{\gamma}|+8\alpha'H_{\gamma}+8\eta'\ell(\gamma)}$. Contacts remain within $R_*$ of the restricted support network, so \eqref{eq:marginal-hull-extent} applies to the square, including at its corners. The cyclic conversion \eqref{eq:marginal-hull-root} has the same uniform geometric sum $1+2/(e^{\alpha'}-1)$. The web-tree recursion therefore gives positive majorants $u_p$ with
\begin{equation}
    \begin{aligned}
        \sup_b\sum_{p\, | \,b\in A_p}u_pe^{2a'(p)+2\eta'\ell(p)}&\leqslant C_*'\tau\;,\\
        \sup_x\sum_{W\, | \,x\in h_W}u_We^{2a'(W)+2\eta'\ell(W)}&\leqslant C_*'\tau^2\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The source-only spatial load is also $O(\tau^2)$. The coupling $g_0$, chosen last, satisfies $K_2^{s_*}\tau\leqslant 1/2$, $C_*'\tau\leqslant 1/4$ and $C_*'\tau^2\leqslant \alpha'/4$. The incompatibility sum is then at most $a'(p)/4$. The pinned-tree proof of \eqref{eq:marginal-pinned-bound} yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-rooted-majorant}
    \sum_{\Gamma\, | \,j\in J_{\Gamma}}U(\Gamma)e^{\eta'\ell(\Gamma)}\leqslant C\tau^2\;,
\end{equation}
where $U$ is the absolute Ursell coefficient times the positive object majorants. The factor $2^{| S|}$ for source variables $| t_a|\leqslant 2$ is included in $K_2$. Thus the regional source logarithm exists on that polydisc and vanishes at zero source. Its exponential is the ratio \eqref{eq:regional-square-scalar}, proving nonvanishing.

For the boundary comparison, the periodic resolvent identity is
\begin{equation}
    C_{D,T}-(C_T)_{D,D}
        = C_{D,T}(H_T)_{D,D^c}(C_T)_{D^c,D}\;.
\end{equation}
If $u\in D$, $w\in D^c$ and $d_T(u,w)\leqslant R_H$, let $s= d_T(b,u)+d_T(w,c)$. The periodic triangle inequalities give
\begin{equation}
    d_T(b,D^c)+d_T(c,D^c)+d_T(b,c)\leqslant 2s+2R_H\;.
\end{equation}
Half the inverse-decay exponent pays these distances; the remaining convolution is bounded by a fixed neighbour count times $\sup_b\sum_u e^{-\mu d_T(b,u)/2}$. Periodic shells have at most the infinite-lattice shell counts, so this sum is uniform even for wrapping or disconnected $D$. Therefore
\begin{equation}
    \| C_{D,T}(b,c)-C_T(b,c)\|
        \leqslant Ce^{-a(d_T(b,D^c)+d_T(c,D^c)+d_T(b,c))}\;.
\end{equation}

The principal covariances are interpolated as in \eqref{eq:regional-density-derivative}. On a carrier $A$ of size $k$, let $B_{bc}\coloneqq A_0e^{-\mu_0d_T(b,c)}$ be a common positive edge majorant and $h_A= e^{-a d_T(A,D^c)}$. The covariance direction satisfies $\|\mathcal D_A\|\leqslant Ckh_A$ and $\|\mathcal D(b,c)\|\leqslant Ch_AB_{bc}$. For forest degrees $d_b$, the radii are
\begin{equation}
    r_{\{ b,c\}}\coloneqq\frac{\lambda}{32d_bd_cB_{bc}},
    \qquad r_0\coloneqq\frac{\lambda}{32Ckh_A}\;.
\end{equation}
The forest perturbation has norm at most $\lambda/32$, and the extra centre direction $\mathcal D_A\circ w^F$ has the same bound on its circle, since a positive Schur mask with unit diagonal is contractive. The total is below $\lambda/8$, so the normalised density has the Gaussian majorant \eqref{eq:marginal-density-majorant}. Replacing one edge direction by $E_e(\mathcal D)$ instead uses radius $\lambda/(32d_bd_cCh_AB_{bc})$ and costs $Ch_A$ against the same forest majorant. Summing the centre and edge derivatives costs at most $C(k+| F|+1)^2h_A$. Zero directions give zero derivatives, and no covariance entry occurs in a denominator.

Constant-conjugation invariance survives differentiation. A single marked component therefore retains its quadratic character gain, also when it crosses a corner. The product rule over repeated object occurrences and \eqref{eq:regional-square-rooted-majorant} give the differentiated cluster bound used in the regional proposition, with the same $\tau^2$ gain.

Each source cluster is allocated to its marked coarse segments with weight $| J_{\Gamma}|^{-1}$. A network joins its carrier, stencil edges and contour intervals with length at most $C_{\rm net}\ell(\Gamma)+R_0$. The interval may turn a corner, but its fine-path length is still bounded by $c_h\ell$; it is anchored at the source mark in segment $j$, hence within $R_0$ of $K_j$.

For $d_j>2R_*+2R_0$, the clusters are split at $\ell= d_j/(2C_{\rm net})$. Short clusters have their original stencils inside $D$, identical labels and cyclic intervals in both expansions, and carriers at distance at least $d_j/2-R_0$ from $D^c$, whose fixed loss is absorbed in the constant. Their covariance derivative is bounded by the preceding estimate. Long clusters are paid by \eqref{eq:regional-square-rooted-majorant}. Bounded $d_j$ are covered by the same rooted bound after enlarging $C$. This proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-boundary-comparison}
    | F_{D,C,T}-F_{C,T}|\leqslant C\tau^2\sum_{j=0}^{4n-1}e^{-cd_j}\;.
\end{equation}
No side-endpoint terms occur because both contours are the same closed square.

For the periodic comparison, the Neumann estimate for the free inverse gives $\| C_{\infty}(e,f)\|\leqslant \gamma_L^{-1}e^{-\mu_L\|\ell(e)-\ell(f)\|_{\infty}}$. Since $d_T(e,f)\leqslant L\|\ell(e)-\ell(f)\|_{\infty}+2L$ for fixed lifts, it gives exponential decay in fine units with exponent $\nu=\mu_L/L$. Periodising this free inverse solves the torus inverse equation. For lifted separation $d\leqslant N_{\min}/4$, summing the image shells gives
\begin{equation}
    \| C_T(e,f)-C_{\infty}(e,f)\|
        \leqslant Ce^{-\nu(N_{\min}-d)}
        \leqslant Ce^{-\nu N_{\min}/2}e^{-\nu d}\;.
\end{equation}
The same density-direction radii apply, with $h_A\coloneqq e^{-\nu N_{\min}/2}$ and a reduced common decay exponent.

A rooted cluster with $C_{\rm net}\ell+R_0< N_{\min}/4$ lifts uniquely. Projection is injective on its network, preserves carrier intersections, and preserves the fixed ordered square traversal list and its cyclic intervals. Distinct square images are farther than $2N_{\min}/3$ under the stated period hypothesis, so all its source marks lift to the chosen square. Thus the short torus and bulk clusters correspond with identical combinatorics; only their covariance marginals differ. The other clusters, including winding ones, are paid by their extent tails. Summing over $4n$ roots gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regional-square-periodic-comparison}
    | F_{C,T}-F_{C,\infty}(n)|\leqslant C\tau^2(4n)e^{-c\iota_T}\;.
\end{equation}

Finally, \eqref{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound} applies. The straight sum equals $-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)$ and the four oriented corner logarithms sum to $4\log z_{\mathrm c}^{\sigma}$, by their definitions. Let
\begin{equation}
    E^{\circ}_{D,C_n,T}\coloneqq(F_{D,C,T}-F_{C,T})
        +(F_{C,T}-F_{C,\infty}(n))+E_n^{\sigma}\;.
\end{equation}
Equations~\eqref{eq:regional-square-boundary-comparison}, \eqref{eq:regional-square-periodic-comparison} and \eqref{eq:corner-reference-matching} give the result. Every logarithm is the connected source branch, so the exponential identity has no branch ambiguity. The adjacent-side clusters and straight endpoint deficits are contained in the corner coefficient.
\end{proof}

For fixed geometry, $E^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}$ depends only on the regional labels and is therefore measurable under the original history sum. Its bound is finite at fixed cutoff.

The boundary sum in \eqref{eq:regional-square-error} can be of order $n$ for a loop running near the integration boundary.

\section{The Insertion Retained after One Step}
\label{sec:remaining-physical-comparison}

The first step produces a function of the coarse field through \eqref{eq:outgoing-loop}. Its representation below retains the closed flux insertions generated by the block average, together with the other source terms. The scalar factor extracted from the reference integral is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:extracted-loop-scalar}
    \kappa_C\coloneqq e^{-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C)}
        \bigl(z_{\mathrm c}^{\sigma}(g_0,\pi/2)\bigr)^4\;.
\end{equation}
Throughout this section the cutoff prescription is fixed, the contour is the counterclockwise $(e_1,e_2)$ square or one of its coarse translates, and the period, collar, and coupling hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} hold. The physical conditional cutoff and its flat projection use the same fixed $\sigma$ (the cutoff norm $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ of \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}, not the Haar density $\sigma$) and threshold $r=\delta_0/g_0$. The scale parameters satisfy \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes} and the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}. Closeness to the integration boundary remains in $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$, the error of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} at the carrier $I$, defined at the end of this subsection.

The first step is the operator \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator} with the averaging operation \eqref{eq:global-average}, Borel and gauge covariant by Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}, and $\rho_1$, $N_1$ are the measures \eqref{eq:first-step}. Besides Ba{\l}aban's construction \cite{BalabanCRE} as recorded in (B1)--(B4), the representation below uses
\begin{itemize}
\item the Borel choices of minimal configurations of Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser},
\item the Borel background $U_1$ and row solutions of the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data},
\item the bijection $\Psi_{\xi}\colon\mathcal D_{\xi}\to\mathcal A_{\xi}$ with invertible differential of Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection}, which is the (1.22) part of (B4)(ii) (its hypotheses: $\delta_0\leqslant \delta_G$ is listed among the further conditions of Section~\ref{app:thresholds} and holds for small $g_0$, as $\delta_0= g_0r(g_0)\to0$; the bound \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs} on $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ (\cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE}, Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}) at the tolerance $\delta_0/40$ is the condition ``$MR_1$ large'' of item 5 there, met for small $g_0$ at fixed $M$ since $R_1\to\infty$, with $\varepsilon_1/\delta_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)A_0/A_1$ by \cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE} and the constants of that lemma fixed before $g_0$),
\item the invertible differential of $B\mapsto U(B)$ (the (1.14) part of (B4)(ii)) and the nonvanishing Jacobian of (1.14) ((B4)(iii); its positivity on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), is used below only to match the $\operatorname{Tr}\log$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} with $\log|\det|$),
\item Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(ii),(iv) and Lemma~\ref{lem:collar} for the $a$-independence of the exterior factors and the box form of the integration fibre,
\item Lemmas~\ref{lem:charts} and~\ref{lem:collar} for the boundedness of the integrand on the box,
\item the row factorisation of the Jacobian of (1.14) (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum}, from Lemmas~\ref{lem:two-block} and~\ref{lem:row-locality}),
\item the list of operations after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} with \eqref{eq:one-step-physical-partition},
\item the disintegration theorem for standard Borel spaces \cite[(17.35), Theorem 15.6]{Kechris},
\item for the coverage event, the stencils of Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}, Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} and Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The Conditional Integral}

This section uses the unrestricted transformation of \cite{BalabanCRE} (0.1) and the first-step identities (1.11)--(1.15) with the cutoff (1.25), as recorded in Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} under (B1)--(B4), with the averaging choice permitted after (0.1); of \cite[(1.26)--(1.29)]{BalabanCRE} only (1.27) enters, as the definition of the first-step coupling $g_1(g_0)$ in $R_1$ and $\varepsilon_1$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}). The outer data $\xi$ consist of the region labels, the coarse field $V$, the exterior fine field $V_0$ and the exterior free fluctuation $A_{\mathrm e}$ in those identities.

For the integrations, the positive fine bonds are partitioned into $E_{\Omega}=\{ b\in E\, | \,b_-\in\Omega_1\text{ or }b_+\in\Omega_1\}$ and $E\setminus E_{\Omega}$. This disjoint integration convention assigns crossing bonds to $E_{\Omega}$ and specifies $V_0$ only on bonds with both endpoints outside $\Omega_1$. Let $E_{\Omega,*}$ be the free bonds remaining after the designated-bond elimination on $\Omega_1$, and let $D\coloneqq I=\Lambda_1^*$ be the bonds integrated in $\Lambda_1$, the carrier $D_+$ of Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} (the comparison there holds for every $D_-\subseteq D\subseteq D_+$; this section is at $D= D_+= I$, the carrier of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1}, which the definition of the integration fibre \eqref{eq:retained-change-domain} as a section of $\mathcal D_{\xi}\subseteq\mathfrak g^J\times\mathfrak g^I$ requires).

Let $J= E_{\Omega,*}\setminus D$. The variable $a\in\mathfrak g^D$ is integrated and $A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^J$ is held fixed. With $i_D$ and $i_J$ denoting extension by zero into $\mathfrak g^{E_{\Omega,*}}$, let $z_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq i_Da+i_JA_{\mathrm e}$. Lebesgue measure $\dd a$ is the product measure from the fixed Lie-algebra inner product.

$U_1(\xi)$ is the critical configuration of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE}, in its axial mean gauge ((B1)). Let $\mathsf C_{\xi}$ be the linear solution map from free fields to fields satisfying the linearised constraints in \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}, and let $\mathsf H_{\xi}\coloneqq\mathsf C_{\xi}^*\Delta_{1,\xi}\mathsf C_{\xi}$, with $\Delta_{1,\xi}$ given by \cite[(1.16)]{BalabanCRE}. Let $h_{\xi}$ be the designated-bond right inverse of the linearised constraint and $\widetilde D_{\xi}$ the analytic correction of \cite[(1.14)]{BalabanCRE}, as identified in (B4)(i) (the corresponding construction for Ba{\l}aban's own step is the one following \cite[(2.10), p.~267]{BalabanRG1}): they are $h_{U_1}$ and $\widetilde D_{U_1}$ of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}, with the row solutions and their domains defined there. The inverse boundary change $\Psi_{\xi}$ is \cite[(1.22)]{BalabanCRE}, acting on the free fields in $\mathfrak g^{E_{\Omega,*}}$ and equal to the identity off $S_1^*$. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-reconstruction}
    \begin{aligned}
        q_{\xi}(s)&\coloneqq s-h_{\xi}\widetilde D_{\xi}(s)\;,\\
        U_{\xi}(a,b)&\coloneqq
            \exp\bigl(iq_{\xi}(g_0\mathsf C_{\xi}\Psi_{\xi}(z_{\xi}(a)))(b)\bigr)
                U_1(\xi,b)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The second formula applies on $E_{\Omega}$; on $E\setminus E_{\Omega}$, $U_{\xi}= V_0$. The map $\mathsf C_{\xi}$ takes $\mathfrak g^{E_{\Omega,*}}$ into $\mathfrak g^{E_{\Omega}}$. The variable $a$ on $I$, and $A_{\mathrm e}$ on $J\setminus S_1^*$, are the principal fluctuation variables of \cite[(1.13)]{BalabanCRE}, the chart logarithms of $UU_1(\xi)^{-1}$ divided by $g_0$ on those free bonds ($\Psi_{\xi}$ is the identity there; $I\cap S_1^*=\varnothing$ by \eqref{eq:c-collar-distance}); on $S_1^*\subseteq J$, $A_{\mathrm e}$ is the variable of (1.22), the (1.13) variable there being $\psi_b(A_{\mathrm e}(b))$; and the domain of the $a$-integration is specified in these variables below. With $\chi_0'(\Omega_1)$ denoting the product of the group tests (1.8) retained in (1.11), let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-source-domain}
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathcal U_{\xi}&\coloneqq\bigl\{ U\in G^E\, | \,
            U|_{E\setminus E_{\Omega}}= V_0,
            M(U)|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}}= V|_{\Omega_1^{[1]}},
            \mathcal I_{\xi}(U)>0\bigr\}\;,\\
        t_{\xi}(U)&\coloneqq\frac{1}{i}\log(UU_1(\xi)^{-1})|_{E_{\Omega}}\;,\\
        \widehat{\mathcal A}_{\xi}&\coloneqq\bigl\{ g_0^{-1}t_{\xi}(U)|_{E_{\Omega,*}}
            \, | \,U\in\mathcal U_{\xi},\ UU_1(\xi)^{-1}\text{ in the chart domain on }E_{\Omega}\bigr\}\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $\mathcal I_{\xi}(U)$ is the nonnegative factor multiplying the group Dirac factors in \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE}, including $\chi_1$, $\zeta$, $\chi_0'$ and the gauge-fixing and action exponential, and $t_{\xi}$ is defined where $UU_1(\xi)^{-1}$ lies in the chart domain bond by bond on $E_{\Omega}$, as the chart logarithm of \cite[(1.13)]{BalabanCRE}. Thus $\mathcal U_{\xi}\supseteq D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$, the fibre of the full integration domain of \cite{BalabanCRE} (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), the fibre defined by all factors of (1.11) and not by the starred group tests $\chi_0'$ alone, with equality at every outer datum satisfying the exterior constraint $V(c)= M(V_0,c)$ on the rows $c$ of $\Omega_1^c$ ($\bar V_0= V$, Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), the one condition of $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ absent from $\mathcal U_{\xi}$ (the outer measure $\omega$ defined below is carried by that set), when $\mathcal I_{\xi}(U)>0$ is read as including that the averages and means in (1.11) are defined (the domain convention recorded in (B1)); the fluctuations $UU_1^{-1}$ of $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ lie in the chart domain by (B1).

The linearising change (1.14) is the map $A\mapsto A-h_{\xi}\widetilde D_{\xi}(A)$ on the open set $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv), which contains $g_0\mathsf C_{\xi}\mathcal A_{\xi}$, whose Jacobian is the determinant of (B4)(iii); restricted to the constraint surface, the range of $g_0\mathsf C_{\xi}$, it is $z\mapsto q_{\xi}(g_0\mathsf C_{\xi} z)$, and on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ it is $q_{U_1}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-local-phase}: $q_{\xi}(g_0\mathsf C_{\xi} B)= q_{U_1}(B)$ for $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$, with the row solutions of (B4)(i) and $\mathsf C_{\xi}=\mathsf C_{U_1}$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}). The Jacobian of $q_{\xi}$ involves $\widetilde D_{\xi}$ on $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$, a neighbourhood of $g_0\mathsf C_{\xi}\mathcal A_{\xi}$ in $\mathfrak g^{E_{\Omega}}$ on which the row solutions are defined and analytic ((B4)(i), Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv)); data that are not branches contribute zero.

The boundary change is $\Psi_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map}, \cite[(1.22)]{BalabanCRE} with the cutoff $g$ on the bonds of $(R_1^{\sim2}\cap S_1)^*$, the set defined at p.251, and its second form ($g$ replaced by $1$, the form of p.252) on the other bonds of $S_1^*$, a set differing from the one printed at p.252 as recorded in Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}, from new free variables to old free variables. The change of variables on these branches is Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection} (the (1.22) part of (B4)(ii)): $\Psi_{\xi}$ maps $\mathcal D_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:c-new-variable-domain} bijectively onto $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain}, and $\mathcal A_{\xi}\subseteq\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\xi}$, since for $B\in\mathcal A_{\xi}$ the field $U(B)$ lies in $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)\subseteq\mathcal U_{\xi}$ with $t_{\xi}(U(B))= q_{U_1}(B)$ chart-valued and $g_0^{-1}q_{U_1}(B)|_{E_{\Omega,*}}= B$. The integration fibre over $A_{\mathrm e}$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-change-domain}
    \mathcal D_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})\coloneqq
        \bigl\{ a\in\mathfrak g^D\, | \,(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}\bigr\}\;,
\end{equation}
the open box $\{\Theta_{\xi}=1\}$ on a branch (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(iv)). The real coordinate changes and their inverses are restricted to these domains. Their transformed indicators are retained in $\Theta_D^{\sigma}$ and the exterior factors (1.25). Values outside the admitted domains contribute zero.

Let $v_{\xi},V_{\xi}$ be the functions in \cite[(1.15)--(1.16)]{BalabanCRE}: $v_{\xi}$ contains the Haar logarithms and the logarithm of the Jacobian of the linearising substitution (1.14) (\cite[p.~249]{BalabanCRE} says that $v$ is the sum of the first two terms under the second exponential ``in (1.15)''; as printed this points to (1.15) itself, whose second exponential begins with the quadratic form and $v$; the display meant is (1.14), whose second exponential begins with $\log\sigma(A-h\widetilde D(A))+\operatorname{Tr}\log(I-h(\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D)(A))$, and $v$ is read as the normalised Haar logarithm plus $\log|\det(\id-h_{\xi}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D_{\xi})|$, Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} and the paragraph following \eqref{eq:retained-positive-kernel}), and $V_{\xi}$ contains the remaining Taylor residual of the action and gauge fixing. These are the full functions, before the boundary change. For $z$ in their real domain let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-prechange-density}
    p_{\xi}(z)\coloneqq\exp\left[
        -\frac{1}{2}\langle z,\mathsf H_{\xi} z\rangle
        +v_{\xi}(g_0\mathsf C_{\xi} z)
        -g_0^{-2}V_{\xi}(g_0\mathsf C_{\xi} z)\right]\;.
\end{equation}
With $\Theta_D^{\sigma}(a)=\prod_{b\in D}\mathbf1_{\{| a(b)|_{\sigma}< r\}}$, in the bond norm of \cite[(1.18)]{BalabanCRE}, written $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ as in \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff} with the fixed $\sigma$ of this section, which is the norm of the integration-carrier cutoff \eqref{eq:native-source-young-cutoff} (so at $D= I$, $\Theta_D^{\sigma}=\Theta_{\xi}$ on $\mathfrak g^I$, the integration fibre \eqref{eq:retained-change-domain} is the box $\{\Theta_D^{\sigma}=1\}$ on a branch, and $\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})}\Theta_D^{\sigma}=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})}$ there), the conditional density and integral are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-positive-kernel}
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathcal K_{\xi}(a)&\coloneqq
            \mathbf1_{\mathcal D_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})}(a)\Theta_D^{\sigma}(a)
            p_{\xi}(\Psi_{\xi}(z_{\xi}(a)))
            |\det D\Psi_{\xi}(z_{\xi}(a))|\;,\\
        \mathcal J_{\xi}[f]&\coloneqq\int
            f(U_{\xi}(a))\mathcal K_{\xi}(a)\,\dd a\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Here $\mathcal J_{\xi}$ and $\mathcal K_{\xi}$ are the $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}$ and $\mathcal K_{\xi}$ of the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}, written in the variable $a$ of the integration fibre.

The determinant inside $v_{\xi}$, the Jacobian of \cite[(1.14)]{BalabanCRE} (not $|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|$, the Jacobian of the boundary change in \eqref{eq:retained-positive-kernel}), is that of the map $A\mapsto A-h_{\xi}\widetilde D_{\xi}(A)$ on $\mathfrak g^{E_{\Omega}}$, the phases on all bonds of $\Omega_1$; it equals the determinant of its designated block, the product over the rows of the determinants in \eqref{eq:native-source-jacobian-primitive} (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:primitive-sum}: $h_{\xi}$ has outputs on the designated bonds only, so the free rows of $\id-h_{\xi}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D_{\xi}$ are identity rows, $b_0(c)$ is the only designated bond of $\mathcal E_c$, Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}, and $\widetilde D_{\xi,c}$ depends on $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$ only, Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}).

Every change of variables uses its absolute real Jacobian: $v_{\xi}$ contains $\log|\det(\id-h_{\xi}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D_{\xi})|$, the sum over the rows of \eqref{eq:native-source-jacobian-primitive}, and the logarithms of the positive normalised Haar density, so $p_{\xi}>0$ where it is defined and $\mathcal K_{\xi}\geqslant 0$; the determinant is positive on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ ((B4)(iii), Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iv)) and the real logarithm written in \cite{BalabanCRE} agrees with this. The definition retains $p_{\xi}\circ\Psi_{\xi}$ without a truncation of the boundary terms described after \cite[(1.24)]{BalabanCRE}.

The exterior expression of \cite{BalabanCRE} is the sum over region labels and integral over $(V_0,A_{\mathrm e})$, with the constraint $\delta(\bar V_0V^{-1})$, the retained region indicators, $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$, Haar factors and the prefactors of (1.15), including $z^{(0)}$. Its exterior factors are evaluated at their transformed arguments. After splitting the good tests into their $D$ and exterior bond factors, the factors remaining from (1.25) are independent of $a$: Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(ii), under the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} (its collar hypothesis is their condition $LMR_1>4R_{\mathrm c}+4L^2M_2R_1+8$; the collar \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes} is that of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}), separates the bad and changed tests from $D$, and factors of good tests on $D$ are redundant by idempotence. Those exterior factors, including any dependence on $A_{\mathrm e}$, remain in $\mathcal O_V$.

The maps in these integrals are jointly Borel in their parameters and integration variables, by the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}: the background $U_1$ is Borel on the Borel set of admissible pairs (the uniqueness statement of \cite{BalabanCRE} for the critical point in the domain of integration in (1.11), (B1), and the theorems for Borel graphs with singleton sections); pairs that are not admissible have $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)=\varnothing$, hence zero source weight. The configuration of \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE} is the configuration described at p.251, on its prescribed determining data, the notation $M^{\bigcdot }(W)$ being the level-wise collection $M^j(W)$ of \cite[(2.11)]{BalabanCRE}, at the first step $W$ and $M(W)$; the measurable choices of $U_{1,\square'}(V)$ and of $U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ are the Borel choices of Lemma~\ref{lem:borel-minimiser}, fixed in (B1). The value of $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ used in (1.22) is $L\frac1i\log(U_1U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)^{-1})$ by (1.21), the chart logarithm of a relative configuration lying in the chart domain on $S_1^*$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}), and is Borel in $(V,V_0)$. The maps $Q_1^{s*}$ in \cite[(1.3)]{BalabanCRE} and the averages on these regular data are Borel as well.

The matrix coefficients of $\mathsf C_{\xi},h_{\xi}$ are obtained by inversion of the invertible designated coefficient operators $\alpha_c(U_1)$, so they are Borel in the background.
