The row solutions $\widetilde D_{\xi}$ of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} are Borel on $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ jointly with the branch data, by the Lusin--Novikov argument of the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} (the set $\mathsf P$ of pairs $(B,d)$ with $d$ a chart-class solution family at $g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ for which $U_d(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ with the cutoff (1.25) nonzero is Borel with sections of at most one point, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii)), and so is $\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D_{\xi}$ (measurability paragraph).

In \cite[(1.22)]{BalabanCRE}, the cutoff $g$ is the fixed $C^{\infty}$ function of the paragraph defining \eqref{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map}, each $\psi_b$ is $C^{\infty}$ on its open domain $\mathcal W_b$ (the chart logarithm and the exponential are analytic there), and the boundary data have just been shown Borel. Hence $\Psi_{\xi}(z)$ and its Jacobian are jointly Borel, and $C^{\infty}$ in $z$. The sets $\mathcal A_{\xi}$ and $\mathcal D_{\xi}$, and the integration fibres \eqref{eq:retained-change-domain}, sections of the Borel set $\mathcal D_{\xi}$, are Borel (measurability paragraph).

The Hessian coefficients, $v_{\xi}$, $V_{\xi}$ and the constraint factor $z^{(0)}$ are Borel: each is a finite sum or product of the Haar logarithm, the plaquette and gauge terms of the action and gauge fixing, the row determinants and the coefficients of $\alpha_c(U_1)^{-1}$, evaluated at the background, the phase and the row solutions, that is a continuous function of $(U_1,A,\widetilde D_{\xi}(A),\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\widetilde D_{\xi}(A))$ and of the Taylor coefficients at $A=0$ of the germs of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}, themselves continuous in $U_1$ by the implicit function theorem, composed with maps that are Borel jointly in the branch data and $a$ (the background, the row solutions and their derivative, measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}). The vacuum exponential is a constant, and $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ is a finite product of small-field tests, indicators of sets defined by inequalities between continuous functions of $(V,V_0)$ on the open set where the local means entering them are defined, and of gauge-fixing exponentials of continuous functions of $(V,V_0)$ on that set, every factor being set to zero where a local mean it contains is undefined (the convention of this paper for $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$, matching the chart convention of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} for the tests); so $\zeta(\Omega_1^c)$ is Borel as well.

Together with the indicators, these facts prove joint Borel measurability of $U_{\xi}(a)$, $\mathcal K_{\xi}(a)$ and the outer weights.

For an empty carrier, its Lie-algebra space is a point with unit measure; empty sums equal zero, and empty products and zero-dimensional determinants equal one. If $\Omega_1$ is empty, $U_1= U_{\xi}= V_0$ on every bond.

The exterior group Dirac factors have a kernel interpretation as well. Let $\omega$ be the joint outer measure in \cite[(1.15), (1.25)]{BalabanCRE}, retaining $V$, the region labels, $V_0$ and $A_{\mathrm e}$: in the notation of \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}, $\int F\,\dd\omega=\int\mathcal O[F](V)\,\dd V$ for nonnegative Borel $F$ of the outer data, in the sense fixed in Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} (the integral of $F$ against the measure in $V$ that the outer operation defines; $\mathcal O[F](V)$ is not a density). It contains exactly the exterior factors specified above. Its group Dirac factors are read by first integrating them against the corresponding coarse bond variables, with Haar measure on the remaining coarse variables; this defines a positive joint measure.

Its weighted measure $\bar\eta=\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]\omega$ is finite and its $V$ marginal is the measure $\rho_1$ of \eqref{eq:first-step}: the operations in \cite[(1.1)--(1.25)]{BalabanCRE}, performed as listed after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} with a bounded Borel test $h(V)$ retained (signed; $h(V)= h(\mathsf M(U))$ is invariant under the gauge transformations $u$ of (1.5), which are the identity at the block centres (the printed ``$z\neq y$'' in \cite[(1.5)]{BalabanCRE} read as $x\neq y$, as in (1.7)), Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}(ii), so the Faddeev--Popov step applies with it inserted; every integral below is finite: $\int\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]\,\dd\omega=\mathcal Z_0<\infty$ is the case $h=1$ of the first identity below, both sides being the integral of one nonnegative Borel integrand over all variables by Tonelli, and $|\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}]|\leqslant \mathcal J_{\xi}[1]$) and with insertion $1$ or $W_{\chi}$, give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-outer-measure-identities}
    \begin{aligned}
        \int h(V)\,\dd\rho_1(V)
            &=\int h(V)\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]\,\dd\omega(V,\xi)\;,\\
        \int h(V)\,\dd N_1(V)
            &=\int h(V)\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )]\,\dd\omega(V,\xi)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Taking $h=1$ in the first equality gives $\bar\eta$ the total mass $\mathcal Z_0<\infty$. Let $Q_V$ be the regular conditional probability of $\bar\eta$ on the outer data given $V$, defined for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$ (disintegration of the finite measure $\bar\eta$ with respect to its marginal $\rho_1$ along the coordinate projection $\xi\mapsto V$: the measure disintegration theorem for standard Borel spaces, \cite[(17.35)]{Kechris}, stated there as an exercise with the standard proof, through a Borel isomorphism $\phi$ \cite[Theorem 15.6]{Kechris} of the outer space with $[0,1]$ and the Radon--Nikodym derivatives with respect to $\rho_1$ of the countably many measures $B\mapsto\bar\eta(\{\xi:V(\xi)\in B,\ \phi(\xi)\leqslant t\})$, $t$ rational, regularised to a Borel map $V\mapsto Q_V$ into the probability measures; the outer space, a finite union over the region labels of products of the compact groups $G^{E_1}$, $G^{E\setminus E_{\Omega}}$ and the Euclidean space $\mathfrak g^J$, is Polish, hence standard Borel, and on the branches $\bar\eta$ is carried by a bounded set, $g_0A_{\mathrm e}(b)$ lying in the chart ball for every $b\in J$, so the compact case would suffice. The theorem gives: $Q_V$ is a probability measure for every $V$ off a Borel $\rho_1$-null set, $V\mapsto Q_V(E)$ is Borel for every Borel $E$, $\bar\eta(E)=\int Q_V(E)\,\dd\rho_1(V)$, $Q_V$ is concentrated on the fibre $\{\xi:V(\xi)= V\}$ for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$, and two such maps agree for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$; the concentration is what replaces $h(V(\xi))$ by $h(V)$ in the identity displayed below, and the uniqueness makes $\mathcal O_V$ below independent of the version off a $\rho_1$-null set).

For a nonnegative measurable outer function $F$, the exterior operator is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-outer-kernel}
    \mathcal O_V[F]\coloneqq
        \int_{\{0<\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]<\infty\}}
            \frac{F(\xi)}{\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]}\,\dd Q_V(\xi)\;.
\end{equation}
This defines a positive kernel for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$. It gives $\omega$ back on finite-positive-mass outer data: $\int h(V)\mathcal O_V[F]\,\dd\rho_1(V)=\int h(V)F(\xi)\mathbf 1_{\{0<\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]<\infty\}}\,\dd\omega(V,\xi)$ for nonnegative Borel $F$ and bounded Borel $h\geqslant 0$, since $\dd\bar\eta=\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]\,\dd\omega$, and for signed bounded Borel $h$ whenever $\int F\mathbf 1_{\{0<\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]<\infty\}}\,\dd\omega<\infty$.

In this sense $\mathcal O_V$ represents the exterior expression of \cite{BalabanCRE}: integrated against bounded Borel $h(V)$, it reproduces the $\omega$-integral of every outer function supported on the branches.

On the Borel $\rho_1$-null set where $Q_V$ is not defined, $\mathcal O_V=0$, so that $V\mapsto\mathcal O_V[F]$ is Borel. It extends linearly to complex $F$ whenever $\mathcal O_V[| F|]<\infty$. In particular $\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]]= Q_V(\{0<\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]<\infty\})=1$ for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$, by the next paragraph. The changes of variables are those of the unrestricted construction of \cite{BalabanCRE}, recorded after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}.

The outer data with $0<\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]<\infty$ are exactly the branches in the sense of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}: $\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]=0$ when the integration fibre $\mathcal D_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ is empty, that is off the branches of that section, while on a branch $\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]<\infty$ (measurability paragraph) and $\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]>0$, since $\mathcal K_{\xi}>0$ on the nonempty open box $\mathcal D_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ ($p_{\xi}>0$, $|\det D\Psi_{\xi}|>0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection}, and $\Theta_D^{\sigma}=1$ there).

Zero-mass data are $\bar\eta$-null, hence $Q_V$-null for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$. Data with infinite conditional mass are $\omega$-null, since $\int\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]\,\dd\omega=\mathcal Z_0<\infty$ (the case $h=1$ of \eqref{eq:retained-outer-measure-identities}, with $\mathcal Z_0=\rho_1(G^{E_1})$ by \eqref{eq:one-step-physical-partition}), hence $\bar\eta$-null and $Q_V$-null for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$. So $Q_V$ is carried by the branches for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$. All branch contractions below are zero off the branches.

Coverage uses the fixed geometric stencils $\Lambda_b$ of Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}: $\Lambda_b=\{ b\}$ for a free bond, and $\Lambda_{b_0(c)}=\mathcal S_c\cap E_*$ for a designated bond, where $\mathcal S_c$ contains the bonds with both endpoints in the two endpoint blocks of $c$. Let $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ consist of the branches on which every fine contour bond is a bond of $\Omega_1$ and $\Lambda_b\subseteq D$ for every such bond. The geometric condition depends only on region labels, and is precisely the coverage used in Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}; at the carrier $D= I$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1} it is the covered event of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} and of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}, since $\Lambda_b=\mathcal F_b$ for every fine bond ($\mathcal S_c\cap E_*=\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$, both being the free positive bonds with both endpoints in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$, \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-bonds} and \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-extension-support}).

Since \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes} supplies the collar condition at the carrier $D= I(\xi)$ of every branch, Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} defines $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$.

\subsection{The Closed Flux Insertions}

Let $\bar C\coloneqq(c_1,\ldots,c_m)$ be the oriented coarse square, with $m=4n$, and let $C$ be the concatenation of its straight fine paths. Let $\xi$ be a covered conditional history, with constrained background $U_1= U_1(\xi)$. For each positive coarse bond traversed by $\bar C$, the first and last fine bonds of its straight path lie inside its initial and final blocks, respectively, since $L\geqslant 3$. Coverage puts these bonds in $\Omega_1$. As $\Omega_1$ is a union of blocks, both endpoint blocks lie there. In particular $c$ is a bond of the coarse region $\Omega_1^{(1)}$, so \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} imposes $M(U_1,c)= V(c)$. Here a bond of a region has at least one endpoint in that region, as in \cite[Introduction]{BalabanVAR}; both endpoints belong in this case. Reversed traversals use the constraint on the underlying positive bond. All relative logarithms are in the regular chart used in \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average}.

For a positive coarse bond $c$, $Y_c$ is defined by the first formula below. The averaging constraint and \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} then give the second:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-flux}
    Y_c(\xi)= e^{-i\beta_c(U_1)},
    \qquad P_c(U_1)= Y_c(\xi)V(c)\;.
\end{equation}
Thus $Y_c$ depends on the closed relative contours inside the two endpoint blocks of $c$. Let $V(c^{-1})\coloneqq V(c)^{-1}$. For a reversed traversal,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-flux-reversal}
    Y_{c^{-1}}(\xi)= V(c)^{-1}Y_c(\xi)^{-1}V(c),
    \qquad P_{c^{-1}}(U_1)= Y_{c^{-1}}(\xi)V(c)^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}
The second identity follows by inverting $P_c= Y_cV(c)$. The factor is therefore based at the initial vertex of the reversed traversal as well.

The closed contraction is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-loop-insertion}
    \mathcal L_{\xi}(C;V)
        \coloneqq\chi\left(Y_{c_1}(\xi)V(c_1)
            \cdots Y_{c_m}(\xi)V(c_m)\right)
        = W_{\chi}(C;U_1(\xi))\;.
\end{equation}
This equality follows by substituting \eqref{eq:retained-flux} and \eqref{eq:retained-flux-reversal} in the ordered fine holonomy.

Under a site gauge $u$, the closed logarithms in \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} and their exponentials are conjugated at $c_-$. Consequently
\begin{equation}
    Y_{c_i}\longmapsto u(c_{i,-})Y_{c_i}u(c_{i,-})^{-1},
    \qquad V(c_i)\longmapsto
        u(c_{i,-})V(c_i)u(c_{i,+})^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}
The intermediate gauge factors cancel in the ordered product and its character is invariant. All subsequent insertions in this section are closed contractions.

Different histories at the same $V$ can have different constrained backgrounds and different insertions.

\subsection{The Numerator Carried to the Next Transformation}

The exterior operator $\mathcal O_V$ of \eqref{eq:retained-outer-kernel} and the conditional integral $\mathcal J_{\xi}$ defined before it give, for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-conditional-law}
    \mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]]=1,
    \qquad W_1(C;V)=\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )]]\;,
\end{equation}
that is, $\dd N_1=\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )]]\,\dd\rho_1$.

The identities in \eqref{eq:retained-conditional-law} are identities of measures on $G^{E_1}$, tested against bounded Borel functions. Let $\mathfrak M$ be the image of $\rho_0(U)\,\dd U$ under $U\mapsto(M(U),U)$, a finite positive measure on $G^{E_1}\times G^E$ (the blocking kernel (0.1) with bare weight $\rho_0\,\dd U$, in the reading of \eqref{eq:bare-blocking-operator}). Its $V$ marginal is $\rho_1$. Disintegration on these standard Borel spaces supplies conditional probabilities $\nu_V$ on fine fields, for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$. For bounded Borel functions $f$ on $G^E$ and $h$ on $G^{E_1}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-disintegration}
    \int h(V)f(U)\,\dd\mathfrak M(V,U)
        =\int h(M(U))f(U)\rho_0(U)\,\dd U
        =\int h(V)
            \left(\int f(U)\,\dd\nu_V(U)\right)\,\dd\rho_1(V)\;.
\end{equation}
In particular, with $f= W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )$ and \eqref{eq:first-step}, $\int h\,\dd N_1=\int h(V)\int W_{\chi}(C;U)\,\dd\nu_V(U)\,\dd\rho_1(V)$, so $W_1(C;V)=\int W_{\chi}(C;U)\,\dd\nu_V(U)$ for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$, the conditional form of \eqref{eq:outgoing-loop}; the operations below act on the middle member of \eqref{eq:retained-disintegration}.

The averaging operation is \eqref{eq:global-average}, Borel and gauge covariant by Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}; \eqref{eq:nonlinear-average} is its formula on $\mathcal O_c$, which contains every configuration of $D^{(11)}$ on the rows of $\Omega_1$ (the domain convention recorded in (B1)).

For $f=1$ or $W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )$, the operations of \cite[(1.1)--(1.25)]{BalabanCRE} listed after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} are applied with $h(V)$ retained. The partitions are pointwise decompositions of unity. The Faddeev--Popov step (1.5)--(1.6) is applied to the operator (0.1) with the averaging choice \eqref{eq:global-average}, whose covariance on all of $G^E$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}(ii); the closed Wilson character ($| W_{\chi}|\leqslant 1$, $\chi$ being a normalised irreducible character) is invariant under its fine gauges. The changes of variables pull that character back to $W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a))$, and $h(V)$ stays fixed: the gauge transformations of (1.5) are the identity at the block centres, so $M(U)$, hence $h(M(U))$, is unchanged by them (Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}(ii)), and the later changes of variables are at fixed $V$. Cutoff factors are removed only where \cite{BalabanCRE} states they equal one, and the boundary change is retained as \eqref{eq:retained-positive-kernel}.

Thus the operations supply \eqref{eq:retained-outer-measure-identities} against every bounded Borel $h$; since $|\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}]|\leqslant \mathcal J_{\xi}[1]$ (nonnegativity of \eqref{eq:retained-positive-kernel}), $\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}]$ vanishes where $\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]=0$, and $\{\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]=\infty\}$ is $\omega$-null, so both $\omega$-integrals are integrals over the branches, and with \eqref{eq:retained-outer-kernel} they give $\int h\,\dd\rho_1=\int h(V)\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]]\,\dd\rho_1(V)$ and $\int h\,\dd N_1=\int h(V)\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}(C;\bigcdot )]]\,\dd\rho_1(V)$. Equality of these finite measures gives the $\rho_1$-almost-everywhere identities \eqref{eq:retained-conditional-law}, the second by the uniqueness of the Radon--Nikodym derivative \eqref{eq:outgoing-loop}.

Nonnegativity of \eqref{eq:retained-positive-kernel} gives $|\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}]|\leqslant \mathcal J_{\xi}[1]$, hence $|\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[W_{\chi}]]|\leqslant \mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]]=1$, the bound $| W_1|\leqslant 1$ of Section~1.

For the covered branches $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ defined above, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-leading-source}
    \mathcal L_{\xi}^{(0)}(C;V)\coloneqq
    \begin{cases}
        \kappa_C e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}\mathcal L_{\xi}(C;V),
            &\xi\in A_{\mathrm{cov}},\\
        0,&\xi\notin A_{\mathrm{cov}}.
    \end{cases}
\end{equation}
Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} (Appendix~\ref{app:regional-scalar}) identifies its coefficient with $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$ on covered histories, with $E^{\circ}_{\xi}= E^{\circ}_{I,C_n,T}$ at the carrier $D= I= D_+$ (all free bonds with an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$, the convention of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1}). Its period and coupling hypotheses are fixed for the square; its boundary-distance terms allow arbitrary covered regional labels. The error $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ depends only on those discrete labels; the background and branch indicator are Borel by the preceding construction, so this leading term is measurable.

The other source terms are retained as the following conditional integral, with the same denominator:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-source-correction}
    \mathcal H_{\xi}(C;V)=
        \frac{1}{\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]}
        \int\left[W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a))-\mathcal L_{\xi}^{(0)}(C;V)\right]
            \mathcal K_{\xi}(a)\,\dd a\;.
\end{equation}
On an uncovered branch, $\mathcal L_{\xi}^{(0)}=0$ and $\mathcal H_{\xi}$ is the normalised conditional Wilson integral. Its history average enters \eqref{eq:thm-main-identity} through the defect and boundary terms $E_{\mathrm{def}}$, $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:c4c-5-2}, which Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}(ii) bounds.

For this fixed square, \eqref{eq:regional-square-error} and $|\chi|\leqslant 1$ give $|\mathcal L_{\xi}^{(0)}|\leqslant B_C$, where $B_C\coloneqq|\kappa_C|\exp(C\tau^2(9n+1))<\infty$ (the constant $C$ of \eqref{eq:regional-square-error}, not the contour). Consequently $\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]|\mathcal H_{\xi}|\leqslant (1+B_C)\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]$. The numerator terms below are therefore integrable for the complex extension of \eqref{eq:retained-outer-kernel} at $\rho_1$-almost every $V$.

Substitution in \eqref{eq:retained-conditional-law} gives the following first-step identity for $\rho_1$-almost every $V$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-first-step-numerator}
    W_1(C;V)=\mathcal O_V\left[
        \mathcal J_{\xi}[1]
        \bigl(\mathcal L_{\xi}^{(0)}(C;V)+\mathcal H_{\xi}(C;V)\bigr)\right]\;.
\end{equation}
More explicitly, let $\nu_{\xi}=(U_{\xi})_*(\mathcal K_{\xi}(a)\,\dd a/\mathcal J_{\xi}[1])$ be the probability measure on fine fields carried by the branch. Under a fine gauge transformation $u$ (acting on $V$ at the block centres, Lemma~\ref{lem:global-average}(ii)), $\nu_{\xi}$ is replaced by its pushforward $(U\mapsto U^u)_*\nu_{\xi}$, together with $U_1^u$ and $V^u$. Both closed characters in \eqref{eq:retained-source-correction} are invariant, $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ depends only on the unchanged region labels, and change of variables preserves the normalised conditional integral. An axial-gauge representative and its conditional measure are transported together. The physical denominator is $\mathcal Z_0=\rho_1(G^{E_1})$.

For $\rho_1$-almost every $V$, the scalar-extracted outgoing observable is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:retained-outgoing-observable}
    \widehat W_1(C;V)\coloneqq\frac{W_1(C;V)}{\kappa_C}
        =\frac{\mathcal O_V\left[\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]
            \bigl(\kappa_C^{-1}\mathcal L_{\xi}^{(0)}(C;V)
                +\kappa_C^{-1}\mathcal H_{\xi}(C;V)\bigr)\right]}
            {\mathcal O_V[\mathcal J_{\xi}[1]]}\;.
\end{equation}
The factor $\kappa_C$ is nonzero: \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass} defines its finite perimeter exponent and \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor} writes $z_{\mathrm c}$ as the exponential of the convergent corner sum.

The pair of the complex measure $\kappa_C^{-1}N_1$ and the measure $\rho_1$ is the input to the next blocking transformation ($T$ acting on measures by the pushforward $T\mu= M_*\mu$ of Section~1). Equation~\eqref{eq:retained-loop-insertion} displays its leading closed insertion; \eqref{eq:retained-source-correction} specifies the other source terms carried with it. Iterating this representation requires local estimates for their transformed activities, including correlations between attachments and their boundary dependence.

\section{The Exponential Moment of the Leading Error}
\label{sec:leading-moment}

This section bounds the history average of $e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}$, where $E^{\circ}_{\xi}\coloneqq E^{\circ}_{I,C_n,T}$ is the exponent of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} at the carrier $I=\Lambda_1^*$.

The conventions are those of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1}: $C= C_n$ has $n_C=4nL$ contour bonds, $C_j$ is the set of contour bonds of the coarse segment $j\in J_C$, $K_j$ is the union of their free-input stencils, $d_j$ and $\iota_T$ are the distances \eqref{eq:c4c-1-1}, and $d_T$ is the periodic fine-bond metric $d_T(b,c)= d_{\infty,T}(x_b,x_c)+\mathbf 1\{\text{directions differ}\}$ fixed after \eqref{eq:marginal-covariance-input}, with $x_b$ the initial site of $b$. The periods are compatible and even (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}). $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ and $\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}$ are the history expectation \eqref{eq:c3-6-1} and its probability (weight $\mathsf w_{\xi}$, normalisation $\mathcal Z_0$), $B_{\xi}=\Lambda_1^c$ is the filled bad region and $E(X)$ the set of positive fine bonds with at least one endpoint in $X$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}), and $q= n_W\max(z_P,z_G)$ is the one-point rate of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}, with $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ for $0< g_0< g_*$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}).

A free bond outside the carrier is marked: $I$ is the set of all free bonds with an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$, so a free bond $b\notin I$ has both endpoints in $B_{\xi}$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:outside-carrier-marked}
    \mathbf 1\{ b\notin I\}\leqslant \mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}\;.
\end{equation}

\subsection{Scales}

$r=\delta_0/g_0= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$, with $\varepsilon_0= g_0A_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ and $\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$ \cite[pp.~246--247]{BalabanCRE}. By \cite[(2.6), p.~255]{BalabanCRE} ($n=1$, $m=0$), $g_1\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_0$ and $g_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_1$, so for small $g_0$, $\tfrac12\log g_0^{-2}\leqslant \log g_1^{-2}\leqslant 2\log g_0^{-2}$. $R_1$ is the smallest power of $L$ with $R_1\geqslant (\log g_1^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$ \cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE}, so $R_1\leqslant L(2\log g_0^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$, and with $p_0(g)= A_0(\log g^{-2})^{p_0}$ \eqref{eq:c3-1-1},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c5-3-1}
    \ell= LMR_1\leqslant L^2M(2\log g_0^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}\;,\qquad\pi_*=\min(p_0(g_0),p_0(g_1))\geqslant A_0\bigl(\tfrac12\log g_0^{-2}\bigr)^{p_0}\;,
\end{equation}
where $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r\geqslant 10$ \cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE}.

\subsection{The Refined Split}

\begin{corollary}[The Refined Split]\label{cor:refined-split}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, with its constants $C$ and $c$, and with $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$, on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:refined-split}
    | E^{\circ}_{\xi}|\leqslant C\tau^2(2+1/c)+C\tau^2\sum_{j\in J_C}e^{-cd_j}\;.
\end{equation}
For $n\geqslant 1$ the condition $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$ holds when $N_{\min}\geqslant 4R_0+(4/c)\log(4n)$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} bounds $| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|$ by $C\tau^2[\sum_je^{-cd_j}+4ne^{-c\iota_T}+(n+1)e^{-cn}]$, and $(n+1)e^{-cn}\leqslant 1+\sup_{x\geqslant 0}xe^{-cx}=1+1/(ec)\leqslant 1+1/c$. When $N_{\min}\geqslant 4R_0+(4/c)\log(4n)$, $\iota_T= N_{\min}/4-R_0\geqslant (1/c)\log(4n)$, so $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$.
\end{proof}

Under the torus condition the only part of the bound that grows with $n$ is the boundary sum $\sum_je^{-cd_j}\leqslant 4n$. Each of its terms is at most $1$ and exponentially small in $d_T(K_j,I^c)-R_0$, and the sum is zero when $I^c=\varnothing$.

\subsection{The Joint Witness Bound}

\begin{lemma}[Joint Witness Bound]\label{lem:c5-7-joint}
Let $K=256$ be the constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}, $\sigma_K\coloneqq 2K\ell+4$ and $C_K\coloneqq 4(2\sigma_K+1)^4=4(4K\ell+9)^4$, an upper bound on the number of bonds whose initial site lies within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $\sigma_K$ of a given site. For $g_0$ below the thresholds of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} and~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}, for every finite set $\mathsf S$ of bonds and every subset $\mathsf S'$ of $\mathsf S$ whose initial sites are at pairwise $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $>\sigma_K$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c5-7-joint-I}
    \begin{gathered}
    \mathbb P_{\mathrm h}\bigl(\mathsf S\subseteq E(B_{\xi})\bigr)=\mathcal Z_0^{-1}\int\mathcal O\Bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\prod_{z\in\mathsf S}\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}\Bigr]\dd V\leqslant q^{\,|\mathsf S'|}\;,\quad\text{and}\\
    \mathbb P_{\mathrm h}\bigl(\mathsf S\subseteq E(B_{\xi})\bigr)\leqslant q^{\,|\mathsf S|/C_K}\;.
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The marks $\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}$ are functions of the regions and of the deterministic filling, they take the values $0$ and $1$, and $\prod_{z\in\mathsf S}\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}\leqslant \prod_{z\in\mathsf S'}\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}$. The reversal of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-3} is a change of variables for integrals of the density times a nonnegative function of $U$ and the regions, so it applies with the product of the marks of $\mathsf S'$ inserted.

After the reversal, on the support of the cutoffs, each mark is dominated by $\mathbf 1_{W_z}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}, \eqref{eq:c3-7-9}). Here $W_z$ is taken as the union, over the plaquette labels $p$ and the gauge-variable labels $w$ all of whose sites (the four corners of $p$; the centre of $w$ and the site of its variable) lie within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $K\ell+1$ of $x_z$, of the single-witness events $\{| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta\}$ and $\{| w-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta\}$. The domination holds with this union. The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} places the witness in the neighbourhood $N(Q)$ of a bad test cube $Q$, every site of a witnessing plaquette within $117\ell+1$ of $x_z$, and the centre of a gauge label lies within $L$ of the site of its variable; so every site of the witnessing label lies within $117\ell+L+1\leqslant K\ell+1$ of $x_z$.

The union has at most $7(2K\ell+3)^4\leqslant n_W$ labels: at most $(2K\ell+3)^4$ sites lie within $K\ell+1$ of $x_z$, a plaquette is fixed by its base site and one of six plane orientations, and a gauge label by the noncentral site of its variable, which determines the centre (the centre of its block). So $\bigcap_{z\in\mathsf S'}W_z$ is contained in a union of at most $n_W^{|\mathsf S'|}$ intersections of single-witness events, one label per bond of $\mathsf S'$.

For each such choice, two bonds of $\mathsf S'$ have initial sites at distance $>\sigma_K=2(K\ell+1)+2$, so their labels have all their sites at distance $>2$ from each other: the chosen gauge variables are distinct, and the chosen plaquettes have distinct base cubes $C_x$ (the closed unit cube whose minimal corner $x$ is the plaquette's base site). Under the product measure $\mu_0\otimes q_g^{\otimes\mathcal I}\otimes\mathrm{Haar}^{\otimes T}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-9} the probability of the intersection factorises into the $\mu_0$-probability of the plaquette events and the product of the $q_g$-probabilities of the gauge-variable events, each of the latter at most $z_G$ \eqref{eq:c3-7-13}.

For the plaquette events the chessboard estimate \eqref{eq:c3-7-chessboard} applies with $f_x$, for each chosen base cube $C_x$, the indicator $\mathbf 1\{| U(\partial p_0)-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta\}$ of the plaquette $p_0$ of $C_0$ whose transport $f_x^{[x]}$ is the indicator of the chosen plaquette of $C_x$, and $f_x=1$ for the other cubes. Every plaquette of $C_x$ is the transport of a plaquette of $C_0$ of the same plane orientation: a reflection in direction $\rho$ carries the transverse coordinate $t\in\{0,1\}$ of a face to $1-t$, so the face of $C_0$ with transverse coordinates $(t_{\rho})$ is carried to the face of $C_x$ with transverse coordinates $x_{\rho}+t_{\rho}$ or $x_{\rho}+1-t_{\rho}$ according to the parity of $x_{\rho}$, and the indicator does not depend on the orientation or the base point of the plaquette. Each root $(\int\prod_yf_x^{[y]}\,\dd\mu_0)^{1/V_T}$ of a disseminated expectation is at most $z_P$ by the computation in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}, which applies to every plaquette of $C_0$: its dissemination contains $V_T/4$ distinct plaquettes of its orientation, each with $s_G\geqslant b_G\theta^2$ on the event, and \eqref{eq:c3-7-11} bounds $\mathcal Z_0$ below. Hence each choice has probability at most $\max(z_P,z_G)^{|\mathsf S'|}$, and the union bound over the choices gives $(n_W\max(z_P,z_G))^{|\mathsf S'|}= q^{|\mathsf S'|}$.

As in Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-3}, the product measure represents the integral before the history conditions; the factorisation is that of the physical measure after the reversal, and the correlation of distinct plaquettes under $\mu_0$ is paid by the chessboard estimate.

For the second bound let $\mathsf S'$ be a maximal separated subset of $\mathsf S$. Every bond of $\mathsf S$ has its initial site within $\sigma_K$ of the initial site of a bond of $\mathsf S'$, and at most $C_K$ bonds have their initial site within $\sigma_K$ of a given site, so $|\mathsf S'|\geqslant |\mathsf S|/C_K$. When $q\leqslant 1$ this gives $q^{|\mathsf S'|}\leqslant q^{|\mathsf S|/C_K}$. When $q>1$ the second bound holds because the left side is a probability, at most $1\leqslant q^{|\mathsf S|/C_K}$. The count $C_K$ is an upper bound on every torus, so the argument holds also on periods at most $2\sigma_K+1$, where a separated subset has at most one bond.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Exponential Moment of the Boundary Sum}

\begin{lemma}[Exponential Moment of the Boundary Sum]\label{lem:c5-7-expmoment}
For $c>0$ let $R_0'\coloneqq \lceil R_0\rceil+2L+1$ and, for a bond $b$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c5-7-boundary-marks}
    \varphi_c(b)\coloneqq \sum_{r\in C}e^{-c(d_T(r,b)-R_0')_+}\leqslant \Phi_c\coloneqq 4(2R_0'+1)(1+1/c)+8/c^2\;,
\end{equation}
and $N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\coloneqq \sum_{s\geqslant 0}4(2s+1)^4e^{-c(s-R_0')_+}<\infty$. For $g_0$ below the thresholds of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} and~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}, pointwise on every branch, and for every $\lambda>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c5-7-expmoment-I}
    \begin{gathered}
    \sum_{j=0}^{4n-1}e^{-cd_j}\leqslant \sum_b\varphi_c(b)\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}\;,\\
    \mathcal Z_0^{-1}\int\mathcal O\Bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\exp\Bigl(\lambda\sum_{j=0}^{4n-1}e^{-cd_j}\Bigr)\Bigr]\dd V\leqslant \exp\bigl[n_C\,\lambda N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\,e^{\lambda\Phi_c}\,q^{1/C_K}\bigr]\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
the sum running over all bonds $b$ of the torus. The second bound is uniform in the volume, and it holds also with $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}$ omitted.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The bound in \eqref{eq:c5-7-boundary-marks}: the initial sites of the contour bonds lie on the four lines of the square, each meeting an $\ell^{\infty}$ ball of radius $s$ in at most $2s+1$ sites, so at most $4(2s+1)$ contour bonds $r$ have $d_T(r,b)\leqslant s$ ($d_T(r,b)\geqslant \| x_r-x_b\|_{\infty}$). Hence $\varphi_c(b)\leqslant 4(2R_0'+1)+\sum_{u\geqslant 1}4(2(R_0'+u)+1)e^{-cu}\leqslant 4(2R_0'+1)(1+1/c)+8/c^2$, using $\sum_{u\geqslant 1}e^{-cu}\leqslant 1/c$ and $\sum_{u\geqslant 1}ue^{-cu}\leqslant 1/c^2$.

The range of the stencils: let $\varrho_K\coloneqq \max_j\max_{k\in K_j}\min_{r\in C_j}d_T(k,r)$. The free-input stencil of a contour bond $r$ is $\Lambda_r=\{ r\}$ for a free bond, and $\Lambda_{b_0(c)}=\mathcal S_c\cap E_*$ for a designated bond, with $\mathcal S_c$ the positive fine bonds with both endpoints in the two endpoint blocks of $c$ (Appendix~\ref{sec:perimeter-attempt}). For a free contour bond $r$, $d_T(r,r)=0$. For a designated $r= b_0(c)$, the stencil bonds and $r$ itself, a bond of the row $c$, have both endpoints in the two endpoint blocks of $c$. These are two adjacent blocks of side $L$, any two sites of which are within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2L-1$ of each other, so $d_T(k,r)\leqslant 2L-1+1=2L$. Hence $\varrho_K\leqslant 2L+1$ and $R_0+\varrho_K\leqslant R_0'$.

The pointwise bound: $d_j=(d_T(K_j,I^c)-R_0)_+$ with $d_T(K_j,I^c)=\min_{b\notin I}d_T(K_j,b)$, and $x\mapsto e^{-c(x-R_0)_+}$ is nonincreasing, so $e^{-cd_j}\leqslant \sum_{b\notin I}e^{-c(d_T(K_j,b)-R_0)_+}$, both sides being zero if $I^c=\varnothing$. For $k\in K_j$ the triangle inequality gives $d_T(k,b)\geqslant \min_{r\in C_j}d_T(r,b)-\varrho_K$, so $e^{-c(d_T(K_j,b)-R_0)_+}\leqslant e^{-c(d_T(C_j,b)-R_0')_+}\leqslant \sum_{r\in C_j}e^{-c(d_T(r,b)-R_0')_+}$. The segments partition the contour bonds, so $\sum_j\sum_{r\in C_j}=\sum_{r\in C}$, and $\sum_je^{-cd_j}\leqslant \sum_{b\notin I}\varphi_c(b)$. By \eqref{eq:outside-carrier-marked} this is at most $\sum_b\varphi_c(b)\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}$, the added terms being nonnegative.

The moment: let $m_b\coloneqq\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}$. By the pointwise bound and $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\leqslant 1$ the integrand is at most $\mathsf w_{\xi}\prod_b(1+(e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1)m_b)$, since $e^{\lambda wm}=1+(e^{\lambda w}-1)m$ for $m\in\{0,1\}$; the product is finite. It expands into the sum over the sets $\mathsf S$ of bonds of $\prod_{b\in\mathsf S}(e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1)\prod_{b\in\mathsf S}m_b$. Every term is nonnegative, so the history average ($\mathsf w_{\xi}\geqslant 0$, $\mathcal O$ positive, Tonelli) is at most $\sum_{\mathsf S}\prod_{b\in\mathsf S}(e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1)\,q^{|\mathsf S|/C_K}$ by the second bound of \eqref{eq:c5-7-joint-I}. This sum equals $\prod_b(1+(e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1)\hat q)$ with $\hat q\coloneqq q^{1/C_K}$, and $\prod_b(1+(e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1)\hat q)\leqslant \exp(\hat q\sum_b(e^{\lambda\varphi_c(b)}-1))$. Finally $e^x-1\leqslant xe^x$ for $x\geqslant 0$, $\varphi_c(b)\leqslant \Phi_c$, and $\sum_b\varphi_c(b)=\sum_{r\in C}\sum_be^{-c(d_T(r,b)-R_0')_+}\leqslant n_CN'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$, since at most $4(2s+1)^4$ bonds have initial site within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $s$ of $x_r$. The indicator $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}$ entered only through $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\leqslant 1$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Moment of the Leading Error}

\begin{corollary}[The Moment of the Leading Error]\label{cor:leading-moment}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} and Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split}, with the constants $C$ and $c$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} and $N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$, $\Phi_c$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment}, and for $0< g_0< g_*$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c5-7-expbound-I}
    \begin{gathered}
    \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}\bigr]\leqslant \exp\bigl[C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q\bigr]\;,\\
    \delta^I_q\coloneqq C\tau^2N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\,e^{C\tau^2\Phi_c}\,q^{1/C_K}\leqslant \exp\bigl[-c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)\bigr]\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
the last inequality for $g_0$ below a further threshold, depending on $L$, $M$, $M_1$, $M_2$, the group, the character, the source constants and $c$. Hence the leading term $\kappa_{C_n}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)]$ of \eqref{eq:c4c-5-3} has modulus at most $|\kappa_{C_n}|\exp[C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q]$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:leading-moment-difference}
    \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}-1|\bigr]\leqslant \exp\bigl[C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q\bigr]-1\;.
\end{equation}
Moreover, with $c'\coloneqq A_0^22^{-2p_0}/(4(4K+9)^4(L^2M)^42^{4\mathfrak r})$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c5-7-delta-small}
    \pi_*^2/C_K\geqslant c'(\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0-4\mathfrak r}\;,\qquad 2p_0-4\mathfrak r\geqslant 6\mathfrak r\geqslant 12\;,
\end{equation}
so $\delta^I_q$ is smaller than every power of $g_0$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, \eqref{eq:refined-split} gives $e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}\leqslant e^{C\tau^2(2+1/c)}\exp(C\tau^2\sum_je^{-cd_j})$, and the second bound of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expmoment-I} at $\lambda= C\tau^2$ gives the first inequality of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expbound-I}.

The leading term: $| W_{\chi}|\leqslant 1$ and $| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}|\leqslant e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}$.

For \eqref{eq:leading-moment-difference}, pointwise $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}| e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}-1|\leqslant \mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}(e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|}-1)\leqslant e^{C\tau^2(2+1/c)}\exp(C\tau^2\sum_je^{-cd_j})-1$, the last member being nonnegative; its history average is at most $\exp[C\tau^2(2+1/c)+n_C\delta^I_q]-1$ by \eqref{eq:c5-7-expmoment-I} with the indicator omitted and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$ ($\mathcal Z_0=\int\mathcal O[\mathsf w_{\xi}]\,\dd V$).

\eqref{eq:c5-7-delta-small}: $C_K=4(4K\ell+9)^4\leqslant 4(4K+9)^4\ell^4\leqslant 4(4K+9)^4(L^2M)^42^{4\mathfrak r}(\log g_0^{-2})^{4\mathfrak r}$ and $\pi_*^2\geqslant A_0^22^{-2p_0}(\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0}$ by \eqref{eq:c5-3-1}, and $2p_0-4\mathfrak r\geqslant 6\mathfrak r$ by $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r$.

The smallness of $\delta^I_q$: since $\tau<1$ (fixed after \eqref{eq:marginal-fixed-forest-bound}) and $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ for $g_0< g_*$, $\log\delta^I_q\leqslant \log C+\log N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)+C\Phi_c-c_*\pi_*^2/C_K$, where $N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$ and $\Phi_c$ are constants of $c$, $L$ and the fixed range $R_0$. By \eqref{eq:c5-7-delta-small}, $c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)\geqslant \log C+\log N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)+C\Phi_c$ for $g_0$ below a threshold depending on the listed quantities, and then $\delta^I_q\leqslant \exp[-c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)]\leqslant \exp[-(c_*c'/2)(\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0-4\mathfrak r}]$, which is smaller than every power of $g_0$ since $2p_0-4\mathfrak r>1$.
\end{proof}

\section{Two Disjoint Squares}\label{sec:two-loops}

This section extends the extraction of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} and Appendices~\ref{app:signed-defects} and~\ref{app:regional-scalar} from one square to the product of the Wilson functions of two vertex-disjoint squares in planes parallel to that of $e_1,e_2$. The objects of this section are defined for the pair and compared with the single-square objects of each square.

\subsection{Setting}\label{sec:two-loops-setting}
Let $C_1,C_2$ be coarse translates of the counterclockwise squares with vertices $0,n_iLe_1,n_iL(e_1+e_2),n_iLe_2$, $i=1,2$, in fine-lattice units (so both lie in planes parallel to that of $e_1,e_2$); let $V(C_i)$ be the set of fine sites of $C_i$, the endpoints of its bonds; the squares are vertex-disjoint, $V(C_1)\cap V(C_2)=\varnothing$.

Let $\chi_1,\chi_2$ be normalised characters of irreducible unitary representations $\pi_1,\pi_2$ of $G$, $\chi_i=\dim(\pi_i)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\pi_i$. The reversed orientation of $C_i$ is the case $\bar\chi_i$, since $\chi_i(U^{-1})=\overline{\chi_i(U)}$. Let $C= C_1\sqcup C_2$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-observable}
    W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U)=\chi_1\bigl(\Hol_UC_1\bigr)\,\chi_2\bigl(\Hol_UC_2\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
The traversal set is $\mathcal I_C=\mathcal I_{C_1}\sqcup\mathcal I_{C_2}$, the traversals of each $C_i$ numbered cyclically from the base point used for the single-square objects of $C_i$; $n_{C_i}=4n_iL$ and $n_C= n_{C_1}+n_{C_2}$. Each square satisfies the square/torus geometry of Section~\ref{sec:extent-weights} with its own side, $K_{\mu}\geqslant 3(n_i+2)$ for every coarse period and $i=1,2$.

For $a\in\mathcal I_{C_i}$ let $\delta_a$ be the periodic $\ell^{\infty}$ fine distance from the initial site of the traversal $a$ to $V(C_{3-i})$, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-cross-sum}
    \Delta_{\times}\coloneqq\sum_{a\in\mathcal I_C}e^{-c_{\times}\delta_a/(LM)}\leqslant n_Ce^{-c_{\times} d/(LM)}\;,\qquad d\coloneqq\min_{a\in\mathcal I_C}\delta_a\;,
\end{equation}
with the constant $c_{\times}>0$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}, fixed before the coupling.

A superscript or subscript $i$ marks the single-square objects of the square $C_i$ with the character $\chi_i$: the contact sets $\mathsf T^i_D=\mathsf T_D\cap\mathcal I_{C_i}$, the groups of Definition~\ref{def:groups} for the contour $C_i$ alone, their reference scalars $a^{(i)}_W$ of \eqref{eq:part1-reference-group}, the reference gas $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_i}$ of \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas}, and the single-square lemmas of Appendix~\ref{app:signed-defects} with $C= C_i$. All of them are formed on the same branch $\xi$ with the same carrier, cubes, hosts, measures and cluster occurrences: the domains, probe measures $\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}$, vacuum clusters and reference data of Sections~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}--\ref{sec:joint-extraction} do not involve the observable, which enters only through the contact sets, $f_{\xi}$, $f^{\circ}_{\xi}$ and the reference scalars $a_W$.

The coupling is below the thresholds of the single-square results for $\chi_1$ and for $\chi_2$ and below those of this section.

Covered and far are taken for both squares: $\xi\in A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ means that $\xi$ is covered (Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}) for the contour $C= C_1\sqcup C_2$, which, the conditions being imposed bond by bond, is the intersection of the covered events of $C_1$ and $C_2$; a history is far when $\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma_C,E(\Lambda_1^c))> b$ with $\Gamma_C=\Gamma_{C_1}\cup\Gamma_{C_2}$, that is far for both squares.

\subsection{Groups for Two Squares}\label{sec:two-loops-groups}
For the pair, $f_{\xi}(a)= W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U_{\xi}(a))$, and the contact set $\mathsf T_D$ of \eqref{eq:part1-contact-set} is taken over $n\in\mathcal I_C$. The argument preceding Definition~\ref{def:groups} applies verbatim up to the formation of the components: unmarked domains contribute zero, $q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)$ is expanded by \eqref{eq:c-cluster-expansion}, and the graph on the marked roots and the cluster occurrences of a term has components $\gamma$, each with a marked root and the contact set $\mathsf T_{\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal I_C$, the union of the contact sets of its roots.

For $i=1,2$ let $H^i_{\gamma}\coloneqq\varnothing$ if $\mathsf T_{\gamma}\cap\mathcal I_{C_i}=\varnothing$; otherwise $H^i_{\gamma}$ is the hull of $\mathsf T_{\gamma}\cap\mathcal I_{C_i}$ in the cyclic set $\mathcal I_{C_i}$, defined as in Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}: the shortest cyclic interval containing it when that interval has fewer than $n_{C_i}/2$ positions, and $\mathcal I_{C_i}$ otherwise. Let $H_{\gamma}\coloneqq H^1_{\gamma}\sqcup H^2_{\gamma}$.

Two components overlap when $H^i_{\gamma}\cap H^i_{\gamma'}\neq\varnothing$ for some $i$; the overlap classes are the connected components of the overlap graph on the components of the term. A set $K$ of components is long on $C_i$ when $\bigl|\bigcup_{\gamma\in K}H^i_{\gamma}\bigr|\geqslant n_{C_i}/2$.

\begin{definition}[Groups for Two Squares]\label{def:two-loop-groups}
A partition $\mathfrak P$ of the components of a term is admissible if (A1) every overlap class lies in one block, and (A2) a block that is long on $C_i$ contains every component $\gamma$ with $\mathsf T_{\gamma}\cap\mathcal I_{C_i}\neq\varnothing$. The groups of the term are the blocks of its finest admissible partition (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(a)). A group $W$ consists of its root family $\mathcal A(W)$, its ordered list of cluster occurrences, and its interval set $\mathcal H(W)\coloneqq\mathcal H_1(W)\sqcup\mathcal H_2(W)$, where $\mathcal H_i(W)\coloneqq\mathcal I_{C_i}$ if $W$ is long on $C_i$, read from the base point of $C_i$, and $\mathcal H_i(W)=\bigcup_{\gamma\in W}H^i_{\gamma}$ otherwise, a finite union of cyclic intervals (a cyclic interval or $\mathcal I_{C_i}$ for a $C_i$-group, by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(d)); as in Definition~\ref{def:groups}, these data arise from a term, and conversely the term with root family $\mathcal A(W)$ and cluster list of $W$ has $W$ as its only group, with the same interval set (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(a)). Its weight $w_{\xi}(W)$ is \eqref{eq:part1-group-weight}.

$W$ is a $C_i$-group if $\mathcal H_{3-i}(W)=\varnothing$ and a cross group if $\mathcal H_1(W)\neq\varnothing\neq\mathcal H_2(W)$. Every group has $\mathcal H(W)\neq\varnothing$ (each component has a marked root), so it is exactly one of a $C_1$-group, a $C_2$-group and a cross group.

Two groups are compatible when all their constituent domains are mutually compatible and $\mathcal H_i(W)\cap\mathcal H_i(W')=\varnothing$ for $i=1,2$. A compatible group family is a finite set of pairwise compatible groups; the singleton clause of Definition~\ref{def:groups} is not imposed (for families of $C_i$-groups it is implied, Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(c)). For a compatible group family, $\mathcal A(\mathcal S)$ and $A_{\xi}(\mathcal S)$ are \eqref{eq:part1-closed-family-pairing}.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Two-Square Grouping]\label{lem:two-loop-grouping}
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Every term has a finest admissible partition; each of its blocks that is long on neither square is an overlap class. If no component of the term has a contact on $C_{3-i}$, it is the grouping of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} for the square $C_i$. For a group $W$ of a term, the term $T_W$ with root family $\mathcal A(W)$ and the cluster list of $W$ has $W$ as its only group, with the same interval set.
\item[(b)] The groups of a term are pairwise compatible, and Lemma~\ref{lem:grouped-source} holds for the pair: $F_{\xi}(0)=\sum_{\mathfrak B\text{ compatible}}A_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$, absolutely convergent.
\item[(c)] A $C_i$-group of the pair is a group of the single square $C_i$ (Definition~\ref{def:groups} with $C= C_i$) none of whose roots has a contact on $C_{3-i}$; conversely every such single-square group is a $C_i$-group of the pair, with the same interval, weight and footprint (the footprint of a group of the pair is defined in Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-pins}). Two $C_i$-groups are compatible for the pair if and only if they are compatible for the square $C_i$; a $C_1$-group and a $C_2$-group are compatible if and only if their constituent domains are mutually compatible.
\item[(d)] If $W$ is a $C_i$-group that is not long on $C_i$, then $\mathcal H_i(W)$ is a cyclic interval of fewer than $n_{C_i}/2$ traversals.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The one-block partition is admissible. If $\mathfrak P$ and $\mathfrak Q$ are admissible, so is their common refinement, whose blocks are the nonempty sets $P\cap Q$: (A1) holds because every overlap class lies in one block of each; for (A2), if $P\cap Q$ is long on $C_i$, then so are $P\supseteq P\cap Q$ and $Q\supseteq P\cap Q$ (the union of hulls is monotone), so both contain every component with a contact on $C_i$, and so does $P\cap Q$. There are finitely many components, so the common refinement of all admissible partitions is admissible and is the finest.

If a block $P$ of the finest partition is long on neither square and contains two overlap classes, the partition with $P$ replaced by its overlap classes satisfies (A1), its new blocks are long on neither square (they are subsets of $P$), and the other blocks are unchanged, so it is admissible and strictly finer, a contradiction.

If no component has a contact on $C_{3-i}$, condition (A2) on $C_{3-i}$ is void; if no overlap class is long the overlap classes form an admissible partition, hence the finest, and these are the classes of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} for $C_i$ with the intervals $\mathcal H(K)$ there, which equal the unions of the members' hulls; if some overlap class is long, every admissible partition has a long block containing it, which by (A2) contains every component (each has a contact on $C_i$), so the finest partition is the single class of all components, the whole-contour group of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}.

The term of a group: let $\mathfrak P$ be the finest admissible partition of a term $T$ and $W\in\mathfrak P$. Every cluster occurrence of $W$ hits a root of $T$, which is joined to it by an edge and so lies in its component, hence in $W$; so $T_W$ is a term of \eqref{eq:c-cluster-expansion}. Edges are defined pairwise, so the graph of $T_W$ is the subgraph of that of $T$ induced on $W$, and $W$ being a union of components of $T$, the components of $T_W$ are those of $T$ in $W$, with the same contact sets, hulls and long-ness; by (A1) $W$ is a union of overlap classes of $T$, which are the overlap classes of $T_W$. Let $\mathfrak P'$ be an admissible partition of $T_W$ and $\mathfrak P''=\mathfrak P'\cup(\mathfrak P\setminus\{ W\})$. (A1) holds for $\mathfrak P''$, and (A2) for its blocks outside $W$; if $Q\in\mathfrak P'$ is long on $C_i$, then $W\supseteq Q$ is long on $C_i$, so $W$ contains every component of $T$ with a contact on $C_i$ by (A2) for $\mathfrak P$, and all of them lie in $Q$ by (A2) for $\mathfrak P'$. So $\mathfrak P''$ is admissible for $T$, $\mathfrak P$ refines it, and $\mathfrak P'=\{ W\}$. Long-ness and hulls being the same in $T$ and $T_W$, the interval set is the same.

(b) Distinct groups of a term have disjoint intervals: if neither is long on $C_i$, their $C_i$-parts are unions of hulls of components in different blocks, hence of different overlap classes by (A1), and such hulls are disjoint; if one is long on $C_i$, it contains every component with a contact on $C_i$, so the other has $\mathcal H_i=\varnothing$. Domains in different groups are compatible as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:grouped-source} (no edge of the term's graph joins different components). Every component's hull satisfies $H^i_{\gamma}\subseteq\mathcal H_i(W)$ for its group $W$: trivially if $W$ is long on $C_i$, and by definition otherwise.

Reversibility: let $\mathfrak B\coloneqq\{ W_1,\ldots,W_m\}$ be a compatible family, each $W_j$ being the only group of its own term by (a), and let $\mathfrak P$ be the finest admissible partition of the union term, whose components are those of the $W_j$ (compatibility excludes edges between groups). $\mathfrak B$ is admissible for the union term: components of different $W_j$ have hulls in disjoint intervals, so they do not overlap and (A1) holds; if $W_j$ is long on $C_i$, then $\mathcal H_i(W_j)=\mathcal I_{C_i}$, so every other $W_k$ has $\mathcal H_i(W_k)=\varnothing$, no contact on $C_i$, and $W_j$ contains every component with a contact on $C_i$. Hence $\mathfrak P$ refines $\mathfrak B$. The restriction of $\mathfrak P$ to the components of $W_j$ is admissible for the term of $W_j$ alone: its overlap classes are those of the union term inside $W_j$, and a block of $\mathfrak P$ inside $W_j$ that is long on $C_i$ contains every component of the union term with a contact on $C_i$, in particular those of $W_j$. Since $\{ W_j\}$ is the finest admissible partition of that term, $\mathfrak P$ restricted to $W_j$ is the single block $W_j$, so $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak B$, with the same intervals.

The rest of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:grouped-source} (interleaving count, multiplicities of identical occurrences, absolute convergence) does not involve the intervals and applies verbatim.

(c) Let $W$ be a $C_i$-group of the pair. Its roots are marked and $\mathcal H_{3-i}(W)=\varnothing$, so every root $D$ has $\mathsf T_D=\mathsf T^i_D\neq\varnothing$, and the components, their hulls on $C_i$, the overlap graph and the long-ness on $C_i$ of the term $T_W$ of $W$ are the same for the pair and for the square $C_i$. So $T_W$ is a term of \eqref{eq:c-cluster-expansion} for the square $C_i$ (its roots are marked for $C_i$, and its clusters hit $\mathcal A(W)$ by (a)), no component of which has a contact on $C_{3-i}$; by (a) its finest admissible partition $\{ W\}$ is its grouping of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} for $C_i$, with $\mathcal H(W)=\mathcal H_i(W)$.

Conversely, if $W$ is a group of $C_i$ whose roots have no contact on $C_{3-i}$, its term (Definition~\ref{def:groups}) is a term of the pair, with $\mathsf T_D=\mathsf T^i_D\neq\varnothing$ for its roots, and by (a) its pair grouping is its grouping for $C_i$, the single group $W$, with $\mathcal H_i(W)=\mathcal H(W)$ and $\mathcal H_{3-i}(W)=\varnothing$. The weight \eqref{eq:part1-group-weight} and the footprint of Section~\ref{sec:c4-6} depend on the roots, the cluster list and the interval only. Compatibility for the pair of two $C_i$-groups is compatibility of domains and disjointness of the $C_i$-intervals, which is Definition~\ref{def:groups} for $C_i$ (its singleton clause for a whole-contour group being implied by the disjointness, since every group has a nonempty interval); for a $C_1$-group and a $C_2$-group the interval condition is void.

(d) $W$ is not long on $C_{3-i}$, since $\mathcal H_{3-i}(W)=\varnothing$, so by (a) it is an overlap class; its members have hulls on $C_i$ only, so they are chained by intersections of these hulls, and $\mathcal H_i(W)$ is a union of chained cyclic intervals with fewer than $n_{C_i}/2$ positions in total, which is a cyclic interval by the argument of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Reference Scalars and the Joint Extraction}\label{sec:two-loops-extraction}
For a $C_i$-group $W$ let $P^{\circ}_W(a)$ be the ordered product of the reference links along the consecutive traversals of $\mathcal H_i(W)$, in the cyclic order of $C_i$ starting from the first traversal of the interval (from the base point of $C_i$ if $W$ is long on $C_i$), as in Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}, and define $a_W$ by \eqref{eq:part1-reference-group} with $\chi_i$ in place of $\chi$; $\mathcal H_i(W)$ is a cyclic interval or $\mathcal I_{C_i}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(d), and $a_W= a^{(i)}_W$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(c), since the reference links and the measures $\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f,\circ}_{\xi,D}$ do not involve the observable (Lemma~\ref{lem:probe-measures}). For a cross group $a_W\coloneqq 0$. With these numbers let, for the pair,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-reference-gas}
    S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}=\sum_{\mathfrak B\text{ compatible}}\prod_{W\in\mathfrak B}a_W\;,
\end{equation}
in which a family containing a cross group contributes zero; the restricted sums $S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}$ run over the families compatible with every member of $\mathfrak B$, and the joint defect $R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$ is \eqref{eq:part1-joint-defect}.

\begin{lemma}[Schur Identity and Joint Extraction for Two Squares]\label{lem:two-loop-schur}
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] For a $C_i$-group $W$ and $h\in G$, \eqref{eq:part1-closed-schur} holds with $\chi_i$ in place of $\chi$.
\item[(b)] Proposition~\ref{prop:joint-extraction} holds for the pair: \eqref{eq:part1-scalar-extraction} and \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity} hold with $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$ of \eqref{eq:two-loop-reference-gas}, the sums converging absolutely.
\item[(c)] At the reference data, $R^{\circ}_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)=0$ for every nonempty compatible family $\mathfrak B$ without cross groups.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:schur} for the square $C_i$: it uses only the invariance of the reference measures under the constant gauge rotations $R_u$, the covariance $P^{\circ}_W(R_ua)= uP^{\circ}_W(a)u^{-1}$ and Schur's lemma for $\pi_i$.

(b) The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:joint-extraction} is the Boolean inversion of \eqref{eq:part1-joint-defect} and an absolutely convergent rearrangement; it uses only $| a_W|\leqslant \beta_W$, which holds for $a_W=0$, the finiteness of $\sum_W\beta_W$ (a group is determined by its root family, cluster list and interval, Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}) and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(b) in place of Lemma~\ref{lem:grouped-source}.

(c) Let $\mathcal S$ be a compatible family of $C_1$- and $C_2$-groups. The contacts on $C_i$ of the roots of a $C_i$-group $W$ lie in $\mathcal H_i(W)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(b)), and the roots of a $C_{3-i}$-group have no contact on $C_i$. So, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}, a traversal outside every interval of $\mathcal S$ has the reference link $\id$, and a traversal in $\mathcal H_i(W)$ has at $\mathsf e_{\mathcal A(\mathcal S)}a$ its link at $\mathsf e_{\mathcal A(W)}a$, since it lies in no contact set of a root of another group; the links of $\mathcal H_i(W)$ multiply to $P^{\circ}_W(a)$.

Number the $C_i$-groups of $\mathcal S$ in the cyclic order of $C_i$; by cyclicity of the trace the reference Wilson function at $\mathsf e_{\mathcal A(\mathcal S)}a$ is $\prod_{i=1,2}\chi_i\bigl(\prod_{W\in\mathcal S,\ C_i\text{-group}}P^{\circ}_W(a)\bigr)$, the product over the $C_i$-groups in that order (an empty product being $\id$), and a family containing a group long on $C_i$ has no other $C_i$-group. Integrate one group at a time by Fubini, with (a) for the group integrated, the product of the other $P^{\circ}$ of the same square as $h$, and the character of the other square as a constant factor: $A^{\circ}_{\xi}(\mathcal S)=\prod_{W\in\mathcal S}a_W$. Hence $R^{\circ}_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)=\prod_{W\in\mathfrak B}a_W\sum_{\mathcal S\subseteq\mathfrak B}(-1)^{|\mathfrak B\setminus\mathcal S|}=0$ for $\mathfrak B\neq\varnothing$.
\end{proof}

For a family containing a cross group, $R^{\circ}_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$ need not vanish (for instance $R^{\circ}_{\xi}(\{ W\})= A^{\circ}_{\xi}(\{ W\})$ for a cross group $W$); the defects of such families are bounded directly (Lemmas~\ref{lem:two-loop-defect} and~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}). In place of the second equality of \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas}, Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(b) at the reference data (its proof uses only the field-independent geometry, as in Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}) and the Fubini step of (c) give
\[
    \frac{\int f^{\circ}_{\xi} K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}\,\dd a}{I^{\circ}_{\xi;0}}= S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}+\sum_{\mathfrak B\text{ compatible, with a cross group}}A^{\circ}_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)\;.
\]
The pair scalar is identified with the single-square scalars by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}(b).

\subsection{The Defects of a Family with Cross Groups}\label{sec:two-loops-defects}
For a $C_i$-group $W$ the closed contraction $c_W(U_1;h)$ of \eqref{eq:c4-6-2}, its defect $d_W$ and $\mathfrak d_W(U_1)$ of \eqref{eq:c4-6-3} are formed with $\chi_i$ and the interval $\mathcal H_i(W)$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(c) they are the single-square quantities of $C_i$.

For every group, cross groups included, $M(W)$ is the positive majorant of Section~\ref{sec:c4-6-2}: the product of the root weights $\rho\,m(D)$, the cluster weights $M_v(\mathfrak c_j)$ and $1/k(W)!$, with $\rho$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-source}; for $C_i$-groups this only enlarges the single-square majorant, so every single-square bound by $M(W)$ still holds. Let $K_{\chi}\coloneqq\max(K_{\chi_1},K_{\chi_2})$ with the constants of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-1}(a).

\begin{lemma}[Sources with Two Closed Words]\label{lem:two-loop-source}
Let $f(a)\coloneqq\prod_{i=1,2}\dim(\pi_i)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}Y_i(a)$, where $Y_i(a)$ is an ordered product of the matrices $\pi_i(U_{\xi}(a)(r))^{\pm1}$ of a set of reconstructed contour links of $C_i$, each traversal used at most once, and of fixed unitary matrices of $V_{\pi_i}$. Then \eqref{eq:c4-4-3}, \eqref{eq:c4-10-8}--\eqref{eq:c4-10-9}, the undifferentiated bound \eqref{eq:c4-7-6} and the last statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-2}, and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} hold for $f$, with $C_{\chi}$ enlarged once to a constant $C^{\mathrm{src}}_{\chi_1\chi_2}$ of $(\chi_1,\chi_2)$, so that $u= C^{\mathrm{src}}_{\chi_1\chi_2}g_0(1+r)$, and $g_0$ so small that $u\leqslant u_*$ and $v\leqslant 1$; in particular $|\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)|\leqslant \prod_{D\in\mathcal A}\rho\,m(D)$ for every nonempty compatible root family $\mathcal A$, with $\rho$ of \eqref{eq:c4-4-8} formed with this $u$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$f$ is the normalised trace of $Y_1(a)\otimes Y_2(a)$ on $V_{\pi_1}\otimes V_{\pi_2}$, and $| f|\leqslant 1$; since $\operatorname{tr}(A\otimes B)=\operatorname{tr}A\operatorname{tr}B$, the normalised trace on $V_{\pi_1}\otimes V_{\pi_2}$ satisfies $|\dim^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(M_1\cdots M_k)|\leqslant \prod_j\| M_j\|_{\mathrm{op}}$.

The proof of \eqref{eq:c4-10-8} uses only this inequality, the unitarity of the untouched factors, the row locality and the fixed derivative constants of the rows. For the row locality: $V(C_1)\cap V(C_2)=\varnothing$, so the bond sets of $C_1$ and $C_2$ are disjoint, each bond carries at most one traversal of $C_1\cup C_2$, and the number of reconstructed links a free label affects is the geometric count of bonds $r$ with the label in $\mathcal F_r$, at most $K$ as for one square, each traversal being used at most once in the two words together; the row input count, which fixes the derivative order of \eqref{eq:c4-10-4}, is unchanged. Then the product rule distributes the derivatives over the links of both words, with at most $K^q$ row assignments, and every untouched factor, a reconstructed link or a fixed matrix, is unitary in $V_{\pi_1}\otimes V_{\pi_2}$. The remainder bounds \eqref{eq:c4-10-9} follow by the same Taylor argument.

The proofs of \eqref{eq:c4-7-6}, of the last statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-2} and of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} use, besides these bounds, only properties of the selected measures (the reversal of a root with empty ordinary selection, the Cauchy difference in $\zeta_j$, the majorants $M_{\ell}$ and \eqref{eq:c4-4-7}) and the vanishing of $\Delta_{\mathsf J}f$ when a selected label does not influence the words; none of them uses the form of $f$ otherwise.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Defect Factorisation for Two Squares]\label{lem:two-loop-defect}
On a branch covered for $C_1\sqcup C_2$ (Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-setting}), for every compatible family $\mathfrak B$ with cross groups $\mathfrak B_{\times}\subseteq\mathfrak B$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-defect}
    | R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)|\leqslant \prod_{W\in\mathfrak B\setminus\mathfrak B_{\times}}K_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)\prod_{W\in\mathfrak B_{\times}}M(W)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-1}(b), a traversal of $\mathcal H(W)$, $W\in\mathfrak B$, has no contact with a root of another group of $\mathfrak B$ (the intervals are disjoint and contain the contacts), so its reconstructed link depends only on the root variables of $W$, and a traversal outside every interval has its background link $U_1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}, Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-1}).

For a $C_i$-group $W\in\mathfrak B$ let $X_W= w_{\xi}(W)\int\pi_i(T_WP_W^{-1})\,\dd\bigotimes_{D\in\mathcal A(W)}\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}$ and $\Upsilon_W= X_W-a_W\id$, with $T_W$, $P_W$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4-6-1}.

Since $a_W=0$ for cross groups, the term of $\mathcal S$ in \eqref{eq:part1-joint-defect} vanishes unless $\mathcal S\supseteq\mathfrak B_{\times}$. Let $a_{\times}$ be the root variables of the cross groups, held fixed. For $i=1,2$ let $Y_i$ be the ordered product, in the cyclic order of $C_i$ starting at the first traversal of the interval of a $C_i$-group of $\mathfrak B$ if there is one and at the base point of $C_i$ otherwise (the trace is cyclic; as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-1}(b)), of the following factors: for a $C_i$-group $W\in\mathfrak B$, the matrix $\Upsilon_W\pi_i(P_W)$ at the position of $\mathcal H_i(W)$; for a traversal in $\mathcal H_i(W)$ of a cross group $W$, its reconstructed link at $a_{\times}$; for every other traversal, its background link. Expanding each $\Upsilon_W= X_W-a_W\id$ and using Fubini over the product measures of the $C_1$- and $C_2$-groups, exactly as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-1}(b), the term of $\mathcal S\supseteq\mathfrak B_{\times}$ is reproduced, because $f_{\xi}$ at $\mathsf e_{\mathcal A(\mathcal S)}a$ is the product of the two normalised traces and each $X_W$ enters exactly one of them; hence
\begin{equation*}
    R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)=\Bigl(\prod_{W\in\mathfrak B_{\times}}w_{\xi}(W)\Bigr)\int\prod_{i=1,2}\frac{\operatorname{tr}Y_i(a_{\times})}{\dim\pi_i}\,\dd\bigotimes_{W\in\mathfrak B_{\times}}\bigotimes_{D\in\mathcal A(W)}\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}(a_{\times})\;.
\end{equation*}
The integrand is multilinear in the matrices $\Upsilon_W$, $W\in\mathfrak B\setminus\mathfrak B_{\times}$. With $\Upsilon_W=\|\Upsilon_W\|_{\mathrm{op}}T_W'$ and $\| T'_W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 1$, each contraction $T'= V| T'|$ (polar decomposition, $V$ unitary) is $T'=\frac12(Ve^{iA}+Ve^{-iA})$ with $A=\arccos| T'|$, an average of two unitary matrices. The integrand is then $\prod_W\|\Upsilon_W\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ times an average of $2^{|\mathfrak B\setminus\mathfrak B_{\times}|}$ functions of the form of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-source}, depending on $a_{\times}$ only through the links of the cross groups' traversals. If $\mathfrak B_{\times}\neq\varnothing$, that lemma applied to the compatible root family $\mathcal A(\mathfrak B_{\times})$ bounds each such integral by $\prod_{D\in\mathcal A(\mathfrak B_{\times})}\rho\,m(D)$ in modulus; if $\mathfrak B_{\times}=\varnothing$, there is no integral, and each of the unitary words has normalised traces of modulus at most one (for $\mathfrak B=\varnothing$ the bound is $| f_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant 1$).

Further $| w_{\xi}(W)|\leqslant \prod_jM_v(\mathfrak c_j)/k(W)!$: by \eqref{eq:part1-vacuum-cluster} the cluster weight is $\varphi^T/m!$ times the product of the activities, $|\varphi^T|$ is at most the number of spanning trees of the incompatibility graph (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}, Section~\ref{app:kp}), and the activities are bounded by $m(D)$ by \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-raw-activity-payment} of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds}. Together with $\|\Upsilon_W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant K_{\chi_i}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)\leqslant K_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)$ for a $C_i$-group (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-1}(a) for the square $C_i$) this is \eqref{eq:two-loop-defect}; the bound holds with $K_{\chi_i}$ on the $C_i$-groups.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Pins for the Groups of Two Squares}\label{sec:two-loops-pins}
For a group $W$ of the pair, $n(W)$, $\mathfrak s(W)= n(W)+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)$, the footprint $F(W)$, $X(W)$, $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ and the envelope $\mathfrak E(W)$ are defined as in Section~\ref{sec:c4-6} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}, with $\mathcal H(W)=\mathcal H_1(W)\sqcup\mathcal H_2(W)$ and the traversals of both squares; for components, $t_{\gamma}$, $n_{\gamma}$, $X_{\gamma}$, $F(\gamma)$ and $\mathfrak s(\gamma)= n_{\gamma}+| H_{\gamma}|/(LM)$ are those of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-2} with $H_{\gamma}= H^1_{\gamma}\sqcup H^2_{\gamma}$, and $\sigma_K=\sum_{\gamma\in K}\mathfrak s(\gamma)$. Let $A'_E\coloneqq 17(2R_{\mathrm e}+1)^4$.

\begin{lemma}[Pins for Two Squares]\label{lem:two-loop-pins}
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-2}, with its constant $C$ enlarged by a fixed factor:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env} holds for every group $W$ of the pair with $16n(W)+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)$ and $17\mathfrak s(W)$ in place of the bounds $8+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)$ and $9\mathfrak s(W)$ of its part (a), $A'_E$ in place of $A_F$ and $A_E$, and $\operatorname{dist}(\Delta,C)$ the distance to $V(C_1)\cup V(C_2)$; if $W$ is a cross group, $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))\subseteq\mathfrak E(W)$ contains a cube containing a site of $V(C_1)$ and a cube containing a site of $V(C_2)$.
\item[(b)] Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2} holds for the components of the pair, with $| H^i_{\gamma}|\leqslant A_{\mathrm h}LMn_{\gamma}$ for $i=1,2$, the hull pin \eqref{eq:c4-8-5} for $a\in\mathcal I_{C_i}$ taken with the contour distance $d_{C_i}$ of $C_i$, and the sum over $a'\in\mathcal I_C$ in \eqref{eq:c4-8-6}.
\item[(c)] Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-3}(a) holds for the overlap classes of the pair. A class long on $C_i$ satisfies $\sigma_K\geqslant n_{C_i}/(2LM)$ and $\sum_{K\text{ long on }C_i}t_Ke^{34\eta\sigma_K}\leqslant C\rho n_{C_i}e^{-15\eta n_{C_i}/(LM)}$. The groups long on some square have total weighted mass $\sum_{W\text{ long}}M(W)e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\leqslant 2C\rho\bigl(n_{C_1}e^{-10\eta n_{C_1}/(LM)}+n_{C_2}e^{-10\eta n_{C_2}/(LM)}\bigr)\leqslant C'\rho$ with $C'\coloneqq 2CLM/(5e\eta)$, uniformly in $n_1,n_2$.
\item[(d)] The pins \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} hold for the groups of the pair, with $\mathcal I_C$ the traversals of both squares; for every group $W$ of the pair, cross groups included, $\sum_{W'\not\sim W}| a_{W'}| e^{3\eta\mathfrak s(W')}\leqslant \frac18\eta\mathfrak s(W)$, the sum over the groups of the pair; and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-3} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2} hold for the reference gas \eqref{eq:two-loop-reference-gas}, with $C\rho n_C$ in \eqref{eq:c4-9-4}.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) Count. On each square, $\mathcal H_i(W)$ is empty, or $\mathcal I_{C_i}$, or, if $W$ is not long on $C_i$, a nonempty union of member hulls with fewer than $n_{C_i}/2$ positions in total; in the second case each member hull is a cyclic interval (none is the whole of $\mathcal I_{C_i}$), each maximal cyclic interval of the union has fewer than $n_{C_i}/2$ positions because the union does, and there are at most $| W|$ of them, where $| W|$, the number of components of $W$, is at most $n(W)=\sum_{\gamma} n_{\gamma}$ since $n_{\gamma}\geqslant 1$. As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}(a), a cyclic interval of fewer than $n_{C_i}/2$ traversals meets each side in one run and lies in at most $8+t/(LM)$ cubes for $t$ traversals, and so does $\mathcal I_{C_i}$; summing over at most $2n(W)$ intervals, $|\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))|\leqslant 16n(W)+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)$, so $| X(W)\cup\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))|\leqslant 17\mathfrak s(W)$ and $| F(W)|\leqslant |\mathfrak E(W)|\leqslant A'_E\mathfrak s(W)$.

Connectivity. For a component $\gamma$, $X_{\gamma}$ is connected (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}(b)); $\pi_1(H^i_{\gamma})$ is connected, $H^i_{\gamma}$ being a cyclic interval or $\mathcal I_{C_i}$, and it contains the cube of the initial vertex of a contact of $\gamma$ on $C_i$, which is at index distance at most one from a cube of a root of $\gamma$; so $X_{\gamma}\cup\pi_1(H_{\gamma})$ is connected. Two overlapping components share a traversal, hence the cube of its initial vertex. So $X(W)\cup\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ is connected if $W$ is an overlap class, which by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(a) covers every group long on neither square.

Let $W$ be long on $C_i$. Each overlap class in $W$ has a component with a contact on $C_i$, or $W$ is also long on $C_{3-i}$ and the class has a contact on $C_{3-i}$: otherwise splitting this class off $W$ gives an admissible partition (the remainder is nonempty, since it contains the components of $W$ with a contact on $C_i$; it keeps every component with a contact on a square on which $W$ is long and keeps the same union of hulls there, the class is long on no square, being a subset of $W$ without contacts on those squares and with the union of its hulls on the other square inside that of $W$), contradicting the finest choice. If $W$ is long on $C_i$ only, every class in $W$ meets the connected set $\pi_1(\mathcal I_{C_i})$, so the union is connected. If $W$ is long on both squares and no class in $W$ has contacts on both, then splitting $W$ into its classes with contacts on $C_1$ and those with contacts on $C_2$ is admissible (each part contains every component with a contact on the square on which it is long, and has no contact on the other square), a contradiction; so some class of $W$ meets both $\pi_1(\mathcal I_{C_1})$ and $\pi_1(\mathcal I_{C_2})$, and the union is connected. Hence $\mathfrak E(W)$ is connected. The statements (c) and (d) of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env} then follow by its proof. For a cross group both $\mathcal H_1(W)$ and $\mathcal H_2(W)$ are nonempty, and $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ contains the cubes of their vertices.

(b) The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2}. Part (a) there does not involve hulls. In (b) the contacts of $\gamma$ on $C_i$ lie within $2L$ of $X_{\gamma}$, and the square geometry of $C_i$ (Section~\ref{sec:extent-weights}) gives $| H^i_{\gamma}|\leqslant A_{\mathrm h}LMn_{\gamma}$ and $d_{C_i}(a,a')\leqslant A_{\mathrm h}LMn_{\gamma}$ for $a\in H^i_{\gamma}$ and a contact $a'$ of $\gamma$ on $C_i$; the contour sum is over $\mathcal I_{C_i}$. In \eqref{eq:c4-8-6} the sum over the traversals of each square is bounded as there, and there are two squares. For part (c) of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2}: for the pair $\mathfrak s(\gamma)\leqslant (1+2A_{\mathrm h})n_{\gamma}\leqslant 2A_{\mathrm s}n_{\gamma}$, so $100\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)\leqslant 200\eta A_{\mathrm s}n_{\gamma}<\varpi n_{\gamma}/40$ by $1000\eta A_{\mathrm s}<\varpi/8$, and the pins with the weight $e^{100\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}$ are dominated by those of (b) with the weight $e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/4}$, with a margin $e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/8}$; $\eta$ is not changed. In the footprint pin, at most $CLM$ traversals of each square have stencils meeting a given cube, so at most $2CLM$ in all, and the footprint pin holds with the constant doubled.

(c) The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-3}(a) applies with $H_{\gamma}= H^1_{\gamma}\sqcup H^2_{\gamma}$: the components whose hulls meet $H_{\gamma}$ have weighted mass at most $C\rho| H_{\gamma}|$ by the hull pins of (b) at the traversals of $H_{\gamma}$, and an overlap class long on neither square has the interval $\bigcup_{\gamma} H_{\gamma}$, of size at most $\sum_{\gamma}| H_{\gamma}|\leqslant LM\sigma_K$. A class long on $C_i$ has $\sigma_K\geqslant \sum_{\gamma}| H^i_{\gamma}|/(LM)\geqslant n_{C_i}/(2LM)$; anchoring it at a traversal of $\bigcup_{\gamma} H^i_{\gamma}$ ($n_{C_i}$ choices) and using the class pin with the weight $e^{64\eta\sigma_K}$ gives the stated sum, the exponent $30\eta\sigma_K$ being at least $15\eta n_{C_i}/(LM)$.

Long groups: if no overlap class of a term is long, the overlap classes are admissible and no group is long. Let $W$ be long; it contains an overlap class $K_0$ long on some square $C_{i_0}$: otherwise replacing $W$ by its overlap classes keeps (A1), the new blocks are long on no square, and the other blocks are unchanged, so the new partition is admissible, and it is strictly finer unless $W$ is a single class, which is then not long; the first contradicts the finest choice, the second the assumption that $W$ is long. $W$ is long on $C_{i_0}$, and by the splitting argument of (a) it is the union of the overlap classes with a contact on a square on which it is long. As in Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-3}(c), the sum of $M(W)$ over the groups with a given set of components is at most $\prod_{\gamma} t_{\gamma}$, and $\mathfrak s(W)\leqslant \sum_{\gamma\in W}\mathfrak s(\gamma)+\sum_{i:\,W\text{ long on }C_i}n_{C_i}/(LM)$.

If $W$ is long on $C_{i_0}$ only, the classes other than $K_0$ are anchored at traversals of $C_{i_0}$ and sum to at most $e^{C\rho n_{C_{i_0}}}$ with their weights $e^{64\eta\sigma}$, the interval weight is $e^{4\eta n_{C_{i_0}}/(LM)}$, and $K_0$ contributes $C\rho n_{C_{i_0}}e^{-15\eta n_{C_{i_0}}/(LM)}$; with $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta$ the product is at most $C\rho n_{C_{i_0}}e^{-10\eta n_{C_{i_0}}/(LM)}$. If $W$ is long on both squares, let $j\neq i_0$; since $\sum_{\gamma\in W}| H^j_{\gamma}|\geqslant n_{C_j}/2$ and $| H^j_{\gamma}|\leqslant LM\mathfrak s(\gamma)$, $1\leqslant e^{-15\eta n_{C_j}/(LM)}\prod_{\gamma\in W}e^{30\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}$; inserting this factor, the classes other than $K_0$ are anchored at traversals of $C_1$ or $C_2$ and sum to at most $e^{C\rho n_C}$ with the weights $e^{64\eta\sigma}$, the interval weight is $e^{4\eta n_C/(LM)}$, and $K_0$ contributes $C\rho n_{C_{i_0}}e^{-15\eta n_{C_{i_0}}/(LM)}$ with the weight $e^{34\eta\sigma_{K_0}}$; the product is at most $C\rho n_{C_{i_0}}e^{-10\eta n_C/(LM)}\leqslant C\rho n_{C_{i_0}}e^{-10\eta n_{C_{i_0}}/(LM)}$.

The groups long on $C_i$ only thus contribute at most $C\rho n_{C_i}e^{-10\eta n_{C_i}/(LM)}$, and the groups long on both squares at most that for each $i_0= i$; summing over the four pairs (set of long squares, $i_0$) gives the bound, and $xe^{-10\eta x/(LM)}\leqslant LM/(10e\eta)$ for $x= n_{C_1},n_{C_2}$ gives $C'=2CLM/(5e\eta)$.

(d) The pins over groups long on neither square are the class pins of (c), as in Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-3}: such a group is an overlap class $K$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(a)), the sum of $M(W)$ over the groups with class $K$ is at most $t_K$, $\mathfrak s(W)\leqslant \sigma_K$ and $F(W)\subseteq\bigcup_{\gamma\in K}F(\gamma)$; the long groups are bounded by their total mass (c), so \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} holds with the constant $C+C'$.

For the second statement, a group $W'\not\sim W$ has a footprint cube in $\mathfrak N_1(F(W))$ or a traversal in $\mathcal H(W)$ by (a) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}(d), so the pins give at most $C\rho(3^4| F(W)|+|\mathcal H(W)|)\leqslant C\rho(3^4A'_E+LM)\mathfrak s(W)$, which is at most $\eta\mathfrak s(W)/8$ under $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$ with the constant $C$ of (c) replaced by $C(1+2LM/(5e\eta))(1+3^4A'_E/(LM))$; this factor, together with the doubling in (b), is the enlargement of the lemma, fixed with $\eta$ before the coupling (and $e^{3\eta\mathfrak s}\leqslant e^{4\eta\mathfrak s}$, $| a_{W'}|\leqslant M(W')$).

The proofs of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-6-3} and~\ref{lem:c4-9-2} then apply verbatim; the species of the reference gas are the groups with $a_W\neq0$, all of them $C_1$- or $C_2$-groups, and the exclusion ratio \eqref{eq:c4-6-7} holds for every compatible family $\mathfrak B$ of groups of the pair, cross groups included, because the criterion was proved for every $W$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Cross Terms}\label{sec:two-loops-cross}
