Covered and far histories are those of Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-setting}. A single-square group $W$ of $C_i$ touches $C_{3-i}$ if some root $D$ of $W$ has $\mathsf T_D\cap\mathcal I_{C_{3-i}}\neq\varnothing$, with the contact set $\mathsf T_D$ of the pair. Let $c_{\times}\coloneqq 2\eta/A'_E$.

\begin{lemma}[The Cross Terms]\label{lem:two-loop-cross}
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins} and, for (c), those of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-4} for each square, with a constant $C_{\times}$ fixed before the coupling and independent of $n_1$, $n_2$ and the positions of the squares, and with $C_{\chi}\coloneqq\max_iC_{\chi_i}$ and $c=\min_ic_i$ formed from the constants $C_{\chi_i}$, $c_i$ of \eqref{eq:c4-6-8} for the square $C_i$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] On every branch $\xi$, for every cross group $W$ of the pair and every $a\in\mathcal H(W)$, $\mathfrak s(W)>\delta_a/(A'_ELM)$; and $\sum_{W\text{ cross}}M(W)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\leqslant C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}$.
\item[(b)] Let $\mathscr L$ and $\mathscr L_i$ be the connected-cluster logarithms of the reference gas \eqref{eq:two-loop-reference-gas} of the pair and of the reference gas of the single square $C_i$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}), and $E^{\times}_{\xi}=\mathscr L-\mathscr L_1-\mathscr L_2$. Then, on every branch $\xi$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-factorisation}
    S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}= S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_1}S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_2}e^{E^{\times}_{\xi}}\;,\qquad| E^{\times}_{\xi}|\leqslant C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}\;;
\end{equation}
in particular $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$ on every branch.
\item[(c)] On covered far histories, with $\mathscr R_{\xi}$ the family sum \eqref{eq:c4-1-1} of the pair,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-family-sum}
    |\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant | S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\Bigl[\exp\Bigl(C_{\chi} n_C\rho\bigl(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)}\bigr)+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}\Bigr)-1\Bigr]\;.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Distance from an envelope. Let $\mathfrak X$ be a finite set of cubes, connected under adjacency, with $|\mathfrak X|\leqslant k$. As in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}(c), any two sites in cubes of $\mathfrak X$ are at periodic fine $\ell^{\infty}$ distance less than $kLM$. Hence if $\mathfrak X$ contains the cube of the initial vertex of a traversal $a\in\mathcal I_{C_i}$ and a cube containing a site of $V(C_{3-i})$, then $\delta_a< kLM$.

(a) For a cross group $W$, $\mathfrak E(W)$ is connected, has at most $A'_E\mathfrak s(W)$ cubes and contains the cubes of the initial vertices of the traversals of $\mathcal H(W)$ and a cube containing a site of $V(C_1)$ and one containing a site of $V(C_2)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(a)); so $\delta_a< A'_ELM\mathfrak s(W)$ for every $a\in\mathcal H(W)$. Every group has a nonempty interval, so, pinning a cross group at a traversal of its interval and using $\mathfrak a_W/8\leqslant \eta\mathfrak s(W)$, $e^{-3\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\leqslant e^{-3\eta\delta_a/(A'_ELM)}\leqslant e^{-c_{\times}\delta_a/(LM)}$ and the pin \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} of the pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(d)),
\[
    \sum_{W\text{ cross}}M(W)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\leqslant \sum_{a\in\mathcal I_C}e^{-c_{\times}\delta_a/(LM)}\sum_{W\,|\,a\in\mathcal H(W)}M(W)e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\leqslant C\rho\Delta_{\times}\;.
\]

The pins of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins} and \eqref{eq:c4-6-5}, the criterion \eqref{eq:two-loop-weighted-kp} below and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2} use only $| a_W|\leqslant M(W)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} at the reference data, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}), the smallness of $\rho$ and the field-independent geometry; coverage and farness enter only Lemmas~\ref{lem:two-loop-defect} and~\ref{lem:c4-6-4}, so (a) and (b) hold on every branch.

(b) The three gases. The species of the pair gas with nonzero activity are its $C_1$- and $C_2$-groups; the species of the gas of $C_i$ are the single-square groups of $C_i$, with the activities $a^{(i)}_W$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-grouping}(c) and the equality $a_W= a^{(i)}_W$ of Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-extraction}, the $C_i$-groups of the pair are the single-square groups of $C_i$ that do not touch $C_{3-i}$, with the same activities, and the compatibility relation of the pair restricted to them is that of the square $C_i$.

Each gas satisfies the Kotecký--Preiss criterion in the following weighted form: for every species $W$ of that gas,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-weighted-kp}
    \sum_{W'\not\sim W}| a_{W'}| e^{3\eta\mathfrak s(W')}\leqslant \frac18\eta\mathfrak s(W)\;,
\end{equation}
for the pair by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(d), and for the square $C_i$ by the proof of \eqref{eq:c4-6-6}, which bounds $e^{\mathfrak a_{W'}}$ by $e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W')}$ and so bounds $e^{3\eta\mathfrak s(W')}$ in the same way. This is the criterion of Section~\ref{app:kp} for the weights $\widetilde z_W=| a_W| e^{2\eta\mathfrak s(W)}$ and sizes $\eta\mathfrak s(W)$, so the rooted-tree argument there gives, for every species $W$ of each gas,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-pinned-cluster}
    \sum_{\mathfrak c}m_W(\mathfrak c)|\Psi(\mathfrak c)| e^{2\eta\sum_{W'\in\mathfrak c}\mathfrak s(W')}\leqslant | a_W| e^{3\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\;,
\end{equation}
the sum over the cluster tuples $\mathfrak c$ of that gas, $\Psi(\mathfrak c)=\frac{\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)}{m!}\prod_{W'\in\mathfrak c}a_{W'}$, $m_W(\mathfrak c)$ the multiplicity of $W$ in $\mathfrak c$. The logarithms $\mathscr L$, $\mathscr L_i$ are the absolutely convergent series $\sum_{\mathfrak c}\Psi(\mathfrak c)$ of the three gases, $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}= e^{\mathscr L}$ and $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_i}= e^{\mathscr L_i}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}, for the pair by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(d)), which gives the identity in \eqref{eq:two-loop-factorisation}.

Cancellation. A cluster tuple of the pair gas all of whose members are $C_i$-groups is a cluster tuple of the gas of $C_i$ with the same $\Psi$: the Ursell coefficient depends only on the incompatibility graph of the tuple, which is the same for both gases, and the activities agree. Conversely a tuple of the gas of $C_i$ none of whose members touches $C_{3-i}$ is such a tuple of the pair gas. Hence $E^{\times}_{\xi}=\sum_{\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_0}\Psi(\mathfrak c)-\sum_{i=1,2}\sum_{\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_i}\Psi(\mathfrak c)$, where $\mathcal X_0$ is the set of tuples of the pair gas containing a $C_1$-group and a $C_2$-group, and $\mathcal X_i$ the set of tuples of the gas of $C_i$ containing a group that touches $C_{3-i}$; the rearrangement is justified by absolute convergence.

Extent of the bridging tuples. Let $\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_0\cup\mathcal X_1\cup\mathcal X_2$, let $W\in\mathfrak c$ and $a\in\mathcal H(W)$, $a\in\mathcal I_{C_i}$. The union $\mathfrak X$ of the envelopes of the members of $\mathfrak c$ is connected: each envelope is connected (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(a) for the pair, Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}(b) for a single square), the incompatibility graph of a tuple with $\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)\neq0$ is connected, and two incompatible members have footprints at index distance at most one or a common traversal in their intervals (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}(d), for the pair by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(a)), the footprints and the cubes of the traversal vertices lying in the envelopes.

$\mathfrak X$ contains the cube of the initial vertex of $a$, and a cube containing a site of $V(C_{3-i})$: for $\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_0$, the cube of a traversal vertex of the interval of a member that is a $C_{3-i}$-group; for $\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_j$ (then $i= j$), the cube of the initial vertex of a contact $n\in\mathsf T_D\cap\mathcal I_{C_{3-i}}$ of a root $D$ of a member $W_0$ touching $C_{3-i}$, which is within $2L$ of $D$ (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}: the stencil bond of the contact has its endpoints in $D$), hence at index distance at most one from a cube of $X(W_0)$ and in $\mathfrak E(W_0)$, since $R_{\mathrm e}\geqslant 1$. With $|\mathfrak X|\leqslant A'_E\sum_{W'\in\mathfrak c}\mathfrak s(W')$ ($A_E\leqslant A'_E$), the distance bound gives $\sum_{W'\in\mathfrak c}\mathfrak s(W')>\delta_a/(A'_ELM)$.

Bound. Every member of a tuple has a nonempty interval. Pinning each bridging tuple at a member $W$ and a traversal $a\in\mathcal H(W)$, by \eqref{eq:two-loop-pinned-cluster} and the extent bound,
\[
    \begin{aligned}
    \sum_{\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_0}|\Psi(\mathfrak c)|&\leqslant \sum_{a\in\mathcal I_C}e^{-2\eta\delta_a/(A'_ELM)}\sum_{W\,|\,a\in\mathcal H(W)}\sum_{\mathfrak c}m_W(\mathfrak c)|\Psi(\mathfrak c)| e^{2\eta\sum_{W'\in\mathfrak c}\mathfrak s(W')}\\
    &\leqslant \sum_{a\in\mathcal I_C}e^{-c_{\times}\delta_a/(LM)}\sum_{W\,|\,a\in\mathcal H(W)}M(W)e^{3\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\;,
    \end{aligned}
\]
the inner sums over the species of the pair gas, and the pin \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} of the pair bounds the last sum by $C\rho\Delta_{\times}$. The same computation in the gas of $C_i$, with the single-square pin \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} for $C_i$ (with $| a^{(i)}_W|\leqslant M_i(W)$ and $\rho_i\leqslant \rho$, since \eqref{eq:c4-4-8} is increasing in $u$) and the traversals of $\mathcal I_{C_i}$, bounds $\sum_{\mathfrak c\in\mathcal X_i}|\Psi(\mathfrak c)|$ by $C\rho\sum_{a\in\mathcal I_{C_i}}e^{-c_{\times}\delta_a/(LM)}$. Summing, $| E^{\times}_{\xi}|\leqslant 2C\rho\Delta_{\times}$. The series are those of the countable index sets; their absolute convergence is Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}.

Finally $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_i}|\leqslant 1$ on every branch, by the second equality of \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas} and $K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}>0$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-4}: a normalised integral of a normalised character against a positive kernel), so $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant e^{| E^{\times}_{\xi}|}\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$.

(c) By Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-schur}(b) the family sum of the pair is \eqref{eq:c4-1-1}, $\mathscr R_{\xi}=\sum_{\mathfrak B\neq\varnothing}S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$ over the compatible families of groups of the pair. By the ratio bound \eqref{eq:c4-6-7} for the pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-pins}(d), valid for families containing cross groups) and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-defect},
\[
    \bigl| S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)\bigr|\leqslant | S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\prod_{i=1,2}\ \prod_{W\in\mathfrak B,\ C_i\text{-group}}K_{\chi_i}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\prod_{W\in\mathfrak B,\ \text{cross}}M(W)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\;,
\]
with $K_{\chi_i}$ on the $C_i$-groups (the last sentence of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-defect}). The $C_i$-groups of the pair are single-square groups of $C_i$ with the same $\mathfrak d_W$ and $\mathfrak a_W$, and the pair's $\rho$ dominates that of the square $C_i$, as in (b), so Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-4} for $C_i$ (on histories covered and far for both squares) bounds the sum of the first factors over the $C_i$-groups by $C_{\chi_i}n_{C_i}\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-c_ib/(LM)})$; the sum over all non-cross groups is at most $C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})$, and (a) bounds the sum of the second factors. Dropping the compatibility constraints, the sum over nonempty families is at most the exponential of the one-group sum minus one, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-5}. The constant $C_{\times}$ is the largest of those above.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The Scalar of the Pair]\label{cor:two-loop-scalar}
Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross} and of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} for each square, on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-scalar}
    S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}=\kappa_{C_1}\kappa_{C_2}\,e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}+E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}+E^{\times}_{\xi}}\;,
\end{equation}
with $E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}$ the error \eqref{eq:c4c-5-2} of the square $C_i$, bounded by \eqref{eq:c4c-5-1} with $n_i$, $J_{C_i}$ and the carrier distances $d_j$ of the segments of $C_i$, and $| E^{\times}_{\xi}|\leqslant C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ the branch is covered for each square, so Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} gives $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_i}=\kappa_{C_i}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}}$, and \eqref{eq:two-loop-factorisation} gives the result.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:two-loop-theorem}}\label{sec:two-loops-proof}
The single-contour statements used by Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem} outside the extraction (Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-2-1}, \ref{lem:c3-3-2}, \ref{lem:exterior-response-bound}, Corollary~\ref{cor:c3-6-1}, Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-1}, \ref{lem:c3-7-4}, Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}, \eqref{eq:c4-8-1} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment}) involve the contour through its observable $f_{\xi}$, the set $I_C$ of its free inputs \eqref{eq:c3-2-1}, the set $\Gamma_C$ of its contour bonds and free-input templates (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}) and its segments, and, in Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1} and \eqref{eq:c4-8-1}, through the bound $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant 1$ of \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas}, which for the pair is replaced by $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$ of (b) of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}.

For the pair, $f_{\xi}$ is \eqref{eq:two-loop-observable} at the reconstructed field, $I_C= I_{C_1}\cup I_{C_2}$, $\Gamma_C=\Gamma_{C_1}\cup\Gamma_{C_2}$, so that $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_{C_1}+C_Ln_{C_2}= C_Ln_C$, and $J_C= J_{C_1}\sqcup J_{C_2}$ is the set of the $4n_1+4n_2$ coarse segments of the two squares, $d_j$ being the distance \eqref{eq:c4c-1-1} of the square of the segment $j$ at the common carrier $I$. The constants $C$, $c$ are those of Definition~\ref{def:two-loop-constants}.

\begin{lemma}[Single-Contour Inputs for the Pair]\label{lem:two-loop-inputs}
Under the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:two-loop-theorem}:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} holds for the pair with $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1}+C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_2}$ in place of $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$, and so do Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2}, Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} and Corollary~\ref{cor:c3-6-1}; \eqref{eq:c3-7-14} holds for the pair with $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1\chi_2}$.
\item[(b)] On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $f_{\xi}(0)= W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U_1)$ and $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$, and \eqref{eq:c4-8-1} holds for the pair, every term being integrable against the history weight.
\item[(c)] On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 1+e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$; and $\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(\mathsf N_b)\leqslant 4C_Ln_C(2b+3)^4q_{\mathrm{pt}}$ and $| E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}$, with $\mathsf N_b$ and $E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4-2} formed with $\Gamma_C$ and $\mathscr R_{\xi}$ of the pair.
\item[(d)] Let $\varphi_c(b)\coloneqq \sum_{r\in C_1\sqcup C_2}e^{-c(d_T(r,b)-R_0')_+}$, the sum of the functions $\varphi_c$ of \eqref{eq:c5-7-boundary-marks} of the two squares. Pointwise on every branch, $\sum_{j\in J_C}e^{-cd_j}\leqslant \sum_b\varphi_c(b)\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}$, with $\varphi_c(b)\leqslant 2\Phi_c$ and $\sum_b\varphi_c(b)\leqslant n_CN'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$; and for every $\lambda>0$, also with $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}$ omitted,
\[
    \mathcal Z_0^{-1}\int\mathcal O\Bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\exp\Bigl(\lambda\sum_{j\in J_C}e^{-cd_j}\Bigr)\Bigr]\dd V\leqslant \exp\bigl[n_C\lambda N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\,e^{2\lambda\Phi_c}\,q^{1/C_K}\bigr]\;.
\]
\item[(e)] For $g_0$ below a further threshold depending on $L$, $M$, $M_1$, $M_2$, the group, the characters, the source constants and $c$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:two-loop-moment}
    \delta^{I,2}_q\coloneqq C\tau^2N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)\,e^{2C\tau^2\Phi_c}\,q^{1/C_K}\leqslant \exp\bigl[-c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)\bigr]\;.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) On the enlarged box the real reconstruction gives group-valued links (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2}), so $|\chi_i(Y_i)|\leqslant 1$ for the ordered link product $Y_i$ of $C_i$ and $| f_{\xi}|\leqslant 1$. By the product rule, $\nabla_bf_{\xi}=(\nabla_b\chi_1(Y_1))\chi_2(Y_2)+\chi_1(Y_1)\nabla_b\chi_2(Y_2)$, and on a branch covered for the pair, which is covered for each square (Section~\ref{sec:two-loops-setting}), the proof of \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} for the square $C_i$ gives $h(\nabla_b\chi_i(Y_i))\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_i}g_0\mathbf 1_{I_{C_i}}(b)$, so $h(\nabla_bf_{\xi})\leqslant |\chi_2(Y_2)|\,h(\nabla_b\chi_1(Y_1))+|\chi_1(Y_1)|\,h(\nabla_b\chi_2(Y_2))\leqslant (C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1}\mathbf 1_{I_{C_1}}(b)+C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_2}\mathbf 1_{I_{C_2}}(b))g_0\leqslant (C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1}+C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_2})g_0\mathbf 1_{I_C}(b)$, which is \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} for the pair.

Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2} uses the observable through $\widetilde f= f_{\xi}\circ T$, $|\widetilde f|\leqslant 1$ and \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} composed with $DT$; Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} uses it through Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2} and the support $I_C$; Corollary~\ref{cor:c3-6-1} is that lemma averaged. The enlargement in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} multiplies the constant of \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} by a factor independent of the character, so the enlarged pair constant is the sum of the enlarged constants of $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2$.

The proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5} combines Corollary~\ref{cor:c3-6-1} with Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-1} and~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}, whose bounds are sums of one-point marks over the members of $\Gamma_C$; with $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_C$ it gives \eqref{eq:c3-7-14} with $C_L\max((C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1}+C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_2})S_c,1)= C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1\chi_2}$.

(b) Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} is proved bond by bond, so on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $U_{\xi}(0)(r)= U_1(r)$ for every bond $r$ of $C_1$ and of $C_2$, and $f_{\xi}(0)= W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U_1)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}(b), $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant | S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_1}|| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_2}| e^{| E^{\times}_{\xi}|}\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$, where $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_i}|\leqslant 1$ because it is a normalised integral of a normalised character against the positive reference kernel (proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3}).

The derivation of \eqref{eq:c4-8-1} in Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-1} multiplies \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity}, which holds for the pair by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-schur}(b), by $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}$ and writes $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]=\mathsf w_{\xi} F_{\xi}(1)$ on $A^c_{\mathrm{cov}}$; \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} holds with $W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C)$ in place of $W_{\chi}(C)$, $f_{\xi}$ being jointly Borel with $| f_{\xi}|\leqslant 1$ (the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}). Its integrability uses $| F_{\xi}(s)|\leqslant 1$ ($F_{\xi}(s)=\int f_{\xi}\,\dd\nu_{\xi;s}$ with $| f_{\xi}|\leqslant 1$), $|\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]|\leqslant (C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_1}+C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi_2})g_0r| I_C|$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ by (a), and a bound on $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)$, which is now $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$ in place of $3$.

(c) On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, $\mathscr R_{\xi}= F_{\xi}(0)-S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)$ by \eqref{eq:part1-scalar-extraction} for the pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-schur}(b)), so $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 1+e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}\leqslant 2e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}$ by (b). The union bound of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}, over the at most $C_Ln_C$ members of $\Gamma_C$, gives the bound on $\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(\mathsf N_b)$. Positivity of $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ then gives $| E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant 2e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}\cdot4C_Ln_C(2b+3)^4q_{\mathrm{pt}}$, and the last step of that proof gives $8C_L(2b+3)^4q_{\mathrm{pt}}\leqslant C'_Le^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}$.

(d) The first inequality of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expmoment-I} is proved segment by segment, the term of a segment being bounded through the contour bonds of its own square (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-expmoment}). The two squares' inequalities at the common carrier add up to the pointwise bound. Each square's $\varphi_c$ is at most $\Phi_c$ and has sum at most $n_{C_i}N'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c)$, by the counts of that proof. The rest of that proof applies with the weights $w_b=\varphi_c(b)\leqslant 2\Phi_c$: the expansion over the marks $\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}$, one per bond, and the joint bound \eqref{eq:c5-7-joint-I}, which holds for every finite set of bonds. They bound the average by $\exp(\hat q\sum_b(e^{\lambda w_b}-1))$ with $\hat q\coloneqq q^{1/C_K}$. Since $e^x-1\leqslant xe^x$ for $x\geqslant 0$, this is at most $\exp(\hat q\lambda e^{2\lambda\Phi_c}\sum_bw_b)$, and the indicator enters only through $\mathbf 1\leqslant 1$.

(e) Since $\tau<1$ and $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}), $\log\delta^{I,2}_q\leqslant \log(CN'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c))+2C\Phi_c-c_*\pi_*^2/C_K$. Moreover $\pi_*^2/C_K\geqslant c'(\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0-4\mathfrak r}$ with $2p_0-4\mathfrak r\geqslant 12$, by \eqref{eq:c5-7-delta-small}. So $c_*\pi_*^2/(2C_K)\geqslant \log(CN'_{\mathrm{lat}}(c))+2C\Phi_c$ for small $g_0$, which is \eqref{eq:two-loop-moment}.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:two-loop-theorem}]
(i) By Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(b),
\[
\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C)]=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}(C;U_1)]+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\;,
\]
with all terms integrable. On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, \eqref{eq:two-loop-scalar} (Corollary~\ref{cor:two-loop-scalar}) applies. Its hypotheses are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross} and, for each square, those of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, which (H2) and (H3) for that square imply as in the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}. After the substitution the first integrand is still exactly $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)$. The statements on $\kappa_{C_i}$ are Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}(i) for $(C_i,\chi_i)$.

(ii) The pair's $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ is contained in the covered event of each square, on which Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1} bounds $E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}$ with the constants $C_i$, $c_i$ of $\chi_i$; these bounds are at most the stated ones, since $C_i\leqslant C$ and $e^{-c_ix}\leqslant e^{-cx}$ for $x\geqslant 0$. The elementary bounds give $C\tau^2(9n_i+1)$, as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}. The bound on $E^{\times}_{\xi}$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-cross}(b) with \eqref{eq:two-loop-cross-sum}.

As in Section~\ref{sec:c4-2}, $E_{\mathrm{def}}= E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}+E^{\mathrm{far}}_{\mathrm{def}}$, both terms being integrable by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(c). The near term is bounded in Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(c). The histories of $A_{\mathrm{cov}}\cap\mathsf N_b^c$ are covered and far for the pair. On them \eqref{eq:two-loop-family-sum} and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(b) give $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}(e^{X+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}-1)$ with $X\coloneqq C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})$. So $| E^{\mathrm{far}}_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}(e^{X+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}-1)$, by the positivity of $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$. The bound on $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ is \eqref{eq:c3-7-14} for the pair (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(a)).

(iii) The first bound follows from the positivity of $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$, $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$, $| W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}|\leqslant 1$ and $| e^z|\leqslant e^{| z|}$ with (ii).

Under the condition of (H3) for (iii) for the square $C_i$, $4n_ie^{-c_i\iota_T}\leqslant 1$. So Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split} for the square $C_i$ gives $| E^{\circ}_{\xi,i}|\leqslant C_i\tau^2(2+1/c_i)+C_i\tau^2\sum_{j\in J_{C_i}}e^{-c_id_j}\leqslant C\tau^2(2+1/c)+C\tau^2\sum_{j\in J_{C_i}}e^{-cd_j}$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$. Hence $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}|+| E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}|}\leqslant e^{2C\tau^2(2+1/c)}\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\exp(C\tau^2\sum_{j\in J_C}e^{-cd_j})$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(d) at $\lambda= C\tau^2$, with (e), gives \eqref{eq:thm-two-moment}.

The modulus of the leading term is at most $|\kappa_{C_1}\kappa_{C_2}| e^{C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{| E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}|+| E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}|}]$, by $| W_{\chi_1,\chi_2}|\leqslant 1$ and (ii). Pointwise on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, with $z= E^{\circ}_{\xi,1}+E^{\circ}_{\xi,2}+E^{\times}_{\xi}$, $| e^z-1|\leqslant e^{| z|}-1\leqslant e^{2C\tau^2(2+1/c)+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}}\exp(C\tau^2\sum_{j\in J_C}e^{-cd_j})-1$, a nonnegative function. Its $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$-average without the indicator is at most $\exp[2C\tau^2(2+1/c)+C_{\times}\rho\Delta_{\times}+n_C\delta^{I,2}_q]-1$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:two-loop-inputs}(d) and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$.
\end{proof}

\section{Towards the Next Step}\label{sec:next-step}
The statement of this section is a conjecture; nothing in the other sections uses it. It concerns loops whose side is a power of the block size, $n= L^k$ with an integer $k\geqslant 0$, after $k+1$ steps (the letter $K$ is the exponent of \cite{BalabanRG1} in (H3) and the index of $\sigma_K$, $C_K$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:c5-7-joint}).

On a torus of (H3) the lattice $L^{k+1}\mathbb Z^4$ and its plaquettes are defined ($K_{\mu}=2L^{m-1}\geqslant 3(n+2)$ forces $m\geqslant k+2$, so $L^{k+1}$ divides every period $N_{\mu}=2L^m$), and a translation of $C_n$ does not change $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]$ (the Wilson measure $\rho_0(U)\,\dd U$ on the periodic torus is invariant under lattice translations, its action being a sum over all plaquettes and the Haar measure a product measure; Section~\ref{sec:extent-weights} uses the remaining lattice symmetries), so the corners of $C_n$ are taken in $L^{k+1}\mathbb Z^4$; then $C_n$, of side $L^{k+1}$ fine units, is a contour of the lattice of spacing $L^j\varepsilon$ for every $j\leqslant k+1$ and the boundary of a single plaquette of the lattice of spacing $L^{k+1}\varepsilon$. The scales $\tau$ and $\pi_*$ are those of the notation paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:main-result}, at the bare coupling $g_0$.

\begin{conjecture}[The Loop along the Scales]\label{conj:iteration}
Let $G$, $\chi$ be as in (H1), and let the cutoff prescription $\sigma$ and the constants be fixed as in (H2). There are $C,c>0$, depending on $L$, the group, the character, $\sigma$ and the constants fixed in (H2) only, thresholds $g^*_j>0$ ($j\geqslant 1$) and, for $0< g_0< g^*_j$, real numbers $\delta m_j$ and complex numbers $\zeta_j$, depending on $g_0$, $\varepsilon$, $j$, $L$, the group, the character, $\sigma$ and the fixed prescriptions listed in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}(i) only, with $z_j\coloneqq e^{\zeta_j}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-iteration-coefficients}
    \delta m_1=\delta m^{\sigma}(g_0,\varepsilon)\;,\qquad\zeta_1=\frac14\sum_{(v,w)\in\mathscr C_{\square}}\zeta^{\sigma}_{v,w}(g_0)\;,\qquad|\delta m_j|\,L^j\varepsilon\leqslant C\tau^2\;,\qquad|\zeta_j|\leqslant C\tau^2\;,
\end{equation}
so that $z_1= z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}(g_0,\pi/2)$ \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor}, such that for every integer $k\geqslant 0$, with $n= L^k$, there is $g_{\mathrm{it}}(k)\leqslant \min_{j\leqslant k+1}g^*_j$ such that for $0< g_0< g_{\mathrm{it}}(k)$, on every torus of (H3) whose exponent $m$ exceeds a bound depending on $k$ and $g_0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:conj-iteration}
    \begin{gathered}
        \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]=\kappa^{(k+1)}_{C_n}(1+R)+R'\;,\qquad
        \kappa^{(k+1)}_{C_n}=\exp\Bigl(-P(C_n)\sum_{j=1}^{k+1}\delta m_j\Bigr)\prod_{j=1}^{k+1}z_j^4\;,\\
        | R|\leqslant C\bigl[(k+2)\tau^2+n_Ce^{-c\pi_*^2}\bigr]\;,\qquad| R'|\leqslant Cn_Ce^{-c\pi_*^2}\;.
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\end{conjecture}

\begin{remark}[Content of the Conjecture and What a Proof Needs]\label{rem:next-step}
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)] The $j$-th coefficients do not depend on the size of the loop: the perimeter part is a sum over the scales of perimeter coefficients, each of size $\tau^2$ in units of its own lattice spacing, so $| P(C_n)\sum_j\delta m_j|\leqslant 4C\tau^2n(1+L^{-1}+L^{-2}+\cdots)$, while the corner factors contribute one factor $z_j^4$ per scale, $k+1=\log_L(nL)$ in all. For $k=0$ the statement is Theorem~\ref{thm:main-theorem}, with the relative form of the far-history bound of Remark~\ref{rem:main-regime}(1), which places the second term of the bound on $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ in $\kappa_{C_1}R$, together with the claim that the leading expectation $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_1;U_1)]$ of the single-plaquette loop is $1+O(\tau^2+n_Ce^{-c\pi_*^2})$; the first step gives the bounds \eqref{eq:thm-main-bounds}, the upper bounds of (iii) and, by Corollaries~\ref{cor:main-factorisation} and~\ref{cor:main-leading-size} at $n=1$, $1+O(\tau^2+\varepsilon_1+(L^2+LC_L)q+n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q)$, in which the area term $\varepsilon_1$ of the bound, of order $g_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ by \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} as quoted in Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, is not $O(\tau^2)$; whether the leading expectation itself is $1+O(\tau^2)$ is not decided here.
\item[(2)] For $j\geqslant 2$ the coefficients $\delta m_j$, $z_j$ are not defined in this paper; they are to be the perimeter coefficient and the corner factor of the $j$-th step, computed from the density after $j-1$ steps as \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass} and \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor} compute them from the flat reference integrals $N^{\sigma}_{C,T}$, $D^{\sigma}_T$ of \eqref{eq:marginal-literal-ratio}, in which case the conjecture says that the coefficients of every step have the size that Sections~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} and~\ref{sec:marginal-corner} prove for the first.

At the stated precision the corner factors are not separately determined: $| z_j^4-1|=| e^{4\zeta_j}-1|\leqslant e^{4C\tau^2}-1$, so $|\prod_{j\leqslant k+1}z_j^4-1|\leqslant e^{4C(k+1)\tau^2}-1\leqslant 8C(k+1)\tau^2$ once $4C(k+1)\tau^2\leqslant 1$, and replacing every $z_j$ by $1$ replaces $1+R$ by $\prod_jz_j^4(1+R)$, with $|\prod_jz_j^4(1+R)-1|\leqslant 8C(k+1)\tau^2(1+| R|)+| R|$, which a larger $C$ in the bound on $R$ absorbs below a threshold depending on $k$; the $z_j$ record where the term $(k+2)\tau^2$ of $R$ comes from. With the threshold $g_{\mathrm{it}}(k)$ depending on $k$, $R'$ is not needed either: $|\kappa^{(k+1)}_{C_n}|\geqslant e^{-8C\tau^2(n+k+1)}$ ($L\geqslant 2$), so once $8C\tau^2(n+k+1)\leqslant 1$ the bound on $R'$ is at most $eCn_Ce^{-c\pi_*^2}|\kappa^{(k+1)}_{C_n}|$ and $R'$ can be moved into $\kappa^{(k+1)}_{C_n}R$ at the cost of replacing $C$ by $(1+e)C$; it is substantive in the form with a threshold independent of $k$.

Since $\delta m_1=\delta m^{\sigma}$ is given, what the statement determines beyond the first step and beyond $O((k+2)\tau^2)$ is $P(C_n)\sum_{j\geqslant 2}\delta m_j$, of size at most $4C\tau^2(n-1)/(L-1)$, modulo $O((k+2)\tau^2)$. For $k\leqslant 1$ this is at most $4C\tau^2$, so nothing beyond the first step is determined; in general the scales $j$ with $L^{k+1-j}\leqslant k+2$ contribute at most $4C\tau^2(k+2)L/(L-1)$, also of order $(k+2)\tau^2$, and the content lies in the scales $j\geqslant 2$ with $L^{k+1-j}> k+2$.
\item[(3)] A proof by $k+1$ applications of the first step needs the following ((c) only for a threshold independent of $k$), none of which is proved here beyond the first step.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] A local form of the leading term: on the covered event, $W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)e^{E^{\partial}_{\xi}}$ as a function of the coarse field $V$ near the loop, a coarse Wilson loop times the exponential of a sum over the coarse bonds of the loop of terms depending on $V$ within a fixed distance of the bond, analytic on the small-field chart, gauge covariant and bounded by $C\tau^2$, with the history labels absorbed into the large-field expansion of $\rho_1$; this is what turns the output of the step, the pair of the complex measure $\kappa_{C_n}^{-1}N_1$ and the measure $\rho_1$ (Remark~\ref{rem:main-regime}(2)), into an input of the same type.
\item[(b)] General-step analogues of (B1)--(B4), which Section 2 of \cite{BalabanCRE} does not state as such: it formulates the inductive assumption with the operations corresponding to $\mathbf T_1$ left undefined, only their general properties being formulated (p.254), their inductive definition being deferred to its next section and forthcoming papers (pp.254--255), and with modifications connected with new terms obtained by the $\mathbf R$-operations (p.254), among them the admitted case $\Lambda_j=\Omega_j$ (p.255); the sets $S_j\subset\Omega_j\cap\Lambda_j^c$ and the functions $\chi(\Omega_j\cap\Lambda_j^c,S_j)$, $\zeta(\Omega_j^c)$ are the general-step forms of the first-step objects of \cite[(1.29), pp.~254--255]{BalabanCRE}; the geometry and the scales are \cite[(2.1)--(2.9)]{BalabanCRE}, with the couplings of the first $k+1$ scales compared through the first inequality $g_n\leqslant (1+g_n^2\beta'(n-m))^{1/2}g_m$ of \cite[(2.6), p.~255]{BalabanCRE}, $g_{k+1}^2\beta'(k+1)$ being small for $g_0< g_{\mathrm{it}}(k)$ (Section~\ref{app:thresholds} quotes (2.6) for the first step).
\item[(c)] The defect: the far-history part of \eqref{eq:c4-12-7} is relative to $|\kappa_{C_n}|$ but of order $x= C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})$ when $x\leqslant 1$, polynomially small per contour bond (Remark~\ref{rem:main-regime}(1)); for a threshold independent of $k$ it must be shown to be a perimeter-local correction, absorbed in $\delta m_2$ and $z_2$ at the next step. Below a threshold depending on $k$ it is at most $C\tau^2$ relative to $|\kappa_{C_n}|$ ($\rho\leqslant C\tau^2$, $\varepsilon_1\to0$ and $e^{-cb/(LM)}\to0$ at fixed $n_C$) and goes into $R$, as at $k=0$.
\item[(d)] The absolute terms $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ and the near-history part of $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ at the $j$-th step, of order $4L^{k+2-j}e^{-c\pi_{*,j}^2}$ for the loop of $4L^{k+2-j}$ bonds of the lattice of spacing $L^{j-1}\varepsilon$, with $\pi_{*,j}\coloneqq\min(p_0(g_{j-1}),p_0(g_j))$ the scale of that step, $\pi_{*,j}^2\geqslant \pi_*^2/2$ once $g_i^2\beta'i\leqslant 1$ for $i\in\{ j-1,j\}$ and $(1-\log2/\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0}\geqslant 1/2$ (the first inequality of \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} with $m=0$, $n= i\geqslant 1$ gives $g_i^2\leqslant (1+g_i^2\beta'i)g_0^2\leqslant 2g_0^2$, hence $\log g_i^{-2}\geqslant \log g_0^{-2}-\log2$ and $p_0(g_i)^2\geqslant p_0(g_0)^2/2\geqslant \pi_*^2/2$; for $i=0$ this is $p_0(g_0)\geqslant \pi_*$), and entering multiplied by the leading coefficients of the steps $1,\ldots,j-1$, whose product must be bounded; so that their sum over the steps is at most $Cn_Ce^{-c\pi_*^2}$; their relative size is discussed in Remark~\ref{rem:main-regime}(1).
\item[(e)] At every step the remainder of Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation}, which at the first step is at most $e^{n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q}-1$, and the torus and corner part $E^{\circ}_{T,n}$, at most $C\tau^2(2+1/c)$, one source of the term $(k+2)\tau^2$.
\item[(f)] The endpoint: the leading expectation of the single-plaquette loop at the last step is $1+O(\tau^2)$; at the first step Corollary~\ref{cor:main-leading-size} gives $1+O(\tau^2+\varepsilon_1+(L^2+LC_L)q+n_C\delta^{\sharp}_q)$ only, and its area term $\varepsilon_1$, which comes from the deterministic bound on the plaquettes of the background, must be replaced by a bound of order $\tau^2$.
\item[(g)] The terms of the $\mathbf R$-operations at every step, by which the general representation modifies the first-step representation \cite[(1.28)--(1.30), p.~254]{BalabanCRE}.
\end{itemize}
\end{itemize}
\end{remark}

\appendix
\section{The Flat Covariance}\label{app:flat-covariance}

The bulk coefficient uses the flat fluctuation operator on the infinite lattice with the same periodic block grid and constraint extension. A uniform lower bound on compatible finite tori comes first; the operator is then constructed and its inverse compared with the finite-torus inverses.

The spatial dimension is four throughout this comparison. For a site field $\lambda$, let $(D\lambda)(x,x')\coloneqq\lambda(x')-\lambda(x)$. For an oriented plaquette $p$, let $(\operatorname{curl}a)(p)\coloneqq a(\partial p)$, where $a(\gamma)$ is the signed sum along an oriented path $\gamma$. All squared norms in this comparison sum the Lie-algebra inner product over positive bonds, plaquettes or sites of the indicated carrier. The mean path sum is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-mean-path}
    (\Phi a)(y,x)\coloneqq\frac{1}{|\mathcal G(y,x)|}
        \sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal G(y,x)}a(\gamma)\;.
\end{equation}
\cite[(0.8) and (2.5)]{BalabanRG1} identify $G^{(2)}(a)=\|\Phi a\|^2$. Differentiating \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, with $x'= x+Le_{\mu}$ for $c=(y,y+Le_{\mu})$, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-two-averages}
    \begin{aligned}
        (Q_1a)(c)&= L^{-5}\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y}a([x,x'])\;,\\
        (Qa)(c)&=(Q_1a)(c)
            +L^{-5}\sum_{x\in\mathcal B_y}
                ((\Phi a)(y,x)-(\Phi a)(y+Le_{\mu},x'))\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The operator $Q_1$ is the straight-path average in \cite[(2.125)]{BalabanPRT2}; it differs from $Q$. Telescoping these paths gives $Q(D\lambda)(c)=(\lambda(c_+)-\lambda(c_-))/L$.

The lower corner of each block is $o_y= y-\frac{L-1}{2}\sum_{\mu=1}^4 e_{\mu}$. Let $\kappa_{y,x}$ traverse the coordinate displacements from $o_y$ to $x$ in the order $1,\ldots,4$. The union of these paths is a spanning tree. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-tree-gauge}
    \lambda(x)\coloneqq a(\kappa_{y,x})-a(\kappa_{y,y}),
    \qquad b\coloneqq a-D\lambda,
    \qquad E(y,x)\coloneqq(\Phi a)(y,x)-\lambda(x)\;.
\end{equation}
The block partition makes $\lambda$ a periodic site field, and $\lambda(y)=0$. Every tree bond of $b$ vanishes. Moreover $Qb= Qa$ and $\operatorname{curl}b=\operatorname{curl}a$.

The Lie-algebra element $E(y,x)$ is a mean of the signed sums of $a$ around the closed walks obtained by adjoining a mean path from $y$ to $x$ to the reverse tree path. Each walk lies inside its block and has length at most $12(L-1)$. It is filled by commuting adjacent steps in different directions and cancelling opposite steps in each direction. Every commutation adds one unit plaquette. It remains inside the block, because exchanging two different directions preserves the intermediate coordinate ranges. Sorting the directions takes at most the square of the walk length commutations. Thus a filling has integer plaquette coefficients with total absolute sum at most $J_L=144(L-1)^2$. Cauchy--Schwarz and averaging give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-filling-bound}
    \| E\|^2\leqslant K_L\|\operatorname{curl}a\|^2,
    \qquad K_L= L^4J_L^2\;.
\end{equation}
There are $L^4$ site tests per block and the interior plaquettes of different blocks are disjoint, so this constant is independent of their number. Also $\|\lambda\|^2\leqslant 2\|\Phi a\|^2+2\| E\|^2$ and $\| D\lambda\|^2\leqslant 16\|\lambda\|^2$.

For $Qa=0$, equation \eqref{eq:covariance-two-averages} applied to $b$ has $\Phi b= E$. Jensen's inequality and the eight incidences of a block with coarse bonds imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-constraint-error}
    \| Q_1b\|^2\leqslant 16L^{-6}\| E\|^2\;.
\end{equation}
For the block-tree gauge, the following periodic bound holds with $A_L\coloneqq 384L^5$:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-hard-bound}
    \| b\|^2\leqslant A_L
        (\|\operatorname{curl}b\|^2+L^2\| Q_1b\|^2)\;.
\end{equation}
For the proof, the coordinate permutation $R(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)=(x_4,x_3,x_2,x_1)$ reverses the block-tree order. Its pushforward on positive bonds is $(R_*b)(Rx,Rx+e_{5-\mu})= b(x,x+e_{\mu})$. It preserves the bond and curl norms, and \eqref{eq:covariance-two-averages} gives $(Q_1R_*b)(Rc)=(Q_1b)(c)$. Thus it suffices to prove the same bound for the reversed order $4,\ldots,1$, after translating a block corner to the origin. The inner product remains the fixed $\tr_N$ inner product throughout.

\paragraph{Direct Face Estimates in the Positive-Bond Norm.}
The fine lattice has $N_{\mu}= LK_{\mu}$ sites in direction $\mu$, with odd $L\geqslant 3$ and $K_{\mu}\geqslant 3$. The preceding axis reversal permutes the periods to $(N_4,N_3,N_2,N_1)$ and reduces the proof to the tree order $4,\ldots,1$. Its inverse restores the original order at the end. A local calculation uses the translated block $B_0=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^4$. All norms and sums below count positive bond or plaquette labels once, with the fixed $\mathfrak g$ inner product.

For a block $B$, let $\mathcal E_B^+$ be its positive fine bonds with both endpoints in $B$, and let $\mathcal P_B^+$ be its positive plaquettes with all vertices in $B$. For a boundary face $\Sigma\subset B$, let $\mathcal E_{\Sigma}^+$ be its positive fine bonds with both endpoints in $\Sigma$. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-block-face-energies}
    I_B\coloneqq\sum_{r\in \mathcal E_B^+}\| b(r)\|_{\mathfrak g}^2,
    \qquad
    T_{\Sigma}\coloneqq\sum_{r\in \mathcal E_{\Sigma}^+}\| b(r)\|_{\mathfrak g}^2,
    \qquad
    F_B\coloneqq\sum_{p\in \mathcal P_B^+}
        \|(\operatorname{curl}b)(p)\|_{\mathfrak g}^2\;.
\end{equation}
These are scalar quadratic forms in the tree-gauged field. For the flat comparison, a linear gauge change $a\mapsto a+D\omega$ preserving its coarse average has constant values $\omega(y)$ on the connected coarse lattice. Equation \eqref{eq:covariance-tree-gauge} then leaves $b$ unchanged. Constant colour conjugation sends $b$ to $\operatorname{Ad}_g b$ and preserves every inner product below.

\paragraph{The Block-Face Trace Bound.}
Let $b_{\nu}(x)\coloneqq b(x,x+e_{\nu})$ for an internal positive bond of $B_0$, so $x_{\nu}\leqslant L-2$. The source tree condition makes $b_{\nu}(x)=0$ whenever $x_1=\cdots= x_{\nu-1}=0$; in particular $b_1=0$. For $k<\nu$ and integers $0\leqslant t< x_k$, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-telescoping-point}
    u^{(k)}(x,t)\coloneqq(0,\ldots,0,t,x_{k+1},\ldots,x_4)\;.
\end{equation}
Here the $t$ is the $k$th component. Let $F_{k\nu}(u)$ be the curl on the positive $(k,\nu)$ plaquette based at $u$. On the plane $u_1=\cdots= u_{k-1}=0$, both $k$-direction sides of that plaquette vanish by the tree condition. Successive telescoping therefore gives the identity used before \cite[(2.123)]{BalabanPRT2}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-tree-telescoping}
    b_{\nu}(x)=
        \sum_{k=1}^{\nu-1}\sum_{t=0}^{x_k-1}
            F_{k\nu}(u^{(k)}(x,t))\;.
\end{equation}
Every displayed plaquette lies inside $B_0$. The number of terms is at most $3(L-1)$.

Let $x_{\mu}=\alpha$, with $\alpha\in \{0,L-1\}$, be a face and $\nu\ne \mu$ a tangential component. For a fixed $(k,\nu)$ plaquette in \eqref{eq:direct-tree-telescoping}, its multiplicity in the face sum is bounded by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-face-multiplicities}
    \begin{array}{c| c}
        \mu< k & L^{k-2}\,L\leqslant L^2\\
        \mu= k & L^{k-1}\leqslant L^2\\
        \mu> k,\ \mu\ne \nu & L^{k-1}\,L\leqslant L^2
    \end{array}\;.
\end{equation}
In the first row, one of the $k-1$ otherwise free earlier components is fixed by the face. In the second row, $x_k$ is fixed, so a given $t$ occurs at most once. In the third row, the two distinct indices $\mu,\nu$ exceed $k$, hence $k\leqslant 2$. In all rows, later components are fixed by the plaquette label. Without the face restriction the multiplicity is at most $L^{k-1}L\leqslant L^3$. For different $\nu$, the plaquette pairs $(k,\nu)$ are disjoint. Cauchy--Schwarz in \eqref{eq:direct-tree-telescoping}, followed by these counts, proves
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-block-face-bound}
    I_B\leqslant 3(L-1)L^3F_B\leqslant 4L^4F_B,
    \qquad
    T_{\Sigma}\leqslant 3(L-1)L^2F_B\leqslant 4L^3F_B\;.
\end{equation}
The first estimate is the positive-label version of \cite[(2.123)]{BalabanPRT2}. The second is the face restriction of its telescoping calculation.

\paragraph{The Interface Poincare Estimate.}
Let $F=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^3$ and let $\mathcal E_F^+$ be its positive nearest-neighbour edges. The Neumann graph Laplacian $\mathcal L_F \colon \mathfrak g^F \to \mathfrak g^F$ acts componentwise. For $s\in F$, it is given by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-face-laplacian}
    (\mathcal L_Fv)(s)\coloneqq
        \sum_{\substack{s'\in F\\ | s'-s|_1=1}}
            (v(s)-v(s'))\;.
\end{equation}
It has quadratic form $\sum_{(s,s')\in \mathcal E_F^+}\| v(s')-v(s)\|^2$. For $m\in \{0,\ldots,L-1\}^3$, its real scalar eigenbasis and eigenvalues are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-face-spectrum}
    v_m(s)=\prod_{i=1}^3
        \cos\left(\frac{\pi m_i(s_i+1/2)}{L}\right),
    \qquad
    \lambda_m=4\sum_{i=1}^3
        \sin^2\left(\frac{\pi m_i}{2L}\right)\;.
\end{equation}
The one-dimensional cosine identity verifies the eigenvalue at interior and endpoint vertices; finite cosine orthogonality gives a basis. Only $m=0$ is constant. Since $\sin t\geqslant 2t/\pi$ for $0\leqslant t\leqslant \pi/2$, every nonzero eigenvalue is at least $4/L^2$. Applied to each orthonormal colour component, with $\bar v\coloneqq L^{-3}\sum_{s\in F}v(s)$, this gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-face-poincare}
    \sum_{s\in F}\| v(s)-\bar v\|^2
        \leqslant \frac{L^2}{4}
            \sum_{(s,s')\in \mathcal E_F^+}
                \| v(s')-v(s)\|^2\;.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Crossing Bonds and the Exact Average.}
For a positive coarse bond $c$ in direction $\mu$, its two endpoint blocks are $B_-= o+\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^4$ and $B_+= B_-+Le_{\mu}$. The transverse label set is $F_c=\{0,\ldots,L-1\}^{\{\nu\ne \mu\}}$, identified with $F$ by increasing transverse index. In that label set, $e_{\nu}$ denotes its transverse coordinate unit vector. For $s\in F_c$, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-data}
    x_c(s)\coloneqq o+(L-1)e_{\mu}+\sum_{\nu\ne \mu}s_{\nu} e_{\nu},
    \qquad
    t_c(s)\coloneqq b(x_c(s),x_c(s)+e_{\mu}),
    \qquad
    J_c\coloneqq\sum_{s\in F_c}\| t_c(s)\|^2\;.
\end{equation}
Let $\Sigma_-$ and $\Sigma_+$ be the facing boundary faces in $B_-$ and $B_+$. For $\nu\ne \mu$ and $s,s+e_{\nu}\in F_c$, the plaquette based at $x_c(s)$ has curl
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-curl}
    t_c(s)-t_c(s+e_{\nu})
        +b_{\nu}(x_c(s)+e_{\mu})-b_{\nu}(x_c(s))\;.
\end{equation}
For $\nu<\mu$ its sign is opposite to the positive plaquette convention; its squared norm is unchanged. Let $F_c^{\mathrm{cr}}$ be the sum of these squared curls, each transverse edge once. The inequality $\| u+v+w\|^2\leqslant 3(\| u\|^2+\| v\|^2+\| w\|^2)$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-gradient}
    \sum_{\nu\ne \mu}
        \sum_{\substack{s\in F_c\\s+e_{\nu}\in F_c}}
            \| t_c(s+e_{\nu})-t_c(s)\|^2
        \leqslant 3(F_c^{\mathrm{cr}}+T_{\Sigma_-}+T_{\Sigma_+})\;.
\end{equation}

Let $I_{B,\mu}$ be the part of $I_B$ in direction $\mu$, and let $\bar t_c\coloneqq L^{-3}\sum_{s\in F_c}t_c(s)$. The straight-path formula \eqref{eq:covariance-two-averages} has the exact decomposition
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-average}
    \begin{aligned}
        (Q_1b)(c)&= L^{-1}\bar t_c+q_c\;,\\
        q_c&= L^{-5}\sum_{s\in F_c}
                \sum_{i=0}^{L-2}(i+1)
                    b_{\mu}\left(o+ie_{\mu}+
                        \sum_{\nu\ne \mu}s_{\nu} e_{\nu}\right)\\
            &\quad+L^{-5}\sum_{s\in F_c}\sum_{j=0}^{L-2}(L-1-j)
                    b_{\mu}\left(o+(L+j)e_{\mu}+
                        \sum_{\nu\ne \mu}s_{\nu} e_{\nu}\right)
            \;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Indeed, an internal lower-block bond at position $i$ belongs to $i+1$ starting paths, and an internal upper-block bond at position $j$ belongs to $L-1-j$ paths. Each crossing bond belongs to $L$ paths. This is the positive-label content of \cite[(2.125)]{BalabanPRT2}. There are at most $2L^4$ internal bonds in this sum, and every coefficient is at most $L^{-4}$. Cauchy--Schwarz therefore yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-mean}
    \| q_c\|^2\leqslant 2L^{-4}(I_{B_-,\mu}+I_{B_+,\mu}),
    \qquad
    L^3\|\bar t_c\|^2
        \leqslant 2L^5\|(Q_1b)(c)\|^2
            +4L(I_{B_-,\mu}+I_{B_+,\mu})\;.
\end{equation}
Combining the exact mean/variance decomposition of $J_c$ with \eqref{eq:direct-face-poincare}, \eqref{eq:direct-interface-gradient} and \eqref{eq:direct-interface-mean} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-bound}
    J_c\leqslant \frac{3L^2}{4}
        (F_c^{\mathrm{cr}}+T_{\Sigma_-}+T_{\Sigma_+})
        +2L^5\|(Q_1b)(c)\|^2
        +4L(I_{B_-,\mu}+I_{B_+,\mu})\;.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{The Periodic Sum and Its Payments.}
All sums over $c$ run over the positive coarse bonds $E_1$, and $\mu(c)$ is the direction of $c$. Let $\mathscr I\coloneqq\sum_B I_B$, $\mathscr F=\|\operatorname{curl}b\|^2$ and $\mathscr Q=\| Q_1b\|^2$. Every positive fine bond is either internal to exactly one block or crosses exactly one positive coarse interface, so $\| b\|^2=\mathscr I+\sum_cJ_c$.

Every plaquette counted by $F_c^{\mathrm{cr}}$ crosses only the $\mu$-interface: its transverse edge remains inside the face. It is therefore counted for at most one $c$. Each block has eight incident faces, and an internal $\mu$-bond enters the last term of \eqref{eq:direct-interface-bound} only for the incoming and outgoing $\mu$-interfaces. Consequently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-interface-incidences}
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathscr I&\leqslant 4L^4\mathscr F\;,\\
        \sum_cF_c^{\mathrm{cr}}&\leqslant \mathscr F\;,\\
        \sum_c(T_{\Sigma_-}+T_{\Sigma_+})&\leqslant 32L^3\mathscr F\;,\\
        \sum_{c \in E_1}
            (I_{B_-,\mu(c)}+I_{B_+,\mu(c)})&=2\mathscr I\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Thus summing \eqref{eq:direct-interface-bound} gives the explicit payment
\begin{equation}\label{eq:direct-hard-bound-payment}
    \begin{aligned}
        \| b\|^2
        &\leqslant (1+8L)\mathscr I
            +\frac{3L^2}{4}\mathscr F
            +24L^5\mathscr F+2L^5\mathscr Q\\
        &\leqslant \left(4L^4+56L^5+\frac{3L^2}{4}\right)\mathscr F
            +2L^5\mathscr Q\\
        &\leqslant 384L^5(\mathscr F+L^2\mathscr Q)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
The last inequality uses $L\geqslant 3$; its coefficients are bounded by $61L^5$ and $2L^5$, respectively. This proves \eqref{eq:covariance-hard-bound}.

Combining the bound \eqref{eq:covariance-hard-bound} with the constraint-error bound gives $\| b\|^2\leqslant A_L(1+16L^{-4}K_L)\|\operatorname{curl}a\|^2$. Since $a= b+D\lambda$, the bound $\| a\|^2\leqslant 2\| b\|^2+2\| D\lambda\|^2$ proves, for $Qa=0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:flat-coercivity}
    \| a\|_2^2\leqslant C_L
        \bigl(\|\operatorname{curl}a\|_2^2+G^{(2)}(a)\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
An explicit admissible constant is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-coercivity-constant}
    C_L\coloneqq\max(64,\,2A_L(1+16L^{-4}K_L)+64K_L)\;.
\end{equation}
At the flat background, differentiating the original action and exponential gauge functional in \eqref{eq:action-primitive} gives $\langle a,\Delta_1a\rangle=\|\operatorname{curl}a\|^2+\|\Phi a\|^2$. Substituting $a=\mathsf C B$ in \eqref{eq:flat-coercivity} uses $Q\mathsf C B=0$ and $\|\mathsf C B\|\geqslant \| B\|$, because the free bonds are unchanged. Consequently the free Hessian satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:covariance-uniform-gap}
    \mathsf H\geqslant \gamma_L I,
    \qquad \gamma_L= C_L^{-1}\;.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Construction on the Infinite Lattice.}
Let $E_{\infty}\coloneqq\mathbb Z^4\times\{1,2,3,4\}$ denote positive fine bonds, with $(x,\mu)$ representing $(x,x+e_{\mu})$. The coarse centres are $L\mathbb Z^4$, with the centred blocks and path families specified above. Removing the designated bonds gives $E_{*,\infty}$. The square-summable field spaces use the same real Lie-algebra inner product as the finite-torus calculation. On finitely supported fields, $\Phi_{\infty}$ and $Q_{\infty}$ are defined by \eqref{eq:covariance-mean-path}--\eqref{eq:covariance-two-averages}, and $\mathsf C_{\infty}$ by \eqref{eq:constraint-extension}. The designated coefficient is $Q_{0,\infty}= L^{-4}I$, so the inverse in that definition is fibrewise. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-operator-definition}
    \Delta_{\infty}\coloneqq\operatorname{curl}^*\operatorname{curl}
        +\Phi_{\infty}^*\Phi_{\infty},
    \qquad
    \mathsf H_{\infty}\coloneqq\mathsf C_{\infty}^*\Delta_{\infty}\mathsf C_{\infty}\;.
\end{equation}
The coefficient $Q_{0,\infty}$ follows from \eqref{eq:covariance-two-averages}. The within-block paths entering $\Phi$ contain no designated bond. For $b_0(c)$, precisely $L$ of the translated straight paths in the sum for $Q_1(c)$ traverse that bond: their transverse coordinates equal those of the coarse centres, and their longitudinal initial positions range over the $L$ sites of the block. No translated path for another coarse bond contains it. Hence its coefficient is $L^{-5}L= L^{-4}$ and all off-diagonal coefficients vanish.

The action normalisation also agrees with the finite-torus Hessian. At the identity, the first plaquette phase is $\operatorname{curl}a$ and the first mean-transport phase is $\Phi a$. The mixed second derivative of $1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_N e^{i(sX+tY)}$ at zero is $\tr_N(XY)$, the prescribed real inner product. The terms from second derivatives of the phases multiply the zero first derivative of this class function. Summing over the plaquettes and mean transports gives $\Delta_1=\operatorname{curl}^*\operatorname{curl}+\Phi^*\Phi$ with the same normalisation on every torus.

Each map has finite range, bounded coefficients and finitely many entry types modulo $L\mathbb Z^4$. Its row and column absolute sums are bounded, so it extends uniquely to a bounded operator on its square-summable carrier. In particular $\mathsf H_{\infty}$ is bounded and self-adjoint on all of $\ell^2(E_{*,\infty};\mathfrak g)$.

For every finitely supported $B$, the support of $\mathsf C_{\infty} B$ and all action terms meeting that latter support embed without wraparound in a sufficiently large compatible torus. Their quadratic form and norm are unchanged. Equation~\eqref{eq:covariance-uniform-gap} therefore applies to this same field. Density of finitely supported fields gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-uniform-gap}
    \gamma_L I\leqslant \mathsf H_{\infty}\leqslant h_L I,
    \qquad
    h_L=\max_{e\in E_{*,\infty}/L\mathbb Z^4}
        \sum_{f\in E_{*,\infty}}\|\mathsf H_{\infty}(e,f)\|\;.
\end{equation}
The maximum uses representatives of the finitely many free-bond types. Symmetry gives the same column bound. Thus $h_L$ is finite and independent of the torus and coupling, with $h_L\geqslant \gamma_L>0$.

Let $b_L\coloneqq h_L+\gamma_L$ and $\vartheta_L=1-\gamma_L/b_L$. Then $0<\vartheta_L<1$ and $\| I-\mathsf H_{\infty}/b_L\|\leqslant \vartheta_L$. The inverse is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-neumann-inverse}
    \mathsf H_{\infty}^{-1}
        =\frac{1}{b_L}\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}
            (I-\mathsf H_{\infty}/b_L)^j\;.
\end{equation}
The series converges in operator norm. The fine-field covariance is the bounded positive operator $\mathsf K_{\infty}=\mathsf C_{\infty}\mathsf H_{\infty}^{-1}\mathsf C_{\infty}^*$. At the flat background every colour component has the same scalar operator, with scalar bond kernel $K_{\infty}(b,b')$.

\paragraph{Decay with Finite Constants.}
Let $\ell(b)\in\mathbb Z^4$ be the coarse index of the block containing the initial point of $b$, and let $d(b,b')\coloneqq\|\ell(b)-\ell(b')\|_{\infty}$. Let $R_H$ be the maximum of $1$ and the distances $d(e,f)$ for nonzero entries of $\mathsf H_{\infty}$. Let $R_C$ be the maximum of $d(b,e)$ for nonzero entries of $\mathsf C_{\infty}$. These maxima can be taken over the finitely many entry types modulo coarse translation. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-decay-constants}
    c_L^{\mathsf C}\coloneqq\max_{b\in E_{\infty}/L\mathbb Z^4}
        \sum_{e\in E_{*,\infty}}\|\mathsf C_{\infty}(b,e)\|,
    \qquad
    \mu_L\coloneqq\frac{-\log\vartheta_L}{R_H},
    \qquad
    A_L^{\mathrm{ker}}\coloneqq\frac{(c_L^{\mathsf C})^2}{\gamma_L}e^{2\mu_LR_C}\;.
\end{equation}
The $j$th power in \eqref{eq:bulk-neumann-inverse} has zero $(e,f)$ entry if $jR_H< d(e,f)$, and its norm is at most $\vartheta_L^j$. Summing the remaining terms bounds the inverse entry by $\gamma_L^{-1}e^{-\mu_Ld(e,f)}$. Using the two finite rows of $\mathsf C_{\infty}$ and $d(e,f)\geqslant d(b,b')-2R_C$ yields
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-kernel-decay}
    | K_{\infty}(b,b')|
        \leqslant A_L^{\mathrm{ker}}e^{-\mu_Ld(b,b')}\;.
\end{equation}

\paragraph{Comparison with the Periodic Covariance.}
Let the torus be compatible, with fine periods $N_{\alpha}= LK_{\alpha}$ and $K_{\alpha}\geqslant 3$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^4$, let $Nz\coloneqq(N_1z_1,\ldots,N_4z_4)$. The local torus definitions of $Q,\Phi,\mathsf C,\Delta_1$ are the periodisations of their infinite-lattice definitions. Periodisation preserves their finite-range products. The absolutely convergent periodisation of the free inverse therefore solves the finite-torus inverse equation: applying $\mathsf H_T$ gives the periodised Kronecker delta. Uniqueness of the inverse and multiplication by the two constraint-extension maps give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-periodisation}
    K_T(b,b')=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^4}K_{\infty}(b,b'+Nz)\;.
\end{equation}
Bonds on the right have fixed lifts and unchanged orientations. Let $K_{\min}\coloneqq\min_{\alpha} K_{\alpha}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-image-constant}
    B_L^{\mathrm{img}}
        =\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^4\setminus\{0\}}
            e^{-\mu_L(\| z\|_{\infty}-1)}<\infty\;.
\end{equation}
The shell of maximum norm $j$ has $(2j+1)^4-(2j-1)^4$ points. Since $d(b,b'+Nz)\geqslant K_{\min}\| z\|_{\infty}-d(b,b')$, the image sum satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:bulk-image-error}
    | K_T(b,b')-K_{\infty}(b,b')|
        \leqslant A_L^{\mathrm{ker}}B_L^{\mathrm{img}}
            e^{-\mu_L(K_{\min}-d(b,b'))}\;.
\end{equation}
Thus every fixed finite collection of covariance entries converges as all coarse periods tend to infinity. The limiting connected-cluster construction uses the infinite-lattice covariance.

\section{Background Estimates at the First Step}
\label{app:background-estimates}

This appendix proves the estimates stated in Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}: Lemmas~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, \ref{lem:charts}, \ref{lem:gaussian-payment}, \ref{lem:activity-bounds} and~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}. It fixes every constant named there that Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} does not fix itself, and places all of them in the one order of choice stated in Section~\ref{app:thresholds}: $L$ and the group with the group constants $c_{\mathrm h}=\sqrt N$, $c_{\mathrm n}=1/N$, $\varrho_G=\pi/\sqrt N$, $c$, $r_G$, $c_G$ below; the constants of the lemmas of this appendix in the order of their proofs; $M_1$, $M_2$ and $M$ with the constants chosen after them; the coupling $g_0$, through the thresholds collected there; and last the torus, whose periods satisfy the conditions of \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} (multiples of $LMR_1$, at least $8M$; the scale $R_1$ depends on $g_0$, so the period conditions are imposed after $g_0$).

Group constants: $c$ is a constant with $\| e^{iX}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c\,h(X)$ for all $X\in\mathfrak g$ ($c=\sqrt N$ serves, as $\| e^{iX}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \| X\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt Nh(X)$). For every $N\times N$ matrix $Y$ let $h(Y)\coloneqq(N^{-1}\tr Y^*Y)^{1/2}$, which extends the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm of $\mathfrak g$ to all matrices; then $\| Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant (\tr Y^*Y)^{1/2}=\sqrt N\,h(Y)$, so $\| Y\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}| Y|$ for every matrix $Y$ and either cutoff norm $|\bigcdot |$ (the operator norm or $h$), not only for Hermitian $Y$.

The exponential map restricts to an analytic diffeomorphism from the ball $\{ X\in\mathfrak g\, | \,h(X)<\varrho_G\}$ onto an open neighbourhood $N_G$ of the identity in $G$ (the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}), with inverse $\log_G$; since $G$ is compact and $\| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ vanishes on $G$ only at the identity, there is $r_G\in(0,1]$ with $\{ g\in G\, | \,\| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant r_G\}\subset N_G$. The constant $c_G$ with $h(\log_Gg)\leqslant c_G\| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ on that set exists: $\log_G$ is analytic, so Lipschitz with some constant $c'$ on $\{\| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant r'\}$ for some $r'\in(0,r_G]$, and on $r'\leqslant \| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant r_G$ one has $h(\log_Gg)<\varrho_G\leqslant (\varrho_G/r')\| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, so $c_G=\max(c',\varrho_G/r')$ serves.

The radius $r_M$ of the local group mean is fixed in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}. The phase norm of Lemmas~\ref{lem:two-block} and~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality} is $\| A\|_{\infty}=\max_bh(A_b)$, and operator norms of entries and their derivatives are taken with respect to the Hilbert norms induced by $h$. Throughout, a branch is a branch in the sense of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} (an admissible pair with $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ for some $a$); the reference data of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} are treated in Section~\ref{app:reference-check}.

\subsection{Cubes, Localisation Domains and Tree Lengths}
\label{app:domain-geometry}

The partitions $\pi_0$ (side $M$) and $\pi_1$ (side $LM$) of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} have cubes $Q_z= Mz+[-M/2,M/2]^4$ and $\Delta_z= LMz+[-LM/2,LM/2]^4$, reduced modulo the periods, with $M_1$ and $M$ odd. Cube faces therefore lie at half-integer fine coordinates: every lattice site lies in the interior of exactly one cube of each partition, a fine bond meets at most two cubes of each partition, and a fine bond lies in the interior of a union of cubes exactly when both its endpoints lie in cubes of that union. A cube has $M^4$ sites and meets at most $8M^4$ positive fine bonds.

Two cubes of the same partition are wall adjacent when they share a three-dimensional face; a localisation domain of $\pi_i$ is a finite nonempty union of cubes of $\pi_i$ that is connected under wall adjacency (\cite[p.~257]{BalabanRG1}). A localisation domain $Y$ of $\pi_i$ has $N_i(Y)$ cubes and, following \cite[p.~257]{BalabanRG1}, tree length
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-tree-length}
    d_i(Y)=\inf\{\,|\tau|\, | \,\tau\subset Y\text{ a connected finite union of segments meeting every cube of }Y\,\},
\end{equation}
the Euclidean length $|\tau|$ being measured in units of the cube side. Let $\ell_i(Y)\coloneqq d_i(Y)+5$. Two domains are compatible when they share neither a cube nor a wall (\cite[(2.11)]{BalabanRG2}); a domain is incompatible with itself.

\begin{lemma}[Geometry of Localisation Domains]\label{lem:c2-domain-geometry}
Let $Y,Y_1,\ldots,Y_m$ be localisation domains of one partition and $C_{\mathrm g}=162$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $N_i(Y)\leqslant C_{\mathrm g}\ell_i(Y)$ and $\ell_i(Y)\leqslant N_i(Y)+4$.
\item If $\bigcup_jY_j$ is a localisation domain, then $\ell_i(\bigcup_jY_j)\leqslant \sum_j\ell_i(Y_j)$.
\item If $Z$ is a localisation domain containing $Y_1,\ldots,Y_k$ ($k\geqslant 0$, pairwise disjoint) and $Z\setminus\bigcup_jY_j$ consists of $n$ cubes, then $\ell_i(Z)\leqslant \sum_j\ell_i(Y_j)+5n$.
\item The number of localisation domains with $n$ cubes containing a given cube is at most $64^{n-1}$, and for $s> C_{\mathrm g}\log64$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-animal-sum}
    \sum_{Y\ni Q}e^{-s\ell_i(Y)}\leqslant B(s)=\frac{e^{-s/C_{\mathrm g}}}{1-64e^{-s/C_{\mathrm g}}}
\end{equation}
for every cube $Q$, on every torus. For $s\geqslant C_{\mathrm g}(\log64+\log2)$, $B(s)\leqslant 2e^{-s/C_{\mathrm g}}$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) Let $\tau$ realise \eqref{eq:c2-tree-length} up to $\varepsilon\in(0,1/2)$. A closed traversal of $\tau$ (each segment twice) has length at most $2(d_i(Y)+\varepsilon)$, so sample points along it at arclength spacing one number at most $2d_i(Y)+2$. Every cube of $Y$ contains a point of $\tau$, which is within arclength $1/2$, hence Euclidean and $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $1/2$, of a sample; the centre of that cube is then within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance one of the sample. Cube centres form a unit lattice, so at most $3^4=81$ cubes are assigned to each sample, and $N_i(Y)\leqslant 81(2d_i(Y)+2)\leqslant 162\,\ell_i(Y)$. For the second inequality, the centres of wall-adjacent cubes are joined along a spanning tree of the wall-adjacency graph; each of the $N_i(Y)-1$ edges has length one and lies in $Y$, so $d_i(Y)\leqslant N_i(Y)-1$.

(ii) Let $\tau_j\subset Y_j$ be trees with $|\tau_j|\leqslant d_i(Y_j)+\varepsilon$. The graph on $\{ Y_j\}$ with an edge when $Y_j\cap Y_k\ne\varnothing$ is connected: a wall-adjacent chain of cubes of the union passes from $Y_j$ to $Y_k$ through consecutive cubes that share a wall, hence through domains that intersect. For each edge of a spanning tree, let $x\in Y_j\cap Y_k$, let $Q_j\ni x$ be a cube of $Y_j$ and $p_j\in\tau_j\cap Q_j$; the segment $[p_j,x]\subset Q_j$ (length at most the diameter $2$ of a unit cube in $\mathbb R^4$) is added, and likewise for $k$. The result is a connected union of segments inside $\bigcup Y_j$ meeting every cube, of length at most $\sum_j(d_i(Y_j)+\varepsilon)+4(m-1)$. Letting $\varepsilon\to0$, $d_i(\bigcup Y_j)+5\leqslant \sum_jd_i(Y_j)+4m+1\leqslant \sum_j(d_i(Y_j)+5)$ for $m\geqslant 1$.

(iii) This is (ii) for the family consisting of $Y_1,\ldots,Y_k$ and the $n$ single cubes, each of which has $\ell_i=5$.

(iv) A depth-first traversal of a spanning tree of the wall-adjacency graph of a domain with $n$ cubes, started at the given cube, is a word of length $2(n-1)$ over the eight wall directions, and determines the domain; this gives $64^{n-1}$. By (i), $e^{-s\ell_i(Y)}\leqslant e^{-sN_i(Y)/C_{\mathrm g}}$, so the rooted sum is at most $\sum_{n\geqslant 1}64^{n-1}e^{-sn/C_{\mathrm g}}= B(s)$. The last claim is $64e^{-s/C_{\mathrm g}}\leqslant 1/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Scale Comparison]\label{lem:c2-scale}
Let $Z$ be a localisation domain of $\pi_0$, $\widetilde Z$ the union of the $M$-cubes meeting $Z$, and $Z'$ the union of the $LM$-cubes meeting $\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$.

This is the enlargement rule of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}, which takes the $LM$-cubes meeting $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ for some cube $Q$ of $Z$: indeed $\widetilde Z=\bigcup_{Q\subseteq Z}Q^{\sim}$, an $LM$-cube meeting $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ meets $\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$, and conversely an $LM$-cube $\Delta$ meeting $\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$ contains a nonempty open subset of $\widetilde Z$, a finite union of the closed sets $Q^{\sim}$, one of which therefore contains a nonempty open subset of $\Delta$ (a finite union of closed sets with empty interiors has empty interior), so $\Delta$ meets $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ for that $Q$. The same argument shows, for a union $Z_0$ of $M$-cubes with wall components $Z_{0,j}$, that $Z_0'=\bigcup_jZ_{0,j}'$.

Then $Z\subset\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$, $\widetilde Z\subset Z'$, $Z'$ is a localisation domain of $\pi_1$, every point of $\widetilde Z$ is within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2M$ of every tree realising $d_0(Z)$ up to any $\varepsilon>0$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-scale-inequality}
    \ell_1(Z')\leqslant a^{\mathrm{sc}}_L\ell_0(Z)+b^{\mathrm{sc}}_L,\qquad a^{\mathrm{sc}}_L=\frac{2049}{L},\quad b^{\mathrm{sc}}_L=5+\frac{1024}{L}\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Every $M$-cube meeting a point of $Z$ belongs to $\widetilde Z$, so $Z\subset\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$. An $M$-cube $\widetilde Q$ of $\widetilde Z$ lies in a single $LM$-cube, which meets $\operatorname{int}\widetilde Q\subset\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$; hence $\widetilde Z\subset Z'$. If $\widetilde Q$ meets $Q\subset Z$ only at a lower-dimensional face, the cubes between them sharing walls also meet $Q$, so $\widetilde Z$ is wall connected, $\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$ is connected, and the $LM$-cubes meeting a connected open set are wall connected (a path avoiding lower-dimensional faces passes between consecutive cubes through a common wall).

Let $\tau\subset Z$ meet every $M$-cube of $Z$ with $|\tau|\leqslant M(d_0(Z)+\varepsilon)$ in fine units. For $x\in\widetilde Z$, let $\widetilde Q\ni x$, let $Q\subset Z$ be a cube meeting $\widetilde Q$, and let $y\in\widetilde Q\cap Q$ and $p\in\tau\cap Q$; then $| x-p|_{\infty}\leqslant | x-y|_{\infty}+| y-p|_{\infty}\leqslant 2M$.

For \eqref{eq:c2-scale-inequality}, samples along a closed traversal of $\tau$ at arclength spacing $LM$ number at most $2(d_0(Z)+\varepsilon)/L+1$, and every point of $\tau$ is within Euclidean distance $LM/2$ of a sample. For $\Delta\subset Z'$ let $x_{\Delta}\in\Delta\cap\operatorname{int}\widetilde Z$; by the preceding paragraph it is within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2M+LM/2\leqslant 7LM/6$ of a sample ($L\geqslant 3$), so the centre of $\Delta$ is within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $5LM/3<2LM$ of that sample. The centres of $LM$-cubes form a lattice of spacing $LM$, and an open $\ell^{\infty}$ ball of radius $2LM$ contains at most $4^4=256$ of its points. Hence $N_1(Z')\leqslant 256(2(d_0(Z)+\varepsilon)/L+1)$.

A connected union of segments in $Z'$ meeting every $LM$-cube of $Z'$ consists of $\tau\subset Z\subset Z'$ and, for each $\Delta\subset Z'$ not met by $\tau$, the segments $[x_{\Delta},y]\subset\widetilde Q\subset Z'$ and $[y,p]\subset Q\subset Z'$ chosen above, each of length at most $2M$. Its length is at most $M(d_0(Z)+\varepsilon)+4MN_1(Z')$, so
\begin{equation*}
    d_1(Z')\leqslant \frac{d_0(Z)+\varepsilon}{L}+\frac{4}{L}\cdot256\Bigl(\frac{2(d_0(Z)+\varepsilon)}{L}+1\Bigr)\leqslant \frac{2049}{L}(d_0(Z)+\varepsilon)+\frac{1024}{L}\;.
\end{equation*}
Letting $\varepsilon\to0$, adding $5$ to both sides, and using $d_0(Z)\leqslant \ell_0(Z)$ gives \eqref{eq:c2-scale-inequality}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Regular-Background Bounds}
\label{app:regular-covariance}

\begin{lemma}[Entry Range and Stencils]\label{lem:c2-entry-range}
For free bonds $b,b'$ let $z(b)$ be the coarse label of the block containing $b_-$ and $f_{bb'}(U)$ the entry function \eqref{eq:c-entry-function} with its entry stencil $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ (the union of the background sets of the terms of \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition} whose free-input set contains both $b$ and $b'$). If $| z(b)-z(b')|_1>2$ then $\mathcal T_{bb'}=\varnothing$ and $f_{bb'}=0$. The stencil of a nonzero entry consists of bonds $e$ with $| z(e)-z(b)|_1\leqslant 2$; in fine units all bonds and sites of $\mathcal S_{bb'}$, and both endpoints of $b$ and $b'$, lie within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $3L$ of $b_-$, so $\rho_L=4L$ is an admissible entry range in Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}. Each row has at most $164L^4$ nonzero entries.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition} and its support sets, a term containing the free input $b$ is $\mathfrak a_p$ with $b\in\mathcal F_r$ for a boundary bond $r$ of $p$, $\mathfrak g_y$ with $b\in\mathcal E_y$, or $\mathfrak t_c$ with $b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$. The free inputs of a bond $r$ have block labels among the endpoint blocks of $r$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}): $z(r)$ for a free bond, $\{ c_-,c_+\}$ for $r= b_0(c)$. The four vertices of a fine plaquette in directions $\mu,\nu$ have block labels differing only in the $\mu$ and $\nu$ coordinates, by at most one each, so these labels, and the endpoint blocks of its boundary bonds, lie in a set of $\ell^1$ diameter at most two. The free inputs of $\mathfrak g_y$ lie in one block, those of $\mathfrak t_c$ in the two blocks of $c$. Hence two free inputs of one term have $| z(b)-z(b')|_1\leqslant 2$, and the background bonds of that term (plaquette bonds, the sets $\mathcal E_c$, and for $\mathfrak t_c$ the plaquettes meeting $b_0(c)$, whose vertices lie in the two blocks of $c$) have block labels within $\ell^1$ distance two of $z(b)$. A site of a block with label within $\ell^1$ distance two of $z(b)$ is within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2L+(L-1)<3L$ of $b_-$; the endpoints of $b$ and $b'$ are such sites or within one of them. The $\ell^1$ ball of radius two in $\mathbb Z^4$ has $41$ points and a block has at most $4L^4$ positive bonds with initial site in it.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Plaquette Deviation on the Collar]\label{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation}
Let $B_3$, $\delta_{\mathrm c}$ and the $O(1)$ be the constants of the comparison following \cite[(1.19)]{BalabanCRE}, as recorded in (B3)(iii): for every $L^2M_2R_1$-cube $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1$ (the $\square'\subset R_1^c$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, for which $\square'^{\sim4}\subseteq\Omega_1$, p.250), $| U_1(e)U_{1,\square'}(e)^{-1}-1|< O(1)B_3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}\varepsilon_1$ on the bonds $e$ of $\square'^{\sim2}$ (p.250).

\cite{BalabanCRE} does not state the dependence of these constants, which are Ba{\l}aban's ((H4)): $B_3$ is that of \cite[Theorem~1, p.~279]{BalabanVAR} and the $\delta$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} the rate of the exponential decay property \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR}, which Ba{\l}aban invokes in \cite[p.~266]{BalabanCRE}; Ba{\l}aban reuses the symbols $B_3$ and $\delta$ at every step (p.268, the regularity bound $|\partial U_{k+1}-1|<2B_3\varepsilon_{k+1}(L^{-1}\eta)^2$ and the comparison with $B_3\exp(-\delta LM_2R_{k+1})44d^2B_3\varepsilon_{k+1}$) and derives the comparison (3.19) from these facts and the bounds (106)--(108), (159)--(163) of \cite{BalabanAVG} (p.268). The property used is the one recorded in (B3)(iii) and (H4): $B_3$, $\delta_{\mathrm c}$ and the $O(1)$ do not depend on the coupling $g_0$ or on the branch, so that at fixed $L$ and $M_2$ the factor $e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}$ tends to zero as $g_0\to0$. The $\delta$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} is written $\delta_{\mathrm c}$ here to distinguish it from the Mayer constant $\delta$ of Section~\ref{app:mayer-constants}.

The coupling threshold is reduced until $4\,O(1)B_3L^2e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}\leqslant 1$, which holds for small $g_0$ because the constants do not depend on $g_0$ and $R_1\geqslant (\log g_1^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}\to\infty$ as $g_0\to0$ (\cite[(2.5) and (2.6), p.~255]{BalabanCRE}: $g_1\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_0$ and $g_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_1$, so $g_1\to0$ with $g_0$), and $R_{\mathrm c}$ satisfies Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}. Here $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ is the constant of the same name in \cite[p.~246, (2.4)]{BalabanCRE} and $g_1$ the first-step coupling.

On every branch, every fine plaquette $p$ having a bond within distance $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-plaquette-deviation}
    \| U_1(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $b$ be such a bond and $\square'$ the cube of the partition of \cite[(1.18)]{BalabanCRE} into cubes of side $L^2M_2R_1$ that contains $b_-$ (a partition, so the cube is unique). By Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i) (stated for $d(b,I)\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$; the standing condition $LMR_1>4R_{\mathrm c}+4L^2M_2R_1+8$ gives $3R_{\mathrm c}+1+L^2M_2R_1< LMR_1-1$), $b_-\in\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ and $\square'$ is a good cube of \cite[(1.18)]{BalabanCRE}, $\square'\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1'\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\cap R_1^c$; since $M\geqslant 8LM_2$, the layer of $LMR_1$-cubes around $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ inside $\Omega_1$ contains $\square'^{\sim4}$, as \cite{BalabanCRE} states after (1.19).

The outer weight \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation} contains the background test $\chi_1(\Omega_1)$ of \cite[(2.17)]{BalabanCRE} at $k=1$, a function of $V$, and it is nonzero on a branch: the pair is admissible, so $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)\ne\varnothing$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), and $\chi_1(\Omega_1)\ne0$ at every point of $D^{(11)}$. That test is written on the lattice $T_{\eta}$, $\eta= L^{-1}$, whose unit is the block side, so its cubes of side $LM_2R_1$ have fine side $L^2M_2R_1$ and the plaquette threshold $\varepsilon_1\eta^2$ is $\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$ (\cite[(1.4), p.~246]{BalabanCRE}, prints the step-one test of the $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes with the threshold $\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$ directly); its partition is ``compatible with all other partitions'' (\cite[p.~257]{BalabanCRE}; the term is not defined there, pp.245 and 257, and in the sense of \cite[p.~98]{BalabanREG}, (H4), the cubes of the coarser of two compatible partitions are unions of cubes of the finer), in particular with the partition of (1.18) into cubes of the same side, and two compatible partitions into cubes of equal side coincide. Hence on the branch $\sup_{p'\subset\square'^{\sim}}| U_{1,\square'}(\partial p')-1|<\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$ for the local minimum $U_{1,\square'}$ of \cite[(2.16)]{BalabanCRE}; a gauge transformation conjugates the plaquette holonomy and $|\bigcdot |$ is $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant, so the bound holds for the axial-gauge representative of $U_{1,\square'}$ (p.247) to which the comparison (B3)(iii) refers. The plaquette $p$ contains $b$, hence lies in $\square'^{\sim}$.

The comparison (B3)(iii), stated for the cubes $\square'\subset R_1^c$, for which $\square'^{\sim4}\subset\Omega_1$ and $U_1$, $U_{1,\square'}$ are determined by the same averages on $\square'^{\sim3}$, applies to this $\square'$ and gives $| U_1(e)U_{1,\square'}(e)^{-1}-1|< O(1)B_3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}\varepsilon_1$ on the bonds $e$ of $\square'^{\sim2}$, hence $\| U_1(e)-U_{1,\square'}(e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\| U_1(e)U_{1,\square'}(e)^{-1}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}| U_1(e)U_{1,\square'}(e)^{-1}-\id|\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}O(1)B_3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}\varepsilon_1\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}/4$ there (unitary invariance of the operator norm, the norm comparison of the preamble, valid for every matrix, and the threshold above).

Writing the plaquette holonomy as an ordered product of four unitaries and telescoping, $\| U_1(\partial p)-U_{1,\square'}(\partial p)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sum_{e\subset\partial p}\| U_1(e)-U_{1,\square'}(e)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$. With $\| U_{1,\square'}(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}| U_{1,\square'}(\partial p)-1|< c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$ this gives $\| U_1(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Local Gauge on a Rectangle]\label{lem:c2-local-gauge}
