Let $\mathfrak P$ be a product of fine integer intervals of side at most $s_{\mathfrak P}$ (a lifted rectangle, injective modulo the periods), and let $U$ be a configuration whose plaquettes inside $\mathfrak P$ satisfy $\| U(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1$ with $6c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_1\leqslant r_G$. There is a site gauge $u$ on $\mathfrak P$ such that every bond $b\subset\mathfrak P$ has $U^u(b)= e^{iA_b}$ with $A_b\in\mathfrak g$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-local-gauge-bound}
    h(A_b)\leqslant \widehat\mu_{\mathfrak P}=6c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_1\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $x_0$ be the corner of $\mathfrak P$ with minimal coordinates. For $x\in\mathfrak P$ let $P(x)$ be the lattice path from $x_0$ to $x$ that runs first in direction $e_1$, then $e_2,e_3,e_4$; it stays in $\mathfrak P$. These paths form a spanning tree; let $u(x_0)\coloneqq\id$ and $u(x')\coloneqq u(x)U(x,x')$ along tree bonds oriented away from the root. Then $U^u(x,x')= u(x)U(x,x')u(x')^{-1}=\id$ on tree bonds, and for any bond $(x,x')\subset\mathfrak P$, $U^u(x,x')= U(P(x))U(x,x')U(P(x'))^{-1}$ is the holonomy of the closed loop $P(x)\cdot(x,x')\cdot P(x')^{-1}$ based at $x_0$.

Let $(x,x')$ have direction $e_{\mu}$, so $x'= x+e_{\mu}$. The two tree paths share their runs in directions $\nu<\mu$ and their first $x_{\mu}-x_{0,\mu}$ steps in direction $\mu$; after conjugation by the holonomy of that common initial segment, which preserves $\|\bigcdot -\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, the loop becomes $B\cdot(x,x')\cdot B'^{-1}\cdot(y+e_{\mu},y)$, where $B=(b_1,\ldots,b_k)$ is the staircase from $y=(x_1,\ldots,x_{\mu},x_{0,\mu+1},\ldots,x_{0,4})$ to $x$ in directions $\nu>\mu$, $B'$ its translate by $e_{\mu}$, and $k\leqslant 3s_{\mathfrak P}$. With $\mathcal L_j$ the loop built from $(b_1,\ldots,b_j)$, $\mathcal L_j=(b_1\cdots b_{j-1})\,\partial p_j\,(b_1\cdots b_{j-1})^{-1}\cdot\mathcal L_{j-1}$, where $\partial p_j= b_je_{\mu} b_j'^{-1}e_{\mu}^{-1}$ is the boundary of the plaquette spanned by $b_j$ and $e_{\mu}$, which lies in $\mathfrak P$. Hence the holonomy of the loop is an ordered product of $k$ conjugates of plaquette holonomies, and telescoping gives $\| U^u(x,x')-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 2kc_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1\leqslant 6c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_1\leqslant r_G$.

The element $g= U^u(x,x')\in G$ therefore lies in $N_G$, and $A_b=\log_Gg\in\mathfrak g$ is the unique $X$ in the ball $h(X)<\varrho_G$ with $e^{iX}= g$ (the group chart of the conventions), with $h(A_b)\leqslant c_G\| g-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 6c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_1$.
\end{proof}

Where it is applied with Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} below, the plaquette hypothesis holds because $2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1L^{-2}\leqslant 2c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_1$. The proof uses $\varepsilon_1$ only through the plaquette hypothesis and the condition $6c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_1\leqslant r_G$; so the lemma holds with any $\varepsilon>0$ in place of $\varepsilon_1$, with the bound $6c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon$ in \eqref{eq:c2-local-gauge-bound}. Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness} uses it with $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0/2$.

The radius $\tau_L$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} is reduced so that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-tau-final}
    \tau_L\leqslant \min\Bigl(1,\ 2c_Gr_G,\ \frac{r_G}{2(L-1)c},\ \frac{r_M}{4(L-1)c\,c_G}\Bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
with $c$, $r_G$, $c_G$ the group constants of the preamble (depending on the group only) and $r_M$ the radius of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means} (depending on $L$ and the group); this is the final value of $\tau_L$, used in every statement. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-radius-replay}
    \begin{gathered}
    c_{1,L}\coloneqq 320000\,m_L,\qquad
    R_{\mathrm p}\coloneqq\max\Bigl(2,\Bigl\lceil2\sqrt{c_{1,L}/\gamma_L}\Bigr\rceil\Bigr),\\
    s_{\mathfrak P}\coloneqq L(2R_{\mathrm p}+5)+1,\qquad
    C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}\coloneqq 6c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
and let the collar range satisfy $R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant \max(2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1,\ s_{\mathfrak P}+2)$. Every coarse period exceeds $2R_{\mathrm p}+8$, so that the coarse $\ell^{\infty}$ ball of radius $R_{\mathrm p}+3$ about any coarse label lifts injectively, and $\varepsilon_1$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convex-background-thresholds}
    \widehat\mu= C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}\varepsilon_1<\frac{\tau_L}{2},\qquad
    \max(1,c_L)\widehat\mu<\frac{\gamma_L}{4}\;.
\end{equation}
Since $\tau_L\leqslant 2c_Gr_G$, the first condition gives $6c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_1=\widehat\mu/c_G< r_G$, the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge}.

\begin{lemma}[Regional Entries]\label{lem:c2-regional-entry}
Let $\Omega$ be a region and $U$ a background on which the regional form $\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U$ is defined (Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}: $\mathsf M(U)$ defined and $\alpha_c(U)$ invertible on the rows of $\Omega^{[1]}$, the local group means $\mathcal U_U(y,x)$ defined for $y\in\Omega^{(1)}$). For all $(b,b')\in\Omega^*\times\Omega^*$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convex-regional-entry}
    (\mathsf H^{\Omega}_U)_{bb'}= f_{bb'}(U|_{\mathcal S_{bb'}})\;,
\end{equation}
the entry function \eqref{eq:c-entry-function} evaluated on the background restricted to the entry stencil $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}, and $f_{bb'}=0$ when $| z(b)-z(b')|_1>2$. In particular, on every branch, $(H_{\xi})_{bb'}= f_{bb'}(U_1|_{\mathcal S_{bb'}})$ for all $b,b'\in\Omega_1^*$, and for $b,b'\in I$ the stencil $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ lies inside $\Omega_1$ (within $3L< R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i)).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is the compression identity \eqref{eq:c-regional-compression} of Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}, whose proof is recalled: the regional form is the sum of the terms of \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-quadratic-decomposition} with index in $\Omega$ (plaquettes meeting $\Omega$, centres in $\Omega$, rows in $\Omega^{[1]}$), its entry at $(b,b')$ is the sum of the polarised entries of those of these terms whose free-input set contains $b$ and $b'$, and every term whose free-input set contains a bond $b$ of $\Omega^*$ has its index in $\Omega$: a plaquette term $\mathfrak a_p$ with $b\in\mathcal F_r$, $r\subset\partial p$, has $r= b$ or $r= b_0(c)$ with $b\in\mathcal E_c$, and in either case $p$ contains a bond with an endpoint in the block of the endpoint of $b$ that lies in $\Omega$ ($b$ has such an endpoint, being a bond of $\Omega$; the bonds of $\mathcal E_c$ have both endpoints in the two blocks of $c$, and $b_0(c)$ has one endpoint in each), and that block lies in $\Omega$, a union of blocks; a gauge term $\mathfrak g_y$ with $b\in\mathcal E_y$ has $y\in\Omega$; a row term $\mathfrak t_c$ with $b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$ has an endpoint block of $c$ containing an endpoint of $b$, so $c\in\Omega^{[1]}$.

Hence the set of terms contributing to the regional entry is exactly $\mathcal T_{bb'}$, and the entry is $f_{bb'}(U|_{\mathcal S_{bb'}})$, a finite formula in the background on the stencil in which the rowwise elimination \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-elimination} uses only the rows of the terms in $\mathcal T_{bb'}$, which are rows of $\Omega^{[1]}$, where $\alpha_c(U)$ is invertible: the rows of $\mathfrak g_y$ and $\mathfrak t_c$ are rows with a centre in $\Omega$ by the above, and a row $c'$ of $\mathfrak a_p$ has $b_0(c')\subset\partial p$, whose endpoints are the two sites of the segment between the centres of $c'$ next to the common face of its blocks; the other two vertices of $p$ are their translates by one unit in a direction perpendicular to $c'$, which stay in the same two blocks as $L\geqslant 3$; so all four vertices of $p$ lie in the two blocks of $c'$, one of which meets $\Omega$ since $p$ does, hence lies in $\Omega$, and $c'\in\Omega^{[1]}$.

The vanishing for $| z(b)-z(b')|_1>2$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}. For the last claim, by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range} every site of $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ is within $3L$ of $b_-\in I$, hence within $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ and in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}]
For $B\in\mathfrak g^I$ extended by zero, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} gives
\[
    \langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle=\sum_{b,b'\in I}\langle B_b,f_{bb'}(U_1|_{\mathcal S_{bb'}})B_{b'}\rangle
\]
with the local entries, whose stencils lie inside $\Omega_1$; the vanishing $H_{\xi,II}(b,b')=0$ for $d(b,b')>\rho_L$ is Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}. The quantities $m_L$, $c_L$ of \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-entry-constants} bound the row sums $\sum_{b'}$ of $\| f_{bb'}(A)\|$ and $\| Df_{bb'}(A)\|$ over $\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L$; since $f_{b'b}(A)= f_{bb'}(A)^*$ (the form is symmetric) and hence $Df_{b'b}(A)[X]=(Df_{bb'}(A)[X])^*$, the column sums obey the same bounds.

\emph{Partition of unity.} Let $\mathcal Z_T$ be the coarse grid and $\psi(u)=\prod_{\mu=1}^4(1-| u_{\mu}|/R_{\mathrm p})_+$ on the lifted coarse ball of radius $R_{\mathrm p}$, extended by zero and periodised (injectively, by the period condition). For $w\in\mathcal Z_T$ let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-partition}
    \chi_w(b)\coloneqq\frac{\psi(z(b)-w)}{S^{1/2}},\qquad S\coloneqq\sum_{u}\psi(u)^2=\Bigl(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}(1-| k|/R_{\mathrm p})_+^2\Bigr)^4\geqslant \Bigl(\frac{R_{\mathrm p}}{4}\Bigr)^4\;,
\end{equation}
the last inequality because at least $R_{\mathrm p}$ integers $k$ satisfy $| k|\leqslant R_{\mathrm p}/2$ and each contributes at least $1/4$. Then $\sum_w\chi_w(b)^2=1$ for every $b$. A one-step difference $|\psi(u)-\psi(u+e_{\nu})|$ is at most $1/R_{\mathrm p}$, since only one factor changes and the others are at most one, and it vanishes unless $u$ or $u+e_{\nu}$ lies in the support, a set of at most $(2R_{\mathrm p}+2)^4\leqslant (5R_{\mathrm p})^4$ points. Telescoping along a coarse path of $n=| z(b)-z(b')|_1$ steps and using $(\sum_{i=1}^na_i)^2\leqslant n\sum a_i^2$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-cutoff-error}
    \begin{aligned}
    \sum_w(\chi_w(b)-\chi_w(b'))^2&\leqslant \frac{1}{S}\,n\sum_{i=1}^n\sum_w(\text{one-step difference})^2\\
    &\leqslant \frac{256}{R_{\mathrm p}^4}\,n^2\,\frac{(5R_{\mathrm p})^4}{R_{\mathrm p}^2}=\frac{160000}{R_{\mathrm p}^2}\,| z(b)-z(b')|_1^2\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Since $\sum_w\chi_w(b)\chi_w(b')-1=-\frac12\sum_w(\chi_w(b)-\chi_w(b'))^2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range} ($n\leqslant 2$ on nonzero entries) and the Schur bound $\sum_{b,b'}\| f_{bb'}\| h(B_b)h(B_{b'})\leqslant m_L\| B\|^2$, valid because row and column sums of $\| f_{bb'}\|$ are at most $m_L$ (shown below), give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-localisation-error}
    \Bigl|\sum_w\langle\chi_wB,H_{\xi}\chi_wB\rangle-\langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle\Bigr|\leqslant \frac12\cdot\frac{160000\cdot4}{R_{\mathrm p}^2}\,m_L\| B\|^2=\frac{c_{1,L}}{R_{\mathrm p}^2}\| B\|^2\leqslant \frac{\gamma_L}{4}\| B\|^2\;.
\end{equation}

\emph{Local comparison.} Let $\chi_wB\ne0$; since $B$ is supported on $I$, some $b\in I$ has $\chi_w(b)\neq0$, so the patch $\{ b\, | \,| z(b)-w|_{\infty}\leqslant R_{\mathrm p}\}$ meets $I$. Let $\mathfrak P_w$ be the lifted rectangle of fine sites in blocks with $| z-w|_{\infty}\leqslant R_{\mathrm p}+2$, of side at most $L(2R_{\mathrm p}+5)+1= s_{\mathfrak P}$; it lies within fine distance $s_{\mathfrak P}+1\leqslant 2R_{\mathrm c}-1$ of $I$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} applies to all its plaquettes and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge} gives a gauge $u_w$ on $\mathfrak P_w$ with phases $h(A_e)\leqslant \widehat\mu$, extended by the identity. By Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range} the stencils of all entries with both labels in the patch lie in $\mathfrak P_w$. With $T_w= R_{u_w,*}$ the orthogonal action of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality},
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
    \langle\chi_wB,H_{\xi}\chi_wB\rangle&=\sum_{b,b'}\langle(T_w\chi_wB)_b,f_{bb'}(A)(T_w\chi_wB)_{b'}\rangle\\
    &=\langle T_w\chi_wB,\mathsf H_{\id}T_w\chi_wB\rangle+\sum_{b,b'}\langle(T_w\chi_wB)_b,(f_{bb'}(A)-f_{bb'}(0))(T_w\chi_wB)_{b'}\rangle\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
where $f_{bb'}(A)$ is the entry at the gauge-transformed background $U_1^{u_w}= e^{iA}$ on the stencil; the first equality is the entrywise gauge covariance \eqref{eq:c-entry-gauge-covariance}, $f_{bb'}(U^u)=\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_-)}f_{bb'}(U)\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b'_-)}^{-1}$, together with $(T_w\chi_wB)_b\coloneqq\operatorname{Ad}_{u_w(b_-)}\chi_w(b)B_b$ and the invariance of the inner product.

The map $A\mapsto f_{bb'}(A)$ is analytic on $\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}) and $\| A\|_{\infty}\leqslant \widehat\mu<\tau_L/2$, so $\| f_{bb'}(A)-f_{bb'}(0)\|\leqslant \sup_{t\in[0,1]}\| Df_{bb'}(tA)\|\,\widehat\mu$, and the row and column sums of these bounds are at most $c_L\widehat\mu$ by \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-entry-constants}; the Schur test gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-local-error}
    \Bigl|\langle\chi_wB,H_{\xi}\chi_wB\rangle-\langle T_w\chi_wB,\mathsf H_{\id}T_w\chi_wB\rangle\Bigr|\leqslant c_L\widehat\mu\,\|\chi_wB\|^2\;.
\end{equation}
The operator $\mathsf H_{\id}$ is the flat Hessian $\mathsf H$ of \eqref{eq:flat-covariance}: at the identity $J_{\id}=0$, every relative mean $\mathcal U_{\id}(y,x)$ is the identity, so $\mathscr G_{\id}$ is the gauge functional of \eqref{eq:action-primitive}, and $\mathsf C_{\id}$ is \eqref{eq:constraint-extension}. By \eqref{eq:covariance-uniform-gap} on the branch's torus, $\langle T_w\chi_wB,\mathsf H_{\id}T_w\chi_wB\rangle\geqslant \gamma_L\|\chi_wB\|^2$. Summing over $w$ and using $\sum_w\|\chi_wB\|^2=\| B\|^2$ and \eqref{eq:convex-background-thresholds},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:regular-covariance-lower-bound}
    \langle B,H_{\xi} B\rangle\geqslant \Bigl(\gamma_L-\frac{c_{1,L}}{R_{\mathrm p}^2}-c_L\widehat\mu\Bigr)\| B\|^2\geqslant \frac{\gamma_L}{2}\| B\|^2\;.
\end{equation}

\emph{Upper bound.} For a row $b\in I$ all entries $f_{bb'}$, $b'$ any free bond, have stencils in $\mathfrak P_{z(b)}$ (the patch of $w= z(b)$ meets $I$ at $b$; a nonzero entry has its stencil within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $3L$ of $b_-$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}, hence in blocks $z$ with $| z-z(b)|_{\infty}\leqslant 3\leqslant R_{\mathrm p}+2$); in the gauge $u_{z(b)}$ of that patch their phases are at most $\widehat\mu\leqslant \tau_L$, and $\| f_{bb'}\|$ is unchanged by the fibre rotations of \eqref{eq:c-entry-gauge-covariance}, which are orthogonal. Hence, by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} on $\Omega_1^*\times\Omega_1^*$ and \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-entry-constants}, $\sum_{b'\in\Omega_1^*}\|(H_{\xi})_{bb'}\|=\sum_{b'\in\Omega_1^*}\| f_{bb'}(U_1|_{\mathcal S_{bb'}})\|\leqslant m_L$, which is the row-sum statement of the lemma; in particular $\sum_{b'\in I}\| f_{bb'}(U_1)\|\leqslant m_L$, and by the symmetry noted at the start the column sums of $H_{\xi,II}$ obey the same bound. The Schur test gives $\| H_{\xi,II}\|\leqslant m_L$. Both bounds pass to principal restrictions: the lower bound by compression, the upper by the Schur test on fewer entries. This proves \eqref{eq:c-regular-two-sided} and the range statement.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Uniform Charts and Primitive Bounds}
\label{app:charts}

Primitives are evaluated on the input $A= g_0\mathsf C_UB$ with the free vector $B= a+tA_{\mathrm e}$, $t\in[0,1]$ (the vacuum potentials of Section~\ref{sec:selected-integrals} have $t=0$). For a coarse row $c$ the relevant input is $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$, with the Hilbert norm on $\mathfrak g^{\mathcal E_c}$ (written $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|$ or $\| A\|$).

Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}, \ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}, and~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} prove Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} for every row $c$ and every centre $y$ within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$, with the primitive sizes \eqref{eq:c2-primitive-sizes}.

\begin{definition}[Gauge Patches]\label{def:gauge-patch}
A background $U$ admits a gauge patch on a set $S$ of bonds when there is a site gauge $u$ in which the phases $\phi$, $U^u= e^{i\phi}$, satisfy $\|\phi\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L/2$ on $S$. For a phase $q$, $q^u\coloneqq R_uq$ with $(R_uq)(b)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ad}_{u(b_-)}q(b)$, so that $\| q^u|_S\|=\| q|_S\|$. Norms of phases on $S$ are the Hilbert norms of $\mathfrak g^{S}$ and of its complexification (so $\| d\|= h(d)$ for a single $d\in\mathfrak g$).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform Implicit Chart]\label{lem:c2-uniform-chart}
There are constants $\varrho_*,\vartheta_*>0$, $H_*,K_*\geqslant 1$, $C_{\mathsf C}\geqslant \max(1,(4L^3(L-1))^{1/2})$, and $C^{\mathrm a}_k$ for $0\leqslant k\leqslant 5$, depending on $L$ and the group only, with $2\vartheta_*<\varrho_*$, $2\vartheta_*\leqslant \varrho_G$, $\vartheta_*\leqslant \tau_L/2$ and $4K_*H_*\vartheta_*<1$, such that for every background $U$ admitting a gauge patch on $\mathcal E_c$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\| h_U(c)\|\leqslant H_*$; $\|\mathsf C_UB\|_{\mathcal E_c}\leqslant C_{\mathsf C}\max_{b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}| B_b|$ and $\|\mathsf C_UB\|_{\mathcal E_c}\leqslant C_{\mathsf C}\| B|_{\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}\|$ (Hilbert norms); and $\mathcal N_{U,c}$ is analytic on the open complex ball $\| A\|<2\varrho_*$ of $\mathfrak g^{\mathcal E_c}_{\mathbb C}$, real on real $A$, with $\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$, $D\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$ and $\| D^2\mathcal N_{U,c}\|\leqslant K_*$ on the closed ball $\| A\|\leqslant \varrho_*$.
\item On the open complex ball $\| A\|<\vartheta_*$ there is an analytic function $\varphi_c=\widetilde D_{U,c}$, real on real $A$, with $\varphi_c(0)=0$, $D\varphi_c(0)=0$, such that for every $A$ in that ball $\varphi_c(A)$ is the unique solution $d$ of the row equation \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit} with $\| d\|\leqslant 2K_*\vartheta_*^2\eqqcolon\rho_{\mathrm d}$ (for real $A$, the small solution of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}); it agrees with the germ of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality} and satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convex-uniform-implicit-chart}
    \|\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)\|\leqslant 2K_*\| A\|^2,\qquad
    \| D_A\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)\|\leqslant C_{\mathsf D}\| A\|\;,\qquad C_{\mathsf D}\coloneqq 4K_*\;.
\end{equation}
\item On the closed real ball $\| A\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ the row determinant of $c$ (Definition~\ref{def:chart-functions}) is positive. On a complex neighbourhood of the closed complex ball $\| A\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ the functions $\widetilde D_{U,c}$, the phase $q_U(A)|_{\mathcal E_c}= A-h_U\widetilde D_U(A)$, the normalised Haar logarithm $\log\bigl(\sigma(q_U(A)(b))/\sigma(0)\bigr)$, $b\in\mathcal E_c$, and the logarithm of the row determinant (both logarithms continued analytically from the real ones) are analytic, and on the closed ball their derivatives of order $k\leqslant 5$ are bounded in operator norm by $C^{\mathrm a}_k$; for $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ this holds for $k\leqslant 6$ with $C^{\mathsf D}_k\coloneqq e^kk!\,2K_*\vartheta_*^2(2/\vartheta_*)^k$. The two logarithms vanish at $A=0$, and the first derivative of the Haar logarithm vanishes there.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform Local Means]\label{lem:c2-uniform-means}
With the constants of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}, there are $r_M,r'_M>0$ with $r'_M\leqslant \varrho_G$, depending on $L$ and the group only, such that the following holds. Let $U$ admit a gauge patch $u$ on $\mathcal E_y$ for a block centre $y$. For every real $q$ with $\| q|_{\mathcal E_y}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*$, the path transports $(e^{iq^u}U^u)(\gamma)$, $\gamma\in\mathcal G(y,x)$, $x\in\mathcal B_y$, are within $r_G$ of $\id$ in operator norm, their logarithms $\log_G$ have $h< r_M$, and the local group mean $\mathcal U_{e^{iq^u}U^u}(y,x)$ of \eqref{eq:action-primitive} (\cite[(0.10)--(0.11)]{BalabanRG1}), the unique solution near the diagonal value, exists, of the form $e^{iX}$ with $h(X)< r'_M\leqslant \varrho_G$; the relative mean $\mathcal U_{e^{iq}U}(y,x)\mathcal U_U(y,x)^{-1}$ lies within $r_G$ of $\id$ in operator norm (the domain of $\log_G$), and it and the gauge term $\mathscr G_{y,U}(q)$ are restrictions to real $q$ of functions analytic on the open complex ball $\| q|_{\mathcal E_y}\|<2\vartheta_*$, with derivatives up to order five bounded by $C^{\mathrm a}_k$ on the closed complex ball of radius $\vartheta_*$, uniformly in the background, and $\mathscr G_{y,U}(0)=0$, $D\mathscr G_{y,U}(0)=0$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} and~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}]
All formulas depending on $\vartheta_*$, including $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ and $C^{\mathsf D}_k$, use its final reduced value. There are finitely many row types modulo $L\mathbb Z^4$. For each type the maps $U\mapsto h_U(c)$, $\mathsf C_U$ and $(U,A)\mapsto\mathcal N_{U,c}(A)$ are compositions of exponentials, relative block averages, the fibre inverse $\alpha_c(U)^{-1}$ and the chart logarithm, all analytic for phases $\|\phi\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L$ and $A$ near zero (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block} gives the singular-value bound $L^{-4}/2$ on $\alpha_c$), and real for real arguments.

Under the simultaneous gauge transformation of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}, $Q_U,h_U,\mathsf C_U$ and $\mathcal N_U$ intertwine with the orthogonal fibre action $R_{u,*}$ (proof of that lemma), which preserves the Hilbert norms and the maximum norm $\max_b| B_b|$ ($|\bigcdot |$ is $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant); so the bounds in (i)--(iii) may be proved in the gauge $u$ and transferred to $U$.

The set of phase configurations with $\|\phi\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L/2$ on $\mathcal E_c$ is compact, so a common complex radius $2\varrho_*$ of analyticity and bounds $H_*,K_*,C_{\mathsf C}$ exist (the two bounds on $\mathsf C_U$ are two operator norms of the same linear map, each bounded on the compact set; $C_{\mathsf C}$ is the larger, increased if necessary to $\max(1,(4L^3(L-1))^{1/2})$, which only weakens the inequalities); $\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$ because the zero fluctuation reproduces the background averages, and $D\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$ as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}.

(ii) Let $A$ be in the complex ball with $\| A\|\leqslant \vartheta\leqslant \vartheta_*$ and let $\Phi(d)\coloneqq\mathcal N_{U,c}(A-h_Ud)$ on the closed complex ball $\| d\|\leqslant 2K_*\vartheta^2$. Then $\| A-h_Ud\|\leqslant \vartheta+2H_*K_*\vartheta^2\leqslant 2\vartheta\leqslant \varrho_*$; Taylor's formula with $\mathcal N(0)=0$, $D\mathcal N(0)=0$ gives $\|\Phi(d)\|\leqslant \frac12K_*(2\vartheta)^2=2K_*\vartheta^2$, and $\| D\Phi(d)\|\leqslant \| D\mathcal N(A-h_Ud)\| H_*\leqslant K_*\cdot2\vartheta H_*<\frac12$. So $\Phi$ is a contraction of the closed ball into itself, with a unique fixed point; taking $\vartheta=\vartheta_*$ gives the uniqueness in the ball $\| d\|\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm d}$ for every $A$ with $\| A\|<\vartheta_*$, and taking $\vartheta=\| A\|$ gives the first bound of \eqref{eq:convex-uniform-implicit-chart}; the fixed point $\varphi_c(A)$ is analytic in $A$ on the open ball as the uniform limit of the analytic iterates $\Phi^n(0)$ (each iterate is analytic in $A$, and the convergence is geometric, uniformly in $A$), and it is real for real $A$ because the iterates are.

Differentiating the fixed-point equation, $D_A\widetilde D=(\id+D\mathcal N(x)h_U)^{-1}D\mathcal N(x)$ with $x= A-h_U\widetilde D$, $\| D\mathcal N(x)\|\leqslant K_*\| x\|\leqslant 2K_*\| A\|$ and $\|(\id+D\mathcal N(x)h_U)^{-1}\|\leqslant 2$; this is the second bound, and $D\varphi_c(0)=0$. The germ of Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}, constructed there from Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}, $\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$, $D\mathcal N_{U,c}(0)=0$ and the analyticity of $\mathcal N_{U,c}$ near zero, is the solution near zero, and uniqueness in the ball identifies the two.

(iii) Cauchy's estimate on the ball of radius $\vartheta_*$, where $\|\widetilde D_{U,c}\|\leqslant 2K_*\vartheta_*^2$, bounds the $k$-th derivative at a point of the closed ball of radius $\vartheta_*/2$ in a fixed direction $v$, $\| v\|\leqslant 1$, by $k!\,2K_*\vartheta_*^2(\vartheta_*/2)^{-k}$ for every $k$, and the polarisation identity for symmetric $k$-linear maps bounds the operator norm of $D^k\widetilde D_{U,c}$ by $e^k$ times the diagonal bound; this gives $C^{\mathsf D}_k$ for $0\leqslant k\leqslant 6$. The constants $C^{\mathrm a}_k$ bounding the other functions are chosen at the end of the proof. The phase $q_U(A)|_{\mathcal E_c}= A-h_U\widetilde D_U(A)$ is a composition of $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ with the fixed linear map $h_U(c)$ of norm at most $H_*$, so it is analytic on the ball of radius $\vartheta_*$ and its derivatives are bounded by the chain rule.

The Haar density: $\sigma(q)\,\dd q$ is the pullback of Haar measure under $q\mapsto e^{iq}$ on the chart ball $h(q)<\varrho_G$, so $\sigma(q)=\sigma(0)|\det D(q\mapsto e^{iq})(q)|$, the determinant of the differential taken with respect to left-invariant frames; the determinant is analytic in $q$ and nonvanishing on the chart ball (the chart has invertible differential, conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}), so it has constant sign on the connected ball, positive since it equals one at $q=0$; thus $\sigma$ is analytic and positive there, and even, $\sigma(-q)=\sigma(q)$, because Haar measure is invariant under $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ and $e^{-iq}=(e^{iq})^{-1}$. Hence $\log(\sigma/\sigma(0))$, the real logarithm, extends analytically to a complex neighbourhood of the real chart ball, vanishes at $0$ with vanishing first derivative (evenness), and its composition with $q_U(A)(b)$ (a phase with $h(q_U(A)(b))\leqslant \| A\|+H_*2K_*\| A\|^2\leqslant \vartheta_*$ on the ball) is analytic on a complex neighbourhood of the closed ball $\| A\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ after reducing $\vartheta_*$ so that the compositions stay in the domain of analyticity, with derivatives bounded on the closed ball by the chain rule, and its first derivative at $A=0$ is $D\log\sigma(0)\circ Dq_U(0)=0$.

The determinant argument $\id-h_U(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)$ equals $\id$ at $A=0$ since $D\widetilde D(0)=0$, and is within $H_*C_{\mathsf D}\vartheta_*/2<1/2$ of $\id$ in operator norm on the ball; for real $A$ it is a real endomorphism of $\mathfrak g$ within $1/2$ of $\id$, whose eigenvalues have positive real part, so its determinant is positive, and on a complex neighbourhood of the closed ball $\| A\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ the determinant stays in the disc of radius $1/2$ about $1$ (after reducing $\vartheta_*$ once more if needed, by continuity and compactness), where $\log$ is analytic; so the real logarithm of the determinant extends analytically to that neighbourhood and vanishes at $A=0$, where the determinant is one. Its derivatives of order $k\leqslant 5$ are bounded on the closed ball by the chain rule, since the argument contains $\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c}$ and so involves the derivatives of $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ up to order six, bounded above.

The bounds are uniform in the background by the compactness of the set of phase configurations. All reductions of $\vartheta_*$ are by constants depending on $L$ and the group only, over the finitely many row types.

\emph{Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}.} The fibre action is orthogonal on real phases and unitary on their complexifications, so it preserves the phase balls and operator norms of multilinear derivatives. In the gauge $u$ the links of $\mathcal B_y$ are $e^{i\phi}$ with $\|\phi\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L/2$, and $h(q_b)\leqslant \| q|_{\mathcal E_y}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*\leqslant \tau_L/2$ for every $b\in\mathcal E_y$. A path of $\mathcal G(y,x)$ has at most $2(L-1)$ bonds (four coordinate runs of length at most $(L-1)/2$), and for unitaries $\| U_1\cdots U_n-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sum_j\| U_j-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, so every path transport $g_{\gamma}=(e^{iq^u}U^u)(\gamma)$ lies within $2(L-1)c(\tau_L/2+\vartheta_*)\leqslant 2(L-1)c\,\tau_L\leqslant r_G$ of $\id$ in operator norm, by \eqref{eq:c2-tau-final}; hence $A_{\gamma}=\log_Gg_{\gamma}$ is defined with $h(A_{\gamma})\leqslant c_G\cdot2(L-1)c\,\tau_L\leqslant r_M/2$, again by \eqref{eq:c2-tau-final}.

The local group mean of a family $(g_{\gamma})_{\gamma\in\mathcal G(y,x)}$ is the solution $\mathcal U$ near the diagonal value of $\sum_{\gamma}\log_G(g_{\gamma}\mathcal U^{-1})=0$; with $g_{\gamma}= e^{iA_{\gamma}}$ and $\mathcal U= e^{iX}$, let $F(X,(A_{\gamma}))\coloneqq\sum_{\gamma}\log_G(e^{iA_{\gamma}}e^{-iX})$, an analytic map on a neighbourhood of $(0,0)$ in $\mathfrak g\times\mathfrak g^{\mathcal G(y,x)}$ with $F(0,0)=0$ and $D_XF(0,0)=-n\,\id$, $n=|\mathcal G(y,x)|$ (as $D\log_G(\id)=\id$). The product neighbourhood in the complexified Lie-algebra variables is chosen so that every $e^{iA_{\gamma}}e^{-iX}$ lies in the analytic logarithm domain there. The analytic implicit function theorem on that neighbourhood gives radii $r_M,r'_M>0$, with $r'_M\leqslant \varrho_G$ (any smaller solution radius is admissible together with a correspondingly smaller $r_M$), and an analytic map $X= X((A_{\gamma}))$ on $\max_{\gamma} h(A_{\gamma})< r_M$, with $h(X)< r'_M$, such that $X((A_{\gamma}))$ is the unique solution of $F=0$ with $h(X)< r'_M$; there are finitely many values of $n$ (one per $x\in\mathcal B_y$ modulo translations), so $r_M$, $r'_M$ and the derivative bounds of $X$ are constants of the group and $L$.

This solution is the fixed mean used in Stage 1. \cite[(0.8)]{BalabanRG1} places that specified analytic mean near the identity for input families near the identity, and (0.10) says it solves this equation. The radius $r_M$ is reduced, before the final choice of $\tau_L$, so that all families $\{ e^{iA_{\gamma}}\}$ with $\max_{\gamma} h(A_{\gamma})< r_M$ lie in the small-diameter domain of the specified mean, that this mean has logarithm of norm below $r'_M$, and that all relative logarithms use the common chart. The operator-norm diameter $\max_{\gamma,\gamma'}\| g_{\gamma}-g_{\gamma'}\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ is unchanged by the two-sided multiplication $g_{\gamma}\mapsto u(y)g_{\gamma} u(x)^{-1}$. Thus the original-gauge families lie in the same small-diameter domain. Their relative products with the mean transform by conjugation at $y$, which preserves the $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant logarithm chart, so the original-gauge relative logarithms are defined as well. Local uniqueness from the implicit function theorem then identifies it with $e^{iX}$. Its left-right covariance is \cite[(0.6)]{BalabanRG1}. Thus for any admissible gauge $u$ its value in the original gauge is $u(y)^{-1}\mathcal U_{U^u}(y,x)u(x)$; the value is independent of the choice of admissible gauge because both expressions are values of the same specified mean.

Since $h(A_{\gamma})\leqslant r_M/2< r_M$ for the transport families above, the mean $\mathcal U= e^{iX((A_{\gamma}))}$ exists, lies in the chart domain, and is the unique solution near the diagonal value in the sense of \eqref{eq:action-primitive}.

Let $A_{\gamma}(q^u)\coloneqq\log_G((e^{iq^u}U^u)(\gamma))$ and $X(q^u)= X((A_{\gamma}(q^u))_{\gamma})$, and let $M_x(q)\coloneqq\mathcal U_{e^{iq}U}(y,x)\mathcal U_U(y,x)^{-1}$ and $M_x^u(q^u)=\mathcal U_{e^{iq^u}U^u}(y,x)\mathcal U_{U^u}(y,x)^{-1}$. Gauge covariance gives $M_x^u(q^u)= u(y)M_x(q)u(y)^{-1}= e^{iX(q^u)}e^{-iX(0)}$, with inverse $M_x^u(q^u)^{-1}= e^{iX(0)}e^{-iX(q^u)}$; both are compositions of the analytic map $X$ with $\log_G$, the exponentials of the phases and the fixed links, so they extend analytically to a complex ball $\| q|_{\mathcal E_y}\|<2\vartheta_*$ (after reducing $\vartheta_*$ by a constant of the group and $L$). For real $q$, $M_x(q)$ is unitary and $\| M_x(q)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\| e^{iX(q^u)}-e^{iX(0)}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant C\| q|_{\mathcal E_y}\|$ with a constant $C$ of $L$ and the group (the derivatives of $X$ on the ball $\max_{\gamma} h(A_{\gamma})\leqslant r_M/2$, of $\log_G$ on the $r_G$-ball and of the products of exponentials are bounded), so after reducing $\vartheta_*$ once more $M_x(q)$ lies within $r_G$ of $\id$ for $\| q|_{\mathcal E_y}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*$.

The gauge term is $\mathscr G_{y,U}(q)=\sum_x(1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_NM_x(q))$; for real $q$, $\operatorname{Re}\tr_NM_x(q)=\frac12(\tr_NM_x(q)+\tr_NM_x(q)^{-1})$ because $M_x(q)$ is unitary, and the right side is the analytic continuation to the complex ball. The derivatives up to order five of $M_x$ and $\mathscr G_{y,U}$ are bounded on the closed ball of radius $\vartheta_*$ by constants $C^{\mathrm a}_k$ uniform in the background, because they are analytic jointly in $q$ and in the phases $\phi$ of the links of $\mathcal B_y$ in the gauge $u$, and the set $\|\phi\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_L/2$ is compact. $\mathscr G_{y,U}(0)=0$ because $M_x(0)=\id$, and $D\mathscr G_{y,U}(0)=0$ because each summand is nonnegative on real $q$ and vanishes at $q=0$.

The gauge $u$ multiplies every transport from $y$ to $x$ on the left by $u(y)$ and on the right by $u(x)^{-1}$, and the mean equation is covariant under this ($\mathcal U\mapsto u(y)\mathcal Uu(x)^{-1}$, so $M_x\mapsto u(y)M_xu(y)^{-1}$, which preserves $\| M_x-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ and $\tr_NM_x$), so the relative-mean and gauge-functional bounds hold for $U$ itself.

For each $0\leqslant k\leqslant 5$, $C^{\mathrm a}_k$ is the maximum of one, $C^{\mathsf D}_k$, and the uniform derivative bounds for the phase, the two logarithms, the relative means, and the gauge functional obtained in (iii) and in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}; these are finite and uniform by the compact phase sets, the finitely many templates, and the stated analytic neighbourhoods.
\end{proof}

Let $c$ be a row within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ (a near row); by Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} every row of a near primitive (a primitive whose free-input set meets $I$) is within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, since its bonds are within $4L+3\leqslant 2R_{\mathrm c}$ of a free-input bond in $I$, and every row of a plaquette with a bond in $\mathcal E_c$ for such a row $c$ is within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ (its bonds are within $2L-1+1$ of a bond of $\mathcal E_c$).

The two-block set $\mathcal E_c$ lies inside a lifted rectangle of side $2L+1\leqslant s_{\mathfrak P}$ all of whose bonds are within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L+2L+1\leqslant 3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ (as $R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant 2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1=4L+5$); Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} and~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge} give a gauge on it with phases at most $\widehat\mu<\tau_L/2$ (the bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge} is monotone in the side), and Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(iii) (range $3R_{\mathrm c}$) bounds the retained inputs $A_{\mathrm e}(b)$, $b\in\mathcal E_c\cap J$, by $r_{\mathrm e,\xi}$.

Likewise a block $\mathcal B_y$ with centre $y$ within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ is a lifted rectangle of side $L\leqslant s_{\mathfrak P}$ whose bonds are within $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, so Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} and~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge} apply to it directly. For real $B\in\mathcal U_y$, the block input satisfies $\| g_0B|_{\mathcal E_y}\|\leqslant 2C_{\mathsf C}g_0(1+2r)\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$ by threshold item 3 and $C_{\mathsf C}\geqslant |\mathcal E_y|^{1/2}$. Hence the conclusions of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means} apply on the entire block polydisc $\mathcal U_y$. So Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} and~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means} apply to every row and every centre within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$, in particular to every row of every near primitive and of every plaquette with a bond in the two-block set of such a row.

Let $s_{\xi}\coloneqq 1+r+r_{\mathrm e,\xi}\leqslant 1+2r$. The next lemma shows that Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i)--(iii) apply at every row of $\Omega_1^{[1]}$, near or far, and that the arguments of the whole fibre $D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ lie in its balls.

\begin{definition}[Fibre Data]\label{def:fibre-data}
Let $n_{\mathcal E}$ be the largest number of bonds of a two-block set $\mathcal E_c$ of \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-bonds} (a constant of $L$), $O(L^2)$ the constant of \cite[p.~247]{BalabanCRE} in (B1)(ii), and $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ an admissible pair, with the background $U_1= U_1(V,V_0)$ of (B1) on the bonds of $\Omega_1$ and $V_0$ on the other bonds. Phases $A\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1}$ are extended by zero, and
\begin{equation*}
    \varphi(A)\coloneqq (\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c}))_{c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}}\;,\qquad\Theta(A)\coloneqq A-h_{U_1}\varphi(A)
\end{equation*}
wherever every component is defined. For $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$,
\begin{gather*}
    A'\coloneqq\tfrac1i\log(UU_1^{-1})\text{ on the bonds of }\Omega_1\;,\qquad d\coloneqq\mathcal N_{U_1}(A')\;,\\
    A\coloneqq A'+h_{U_1}d\;,\qquad B\coloneqq g_0^{-1}A'|_{\Omega_1^*}\;,
\end{gather*}
and
\begin{equation*}
    \mathcal N_{\Theta}\coloneqq\{ A\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1}:\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*/2\text{ for every }c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}\}\;.
\end{equation*}
\end{definition}

The logarithm defining $A'$ exists by (B1), and $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ by the decomposition step of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} after \eqref{eq:c-free-variable-domain}, which uses (B1), the constraint, $LQ_{U_1}h_{U_1}=\id$, and the invertibility of $\alpha_c(U_1)$ in the elimination maps \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-elimination}, given by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(i) and Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}. Threshold item 6 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds} is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-fibre-thresholds}
    3c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_0\leqslant \tfrac12\tau_L,\qquad
    n_{\mathcal E}^{1/2}c_Gc_{\mathrm h}\,2\,O(L^2)\,\varepsilon_0\leqslant \tfrac14\vartheta_*\;.
\end{equation}
The first condition gives $3c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_0\leqslant \tau_L/(2c_G)\leqslant r_G$, since $\tau_L\leqslant 2c_Gr_G$ by \eqref{eq:c2-tau-final}.

\begin{lemma}[Fibre Smallness]\label{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}
Let $g_0$ satisfy threshold items 5 and 6 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, and let the data be those of Definition~\ref{def:fibre-data}.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every row $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$, $U_1$ admits a gauge patch on $\mathcal E_c$, with a site gauge on $\mathfrak P_c\coloneqq\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$, the union of the two blocks of $c$. Hence Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i)--(iii) hold at $c$ for $U= U_1$: the function $\varphi_c=\widetilde D_{U_1,c}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii) is analytic on the ball $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$, real on real phases, with $\varphi_c(0)=0$, $D\varphi_c(0)=0$, and for every $A$ in that ball $\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$ is the unique solution $d_c$ of the row equation of $c$ with $h(d_c)\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm d}$.
\item For $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ and every row $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$
\begin{equation*}
    \| A'|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \tfrac14\vartheta_*,\qquad
    h(d_c)\leqslant \tfrac1{32}K_*\vartheta_*^2<\rho_{\mathrm d},\qquad
    \| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\tfrac12\vartheta_*,\qquad
    d_c=\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})\;.
\end{equation*}
\item For every $B\in\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1^*}$, every family $d$ of chart class at $A= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}B$ (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}) with $U_d(B)\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ is $d=\varphi(A)$.
\item $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ is open, and by (ii) it contains the argument $A$ of every $U\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$. On $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ the family $\varphi$ is analytic, real on real phases, and solves the row equations \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit}; the phase $\Theta(A)$ has $\|\Theta(A)|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$ at every row and is chart-valued, $h(\Theta(A)(b))<\vartheta_*<\varrho_G$ on every bond $b$ of $\Omega_1$; for every row, $\| h_{U_1}(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})\|\leqslant 4H_*K_*\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<1$; and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-fibre-jacobian}
    \det\Bigl(\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\varphi(A)\Bigr)=\prod_{c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}}\det\nolimits_{\mathfrak g}\bigl(\id-h_{U_1}(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})\bigr)>0\;.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(i) The set $\mathfrak P_c$ is a lifted rectangle of side at most $2L+1\leqslant s_{\mathfrak P}$, injective modulo the periods (every fine period is at least $8M>2L+1$), and it contains every bond of $\mathcal E_c$, both endpoints of such a bond lying in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$ by \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-bonds}. The two blocks of $c$ lie in $\Omega_1^{\sim}$ ((B1)(iv)) and $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ ((B1)(iii)), so (B1)(i) gives $| U_1(\partial p)-1|<\varepsilon_0$, hence $\| U_1(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}\varepsilon_0=2c_{\mathrm h}(\varepsilon_0/2)$ by the norm comparison of the preamble, for every plaquette $p\subset\mathfrak P_c$. By the consequence $3c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_0\leqslant r_G$ of \eqref{eq:c2-fibre-thresholds} noted after it, $6c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}(\varepsilon_0/2)\leqslant r_G$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge} with $\varepsilon_0/2$ in place of $\varepsilon_1$ (the remark after its proof) gives a site gauge on $\mathfrak P_c$ with phases $h(A_b)\leqslant 3c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_0\leqslant \tau_L/2$, by the first condition. This is the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} at $c$.

The phases of $\mathfrak g^{\Omega_1}$, extended by zero, form the subspace of $\mathfrak g^{\mathcal E_c}$ of the phases vanishing on the bonds of $\mathcal E_c$ off $\Omega_1$; for $A$ in it and $d\in\mathfrak g$ the phase $A-h_{U_1}(c)d$ lies in it, since $b_0(c)$ is a bond of $\Omega_1$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i)--(iii) hold on it by restriction.

(ii) By (B1)(ii)--(iii), $| U'(b)-1|<2\,O(L^2)\varepsilon_0$ for $U'= UU_1^{-1}$ on every bond $b$ of $\Omega_1$: every such bond, the designated bonds included, is a bond of $\square'^{\sim2}$ for the $L^2M_2R_1$-cube $\square'\subset\Omega_1$ that contains an endpoint of $b$ in $\Omega_1$ ($\Omega_1$ is a union of $LMR_1$-cubes, p.248, each a union of $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes: the partitions of \cite[p.~245]{BalabanCRE} are compatible, that is nested, (H4), and all sides are powers of $L$, the paragraph following \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}). By item 5, $2\,O(L^2)\varepsilon_0< r_G/\sqrt N$, so $\| U'(b)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_{\mathrm h}| U'(b)-1|< r_G$ and $h(A'(b))\leqslant c_G\| U'(b)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant c_Gc_{\mathrm h}\,2\,O(L^2)\varepsilon_0$ (preamble); $\mathcal E_c$ has at most $n_{\mathcal E}$ bonds, and $A'$ vanishes on those off $\Omega_1$, so the second condition of \eqref{eq:c2-fibre-thresholds} gives $\| A'|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/4<\varrho_*$.

The row component $d_c=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A')$ depends on $A'|_{\mathcal E_c}$ only (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}), and Taylor's formula with Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i), which applies by (i), gives $h(d_c)\leqslant \frac12K_*(\vartheta_*/4)^2=\frac1{32}K_*\vartheta_*^2<2K_*\vartheta_*^2=\rho_{\mathrm d}$.

The only designated bond in $\mathcal E_c$ is $b_0(c)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}) and $h_{U_1}$ has its outputs at the designated bonds, so $A|_{\mathcal E_c}= A'|_{\mathcal E_c}+h_{U_1}(c)d_c$, and $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/4+H_*K_*\vartheta_*^2/32<\vartheta_*/2$ by $4K_*H_*\vartheta_*<1$. Finally $A'|_{\mathcal E_c}= A|_{\mathcal E_c}-h_{U_1}(c)d_c$, so $d_c=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A|_{\mathcal E_c}-h_{U_1}(c)d_c)$ solves the row equation of $c$ at $A$, with $h(d_c)\leqslant \rho_{\mathrm d}$ and $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*$; by the uniqueness in (i), $d_c=\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$.

(iii) Since $d$ is of chart class, $q_d(B)= A-h_{U_1}d$ is the chart logarithm of $U_d(B)U_1^{-1}$ on the bonds of $\Omega_1$, so it is the phase $A'$ of (ii) for $U= U_d(B)$. The row equations give $d_c=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A-h_{U_1}d)=\mathcal N_{U_1,c}(A')$, that is $d=\mathcal N_{U_1}(A')$, and $A= A'+h_{U_1}d$. So $A'$, $d$ and $A$ are the quantities of (ii) for $U= U_d(B)$, and (ii) gives $d_c=\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$ for every row.

(iv) $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ is a finite intersection of preimages of open balls under restriction maps, hence open, and it contains the arguments by (ii). By (i) each component $\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$ is analytic and real on $\mathcal N_{\Theta}$ and solves the row equation of $c$ at $A$; the row equations decouple ($(A-h_{U_1}\varphi(A))|_{\mathcal E_c}= A|_{\mathcal E_c}-h_{U_1}(c)\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$, Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}), so $\varphi$ solves the system \eqref{eq:native-source-local-implicit}.

By \eqref{eq:convex-uniform-implicit-chart} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i), $\|\Theta(A)|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|+2H_*K_*\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|^2<\vartheta_*/2+H_*K_*\vartheta_*^2/2<\vartheta_*$.

Every bond $b$ of $\Omega_1$ lies in $\mathcal E_c$ for a row $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$: $b$ has an endpoint in $\Omega_1$, whose block $\mathcal B_y$ lies in $\Omega_1$ ($\Omega_1$ is a union of blocks); if both endpoints of $b$ lie in $\mathcal B_y$, any coarse bond $c$ with $c_-= y$ serves, and otherwise the coarse bond joining $y$ and the centre of the block of the other endpoint does; in both cases a block centre of $c$ lies in $\Omega_1$, so $c\in\Omega_1^{[1]}$, and $b\in\mathcal E_c$ by \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-bonds}. Hence $h(\Theta(A)(b))\leqslant \|\Theta(A)|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*\leqslant \varrho_G/2$.

By \eqref{eq:convex-uniform-implicit-chart} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i), $\| h_{U_1}(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\varphi_c\|\leqslant H_*C_{\mathsf D}\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|=4H_*K_*\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<2H_*K_*\vartheta_*<1$.

The matrix $\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\varphi$ has rows indexed by $\Omega_1^{[1]}$ and columns by the bonds of $\Omega_1$, $h_{U_1}$ maps row $c$ to the bond $b_0(c)$, and $\partial_{A(b_0(c'))}\varphi_c=0$ for $c'\neq c$, since $\varphi_c$ depends on $A|_{\mathcal E_c}$, which contains no designated bond other than $b_0(c)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}). So, in the ordering (free bonds, designated bonds), $\id-h_{U_1}\frac{\delta}{\delta A}\varphi$ is block triangular, with identity block on the free bonds and designated block $\operatorname{diag}_c(\id-h_{U_1}(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\varphi_c)$; this gives the product in \eqref{eq:c2-fibre-jacobian}. Each factor is positive by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii), which applies by (i), since $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|<\vartheta_*/2$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Primitive Bounds]\label{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}
Let $g_0$ satisfy threshold item 3 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, $4C_{\mathsf C}g_0(1+2r)\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ (hence $4C_{\mathsf C}g_0s_{\xi}\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$, and $g_0s_{\xi}\leqslant \vartheta_*/(8C_{\mathsf C})\leqslant 1$, since $C_{\mathsf C}\geqslant 1$ and $\vartheta_*\leqslant \tau_L/2\leqslant 1/2$ by \eqref{eq:c2-tau-final}). Then on the enlarged box $\{| a_b|\leqslant 2r\ \forall b\in I\}$ and for $t\in[0,1]$, every primitive $p_{\alpha}$ with free-input set $S_{\alpha}$ meeting $I$ is, at the input $a+tA_{\mathrm e}$, the restriction to real arguments of a function analytic in $(a,t)$ on a complex neighbourhood of the enlarged box times $[0,1]$, and with a constant $C_{\mathrm p}$ depending on $L$ and the group only,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-primitive-sizes}
    | p_{\xi,\alpha}(a+tA_{\mathrm e})|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}^3,\qquad
    | p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}(a+tA_{\mathrm e})|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0^2s_{\xi}^2,\qquad
    | p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}(a+tA_{\mathrm e})|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}\;,
\end{equation}
and for each of the three kinds, in the Hilbert norms on $\mathfrak g^{S_{\alpha}}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:convex-primitive-derivatives}
    \| D_a^2p_{\alpha}\|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi},\qquad
    \| D_ap_{\alpha}\|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}^2,\qquad
    | p_{\alpha}(a+tA_{\mathrm e})-p_{\alpha}(tA_{\mathrm e})|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}^3\;,
\end{equation}
and $\| D_a^3p_{\alpha}\|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0$, $\| D_a^4p_{\alpha}\|\leqslant C_{\mathrm p}g_0^2$; the same four derivative bounds hold for the derivatives $D_B^kp_{\alpha}$, $k=1,\dots,4$, in the full input $B= a+tA_{\mathrm e}$ on $\mathfrak g^{S_{\alpha}}$, retained inputs included (the input of the primitive is linear in $B$ with the same norm bound).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\emph{The input of a primitive.} On the enlarged box, $| a_b+tA_{\mathrm e}(b)|\leqslant 2r+r_{\mathrm e,\xi}\leqslant 2s_{\xi}$ for every bond $b$ within $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(iii) bounds the retained inputs by $r_{\mathrm e,\xi}$), in particular for the free bonds of the two-block sets of the near rows and for the free bonds of the plaquettes and blocks of the near primitives. The rows of a near primitive are within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ (applicability paragraph).

The \emph{input} $\mathfrak u$ of a primitive is the vector $g_0\mathsf C_UB$ restricted to the following bond set $S$: for a plaquette primitive $E_{\xi,p}$, $p_{\xi,p}$ the union of the sets $\mathcal E_c$ over the rows $c$ of $p$ (at most four) together with the free bonds of $\partial p$ not in those sets; for the Haar primitive $p^{\mathrm H}_{\xi,b}$ the set $\mathcal E_c$ when $b= b_0(c)$ and $\{ b\}$ when $b$ is free; for the Jacobian primitive $p^{\mathrm J}_{\xi,c}$ the set $\mathcal E_c$; for a gauge primitive $E_{\xi,y}$, $p_{\xi,y}$ the set $\mathcal E_y$ (on which $\mathsf C_U$ is the identity, all its bonds being free).

The primitive is a function of the phase $q_U(B)$ on its bonds, and that phase is a function of the input: on $\mathcal E_c$ it is $\mathfrak u|_{\mathcal E_c}-h_U\widetilde D_{U,c}(\mathfrak u|_{\mathcal E_c})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii)), and on a free bond outside the row sets it is $\mathfrak u_b= g_0B(b)$. With $B= a+tA_{\mathrm e}$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i) each row component satisfies $\|\mathfrak u|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant C_{\mathsf C}g_0\cdot2s_{\xi}\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$ and each free-bond component outside the row sets $h(\mathfrak u_b)\leqslant |\mathfrak u_b|\leqslant 2g_0s_{\xi}\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$ (threshold item 3 and $C_{\mathsf C}\geqslant 1$), so for the plaquette, Haar and Jacobian primitives (at most four rows and four further free bonds)
\begin{equation*}
    \|\mathfrak u\|\leqslant 16C_{\mathsf C}g_0s_{\xi},\qquad\| D_a\mathfrak u\|\leqslant 5C_{\mathsf C}g_0,\qquad\|\partial_t\mathfrak u\|\leqslant 16C_{\mathsf C}g_0s_{\xi}\;,
\end{equation*}
the second in the operator norm from the Hilbert norm of $\mathfrak g^{S_{\alpha}}$ (the Hilbert bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i) on each of at most four rows, plus the identity on the free bonds); for the gauge primitive, whose input $g_0B|_{\mathcal E_y}$ has $|\mathcal E_y|=4L^3(L-1)$ free bonds, $\|\mathfrak u\|\leqslant g_0|\mathcal E_y|^{1/2}\cdot2s_{\xi}\leqslant 2C_{\mathsf C}g_0s_{\xi}\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$ (as $C_{\mathsf C}\geqslant (4L^3(L-1))^{1/2}$ and $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |$), $\| D_a\mathfrak u\|\leqslant g_0$ and $\|\partial_t\mathfrak u\|\leqslant 2C_{\mathsf C}g_0s_{\xi}$, so the three displayed bounds hold for all four kinds.

The input is linear in $B$, hence affine in $(a,t)$ and linear in $a$ at fixed $t$; $D_a\mathfrak u$ is the restriction of $D_B\mathfrak u= g_0\mathsf C_U|_{S}$ to the $a$-directions, and the same count gives $\| D_B\mathfrak u\|\leqslant 5C_{\mathsf C}g_0$ (respectively $\leqslant g_0$ for the gauge primitive), so every bound below on a derivative in $a$ holds verbatim for the derivative of the same order in $B$ on $\mathfrak g^{S_{\alpha}}$, retained inputs included.

Each primitive is $\varphi(\mathfrak u)$ for a function $\varphi$ of the input analytic on a complex neighbourhood of the closed set $\mathcal P=\{\mathfrak u\in\mathfrak g^S_{\mathbb C}:\|\mathfrak u|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2\text{ for each row }c\text{ of the primitive},\ h(\mathfrak u_b)\leqslant \vartheta_*/2\text{ for each free bond }b\text{ of }S\text{ outside the row sets}\}$ (for the gauge primitive, the closed ball $\|\mathfrak u\|\leqslant \vartheta_*$ of $\mathfrak g^{\mathcal E_y}_{\mathbb C}$), with derivatives up to order five bounded on $\mathcal P$ by constants of $L$ and the group: Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii) for the row solution, the phase and the two logarithms, each a function of one row component (the Haar logarithm at a free bond outside the row sets is the function of (iii) at a free bond of a two-block set, where $q_U(A)(b)= A(b)$, a function of the single component $\mathfrak u_b$); for the plaquette term, with $W(q)\coloneqq(e^{iq}U)(\partial p)$, $s_{p,U}(q)=1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_NW(q)$ equals $1-\frac12(\tr_NW(q)+\tr_NW(q)^{-1})$ for real $q$, $W(q)$ being unitary, and $W(q)$ and $W(q)^{-1}$ are ordered products of the fixed links and of $e^{\pm iq(b)}$, entire functions of the phases $q(b)$, which are analytic functions of one row component (with $h(q_U(A)(b))\leqslant \| A\|+H_*2K_*\| A\|^2\leqslant \vartheta_*$ on the ball) or are free-bond components of $\mathfrak u$; this defines the analytic function $s_{p,U}(q_U(\bigcdot ))$, with derivatives bounded on $\mathcal P$ by the chain rule; for the gauge term, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}.

The segment from $0$ to $\mathfrak u$ lies in $\mathcal P$, each component of $\mathfrak u$ being within $\vartheta_*/4$ of zero. Hence every primitive at the input $a+tA_{\mathrm e}$ is the restriction to real $(a,t)$ of a function analytic in $(a,t)$ on a complex neighbourhood of the enlarged box times $[0,1]$ (the composition of $\varphi$ with the affine map), and the bounds below are uniform there.

\emph{Energy residual.} $E_{\xi,\alpha}(a+tA_{\mathrm e})= g_0^{-2}\varphi(\mathfrak u)$ with $\varphi(\mathfrak u)\coloneqq-[s_{\alpha,U}(q_U(\mathfrak u))-s_{\alpha,U}(0)]$ for a plaquette and $\varphi(\mathfrak u)=-\mathscr G_{y,U}(\mathfrak u)$ for a centre. Since $\mathfrak u$ is linear in $B$, the Taylor polynomial of degree two in $B$ at $B=0$ subtracted in \eqref{eq:native-source-energy-residual} is that of $\varphi$ at $0$ composed with the linear map, so $p_{\xi,\alpha}= g_0^{-2}[\varphi(\mathfrak u)-D\varphi(0)\mathfrak u-\frac12D^2\varphi(0)[\mathfrak u,\mathfrak u]]$, the second-order Taylor residual at the input, bounded by $g_0^{-2}\frac16\| D^3\varphi\|\|\mathfrak u\|^3\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}^3$ (the segment from $0$ to $\mathfrak u$ lies in $\mathcal P$).

Its first derivative in $a$ is $g_0^{-2}(D\varphi(\mathfrak u)-D\varphi(0)-D^2\varphi(0)\mathfrak u)D_a\mathfrak u$, bounded by $g_0^{-2}\frac12\| D^3\varphi\|\|\mathfrak u\|^2\cdot5C_{\mathsf C}g_0\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}^2$; its second derivative is $g_0^{-2}(D^2\varphi(\mathfrak u)-D^2\varphi(0))[D_a\mathfrak u,D_a\mathfrak u]$, bounded by $g_0^{-2}\| D^3\varphi\|\|\mathfrak u\|(5C_{\mathsf C}g_0)^2\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}$; its third and fourth derivatives are $g_0^{-2}D^3\varphi(\mathfrak u)[D_a\mathfrak u]^3$ and $g_0^{-2}D^4\varphi(\mathfrak u)[D_a\mathfrak u]^4$, bounded by $Cg_0$ and $Cg_0^2$.

The Taylor polynomial subtracted is that of the germ (Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}), which is the Taylor polynomial of $\varphi$ at $0$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii).

\emph{Haar logarithm.} $\psi(\mathfrak u)=\log\sigma(q_U(\mathfrak u)(b))-\log\sigma(0)$, the primitive \eqref{eq:native-source-haar-primitive}, has $\psi(0)=0$ and $D\psi(0)=0$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii): $\sigma$ is even and $Dq_U(0)$ is linear). Hence $|\psi(\mathfrak u)|\leqslant \frac12\| D^2\psi\|\|\mathfrak u\|^2\leqslant Cg_0^2s_{\xi}^2$, $\| D_a\psi\|\leqslant \| D^2\psi\|\|\mathfrak u\|\cdot5C_{\mathsf C}g_0\leqslant Cg_0^2s_{\xi}\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}^2$, $\| D_a^2\psi\|\leqslant \| D^2\psi\|(5C_{\mathsf C}g_0)^2\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}$, and the third and fourth derivatives are bounded by $Cg_0^3\leqslant Cg_0$ and $Cg_0^4\leqslant Cg_0^2$.

\emph{Constraint logarithm.} $\lambda(\mathfrak u)=\log|\det_{\mathfrak g}(\id-h_U(c)\partial_{A(b_0(c))}\widetilde D_{U,c}(\mathfrak u))|=\log\det_{\mathfrak g}(\cdots)$ (the determinant is positive, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii)) has $\lambda(0)=0$ and derivatives up to order five bounded on $\mathcal P$. Hence $|\lambda(\mathfrak u)|\leqslant \| D\lambda\|\|\mathfrak u\|\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}$, $\| D_a\lambda\|\leqslant \| D\lambda\|\cdot5C_{\mathsf C}g_0\leqslant Cg_0\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}^2$, $\| D_a^2\lambda\|\leqslant \| D^2\lambda\|(5C_{\mathsf C}g_0)^2\leqslant Cg_0^2\leqslant Cg_0s_{\xi}$ (as $g_0\leqslant 1$ and $s_{\xi}\geqslant 1$), and the third and fourth derivatives are bounded by $Cg_0^3\leqslant Cg_0$ and $Cg_0^4\leqslant Cg_0^2$.

Let $C'_{\mathrm p}$ be the maximum over the finitely many templates of the constants $C$ above and let $C_{\mathrm p}\coloneqq 2C'_{\mathrm p}$. Then \eqref{eq:c2-primitive-sizes}, the first two bounds of \eqref{eq:convex-primitive-derivatives}, and the third- and fourth-order bounds hold, and the last bound of \eqref{eq:convex-primitive-derivatives} is the difference of two values each bounded by $C'_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}^3$ (for all three kinds, since $s_{\xi}\geqslant 1$ and $g_0\leqslant 1$), hence by $2C'_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}^3= C_{\mathrm p}g_0s_{\xi}^3$.

\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}(i)--(iii) and~(vi)]
Let $c$ be a row within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$; by the applicability paragraph Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} applies to it, and (ii)--(iii) give, for every real $A$ with $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$, the unique small solution $\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$ with $\varphi_c$ analytic on the complex ball of radius $\vartheta_*$ and real on real phases, $\varphi_c(0)=0$, $D\varphi_c(0)=0$, the positivity of the determinant, and the analyticity of the row solution, the phase and the two logarithms on a complex neighbourhood of the closed ball of radius $\vartheta_*/2$, with derivatives up to order five bounded on that ball.

For $B\in\mathcal U_c$, $\max_{b\in\mathcal E_c\cap E_*}| B(b)|<2+4r=2(1+2r)$ and $\| g_0\mathsf C_UB\|_{\mathcal E_c}\leqslant 2C_{\mathsf C}g_0(1+2r)\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$ by threshold item 3, so $g_0\mathsf C_U\mathcal U_c$ lies in the phase ball; $B\mapsto g_0\mathsf C_UB$ is linear with norm at most $g_0C_{\mathsf C}\leqslant C_{\mathsf C}$ for the Hilbert norms (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i)), so the derivatives in $B$ are bounded by the same constants times $C_{\mathsf C}^{\,k}$.

For $c$ within $2R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$, the plaquette term of a plaquette $p$ with a bond in $\mathcal E_c$ is analytic in $B$ on the intersection of the polydiscs of the rows of $p$, as above, and these rows are within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ (applicability paragraph), so the chart applies to each of them.

For a centre $y$ within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-local-gauge} applied to the block $\mathcal B_y$ (applicability paragraph) gives a gauge with phases at most $\widehat\mu<\tau_L/2$ on $\mathcal E_y$; every bond of $\mathcal E_y$ is free, so $q_U(B)= g_0B$ there and $\| g_0B|_{\mathcal E_y}\|\leqslant g_0|\mathcal E_y|^{1/2}\max_b| B(b)|\leqslant g_0(4L^3(L-1))^{1/2}\cdot2(1+2r)\leqslant 2C_{\mathsf C}g_0(1+2r)\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$ under threshold item 3 (using $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |$, $|\mathcal E_y|=4L^3(L-1)$ and $C_{\mathsf C}\geqslant (4L^3(L-1))^{1/2}$); Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means} then gives the existence of the relative means within $r_G$ of $\id$ and the analyticity and derivative bounds of $\mathscr G_{y,U}(g_0B|_{\mathcal E_y})$ on $\mathcal U_y$. The values at $q=0$ of the plaquette and gauge terms are subtracted in the primitives.

Finally, where $(A_{\mathrm e},a)\in\mathcal D_{\xi}$ and $c$ is within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$, the phase $A= g_0\mathsf C_U\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})$ has $\| A|_{\mathcal E_c}\|\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$, because $a$ is in the open box and $\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})= a+A_{\mathrm e}$ with $| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|< r$ on the two-block set (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i),(iii),(iv)), so $\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\in\mathcal U_c$ and the bound on $g_0\mathsf C_U\mathcal U_c$ applies; $\varphi_c(A|_{\mathcal E_c})$ is the row solution $\widetilde D_c(A)$ of (B4)(i), which is that of \cite{BalabanCRE} by (B4)(i) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}(iii), and the phase, the Haar density, the Jacobian and the plaquette and gauge terms of \cite[(1.14)--(1.15)]{BalabanCRE} are the same functions of it.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Host Multiplicity and Potential Size]\label{lem:c2-potential-size}
Let $\mathfrak T$ be the set of primitive templates (kind, label and free-input shape, including the shapes truncated by $\Omega_1$) modulo $L\mathbb Z^4$, each anchored at one of its input bonds, and let $D_{\mathrm h}$ be one plus the maximum $\ell^{\infty}$ diameter of a lifted host \eqref{eq:part1-potential-host} and $B_{\mathrm h}$ the maximum number of $M$-cubes in one, both over $\mathfrak T$. With
\begin{equation}\label{eq:part1-host-multiplicity}
    N_{\mathrm h}=|\mathfrak T|(2\lceil D_{\mathrm h}\rceil+3)^4,\qquad
    C_0= N_{\mathrm h}C_{\mathrm p}e^{\kappa(B_{\mathrm h}+4)},\qquad
    \omega(g_0)= C_0g_0(1+r)^3\;,
\end{equation}
at most $N_{\mathrm h}$ primitives are assigned to any host $Y$, $d_0(Y)\leqslant B_{\mathrm h}+4$, and on the enlarged box, for every host,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-interaction-size}
    \sup|\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)|\leqslant \omega(g_0)e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $v$ be a vertex of $Y$. Every primitive assigned to $Y$ has its stencil, hence its anchor, in the lifted host, within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $D_{\mathrm h}$ of $v$; there are at most $(2\lceil D_{\mathrm h}\rceil+1)^4$ such anchor positions, and a template with an anchor position determines the primitive. Projection to the torus only identifies positions. By Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(i), $d_0(Y)\leqslant N_0(Y)-1\leqslant B_{\mathrm h}$. At $t=0$, $s_{\xi}$ may be replaced by $1+r$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}, since no retained input enters; each of the three kinds is then bounded by $C_{\mathrm p}g_0(1+r)^3$, and $|\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,a)|\leqslant N_{\mathrm h}C_{\mathrm p}g_0(1+r)^3\leqslant N_{\mathrm h}C_{\mathrm p}g_0(1+r)^3e^{\kappa(B_{\mathrm h}+4)}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}$.
\end{proof}

The definition gives $C_0\geqslant C_{\mathrm p}$, since $N_{\mathrm h}\geqslant 1$ and the exponential factor is at least one. The constant $C_0$ depends on $L$, the group, $M$ and $\kappa$ (through $B_{\mathrm h}$, $D_{\mathrm h}$), not on the volume, the branch or $g_0$.

The hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:ibp} holds for $f= f_{\xi}$ on the enlarged box, which is a neighbourhood of the closed cutoff box: the exponent $\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}$ is a quadratic polynomial plus $P_{\xi,t}$, a finite sum of near primitives, each analytic there by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}; and $f_{\xi}(a)= W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a))$ is a character of a product of the reconstructed links \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field} over the contour bonds, each of which depends on $a$ through the rows of a free-input set meeting $I$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}(i) puts $\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})= a+A_{\mathrm e}$ on those rows, so the phase is \eqref{eq:native-collar-source-phase}), where $q_U$ is analytic in $a$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii)--(iii); contour bonds whose rows do not meet $I$ do not depend on $a$. Both factors are therefore analytic on the enlarged box, uniformly in $t\in[0,1]$.

\subsection{Proof of the Gaussian Payment}
\label{app:fixed-kernel-payment}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}]
\emph{Tail of the walk series.} Throughout, $E_0$, $C_{E_0}$, $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)$ are as in \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-C-Gamma} and the sentence preceding it (their block decomposition is \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-exact-blocks}), and $S_{Z_0}(1)=\mathsf G^{1/2}$. Let $\mathsf N$ be the set of bonds $b'\in I$ with $d_{\infty,T}(b'_-,Z_0)\leqslant R+1$. Since $\iota_{E_0}^*H$ has nonzero entries $H(b,b')$ only for $d(b_-,b'_-)\leqslant R$ and $b\in E_0$ meets $Z_0$, $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)-\Gamma_{E_0}(1)=\iota_{E_0}^*H\Pi_{I\setminus E_0}\Pi_{\mathsf N}(S_{Z_0}(\sigma)-\mathsf G^{1/2})$.

A walk $\omega=(r;b_0,\ldots,b_{m+1})$ with $b_0\in\mathsf N$ has $| w_{\omega}(\sigma)-1|\ne0$ only if $D(\omega)$ meets a cube $\Delta\not\subseteq Z_0'$. The open $M$-neighbourhood of $Z_0$ is $\bigcup_{Q\subseteq Z_0}\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$, and by definition every $LM$-cube meeting it lies in $Z_0'$ (Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}). Hence $D(\omega)$ contains a point at distance at least $M$ from $Z_0$, and at least $M-R-1$ from $b_{0,-}$.

Each block of $\mathsf A_H^r$ ($r< n_*$) or $\mathsf P_H$ vanishes beyond distance $R_*$, and $D_b$ lies within $\rho_{\mathrm w}$ of $b_-$, so $D(\omega)$ lies within $(m+1)R_*+\rho_{\mathrm w}$ of $b_{0,-}$. By \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-collar-size}, $M/4\geqslant \rho_{\mathrm w}+R+R_*+2$, so $(m+1)R_*\geqslant M-R-1-\rho_{\mathrm w}\geqslant \frac34M+R_*+1$ and $m> M/(2R_*)\geqslant N_M$. The absolute block row sum of the terms with $m\geqslant N_M$ is, by the bounds in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-series} and $| w_{\omega}-1|\leqslant 2a_*^{m+1}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-rooted-tail}
    s_H^{-1/2}\sum_{r< n_*}\sum_{m\geqslant N_M}a_{n_*m+r}\,2a_*^{m+1}V_*\beta^m
    \leqslant 2s_H^{-1/2}\frac{n_*V_*a_*}{1-a_*\beta}4^{-N_M}=\delta_M\;,
\end{equation}
using $a_*\beta\leqslant 1/4$. The absolute block column sums of these terms obey the same bound, because every walk in the tail has $m\geqslant N_M$ whatever its first bond. Schur's test gives $\|\Pi_{\mathsf N}(S_{Z_0}(\sigma)-\mathsf G^{1/2})\|\leqslant \delta_M$. With $\| H\|\leqslant h_+$ this is the first bound of (i); with $\| C_{E_0}\|\leqslant \gamma^{-1}$, since $\iota_{E_0}^*H\iota_{E_0}\geqslant \gamma$, the second follows.

\emph{Reserve identity.} Let $\Gamma\coloneqq\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)=\Gamma_1+i\Gamma_2$ with real $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$; $\Gamma_{E_0}(1)$ is real, so $\Gamma_2=\operatorname{Im}(\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)-\Gamma_{E_0}(1))$. The quadratic form in \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-density} is bilinear, so for real $X$, $\operatorname{Re}\langle\Gamma X,C_{E_0}\Gamma X\rangle=\langle\Gamma_1X,C_{E_0}\Gamma_1X\rangle-\langle\Gamma_2X,C_{E_0}\Gamma_2X\rangle$ and $| e^{-\langle B,\Gamma X\rangle}|= e^{-\langle B,\Gamma_1X\rangle}$ for real $B$.

For $0\leqslant \alpha_G<\gamma$ let $C_{E_0,\alpha_G}\coloneqq(\iota_{E_0}^*H\iota_{E_0}-\alpha_G)^{-1}$. The Gaussian integral over $B$ with density $(2\pi)^{-d_G| E_0|/2}\det(C_{E_0})^{-1/2}e^{-\frac12\langle B,(C_{E_0}^{-1}-\alpha_G)B\rangle-\langle B,\Gamma_1X\rangle}$ equals $\det_{E_0}(\id-\alpha_GC_{E_0})^{-1/2}e^{\frac12\langle\Gamma_1X,C_{E_0,\alpha_G}\Gamma_1X\rangle}$. Collecting the $X$-exponent,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-actual-reserve-form}
    \begin{gathered}
    \begin{aligned}
    &\int\Bigl| e^{-\frac12\langle\Gamma X,C_{E_0}\Gamma X\rangle}e^{-\langle B,\Gamma X\rangle}\Bigr| e^{\frac{\alpha_G}{2}\| B\|^2}\dd\mu_{C_{E_0}}(B)\\
    &\qquad=\det_{E_0}(\id-\alpha_GC_{E_0})^{-1/2}e^{\frac12\langle X,T_{\alpha_G}X\rangle},
    \end{aligned}\\
    T_{\alpha_G}=\Gamma_1^{\mathsf T}(C_{E_0,\alpha_G}-C_{E_0})\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2^{\mathsf T}C_{E_0}\Gamma_2\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
a real symmetric positive semidefinite matrix on $\mathfrak g^I$ ($C_{E_0,\alpha_G}\geqslant C_{E_0}$ for $\alpha_G\geqslant 0$). By Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks} the columns of $\Gamma$ outside $J_Z$ vanish, so $T_{\alpha_G}$ is supported on $J_Z$, and $\int e^{\frac12\langle X,T_{\alpha_G}X\rangle}\dd\mu_0(X)=\det_{J_Z}(\id-T_{\alpha_G})^{-1/2}$ when $\| T_{\alpha_G}\|<1$. Integrating \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-actual-reserve-form} against $\mu_0$ therefore gives the integral of (ii) in closed form, $\det_{E_0}(\id-\alpha_GC_{E_0})^{-1/2}\det_{J_Z}(\id-T_{\alpha_G})^{-1/2}$, once $\| T_{\alpha_G}\|<1$ is shown.

\emph{Norm of $T_{\alpha_G}$.} The resolvent identity gives $C_{E_0,\alpha_G}-C_{E_0}=\alpha_GC_{E_0,\alpha_G}C_{E_0}$, of norm at most $\alpha_G/(\gamma(\gamma-\alpha_G))$. By (i) and $\delta_M\leqslant 1$, $\|\Gamma_1\|\leqslant \|\Gamma_{E_0}(1)\|+h_+\delta_M\leqslant h_+\gamma^{-1/2}+h_+= A_*$, since $\|\Gamma_{E_0}(1)\|\leqslant \| H\|\|\mathsf G^{1/2}\|\leqslant h_+\gamma^{-1/2}$ ($\mathsf G= H^{-1}$ and $H\geqslant \gamma$); and $\|\Gamma_2\|\leqslant h_+\delta_M$. Hence, for $\alpha_G\leqslant \min(\gamma/2,\gamma^2/(16A_*^2))$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-reserve-payment}
    \| T_{\alpha_G}\|\leqslant \frac{\alpha_GA_*^2}{\gamma(\gamma-\alpha_G)}+\frac{h_+^2\delta_M^2}{\gamma}\leqslant \frac{2\alpha_GA_*^2}{\gamma^2}+\frac18\leqslant \frac14\;.
\end{equation}

\emph{Determinant bounds.} The eigenvalues of $\alpha_GC_{E_0}$ lie in $[0,1/2]$ and $-\frac12\log(1-t)\leqslant t$ for $t\leqslant 1/2$, so $\log\det_{E_0}(\id-\alpha_GC_{E_0})^{-1/2}\leqslant \alpha_G\operatorname{tr}C_{E_0}\leqslant (\alpha_G/\gamma)d_G| E_0|$. The eigenvalues of $T_{\alpha_G}$ lie in $[0,1/4]$ and $-\frac12\log(1-t)\leqslant \frac23t$ there, so $\log\det_{J_Z}(\id-T_{\alpha_G})^{-1/2}\leqslant \frac23\operatorname{tr}T_{\alpha_G}\leqslant \frac23d_G| J_Z|\| T_{\alpha_G}\|$. With $E_0\subseteq J_Z$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks}),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-trace-payment}
    \begin{gathered}
    \begin{aligned}
    \log\bigl[\det_{E_0}(\id-\alpha_GC_{E_0})^{-1/2}\det_{J_Z}(\id-T_{\alpha_G})^{-1/2}\bigr]
    &\leqslant d_G| J_Z|\Bigl(\frac{\alpha_G}{\gamma}+\frac{4\alpha_GA_*^2}{3\gamma^2}+\frac{2h_+^2\delta_M^2}{3\gamma}\Bigr)\\
    &\leqslant C_{\mathrm d}(\alpha_G+\delta_M^2)| J_Z|,
    \end{aligned}\\
    C_{\mathrm d}= d_G\max\Bigl(\frac1\gamma+\frac{4A_*^2}{3\gamma^2},\frac{2h_+^2}{3\gamma}\Bigr)\;.
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
A bond of $J_Z$ has its initial site in a cube of $Z$, so $| J_Z|\leqslant 4(LM+1)^4N_1(Z)$. Since $n_*,R_*,C_{\mathrm w}$ are fixed before $M$ and $\delta_M=2C_{\mathrm w}4^{-\lfloor M/(2R_*)\rfloor}$ decays exponentially in $M$, there is $M$ with $4C_{\mathrm d}\delta_M^2(LM+1)^4\leqslant 1/2$; then $\alpha_G\leqslant (8C_{\mathrm d}(LM+1)^4)^{-1}$ gives the bound $e^{N_1(Z)}$.

Both $C_{E_0}$ and $\Gamma_{E_0}$ are block diagonal over the components $D$ of $Z$ by \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-exact-blocks}, hence so are $T_{\alpha_G}$ and both determinants, which proves the factorisation.

\emph{Bad-bond reserve.} On $\{| B_b|\geqslant r\}$, $h(B_b)^2\geqslant c_{\mathrm n}| B_b|^2\geqslant c_{\mathrm n}r^2$, so $\mathbf 1_{\{| B_b|\geqslant r\}}\leqslant e^{\frac{\gamma_2}{2}(h(B_b)^2-c_{\mathrm n}r^2)}$; the product over $\mathsf P$ is (iii).
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Mayer Constants and the Activity Bounds}
\label{app:mayer-constants}

The following constants depend on $L$ and the group only and are fixed in this order: $C_{\mathrm g}=162$ and $\delta=1/40$; a decay rate $\kappa\geqslant 3$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-kappa-choice}
    \delta\kappa\geqslant 2C_{\mathrm g}\log128,\qquad
    \lambda'=(1-5\delta)\frac{L\kappa}{2049},\qquad
    \lambda_*=\lambda'-2C_{\mathrm g}\geqslant 2C_{\mathrm g}\log128\;;
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-mayer-constants}
    \begin{gathered}
    \alpha_6=\min\Bigl(\frac18,\frac{\delta\kappa}{2C_{\mathrm g}B(\delta\kappa/2)}\Bigr),\qquad
    \kappa_1-1\geqslant 5\lambda'+1,\\
    \theta=\frac{\lambda_*}{16C_{\mathrm g}},\qquad
    C_{\mathrm s}=\frac{2049L^3C_{\mathrm g}B(\delta\kappa)e^{L\kappa/2}}{\delta\kappa}\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
and a number $\omega_*>0$ with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-vacuum-KP-budget}
    \eta_*=2e^{1/2+5\kappa}\omega_*\leqslant \frac{\alpha_6}{4},\qquad
    \varepsilon_*=\frac{C_{\mathrm s}\eta_*}{\alpha_6}\leqslant \min\Bigl(\frac14,\frac{1}{72B(\lambda_*/2)}\Bigr)\;;
\end{equation}
these conditions involve only $\kappa$, $\alpha_6$, $C_{\mathrm s}$ and $\lambda_*$, so $\omega_*$, $\eta_*$ and $\varepsilon_*= C_{\mathrm s}t_0$ are fixed before $M_1$, $M$ and the Gaussian reserve $\alpha_G$, as Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds} states.

Let $t_0\coloneqq\eta_*/\alpha_6\leqslant 1/4$ and, once $\alpha_G$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment} is fixed after $M$, $\gamma_2=\alpha_G/2$, so $a_{\mathrm{bad}}= c_{\mathrm n}\alpha_Gr^2/4$. The coupling is then taken so small that $\omega(g_0)\leqslant \omega_*$, the chart condition of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} holds, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-bad-budget}
    a_{\mathrm{bad}}\geqslant \max\Bigl(160\bigl(\kappa+\log(8M^4+8)+1\bigr),\ 64\log\frac1{\eta_*}\Bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
These are compatible because $r= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ (the radius of the literal cutoff \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}) tends to infinity while $g_0(1+r)^3\to0$.

The bounds $B(\delta\kappa/2)\leqslant 2e^{-\delta\kappa/(2C_{\mathrm g})}$, $B(\delta\kappa)\leqslant 2e^{-\delta\kappa/C_{\mathrm g}}$ and $B(\lambda_*/2)\leqslant 2e^{-\lambda_*/(2C_{\mathrm g})}$ hold by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(iv) and \eqref{eq:c2-kappa-choice}.

\begin{lemma}[Cover Sum]\label{lem:c2-cover-sum}
For every nonempty union $Y_0$ of $M$-cubes,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-cover-sum}
    \sum_{\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbf D_0\, | \,\bigcup_{Y\in\mathcal D}Y= Y_0}\ \prod_{Y\in\mathcal D}\alpha_6e^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Y)}\leqslant 1\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The members of $\mathbf D_0$ are localisation domains of $\pi_0$ and $\mathcal D$ is a set of distinct domains. For a cover, $\sum_{Y\in\mathcal D}\ell_0(Y)\geqslant \sum_YN_0(Y)/C_{\mathrm g}\geqslant N_0(Y_0)/C_{\mathrm g}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(i), so $\prod_Ye^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Y)/2}\leqslant e^{-\delta\kappa N_0(Y_0)/(2C_{\mathrm g})}$. Dropping the cover constraint, the remaining sum over sets of domains contained in $Y_0$ is at most $\prod_{Y\subseteq Y_0}(1+\alpha_6e^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Y)/2})\leqslant \exp\bigl(\alpha_6\sum_{Q\subseteq Y_0}\sum_{Y\ni Q}e^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Y)/2}\bigr)\leqslant \exp(\alpha_6B(\delta\kappa/2)N_0(Y_0))$ by \eqref{eq:native-source-animal-sum}. The product of the two bounds is at most one by the choice of $\alpha_6$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Selected Majorant]\label{lem:c2-selected-majorant}
On every branch, with $\mathbf W=\mathbf V_{\xi}$, $\omega(g_0)\leqslant \omega_*$ and the chart condition, every selected integral of Definition~\ref{def:selection} with $F=1$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:fixed-kernel-selected-majorant}
    |\mathcal A^{\mathrm f}_{(\mathcal D,\mathsf P,Z)}[1]|
    \leqslant e^{-(\kappa_1-1)N_1(Z\setminus Z_0')+N_1(Z)-a_{\mathrm{bad}}|\mathsf P|}\prod_{Y\in\mathcal D}\omega_*e^{1/2}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The weakening in \eqref{eq:c-selected-integral} is, for each cube $\Delta$ of $Z\setminus Z_0'$, the operation
\[
    G\mapsto\int_0^1\dd s\oint_{|\sigma_{\Delta}|= e^{\kappa_1}}\frac{G\,\dd\sigma_{\Delta}}{2\pi i(\sigma_{\Delta}-s)^2}
\]
applied to the inner integral (the $t_Y$-, $X$- and $B$-integrals) as a function of $\sigma_{\Delta}$ on the circle; it uses the measurability of the inner integral in $\sigma$ on the distinguished boundary (the integrand is continuous in $\sigma$, since $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)$ is the walk series of Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-series}, and Fubini applies to the iterated integral because the integral of the modulus of the inner integrand is bounded uniformly on the distinguished boundary, by the bounds below) and the bound $\sup_{s\in[0,1],|\sigma|= e^{\kappa_1}}|\sigma-s|^{-2}\cdot e^{\kappa_1}\leqslant e^{\kappa_1}(e^{\kappa_1}-1)^{-2}\leqslant e^{-(\kappa_1-1)}$, the last step because $e^{\kappa_1}\geqslant 3$.

Applying it for each cube of $Z\setminus Z_0'$ bounds \eqref{eq:c-selected-integral} by $e^{-(\kappa_1-1)N_1(Z\setminus Z_0')}$ times the supremum over the distinguished boundary $\{|\sigma_{\Delta}|= e^{\kappa_1}\ \forall\Delta\in\pi_1(Z)\setminus\pi_1(Z_0')\}$ (with $\sigma_{\Delta}=0$ off $Z$, $\sigma_{\Delta}=1$ on $Z_0'$) of the integral of the inner integrand's modulus, which lies in the closed polydisc of Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}.

There, the Mayer integrals $\int_0^1\dd t_Y$ have mass one; $\chi_b\leqslant 1$; by Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(iii) with $\gamma_2\leqslant \alpha_G$, $\prod_{b\in\mathsf P}(1-\chi_b)\leqslant e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}|\mathsf P|}e^{\frac{\alpha_G}{2}\| B\|^2}$; on the box $|\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,B)e^{t_Y\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y,B)}|\leqslant \omega(g_0)e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}e^{\omega(g_0)}\leqslant \omega_*e^{1/2}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-potential-size} and $\omega_*\leqslant 1/2$ (which follows from $\eta_*\leqslant 1/32$); and the integral of the absolute density against $e^{\alpha_G\| B\|^2/2}$ is at most $e^{N_1(Z)}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii).
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds}]
Let $Z$ be a connected final domain. Each selection $(\mathcal D,\mathsf P)$ in \eqref{eq:c-vacuum-activity} determines $Y_0=\bigcup\mathcal D$, the seed $Z_0$ with wall components $Z_{0,1},\ldots,Z_{0,k'}$, the components $Y_i$ of $Y_0$ (each inside one $Z_{0,j}$), $n_j= N_0(Z_{0,j}\setminus Y_0)$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-selected-majorant} and $\omega_*e^{1/2}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}\leqslant \eta_*e^{-\kappa\ell_0(Y)}$, the sum over selections is organised as $\sum_{Y'\subseteq Z}\sum_{Z_0\, | \,Z_0'= Y'}\sum_{Y_0\subseteq Z_0}\sum_{\mathcal D\, | \,\bigcup\mathcal D= Y_0}\sum_{\mathsf P}$ over unions of cubes $Y'$ of $\pi_1$ and $Y_0$ of $\pi_0$, and each inner sum is bounded in turn.

\emph{Potential labels.} The label weight factors as $\eta_*e^{-\kappa\ell_0(Y)}= t_0e^{-(1-\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Y)}\cdot\alpha_6e^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Y)}$. Each $Y\in\mathcal D$ lies in one component $Y_i$, and $\sum_{Y\subseteq Y_i}\ell_0(Y)\geqslant \ell_0(Y_i)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(ii), so with $t_0\leqslant 1$ and at least one label per component, $\prod_{Y\in\mathcal D}t_0e^{-(1-\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Y)}\leqslant \prod_it_0e^{-(1-\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Y_i)}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-cover-sum} sums the second factors to at most one.

\emph{Bad-bond labels.} Given $Y_0$ and $Z_0$, every $b\in\mathsf P$ has $b\cap Y_0=\varnothing$ and both endpoints in cubes of $Z_0$, hence in $Z_0\setminus Y_0$; there are at most $4M^4n$ such bonds. Every cube of $Z_0\setminus Y_0$ meets a bond of $\mathsf P$ and a bond meets at most two cubes, so $|\mathsf P|\geqslant n/2$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-bad-label-sum}
    \sum_{\mathsf P}e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}|\mathsf P|/2}\leqslant e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n/8}\sum_{\mathsf P}e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}|\mathsf P|/4}\leqslant \exp\Bigl[-\frac{a_{\mathrm{bad}}}{8}n+4M^4e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/4}n\Bigr]\leqslant e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n/16}\;,
\end{equation}
