since $4M^4e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/4}\leqslant a_{\mathrm{bad}}/16$: by \eqref{eq:native-source-bad-budget}, $a_{\mathrm{bad}}\geqslant 160(\kappa+1)>1$ and $64M^4e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/4}\leqslant 1$ (as $a_{\mathrm{bad}}/4\geqslant 40\log(8M^4+8)\geqslant \log(64M^4)$).

The unused half $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}|\mathsf P|/2}\leqslant e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n/4}$ leaves in total $e^{-5a_{\mathrm{bad}}n/16}=\prod_je^{-5a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/16}$, of which $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/32}$, $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/64}$ and $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/64}$ are used below.

\emph{Component reserve.} For a component $Z_{0,j}$ containing $k_j\geqslant 1$ components $Y_i$ of $Y_0$, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(iii) gives $\ell_0(Z_{0,j})\leqslant \sum_{i}\ell_0(Y_i)+5n_j$, so with $a_{\mathrm{bad}}/32\geqslant 5\kappa$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-component-reserve}
    t_0^{k_j}e^{-(1-\delta)\kappa\sum_i\ell_0(Y_i)}e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/32}\leqslant t_0e^{-(1-\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}\;.
\end{equation}
If $k_j=0$ then $n_j\geqslant 1$, $\ell_0(Z_{0,j})\leqslant 5n_j$, and $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/32}e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n_j/64}\leqslant e^{-5\kappa n_j}\eta_*\leqslant t_0e^{-(1-\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}$, using $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/64}\leqslant \eta_*\leqslant t_0$.

\emph{Choice of $Y_0$.} With the reserve $e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}n/64}$, $\sum_{Y_0\subseteq Z_0}e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}N_0(Z_0\setminus Y_0)/64}=(1+e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/64})^{N_0(Z_0)}\leqslant \exp(e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/64}C_{\mathrm g}\sum_j\ell_0(Z_{0,j}))\leqslant \prod_je^{\delta\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}$, since $C_{\mathrm g}e^{-a_{\mathrm{bad}}/64}\leqslant 162e^{-5(\kappa+1)/2}\leqslant \kappa/40$ for $\kappa\geqslant 3$. Altogether, writing $\mathfrak M(Z_0,Z)$ for the sum of \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-selected-majorant} over the selections with seed $Z_0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-initial-domain-sum}
    \mathfrak M(Z_0,Z)\leqslant e^{-(\kappa_1-1)N_1(Z\setminus Z_0')+N_1(Z)}\prod_{j}t_0e^{-(1-2\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}\;.
\end{equation}

\emph{Scale change.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-scale}, the enlargement $Z_0'$ of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} (the $LM$-cubes meeting $\operatorname{int}Q^{\sim}$ for some cube $Q$ of $Z_0$) equals $\bigcup_jZ_{0,j}'$, where $Z_{0,j}'$ is the enlargement of the component $Z_{0,j}$ in the sense of that lemma, so \eqref{eq:c2-scale-inequality} applies to each $Z_{0,j}$. Each $Z_{0,j}'$ is connected, so every component $Y'_i$ of $Y'= Z_0'$ is the union of the $Z_{0,j}'$ it contains.

With $e^{-(1-2\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}= e^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}e^{-(1-3\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}$ and \eqref{eq:c2-scale-inequality} in the form $\ell_0(Z_{0,j})\geqslant \frac{L}{2049}\ell_1(Z_{0,j}')-\frac{5L+1024}{2049}$, where $(5L+1024)/2049\leqslant L/2$ for $L\geqslant 3$,
\begin{equation*}
    \prod_{j\, | \,Z_{0,j}'\subseteq Y'_i}e^{-(1-3\delta)\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}\leqslant e^{L\kappa/2\cdot k'_i}\prod_je^{-(1-3\delta)\frac{L\kappa}{2049}\ell_1(Z_{0,j}')}\leqslant e^{L\kappa k'_i/2}e^{-(1-3\delta)\frac{L\kappa}{2049}\ell_1(Y'_i)}\;,
\end{equation*}
by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(ii), where $k'_i$ counts the fine components in $Y'_i$.

The remaining factors $t_0e^{L\kappa/2}e^{-\delta\kappa\ell_0(Z_{0,j})}$ pay for the sum over the set of fine components inside $Y'_i$: each contains an $M$-cube of $Y'_i$, of which there are $L^4N_1(Y'_i)$, so by \eqref{eq:native-source-animal-sum} the sum over single components is $x_i\leqslant L^4N_1(Y'_i)t_0e^{L\kappa/2}B(\delta\kappa)\leqslant \varepsilon_*\frac{\delta L\kappa}{2049}\ell_1(Y'_i)$, using $N_1\leqslant C_{\mathrm g}\ell_1$ and the definitions of $C_{\mathrm s}$ and $\varepsilon_*= C_{\mathrm s}t_0$, and the sum over nonempty sets is at most $e^{x_i}-1\leqslant x_ie^{x_i}$. Let $\Lambda_i\coloneqq\frac{L\kappa}{2049}\ell_1(Y'_i)$ and $y=\delta\Lambda_i$, so $x_i\leqslant \varepsilon_*y\leqslant y$. Then $x_ie^{x_i}e^{-(1-3\delta)\Lambda_i}\leqslant \varepsilon_*ye^{y}e^{-(1-3\delta)\Lambda_i}=\varepsilon_*ye^{-(1-4\delta)\Lambda_i}=\varepsilon_*(ye^{-y})e^{-(1-5\delta)\Lambda_i}\leqslant \varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda'\ell_1(Y'_i)}$, using $ye^{-y}\leqslant 1$, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-enlarged-domain-sum}
    \sum_{Z_0\, | \,Z_0'= Y'}\mathfrak M(Z_0,Z)\leqslant e^{-(\kappa_1-1)N_1(Z\setminus Y')+N_1(Z)}\prod_{Y'_i\in\operatorname{cc}(Y')}\varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda'\ell_1(Y'_i)}\;.
\end{equation}

\emph{Choice of $Y'$.} For nonempty $Y'\subseteq Z$ with $n'\coloneqq N_1(Z\setminus Y')$ cubes outside, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(iii) gives $\ell_1(Z)\leqslant \sum_i\ell_1(Y'_i)+5n'$, so $\prod_ie^{-\lambda'\ell_1(Y'_i)}\leqslant e^{-\lambda'\ell_1(Z)}e^{5\lambda'n'}$, and $\varepsilon_*^{\#\operatorname{cc}(Y')}\leqslant \varepsilon_*$. With $\kappa_1-1\geqslant 5\lambda'+1$,
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
    | k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(Z)|&\leqslant \varepsilon_*e^{N_1(Z)}e^{-\lambda'\ell_1(Z)}\sum_{\varnothing\ne Y'\subseteq Z}e^{-N_1(Z\setminus Y')}\\
    &\leqslant \varepsilon_*e^{(1+e^{-1})N_1(Z)}e^{-\lambda'\ell_1(Z)}\leqslant \varepsilon_*e^{-(\lambda'-2C_{\mathrm g})\ell_1(Z)}\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
which is the first inequality of \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-raw-activity-payment}.

\emph{Criterion.} Let $Z$ be any union of $LM$-cubes, connected or not. A domain $Z'$ incompatible with $Z$ contains one of the at most $9N_1(Z)$ cubes of $Z$ or wall adjacent to $Z$. Since $(1+6\theta)N_1(Z')\leqslant (1+6\theta)C_{\mathrm g}\ell_1(Z')\leqslant \frac{\lambda_*}{2}\ell_1(Z')$ by $C_{\mathrm g}\leqslant \lambda_*/8$ and $6\theta C_{\mathrm g}=3\lambda_*/8$, \eqref{eq:native-source-animal-sum} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:native-source-weighted-vacuum-criterion}
    \sum_{Z'\not\sim Z}| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(Z')| e^{(1+6\theta)N_1(Z')}\leqslant 9N_1(Z)\varepsilon_*B(\lambda_*/2)\leqslant \frac18N_1(Z)\;.
\end{equation}
The reference data are treated in Section~\ref{app:reference-check}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Proof of the Vacuum-Cluster Bounds}
\label{app:kp}

\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}]
Species are the connected final domains $D$, with weights $\widetilde z_D=| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)| e^{2\theta N_1(D)}$ and sizes $a(D)= N_1(D)/8$; two species are incompatible when they share a cube or a wall, and each with itself. By \eqref{eq:native-source-weighted-vacuum-criterion} and $2\theta+\frac18\leqslant 1+6\theta$,
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{D'\not\sim D}\widetilde z_{D'}e^{a(D')}\leqslant \sum_{D'\not\sim D}| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D')| e^{(1+6\theta)N_1(D')}\leqslant a(D)\;.
\end{equation*}

Tuples of species are written $\mathfrak c=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)$ in this proof ($\gamma$ is the spectral bound $\gamma_L/2$). The argument of Section~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} following \eqref{eq:marginal-pinned-bound} applies verbatim to these species, weights and sizes: the absolute Ursell coefficient $|\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)|$ is bounded by the number of spanning trees of the incompatibility graph of $\mathfrak c$, the rooted-tree generating sum with root $D$ is the monotone limit of the recursion \eqref{eq:marginal-pinned-recursion} with $\widetilde z$ in place of $|\widetilde z_p|$, the displayed criterion gives $T^{(k)}_D\leqslant \widetilde z_De^{a(D)}$ inductively, and the factor $1/m!$ in \eqref{eq:part1-vacuum-cluster} together with the multiplicity $m_D(\mathfrak c)$ of $D$ in the tuple reproduces the rooted sum. Hence, for every connected final domain $D$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c2-pinned-vacuum}
    \sum_{\mathfrak c}m_D(\mathfrak c)|\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)| e^{2\theta\sum_jN_1(D_j)}\leqslant | k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)| e^{2\theta N_1(D)+N_1(D)/8}\;.
\end{equation}
Here $\mathcal A$ is any finite set of unions of $LM$-cubes, connected or not; the criterion \eqref{eq:native-source-weighted-vacuum-criterion} was proved for every such union. A tuple hitting $\mathcal A$ contains a member $D'$ incompatible with some $D\in\mathcal A$, so
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
    \sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}|\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)| e^{2\theta\sum_jN_1(D_j)}
    &\leqslant \sum_{D\in\mathcal A}\sum_{D'\not\sim D}\sum_{\mathfrak c}m_{D'}(\mathfrak c)|\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)| e^{2\theta\sum_jN_1(D_j)}\\
    &\leqslant \sum_{D\in\mathcal A}\sum_{D'\not\sim D}| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D')| e^{(2\theta+\frac18)N_1(D')}\leqslant \frac18\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
For \eqref{eq:part1-joint-vacuum-exponential}, at fixed volume there are finitely many species. Let $\mathcal S_+$ be the set of species with $k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)\ne0$; species with $k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)=0$ contribute to neither side (a tuple containing one has $\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}=0$, and the gas does not see them), so they are discarded.

For complex activities $z=(z_D)_{D\in\mathcal S_+}$, the hard-core gas $\Xi(z)=\sum_{\mathcal P\text{ compatible}}\prod_{D\in\mathcal P}z_D$ is a polynomial with $\Xi(0)=1$: the polymer partition function (5.3) of \cite[Chapter~5]{FriedliVelenik} for the polymers $\mathcal S_+$ with the hard-core interaction $\zeta(D,D')=0$ on incompatible and $\zeta(D,D')=1$ on compatible pairs (which satisfies (5.1)--(5.2) there).

Let $S(z)=\sum_{\mathfrak c}\frac{\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)}{m!}\prod_jz_{D_j}$, the sum over all ordered tuples $\mathfrak c=(D_1,\ldots,D_m)$, $m\geqslant 1$, of members of $\mathcal S_+$; this is the cluster series of that gas, since the Ursell function of \cite[(5.6)]{FriedliVelenik} is $\frac1{m!}\sum_G\prod_{\{ i,j\}\in G}(\zeta(D_i,D_j)-1)=\frac{\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)}{m!}$, the sum over the connected graphs $G$ on $\{1,\ldots,m\}$, a factor $\zeta-1$ being $-1$ on an incompatible pair and $0$ otherwise.

\cite[Proposition~5.3]{FriedliVelenik} is the identity $\Xi(z)=\exp(S(z))$ between formal power series in the variables $z_D$ (its proof, (5.4)--(5.8) there, rearranges finitely many terms for each monomial).

By \eqref{eq:c2-pinned-vacuum} with $z_D$ in place of $k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)$ (the bound is monotone in the weights and only uses $| z_D|\leqslant | k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)|$ through the criterion; equivalently \cite[Theorem~5.4]{FriedliVelenik}, whose hypothesis (5.10) is the first display of this proof and whose conclusion (5.9) is this absolute convergence), $S$ converges absolutely at $| z_D|=| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)|$, hence absolutely and uniformly on the closed polydisc $\overline P=\{| z_D|\leqslant | k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)|\ \forall D\in\mathcal S_+\}$ (Weierstrass M-test), so $S$ is continuous on $\overline P$, analytic on the open polydisc $P$, and its Taylor series at $0$ is the formal series $S$ grouped by monomials.

The analytic functions $\Xi$ and $\exp\circ S$ on the connected open set $P\ni0$ have the same Taylor series at $0$, by the formal identity, so they coincide on $P$ (identity theorem) and, by continuity, on $\overline P$; in particular at $z_D= k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)$, where $\Xi(k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})=\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}$ and $S(k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})=\sum_{\mathfrak c}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)$ by \eqref{eq:part1-vacuum-cluster}.

The restricted gas $(\Xi^{\mathrm f}_{\xi})^{[\cup\mathcal A]}$ is the same gas with $z_D=0$ for the $D$ incompatible with $\bigcup\mathcal A$, which are exactly the $D$ incompatible with some member of $\mathcal A$; its expansion is the sum over the tuples none of whose members hits $\mathcal A$. The quotient is therefore $\exp(-\sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c))$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Reference Data}
\label{app:reference-check}

The reference data of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} consist of the identity background $U_1^{\circ}=\id$ on every bond (the constrained minimiser for identity averages, with zero action and zero gauge functional), $V_0^{\circ}=\id$, zero retained input $A^{\circ}_{\mathrm e}=0$ with $\Psi^{\circ}_{\xi}=\id$, and the same $I$, $\Omega_1$, partitions, hosts, cutoff radius $r$ and constants as the underlying branch. They are not a branch, so the conclusions of the lemmas are checked directly.

The reference Hessian is the regional Hessian \eqref{eq:c-regional-hessian} at the identity background on the branch's $\Omega_1$, $H^{\circ}_{\xi}=\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{\id}$, and $H^{\circ}$ denotes its restriction to $I$.

Since $I$, $\Omega_1$ and $R_{\mathrm c}$ are those of the branch, the geometric facts used in Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} (for $b\in I$ every site of a stencil $\mathcal S_{bb'}$ lies within $3L$ of $b_-$, hence within $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ and in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$, by Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range} and~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i)) hold for the reference data as well; Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} is stated for every background on which the regional form is defined, so it applies to the identity background.

\begin{lemma}[Reference Data]\label{lem:c2-reference}
The reference precision $H^{\circ}$ satisfies \eqref{eq:c-regular-two-sided}, as do its principal restrictions, and has the range and gauge law of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}; Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} holds for the reference data (at $U=\id$, $A_{\mathrm e}=0$); Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment} holds for $H^{\circ}$ with the same $\gamma,h_+,R,M,\alpha_G$; and \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-raw-activity-payment} and Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters} hold for the reference activities $k^{\mathrm f,\circ}_{\xi}$ with the same constants. The reference row solutions, phases and primitives are real, and the reference normalisations $K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}$, $I^{\circ}_{\xi;0}$ of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} are positive.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} with the identity background, the entries of $H^{\circ}$ with a label in $I$ are $f_{bb'}(0)$, the entries of the flat Hessian $\mathsf H$ of \eqref{eq:flat-covariance} on the branch's torus. The compression of $\mathsf H\geqslant \gamma_LI$ \eqref{eq:covariance-uniform-gap} to $I$, and further to any subset of $I$, gives the lower bound $\gamma_L\geqslant \gamma_L/2$ for $H^{\circ}$ and for every principal restriction, and the Schur bound with row sums $\sum_{b'}\| f_{bb'}(0)\|\leqslant m_L$ gives the upper bound for $H^{\circ}$ and every principal restriction (a principal restriction has smaller row sums); the range is $\rho_L$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}.

The gauge law of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality} is the entrywise covariance \eqref{eq:c-entry-gauge-covariance}, proved there for every background, hence for $\id$: $f_{bb'}(\id^u)=\mathrm{Ad}_{u(b_-)}f_{bb'}(\id)\mathrm{Ad}^{-1}_{u(b'_-)}$.

Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment} and Lemmas~\ref{lem:walk-series}, \ref{lem:conditioning}, \ref{lem:component-blocks} use only \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-inputs}, the range and the partitions, so they hold for $H^{\circ}$.

Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} applies to the identity background (its hypothesis, a site gauge with phases at most $\tau_L/2$ on the two-block sets and blocks concerned, is satisfied by $u=\id$, $\phi=0$; the geometric facts of the applicability paragraph depend only on $I$, $\Omega_1$, $R_{\mathrm c}$), so Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} holds at $U=\id$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} holds with $r_{\mathrm e}^{\circ}=0$ and $s^{\circ}=1+r\leqslant s_{\xi}$; the hosts and the host multiplicity are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-potential-size}, so \eqref{eq:native-source-interaction-size} holds for $\mathbf V^{\circ}_{\xi}$. The proofs of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-selected-majorant}, \ref{lem:activity-bounds} and~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters} use nothing else about the branch.

Reality: the row solutions are the limits of the contraction iterates of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii), which are real for real phases, so for real inputs the phases, the Haar logarithms, the determinant logarithms (positive determinants) and the plaquette and gauge terms are real, and so are the primitives and $\mathbf V^{\circ}_{\xi}$.

Positivity: $K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_I}\exp(-\frac12\langle a,H^{\circ} a\rangle+P^{\circ}_{\xi,0}(a))$, the function \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation} for the reference data at $t=0$, is a real exponential on the open box, the reference primitives being real, hence positive there; and $I^{\circ}_{\xi;0}=\int K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}\,\dd a$ is positive and finite ($H^{\circ}\geqslant \gamma$ and the exponent is bounded on the box by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}).
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Thresholds}
\label{app:thresholds}

Before the coupling, in this order:
\begin{itemize}
\item $L>11$ odd (\cite[p.~251]{BalabanRG1}, the range in which Ba{\l}aban's results are stated);
\item the group constants $c_{\mathrm h}=\sqrt N$, $c_{\mathrm n}=1/N$, $\varrho_G=\pi/\sqrt N$, $c$, $r_G$, $c_G$, and $r_M,r'_M$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}; these two depend on $L$ and the group);
\item $\tau_L$ by \eqref{eq:c2-tau-final}, with $m_L$, $c_L$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}) and $\gamma_L$ (Appendix~\ref{app:flat-covariance});
\item $R_{\mathrm{loc}}=2L+2$, $R_{\mathrm p}$, $s_{\mathfrak P}$, $R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant \max(2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1,s_{\mathfrak P}+2,4L+5)$ and $C_{L,R_{\mathrm c}}$;
\item the two-block size $n_{\mathcal E}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness} (a constant of $L$);
\item the ranges $R_*$ and $R_H$ of Section~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} (the perimeter range bounding the primitive-label diameters and the source-to-stencil distances, distinct from the walk range $R_*= n_*R$ below, and the range of the flat Hessian, whose entries couple the bonds of a common plaquette or block; both are constants of $L$), hence $R_0=4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$;
\item $\vartheta_*\leqslant \tau_L/2$, $\rho_{\mathrm d}=2K_*\vartheta_*^2$, $C_{\mathsf C}$, $C_{\mathsf D}$, $C^{\mathrm a}_k$ ($0\leqslant k\leqslant 5$) and $C^{\mathsf D}_k$ ($0\leqslant k\leqslant 6$) of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} and $C_{\mathrm p}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds};
\item $\gamma=\gamma_L/2$, $h_+= m_L$, $R$;
\item $C_{\mathrm g}$, $\delta$, $\kappa$, $\lambda'$, $\lambda_*$, $\alpha_6$, $\kappa_1$, $\theta$, $C_{\mathrm s}$ by \eqref{eq:c2-kappa-choice}--\eqref{eq:c2-mayer-constants}, then $\omega_*$, $\eta_*$, $\varepsilon_*$, $t_0$ by \eqref{eq:native-source-vacuum-KP-budget}, with $\omega_*\leqslant 1/2$ (used in Appendix~\ref{app:signed-defects}) (these involve only $\kappa$, $\alpha_6$, $C_{\mathrm s}$, $\lambda_*$, so they are fixed before $M_1$ and $M$, as Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds} states);
\item $n_*$, $R_*$, $C_{\mathrm w}$ (Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}), $A_*$, $C_{\mathrm d}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment});
\item $M_1$ as the $M_1$ of \cite[p.~245]{BalabanCRE}, $M_2$ and $M$ odd powers of $L$ with $M_1< M_2< M$, $M/M_1$ integral, $M\geqslant 8LM_2$, the requirement of \cite[p.~245]{BalabanCRE} that $M$ be large, $\rho_{\mathrm w}= R_*+R+1+2M_1$, \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-collar-size}, $\delta_M\leqslant 1$, $h_+^2\delta_M^2/\gamma\leqslant 1/8$ and $4C_{\mathrm d}\delta_M^2(LM+1)^4\leqslant 1/2$;
\item $\alpha_G$ with $0<\alpha_G\leqslant \min(\gamma/2,\gamma^2/(16A_*^2),(8C_{\mathrm d}(LM+1)^4)^{-1})$, $\gamma_2=\alpha_G/2$;
\item then $N_{\mathrm h}$ and $C_0$ of \eqref{eq:part1-host-multiplicity}, whose hosts depend on the chosen $M$;
\item then the constants of the signed-defect estimates (Appendix~\ref{app:signed-defects}, where they are introduced), in this order: the character constant $K_{\chi}$, the dummy weight $u_*$ of the host comparison, the support reserve $\eta$ of the positive group summation, its pin constant $C_{\mathrm{pin}}$, and the constant $C_M$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1}, all fixed before the coupling, each depending on $L$, $M$, $\kappa$, $\omega_*$, the group, the character and the constants earlier in this order only.
\end{itemize}

Then the constant $\beta_0$ of \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} (p.255; the coupling is then taken small enough for (2.6) to hold with it), the mean radius $\rho_{\mathrm{av}}$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-4}, the constants $C_{L,G}$, $c_{L,G}$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}, and $C_{\mathrm H}$, $c_{\mathrm H}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}, which depend only on $L$, the group, $M_1$, $M_2$, and the constants of \cite{BalabanCRE} and \cite{BalabanVAR}.

The coupling $g_0$ is then taken below a threshold, and the torus is chosen last: every fine period a multiple of $LMR_1$ and at least $8M$ (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}; the partitions of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} need a multiple of $LM$, the hosts of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} need $8M$, and the partitions of \cite{BalabanCRE} into $LMR_1$-cubes need the multiple of $LMR_1$; $R_1= R_1(g_0)$, so the period condition is imposed after the coupling) and every coarse period exceeding $\max(2,2R_{\mathrm p}+8)$.

The statements about a square $C_n$ of side $nL$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}, Appendices~\ref{app:signed-defects} and~\ref{app:regional-scalar}, Section~\ref{sec:leading-moment}) assume in addition the square/torus geometry of Section~\ref{sec:extent-weights}: every coarse period $K_{\mu}\geqslant 3(n+2)$, so that the square and its fixed neighbourhood have unique lifts and the loop is contractible; and Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard} (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}) and Section~\ref{sec:leading-moment} assume compatible even fine periods. These are lower bounds on the periods in terms of the fixed loop and the coupling; for a given loop and coupling they hold on every sufficiently large compatible torus.

In the threshold conditions, $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ with $g_1= g_1(g_0)$ by \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE}; $R_1$ is that of \cite{BalabanCRE}, the smallest power of $L$ with $R_1\geqslant (\log g_1^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$ (p.246, with Ba{\l}aban's exponent written $\mathfrak r$; $\mathfrak r\geqslant 2$ at p.245, $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r$ at p.246, and \cite[(2.5)]{BalabanCRE} for the general step); and the cutoff radius is $r= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$, the radius of the literal cutoff \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}; it is $\delta_0/g_0$ for the $\delta_k= g_kA_1/A_0\,p_0(g_k)$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} as printed at p.265, which identifies $\Theta_{\xi}$ with the test (1.18) (the first member of the equality chain printed for $\delta_0$ at p.247 is corrected in (H4)). The threshold conditions are:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $LMR_1>4R_{\mathrm c}+4L^2M_2R_1+8$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}), $LM_2R_1\geqslant M$ (so that the $LM$-cubes nest in the $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes, \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}) and $4\,O(1)B_3L^2e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}\leqslant 1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation}); both depend on the coupling through $R_1$;
\item \eqref{eq:convex-background-thresholds}, the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, which \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} lists as well;
\item $4C_{\mathsf C}g_0(1+2r)\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds});
\item the activity budgets of Section~\ref{app:mayer-constants}: $\omega(g_0)= C_0g_0(1+r)^3\leqslant \omega_*$ \eqref{eq:part1-host-multiplicity} and \eqref{eq:native-source-bad-budget} with $a_{\mathrm{bad}}\coloneqq c_{\mathrm n}\alpha_Gr^2/4$;
\item Ba{\l}aban's own conditions in \cite{BalabanCRE}, taken over as they stand:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\varepsilon_0$ small (Theorem 1 of \cite{BalabanVAR}, reference [15] of \cite{BalabanCRE}, behind (B1); and, the constants $O(L^2)$ of p.247 and $O(1)$ of \cite[p.~25]{BalabanAVG} being independent of the coupling ((B1), (H4)), so small that $2\,O(L^2)\varepsilon_0$ and $O(1)L^2\varepsilon_0$ lie below $\varrho_G$, $r_G/\sqrt N$, and the small-diameter radius of the group mean, the domain statement of (B1));
\item $MR_1$ large (p.251, the bound on $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ at the tolerance $\delta_0/40$ of \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs}, behind the change of variables (1.22), Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection}: by Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} it is the condition $\frac\pi2LC_{\mathrm H}(1+\beta_0)(A_0/A_1)e^{-c_{\mathrm H}LMR_1}\leqslant \frac1{40}$, with $C_{\mathrm H}$ and $c_{\mathrm H}$ fixed before $g_0$, together with the conditions of that lemma's threshold);
\item $A_0/A_1$ and $M_2R_1$ large (the two qualitative conditions of (B3), pp.248 and 250; the second requires $O(1)B_3e^{-\delta_{\mathrm c}LM_2R_1}\varepsilon_1$ to be much smaller than $\delta_0$, and $\varepsilon_1/\delta_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)A_0/A_1$ stays bounded by \cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE} and $\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$, so $R_1\to\infty$ at fixed $L$, $M_2$ suffices, the constants being independent of the coupling by (B3)(iii)).
\end{itemize}
The conditions on $MR_1$ and $M_2R_1$ depend on the coupling through $R_1$ and are met for small $g_0$ at fixed $M$, $M_2$, since $R_1\to\infty$; the condition on $A_0/A_1$ is met by the choice before the coupling; Ba{\l}aban's conditions on $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$ themselves are not listed in \cite{BalabanCRE} (p.245: $M_1$ the cube size of the previous papers, $M_2$ not too much larger, $M$ much larger than $M_2$, ``dictated by many conditions involving this constant'') and are taken over as the hypothesis that the construction of \cite{BalabanCRE} is valid for the values chosen above, which follow its prescription.
\item the fibre conditions \eqref{eq:c2-fibre-thresholds} of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-fibre-smallness}: $3c_Gc_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_0\leqslant \tau_L/2$ (which gives $3c_{\mathrm h}s_{\mathfrak P}\varepsilon_0\leqslant r_G$, by $\tau_L\leqslant 2c_Gr_G$) and $n_{\mathcal E}^{1/2}c_Gc_{\mathrm h}\,2\,O(L^2)\varepsilon_0\leqslant \vartheta_*/4$, with $n_{\mathcal E}$ the largest number of bonds of a two-block set and $O(L^2)$ the constant of p.247 of item 5.
\end{enumerate}
All hold for small $g_0$; for item 4 because $a_{\mathrm{bad}}\to\infty$ and $g_0(1+r)^3\to0$, and for item 6 because $\varepsilon_0= g_0A_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}\to0$ while its other constants are fixed before the coupling, $O(L^2)$ being independent of the coupling and of the branch by \cite[Lemma~1, p.~79]{BalabanREG} ((B1), (H4)).

The first-step coupling is defined by \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE}, $g_0^{-2}= g_1^{-2}+\beta_1(g_0)$, and \cite[(2.6), p.~255]{BalabanCRE} (with $n=1$, $m=0$) states $g_1\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_0$ and $g_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)g_1$, where $\beta_0>0$ is a constant that "can be chosen arbitrarily small, if $g$ is sufficiently small" (p.255); \cite{BalabanCRE} derives (2.6) from the renormalisation group equations (0.20) of [I] and the properties of the $\beta$-functions (p.255). Hence $g_1\to0$ with $g_0$, so $R_1\to\infty$; and \cite[(2.8), p.~256]{BalabanCRE} (with $n=1$, $m=0$) gives $\varepsilon_1\leqslant (1+\beta_0)\varepsilon_0$, so $\varepsilon_1= g_1A_0(\log g_1^{-2})^{p_0}\to0$ with $\varepsilon_0= g_0A_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$; while $r\to\infty$ and $g_0(1+r)^3\to0$. (The $p_0$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} denotes both the function $p_0(g)= A_0(\log g^{-2})^{p_0}$ and the integer exponent in it.)

The threshold depends on $L$, the group (through $c_{\mathrm h}$, $c_{\mathrm n}$, $\varrho_G$, $c$, $r_G$, $c_G$, $r_M$, $d_G$), the choices $\tau_L$, $\vartheta_*$, $R_{\mathrm c}$, $\kappa$, $\alpha_G$, $\omega_*$ made above, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$, and, through $\varepsilon_1$, $R_1$ and $r$, on the constants $A_0$, $A_1$, $p_0$, $\mathfrak r$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}, the map $g_0\mapsto g_1$ of \cite[(1.27)]{BalabanCRE}, the constants $B_3$, $\delta_{\mathrm c}$ and the $O(1)$ of the comparison after (1.19) (p.268; Ba{\l}aban's constants of (B3)(iii) and (H4)), the threshold $\varepsilon_0$ of Theorem 1 of \cite{BalabanVAR} (reference [15] of \cite{BalabanCRE}) behind (B1), the constant $O(L^2)$ of p.247 (items 5 and 6), the constants $C_{\mathrm H}$ and $c_{\mathrm H}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field} behind (B4)(ii), and the tolerances ``much smaller than $\delta_0$'' of p.250 behind (B3)(ii).

Further conditions are imposed where the appendices and Section~\ref{sec:leading-moment} state them; each is a condition that $g_0$ lie below a threshold depending on $L$, the group, the character, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$, the constants chosen above and those of \cite{BalabanCRE}, holding for all small $g_0$, or a lower bound on the periods in terms of the loop and the coupling, holding on every sufficiently large compatible torus. They are:
\begin{itemize}
\item $\delta_0\leqslant \delta_G$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection});
\item \eqref{eq:c3-1-2} ($r\geqslant 1$ and $C_Pg_0(1+2r)\leqslant \gamma/2$, Section~\ref{sec:c3-1});
\item the threshold $g_*$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}, which contains the threshold of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}, the coupling conditions of \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} and the smallness giving $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7});
\item the thresholds of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1} (its last inequality), the smallness conditions of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-2} on the root weight and the smallness of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-3} (Appendix~\ref{app:signed-defects}, Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3});
\item the further threshold of \eqref{eq:c5-7-expbound-I} (Corollary~\ref{cor:leading-moment});
\item the thresholds of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-seed}, \ref{lem:c3-7-2} and~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} (Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}; every condition there is an upper bound on the witness threshold $\theta$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-4} or a lower bound on $R_1$);
\item the collar conditions \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes}, which are item 1 with $R_0=4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$ in place of $R_{\mathrm c}$, the small-coupling conditions $g_0C_{\mathsf C}(2+4r)<\vartheta_*/2$ and $g_0(2+4r)< a_L$ with the polymer-load inequalities of the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}, and the torus condition $4ne^{-c\iota_T}\leqslant 1$ of Corollary~\ref{cor:refined-split};
\item the coupling conditions of the flat and regional expansions where they are imposed ($\tau<1$, the original chart condition, the smallness of $K_1^{s_*}\tau$ and the straight- and bent-path thresholds of Sections~\ref{sec:marginal-perimeter} and~\ref{sec:marginal-corner}, and the threshold of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-coefficient});
\item $R_{\Upsilon}\geqslant 2$, $u\leqslant u_*$, $v\leqslant 1$ and the small-coupling conditions of Sections~\ref{sec:c4-10-1} and~\ref{sec:c4-11-5} (Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3});
\item the further threshold of Corollary~\ref{cor:main-factorisation} ($C\tau^2L^4C_K\Phi_c\leqslant 1$ and the bound on $\delta^{\sharp}_q$),
\end{itemize}
each stated at the place cited.

\section{The Local Interaction at the Identity}
\label{sec:perimeter-attempt}

\paragraph{Locality of the First-Step Interaction.}
The trace in the bare action is $\tr_N= N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}$ in its fixed unitary embedding, so $\tr_N(\id)=1$. Let $a_{\mathrm{ph}}$ be a radius for the input $A$ of $\widetilde D$, measured in the maximum fine-bond Hilbert--Schmidt norm, on which the local implicit solutions, principal logarithms and composed action and Haar primitives are analytic, with nonzero Jacobian determinants and Haar densities.

The radius $a_L$ is a free-input radius with $a_L\leqslant a_{\mathrm{ph}}/\max(1,\|\mathsf C\|_{\infty\to\infty})$, where the operator norm maps the maximum free-bond Hilbert--Schmidt norm to the maximum fine-bond Hilbert--Schmidt norm. This norm is finite and depends on $L$ only, by the fixed row stencils. The Lie-algebra norm is the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm, and $| A|_{\mathrm{HS}}\leqslant | A|_{\mathrm{op}}$. Thus $c_{\mathrm{cmp}}=1$ is a common norm-comparison constant for both cutoff prescriptions, and $g_0r(g_0)< a_L$ suffices.

The componentwise implicit solutions assemble to a small solution in this maximum norm. Uniqueness of the analytic germ in \cite{BalabanRG1} identifies it with $\widetilde D$ on the smaller common chart.

The following calculation concerns the identity-background, all-regular integral below.

Let $\mathcal S_c$ contain the positive fine bonds with both endpoints in $\mathcal B_{c_-}\cup\mathcal B_{c_+}$, and let $\Lambda_c\coloneqq\mathcal S_c\cap E_*$. At the present torus sizes, the only designated bond in $\mathcal S_c$ is $b_0(c)$. Indeed, an internal path in either block crosses no block interface, and the translated length-$L$ path in \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} crosses only the interface between these two blocks. The reference coarse path crosses the same interface. Thus $\mathcal Q_c$ and $\mathcal N_c$ depend only on the fine bonds in $\mathcal S_c$. In the defining equation for $\widetilde D_c(A)$, the only unknown correction entering those bonds is $\widetilde D_c(A)$ itself. The analytic implicit-function theorem therefore gives a function of $A|_{\mathcal S_c}$ alone, with its radius and constants independent of the number of blocks. Here $h_c= L^3I$ at the identity, since $Q_0= L^{-4}I$.

For a free fine bond $b$, let $\Lambda_b\coloneqq\{ b\}$; for a designated bond $b= b_0(c)$, let $\Lambda_b\coloneqq\Lambda_c$. Both $(\mathsf CB)(b)$ and $q_{g_0}(B)(b)$ depend only on $B|_{\Lambda_b}$.

The index $\alpha$ runs over the plaquettes and the pairs $(y,x)$ in \eqref{eq:action-primitive}. Let $f_{\alpha}(q)$ be the corresponding summand of $\mathscr A(e^{iq})$, a real analytic scalar function near zero in $\mathfrak g^E$, extended holomorphically to complex arguments. Let $\Lambda_{\alpha}$ be the union of the sets $\Lambda_b$ over the bonds in that summand's plaquette or path family. Each $\Lambda_{\alpha}$ lies in at most four adjacent blocks. Each free bond belongs to a bounded number of the sets $\Lambda_{\alpha},\Lambda_b,\Lambda_c$, with a bound depending on $L$, not on the torus.

Let $\psi(A)\coloneqq A-h\widetilde D(A)$. The local scalar functions are the real analytic branches at zero of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:perimeter-literal-local-terms}
    \begin{aligned}
        v_{\alpha}(B)&=-\frac{1}{g_0^2}
            \left(f_{\alpha}(\psi(g_0\mathsf CB))
                -\frac{g_0^2}{2}
                    D^2f_{\alpha}(0)[\mathsf CB,\mathsf CB]\right)\;,\\
        j_b(B)&=\log j_H(q_{g_0}(B)(b))\;,\\
        d_c(B)&=\log\det_{\mathfrak g}
            \left(I-L^3\partial_{A(b_0(c))}
                \widetilde D_c(g_0\mathsf CB)\right)\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Their supports are respectively $\Lambda_{\alpha},\Lambda_b,\Lambda_c$. The full fine Jacobian is block triangular: its nonidentity rows are designated rows, and its designated-to-designated block is diagonal in $c$. Its determinant is consequently the product of the determinants in $d_c$. Each real determinant is positive in the chart connected to zero, so this branch agrees with the absolute determinant in \eqref{eq:literal-residual}. Summing the action Hessians gives $\mathsf H$, and hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:perimeter-literal-local-sum}
    \mathcal P_{g_0}(B)
        =\sum_{\alpha} v_{\alpha}(B)+\sum_{b\in E}j_b(B)
            +\sum_{c\in E_1}d_c(B)\;.
\end{equation}


There is no linear term in either $j_b$ or $d_c$. Haar density in exponential variables has zero derivative at zero. For $d_c$, the quadratic part of $\widetilde D_c$ is the quadratic part of $\mathcal N_c$. Expanding \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} to degree two gives a linear combination of Lie brackets of the bond variables. Differentiating with respect to the designated variable gives a linear combination of adjoint maps. Their traces vanish for a compact Lie algebra. Multiplication by the scalar $L^3$ does not change this conclusion. Each $f_{\alpha}$ and its first derivative vanish at zero, and $\psi(A)= A+O(A^2)$, so the subtracted action term begins at degree three.

In the positive Lie-algebra scalar-product norm, there are constants $a_L,C_L^{\mathrm{loc}}>0$, depending on $L,G$ and the fixed averaging prescription, such that, on the complex polydisc $g_0\max_b\| B(b)\|< a_L$, each term $v$ of \eqref{eq:perimeter-literal-local-sum}, with its indicated support $\Lambda$, satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:perimeter-literal-local-bound}
    | v(B)|\leqslant C_L^{\mathrm{loc}}
        \left(g_0\max_{b\in\Lambda}\| B(b)\|+g_0^2\right)
        \sum_{b\in\Lambda}\| B(b)\|^2\;.
\end{equation}
On a fixed smaller complex chart for the finitely many local templates, their convergent Taylor series and the vanishing orders just proved give a cubic remainder divided by $g_0^2$ for $v_{\alpha}$ and quadratic remainders for $j_b,d_c$. Equivalence of the finite-dimensional local maximum and Euclidean norms gives the displayed inequality. The bounded overlap then yields a torus-independent quadratic majorant on the cutoff. If $c_{\mathrm{cmp}}$ is the fixed norm-equivalence constant from the bond norm of \cite{BalabanCRE} to this norm (the constant of the preceding paragraph), then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:perimeter-literal-total-reserve}
    \sum_{\alpha}| v_{\alpha}(B)|+\sum_b| j_b(B)|+\sum_c| d_c(B)|
        \leqslant C_L^{\mathrm{ov}}
            (c_{\mathrm{cmp}}g_0r(g_0)+g_0^2)\| B\|^2\;.
\end{equation}
The constant $C_L^{\mathrm{ov}}$ includes the bounded overlap and is independent of the torus.

The local scalars are evaluated in the identity-background frame and are invariant under simultaneous constant colour conjugation. This follows from equivariance of the logarithm, averages, and implicit correction of \cite{BalabanRG1}, cyclicity of the action traces, and conjugation invariance of Haar density and determinants.

Their extension to the gauge orbit of this background is unambiguous: if $U^u_0(b)= u(b_-)u(b_+)^{-1}$ and $A^u(b)= u(b_-)A(b)u(b_-)^{-1}$, the transported scalar at $(U^u_0,A^u)$ is its identity-frame value at $A$. Two choices of $u$ representing the same background differ by a constant right factor on the connected torus, and give the same scalar by the stated constant-conjugation invariance.

\section{The Exterior Response and Its History Average}\label{app:exterior-chessboard}
This appendix bounds the exterior response $\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]$ of \eqref{eq:c-exterior-response} on every branch (Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound}, Section~\ref{sec:c3-5}), and pays its history average, together with the uncovered branches of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}, by one-point witness probabilities on compatible even fine periods (Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}, Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}). Section~\ref{sec:c3-9} proves the deterministic comparison of the two minima used by the witness argument and, by the same argument, the bound on the boundary field of \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE} used in Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar} (Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}). The inputs are the Hessian, Schur, chart and primitive bounds of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} and the collar statements of Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}; Remark~\ref{rem:c3-8-1} records the scope of these bounds.

\subsection{Objects and the Conditional Law}\label{sec:c3-1}
Let $\xi$ be the data of a branch (Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}): the integration carrier $I$, the retained free carrier $J$, the exterior field $A_{\mathrm e}\in\mathfrak g^J$, extended by zero on every other free bond, the reconstructed field $U_{\xi}(a)$ of \eqref{eq:c-reconstructed-field}, and the cutoff norm $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ (the bond norm $|\bigcdot |$ of \eqref{eq:literal-cutoff}, operator or normalised Hilbert--Schmidt, fixed once). The inner product $\langle\bigcdot ,\bigcdot \rangle$, the norm $h$ and the product Hilbert norms are those of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}; $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ for both permitted norms. The cutoff radius is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-1-1}
    r\coloneqq\delta_0/g_0=(A_1/A_0)\,p_0(g_0)= A_1(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}\;,
\end{equation}
(the first-step cutoff normalisation \eqref{eq:cre-cutoff-normalisation}, in which $p_0$ denotes both the function $p_0(g)= A_0(\log g^{-2})^{p_0}$ and its exponent, as in \cite{BalabanCRE}), so $r\to\infty$ and $g_0r=\delta_0\to0$ as $g_0\to0$.

Every derivative, overlap, range and Hessian constant below is independent of $g_0$ once $L$, the group, the character and the source constants are fixed; the two conditions
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-1-2}
    r\geqslant 1\qquad\text{and}\qquad C_Pg_0(1+2r)\leqslant \gamma/2\;,
\end{equation}
with $C_P$ the constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1} as enlarged in Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2} (fixed there independently of $g_0$; \eqref{eq:c3-1-2} is imposed with the enlarged constant) and $\gamma=\gamma_L/2$, therefore hold for all $g_0$ below a threshold (the exponent $p_0$ is positive, $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r$ by Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, so $r\to\infty$ while $g_0r\to0$), and they are assumed throughout this appendix, together with the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} and the coupling thresholds of Section~\ref{app:thresholds} under which Lemmas~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, \ref{lem:collar-coverage} and~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} hold (in particular threshold item 3 there, $4C_{\mathsf C}g_0(1+2r)\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$).

If $I=\varnothing$ then $F_{\xi}(1)= F_{\xi}(0)$ (\eqref{eq:convex-response-operands}) and the response \eqref{eq:c-exterior-response} is zero; below $I\neq\varnothing$.

Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-1-3}
    H\coloneqq H_{\xi,II},\qquad \ell_{\xi}\coloneqq H_{\xi,IJ}A_{\mathrm e},\qquad j_{\xi}(a)\coloneqq\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle,\qquad s_{\xi}\coloneqq 1+r+r_{\mathrm e,\xi}\leqslant 1+2r\;,
\end{equation}
with $r_{\mathrm e,\xi}< r$ the retained radius \eqref{eq:convex-native-radius}, the maximum of $| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|_{\sigma}$ over the retained bonds within $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ (zero if there is none). Every retained input entering $H_{\xi,IJ}$ or a near primitive lies in this collar (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}(i)).

The collar bound holds on every branch, independently of contour coverage: by Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(i) every retained bond within $3R_{\mathrm c}$ of $I$ lies in $\mathcal G_{\xi}\setminus S_1^*$ ($\mathcal G_{\xi}$ the union of the good test carriers, \eqref{eq:c-good-region}), its factor in $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}$ is $\mathbf 1\{|\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})(b)|< r\}$ (\eqref{eq:retained-cutoff-composition}) and $\Psi_{\xi}$, the identity off $S_1^*$ (\eqref{eq:native-source-exact-boundary-map}), is the identity there, so a nonzero retained weight forces $| A_{\mathrm e}(b)|< r$; this is Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(iii).

On the open box $\mathcal D_I=\{ a\in\mathfrak g^I\, | \,| a_b|_{\sigma}< r\ \forall b\in I\}$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation} the interpolating law of that display, which at $t=1$ is the conditional law of the branch (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}(ii)), is, exactly, for $t\in[0,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-1-4}
    \dd\nu_{\xi;t}(a)= I_{\xi;t}^{-1}e^{\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}(a)}\,\dd a\;,\qquad
    \mathsf Q_{\xi,t}(a)=-\tfrac12\langle a,Ha\rangle-t\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle+P_{\xi,t}(a)\;,
\end{equation}
zero off $\mathcal D_I$ (the indicator in \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation}), with $\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}$ as in \eqref{eq:native-collar-flux}; $I_{\xi;t}$ is the normaliser of \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation}, and $\dd a$ is the product Lebesgue measure of the fixed inner product.

Throughout $f_{\xi}(a)= W_{\chi}(C;U_{\xi}(a))$ (\eqref{eq:convex-response-operands}) with the exterior data fixed at their branch values, defined where $U_{\xi}(a)$ is (Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}), which includes $\mathcal D_I$, and extended by zero elsewhere (immaterial below, since $\nu_{\xi;t}$ vanishes off $\mathcal D_I$); it is bounded by one, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-1-5}
    L_{\xi,t}=-j_{\xi}+\partial_tP_{\xi,t}\;,\qquad
    \mathcal B_{\xi}[f]=\int_0^1\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f,L_{\xi,t})\,\dd t
\end{equation}
(Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-response}); $L_{\xi,t}=\partial_t\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}$ is called the score below.

Derivatives and operator norms refer to the product Hilbert structure, complexified for complex scalar gradients; the fixed matrix-norm equivalence factors of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} are absorbed into the constants before $g_0$ is chosen.

The inputs are Lemmas~\ref{lem:regular-bounds} and~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} under their stated hypotheses (in force by the preceding paragraph): $\gamma\,\id\leqslant H\leqslant m_L\,\id$ with $\gamma=\gamma_L/2$; finite interaction range; and bounded local first and second derivatives of the near primitives on the enlarged box $| a_b|_{\sigma}\leqslant 2r$ at the inputs $a+tA_{\mathrm e}$, $t\in[0,1]$. They are used at the background $U_1$ of the branch.

\subsection{Local Derivative Bounds}\label{sec:c3-2}
Let $S_{\alpha}$ be the full free-input stencil, retained inputs included, of a near primitive $\mathfrak p_{\alpha}$ (the $p_{\alpha}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}), let $N_{\mathrm{in}}$ bound its size and $N_{\mathrm{ov}}$ the number of primitive stencils meeting any free bond; both are fixed by $L$ and the group.

The distance $d(b,b')$ of two bonds is the periodic $\ell^{\infty}$ distance of their initial sites, plus one for differing directions (the sum of two pseudometrics; a metric, because a positive bond is determined by its initial site and its direction); $d(b,S)=\inf_{b'\in S}d(b,b')$ for a bond set $S$, with $d(b,\varnothing)=+\infty$, and this $d$ is the only bond distance used in this appendix.

Let $R=8L+8$, a range dominating in this metric every near-primitive stencil diameter (at most $4L+1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}, $R_{\mathrm{loc}}=2L+2$) and the Hessian range (at most $\rho_L+1=4L+1$ in this metric, $\rho_L=4L$ being the $\ell^{\infty}$ range of the initial sites of the nonzero entries of $H_{\xi}$: Lemmas~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range} and~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}). Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-2-1}
    \mathsf K_{\xi}\coloneqq\{ b\in I\, : \,d(b,J)\leqslant R\}\;,\qquad
    I_C\coloneqq\{ b\in I\, : \,b\in\mathcal F_r\text{ for some traversal }r\text{ of }C\}\;,
\end{equation}
with $\mathcal F_r$ the free-input stencil \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-extension-support} of the contour bond $r$ (a traversal bond, as in Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives}; the letter $r$ denotes a traversal bond only inside \eqref{eq:c3-2-1} and in the stencils $\mathcal F_r$, and the cutoff radius $r$ of \eqref{eq:c3-1-1} everywhere else); the source depends on the integration field only through $I_C$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}).

\begin{lemma}[Local Bounds]\label{lem:c3-2-1}
There are constants $C_P$, $C_S$ (depending on $L$ and the group only) and $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$ (depending on $L$, the group, the character and the maximal multiplicity with which $C$ traverses a link only, the latter $1$ for the square $C_n$) such that on the enlarged box $\{| a_b|_{\sigma}\leqslant 2r\ \forall b\in I\}$, uniformly in $t\in[0,1]$ and in the branch (the fourth bound on every covered branch, Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}),
\begin{gather}
    \| D^2_aP_{\xi,t}\|\leqslant C_Pg_0s_{\xi}\;,\qquad
    h(\nabla_b\partial_tP_{\xi,t})\leqslant C_Sg_0s_{\xi}\,r_{\mathrm e,\xi}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf K_{\xi}}(b)\;,\qquad
    h((\ell_{\xi})_b)\leqslant m_Lr_{\mathrm e,\xi}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf K_{\xi}}(b)\;,\label{eq:c3-2-2}\\
    \sup_a h(\nabla_bf_{\xi}(a))\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}g_0\mathbf 1_{I_C}(b)\;.\label{eq:c3-2-3}
\end{gather}
Under \eqref{eq:c3-1-2} the function $-\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}$ is strongly convex on $\mathcal D_I$ with Hessian at least $\rho=\gamma/2$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first bound of \eqref{eq:c3-2-2} is the second-derivative bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} on the enlarged box with the finite overlap $N_{\mathrm{ov}}$.

For the second, $\partial_tP_{\xi,t}(a)=\sum_{\alpha} D\mathfrak p_{\alpha}(a+tA_{\mathrm e})[A_{\mathrm e}]$ (by \eqref{eq:native-source-boundary-interpolation}, $P_{\xi,t}$ has no other $t$-dependence), so each summand of $\nabla_b\partial_tP_{\xi,t}$ is $D^2\mathfrak p_{\alpha}$, the full second derivative on $\mathfrak g^{S_{\alpha}}$ (retained inputs included) bounded by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}, applied to a direction at $b\in I$ and to $A_{\mathrm e}|_{S_{\alpha}}$; it vanishes unless $S_{\alpha}$ contains a retained input, which lies in the collar (stencil diameter at most $4L+1<3R_{\mathrm c}$), so $h(A_{\mathrm e}(b'))\leqslant | A_{\mathrm e}(b')|_{\sigma}\leqslant r_{\mathrm e,\xi}$ for each such input ($h\leqslant |\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ for both permitted norms, Section~\ref{sec:c3-1}) and $h(A_{\mathrm e}|_{S_{\alpha}})\leqslant \sqrt{N_{\mathrm{in}}}\,r_{\mathrm e,\xi}$, and summing the at most $N_{\mathrm{ov}}$ stencils meeting $b$ gives the bound; the support statement follows from the range $R$ of the stencils.

The third bound is the row-sum bound $\sum_{b'\in\Omega_1^*}\|(H_{\xi})_{bb'}\|\leqslant m_L$ for the rows $b\in I$, the row-sum statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, applied to $A_{\mathrm e}$ on the collar: $(H_{\xi,IJ})_{bb'}=0$ unless the initial sites are within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $\rho_L$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}), so a nonzero entry has $d(b',I)\leqslant \rho_L+1=4L+1<3R_{\mathrm c}$ ($R_{\mathrm c}\geqslant 2R_{\mathrm{loc}}+1=4L+5$) and $h(A_{\mathrm e}(b'))\leqslant | A_{\mathrm e}(b')|_{\sigma}\leqslant r_{\mathrm e,\xi}$, as for the second bound, and $\rho_L+1\leqslant R$ gives the support statement.

For \eqref{eq:c3-2-3}, on a covered branch every contour bond $r$ lies in $\Omega_1$ with $\mathcal F_r\subseteq I$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}), so each contour link is reconstructed by a row within $R_{\mathrm{loc}}=2L+2\leqslant 2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$, a row of the charts of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}. For the derivative of the normalised character of the ordered link product: by the rowwise reconstruction (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}) and the uniform charts (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}) on the enlarged box with the exterior fixed, whose inputs lie in the phase ball of the charts by Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}, each affected link has a phase derivative bounded by $Cg_0$, a fixed input affects a bounded number of links, each link is traversed by $C$ at most as often as its maximal link multiplicity (once for the square $C_n$, a simple closed contour; the multiplicity enters $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$ as a factor), the derivative of the character is bounded in the invariant tangent norm on the compact group, and the other links remain unitary inside the closed contraction.

The convexity statement is $\gamma\,\id\leqslant H$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}) together with $\| D^2P_{\xi,t}\|\leqslant C_Pg_0s_{\xi}\leqslant C_Pg_0(1+2r)\leqslant \gamma/2$, using $s_{\xi}\leqslant 1+2r$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:collar-coverage}(iii)) and \eqref{eq:c3-1-2}.
\end{proof}

\subsection{An Extension within the Proved Chart}\label{sec:c3-3}
Let $B_{\sigma}\coloneqq\{ x\in\mathfrak g\, : \,| x|_{\sigma}\leqslant 1\}$, let $\Pi_r$ be the Hilbert metric projection onto the closed convex set $\tfrac32rB_{\sigma}$, let $\phi$ be a fixed nonnegative smooth $h$-radial mollifier on $\mathfrak g$ supported in the unit $h$-ball with integral one (in this appendix $\phi$ denotes this mollifier), let $\phi_s(y)\coloneqq s^{-d_G}\phi(y/s)$ for $s>0$ with $d_G=\dim\mathfrak g$, let $\epsilon\coloneqq 1/(4\sqrt N)$, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-3-1}
    T_r(x)\coloneqq\int_{\mathfrak g}\Pi_r(x-y)\,\phi_{\epsilon r}(y)\,\dd y\qquad(x\in\mathfrak g)\;.
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[The Extension Map]\label{lem:c3-3-1}
$T_r$ is smooth and $\operatorname{Ad}$-equivariant, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-3-2}
    T_r(x)= x\ \text{ if }| x|_{\sigma}\leqslant r,\qquad | T_r(x)|_{\sigma}\leqslant \tfrac32r,\qquad \| DT_r\|\leqslant 1,\qquad \| D^2T_r\|\leqslant C_{\sigma}/r\;,
\end{equation}
with $C_{\sigma}\coloneqq 4\sqrt N\,\|\nabla\phi\|_{L^1}$, which depends on $N$ and the fixed mollifier only.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Both norms are $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant, so $B_{\sigma}$ is $\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant and $\operatorname{Ad}$ is $h$-orthogonal; hence metric projection and the $h$-radial mollifier commute with the adjoint action, which gives the equivariance.

If $h(y)\leqslant \epsilon r$ then $| y|_{\sigma}\leqslant \sqrt N\,h(y)\leqslant r/4$ (the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}: $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}\leqslant \sqrt N\,h$), so for $| x|_{\sigma}\leqslant r$ one has $| x-y|_{\sigma}\leqslant \tfrac54r<\tfrac32r$ and $\Pi_r(x-y)= x-y$ (indeed for all $| x|_{\sigma}<\tfrac54r$); the convolution then equals $x$ because the mollifier has integral one and, being $h$-radial, zero first moment.

The range statement is the convexity of $\tfrac32rB_{\sigma}$: $T_r(x)$ is a probability average of its points.

Metric projection is $1$-Lipschitz for $h$ and convolution preserves this, giving $\| DT_r\|\leqslant 1$ in the $h$-operator norm; moving one derivative onto the mollifier of scale $\epsilon r$ bounds $\| D^2T_r\|$ by $\| D\Pi_r\|_{\infty}\|\nabla\phi_{\epsilon r}\|_{L^1}\leqslant \|\nabla\phi\|_{L^1}/(\epsilon r)= C_{\sigma}/r$.
\end{proof}

Let $T$ be the product map on $\mathfrak g^I$ that applies $T_r$ to each bond of $I$, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-3-3}
    \widetilde P_t(a)\coloneqq\sum_{\alpha\ \mathrm{near}}\bigl[\mathfrak p_{\alpha}(Ta+tA_{\mathrm e})-\mathfrak p_{\alpha}(tA_{\mathrm e})\bigr],\qquad
    \widetilde f(a)\coloneqq f_{\xi}(Ta),\qquad
    \widetilde L_t(a)\coloneqq-\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle+\partial_t\widetilde P_t(a)\;.
\end{equation}

\begin{lemma}[The Extended Objects]\label{lem:c3-3-2}
$\widetilde P_t$, $\widetilde f$ and $\widetilde L_t$ are defined and smooth on all of $\mathfrak g^I$, $|\widetilde f|\leqslant 1$, and on $\mathcal D_I$: $\widetilde f= f_{\xi}$, $\widetilde P_t= P_{\xi,t}-P_{\xi,t}(0)$ (the scalar $P_{\xi,t}(0)$ is removed only in the normalised conditional law; the unnormalised integral keeps it) and $\widetilde L_t-L_{\xi,t}=-\partial_tP_{\xi,t}(0)$, a constant, so that $\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(\widetilde f,\widetilde L_t)=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f_{\xi},L_{\xi,t})$. After enlarging $C_P$ (before $g_0$ is chosen; the enlarged constant depends on $L$, the group, $C_{\sigma}$, $C_{\mathrm p}$, $N_{\mathrm{ov}}$ and $N_{\mathrm{in}}$, all fixed before the coupling, and \eqref{eq:c3-1-2} is imposed with it), uniformly in $t\in[0,1]$ and $a\in\mathfrak g^I$: $\| D^2\widetilde P_t\|\leqslant C_Pg_0s_{\xi}$, the block Schur row and column sums of $D^2\widetilde P_t$ are at most $C_Pg_0s_{\xi}$ with range $R$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-3-4}
    h(\nabla_b\partial_t\widetilde P_t)\leqslant C_Sg_0s_{\xi}\,r_{\mathrm e,\xi}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf K_{\xi}}(b)\;,\qquad
    h(\nabla_b\widetilde f)\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}g_0\mathbf 1_{I_C}(b)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The image $Ta$ has cutoff norm at most $\tfrac32r<2r$ on every bond of $I$, so it lies in the enlarged box of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds} (threshold item 3 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}, in force by Section~\ref{sec:c3-1}), where every near primitive and every reconstruction row within $2R_{\mathrm c}+2L$ of $I$ is analytic, the exterior fields being fixed; the real reconstruction gives group-valued links, whence $|\widetilde f|\leqslant 1$.

On $\mathcal D_I$, $T$ is the identity (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-1}), which gives the three identities; a constant shift of one operand leaves the covariance unchanged.

The Hessian of $\widetilde P_t$ is $D^2\mathfrak p_{\alpha}(DT\bigcdot ,DT\bigcdot )+D\mathfrak p_{\alpha}\,D^2T$ summed over the near primitives: the first term is $O(g_0s_{\xi})$ in operator norm by Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1} and $\| DT\|\leqslant 1$, and per stencil by the second-derivative bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}, the second is $O(g_0s_{\xi}^2/r)= O(g_0s_{\xi})$ by the first-derivative bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}, $\| D^2T\|\leqslant C_{\sigma}/r$, $r\geqslant 1$ and $s_{\xi}\leqslant 1+2r\leqslant 3r$. Each input belongs to at most $N_{\mathrm{ov}}$ stencils and each stencil has at most $N_{\mathrm{in}}$ blocks, so summing at most $N_{\mathrm{ov}}N_{\mathrm{in}}$ blocks with this chain-rule bound gives the operator and Schur bounds; the supports and the range are those of the original stencils.

The mixed derivative $\nabla_b\partial_t\widetilde P_t$ contains no second derivative of $T$, since $T$ does not depend on $t$ and is bondwise: $\nabla_b\partial_t\widetilde P_t(a)= DT_r(a_b)^*(\nabla_b\partial_tP_{\xi,t})(Ta)$, so \eqref{eq:c3-2-2} of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1} at $Ta$ and $\| DT\|\leqslant 1$ give the first bound of \eqref{eq:c3-3-4}; the second is \eqref{eq:c3-2-3} composed with $DT$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Covariance Decay at the Hard Boundary}\label{sec:c3-4}
For a positive integer $n$, the barrier and the barrier laws are
\begin{gather}
    \beta_n(a)\coloneqq n\sum_{b\in I}\bigl[\operatorname{dist}_h(\,\bigcdot \,,rB_{\sigma})^2*\phi_{n^{-2}}\bigr](a_b)\;,\label{eq:c3-4-1}\\
    V_{n,t}(a)\coloneqq\tfrac12\langle a,Ha\rangle+t\langle\ell_{\xi},a\rangle-\widetilde P_t(a)+\beta_n(a)\;,\qquad
    \dd\nu_{n,t}\coloneqq Z_{n,t}^{-1}e^{-V_{n,t}(a)}\,\dd a\quad\text{on }\mathfrak g^I\;.\notag
\end{gather}
The squared distance to a convex set is convex and convolution with a nonnegative mollifier preserves convexity, so the barrier Hessian is positive semidefinite; it is diagonal in the bond index because $\beta_n$ is a sum of functions of the single bond variables.

For fixed $n$ the potential is smooth with bounded Hessian (that of the barrier is bounded by $2n$: the gradient $2(x-\Pi_r(x))$ of the squared distance is $2$-Lipschitz, and mollification is an average of translates) and Gaussian confinement, its Hessian is at least $\rho I$ with $\rho=\gamma/2$ as in Section~\ref{sec:c3-2} ($\gamma\,\id\leqslant H$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, and $\| D^2\widetilde P_t\|\leqslant C_Pg_0s_{\xi}\leqslant C_Pg_0(1+2r)\leqslant \gamma/2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2} and \eqref{eq:c3-1-2}--\eqref{eq:c3-1-3}), and its off-diagonal block row and column sums are at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-4-2}
    M_*= m_L+\gamma/2\;,
\end{equation}
with range at most $R$ in the bond distance $d$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-2}, independently of $n$, $t$, the volume and the branch (the barrier is diagonal; the row sums of $H$ are at most $m_L$ by the row-sum statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds}, its column sums equal its row sums since $H_{bb'}= H_{b'b}^{\mathsf T}$ have equal norms, and its range is $\rho_L=4L\leqslant R$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-entry-range}; the Schur sums of $D^2\widetilde P_t$ are at most $C_Pg_0s_{\xi}\leqslant \gamma/2$ with range $R$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2}).

\begin{lemma}[Helffer--Sj\"ostrand Identity and Decay]\label{lem:c3-4-1}
Let $\mathscr A_{n,t}\coloneqq\mathscr L_{n,t}\otimes I+D^2V_{n,t}$ with $\mathscr L_{n,t}\coloneqq-\Delta+\nabla V_{n,t}\cdot\nabla$, on the Hilbert direct sum over $b\in I$ of $L^2(\nu_{n,t};\mathfrak g)$. Then $\mathscr A_{n,t}\geqslant \rho I$ ($\mathscr L_{n,t}=\nabla^*\nabla\geqslant 0$ on $L^2(\nu_{n,t})$ and $D^2V_{n,t}\geqslant \rho I$), and for real $u,v$ in the weighted space $H^1(\nu_{n,t})$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-4-3}
    \operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{n,t}}(u,v)=\langle\nabla u,\mathscr A_{n,t}^{-1}\nabla v\rangle_{L^2(\nu_{n,t})}\;.
\end{equation}
With $\mu= R^{-1}\log(1+\gamma/(4M_*))$ and $\Pi_b$ the projection onto the $b$-component,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-4-4}
    \|\Pi_b\mathscr A_{n,t}^{-1}\Pi_c\|\leqslant \frac4\gamma e^{-\mu d(b,c)}\;,\qquad
    |\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{n,t}}(u,v)|\leqslant \frac4\gamma\sum_{b,c\in I}e^{-\mu d(b,c)}\|\nabla_bu\|_{L^2(\nu_{n,t})}\|\nabla_cv\|_{L^2(\nu_{n,t})}\;.
\end{equation}
For complex $u$ and real $v$, applying \eqref{eq:c3-4-4} to the real and imaginary parts of $u$ gives the same bound with the gradient norm of $u$ read as the sum of the gradient norms of its two parts; each is at most the gradient norm of $u$, so the bound holds with an extra factor two.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The identity \eqref{eq:c3-4-3} is \cite[Proposition 4.5]{Johnsen} (Theorem 1.3 there at $k=0$) for the real-valued $C^2$ potential $V_{n,t}+\log Z_{n,t}$ (normalised; the additive constant leaves the derivatives unchanged; $V_{n,t}$ is real because its quadratic, linear and barrier terms are real and $\widetilde P_t$ is real, the primitives being real on real inputs with a positive determinant, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}). Its conditions are a real $C^2$ normalised potential and the closed range of the operator $A_0$ there; the latter follows from $A_1\geqslant \rho I$, which is $\mathscr A_{n,t}\geqslant \rho I$ here, by \cite[Theorem 1.3]{Johnsen}, as explained there after (4.39). The theorem gives the projection onto the orthogonal complement of the constants as $d_0^*(A_1|_{\overline{\operatorname{ran}}\,d_0})^{-1}d_0$, and at fixed $n$ the bounded Hessian identifies $A_1$ with the displayed operator $\mathscr A_{n,t}$: $A_1$ is the Friedrichs extension of \cite[Lemma 4.2]{Johnsen} with the action (4.22) there, $\mathscr L_{n,t}\otimes I+D^2V_{n,t}$ on gradient fields, and since $D^2V_{n,t}$ is a bounded multiplication operator at fixed $n$ its form domain is that of $\mathscr L_{n,t}\otimes I$ and $A_1$ is the operator sum on the domain of $\mathscr L_{n,t}\otimes I$, a domain the bounded field-independent weights $W_c$ below preserve.

The operands are the source $\widetilde f$, bounded with bounded gradient (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2}), and the score $\widetilde L_t=-\langle\ell_{\xi},\bigcdot \rangle+\partial_t\widetilde P_t$, which grows at most linearly and has bounded gradient by \eqref{eq:c3-3-4}; both lie in $H^1(\nu_{n,t})$.

For a fixed $c\in I$ let $W_c$ multiply the component $b$ by $e^{\mu d(b,c)}$; it is constant in field space, hence commutes with the scalar generator $\mathscr L_{n,t}\otimes I$ and with every diagonal Hessian block, the barrier included, and the off-diagonal Schur bounds give $\| W_c\mathscr A_{n,t}W_c^{-1}-\mathscr A_{n,t}\|\leqslant M_*(e^{\mu R}-1)\leqslant \rho/2$ by the choice of $\mu$. $W_c$ and its inverse are bounded at finite volume, so a resolvent Neumann series gives $\| W_c\mathscr A_{n,t}^{-1}W_c^{-1}\|\leqslant (\rho-\rho/2)^{-1}=4/\gamma$; compressing by $\Pi_b$ on the left and $\Pi_c$ on the right, where $W_c$ acts as $e^{\mu d(b,c)}$ and as $e^{\mu d(c,c)}=1$, gives the first bound of \eqref{eq:c3-4-4}; the second follows from \eqref{eq:c3-4-3} and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The Barrier Limit]\label{lem:c3-4-2}
For $u,v$ bounded or of linear growth with bounded gradients, $\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{n,t}}(u,v)\to\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(u,v)$ as $n\to\infty$. Consequently the second bound of \eqref{eq:c3-4-4} holds for $\nu_{\xi;t}$ on the hard box $\mathcal D_I$, with the gradient norms taken as global suprema, $\|\nabla_bu\|_{\infty}\|\nabla_cv\|_{\infty}$ in place of the $L^2$ norms.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At finite volume $\beta_n\to0$ on the closed cutoff body $\{| a_b|_{\sigma}\leqslant r\ \forall b\}$ and $\beta_n\to\infty$ outside it, the boundary of the body has Lebesgue measure zero, and $\beta_n\geqslant 0$ together with the Gaussian confinement supplies an integrable majorant for $u$, $v$ and $uv$ (bounded or of linear growth); dominated convergence gives the convergence of the unnormalised integrals, and of the normaliser to $\int_{\mathcal D_I}e^{-V^{\circ}_t}\,\dd a>0$ (the box has nonempty interior), where $V^{\circ}_t\coloneqq V_{n,t}-\beta_n$ is the potential without the barrier, independent of $n$, hence of the covariances, to those of the law with density $e^{-V^{\circ}_t}$ on $\mathcal D_I$, which is $\nu_{\xi;t}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2} ($\widetilde P_t= P_{\xi,t}-P_{\xi,t}(0)$ on $\mathcal D_I$, and \eqref{eq:c3-1-4}).

On the right of \eqref{eq:c3-4-4} the $L^2(\nu_{n,t})$ norms depend on $n$, but they are bounded by the global suprema $\|\nabla_bu\|_{\infty}$, $\|\nabla_cv\|_{\infty}$, which do not, and $\mu$ and $4/\gamma$ are independent of $n$, so the bound passes to the limit.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Response}\label{sec:c3-5}
Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-5-1}
    D_{\xi}\coloneqq\sum_{b\in I_C}e^{-\mu d(b,J)/2}\;,
\end{equation}
with $\mu$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-4-1} and the bond distance $d$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-2}; $D_{\xi}=0$ when $J=\varnothing$ (by $d(b,\varnothing)=+\infty$; then also $A_{\mathrm e}=0$ and the score vanishes).

\begin{lemma}[The Exterior Response]\label{lem:exterior-response-bound}
Under \eqref{eq:c3-1-2}, on every covered branch (Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}) and for every $t\in[0,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-5-2}
    |\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f_{\xi},L_{\xi,t})|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}\,g_0r\sum_{b\in I_C}e^{-\mu d(b,J)/2}\;,\qquad
    |\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}\,g_0r\,D_{\xi}\;,
\end{equation}
after enlarging the constant $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1} (the enlarged constant keeps the name); it depends on $L$, $\gamma$, $m_L$, $M_*$, $R$, $N_{\mathrm{in}}$, $N_{\mathrm{ov}}$, $C_P$, $C_S$, $C_{\sigma}$, the character, the group and the fixed source parameters, and is independent of $g_0$, the branch, the volume, $t$ and the barrier index.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-2}, $\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f_{\xi},L_{\xi,t})=\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(\widetilde f,\widetilde L_t)$, and Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-4-2} bounds it by $(8/\gamma)\sum_{b,c\in I}e^{-\mu d(b,c)}\|\nabla_b\widetilde f\|_{\infty}\|\nabla_c\widetilde L_t\|_{\infty}$: the bound \eqref{eq:c3-4-4} is applied to the real and imaginary parts of the complex $\widetilde f$ and the real $\widetilde L_t$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-4-1}), the sum of the two gradient norms being at most $2\|\nabla_b\widetilde f\|_{\infty}$.

By \eqref{eq:c3-3-4} and \eqref{eq:c3-2-2}, $\|\nabla_c\widetilde L_t\|_{\infty}\leqslant (m_L+C_Sg_0s_{\xi})r_{\mathrm e,\xi}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf K_{\xi}}(c)\leqslant (m_L+C_S\gamma/(2C_P))\,r\,\mathbf 1_{\mathsf K_{\xi}}(c)$ (as $r_{\mathrm e,\xi}< r$ and $C_Sg_0s_{\xi}\leqslant C_Sg_0(1+2r)\leqslant C_S\gamma/(2C_P)$ by \eqref{eq:c3-1-2}; the coefficient is a constant fixed before $g_0$) and $\|\nabla_b\widetilde f\|_{\infty}\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}g_0\mathbf 1_{I_C}(b)$ with the constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1}.

On $\mathsf K_{\xi}$, $d(c,J)\leqslant R$, so $d(b,c)\geqslant d(b,J)-R$ and
\begin{equation*}
    e^{-\mu d(b,c)}= e^{-\mu d(b,c)/2}e^{-\mu d(b,c)/2}\leqslant e^{\mu R/2}e^{-\mu d(b,J)/2}\,e^{-\mu d(b,c)/2}\;;
\end{equation*}
the sum of $e^{-\mu d(b,c)/2}$ over all periodic bonds $c$ is bounded by the infinite-lattice shell sum $S_{\mu/2}=\sup_b\sum_ce^{-\mu d(b,c)/2}$ (the nearest-lift map from torus bonds to lattice bonds is injective and the terms are nonnegative), uniformly in the periods.

Collecting the constants, $(8/\gamma)(m_L+C_S\gamma/(2C_P))e^{\mu R/2}S_{\mu/2}$ times the constant of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1}, which depends on $\mu$ through $e^{\mu R/2}$ and $S_{\mu/2}$ and hence on $M_*$, gives the first bound of \eqref{eq:c3-5-2} with the enlarged $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$; integrating over $t\in[0,1]$ in \eqref{eq:c3-1-5} gives the second.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The Surface Terms Are Retained]\label{rem:c3-5-1}
In the notation \eqref{eq:native-collar-mean-direction}--\eqref{eq:native-collar-flux}, Lemma~\ref{lem:ibp} (its hypothesis holds: $f_{\xi}$ is $C^1$ on the enlarged box $\{| a_b|_{\sigma}\leqslant 2r\}$, a neighbourhood of $\overline{\mathcal D_I}$, by the charts of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}, as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-2-1}) writes the integrand of the response as
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-5-3}
    -\mathbb E_{\nu_{\xi;t}}[D_{m_{\xi}}f_{\xi}]+\operatorname{Cov}_{\nu_{\xi;t}}(f_{\xi},\partial_tP_{\xi,t}-D_{m_{\xi}}P_{\xi,t})+\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[f_{\xi}]-\mathbb E_{\nu_{\xi;t}}[f_{\xi}]\,\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[1]\;,
\end{equation}
with the hard-cutoff flux $\mathcal T_{\xi,t}[u]= I_{\xi;t}^{-1}\int_{\partial\mathcal D_I}u\,e^{\mathsf Q_{\xi,t}}\langle m_{\xi},n\rangle\,\dd S$. Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} bounds this whole expression.

The extension $T_r$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-3-1} is the identity on the neighbourhood $\{| a_b|_{\sigma}<\tfrac54r\}$ of $\overline{\mathcal D_I}$ and the barrier limit of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-4-2} returns the original measure, so the boundary traces and the normalised covariance in \eqref{eq:c3-5-3} are those of Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The Physical Substitution}\label{sec:c3-6}
Let $\mathsf w_{\xi}\coloneqq e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}=\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]$ be the branch weight \eqref{eq:c-collar-identity} and $\mathcal O$ the outer operation of \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}, so that $\mathcal Z_0=\int\mathcal O[\mathsf w_{\xi}](V)\,\dd V$ (\eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}). The history expectation and probability are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-6-1}
    \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[X]\coloneqq\mathcal Z_0^{-1}\int\mathcal O[\mathsf w_{\xi} X](V)\,\dd V\;,\qquad
    \mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A)\coloneqq\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_A]\;,
\end{equation}
for nonnegative or bounded Borel functions $X$ of the branch data; $\mathcal O$ has a nonnegative kernel (its Haar and constraint factors are measures and its cutoffs and exponentials are nonnegative, \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}) and $0<\mathcal Z_0<\infty$ (the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}), so $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ is positive, $|\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[X]|\leqslant \sup| X|$ and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[1]=1$.

Let $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ be the set of covered branches of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}: every contour bond is a bond of $\Omega_1$ and $\mathcal F_r\subseteq I$ for every contour bond $r$. The event $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ is determined by $\Omega_1$, $R_1$ and the fixed contour templates ($I=\Lambda_1^*$, the free bonds with an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$, Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}, with $\Lambda_1$ derived from $\Omega_1$ and $R_1$ by \cite[(1.20)]{BalabanCRE} and its filling; the stencils $\mathcal F_r$ are fixed); it and $D_{\xi}$ are measurable functions of the outer branch data, constant in the integration over $a$, and $0\leqslant D_{\xi}\leqslant | I_C|$, a bound by the number of free inputs of the contour.

The combined exterior-response and uncovered contribution to $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C)]$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio} is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-6-2}
    E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\coloneqq\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]+\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c}F_{\xi}(1)\bigr]\;,
\end{equation}
the exterior response on the covered branches and the whole conditional expectation on the uncovered ones (\eqref{eq:c-exterior-response}, \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity}); the integrand is a bounded Borel function of the branch data ($F_{\xi}(t)=\int f_{\xi} K_{\xi;t}\,\dd a/I_{\xi;t}$ is Borel in the branch data for each $t$, by the composition argument of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} applied to the interpolated kernel of \eqref{eq:convex-response-operands} and Fubini's theorem, and $|\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}g_0rD_{\xi}$ is bounded), so \eqref{eq:c3-6-1} applies to it. The quantities $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}D_{\xi}]$ and $\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c)$ are bounded in Section~\ref{sec:c3-7} (Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}).

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:c3-6-1}
Under \eqref{eq:c3-1-2},
\begin{gather}
    \Bigl|\mathcal Z_0^{-1}\int\mathcal O\bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]\bigr](V)\,\dd V\Bigr|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}\,g_0r\,\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}D_{\xi}]\;,\label{eq:c3-6-3}\\
    | E_{\mathrm{bdry}}|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}\,g_0r\,\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}D_{\xi}]+\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c)\;.\notag
\end{gather}
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
$\mathsf w_{\xi}\geqslant 0$ and $\mathcal O$ is positive, so Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} gives the first bound pointwise on the branches; the triangle inequality, \eqref{eq:c3-6-3}, positivity and $| F_{\xi}(1)|\leqslant 1$ give the second.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The History Average by One-Point Witnesses}\label{sec:c3-7}
This section assumes compatible even fine periods: every fine period is a multiple of $\ell= LMR_1$ and at least $8M$ (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}) and even. This is a restriction relative to the compatible periods of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}; it includes the torus with periods $2L^m$ when the partitions fit.

Let $\ell\coloneqq LMR_1$ be the macro side ($R_1$ the scale integer), $B_{\xi}=\Lambda_1^c$ the filled bad region, $E(X)$ the set of positive fine bonds with at least one endpoint in a set $X$ of sites, and $n_C$ the number of contour traversals.

Let $\Gamma_C$ be the deterministic set of the contour bonds together with the free-input templates of their reconstruction rows, projected periodically from the torus templates before any history is selected (so $\mathcal F_r\subseteq\Gamma_C$ for every contour bond $r$, with $\mathcal F_r$ the free-input set of \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-extension-support}, the set appearing in the covered event of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}); there is a constant $C_L$, depending on $L$ only (the templates are fixed lattice stencils), with $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_C$, and $I_C\subseteq\Gamma_C$ on every branch (the designated variables of the integration carrier are eliminated, so their free-input stencils, not the designated bonds, are the members of $\Gamma_C$).

For a positive bond $z$ the marked probability is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-1}
    p_z\coloneqq\mathcal Z_0^{-1}\int\mathcal O\bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}\bigr](V)\,\dd V=\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(z\in E(B_{\xi}))\;;
\end{equation}
the mark depends only on the regions and on the deterministic filling.

\begin{lemma}[Reduction to One-Point Marks]\label{lem:c3-7-1}
Let $c=\mu/2$ and $S_c=\sup_b\sum_ze^{-cd(b,z)}$, the periodic bond shell sum, bounded by its infinite-lattice counterpart uniformly in the periods. Pointwise on every branch
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-2}
    D_{\xi}\leqslant \sum_{b\in\Gamma_C}\sum_ze^{-cd(b,z)}\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}\;,\qquad
    \mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c}\leqslant \sum_{b\in\Gamma_C}\mathbf 1\{ b\in E(B_{\xi})\}\;.
\end{equation}
Hence, if $p_z\leqslant q$ for every positive bond $z$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-3}
    \mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[D_{\xi}]\leqslant C_LS_cn_Cq\;,\qquad \mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c)\leqslant C_Ln_Cq\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$J\subseteq E(B_{\xi})$: a free bond not in $I$ has no endpoint in $\Lambda_1$. So each $b\in I_C\subseteq\Gamma_C$ contributes $e^{-cd(b,J)}\leqslant \sum_{z\in J}e^{-cd(b,z)}\leqslant \sum_ze^{-cd(b,z)}\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}$.

If coverage fails, either a contour bond is not a bond of $\Omega_1$, and then it meets $B_{\xi}$ since $\Lambda_1\subseteq\Omega_1$, or a free input of the contour is not in $I$ (some $b\in\mathcal F_r\setminus I$ for a contour bond $r$, and $\mathcal F_r\subseteq\Gamma_C$), and then it is retained in $J$ or lies outside $\Omega_1$ and meets $B_{\xi}$; in both cases some $b\in\Gamma_C$ lies in $E(B_{\xi})$. Taking $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-2} (Tonelli; all integrands nonnegative) and using $p_z\leqslant q$ and $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_C$ gives \eqref{eq:c3-7-3}.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Cutoff Failures Give Local Witnesses}\label{sec:c3-7-1}
The witness argument operates on the original unresummed cutoffs \cite[(1.1), (1.4), (1.8), (1.18)]{BalabanCRE}, before the boundary substitution; it is proved in Lemmas~\ref{lem:c3-7-block}, \ref{lem:c3-7-seed} and~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} below. Its conclusion: a bad eligible test forces a fine plaquette with $| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta$ in its neighbourhood, or an active mean-transport variable with $| w-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta$ there (the $P_0$ and $P_1$ alternatives need no gauge-variable witness), with the threshold
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-4}
    \theta=\min\Bigl(\varepsilon_0,\ \frac{\varepsilon_1}{4B_3N^{3/2}L^2},\ \frac{\delta_0}{2C_Q}\Bigr)\;,\qquad
    C_Q=(9K_L+2)(1+2B_3N^{3/2}L^2)\;,
\end{equation}
where $K_L$ is the plaquette-filling constant of the loops of \cite[(0.4), (0.11)]{BalabanRG1} and of the bond loops of one block or of two adjacent blocks, defined in the paragraph ``Constants of the block comparison'' below.

The norm is the cutoff norm $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$, and the mean and comparison constants are chosen for it. The seed is used on the original earlier-cutoff and averaging-constraint support. Its common local width $w$ is $LM_2R_1$ or $L^2M_2R_1$, with one convention throughout, and its macro width is $\ell$; these are the conventions of the branch hypotheses of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}.

For a cube $Q$ and $k\geqslant 1$, $Q_w^{[k]}$ denotes $Q$ enlarged by $k$ layers of width $w$ (the $\square'^{\sim k}$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} when $w= L^2M_2R_1$), so that $\operatorname{side}(Q_w^{[k]})=\operatorname{side}(Q)+2kw$ and $Q_w^{[2]}$ is at $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2w$ from the complement of $Q_w^{[4]}$.

An eligible cube is a cube $\square'$ of the partition of \cite{BalabanCRE} into $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes carrying the test (1.18), which Ba{\l}aban performs for $\square'\subset\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ (p.250), so every eligible cube satisfies the hypothesis $Q\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}.

\emph{Constants of the block comparison.} For a block centre $y$ and a site $x$ of its block let $\mathbf G(y,x)$ be Ba{\l}aban's finite family of shortest paths from $y$ to $x$ (\cite[p.~252]{BalabanRG1}, the definition preceding (0.4), used in (0.11)): for each permutation $\pi$ of the axes the path moves first along $e_{\pi(1)}$ by the full coordinate difference, then along $e_{\pi(2)}$, and so on; each coordinate is monotone along the path, so the path stays in the block $B(y)$. Let $\Gamma_x\in\mathbf G(y,x)$ be a fixed representative ($\Gamma_y$ the empty path, with transport $\id$).

Let $K_L$ bound the number of plaquettes needed to fill each closed loop of the following finite family, each filling chosen inside the union of the block or blocks containing the loop (a lattice box, in which every closed lattice loop bounds a plaquette filling):
\begin{itemize}
\item the difference of two paths of one $\mathbf G(y,x)$;
\item the loop $\Gamma_x\cup b\cup(-\Gamma_{x'})$ of a block-internal bond $b=(x,x')$;
\item the loop $\Gamma_x\cup b\cup(-\Gamma_{x'})\cup(-c)$ of an interface bond $b=(x,x')$ of the coarse bond $c$, $x\in B(c_-)$, $x'\in B(c_+)$, $\Gamma_x\in\mathbf G(c_-,x)$, $\Gamma_{x'}\in\mathbf G(c_+,x')$;
