\item the loops $\Gamma\cup[x,x']\cup(-\Gamma')\cup(-c)$ of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, for a site $x\in B(c_-)$, with $[x,x']$ the parallel transport of the coarse bond $c$ to $x$ (\cite[p.~252]{BalabanRG1}, the sentence preceding the definition of the averages: the straight contour of $L$ fine bonds in the direction of $c$ from $x$ to $x'= x+(c_+-c_-)\in B(c_+)$) and paths $\Gamma\in\mathbf G(c_-,x)$, $\Gamma'\in\mathbf G(c_+,x')$.
\end{itemize}
Each loop lies in one block or in the union $B(c_-)\cup B(c_+)$ of two adjacent blocks (the contour $[x,x']$ runs inside this union, a box of sides $2L,L,L,L$), so $K_L$ depends on $L$ only.

The transports of a unitary field $F$ along two paths with the same endpoints differ in $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ by at most the sum of $| F(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}$ over the plaquettes filling their loop (unitary invariance of the norm and telescoping), hence by at most $K_L\eta$ when $| F(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant \eta$ for every plaquette $p$ with its four vertices in $B(c_-)\cup B(c_+)$ (``the plaquettes of the two blocks''; this includes the plaquettes straddling the interface).

For the group mean $M$ of \cite[(0.5)--(0.10)]{BalabanRG1} let $\mathcal N_L$ be the finite set of cardinalities $|\mathbf G(y,x)|$ and, for $n\in\mathcal N_L$, $\mathfrak m_n(A_1,\ldots,A_n)=(1/i)\log M(e^{iA_1},\ldots,e^{iA_n})$; it is analytic near zero with $\mathfrak m_n(0)=0$ and derivative $A\mapsto n^{-1}\sum_jA_j$ at zero (\cite[(0.8)]{BalabanRG1}). Let $r_{\mathrm M}>0$ be a radius such that every $\mathfrak m_n$, $n\in\mathcal N_L$, is analytic on the closed maximum-norm ball of $n$-tuples of radius $r_{\mathrm M}$ (the minimum over the finite set $\mathcal N_L$ of such radii), and $C_{\mathrm M}$ half the maximum over $n\in\mathcal N_L$ of the second-derivative norms on these balls; Taylor's theorem gives $|\mathfrak m_n(A)|_{\sigma}\leqslant \max_j| A_j|_{\sigma}+C_{\mathrm M}(\max_j| A_j|_{\sigma})^2$ for $\max_j| A_j|_{\sigma}\leqslant r_{\mathrm M}$.

On the principal unitary chart $|(1/i)\log W|_{\sigma}\leqslant | W-\id|_{\sigma}+C_{\log}| W-\id|_{\sigma}^2$ with a fixed $C_{\log}$: eigenvalue by eigenvalue, $2\arcsin(t/2)\leqslant t+Ct^2$ for $0\leqslant t\leqslant 2$, $t_j=| e^{i\varphi_j}-1|$, which gives the operator-norm case directly and the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt case with a constant depending on $N$ ($\max_jt_j\leqslant \sqrt N| W-\id|_{\sigma}$).

Let $C'_{\mathrm M}\coloneqq C_{\log}+4C_{\mathrm M}$. If $| W_jW_k^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant \rho$ for all $j$, with $\rho\leqslant 1/\max(1,C_{\log})$ and $2\rho\leqslant r_{\mathrm M}$, then $| M(W_1,\ldots,W_n)-W_k|_{\sigma}\leqslant \rho+C'_{\mathrm M}\rho^2$: after translation by $W_k^{-1}$ (\cite[(0.6)]{BalabanRG1}) the inputs $A_j=(1/i)\log(W_jW_k^{-1})$ have norm at most $\rho+C_{\log}\rho^2\leqslant 2\rho$; the phase $H=\mathfrak m_n(A)$ is Hermitian (\cite[(0.9)]{BalabanRG1}, the $W_j$ being unitary), so $| e^{iH}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant | H|_{\sigma}\leqslant \rho+C_{\log}\rho^2+4C_{\mathrm M}\rho^2$.

Let $\eta_0>0$ satisfy $C'_{\mathrm M}K_L\eta_0\leqslant 1$, $2K_L\eta_0\leqslant r_{\mathrm M}$, $K_L\eta_0\leqslant 1$, $C_{\log}K_L\eta_0\leqslant 1$ (so $\rho= K_L\eta_0\leqslant 1/\max(1,C_{\log})$) and $2K_L\eta_0\leqslant r_G/\sqrt N$, so that every $W\in G$ with $| W-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant 2K_L\eta_0$ lies in the chart domain: $\| W-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt N| W-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant r_G$, and $r_G$ is the radius of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} with this property (every logarithm above is taken at such a $W$: the loops have $| W-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant K_L\eta_0$, the translated means $| W_jW_k^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant \rho\leqslant K_L\eta_0$); for $\eta\leqslant \eta_0$ and $\rho= K_L\eta$ this gives $\rho+C'_{\mathrm M}\rho^2\leqslant 2K_L\eta$. The constants $K_L$, $r_{\mathrm M}$, $C_{\mathrm M}$, $C_{\log}$, $\eta_0$ depend on $L$, the group and the norm only.

\begin{lemma}[Block Comparison]\label{lem:c3-7-block}
Let $F$ be a unitary field on the bonds of two blocks $B(c_-)$, $B(c_+)$ joined by the coarse bond $c$ (or of one block), with $| F(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant \eta\leqslant \eta_0$ for every plaquette with its four vertices in $B(c_-)\cup B(c_+)$ and $| F(y,x)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant \eta$ for its averaged contour variables $F(y,x)= M(\{ F(\Gamma)\}_{\Gamma\in\mathbf G(y,x)})$ (\cite[(0.11)]{BalabanRG1}), $y\in\{ c_-,c_+\}$. Then, with $C_{\mathrm G}\coloneqq 9K_L+2$ and $M(F,c)$ the block average of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-block}
    \begin{gathered}
    | F(b)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{\mathrm G}\eta\ \text{ for a block-internal bond }b,\\
    | F(b)-M(F,c)|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{\mathrm G}\eta\ \text{ for an interface bond }b\in B(c)\;.
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Two paths of $\mathbf G(y,x)$ have transports within $K_L\eta$ of each other, so the group-mean estimate with $\rho= K_L\eta$ puts each $F(\Gamma)$, $\Gamma\in\mathbf G(y,x)$, within $2K_L\eta$ of $F(y,x)$, hence within $(2K_L+1)\eta$ of the identity.

For an internal bond $b=(x,x')$ the loop $\Gamma_x\cup b\cup(-\Gamma_{x'})$ gives $| F(\Gamma_x)F(b)F(\Gamma_{x'})^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant K_L\eta$, and replacing $F(\Gamma_x)$, $F(\Gamma_{x'})$ by the identity costs $2(2K_L+1)\eta$, so $| F(b)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant (5K_L+2)\eta$.

For an interface bond $b=(x,x')$ the loop $\Gamma_x\cup b\cup(-\Gamma_{x'})\cup(-c)$ gives in the same way $| F(b)-F(c)|_{\sigma}\leqslant (5K_L+2)\eta$, $F(c)$ the transport along the straight centre-to-centre path.

By \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, $M(F,c)= e^{iH}F(c)$ with $H$ the average, with weights summing to one (the weight $L^{-4}$ of each site $x\in B(c_-)$ and the path weights of (0.4)), of the logarithms $(1/i)\log F(\Gamma\cup[x,x']\cup(-\Gamma')\cup(-c))$ over the sites $x\in B(c_-)$ and the path pairs $\Gamma\in\mathbf G(c_-,x)$, $\Gamma'\in\mathbf G(c_+,x')$, $[x,x']$ the transported coarse bond; each of these loops belongs to the family defining $K_L$, so each logarithm has norm at most $K_L\eta+C_{\log}(K_L\eta)^2\leqslant 2K_L\eta$ and is Hermitian, so $| M(F,c)-F(c)|_{\sigma}\leqslant | H|_{\sigma}\leqslant 2K_L\eta\leqslant 4K_L\eta$. Together $| F(b)-M(F,c)|_{\sigma}\leqslant (9K_L+2)\eta$.
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Seed Constants]\label{def:seed-constants}
$k_N\coloneqq\sqrt N$ and $\alpha\coloneqq 2k_N^2L^2\theta$, with $\theta$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-4}. For a cube $Q$, $N(Q)$ is the set of fine sites within distance $6\ell$ of $Q$. The block stencil of a bond $b$ is the block or the pair of adjacent blocks containing its endpoints, with the plaquettes having their four vertices in their union and the averaged contour variables of their centres. The seed conditions on $g_0$ are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-seed-conditions}
    \begin{gathered}
        LM_2R_1>4LM_1+4L+8\;,\qquad\theta\leqslant \eta_0\;,\qquad 2B_3k_N^3L^2\theta\leqslant \eta_0\;,\\
        k_N\theta\leqslant c_2'\;,\qquad C_0L^2k_N\theta\leqslant 1\;,\qquad\alpha\leqslant a_1\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
with $\eta_0$, $c_2'$, $C_0$ the constants of \cite[Proposition~1, (51)]{BalabanAVG} and $a_1$ the constant of \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR}.
\end{definition}

$|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ and the norms of \cite{BalabanAVG} and \cite{BalabanVAR} are within factors $k_N$ of each other: each of these is the operator norm or the Hilbert--Schmidt norm in one of its two normalisations, and $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |_{\sigma}\leqslant \|\bigcdot \|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt N\,h$ with the unnormalised Hilbert--Schmidt norm equal to $\sqrt N\,h$ (the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}). Under \eqref{eq:c3-7-seed-conditions}, $B_3\alpha\leqslant B_3a_1\leqslant a_0$. Every seed condition is an upper bound on $\theta$ or a lower bound on $R_1$, and all hold for small $g_0$ since $\theta\leqslant \varepsilon_0\to0$ and $R_1\to\infty$ (\cite[(2.4)--(2.8)]{BalabanCRE}, the definition of $R_1$).

\begin{lemma}[Witnesses for Bad Tests]\label{lem:c3-7-seed}
Let $g_0$ satisfy the seed conditions \eqref{eq:c3-7-seed-conditions}. On the support of the averaging constraint $\delta(\bar UV^{-1})$ of \cite[(1.6), (1.11)]{BalabanCRE}, for the gauge-fixed field $\widetilde U$ of that integrand:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] a $P_0$ test is good whenever every plaquette of its defining enlargement has $| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}<\theta$;
\item[(b)] if every plaquette $p\subseteq N(Q)$ has $| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}<\theta$, where $Q$ is any cube of the partition of \cite{BalabanCRE} into $L^2M_2R_1$-cubes (in particular any cube carrying the test (1.4)), the $P_1$ test of $Q$ is good, and $| U_{1,Q}(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant 2B_3k_N^3\theta\leqslant \varepsilon_1L^{-2}/2$ on $Q_w^{[1]}$ and on $Q_w^{[2]}$, its incident bonds and their block stencils;
\item[(c)] if moreover every active averaged contour variable $w_{yx}=\widetilde U(y,x)$ with $x\in N(Q)$ has $| w_{yx}-\id|_{\sigma}<\theta$, then, for a $Q_1$- or $R_1$-eligible cube $Q$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-seed}
    \sup_{b\in(Q_w^{[2]})^*}|\widetilde U(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_Q\theta\leqslant \frac{\delta_0}{2}<2\delta_0\;,
\end{equation}
so the $Q_1$ test of $Q$ is good.
\end{itemize}
The $R_1$ test is treated in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) is $\theta\leqslant \varepsilon_0$.

Collar payments: $w\leqslant a= L^2M_2R_1$ and $M\geqslant 8LM_2$ give $4w+2L+4\leqslant 4a+2L+4<\ell$, and $w\geqslant LM_2R_1>4LM_1+4L+8$ gives $2w-2LM_1>2L+4$. The $\sim$ operations on $P_0'$, $P_1'$ and $B(P_1^1)^c$ are by $LMR_1$-cubes (\cite[pp.~246 and 248]{BalabanCRE}), so the first inequality places $Q_w^{[4]}$ and the blocks meeting it inside $B(P_1^1)$ for a $Q_1$-eligible cube $Q\subseteq B(P_1^1)^{\sim-1}$ (\cite[(1.8)]{BalabanCRE}) and, by \cite[(1.10)]{BalabanCRE} ($\Omega_1\subseteq B(P_1^1)^{\sim-3}$), for an $R_1$-eligible cube $Q\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ as well; the second places $Q_w^{[2]}$, its incident bonds and their block stencils at distance more than $2L+4$ inside $Q_w^{[4]}$ eroded by $2LM_1$. All these sets lie in $N(Q)$, since they are within $4w+2L+4\leqslant 4a+2L+4<\ell<6\ell$ of $Q$.

(b) The block average is gauge covariant, $M(U^v,c)= v(c_-)M(U,c)v(c_+)^{-1}$ for a gauge transformation $v$: in \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} every loop is based at $c_-$, so its holonomy is conjugated by $v(c_-)$, the chart logarithm is conjugation covariant, and $U(c)$ is a transport from $c_-$ to $c_+$. So the coarse plaquette deviations $|\bar U(\partial p')-\id|_{\sigma}$ of $\bar U= M(U,\bigcdot )$ coincide for $U$ and its gauge transform $\widetilde U$, as do the fine plaquette deviations, and the plaquette hypothesis on $N(Q)$ may be read for either field.

\cite[Proposition~1, (51)]{BalabanAVG}, in the averaging norm (at most $k_N|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$) with $\alpha_0= k_N\theta\leqslant c_2'$ gives $|\bar U(\partial p')-\id|\leqslant L^2k_N\theta+C_0(L^2k_N\theta)^2\leqslant 2L^2k_N\theta$ for every coarse plaquette $p'$ whose blocks lie in $N(Q)$; a further factor $k_N$ converts this to the norm of \cite{BalabanVAR}, so on the support of $\delta(\bar UV^{-1})$ the coarse data $V$ on $Q_w^{[4]}$ satisfy the data bound of \cite{BalabanVAR} with $\alpha=2k_N^2L^2\theta$.

The determining data of $U_{1,Q}$ are those of \cite[(1.2)]{BalabanCRE}: the minimal determining set $\mathbf B_1(Q_w^{[4]})$ with the data $M^{\bigcdot }(Q_1^{s*}V)$, no exterior data. The extension (1.3) has identity block-internal links and interface links $V(c)$; its fine plaquettes are the identity (two internal and two interface links across one coarse bond) or coarse plaquette holonomies (four interface links at a corner of four blocks), and its block averages are $V$ (the loops of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} are the identity on it). So the ordinary and mixed determining plaquettes of \cite[(7)]{BalabanVAR} obey the bound $\alpha\leqslant a_1$, and \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} gives a minimal critical orbit in the class (8) with bound $B_3\alpha$.

\cite[p.~256, (2.12)]{BalabanCRE} defines $U_{1,Q}$ as an element of the unique minimal orbit of the local action over the regular configurations $U$ with $M_{\mathbf B}(U)= V$, and refers for ``regular'' and for the variational theory to \cite{BalabanVAR}; ``regular'' is membership in the class \cite[(6)]{BalabanVAR}, the space \cite[(2)]{BalabanVAR} with a radius $\varepsilon$ satisfying $B_3\alpha\leqslant \varepsilon\leqslant a_0$, the setting of \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} (such $\varepsilon$ exist, as $B_3\alpha\leqslant B_3a_1\leqslant a_0$). Theorem~1 states that the minimal orbit of the class (8) is the unique critical orbit of the class (6), for every such $\varepsilon$, so the choice of the radius is immaterial; a minimal configuration is critical, so the minimal orbit over the regular configurations is this orbit, $U_{1,Q}$ satisfies the bounds (8) with the parameter of \cite{BalabanVAR} (written $\varepsilon_1$ there; not the $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}) equal to $\alpha$, and the axial gauge condition (\cite[p.~247]{BalabanCRE}) fixes the representative.

The construction of $\mathbf B_1$ in \cite[pp.~256--257]{BalabanCRE} (after (2.12); $Q_w^{[4]}$ is a union of $w$-cubes, $w\in\{ LM_2R_1,L^2M_2R_1\}$ a multiple of $LM_1$, hence a union of $LM_1$-cubes and of $M_1$-cubes, $M_1< M_2$ being powers of $L$) gives that the coarse determining interior contains $(Q_w^{[4]})^{\sim-2}$ with the erosion in $M_1$-cubes of $T_{L^{-1}}$, of side $LM_1$ in fine units, so the loss is at most $2LM_1$, and by the collar payment $Q_w^{[2]}$, its incident bonds and their block stencils lie inside it. There \cite[(8)]{BalabanVAR} bounds the fine plaquettes of the minimum by $B_3\alpha L^{-2}$ in the norm of \cite{BalabanVAR}, that is by $k_NB_3\alpha L^{-2}=2B_3k_N^3\theta\leqslant \varepsilon_1L^{-2}/2$ in $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ by \eqref{eq:c3-7-4}; on $Q_w^{[1]}$ this is the good $P_1$ test of \cite[(1.4)]{BalabanCRE}.

(c) The blocks meeting $(Q_w^{[2]})^*$ are active by the collar payments. Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-block} applies to $\widetilde U$ with $\eta=\theta$ (plaquettes and averaged contour variables below $\theta$) and to $U_{1,Q}$ with $\eta=2B_3k_N^3L^2\theta\leqslant \eta_0$ (its plaquette deviations are at most $2B_3k_N^3\theta$ by (b), and its averaged contour variables are the identity in the axial gauge). On the support of the averaging constraint $M(\widetilde U,c)= V(c)$, and $M(U_{1,Q},c)= V(c)$ on the coarse bonds of the determining interior (the constraint of the local problem, data (1.3)). Comparing both fields with the identity for an internal bond, and with $V(c)$ for an interface bond, $|\widetilde U(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}=|\widetilde U(b)-U_{1,Q}(b)|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{\mathrm G}\theta(1+2B_3k_N^3L^2)= C_Q\theta\leqslant \delta_0/2$ by \eqref{eq:c3-7-4}, the good $Q_1$ test of \cite[(1.8)]{BalabanCRE}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[A Bad Test Forces a Witness]\label{lem:c3-7-2}
For $g_0$ below a threshold depending on $L$, the group, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$ and the source constants, on the original cutoff support: every bad $P_0$, $P_1$, $Q_1$ or $R_1$ test forces a plaquette or gauge-variable witness at threshold $\theta$ within distance $K\ell$ of every bond $z\in E(B_{\xi})$ whose membership it causes, with the fixed $K=256$; and the number of plaquette and gauge-variable labels in such a neighbourhood is at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-5}
    n_W\coloneqq 7(2K\ell+7)^4\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The $P_0$, $P_1$ and $Q_1$ alternatives are Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-seed}(a)--(c). For the $R_1$ test, Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-seed}(c) is combined with the comparison of the two minima on the twice enlarged carrier of every eligible cube $Q$, uniformly in its label, proved in Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1} below:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-6}
    \sup_{b\in(Q_w^{[2]})^*}| U_1(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1e^{-c_{L,G}LM_2R_1}<\delta_0/10\;.
\end{equation}
Its only input from the characteristic factors of \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} is their nonvanishing at $U_1$ itself, the membership $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ of (B1) (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}, in the sense recorded there and in (H4)).

On the native principal chart a bad $R_1$ label of the cube $Q$ forces $| g_0A(b)|_{\sigma}\geqslant \delta_0$ at a bond $b\in(Q_w^{[2]})^*$, the carrier of the test in \cite[(1.18)]{BalabanCRE}; the eigenvalue inequality $| e^{iX}-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant (2/\pi)| X|_{\sigma}$, valid when every eigenvalue of $X$ lies in $[-\pi,\pi]$ (as on the chart) in both permitted norms, and \eqref{eq:c3-7-6} give, for the gauge-fixed field $\widetilde U= e^{ig_0A}U_1$ at the free bond $b$ (\cite[(1.13)]{BalabanCRE}: $U'= UU_1^{-1}= e^{iA'}$ with $A'= g_0A$ the fluctuation field; the variable tested in (1.18) is the free variable $A(b)$ of (1.15), and the fluctuation at a free bond is exactly $e^{ig_0A(b)}$, because the substitution (1.14), $A'= B-h_{U_1}\widetilde D(B)$ with $B= g_0\mathsf C_{U_1}A$, changes the phase only at the designated bonds: $h_{U_1}$ is supported on them and $\mathsf C_{U_1}A$ agrees with $A$ on the free bonds, \eqref{eq:constraint-extension} at the background, Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-7}
    |\widetilde U(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant (2/\pi-1/10)\delta_0>\delta_0/2\;.
\end{equation}
If every witness in $N(Q)$ were below $\theta$, \eqref{eq:c3-7-seed} (Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-seed}(c) for the $R_1$-eligible cube $Q$; the earlier cutoffs and $\Omega_1$ are fixed term by term in the sum (1.11), which resums $P_0$, $P_1$, $Q_1$ at fixed $\Omega_1$, and $\Omega_1\subseteq B(P_1^1)^{\sim-3}$ holds for each term; the comparison \eqref{eq:c3-7-6} holds whatever the $R_1$ label of $Q$) would give $|\widetilde U(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_Q\theta\leqslant \delta_0/2$, a contradiction; so the label is excluded.

\cite[(1.1), (1.4), (1.8), (1.18)]{BalabanCRE} are sharp characteristic partitions at their printed thresholds, so these inequalities make the corresponding bad factor vanish; (1.18) is introduced after the logarithmic reconstruction (1.13)--(1.15).

For the distances: before filling, \cite[(1.10), (1.20)]{BalabanCRE} give the bad region as $Q_1'^{\sim4}\cup(B(P_1^1)^c)^{\sim5}\cup R_1'^{\sim1}$, with $B(P_1^1)^c\subseteq P_0'^{\sim2}\cup P_1'^{\sim1}$ (the definition of $P_1^1$ following \cite[(1.4)]{BalabanCRE}, as printed, gives $B(P_1^1)^c= P_0'^{\sim2}$; the reading consistent with the active-region construction of \cite[(3.2)--(3.3)]{BalabanCRE} gives $P_0'^{\sim2}\cup P_1'^{\sim}$; both are contained in $P_0'^{\sim2}\cup P_1'^{\sim1}$), so a point of this region is within $10\ell$ of a bad test.

The modification after (1.20) fills only components contained in cubes of side less than $100\ell$, so every added point is within $100\ell$ of an original unfilled bad point; this also holds if small merged components are filled again, since by induction every current component contains an original bad point and each fill is performed inside a cube of side less than $100\ell$ containing that component (every point of the rectangular hull of such a component is within $100\ell$ of a chosen original bad point of it, and overlapping hulls or later merges preserve the presence of an original point), so there is no cumulative distance loss. \cite[(2.9)]{BalabanCRE} gives, for its scale $R_0$ (the range of its expansions, distinct from the range constant $R_0$ of \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes}), $R_0\leqslant (L+1)R_1$, hence $R_0\leqslant LR_1$ as both are powers of $L$ (the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}).

Including each test's witness neighbourhood and incident bonds, every $z\in E(B_{\xi})$ forces a witness within $K\ell$ of $z$ with $K=256$: a point of the filled bad region is within $100\ell$ of an original bad point, which is within $10\ell$ of a bad test cube $Q$ of side at most $a\leqslant \ell/8$, whose witness lies in $N(Q)$, within $6\ell$ of $Q$; an incident bond adds one; in all $100\ell+10\ell+a+6\ell+1\leqslant 117\ell<256\ell$. The count \eqref{eq:c3-7-5} bounds the plaquette and gauge-variable labels in that neighbourhood, also on a small periodic torus.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The Marked Probability Retains the Physical Normaliser}\label{sec:c3-7-2}

\begin{definition}[The Comparison Measures]\label{def:comparison-measures}
$A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}\coloneqq\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$, and $\mathscr E_{\xi}(B)$ is the pre-boundary-change exponent of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}, its outer prefactor excluded (\eqref{eq:native-collar-full-exponent}). With $s_G(w)\coloneqq 1-\operatorname{Re}\tr_Nw$, the bare probability and the gauge-variable law are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-10}
    \mu_0(\dd U)\coloneqq\mathcal Z_0^{-1}e^{-\mathsf E}e^{-S(U)/g_0^2}\,\dd U\;,\qquad q_g(\dd w)\coloneqq z_g^{-1}\mathbf 1\{| w-\id|_{\sigma}<\varepsilon_0\} e^{-s_G(w)/g_0^2}\,\dd w\;,
\end{equation}
with $z_g$ the integral of the displayed density, the gauge normaliser of \cite{BalabanCRE}. For a positive bond $z$, $W_z$ is the event that some plaquette or some auxiliary gauge variable in the deterministic $K\ell$-neighbourhood of $z$ is a witness at threshold $\theta$; $\mathcal I$ is the set of pairs $(y,x)$ of a block centre $y$ and a noncentral site $x$ of its block, and $T$ the set of centres and unused sites.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The Marked Density and Its Reversal]\label{lem:c3-7-3}
With $c_{\xi}$ of \eqref{eq:native-collar-boundary-constant}, pointwise on $\mathfrak g^I$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-8}
    e^{c_{\xi}}K_{\xi;1}(a)=\mathbf 1_{\mathcal D_I}(a)\,|\det D\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})|\,\exp\mathscr E_{\xi}\bigl(\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})\bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
and the composed retained cutoff $\chi_{\xi,\mathrm e}$ and $\zeta_{\xi}$ multiply both sides; integrating over $a$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-8-weight}
    \mathsf w_{\xi}= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}=\int e^{c_{\xi}}K_{\xi;1}(a)\,\dd a\;,
\end{equation}
the branch constant $c_{\xi}$ and every far primitive present (\eqref{eq:c-collar-identity}). Together with Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}, on compatible even fine periods, for every positive bond $z$, with the measures and the event of Definition~\ref{def:comparison-measures},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-9}
    p_z\leqslant \bigl(\mu_0\otimes q_g^{\otimes\mathcal I}\otimes\mathrm{Haar}^{\otimes T}\bigr)(W_z)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\Psi_{\xi}$ is the identity in every near stencil and its support $S_1^*$ is disjoint from $I$, so $\Psi_{\xi}(a+A_{\mathrm e})= a+A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}$ (\eqref{eq:c-bondwise-shift}). Expanding the quadratic form of $\mathscr E_{\xi}$ into its $II$, $IJ$, $JJ$ blocks, leaving every far primitive at $A^{\Psi}_{\mathrm e}$ and retaining the boundary determinant gives \eqref{eq:c3-7-8}, which is the computation of Lemma~\ref{lem:collar}(ii); the retained cutoff and $\zeta_{\xi}$ are factors of the integrand outside the $a$-integral. Together with the outer prefactor $\kappa_{\xi}$ (\eqref{eq:native-source-outer-prefactor}) the right side recombines into the transformed density of \cite[(1.15)]{BalabanCRE}, boundary Jacobian included.

The changes of variables of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} are reversed with the mark $\mathbf 1\{ z\in E(B_{\xi})\}$ inserted; the reversal is a change of variables for the integral of the density times any nonnegative measurable function of $U$ and of the regions, performed term by term before the characteristic partitions are summed. The reversal is performed in each term of the history sum separately, where the regions, the filling and the labels are fixed, and each change of variables is an identity between integrals of a density times a nonnegative measurable integrand (the term's partitions and cutoffs multiply the integrand and are carried along), so it holds for the mark, and equally for any nonnegative measurable function of $U$, the regions and the labels in its place; the partitions are summed only after the domination by a label-free event below.

The map $\Psi_{\xi}$, the free-variable constraint elimination, the scaling, the nonlinear constraint linearisation of (1.14), the logarithmic chart of (1.13) with its Haar density, and the translation about $U_1$ are undone in this order; the retained cutoff stays composed with $\Psi_{\xi}$ and $\zeta$ remains in that composition, boundary-fluctuation dependence included. The marked integral is then \cite[(1.6)]{BalabanCRE} with its four original partitions and the site-gauge integration, no determinant or normalisation discarded; the unmarked chain is $\mathcal Z_0= e^{-\mathsf E}\int e^{-S(U)/g_0^2}\,\dd U$.

For each active block centre $y$ and noncentral $x$ let $w_{yx}$ be its mean transport after the gauge change; \cite[(0.6)]{BalabanRG1} and \cite[(1.5)]{BalabanCRE} give the Haar substitution $v(x)= w_{yx}^{-1}h_yU(y,x)$, $v(y)= h_y$, with Jacobian one, and the law of $w$ is \eqref{eq:c3-7-10}. Independent $q_g$ variables of integral one are added for the inactive indices, and independent Haar variables for the centres and unused sites. The earlier $P_0$, $P_1$ choices depend on $U$ and its coarse gauge orbit, not on these auxiliary variables.

By Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} the mark is dominated by $\mathbf 1_{W_z}$, and $W_z$ does not depend on the later $Q_1$, $R_1$ labels; only after this enlargement are the characteristic partitions summed to one. This gives \eqref{eq:c3-7-9}.

The plaquette witness norms and the conjugation-invariant gauge-variable norms are gauge-invariant scalars under the simultaneous gauge transformations.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{One-Point Tails and Summation}\label{sec:c3-7-3}

Let $d_G\coloneqq\dim G$ and $b_G\coloneqq 1/(2N)$. The action is $S(U)=\sum_ps_G(U(\partial p))$ over the unoriented plaquettes, \eqref{eq:bare-action}, with the normalised trace $\tr_N= N^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}$, and $s_G(w)\geqslant b_G| w-\id|_{\sigma}^2$. By \eqref{eq:one-step-physical-partition}, $\mathcal Z_0=\int\rho_0\,\dd U= e^{-\mathsf E}\int e^{-S/g_0^2}\,\dd U$ with $\mathsf E= E_{\varepsilon}$ the vacuum scalar of \eqref{eq:bare-action}; $\dd U$, $\dd w$ are normalised Haar measures, and $\mu_0$ and $q_g$ are probability measures by their normalisations $\mathcal Z_0$ and $z_g$ \eqref{eq:c3-7-10}.

There are constants $c_H$, $g_H>0$ depending on the group only such that the Haar measure of the operator ball of radius $g$ about $\id$ is at least $c_Hg^{d_G}$ for $0< g\leqslant g_H$: in the chart, $\dd w=\sigma(A)\,\dd A$ with the continuous Haar density $\sigma$, $\sigma(0)=\sigma_0>0$ (the steps listed after \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}); let $g_H<\varrho_G$ satisfy $\sigma\geqslant \sigma_0/2$ on $\{\| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant g_H\}$, a subset of the chart ball as $h\leqslant \|\bigcdot \|_{\mathrm{op}}$; for $g\leqslant g_H$ the map $A\mapsto e^{iA}$ sends $\{\| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}< g\}$ injectively into the operator ball of radius $g$ ($\| e^{iA}-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}$), so that ball has Haar measure at least $(\sigma_0/2)\operatorname{Leb}\{\| A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1\}\,g^{d_G}\eqqcolon c_Hg^{d_G}$.

The operator ball of radius $g_0$ lies in $\{| w-\id|_{\sigma}<\varepsilon_0\}$ for small $g_0$, since the two norms are comparable with fixed constants and $\varepsilon_0/g_0= A_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}\to\infty$, $A_0>0$ (\eqref{eq:cre-cutoff-normalisation}, \cite[p.~246]{BalabanCRE}: $\varepsilon_0= g_0A_0(\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$).

\begin{definition}[Single-Witness Rates]\label{def:single-witness-rates}
With $c_H$ as above and the number $n_W$ of witness labels of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}, \eqref{eq:c3-7-5}, for $\theta'\in(0,\varepsilon_0]$,
\begin{equation*}
    z_P(\theta')\coloneqq \exp\Bigl[-\frac{b_G\theta'^2}{4g_0^2}+4d_G\log g_0^{-1}+4\log c_H^{-1}+48\Bigr]\;,\qquad z_G(\theta')\coloneqq e^{1/2}(c_Hg_0^{d_G})^{-1}e^{-b_G\theta'^2/g_0^2}\;,
\end{equation*}
and, at the threshold $\theta\leqslant \varepsilon_0$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-4}, $z_P\coloneqq z_P(\theta)$, $z_G\coloneqq z_G(\theta)$, and the one-point rate $q\coloneqq n_W\max(z_P,z_G)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Single-Witness Tails]\label{lem:c3-7-4}
Let $g_0\leqslant g_H$ be small enough that the operator ball of radius $g_0$ lies in $\{| w-\id|_{\sigma}<\varepsilon_0\}$. With $V_T$ the number of fine sites,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-11}
    \mathcal Z_0\geqslant e^{-\mathsf E}(c_Hg_0^{d_G})^{4V_T}e^{-48V_T}\;.
\end{equation}
On compatible even fine periods, for every threshold $\theta'\in(0,\varepsilon_0]$, every plaquette $p$ and every auxiliary gauge variable $w$,
\begin{gather}
    \mu_0\bigl(| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta'\bigr)\leqslant z_P(\theta')\;,\label{eq:c3-7-12}\\
    q_g\bigl(| w-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta'\bigr)\leqslant z_G(\theta')\;,\label{eq:c3-7-13}
\end{gather}
and therefore, for $g_0$ below the threshold of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} (which \eqref{eq:c3-7-9} inherits through Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-3}), $p_z\leqslant q$ for every positive bond $z$, with $q$ of Definition~\ref{def:single-witness-rates}.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On the event that every fine link lies in the operator ball of radius $g_0$ every plaquette has $\| U(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant 4g_0$ (telescoping over its four links) and contributes $s_G(U(\partial p))=\frac1{2N}\sum_j| e^{i\varphi_j}-1|^2\leqslant \frac12\| U(\partial p)-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\leqslant 8g_0^2$ to $S$ ($e^{i\varphi_j}$ the eigenvalues of $U(\partial p)$), and there are at most $6V_T$ plaquettes and $4V_T$ links, which gives \eqref{eq:c3-7-11}.

Let $\theta'\in(0,\varepsilon_0]$. The bound \eqref{eq:c3-7-12} follows from reflection positivity and the chessboard estimate of $\mu_0$ on the even fine periods $N_{\mu}$.

For a coordinate reflection $\vartheta$ through the planes $x_{\mu}=0$, $x_{\mu}= N_{\mu}/2$ let $(\vartheta U)(x,x')\coloneqq U(\vartheta x,\vartheta x')$ (inverse values on reversed bonds; $s_G(W)$ and $| W-\id|_{\sigma}$ are invariant under $W\mapsto W^{-1}$ and under conjugation, so the plaquette terms of $S$ and the plaquette indicators below do not depend on the orientation or the base point of a plaquette) and $\Theta F= F\circ\vartheta$. Every plaquette lies in one of the two closed half-tori; let $U_{\partial}$ be the links in the two planes, $U_+$ the remaining links of one half, and $S_+$ the sum of $s_G(U(\partial p))$ over the plaquettes of that closed half, the plaquettes lying in the planes (functions of $U_{\partial}$) counted with weight $1/2$, so that $S= S_++\Theta S_+$. For a bounded $F$ of the links $(U_+,U_{\partial})$, since $\Theta$ fixes $U_{\partial}$ and carries the Haar measure of $U_+$ to that of the other half,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-rp}
    \int\overline F\,\Theta F\,\dd\mu_0=\frac{e^{-\mathsf E}}{\mathcal Z_0}\int\Bigl|\int Fe^{-S_+/g_0^2}\,\dd U_+\Bigr|^2\,\dd U_{\partial}\geqslant 0\;.
\end{equation}
Let $C_x\coloneqq x+[0,1]^4$, $x$ a fine site, be the closed unit cubes and, for a bounded function $f$ of the links of $C_0$, let $f^{[x]}$ be its transport to $C_x$ by successive reflections (the four coordinate reflections commute and the periods are even, so $f^{[x]}$ depends neither on the order of the directions nor on the winding of the path of reflections; and the reflection through any site plane $x_{\mu}= m$ carries the transport to the slab at position $k$ in direction $\mu$ to the transport to position $2m-1-k$, since every composition of integer-plane reflections carrying position $0$ to position $k$ has orientation $(-1)^k$ in that direction and so coincides with the defining transport). For nonnegative bounded functions $f_x$ of the links of $C_0$, indexed by the fine sites $x$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-chessboard}
    \int\prod_{x}f_x^{[x]}\,\dd\mu_0\leqslant \prod_{x}\Bigl(\int\prod_{y}f_x^{[y]}\,\dd\mu_0\Bigr)^{1/V_T}\;,
\end{equation}
the chessboard estimate. Its proof is the argument of \cite[Theorem~10.11, p.~445]{FriedliVelenik}, with \eqref{eq:c3-7-rp} as the reflection positivity and the link variables with site reflections in place of the spin system there.

In one direction, with $N_{\mu}=2h$: by translation invariance of $\mu_0$, \eqref{eq:c3-7-rp} holds for the reflection through any pair of antipodal site planes $x_{\mu}= k$, $x_{\mu}= k+h$; let $\Phi(f_0,\ldots,f_{2h-1})$ be the $\mu_0$-expectation of the reflected product of functions of the $2h$ closed unit slabs (slab $j$ carrying $f_j^{[j]}$, the transport of $f_j$ to slab $j$); adjacent slabs share only plane links; the two planes bounding $h$ consecutive slabs are fixed by the reflection through them and the plane links interior to these slabs belong to $U_+$, so the product over any $h$ consecutive slabs is a function of $(U_+,U_{\partial})$ for the reflection through the planes bounding it, and \eqref{eq:c3-7-rp} with the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality for the sesquilinear form $(F,F')\mapsto\int\overline F\,\Theta F'\dd\mu_0$ bounds $\Phi^2$ by the product of the two values of $\Phi$ obtained by reflecting either half of the tuple onto the other.

Each function is increased by a positive constant and divided by the $2h$-th root of its fully disseminated expectation (the normalised functions $\widetilde f_j$ have $\Phi(\widetilde f_j,\ldots,\widetilde f_j)=1$); among the finitely many tuples with entries from $\{\widetilde f_0,\ldots,\widetilde f_{2h-1}\}$, let a maximiser of $\Phi$ have a longest constant run (runs counted cyclically), of length $r$; both tuples obtained by reflecting either half onto the other are maximisers as well (the maximum is positive, every function being bounded below by its added constant, and the Cauchy--Schwarz bound, the square of the maximum being at most the product of the two reflected values, forces both to equal the maximum). If $r\leqslant h$, reflecting the half that ends with the run onto the other half gives a maximiser with a constant run of length $2r> r$, contradicting the choice of $r$; so $r> h$, a half lying inside the run is reflected, and the resulting maximiser is constant: the maximum is $\Phi(\widetilde f_j,\ldots,\widetilde f_j)=1$ for some $j$, which gives the one-dimensional inequality for the normalised functions; letting the added constants decrease to zero (dominated convergence) gives it for the $f_j$.

Applying it successively in the four directions (the reflections commute, and the slab functions produced after disseminating in the earlier directions are again nonnegative and bounded) gives the exponent $1/V_T$.

Every plaquette is a translate of a plaquette of $C_0$ and $\mu_0$ is translation invariant, so it suffices to apply \eqref{eq:c3-7-chessboard} with $f_0=\mathbf 1\{| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta'\}$ for a plaquette $p$ of $C_0$ and $f_x=1$ for $x\neq0$: the dissemination $\{ f_0^{[y]}\}_{y}$ contains $V_T/4$ distinct plaquettes of the plane orientation $(\mu\nu)$ of $p$ (the two transverse coordinates of a copy range over one parity class; repeated copies of an indicator do not change the product), each with $s_G\geqslant b_G\theta'^2$ on the event, and $S\geqslant 0$ termwise, so the disseminated expectation is at most $e^{-\mathsf E}e^{-b_G\theta'^2V_T/(4g_0^2)}/\mathcal Z_0$; dividing by \eqref{eq:c3-7-11} and taking the $1/V_T$-th root gives $z_P(\theta')$, a normalised probability estimate.

For \eqref{eq:c3-7-13}, the restriction of one gauge variable to its operator ball of radius $g_0$, where its action is at most $g_0^2/2$ and its cutoff factor is one (the ball lies in $\{| w-\id|_{\sigma}<\varepsilon_0\}$ by the hypothesis on $g_0$), bounds $z_g$ from below by $c_Hg_0^{d_G}e^{-1/2}$; on the event $| w-\id|_{\sigma}\geqslant \theta'$ the action is at least $b_G\theta'^2$, which gives $z_G(\theta')$.

The union bound over the at most $n_W$ witness labels of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} and \eqref{eq:c3-7-9} at the threshold $\theta$ give $p_z\leqslant q$.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The Exterior-Response and Uncovered Term]\label{prop:c3-7-5}
Let
\[
\pi_*=\min(p_0(g_0),p_0(g_1))\;.
\]
There are $c_{\theta}$, $c_*$, $g_*>0$, fixed after $L$, the group, the character, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$ and the source constants, such that $\theta\geqslant c_{\theta} g_0\pi_*$ and $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ for $0< g_0< g_*$, and on compatible even fine periods, for $0< g_0< g_*$ and under \eqref{eq:c3-1-2},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-7-14}
    | E_{\mathrm{bdry}}|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}\,n_C(1+g_0r)\,e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}\;,
\end{equation}
after replacing $C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}$ by $C_L\max(C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}S_c,1)$; $g_*$ is at most the thresholds of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2}, the $g_H$ and the smallness condition of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4}, the threshold of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1} and the coupling below which the comparison of \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE} used in the proof holds. The constants are uniform in the compatible even periods, the contour location and the first-step histories.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\cite[(2.6)--(2.9)]{BalabanCRE} and $\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$ give $\theta\geqslant c_{\theta} g_0\pi_*$ for small coupling: each of the three terms of \eqref{eq:c3-7-4} is at least a fixed constant times $g_0p_0(g_0)$ or $g_1p_0(g_1)$, and $g_1/g_0$ is bounded above and below by \cite[(2.6)]{BalabanCRE}.

Since $\ell= LMR_1$ grows as a fixed power of $\log g_1^{-2}$ (\eqref{eq:c5-3-1}), $\log n_W= O(\log\log g_0^{-2})$; with the exponent of \cite{BalabanCRE}, $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r\geqslant 10$, $\pi_*^2\geqslant A_0^2(\tfrac12\log g_0^{-2})^{2p_0}$ dominates $4d_G\log g_0^{-1}$ and $\log n_W$ for small $g_0$, so $q= n_W\max(z_P,z_G)\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ with $c_*\coloneqq b_Gc_{\theta}^2/8$, for $g_0< g_*$.

Then Corollary~\ref{cor:c3-6-1}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-1} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} give $| E_{\mathrm{bdry}}|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}g_0r\,C_LS_cn_Cq+C_Ln_Cq\leqslant C_L\max(C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}S_c,1)\,n_C(1+g_0r)\,q$, and $q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ gives \eqref{eq:c3-7-14}.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope]\label{rem:c3-8-1}
Lemma~\ref{lem:exterior-response-bound} is proved from the Hessian, Schur, enlarged-chart and primitive derivative bounds of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} and the collar cutoff of Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}, with both hard-cutoff surface terms inside the bounded covariance; it is applied on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$.

Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5} holds on compatible even-period tori and uses the single-witness tails of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} and the reconstruction and measure identities of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}; the filling proximity of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} holds for a simultaneous or an iterated filling of small components.

The $R_1$-label step of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-2} rests on Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}, which uses local data of \cite{BalabanVAR}, with the local hypotheses of the existence and uniqueness theorem \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} verified where this paper's inputs allow and otherwise taken over as the application of \cite{BalabanVAR} to the determining sets of \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE}, uses the derivative-decay results of \cite{BalabanVAR} and the identification \cite[(3.17)--(3.19)]{BalabanCRE} as stated, and accepts Ba{\l}aban's gauge-conversion results at their stated regular-chart hypotheses through the extension statements of \cite{BalabanRG1}; of the characteristic factors of \cite[(1.11)]{BalabanCRE} it uses their nonvanishing at the minimum $U_1$ itself, the membership $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ of (B1) (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}, in the sense recorded in (B1)(iii) and (H4)).

This appendix controls the exterior-response and uncovered term only.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The Minimum Comparison from Local Data}\label{sec:c3-9}
This section proves the deterministic comparison \eqref{eq:c3-7-6} of the two minima from local data and, in Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-6}, the bound on the boundary field of \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE} used in Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar} and (B4) (Lemma~\ref{lem:axial-boundary-field}).

Of the branch hypothesis (B1) of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data} it uses the membership $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ of the minimum in the domain of integration of \cite[(1.11), p.~248]{BalabanCRE} (by \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR}) with the smallness statement (i) derived from it in (B1), the averaging constraint and the source axial mean gauge, which place $U_1$ in the regularity class of \cite{BalabanVAR} near $\Omega_1$ and so identify it with the regular critical orbit constructed below.

The sources are \cite{BalabanVAR}, \cite{BalabanCRE}, \cite{BalabanRG1}, and the averaging paper \cite{BalabanAVG}; Ba{\l}aban's existence and uniqueness result (\cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR}) is used at local hypotheses verified below where this paper's inputs allow, and otherwise as the application of \cite{BalabanVAR} to the determining sets of \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE} (where Ba{\l}aban states that all the results of \cite{BalabanVAR} are used for the averaging); his derivative-decay results (\cite[Proposition~9, (172), and (190)]{BalabanVAR}), the gauge transformation of \cite[Proposition~2]{BalabanVAR} and the identification \cite[(3.17)--(3.19)]{BalabanCRE} are used as stated, and his gauge-conversion results are accepted at their stated regular-chart hypotheses through the extension statements of \cite{BalabanRG1}.

\begin{proposition}[Comparison of the Global and Local Minima]\label{prop:c3-9-1}
There are constants $C_{L,G}$, $c_{L,G}>0$, depending on $L$, $G$, $M_1$, $M_2$ and the source parameters and fixed before $g_0$, independent of the fluctuation, its $R_1$ label, the exterior history and the torus, such that, on compatible even fine periods (every fine period is then at least $2\ell$, which the lifts below need), for every admissible $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$ and every eligible cube $Q\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$, on its twice enlarged free-bond carrier,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-1}
    \sup_{b\in(Q_w^{[2]})^*}| U_1(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1e^{-c_{L,G}LM_2R_1}<\delta_0/10\;,
\end{equation}
for $g_0$ below a threshold depending on $L$, $G$, $M_1$, $M_2$ and the source constants (the conditions $\alpha\leqslant a_1$, $B_3\alpha\leqslant a_0$, the smallness of $\alpha$ at \cite[(172) and (187)]{BalabanVAR}, $CL^2\varepsilon_0\leqslant 1$, $\ell>\max(2L+4,RM_1)$, $LM_2R_1\geqslant 2LM_1+C_L$ and the chart reductions of the proof; this threshold is part of $g_*$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}), the last inequality by Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-5}.
\end{proposition}

The fine periods are multiples of $\ell$ (compatibility, Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}) and, by the hypothesis of the proposition, even (the restriction of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}), and $\ell= LMR_1$ is odd ($L$ is odd and $M$, $R_1$ are powers of $L$, \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}), so every compatible fine period is at least $2\ell$; since $w\leqslant L^2M_2R_1$ and $M\geqslant 8LM_2$ (\eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}), $\operatorname{side}(Q_w^{[4]})\leqslant 9L^2M_2R_1\leqslant 9\ell/8<2\ell$, so this determining box and its fixed-range stencils have lifted copies before the next periodic image for small coupling.

If $\Omega_1$ is the full torus there is no exterior collar to freeze and the same argument uses the periodic problem of \cite{BalabanVAR}.

The quantity in \eqref{eq:c3-9-1} concerns a simultaneously gauge-covariant pair of links: their relative product transforms by conjugation at the initial endpoint, so its norm is gauge invariant. The proof occupies the rest of this section.

\subsubsection{Source Inputs and the Local-Domain Verification}\label{sec:c3-9-1}
$U_1$ is the critical minimum of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE}, the unique critical point in the domain of integration in (1.11), supplied by \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} with the prescribed $V$, $V_0$ and the source axial mean gauge (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}, recorded in (B1) as $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$). This membership gives, by (B1)(i), $| U_1(\partial p)-\id|<\varepsilon_0$ for every plaquette $p\subset\Omega_1^{\sim}$ and the axial condition $| U_1(y,x)-\id|<\varepsilon_0$ at the block centres of $\Omega_1^{\sim(1)}$, so that $U_1$ lies in the regularity class \cite[(6)]{BalabanVAR} with radius $C_L\varepsilon_0$ on the outer domain $\Omega_0$ of \cite{BalabanVAR} below, by the same conjugation and counting argument as for $\widehat U$ in the local-domain verification (\cite{BalabanVAR} counts as plaquettes of a region those with a corner in it, so $\Omega_0$ is taken to be the enlarged domain $\Omega^+$ shrunk by $\ell/2$, a union of $M_1$-blocks every plaquette with a corner in which lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim}$; the remaining separation $\ell/2$ from $\Omega_1$ keeps the spacing condition \cite[(1)]{BalabanVAR}); the localisation below verifies the hypotheses of \cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} for the localised problem near $\Omega_1$. The plaquette variables of $U_1$ on $\Omega_1^{\sim}$ are thus within $\varepsilon_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)^2\varepsilon_1$ of the identity (\cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE}).

The local minimum $U_{1,Q}$ is \cite[(1.2)]{BalabanCRE} with determining set $\mathfrak B_Q\coloneqq\mathbf B_1(Q_w^{[4]})$ and reference data $D^0_Q=\dot M(Q_1^{s*}V)|_{\mathfrak B_Q}$; it has the corresponding mixed-scale regularity of \cite{BalabanVAR}, with the scale-zero boundary bound described below, and the same coarse averages $V$ on the interior determining region (the interior coarse labels of $Q_w^{[4]}$ lie in $\Omega_1$, where the constraint $\mathsf M(U_1)= V$ holds: $Q\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$ is at $\ell^{\infty}$ distance at least $\ell$ from $\Omega_1^c$, and $4w\leqslant 4L^2M_2R_1\leqslant \ell/2$ by $M\geqslant 8LM_2$, \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}; \cite[p.~250]{BalabanCRE} states this containment).

These are the hypotheses of the derivation \cite[(3.17)--(3.19)]{BalabanCRE}, whose only field is the minimum; at $k=0$ the fine spacing is $\eta=1$ and $V^{(0)}= U_1$, $V^{(0)}_Q= U_{1,Q}$.

\emph{The local-domain verification.} The argument runs before the $P_0$, $P_1$, $Q_1$ resummation, at any supported history contributing to the fixed $\Omega_1$, $V$, $V_0$, with fine field $\widehat U$. Let $\Omega^+\coloneqq\Omega_1^{\sim1}$ be the enlarged fine domain (the macro enlargement of \cite[(1.10)]{BalabanCRE}), with $\widehat U= V_0$ fixed on the collar $\Omega^+\setminus\Omega_1$. Outside $\Omega^+$ the original field is retained and its action terms are omitted from the variational problem: once $\ell>2L+4$, every plaquette or block-gauge term containing an unfrozen variable lies in $\Omega^+$, so the omitted terms are constants, and the constrained first variation is exactly that of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} (the gauge functional $G$ of (1.12) has zero first variation at $U_1$, each of its nonnegative summands vanishing there since $U_1(y,x)=\id$ in the source axial mean gauge, \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}, so the first variations of $A+G$ and of $A$ agree on the constraint tangent space at $U_1$).

\cite[(1.10)]{BalabanCRE} and the following sentence separate $\Omega_1$ from the earlier bad regions by at least two macro layers, so every plaquette and averaging stencil in $\Omega^+$ lies in the $P_0$-good region, where at this unresummed stage $|\widehat U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}<\varepsilon_0$.

If the canonical outer operation has already omitted these factors, they equal one on the support of the retained original-field factors ((B3)(i), the form in which the removal statement of \cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE} before (1.11) is recorded), so restoring them changes no integral; since the history summands are nonnegative, a point of nonzero resummed density has at least one supported unresummed history. This restoration concerns $\widehat U$ and controls the prescribed collar $V_0$.

Conjugation and the bounded number of incident plaquettes give $| D^*_{\widehat U}\partial\widehat U|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{inc}}\varepsilon_0$ on the collar and the variable region ($C_{\mathrm{inc}}$ the incidence count), and multiplying by the largest of the fixed scale weights $L^2$, $L^3$ puts $\widehat U$ in the class \cite[(6)]{BalabanVAR} with radius $C_L\varepsilon_0$. Its fixed data are exactly $V_0$ on the fine collar and $V$ on the interior coarse labels, since the original averaging constraint is retained.

The carriers are the positive-bond sets $E(X)$. The fixed fine collar carrier is $E(\Omega^+)\setminus E(\Omega_1)$, so no crossing bond that is a variable of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} is fixed. The hierarchy for \cite{BalabanVAR} has outer fine domain $\Omega^+$, inner block domain $\Omega_1$ and determining set this bond-set difference at scale zero together with $\Omega_1$ at scale one, with the mixed-bond convention of \cite[(7)]{BalabanVAR}; its spacing condition (1) holds because the separating macro layer has width $\ell$, exceeding the fixed $RM_1$ of \cite{BalabanVAR} for small coupling.

For a mixed determining plaquette $p'$, every coarse bond of $p'$ outside the scale-one determining set is replaced by the block average of the scale-zero data, as prescribed in \cite[(7)]{BalabanVAR}: the original constraint makes the resulting loop an ordinary fine plaquette of $\widehat U$ or a coarse plaquette of its block average, and \cite[Proposition~1, (51)]{BalabanAVG}, bounds the latter, in the operator norm of \cite{BalabanAVG}, by $L^2\alpha_0+C(L^2\alpha_0)^2\leqslant 2L^2\alpha_0$ with $\alpha_0=\sqrt N\varepsilon_0$ for $g_0$ small ($CL^2\alpha_0\leqslant 1$; the conversion $\|\bigcdot \|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant \sqrt Nh$ of the conventions covers the case of the normalised Hilbert--Schmidt cutoff norm), which is also the explicit bound of \cite{BalabanCRE} before (1.2).

The constraint \cite[(3)]{BalabanVAR} and \cite[Proposition~1]{BalabanAVG} are stated for Ba{\l}aban's earlier averaging; their use with the averaging \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} is Ba{\l}aban's own transfer in \cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE} (all the results of \cite{BalabanVAR} used for its averaging) and the extension statement of \cite{BalabanRG1} after (0.12), accepted as such. So the entire determining set of the localised problem has data regularity in the sense of \cite{BalabanVAR} at most $C_L\varepsilon_0$ ($C_L$ including $\sqrt N$).

\cite[Theorem~1]{BalabanVAR} therefore constructs the regular critical orbit for these data, at radius $B_3C_L\varepsilon_0$, unique in the regularity class (6) of radius $\varepsilon_0^{\mathrm V}\coloneqq \max(C_L\varepsilon_0,B_3C_L\varepsilon_0)\leqslant a_0$ for small $g_0$, a class containing $U_1$, with both the plaquette and the divergence bounds (2).

The minimum $U_1$ of \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} lies on this orbit: it is critical for the localised problem, since the localisation changes the action by constants only, for every admissible variation, and it lies in the regularity class of \cite{BalabanVAR} on $\Omega^+$ by its membership $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$ (the first paragraph of this subsection); the uniqueness in the class identifies the two.

Restricted to $Q_w^{[4]}$ the same bound gives membership in the local uniqueness class, with fixed scale and norm conversions (that the results of \cite{BalabanVAR} hold for the determining set $\mathbf B_1(Q_w^{[4]})$ of \cite[(1.2)]{BalabanCRE}, whose fine layer has width between $LM_1$ and $2LM_1$, p.256, in place of the spacing condition \cite[(1)]{BalabanVAR} for that layer, is Ba{\l}aban's application of \cite{BalabanVAR} to the determining sets of \cite{BalabanCRE}, p.256, taken over as such); since $\varepsilon_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)^2\varepsilon_1$ by \cite[(2.8), p.~256]{BalabanCRE} (with $n=1$, $m=0$), the radius is $C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1$, below the $a_0$ of \cite{BalabanVAR} for small coupling.

The fine boundary layer of $U_{1,Q}$ has the scale-zero bound of \cite{BalabanVAR}: the plaquettes of its straight-extension data are trivial or equal to coarse plaquette holonomies of $V$, bounded by $2L^2\varepsilon_0$, so its mixed-scale data are regular with the same parameter $C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1$.

\subsubsection{The Boundary Data and Their Size}\label{sec:c3-9-2}
Let $D_Q\coloneqq\dot M(U_1)|_{\mathfrak B_Q}$ and, on the determining set, let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-2}
    B_Q(e)\coloneqq\tfrac1i\log\bigl(D_Q(e)D^0_Q(e)^{-1}\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
Both data are defined by the source averaging operation on this regular configuration; the determining interior carries scale-one coarse bonds and its boundary layer the finer determining variables, as defined after \cite[(2.12)]{BalabanCRE}; the mixed determining plaquettes and the local averages are those of \cite[(1.2), (2.12)--(2.16)]{BalabanCRE}.

For the straight extension of \cite[(1.3)]{BalabanCRE} every intrablock contour is the identity, every centre-to-centre path crossing a specified interface has transport $V(c)$, and every relative closed holonomy of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1} is the identity, so the logarithmic correction vanishes and $\mathsf M(Q_1^{s*}V)(c)= V(c)$; on the interior both data equal $V$, hence $B_Q=0$ there, and $\operatorname{supp}B_Q$ lies in the boundary layer of width $2LM_1$ of $Q_w^{[4]}$, the support statement preceding \cite[(3.18)]{BalabanCRE}.

The principal logarithm is legitimate because the reasoning after \cite[(3.17)]{BalabanCRE} bounds the argument of the logarithm by $C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1$ (the printed coefficient $44d^2B_3$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} belongs to its own regularity coefficient; the enlarged local coefficient is kept inside $C_{L,G}$). Thus
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-3}
    \| B_Q\|_{\infty}\leqslant C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1\;.
\end{equation}
For \cite[(172)]{BalabanVAR} with its absolute constant $C_1$, its small parameter is $\alpha= K_{\alpha}\varepsilon_0$, with $K_{\alpha}$ dominating all determining-data, uniqueness-class and $B_Q$ bounds (for the last, $\varepsilon_1\leqslant (1+\beta_0)\varepsilon_0$ by \cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE}); then $| e^{itB_Q}-\id|\leqslant | tB_Q|\leqslant \alpha$ and $C_1=1$ suffices.

\cite[Proposition~9 and (190)]{BalabanVAR} are applied with this $\alpha$, not with the identically named $\varepsilon_1$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}; for small $g_0$, $\alpha\leqslant a_1$, $B_3\alpha\leqslant a_0$, and $\alpha$ lies below the thresholds of \cite{BalabanVAR} ``for $\varepsilon_1$ sufficiently small'' at (172) and (187) (pp.305 and 308); and $\varepsilon_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)^2\varepsilon_1$ (\cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE}) converts the resulting $C\alpha$ bounds into $C'\varepsilon_1$.

\subsubsection{Integrating the Local Derivative Estimate}\label{sec:c3-9-3}
Let $\mathscr H_Q(B)$ be the relative Landau-gauge logarithm of the local minimal-configuration map of \cite[Proposition~9]{BalabanVAR} on $\mathfrak B_Q$ with reference $U_{1,Q}$, normalised by $\mathscr H_Q(0)=0$; this is the map of \cite[(3.17)]{BalabanCRE}, with its $L^{-1}$ scale factor at $k=0$.

\cite[(3.17)]{BalabanCRE} identifies the map at $B_Q$ with the restriction of $U_1$ up to the source gauge restoration: both lie on the unique regular critical orbit with determining data $D_Q$, the former satisfying the constraint up to the gauge transformation of \cite[Proposition~2]{BalabanVAR}.

For the criticality, a local admissible variation fixes the determining fine layer and the averages on the interior coarse rows; extended by zero outside $Q_w^{[4]}$ it preserves every global average and exterior value in \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE}, because the fixed layer is wider than the plaquette and averaging range. The first variation of the global action vanishes and its local part is the local action variation; the gauge functional of the source axial mean gauge, in which the variational problem \cite[(1.12)]{BalabanCRE} is posed (as recalled in the local-domain verification of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}), has zero first variation at an axial mean configuration, where each of its nonnegative summands attains zero. So the restriction of $U_1$ is critical for the local action, it lies in the uniqueness class of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1} by its regularity there (from $U_1\in D^{(11)}(V,V_0)$), and the uniqueness identifies its orbit with the local analytic solution.

\cite[(190), Proposition~9]{BalabanVAR}, gives the functional derivative with the mixed-scale weights; at one step the scale labels are $0$ and $1$, so the powers of $L$ in those weights are fixed constants, and a determining bond $e$ of the outer layer and an interior bond $b$ satisfy the bound $C_{L,G}e^{-c_{L,G}d(b,e)}$, the unit-density measure at the finer level and the scale-one determining measure contributing fixed $L$-dependent factors.

Here $d(b,e)$ is the $\ell^{\infty}$ distance between the initial vertices of $b$ and $e$ on the fine lattice. The distance in \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR} is that of \cite[(2.46)]{BalabanPRT2} (\cite[p.~288]{BalabanVAR}), which charges one unit for each fine bond of a contour in the scale-zero region and one unit for each coarse bond, of fine length $L$, in the scale-one region, and is evaluated at the block points of the two endpoints; so it is at least $L^{-1}(d(b,e)-L)$, and the rate $\delta_{\mathrm P}/8$ of (190), with $\delta_{\mathrm P}$ the decay rate of \cite[p.~423]{BalabanPBG} ((H4)), gives $c_{L,G}=\delta_{\mathrm P}/(8L)$, the factor $e^{\delta_{\mathrm P}/8}$ entering $C_{L,G}$. Integrating along $tB_Q$, $t\in[0,1]$, and summing the labels,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-4}
    |\mathscr H_Q(B_Q;b)|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1\sum_{e\in\operatorname{supp}B_Q}e^{-c_{L,G}d(b,e)}\leqslant C'_{L,G}\varepsilon_1e^{-c'_{L,G}d(b,\operatorname{supp}B_Q)}\;,
\end{equation}
where for the second inequality each exponential is split into two halves, $e^{-c_{L,G}d(b,e)}\leqslant e^{-c_{L,G}d(b,\operatorname{supp}B_Q)/2}e^{-c_{L,G}d(b,e)/2}$, and the remaining sum over $e$ is bounded by the infinite-lattice sum $\sum_ee^{-c_{L,G}d(b,e)/2}$ over the bonds of $\mathbb Z^4$ (four per site) through injective nearest lifts, a constant depending on $c_{L,G}$ only; so $c'_{L,G}= c_{L,G}/2$ and no volume-dependent constant enters. For a bond $b\in(Q_w^{[2]})^*$ (its initial vertex is within one unit of $Q_w^{[2]}$, a difference absorbed in $C_L$),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-5}
    d(b,\operatorname{supp}B_Q)\geqslant 2w-2LM_1-C_L\geqslant LM_2R_1
\end{equation}
once $w\geqslant LM_2R_1$ (the collar-width convention of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}) and $LM_2R_1\geqslant 2LM_1+C_L$, which holds for small $g_0$ since $R_1\to\infty$ (Section~\ref{app:thresholds}); the first inequality is the distance from $Q_w^{[2]}$ to the complement of $Q_w^{[4]}$ less the width $2LM_1$ of the boundary layer carrying $\operatorname{supp}B_Q$ and the bond offsets. This holds for either candidate common width $w$.

\subsubsection{Restoring the Source Gauge}\label{sec:c3-9-4}
The transformation of \cite[Proposition~2]{BalabanVAR} is not centre-fixing: its condition is $(\overline{R_0u})^j=\id$ on $\Lambda_j$, in particular $u=\id$ on the fine determining layer (\cite[p.~281]{BalabanVAR}), and at one step its interior condition $\overline{R_0u}(y)=\id$ does not imply $u(y)=\id$.

The restoring transformation $u_Q$ is that of \cite[(3.17)]{BalabanCRE}, defined by this source normalisation: the configuration $e^{iL^{-1}\mathscr H_Q(B_Q)}U_{1,Q}$ of Proposition 9 is in the relative gauge of Proposition 2 and satisfies the constraint with data $D_Q$ up to that gauge, so it lies on the orbit of the restriction of $U_1$, and $u_Q$ is the transformation carrying it to $U_1$, whose values at the block centres need not be the identity and are retained. At the first step, with the $\eta=1$ of \cite{BalabanCRE} and its convention (1.17), on the required bonds
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-6}
    U_1(b)= u_Q(b_-)^{-1}e^{iL^{-1}\mathscr H_Q(B_Q;b)}U_{1,Q}(b)\,u_Q(b_+)\;.
\end{equation}
The local inputs of the transferred source estimates are the uniqueness and regularity class of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}, the small supported $B_Q$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-2} and the response bound \eqref{eq:c3-9-4} on both endpoint blocks and the crossing bond.

Let $\rho_{\mathrm{av}}>0$ be an analytic mean neighbourhood radius for the finite source contour families, with derivative bounds on its closed half-radius neighbourhood; the coupling $g_0$ is chosen after it so that the reference path-family diameter and its perturbation are both less than $\rho_{\mathrm{av}}/4$ (the regular-chart reduction).

The block-local gauge inequality \eqref{eq:c3-9-7} below is the transferred source result; the following path description gives its one-step support and its constants. In \cite{BalabanAVG} the equations determining $u_Q$ are (77)--(87), with its expression in the relative fields given in (106)--(108): at one step the product in (106) has a single $j=0$ factor, a reference-unitary conjugation of the inverse block average followed by a local relative path transport, and the centre factor (87) is retained. Unitary conjugations preserve the norm, each path has length at most $(2d+1)L$, so the telescoping product identity bounds the relative deviation by $C_L$ times the largest relative-link deviation in the block, and the analytic averaging bound of (161)--(163) bounds the block-average deviation by the same quantity after reducing the chart. The transferred result reads
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c3-9-7}
    \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_y}| u_Q(x)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{L,G}\sup_{b\in E(\mathcal B_y)}|\mathscr H_Q(B_Q;b)|_{\sigma}\;,
\end{equation}
the factor $L^{-1}$ of \cite[(3.17)]{BalabanCRE} absorbed into the constant.

The restoring map is relative to the reference pair: under a simultaneous gauge change $h$ of field and reference its representative is $u^h_Q(x)= h(x)u_Q(x)h(x)^{-1}$ (by conjugation of the relative action, \cite[(16)--(17)]{BalabanVAR}, and of its reference-dependent gauge condition), so $| u_Q(x)-\id|_{\sigma}$ is a conjugation-invariant scalar of the relative construction; the centre contribution $u_Q(y)$ is retained.

\cite{BalabanAVG} uses its older averaging definition; the application here rests on Ba{\l}aban's extension statements, \cite{BalabanRG1} after (0.10) (the considerations and results of \cite{BalabanRG1}, and those of the earlier papers, hold for every group mean with the properties (0.5)--(0.9)) and \cite{BalabanRG1} after (0.12) (the average (0.12) has properties similar to those of (0.4), all results of \cite{BalabanAVG} hold for it, with proofs mostly unchanged and otherwise with minor modifications, and both definitions are equally good for the purposes of \cite{BalabanRG1}; the coverage of (0.4) rests on this last remark). On these statements \eqref{eq:c3-9-7} is the transfer of the results of \cite{BalabanAVG} to the averaging and mean gauge of \cite{BalabanRG1}; \cite[(3.17)--(3.19)]{BalabanCRE} uses the transferred results in the same way for the later scheme, as does \cite{BalabanRG1} for its gauge conversions ((3.26)--(3.27) with \cite[(77)]{BalabanAVG}, and (3.39) with \cite[(97)]{BalabanAVG}, retaining the centre-block gauge factors; reference [12] of \cite{BalabanRG1} is \cite{BalabanAVG}).

For the bond $b$ of \eqref{eq:c3-9-1}, \eqref{eq:c3-9-4} applies on both endpoint blocks, on $b$ itself and on the paths entering the gauge factors, which enlarges the input set by at most $2L+2$, already included in the $C_L$ of \eqref{eq:c3-9-5}. The relative exponential and both endpoint factors of \eqref{eq:c3-9-6} then give $| U_1(b)U_{1,Q}(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1e^{-c_{L,G}LM_2R_1}$; both endpoint gauge factors of \cite[(3.18)]{BalabanCRE} are retained.

\subsubsection{Conclusion of the Proof}\label{sec:c3-9-5}
\cite[(2.6), (2.8)]{BalabanCRE} bound $\varepsilon_1/\delta_0$ by fixed source constants and $R_1$ grows as a power of $\log g_1^{-2}$, so the bound is $<\delta_0/10$ for small $g_0$, which completes the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}.

\subsubsection{The Boundary Field of Ba{\l}aban's Equation (1.21)}\label{sec:c3-9-6}
The same argument bounds the field $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ of \cite[(1.21)]{BalabanCRE} on the bonds of $S_1^*$, where it enters the change of variables (1.22) through Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection} and \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs}.

\begin{lemma}[The Boundary Field on $S_1$]\label{lem:axial-boundary-field}
There are constants $C_{\mathrm H}$, $c_{\mathrm H}>0$, depending on $L$, $G$, $M_1$, $M_2$, and the source constants and fixed before $g_0$, independent of the fluctuation, its $R_1$ label, the exterior history, and the torus, such that, for $g_0$ below a threshold depending on the same quantities (the conditions of Sections~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}, \ref{sec:c3-9-2}, and~\ref{sec:c3-9-4} and those named in the proof), for every admissible $(\Omega_1,V,V_0)$, every large-fluctuation region $R_1$ of the history sum, and every $b\in S_1^*$, with $U_1'\coloneqq U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,V)$ the representative fixed in (B1),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:axial-boundary-field}
    | U_1(b)U_1'(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{\mathrm H}\varepsilon_1e^{-c_{\mathrm H}LMR_1}\;.
\end{equation}
Consequently $U_1(b)U_1'(b)^{-1}$ lies in the chart domain, $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)= L\log\bigl(U_1(b)U_1'(b)^{-1}\bigr)$ satisfies $|\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)|_{\sigma}\leqslant \frac\pi2LC_{\mathrm H}\varepsilon_1e^{-c_{\mathrm H}LMR_1}$, and \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs} holds once $\frac\pi2LC_{\mathrm H}(1+\beta_0)(A_0/A_1)e^{-c_{\mathrm H}LMR_1}\leqslant \frac1{40}$ (item 5 of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}).
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-9-1}, Sections~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}--\ref{sec:c3-9-4}, for the pair $(U_1,U_1')$ in place of $(U_1,U_{1,Q})$, without the cube localisation: the reference problem is that of \cite{BalabanCRE}, so no lift and no condition on the periods enters. The norm $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ is the cutoff norm of \eqref{eq:boundary-bijection-inputs}.

\emph{The problem and the argument.} $U_1'$ is the minimal configuration for the determining data named at p.251 ((B1)): the conditions of (1.12) on the rows of $(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c$, and on $\Lambda_1^{\sim}\setminus\Lambda_1$ the determining set $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$ with the data $D^0= M^{\bigcdot }(Q_1^{s*}V)$. The configuration, and with it the first equality of (1.21), lives on $\Lambda_1^c=(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c\cup(\Lambda_1^{\sim}\setminus\Lambda_1)$, the union of the two domains on which p.251 determines it, and $\Lambda_1$ carries no variable of the problem; every plaquette with a corner in $\Lambda_1$ has its bonds in $\Lambda_1$ or in the fixed layer, which is at least $LM_1$ wide, so these terms are constants of the problem and are omitted, as are those off $\Omega^+$.

The hierarchy for \cite{BalabanVAR} is that of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1} with $\Lambda_1$ removed from its domains: $V_0$ is fixed on the collar $\Omega^+\setminus\Omega_1$, $\Omega^+=\Omega_1^{\sim1}$, and the action terms off $\Omega^+$ are omitted as constants; the scale-zero determining set is the collar together with the fine layer of $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$, and the scale-one determining set is the set of coarse bonds of $\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c$ off that layer. The data are regular as there: the collar lies in the $P_0$-good region, the plaquettes of $Q_1^{s*}V$ on the layer are trivial or coarse plaquette holonomies of $V$, bounded by $2L^2\varepsilon_0$, and the mixed determining plaquettes are bounded by \cite[Proposition~1, (51)]{BalabanAVG}.

That the results of \cite{BalabanVAR} hold for this determining set, whose fine layer has width between $LM_1$ and $2LM_1$ (p.256), in place of the spacing condition \cite[(1)]{BalabanVAR} for the layer, is Ba{\l}aban's application of \cite{BalabanVAR} to the determining sets of \cite{BalabanCRE} (p.256, and p.251 for this problem), taken over as such, as for $\mathbf B_1(Q_w^{[4]})$ in Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}.

By the first equality of (1.21), $U_1= U_1(\Omega_1\cap\Lambda_1^c,M^{\bigcdot }(U_1))$, $U_1$ lies on the minimal orbit of the same problem with the data $D= M^{\bigcdot }(U_1)$ (the criticality and uniqueness argument of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-3} gives the same identification). \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE} applies \cite[Proposition~9]{BalabanVAR} to this problem (``The dependence is analytic, and the function $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ has the exponential decay property. It was formulated in (190) Sect.~G of [15] for the Landau gauge''); let $\mathscr H$ be its relative Landau-gauge function with reference $U_1'$, normalised by $\mathscr H(0)=0$, and let $B$ be the chart logarithm of $D(D^0)^{-1}$ (the $\frac1i\log$ of \cite{BalabanCRE}), the argument of $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}$ in (1.21).

\emph{Support and size of $B$.} On the rows of $(\Lambda_1^{\sim})^c$ the two data coincide, the conditions there being those of (1.12) for both. On the coarse bonds of $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$ in $\Lambda_1^{\sim}\setminus\Lambda_1$, the only ones entering (p.251), both data equal $V$: these bonds lie in $\Omega_1$, where $\bar U_1= V$, and $M(Q_1^{s*}V)= V$ for the straight extension (Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-2}). So $B$ vanishes off the fine layer of $\mathbf B_1(\Lambda_1^c)$, on which $D$ and $D^0$ are the bond variables of $U_1$ and of $Q_1^{s*}V$ (\cite[(2.11)]{BalabanCRE} at the first step).

That layer lies within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $2LM_1$ of $\Lambda_1$ (\cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE} for the domain $\Lambda_1^c$: the coarse part of $\mathbf B_1(\Omega)$ contains $\Omega^{\sim-2}$, the enlargement taken for $M_1$-cubes, of side $LM_1$ in fine units); its width is between one and two $M_1$-cubes (p.256), and \cite[p.~251]{BalabanCRE} describes it as ``one layer of $M_1$-cubes touching $\partial\Lambda_1$ and contained in $\Lambda_1^c$''. Since $\Omega_1$ and $R_1'$ are unions of $LMR_1$-cubes and $\Lambda_1\subseteq\Omega_1^{\sim-2}\cap(R_1'^{\sim})^c$, every site within $\ell^{\infty}$ distance $LMR_1-1$ of $\Lambda_1$ lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}\setminus R_1'$; for small $g_0$ ($2LM_1+1<LMR_1-1$) the layer therefore lies in $\Omega_1^{\sim-1}$, where $U_1$ is regular and in the source axial mean gauge ((B1)(i)), and the two-block comparison of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-2} gives $\| B\|_{\infty}\leqslant C_{L,G}\varepsilon_1$. \cite[(172)]{BalabanVAR} is met as there, with $\alpha= K_{\alpha}\varepsilon_0$, $K_{\alpha}$ dominating also this bound, and $C_1=1$.

\emph{Distance.} Every site of $S_1=(\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1})\cup R_1$ is thus at $\ell^{\infty}$ distance at least $LMR_1$ from $\Lambda_1$ ($R_1\subseteq R_1'$), and the filling modification after (1.20) only removes cubes from $\Lambda_1$. For $b\in S_1^*$ (it has an endpoint in $S_1$) and $b'$ equal to $b$ or a bond of one of its two endpoint blocks, the initial vertex of $b'$ is within $2L+1$ of a site of $S_1$, and the initial vertex of a bond of the layer is within $2LM_1+1$ of $\Lambda_1$; so, with $d$ the $\ell^{\infty}$ distance between initial vertices of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-3},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:axial-boundary-distance}
    d(b',\operatorname{supp}B)\geqslant LMR_1-2LM_1-2L-2\geqslant \tfrac12LMR_1
\end{equation}
once $LMR_1\geqslant 4LM_1+4L+4$, which holds for small $g_0$ since $R_1\to\infty$.

\emph{The Landau-gauge function.} \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR}, integrated along $tB$, $t\in[0,1]$, and summed over $\operatorname{supp}B$ as in \eqref{eq:c3-9-4}, gives $|\mathscr H(B;b')|_{\sigma}\leqslant C'_{L,G}\varepsilon_1e^{-c'_{L,G}d(b',\operatorname{supp}B)}$ for every bond $b'$ of the problem, with the constants of \eqref{eq:c3-9-4}; the rate $c'_{L,G}=\delta_{\mathrm P}/(16L)$ is fixed before $g_0$, coming from the rate $\delta_{\mathrm P}/8$ of \cite[(190)]{BalabanVAR} in the distance \cite[(2.46)]{BalabanPRT2}, converted to the fine $\ell^{\infty}$ distance in Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-3}, with $\delta_{\mathrm P}$ the decay rate defined in \cite[p.~423]{BalabanPBG} after Theorem~3.12, a constant of $d$ and $L$.

\cite{BalabanVAR} states (190), and the representation (189) behind it, without the calculation (p.308, ``We do not perform these calculations here''); (190) is Ba{\l}aban's statement, taken over as stated.

\emph{Restoring the axial gauge.} As in Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-4}, the configuration $e^{iL^{-1}\mathscr H(B)}U_1'$ of \cite[Proposition~9]{BalabanVAR} lies on the orbit of $U_1$, and the restoring transformation $u$ carrying it to $U_1$, with its centre values retained, gives \eqref{eq:c3-9-6} with $(U_1',\mathscr H)$ in place of $(U_{1,Q},\mathscr H_Q)$ and satisfies the block-local bound \eqref{eq:c3-9-7}, $\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_y}| u(x)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant C_{L,G}\sup_{b'\in E(\mathcal B_y)}|\mathscr H(B;b')|_{\sigma}$: at one step the transformation on a block is fixed by the relative transports along the contours inside that block and by its centre factor (\cite[(77)--(87) and (106)--(108)]{BalabanAVG}, as recorded there), which is the locality of the axial gauge on the unit lattice; \eqref{eq:c3-9-7} is the accepted transfer of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-4}, applied to the function of (1.21) as \cite{BalabanCRE} applies (3.17)--(3.18) to the corresponding function at the general step, ``with similar bounds'' (p.269).

The target is $U_1$ itself: the minimal configurations with the data $D$ form one orbit, in the class of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}, of the gauge transformations equal to the identity on the set $\mathfrak B_k$ of \cite{BalabanVAR} (\cite[p.~256]{BalabanCRE}; \cite[(4) and Theorem~1, pp.~278--279]{BalabanVAR}), in which the axial gauge determines a unique element (\cite[(0.6) and (0.11)]{BalabanRG1}, as recorded in (B1)), and $U_1$ is in the axial gauge (\cite[p.~248]{BalabanCRE}), so it is that element.

At an endpoint off $\Omega_1$, a point of the fixed exterior field $V_0$ (scale-zero data, as in the hierarchy of Section~\ref{sec:c3-9-1}), $u=\id$ (\cite[p.~281]{BalabanVAR} for the transformation of \cite[Proposition~2]{BalabanVAR}, and \cite[(4)]{BalabanVAR} for the orbit element, the collar being part of $\mathfrak B_k$). For $b\in S_1^*$, unitary invariance and conjugation give
\begin{equation*}
    \begin{aligned}
    | U_1(b)U_1'(b)^{-1}-\id|_{\sigma}&\leqslant | u(b_-)-\id|_{\sigma}+L^{-1}|\mathscr H(B;b)|_{\sigma}+| u(b_+)-\id|_{\sigma}\\
    &\leqslant (2C_{L,G}+1)C'_{L,G}\varepsilon_1e^{-c'_{L,G}LMR_1/2}
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation*}
by \eqref{eq:axial-boundary-distance}, which is \eqref{eq:axial-boundary-field} with $C_{\mathrm H}\coloneqq(2C_{L,G}+1)C'_{L,G}$ and $c_{\mathrm H}= c'_{L,G}/2$.

\emph{The consequences.} For small $g_0$ the right side of \eqref{eq:axial-boundary-field} is below $r_G/\sqrt N$, so $U_1(b)U_1'(b)^{-1}$ lies in the chart domain (the norm facts at the start of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:boundary-bijection}), and its chart logarithm $X= L^{-1}\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)$ satisfies $| X|_{\sigma}\leqslant \frac\pi2| e^{iX}-\id|_{\sigma}$, which is the bound on $\mathbf H_{1,Ax}(b)$. With $\varepsilon_1/\delta_0\leqslant (1+\beta_0)A_0/A_1$ (\cite[(2.8)]{BalabanCRE} and $\delta_0=(A_1/A_0)\varepsilon_0$), it is at most $\delta_0/40$ under the stated condition, which holds for small $g_0$ at fixed $L$, $M$, and $M_1$ since $R_1\to\infty$.
\end{proof}

\section{The Signed Integrated Wilson Defects}\label{app:signed-defects}
This appendix bounds the defect term of the branch identity \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity} at the carrier $I$ of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}, under the original history law: the joint defects $R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$ of \eqref{eq:part1-joint-defect} are summed with their restricted reference sums before absolute values are taken, each closed group is compared with its flat value by one background derivative along a local coefficient path, and the comparison is paid by the Gaussian reserve, the positive host comparison and the positive group summation of Sections~\ref{sec:c4-4}, \ref{sec:c4-7} and~\ref{sec:c4-8}. The result is Proposition~\ref{prop:c4-12-3}: on compatible even fine periods and for the square geometry of Section~\ref{sec:extent-weights},
\begin{equation*}
    | E_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}+e^{C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})}-1\;,
\end{equation*}
with $\rho= O(g_0^2(1+r)^4)$, $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$, $b=\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor$, $\pi_*=\min(p_0(g_0),p_0(g_1))$, $C'_L=8C_L$ with the contour constant $C_L$ of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7} and the tail exponent $c_*$ of Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}, and $C_{\chi}$, $c$ fixed before the coupling.

The regional scalar $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$ remains inside the expectation; its identification with the perimeter/corner coefficient is Appendix~\ref{app:regional-scalar}.

\subsection{Operand and Retained Normalisation}\label{sec:c4-1}
The groups $W$ and the compatible families $\mathfrak B$ are those of Definition~\ref{def:groups}; the closed pairings $A_{\xi}(\mathcal S)$, the scalar references $a_W$, the restricted reference sums $S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}$ and the joint defects $R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$ are those of \eqref{eq:part1-closed-family-pairing}, \eqref{eq:part1-reference-group} and Proposition~\ref{prop:joint-extraction}. Every source term, the Wilson contraction $f_{\xi}$ and each group's closed contraction of Definition~\ref{def:groups}, is a gauge-invariant closed contraction (Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-2}). The signed family sum and the defect term are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-1-1}
    \mathscr R_{\xi}\coloneqq\sum_{\substack{\mathfrak B\ne\varnothing\\\mathfrak B\ \mathrm{compatible}}}S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B),\qquad
    E_{\mathrm{def}}\coloneqq\frac{1}{\mathcal Z_0}\int\mathcal O\bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\mathscr R_{\xi}\bigr](V)\,\dd V\;.
\end{equation}
The weight is the branch weight $\mathsf w_{\xi}= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}$ of \eqref{eq:c-collar-identity}, the outer operation $\mathcal O$ of \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation} contains the original cutoffs, $\zeta_{\xi}$ with its boundary-fluctuation dependence, the gauge and Haar factors, the Jacobians, the vacuum prefactor and the deferred integrations, $\mathcal Z_0=\int\mathcal O[\mathsf w_{\xi}]\,\dd V$, and $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$, $\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}$ are the history expectation and probability \eqref{eq:c3-6-1} for this positive weight; $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ is the covered event of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} (every contour bond is a bond of $\Omega_1$ and every free input of the contour lies in $I$).

The weight is positive: $K_{\xi;1}$ is the exponential of a real function times indicators (Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}) and $c_{\xi}$ is real, the logarithm of the positive $a$-independent factor collected in the proof of \eqref{eq:c-collar-identity}.
