At fixed finite volume the signed sum \eqref{eq:c4-1-1} converges absolutely: the family sum \eqref{eq:part1-grouped-source} converges absolutely, and the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:joint-extraction} obtains \eqref{eq:c4-1-1} from it by Boolean inversion over finitely many root families, each with an absolutely convergent cluster-list sum.

\subsection{Histories near the Bad Region}\label{sec:c4-2}
Let $B_{\xi}\coloneqq\Lambda_1^c$ be the filled bad region and $E(B_{\xi})$ the set of positive fine bonds with at least one endpoint in $B_{\xi}$. Let $\Gamma_C$ be the deterministic set of contour bonds and free-input templates of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}, with $|\Gamma_C|\leqslant C_Ln_C$, $n_C$ the number of contour traversals; distances are those of the periodic fine-bond metric $d_T$ of \eqref{eq:marginal-covariance-input}, $d_T(b,c)= d_{\infty,T}(x,y)+\mathbf 1\{ i\ne j\}$ for $b=(x,i)$, $c=(y,j)$. For an integer $b\geqslant 0$ define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-2-1}
    \mathsf N_b\coloneqq\{\xi\, | \,\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma_C,E(B_{\xi}))\leqslant b\}\;,
\end{equation}
with distance to the empty set infinite. This is a measurable history event ($\Lambda_1$ is a function of the history labels).

The near and far parts are $E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf N_b}\mathscr R_{\xi}]$ and $E^{\mathrm{far}}_{\mathrm{def}}=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}\mathbf 1_{\mathsf N_b^c}\mathscr R_{\xi}]$, and $E_{\mathrm{def}}= E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}+E^{\mathrm{far}}_{\mathrm{def}}$ (both integrable, by the bound $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 2$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}).

\begin{lemma}[Near Histories]\label{lem:c4-2-1}
Let $b\geqslant 0$ be an integer and let $q_{\mathrm{pt}}$ be the one-point bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} ($\mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(z\in E(B_{\xi}))= p_z\leqslant q_{\mathrm{pt}}$ for every bond $z$, on compatible even fine periods and for $g_0\leqslant g_H$), with $q_{\mathrm{pt}}\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ for $0< g_0< g_*$ by Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5}. Then $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 2$ pointwise on every branch, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-2-2}
    \mathbb P_{\mathrm h}(\mathsf N_b)\leqslant 4C_Ln_C(2b+3)^4q_{\mathrm{pt}},\qquad
    | E^{\mathrm{near}}_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant 8C_Ln_C(2b+3)^4q_{\mathrm{pt}}\leqslant C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}\;,
\end{equation}
the last inequality for $b=\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor$, $C'_L\coloneqq 8C_L$ and $g_0$ below a threshold depending on $L$, $M_1$, $M_2$, $M$, the group, the character and the source constants.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:part1-scalar-extraction}, $\mathscr R_{\xi}= F_{\xi}(0)-S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)$. Both $F_{\xi}(0)=\int f_{\xi}\,\dd\nu_{\xi;0}$ (\eqref{eq:convex-response-operands}) and $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$ (\eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas}) are normalised integrals of a character of modulus at most one against the real positive kernels $K_{\xi;0}$ (the exponential of a real function times indicators, Section~\ref{sec:boundary-law-collar}) and $K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}), and $| f_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant 1$; hence $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 2$.

The members of $\Gamma_C$ are bonds (contour bonds and the bonds of the free-input templates), and there are at most $4(2b+3)^4$ positive fine-bond labels within $d_T$-distance $b$ of a fixed fine bond (an overcount on short periods), so a union bound over $\Gamma_C$ and the one-point estimate $p_z\leqslant q_{\mathrm{pt}}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} ($p_z$ of \eqref{eq:c3-7-1}) give the first bound; positivity of $\mathsf w_{\xi}$ and $\mathcal O$ and $|\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 2$ give the second.

For the last: $b=\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor$ exceeds every fixed source stencil for small $g_0$, and $\log(2b+3)= O(\log\log g_0^{-2})$ since $\ell= LMR_1\leqslant L^2M(2\log g_0^{-2})^{\mathfrak r}$ (\eqref{eq:c5-3-1}), while $\pi_*=\min(p_0(g_0),p_0(g_1))\geqslant A_0(\tfrac12\log g_0^{-2})^{p_0}$ with $p_0>0$, by $p_0(g)= A_0(\log g^{-2})^{p_0}$ (\eqref{eq:c3-1-1}) and $\log g_1^{-2}\geqslant \frac12\log g_0^{-2}$ (as at \eqref{eq:c5-3-1}); so $4\log(2b+3)\leqslant (c_*/2)\pi_*^2$, that is $8C_L(2b+3)^4e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}\leqslant C'_Le^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}$ with $C'_L\coloneqq 8C_L$, for small $g_0$ at fixed source constants.

The constants are uniform in the compatible even-period tori and the histories.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Interior Operand}\label{sec:c4-3}
The remaining operand is $E^{\mathrm{far}}_{\mathrm{def}}$. The Wilson contraction of a group $W$ depends on the background through its random-field support and through the transports along its contour interval $\mathcal H(W)$. The compared word of a group is the product of these transports, in their order, closed back to the base of the interval (Remark~\ref{rem:c4-5-1}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-1}).

Section~\ref{sec:c4-4} bounds the background derivative of the closed source-containing selected integrals and of their joint vacuum ratio; Sections~\ref{sec:c4-6}, \ref{sec:c4-8} and~\ref{sec:c4-9} sum the groups; Sections~\ref{sec:c4-7} and~\ref{sec:c4-10} supply the derivative bounds.

\subsection{The Joint Signed Selected-Integral Estimate}\label{sec:c4-4}
Let $\mathcal A\coloneqq\{ D_1,\ldots,D_m\}$ be a compatible root family. For each $D_j$ the selected measures are $\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell_j}$ of \eqref{eq:probe-selection-measure} with $\ell_j\coloneqq(\mathcal D_j,\mathsf J_j,\mathsf P_j,Z_j)$, $Z_j= D_j$ and $\mathsf J_j\ne\varnothing$, and $q_j=|\mathsf J_j|$, $q=\sum_jq_j$.

The centred measure $\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}=\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}-k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)\delta_{0,\mathsf L_D}$ of \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-zero-mass} is the sum of the nonempty-probe selections of \eqref{eq:probe-selection-measure}: the empty-probe selections give the mass times $\delta_0$ and disappear under centring (Lemma~\ref{lem:probe-measures}).

The finite-difference operator on a bounded function $f$ of the free variables is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-1}
    \Delta_{\mathsf J}f(B)\coloneqq\sum_{K\subseteq\mathsf J}(-1)^{|\mathsf J\setminus K|}f(\mathbf 1_KB)\;,
\end{equation}
every unselected free label being zero; for several roots $\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f$ is the composition of these operators on their disjoint label sets.

The integrand is a sum of closed Wilson contractions; the source may carry a fixed complementary closed holonomy $h\in G$, transforming by conjugation at the base, and all bounds are uniform in $h$. With \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-active-pairing},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-2}
    \mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)=\sum_{(\ell_j)_{j\leqslant m}\, | \,Z_j= D_j,\ \mathsf J_j\ne\varnothing}\int\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f(B)\,\dd\bigotimes_{j=1}^m\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell_j}(B_j)\;,
\end{equation}
the integral of each Dirac tensor $\bigotimes_{b\in\mathsf J}(\delta_{B_b}-\delta_0)$ against $f$ being the finite difference \eqref{eq:c4-4-1}.

\subsubsection{The Powers Supplied by the Signed Source}\label{sec:c4-4-1}
Let $u= C_{\chi} g_0(1+r)$, the fixed row/character constant $C_{\chi}$ being increased once (Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-4}). On the real protected box the row reconstruction depends on $g_0B$ and has analytic derivative bounds on a larger fixed phase chart (Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}).

Each selected free label affects a bounded number of reconstructed contour links, each link has a bounded input set, and for the square the traversal multiplicity is bounded; applying the product rule inside the closed character therefore gives $C_{\chi}^q$ derivative assignments.

Derivative orders on any one row are bounded by twice its fixed input count plus one, including the remainders below (Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-4}); the higher row derivatives are obtained from the bounded analytic phase map on its larger fixed ball by Cauchy estimates (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(i)--(ii): $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ is analytic on the ball of radius $\vartheta_*$ with $\|\widetilde D_{U,c}(A)\|\leqslant 2K_*\| A\|^2$ and $\| h_U(c)\|\leqslant H_*$, so Cauchy's estimates on the ball of radius $\vartheta_*/2$ bound every order), and the maximum order used is fixed by $L$. All untouched transports are unitary matrices inside the same closed contraction.

For the closed character $f$ of the source (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} below) the mixed integral remainder formula \eqref{eq:c4-10-7} gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-3}
    \sup|\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f|\leqslant u^q\;,
\end{equation}
the supremum over the real protected box, which contains the support of every selected measure in the selected variables (the measure \eqref{eq:probe-selection-measure} carries the cutoffs $\chi_b$ over $E(Y_0)$ in the variables it integrates; its bad cutoffs $1-\chi_b$ act on the labels of $\mathsf P$, which are integrated out, not on the selected probes $\mathsf J$).

For a root with odd $q_j$ take the homogeneous term of degree $q_j$ in its selected variables $B_{D_j}$, the other root variables fixed; it is odd under $B_{D_j}\to-B_{D_j}$, and the difference from it carries an additional factor $u$ (\eqref{eq:c4-10-9}; the choice of the extra increment is bounded by $q_j\leqslant 2^{q_j}$, absorbed in $C_{\chi}$). The same holds simultaneously for any set of odd roots, the product-rule allocation count remaining exponential in $q$. Every term is a closed contraction.

Each selected Gaussian kernel \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-density} with its cutoffs is invariant under $(B_{D_j},X_{D_j})\to(-B_{D_j},-X_{D_j})$ once its ordinary Mayer factors are removed: the determinant, the quadratic cross term, the compensator, the real cutoffs $\chi_b$, $1-\chi_b$ and the spatial Cauchy integrations are even. The tensor product in \eqref{eq:c4-4-2} gives separate integration variables and a separate reversal for each root. Thus the leading odd part integrates to zero in the signed selected integral, also when several roots are present.

Let $\omega(g_0)\coloneqq C_0^{\partial}g_0(1+r)^3$ with the host derivative constant $C_0^{\partial}\geqslant C_0$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}, let $\omega_*$ be the fixed host budget of \eqref{eq:native-source-vacuum-KP-budget}, and let $R_{\Upsilon}\coloneqq\omega_*/(2\omega(g_0))$, with $g_0$ so small that $R_{\Upsilon}\geqslant 2$.

In root $j$ the selected ordinary potentials $\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)$, $Y\in\mathcal D_j$, are multiplied by an independent complex parameter $\zeta_j$, $|\zeta_j|\leqslant R_{\Upsilon}$, the Gaussian kernel, cutoffs and probes being unchanged. If $\mathcal D_j\ne\varnothing$ the selected integral vanishes at $\zeta_j=0$ (each Mayer factor $\int_0^1\zeta\mathbf V e^{t\zeta\mathbf V}\dd t= e^{\zeta\mathbf V}-1$ does), so the Cauchy difference between $\zeta_j=0$ and $\zeta_j=1$ of the analytic function of $\zeta_j$ costs at most $2/(R_{\Upsilon}-1)$ times its supremum on the disc; if $\mathcal D_j=\varnothing$ the density is the even Gaussian/cutoff kernel and the reversal applies. Independent parameters on disjoint roots fit the same local potential budget simultaneously (Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}). Therefore an odd $q_j$ costs
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-4}
    v= u+\frac{2}{R_{\Upsilon}-1}\;.
\end{equation}
Both $u$ and $v$ tend to zero as $g_0\to0$, since $g_0(1+r)^3\to0$ by \eqref{eq:c3-1-1}. ($\omega$ as a background direction, with $\|\omega\|_{\infty}$ and $\mathscr D_{\omega}$, and $\omega(g_0)$, $\omega_*$ as host bounds are distinguished by their arguments.)

\subsubsection{Numerical Majorants Paid with the Same Gaussian Reserve}\label{sec:c4-4-2}
For a selected root $\ell$ define
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-5}
    M_{\ell}\coloneqq\sup_{|\zeta|\leqslant R_{\Upsilon}}\|\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell,\zeta}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\;,
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell,\zeta}$ is the measure \eqref{eq:probe-selection-measure} with each selected ordinary potential replaced by $\zeta$ times that potential; the cutoffs, Gaussian density and normalisers, compensator, integration carriers, weakening contours and seed data are unchanged.

\begin{lemma}[Dummy Comparison]\label{lem:c4-4-1}
There are at most $P_M=4(4M+3)^4$ probe labels with a given host (a label $b$ lies in the interior of its host $Y_b$, a rectangle of at most four $M$-cubes per side, \eqref{eq:c-probe-host}), and each probe host has $N_0(Y_b)\leqslant 4^4\leqslant s_{\mathrm p}=5^4$ cubes (\eqref{eq:c-probe-host}). Let $R_{\Upsilon}\geqslant 2$ and let $g_0$ be below the thresholds of Lemmas~\ref{lem:activity-bounds} and~\ref{lem:c2-selected-majorant}, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-6}
    u_*\coloneqq\min\Bigl(\frac14,\ \frac{\omega_*e^{-\kappa s_{\mathrm p}}}{8P_M}\Bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
a constant fixed after $M$ and before $g_0$. Then for every connected final domain $D$, with $m(D)=\varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda_*\ell_1(D)}$ the majorant of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-7}
    \sum_{\ell\, | \,Z(\ell)= D,\ \mathsf J(\ell)\ne\varnothing}u_*^{q(\ell)}M_{\ell}\leqslant m(D)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For every probe label $b$ the numerical comparison inserts the dummy potential $p^+_b= u_*$ on its protected host box and zero outside; its selected Mayer factor $e^{u_*}-1$ is at least $u_*$. The summed dummy potential at a host is at most $P_Mu_*\leqslant \omega_*e^{-\kappa s_{\mathrm p}}/8\leqslant \omega_*e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}/8$, the input $B_Y$ of \eqref{eq:c4-7-2} (for a probe host $d_0(Y)\leqslant N_0(Y)-1< s_{\mathrm p}$: its cubes form a rectangular array, and a path through the centres of wall-adjacent cubes visiting each once meets every cube and has length $N_0(Y)-1$ in \eqref{eq:c2-tree-length}), while the complex ordinary potentials use at most half the budget $\omega_*e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}$ on $|\zeta|\leqslant R_{\Upsilon}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-potential-size} and $R_{\Upsilon}\omega(g_0)=\omega_*/2$).

The labels with a common host are split as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:probe-measures}; the seeds, conditioning carrier and Gaussian kernel depend on the active hosts only. The split selections with the same active-host set are summed first: Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1} proves that their many-to-one positive sum is dominated hostwise by the undifferentiated majorant \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-selected-majorant}. That majorant pays its determinant and compensator with the Gaussian reserve $\alpha_G$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii)), and the cover and seed sums \eqref{eq:native-source-initial-domain-sum}, \eqref{eq:native-source-enlarged-domain-sum} with the final $Y'$-sum in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds} (Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}) sum the seeds and final domains to $m(D)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Joint Selected-Integral Bound]\label{lem:c4-4-2}
Let $f$ be a normalised character of an ordered closed reconstructed word, optionally closed with its inverse background interval and a fixed complementary $h$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-2}). For $g_0$ small enough that $u\leqslant u_*$ and $v\leqslant 1$, put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-8}
    \rho\coloneqq\Bigl(\frac{u}{u_*}\Bigr)^2+\frac{u}{u_*}\,v\;.
\end{equation}
Then for every compatible root family $\mathcal A$ and every choice of selections $(\ell_j)$ with $\mathsf J_j\ne\varnothing$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-9}
    \Bigl|\int\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f(B)\,\dd\bigotimes_{j=1}^m\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell_j}(B_j)\Bigr|\leqslant \prod_{j=1}^mu^{q_j}v^{q_j\bmod2}M_{\ell_j},\qquad
    |\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)|\leqslant \prod_{D\in\mathcal A}\rho\,m(D)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first bound combines the reversal, the Cauchy differences and \eqref{eq:c4-4-3}--\eqref{eq:c4-4-4} (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-2}): the roots with odd $q_j$ and empty ordinary selection lose their leading odd part to the even kernel and keep the remainder $u^{q_j+1}$, the roots with odd $q_j$ and nonempty ordinary selection pay $u^{q_j}\cdot2/(R_{\Upsilon}-1)$ by the Cauchy difference in $\zeta_j$ (the supremum on the disc being $u^{q_j}M_{\ell_j}$ by \eqref{eq:c4-4-5}), the roots with even $q_j$ pay $u^{q_j}M_{\ell_j}$.

For every nonempty probe set $(u/u_*)^{q_j}v^{q_j\bmod2}\leqslant \rho$ ($q_j=1$ gives $(u/u_*)v$, $q_j\geqslant 2$ gives $(u/u_*)^2$). Summing over the selections of every root with \eqref{eq:c4-4-2} and \eqref{eq:c4-4-7} gives the second bound.
\end{proof}

By \eqref{eq:c4-4-8}, $\rho= O(g_0^2(1+r)^4)$ with constants fixed before the coupling.

\subsubsection{Background Derivative and the Joint Vacuum Ratio}\label{sec:c4-4-3}
For the flat subtraction, $\omega$ is a real background direction along one of the globally small analytic extensions of Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-1}, with the geometry, carriers, cutoff norm, means, Gaussian reserve and walk recipe unchanged. Let $L_f$ be the number of occurrences of contour background links in the closed word whose local coefficient arguments vary; when a group's relative interval is compared this includes the interval and its inverse closing transport. Complementary closed holonomies, outer history variables and physical weights are held fixed, and $\mathscr D_{\omega}$ denotes this derivative.

\begin{lemma}[One Background Derivative]\label{lem:c4-4-3}
On the extensions of Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-1}, with $\rho$, $m(D)$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} and a constant $C$ fixed before the coupling,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-10}
    |\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)|\leqslant C\|\omega\|_{\infty}\Bigl(L_f+\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\Bigr)\prod_{D\in\mathcal A}\rho\,m(D)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The derivative of the selected Gaussian factors (density, normaliser, compensator) inserts a scalar polynomial of degree at most two in $(B,X)$, including the determinant trace; its moment is paid by the joint coercive Gaussian bound of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-3} at cost $CN_1(D)\|\omega\|_{\infty}$. Differentiated walk coefficients sum in the convergent differentiated series of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-2}.

The derivative of a host Mayer $t$-integrand is $\zeta(\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathbf V)e^{t\zeta\mathbf V}(1+t\zeta\mathbf V)$, whose $t$-integral $\zeta(\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathbf V)e^{\zeta\mathbf V}$ vanishes at $\zeta=0$; its size is bounded by the differentiated host comparison of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1}.

A Gaussian derivative is even under each component reversal and the leading source derivative has the parity of the undifferentiated term (\eqref{eq:c4-10-10}), so the signed powers of Section~\ref{sec:c4-4-1} survive one derivative, with the additional factor $C\|\omega\|_{\infty}(L_f+\sum_DN_1(D))$: the source derivative contributes $L_f$ plus the number of selected labels, the latter at most $4(LM+1)^4\sum_DN_1(D)$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}), and the host, Gaussian and walk derivatives contribute one factor $N_1(D)$ each by Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1}. The factor $N_1(D)$ is paid by $m(D)$ in Section~\ref{sec:c4-7}.
\end{proof}

The vacuum ratio is the joint ratio of the whole root family: by \eqref{eq:fixed-probe-active-pairing} and \eqref{eq:part1-joint-vacuum-exponential},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-11}
    q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)=\exp\Bigl[-\sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)\Bigr]\;,
\end{equation}
a cluster hitting several roots being counted once, and its derivative is the derivative of this exponential.

\begin{lemma}[The Joint Ratio and Its Derivative]\label{lem:c4-4-4}
With the constant $C_M$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-12}
    | q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)|\leqslant e^{\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)/8},\qquad
    |\mathscr D_{\omega} q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)|\leqslant \frac{C_M}{2}\|\omega\|_{\infty}\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\,e^{\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)/8}\;,
\end{equation}
and consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-4-13}
    \bigl|\mathscr D_{\omega}[q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)]\bigr|\leqslant C\|\omega\|_{\infty}\Bigl(L_f+\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\Bigr)\prod_{D\in\mathcal A}\bigl[\rho\,m(D)e^{N_1(D)/8}\bigr]\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first bound is Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}. The second is Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-4}. The third follows from the product rule with Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} and~\ref{lem:c4-4-3} and the two bounds of \eqref{eq:c4-4-12}, with the constant $C$ of \eqref{eq:c4-4-10} increased by $C_M/2$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Closed Group Subtraction}\label{sec:c4-6}
\begin{remark}[The Closed Group Contraction]\label{rem:c4-5-1}
The closed contraction of a group is formed with the interval transport relative to its background interval, closed back to its base, and an arbitrary complementary closed holonomy $h$; its flat value is $a_W\chi(h)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}. Products of such closed contractions are bounded by the norm equivalence of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-1}, and the multi-group factorisation is \eqref{eq:part1-closed-family-pairing}.
\end{remark}

\emph{Geometry.} The square/torus geometry of Section~\ref{sec:extent-weights} is in force: $C$ is a coarse square of side $s= nL$ fine bonds on fine periods $LK_i$ with $K_i\geqslant 3(n+2)$, and $n_C=4s$. For a group $W$, $\mathcal H(W)$ is its interval (Definition~\ref{def:groups}: a cyclic interval of fewer than $n_C/2$ contour traversals, or the whole contour read from the base point) and $|\mathcal H(W)|$ the number of traversals in it. Contour hull length is paid by connected spatial extent as in \eqref{eq:marginal-hull-extent}: contacts of diameter $< s/2$ occupy one side or two adjacent sides and fit in an arc of length at most $4\operatorname{diam}+1$; otherwise $n_C\leqslant 8\operatorname{diam}$. Periodic distances between square contacts equal their lifted distances.

For a group $W$ let $n(W)$ be the sum of $N_1$ over its roots and over every constituent domain of every occurrence in its cluster list, with multiplicities; the size and the footprint of $W$ are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-1}
    \mathfrak s(W)\coloneqq n(W)+\frac{|\mathcal H(W)|}{LM}\;,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-footprint}
    \begin{aligned}
    F(W)=\Bigl\{\Delta\in\pi_1\,\Big|\,{}&\Delta\text{ meets a constituent domain of }W\text{, its coefficient stencil halo,}\\
    &\text{or }\mathcal F_r\cup\{ r\}\text{ for a traversal }r\in\mathcal H(W)\Bigr\}\;,
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
where $\pi_1$ is the partition into $LM$-cubes, a cube meets a set of sites or bonds when it contains a site or a bond endpoint of the set, and $\mathcal F_r$ is the free-input stencil of $r$. The ranges are made explicit in Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-env}, which gives $| F(W)|\leqslant C\mathfrak s(W)$.

For a component of the roots/cluster-occurrence graph the union of its domains is wall connected, so its diameter is at most $CLM$ times its cube count, and its contact hull is bounded by the square estimate above; overlapping hulls have a connected interval union, which pays the hull of a group by the sum of its component counts. If all components are merged because some hull is long (Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}), the sum of the component sizes in that class is at least $cn_C/(LM)$. Hence $|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)\leqslant Cn(W)$. Coefficients whose local rectangle fails to lift are kept in the large-domain class of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}.

\subsubsection{The Closed Relative Interval Functional}\label{sec:c4-6-1}
In the reconstructed links along $\mathcal H(W)$ only the root variables of $W$ are nonzero. $T_W(a;U_1)$ is the ordered product of these links (the interval transport) and $P_W(U_1)$ the same product at zero free variable, both with their source orientations and with the same two endpoint vertices. The relative product $T_W(a;U_1)P_W(U_1)^{-1}$ is based and closed at the initial vertex. The scalar closed contraction of $W$ is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-2}
    c_W(U_1;h)\coloneqq w_{\xi}(W)\int\chi\bigl(T_W(a;U_1)P_W(U_1)^{-1}h\bigr)\,\dd\Bigl(\bigotimes_{D\in\mathcal A(W)}\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi,D}\Bigr)(a)\;,
\end{equation}
$h\in G$ a complementary closed holonomy at that base, transforming by simultaneous conjugation; the product $T_WP_W^{-1}$ and $h$ transform at one base, so the displayed scalar is gauge invariant. The group defect and its size are
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-3}
    d_W(U_1;h)\coloneqq c_W(U_1;h)-a_W\chi(h),\qquad\mathfrak d_W(U_1)\coloneqq\sup_{h\in G}| d_W(U_1;h)|\;.
\end{equation}
At the reference data, where the same formula is taken with the reference weights and measures, $c_W(\id;h)= a_W\chi(h)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:schur} (there the interval transport at the root variables is the $P^{\circ}_W(a)$ of that lemma and the background transport is the identity). The weights and measures in $c_W$ are those of the joint extraction, including every cluster occurrence of the group.

\begin{lemma}[Factorisation and Product Inequality]\label{lem:c4-6-1}
Let $\pi$ be the irreducible unitary representation with $\chi=\dim(\pi)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}\pi$.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] There is a constant $K_{\chi}$ of the character such that
\begin{equation*}
    \|\Upsilon\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant K_{\chi}\sup_{h\in G}|\dim(\pi)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\Upsilon\pi(h))|
\end{equation*}
for every $\Upsilon\in\operatorname{End}(V_{\pi})$.
\item[(b)] For a compatible family $\mathfrak B\coloneqq\{ W_1,\ldots,W_m\}$ on a covered branch, $R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)$ is the normalised trace of the ordered product of the matrices $\Upsilon_{W_j}\pi(G_j)$, where $\Upsilon_W= w_{\xi}(W)\int\pi(T_WP_W^{-1})\,\dd\bigotimes\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}-a_W\id$ and $G_j$ is the background transport of the gap after $\mathcal H(W_j)$ composed with $P_{W_j}$.
\item[(c)] Consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-4}
    | R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)|\leqslant \prod_{W\in\mathfrak B}K_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) $\Upsilon\mapsto(h\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(\Upsilon\pi(h)))$ is linear and injective on $\operatorname{End}(V_{\pi})$, since $\pi(G)$ spans $\operatorname{End}(V_{\pi})$ for an irreducible representation (Burnside); so the supremum over $h$ is a norm on the finite-dimensional space $\operatorname{End}(V_{\pi})$, equivalent to the operator norm, and $K_{\chi}$ is the equivalence constant.

(b) In a compatible family a traversal of $\mathcal H(W)$ has no contact with a root of a different group (that contact hull would meet $\mathcal H(W)$), so its reconstructed link uses the root variables of $W$ only (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}); a traversal outside every interval has its background link. The groups are numbered in cyclic order, and the ordered link product starts at the first traversal of $\mathcal H(W_1)$ (cyclicity of the trace). Expanding the ordered product $\prod_j(X_j-a_{W_j}\id)\pi(G_j)$ with $X_j= w_{\xi}(W_j)\int\pi(T_{W_j}P_{W_j}^{-1})\dd\bigotimes\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}$ over subsets $\mathcal S$ of slots, a slot of the first kind contributes the links of $\mathcal H(W_j)$ at the root variables followed by the gap transport, a slot of the second kind contributes $-a_{W_j}$ times the links of $\mathcal H(W_j)$ at zero free variable followed by the gap; by multilinearity of the trace and Fubini over the product measure (as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}) the normalised trace of the term of $\mathcal S$ is $(\prod_{W\notin\mathcal S}(-a_W))\,(\prod_{W\in\mathcal S}w_{\xi}(W))\,\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A(\mathcal S);f_{\xi})=(\prod_{W\notin\mathcal S}(-a_W))A_{\xi}(\mathcal S)$ by \eqref{eq:part1-closed-family-pairing}, since on a covered branch the links outside the intervals are the background links at $U_1$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-1}; Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} gives $f_{\xi}(0)= W_{\chi}(C;U_1)$). Summing over $\mathcal S$ reproduces \eqref{eq:part1-joint-defect}.

(c) $|\operatorname{tr}(Y_1\cdots Y_{2m})|\leqslant \dim(\pi)\prod\| Y_i\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, the gap transports are unitary, and $\|\Upsilon_W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leqslant K_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)$ by (a), since $\dim(\pi)^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\Upsilon_W\pi(h))= d_W(U_1;h)$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Positive Graph Sums for the Reference Factors}\label{sec:c4-6-2}
A cluster occurrence $\mathfrak c$, defined by the ordered tuple $(D_1,\ldots,D_p)$, has cube cost $n(\mathfrak c)=\sum_{D\in\mathfrak c}N_1(D)$ and positive weight
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-Mv}
    M_v(\mathfrak c)=\frac{1}{p!}\sum_{\tau}\prod_{i=1}^pm(D_i)\;,
\end{equation}
the sum over the spanning trees $\tau$ of the incompatibility graph of the tuple: the tree majorant of its Ursell coefficient (the positive tree sum of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters}, Section~\ref{app:kp}). Source roots have the weights $\rho\,m(D)$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2}.

For a group $W$ with root family $\mathcal A(W)$ and cluster list $(\mathfrak c_1,\ldots,\mathfrak c_{k(W)})$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-MW}
    M(W)=\frac{1}{k(W)!}\prod_{D\in\mathcal A(W)}\rho\,m(D)\prod_{j=1}^{k(W)}M_v(\mathfrak c_j)\;;
\end{equation}
it bounds $| a_W|$, the pairings $| w_{\xi}(W)\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A(W);f)|$ for the words of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2}, and the undifferentiated closed source functional $| c_W(U_1;h)|$, the physical and reference data having the same numerical majorant (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2} applies at the reference data too, whose hypotheses Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference} verifies).

The cubes are those of the partition $\pi_1$ (side $LM$, Section~\ref{app:domain-geometry}): $\Delta_z= LMz+[-LM/2,LM/2]^4$ reduced modulo the fine periods, which are multiples of $LM$ by \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions}; every site lies in exactly one cube, and the index distance of two cubes is the periodic maximum-norm distance of their indices $z$.

For a set $S$ of sites, $\pi_1(S)$ is the set of cubes containing a site of $S$, and $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ abbreviates $\pi_1$ of the vertex set of the traversals of $\mathcal H(W)$. For a set $X$ of cubes, $\mathfrak N_R(X)$ is the set of cubes at index distance at most $R$ from a cube of $X$, so $|\mathfrak N_R(X)|\leqslant (2R+1)^4| X|$.

$R_{\mathrm h}$ is the maximal $\ell^{\infty}$ distance from the base of a host \eqref{eq:part1-potential-host}, \eqref{eq:c-probe-host} to a point of the host, a constant fixed by the host constructions of Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}. The coefficient stencil halo of a domain $D$ is the union of the hosts whose base lies within $R_{\mathrm h}$ of $D$. The envelope of a group $W$ is defined with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-envelope}
    \begin{gathered}
    R_{\mathrm e}=\Bigl\lceil\frac{2\max(R_{\mathrm h},L)}{LM}\Bigr\rceil,\qquad A_F= A_E=9(2R_{\mathrm e}+1)^4,\\
    X(W)=\bigcup_D\pi_1(D),\qquad\mathfrak E(W)=\mathfrak N_{R_{\mathrm e}}\bigl(X(W)\cup\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))\bigr)\;,
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
the union over the constituent domains $D$ of $W$ (roots and cluster constituents); $X(W)$ is a set, so $| X(W)|\leqslant n(W)$, which counts with multiplicity.

\begin{lemma}[Footprints and Envelopes]\label{lem:c4-6-env}
For every group $W$:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] $|\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))|\leqslant 8+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)$, $| X(W)\cup\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))|\leqslant 9\mathfrak s(W)$, $F(W)\subseteq \mathfrak E(W)$ and $| F(W)|\leqslant |\mathfrak E(W)|\leqslant A_E\mathfrak s(W)$;
\item[(b)] $\mathfrak E(W)$ is connected under maximum-norm adjacency of cubes (two distinct cubes are adjacent when their index distance is one);
\item[(c)] $\mathcal H(W)\neq\varnothing$, and if $\Delta\in F(W)$ then $\operatorname{dist}(\Delta,C)\leqslant A_ELM\,\mathfrak s(W)$, that is $\mathfrak s(W)\geqslant \operatorname{dist}(\Delta,C)/(A_ELM)$, where $\operatorname{dist}(\Delta,C)$ is the $\ell^{\infty}$ distance in fine units from the nearest site of $\Delta$ to the vertex set of $C$;
\item[(d)] two incompatible groups have footprints in contact (sharing a cube, or adjacent across a face, edge or corner, that is at index distance at most one) or overlapping intervals, so an incompatible $W'$ has a footprint cube in $\mathfrak N_1(F(W))$, a set of at most $3^4A_F\mathfrak s(W)$ cubes, or a traversal in $\mathcal H(W)$.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Ranges, in fine $\ell^{\infty}$ units: the free-input stencil $\mathcal F_r$ of a bond $r$ \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-extension-support} is $\{ r\}$ or $\mathcal E_c\cap E_*$, bonds with both endpoints in two adjacent blocks of side $L$ \eqref{eq:regular-stencil-bonds}, or empty (for a contour bond that is not a bond of $\Omega_1$, the convention of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}), so every endpoint of a bond of $\mathcal F_r\cup\{ r\}$ is within $2L$ of the initial vertex of $r$. The active hosts of a selection with final domain $D$ have their bases in the $R_{\mathrm h}$-neighbourhood of $D$, and each host lies within $R_{\mathrm h}$ of its base, so the halo of $D$ lies within $2R_{\mathrm h}$ of $D$. A root contact $n\in\mathsf T_D$ \eqref{eq:part1-contact-set} has a bond $b\in\mathcal F_{r_n}\cap\mathsf L_D$, whose endpoints lie in $D$ ($Y_b\subseteq D$ by \eqref{eq:probe-eligible-carrier}, and $Y_b$ contains $b$ by its definition \eqref{eq:c-probe-host}), so the initial vertex of $r_n$ is within $2L$ of $D$.

Index conversion: if sites $x\in\Delta_z$ and $y\in\Delta_{z'}$ are at fine distance at most $\rho$, then, for lifts of $x$, $y$ realising that distance and the indices $z$, $z'$ of their lifted cubes, $| LM(z-z')|_{\infty}\leqslant \rho+2\cdot\frac{LM-1}2<\rho+LM$, so the index distance of $\Delta_z$ and $\Delta_{z'}$ is at most $\lceil\rho/(LM)\rceil$; in particular the cube of a site within $2L$ of a cube $\Delta$ is at index distance at most $\lceil2L/(LM)\rceil=1$ from $\Delta$ ($M\geqslant 8$), and a cube meeting the halo of $D$ is at index distance at most $\lceil2R_{\mathrm h}/(LM)\rceil\leqslant R_{\mathrm e}$ from a cube of $D$.

Every root $D$ of $W$ is marked, that is $\mathsf T_D\neq\varnothing$ (\eqref{eq:part1-contact-set} and the construction preceding Definition~\ref{def:groups}), and $\mathsf T_D\subseteq\mathcal H(W)$, because $\mathcal H(W)$ is the hull of the union of the contacts of the group's components, which include the contact sets of its roots. In particular $\mathcal H(W)\neq\varnothing$.

(a) $\mathcal H(W)$ is a cyclic interval of fewer than $n_C/2$ traversals of the square $C$, or the whole contour (Definition~\ref{def:groups}), so the vertices of its traversals on each side form one run of consecutive collinear sites (the whole side, for the whole contour), and $C$ does not wrap around the torus ($LK_i\geqslant 3L(n+2)> nL$). A run of $t$ traversals along a side has $t+1$ consecutive collinear vertices, which lie in at most $\lfloor t/(LM)\rfloor+2$ cubes, since the cubes cut the side into runs of $LM$ consecutive sites; summing over the four sides, $|\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))|\leqslant 8+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)$. Hence $| X(W)\cup\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))|\leqslant n(W)+8+|\mathcal H(W)|/(LM)=\mathfrak s(W)+8\leqslant 9\mathfrak s(W)$ by \eqref{eq:c4-6-1} and $\mathfrak s(W)\geqslant n(W)\geqslant 1$ (a group has a nonempty root family, Definition~\ref{def:groups}, and each root is a connected final domain, a nonempty union of cubes, Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}). A cube of $F(W)$ \eqref{eq:c4-6-footprint} is a cube of a constituent domain, in $X(W)$; or meets the halo of a constituent domain, at index distance at most $R_{\mathrm e}$ from $X(W)$; or contains an endpoint of a bond of the stencil of a traversal of $\mathcal H(W)$, within $2L$ of the initial vertex of that traversal, hence at index distance at most $1\leqslant R_{\mathrm e}$ from $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$. So $F(W)\subseteq \mathfrak E(W)$ and $|\mathfrak E(W)|\leqslant (2R_{\mathrm e}+1)^4\cdot9\mathfrak s(W)= A_E\mathfrak s(W)$.

(b) The set $X(W)\cup\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ is connected under adjacency: the two vertices of a traversal are at fine distance one and consecutive traversals of $\mathcal H(W)$ share a vertex, so the vertices lie in the same or in adjacent cubes, and $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ is connected; each constituent domain is wall connected (Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}), so its cubes are connected; within a cluster occurrence the constituent domains are linked by incompatibilities (a tuple with a disconnected incompatibility graph has $\varphi^T=0$ and does not occur in \eqref{eq:c-cluster-expansion}), a cluster occurrence of $W$ hits a root of $W$ (Definition~\ref{def:groups}: some constituent is incompatible with a root), and incompatible domains share a cube or a wall (Section~\ref{sec:selected-integrals}), that is contain cubes at index distance at most one; finally every root $D$ has a contact $n\in\mathsf T_D\subseteq\mathcal H(W)$ (shown above), the initial vertex of $r_n$ being within $2L$ of $D$, so a cube of $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ is at index distance at most one from a cube of $D$. Thus every constituent domain is joined to $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$ through adjacent cubes, and $\mathfrak E(W)$, the union of the connected boxes $\mathfrak N_{R_{\mathrm e}}(\{\Delta\})$ over the cubes $\Delta$ of a connected set, each containing its centre $\Delta$, is connected.

(c) $\mathcal H(W)\neq\varnothing$ was shown above. A connected set of $k$ cubes contains a path of at most $k$ cubes between any two of them, so the cubes of any two of its sites are at index distance at most $k-1$ and the sites are at fine distance less than $kLM$; with $k\leqslant A_E\mathfrak s(W)$, the $\ell^{\infty}$ diameter of $\mathfrak E(W)$ is at most $A_ELM\,\mathfrak s(W)$. $\mathfrak E(W)$ contains $\Delta\in F(W)$ and the nonempty set $\pi_1(\mathcal H(W))$, whose cubes contain vertices of $C$.

(d) Two groups are compatible when all their constituent domains are mutually compatible and their intervals are disjoint, and a family containing a whole-contour group is a singleton (Definition~\ref{def:groups}). So if $W$ and $W'$ are incompatible, either one of them is a whole-contour group, and then the intervals overlap, as $\mathcal H(W)$ and $\mathcal H(W')$ are nonempty by (c); or the intervals overlap, so $W'$ has a traversal in $\mathcal H(W)$; or some constituent domains $D$ of $W$ and $D'$ of $W'$ share a cube or a wall, so a cube of $D'\subseteq F(W')$ lies at index distance at most one from a cube of $D\subseteq F(W)$, that is in $\mathfrak N_1(F(W))$, and $|\mathfrak N_1(F(W))|\leqslant 3^4| F(W)|\leqslant 3^4A_F\mathfrak s(W)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Positive Group Sums]\label{lem:c4-6-2}
Let $\eta>0$ be chosen after the fixed geometry and forest decay constants, with $1000\eta A_{\mathrm s}<\varpi/8$ as in Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-2}. Under the smallness conditions $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$ and the root-incidence bound of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-2}, which hold for $g_0$ small,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-5}
    \sup_{n\in\mathcal I_C}\sum_{W\, | \,n\in\mathcal H(W)}M(W)e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}+\sup_{\Delta\in\pi_1}\sum_{W\, | \,\Delta\in F(W)}M(W)e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\leqslant C\rho\;,
\end{equation}
with a constant $C$ fixed before the coupling (the constants of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2}(b) and of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-3}), where $\mathcal I_C$ is the set of contour traversals.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
This is Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-3}(d).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The Reference Group Gas]\label{lem:c4-6-3}
Let $\mathfrak a_W\coloneqq\eta\mathfrak s(W)$. Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-2}, for every group $W$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-6}
    \sum_{W'\not\sim W}| a_{W'}| e^{\mathfrak a_{W'}}\leqslant C\rho\bigl(| F(W)|+|\mathcal H(W)|\bigr)\leqslant \frac18\mathfrak a_W
\end{equation}
for $g_0$ small. Hence the reference group gas \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas} has a convergent connected-cluster logarithm, $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}\ne0$, and for every compatible family $\mathfrak B$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-7}
    \Bigl|\frac{S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}}{S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}}\Bigr|\leqslant \exp\Bigl(\frac18\sum_{W\in\mathfrak B}\mathfrak a_W\Bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Incompatibility of $W$ and $W'$ implies contact of their footprints or overlap of their intervals, so the two pin sums \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} (with $| a_{W'}|\leqslant M(W')$ and $e^{\mathfrak a_{W'}}\leqslant e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W')}$) give the first inequality of \eqref{eq:c4-6-6}, and $| F(W)|+|\mathcal H(W)|\leqslant C_1LM\mathfrak s(W)$ with $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$, the constant $C$ there taken to include $C_1$, gives the second. This is the Kotecký--Preiss criterion for the species $W$ with activities $a_W$ and costs $\mathfrak a_W$; the pinned-tree argument of Section~\ref{app:kp} gives the convergent logarithm and the exclusion identity, whose countable-species form is Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}. The restricted ratio is the single joint exclusion ratio of that gas, and the pinned cluster estimate counts each cluster hitting $\mathfrak B$ once, giving \eqref{eq:c4-6-7}.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Subtraction and Its Curvature Payment}\label{sec:c4-6-3}
For a group $W$ the comparison box $Q_W$ is a fine rectangle containing every constituent domain's coefficient halo and every background transport along $\mathcal H(W)$, including the inverse interval closing the source; its lifted side is at most $CLMn(W)$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}). For a fine rectangle $Q$ and a unitary field $U$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-deltaQ}
    \delta_Q(U)=\max_{p\subset Q}| U(\partial p)-\id|_{\sigma}\;,
\end{equation}
the maximum over the plaquettes of $Q$.

A group is small interior when $n(W)< b/(4C_{\mathrm{box}}LM)$ \eqref{eq:c4-8-9}; on far histories its box lies in $\Lambda_1$ and misses $S_1$, and $\mathfrak d_W(U_1)$ is bounded through the coefficient path of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-1} and the tree gauge of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-10-5}. Every other group is bounded by its two undifferentiated endpoint coefficients, and the reserved exponential pays this tail (Section~\ref{sec:c4-12-2}).

\begin{lemma}[The Group Pin Sum]\label{lem:c4-6-4}
On covered far histories, with $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$, $b=\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor$ and constants $C_{\chi}$, $c$ fixed before the coupling,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-8}
    \sum_WK_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\leqslant C_{\chi} n_C\rho\bigl(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)}\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

The proof is in Section~\ref{sec:c4-12-2}.

\subsubsection{The Signed Integrated Bound}\label{sec:c4-6-4}
\begin{lemma}[The Family Sum]\label{lem:c4-6-5}
On covered far histories,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-6-9}
    |\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant | S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\Bigl[\exp\Bigl(C_{\chi} n_C\rho\bigl(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)}\bigr)\Bigr)-1\Bigr]\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
In the sum \eqref{eq:c4-1-1}, by \eqref{eq:c4-6-4} and \eqref{eq:c4-6-7}, $| S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)|\leqslant | S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\prod_{W\in\mathfrak B}K_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}$, and the sum over nonempty compatible families is bounded by the exponential series of the one-group sum \eqref{eq:c4-6-8} minus its zeroth term. The countable-group limit is Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}.
\end{proof}

Together with Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1} this gives the defect bound \eqref{eq:c4-12-7}.

\subsection{The Joint Kernel Payment}\label{sec:c4-7}
This section proves the quantitative inputs of Section~\ref{sec:c4-4}.

\subsubsection{Host Budget and Fixed Parameter Order}\label{sec:c4-7-1}
$C_{\mathrm p}$ bounds one primitive (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-primitive-bounds}) and $C_0= N_{\mathrm h}C_{\mathrm p}e^{\kappa(B_{\mathrm h}+4)}$ bounds their sum at a host (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-potential-size}). Let $C^{\partial}_{\mathrm p}$ be the maximum of the finite local coefficient-derivative bounds of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-1}: the energy primitive is $g_0$ times the third-order Taylor remainder in the protected variables, and its background derivative has the same factor $g_0(1+r)^3$ because its local analytic coefficients and their background derivatives are bounded on the larger fixed row chart; the Haar primitive and its background derivative start at order $g_0^2(1+r)^2$; the constraint-Jacobian primitive and its derivative are bounded by $Cg_0(1+r)$. Let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-1}
    C^{\partial}_0\coloneqq N_{\mathrm h}\max(C_{\mathrm p},C^{\partial}_{\mathrm p})e^{\kappa(B_{\mathrm h}+4)},\qquad
    \omega(g_0)\coloneqq C^{\partial}_0g_0(1+r)^3,\qquad R_{\Upsilon}\coloneqq\frac{\omega_*}{2\omega(g_0)}\;,
\end{equation}
$C^{\partial}_0$ being fixed after $M$ and before $g_0$. Summing the same finite host assignments proves $\sup|\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)|\leqslant \omega(g_0)e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}\|\omega\|_{\infty}$ on the background neighbourhood of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-1} (phases within $\tau_{\mathrm b}$ of the branch background, Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3}), where the primitive bounds hold with the same constants, so that $\omega(g_0)\geqslant C_0g_0(1+r)^3$ also bounds $\sup|\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)| e^{\kappa d_0(Y)}$ there (\eqref{eq:native-source-interaction-size}); in Sections~\ref{sec:c4-4} and~\ref{sec:c4-6} this $\omega(g_0)$ replaces the $\omega(g_0)$ of \eqref{eq:part1-host-multiplicity}, which it dominates. The coupling threshold is $\omega(g_0)\leqslant \omega_*/4$, that is $R_{\Upsilon}\geqslant 2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-1}). Let $N_{\mathrm{type}}$ be the number of tagged ordinary primitive and probe types based in one fine translation cell of the fixed $L$-periodic template and $R_{\mathrm h}$ the maximal base-to-host offset, both fixed by the host constructions \eqref{eq:part1-potential-host}, \eqref{eq:c-probe-host}. Distinct active hosts of a selection with final domain $D$ have a labelled base in the fixed $R_{\mathrm h}$-neighbourhood of $D$, so their number is at most $H_MN_1(D)$ with $H_M\coloneqq N_{\mathrm{type}}(LM+2R_{\mathrm h}+3)^4$, and the selected probe count is at most the number of fine bonds in $D$, $q\leqslant 4(LM+1)^4\sum_DN_1(D)$.

\begin{definition}[Host Weights]\label{def:host-weights}
For a host $Y$ let $n_Y$ be the number of probe labels with host $Y$, and let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-2}
    A_Y\coloneqq\frac{\omega_*}{2}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)},\qquad B_Y\coloneqq n_Yu_*,\qquad v_{\mathrm{ordinary}}\coloneqq e^{A_Y}-1,\qquad v_{\mathrm{probe}}\coloneqq u_*\;.
\end{equation}
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Positive Host Comparison]\label{lem:c4-7-1}
For every host $Y$, with the weights of Definition~\ref{def:host-weights}, $n_Y\leqslant P_M$ and $B_Y\leqslant \frac{\omega_*}{8}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}$. Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] the sum over the nonempty label subsets at $Y$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-3}
    \begin{aligned}
    \sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{\mathrm{ordinary},\mathrm{probes}\}}\prod_{\ell'\in S}v_{\ell'}&\leqslant e^{A_Y}(1+u_*)^{n_Y}-1\leqslant e^{A_Y+B_Y}-1\\
    &\leqslant (A_Y+B_Y)e^{A_Y+B_Y}\leqslant \omega_*e^{1/2}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}\;.
    \end{aligned}
\end{equation}
\item[(b)] For a differentiated host, the summed weight of the label subsets at $Y$ is bounded by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-4}
    R_{\Upsilon}\sup|\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)|\,e^{A_Y}(1+u_*)^{n_Y}\leqslant A_Ye^{A_Y+B_Y}\|\omega\|_{\infty}\leqslant \omega_*e^{1/2}e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}\|\omega\|_{\infty}\;.
\end{equation}
\item[(c)] There is a constant $C_M$, fixed after $M$ and before $g_0$, such that for every connected final domain $D$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-5}
    \sum_{\ell\, | \,Z(\ell)= D}u_*^{q(\ell)}\sup_{|\zeta|\leqslant R_{\Upsilon}}\|\mathscr D_{\omega}\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell,\zeta}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\leqslant C_MN_1(D)\|\omega\|_{\infty}\,\varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda_*\ell_1(D)}\;,
\end{equation}
the derivative including every Gaussian normaliser and the compensator; and $|\mathscr D_{\omega} k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)|\leqslant C_MN_1(D)\|\omega\|_{\infty} m(D)$ for the vacuum activities.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The bound $n_Y\leqslant P_M$ holds because a probe label $b$ lies in its host, whose fine side is at most $4M$, and there are four positive directions per site. The bound on $B_Y$ follows from $n_Y\leqslant P_M$, $u_*\leqslant \omega_*e^{-\kappa s_{\mathrm p}}/(8P_M)$ (\eqref{eq:c4-4-6}), and $d_0(Y)\leqslant N_0(Y)-1< s_{\mathrm p}$ for a probe host (\eqref{eq:c2-tree-length} and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-1}).

(a) After taking absolute values inside the real Mayer $t$-integral the ordinary factor is at most $e^{A_Y}-1$ on $|\zeta|\leqslant R_{\Upsilon}$ (as $R_{\Upsilon}\omega(g_0)=\omega_*/2$). The last inequality of \eqref{eq:c4-7-3} uses $\omega_*\leqslant 1/2$ (the standing choice of Section~\ref{app:thresholds}) and $A_Y+B_Y\leqslant \frac58\omega_*e^{-\kappa d_0(Y)}$.

All split selections with the same active-host set have the same $Y_0$, seed, conditioning carrier and Gaussian kernel and, at fixed bad-bond choice $\mathsf P$ and final domain $Z$, the same final-domain weakening (proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:probe-measures}), so their many-to-one sum is dominated at each host by \eqref{eq:c4-7-3} before the cover and seed sums of Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates} are applied.

(b) is the same comparison with the differentiated host bound of Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}.

(c) There are at most $H_MN_1(D)$ active hosts; the Gaussian and walk derivatives have the same factor after their polynomial moment is paid (Sections~\ref{sec:c4-10-2}, \ref{sec:c4-10-3}): the uniform Gaussian coercivity gives polynomial moments at most $C_MN_1(D)$ times the same exponential volume majorant $e^{N_1(D)}$. The differentiated sum with the positive host comparison (b) gives \eqref{eq:c4-7-5}, and the same sum over the selections with $\mathsf J=\varnothing$ gives the vacuum-activity bound.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The Multi-root Cancellation}\label{sec:c4-7-2}
The input $f$ is a single normalised character of the ordered closed reconstructed word, optionally closed with its inverse background interval and a fixed complementary $h$; for a linear combination the bound is multiplied by the sum of the absolute coefficients. On covered branches its contour input labels lie in $I$, so the retained $A_{\mathrm e}$ and the boundary map do not enter the source rows (Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}); the centred kernel $K_{\xi;0}$ likewise uses zero retained input, and the reference group construction uses the same row and mean conventions.

\begin{lemma}[Commuting Projections]\label{lem:c4-7-2}
Let $O_0$ be the set of roots with odd $q_j$ and empty ordinary selection, $O_1$ the set of roots with odd $q_j$ and nonempty ordinary selection. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-6}
    \Bigl|\int\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f\,\dd\bigotimes_j\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell_j}\Bigr|\leqslant u^q\prod_{j\in O_0\cup O_1}\Bigl(u+\frac{2}{R_{\Upsilon}-1}\Bigr)\prod_jM_{\ell_j}\;,
\end{equation}
with the exponential-in-$q$ constants absorbed in $C_{\chi}$; after one background derivative the same holds with the factor $M_{\ell_j}$ of the differentiated root replaced by $\sup_{|\zeta|\leqslant R_{\Upsilon}}\|\mathscr D_{\omega}\Lambda^{\mathrm f}_{\xi;\ell_j,\zeta}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}$, which \eqref{eq:c4-7-5} sums, and with the additional factor of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-3}. Moreover $\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f=0$ if some selected label does not influence the closed source word, so every surviving root has a contact with $\Gamma_C$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For $j\in O_0$, $P_j$ is the projection onto the homogeneous part of degree $q_j$ of $\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f$ in the selected variables of root $j$, the other root variables fixed; these projections commute. In the expansion of $\prod_{j\in O_0}(P_j+(1-P_j))$ a term containing $P_j$ is odd under the reversal of exactly root $j$ and integrates to zero against that root's even source-free density; only $\prod_{j\in O_0}(1-P_j)$ remains, with one extra $u$ per such root by the mixed Taylor remainder \eqref{eq:c4-10-9} and the fixed row-overlap count.

For $j\in O_1$ the independent $\zeta_j$-integral vanishes at $\zeta_j=0$, so the multivariable Cauchy difference supplies $\prod_{j\in O_1}2/(R_{\Upsilon}-1)$ times the supremum $\prod M_{\ell_j}$ of \eqref{eq:c4-4-5}. Together this is \eqref{eq:c4-7-6}, and for even $q_j$ only $u^{q_j}M_{\ell_j}$ is paid.

After one background derivative the Gaussian derivative is even, the leading source derivative has the same parity in the selected variables (a background derivative hits a row coefficient or a background occurrence of the closed word, not the selected root variables, Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-4}; the resulting bound is \eqref{eq:c4-10-10}) and a differentiated Mayer factor still vanishes at $\zeta_j=0$, so the argument repeats.

The last statement is the pairwise cancellation of $K$ with $K\cup\{ b\}$ in the $K$-sum \eqref{eq:c4-4-1} for a label $b$ of a root that the word does not see.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The Common Hessian Bounds on the Extension}\label{sec:c4-7-3}
\begin{lemma}[Hessian Bounds along the Coefficient Path]\label{lem:c4-7-3}
Let $\tau_{\mathrm b}>0$ be fixed after $\tau_L$, $c_L$, $\gamma_L$ and before $g_0$, with $\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \tau_L/4$, $c_L\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \gamma_L/4$ and the chart conditions of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-1} (the matrix-logarithm neighbourhood and the entry-chart norm, each a smallness condition on $\tau_{\mathrm b}$ in terms of constants fixed before $g_0$). For every $t\in[0,1]$ and every globally small extension $U= e^{itB}U^{\circ}$ with $\| B\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}$ of the flat background on a comparison box, every compression of the regional Hessian to the same $I$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-7}
    \frac34\gamma_L\,\id\leqslant H_{e^{itB}}\leqslant m_L\,\id\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On physical branches Lemma~\ref{lem:regular-bounds} gives $\gamma_L/2\leqslant H_{\xi,II}\leqslant m_L$ with the force--constraint and soft-gauge terms.

The local entry formula $f_{bb'}(A)$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} has row sums at most $m_L$ on the phase box $\tau_L$ by the definition of $m_L$ in \eqref{eq:regular-covariance-entry-constants}, column sums equal to its row sums since $f_{bb'}= f_{b'b}^{\mathsf T}$ have equal norms, entries vanishing beyond the range of that lemma, and Lipschitz bound $c_L$ in the phase; so the extension has operator difference from $H^{\circ}=\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{\id}$ at most $c_L\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \gamma_L/4$ by the Schur test, uniformly in $t$. The flat lower bound $\gamma_L$ (\eqref{eq:covariance-uniform-gap}) passes to every compression to $I$ by the compression argument in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}, and with the difference bound this gives \eqref{eq:c4-7-7}.

The recipe $\gamma=\gamma_L/2$, $h_+= m_L$ of Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel} therefore applies at the physical endpoint and throughout the extension.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Differentiating the Joint Vacuum Ratio}\label{sec:c4-7-4}
$\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)$ is the Ursell expression $\varphi^T(\mathfrak c)\prod_jk^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D_j)/m!$ of \eqref{eq:part1-vacuum-cluster} with the fixed-kernel vacuum activities.

\begin{lemma}[Derivative of the Cluster Sum]\label{lem:c4-7-4}
With the majorant $M_v(\mathfrak c)$ of \eqref{eq:c4-6-Mv} and $n(\mathfrak c)=\sum_{D\in\mathfrak c}N_1(D)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-8}
    |\mathscr D_{\omega}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)|\leqslant C_M\|\omega\|_{\infty}\,n(\mathfrak c)M_v(\mathfrak c)\;,
\end{equation}
and for every finite set $\mathcal A$ of connected final domains
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-7-9}
    \sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}M_v(\mathfrak c)e^{n(\mathfrak c)/2}\leqslant \frac18\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D),\qquad
    \sum_{\mathfrak c\text{ hits }\mathcal A}|\mathscr D_{\omega}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c)|\leqslant \frac{C_M}{2}\|\omega\|_{\infty}\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
\eqref{eq:c4-7-8} is the product rule over the constituents with the activity derivative bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1}(c), summed over the differentiated vertex.

The numerical criterion of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds}, \eqref{eq:native-source-weighted-vacuum-criterion}, is stated for $| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}|$; its proof uses only $| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)|\leqslant m(D)=\varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda_*\ell_1(D)}$, so it gives $\sum_{D'\not\sim D}m(D')e^{(1+6\theta)N_1(D')}\leqslant N_1(D)/8$ as well. The rooted-tree proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters} (Appendix~\ref{app:kp}), applied to the activity $m(D)e^{N_1(D)/2}$ with node cost $N_1(D)/8$, the combined exponent $5/8$ being below $1+6\theta$, gives the first bound of \eqref{eq:c4-7-9}; the family version follows by summing the single-root bound over $D\in\mathcal A$ (clusters hitting several roots being overcounted). Since $n\leqslant 4e^{n/4}\leqslant 4e^{n/2}$, inserting \eqref{eq:c4-7-8} gives the second bound.

Inserting the second bound into the derivative of the exponential \eqref{eq:c4-4-11} proves \eqref{eq:c4-4-12}.

The same $m(D)$ controls the undifferentiated activity along the whole extension ($| k^{\mathrm f}_{\xi}(D)|\leqslant m(D)$ there by Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3} and the host bounds of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10}) and its one-derivative polynomial majorant, the polynomial being paid by the displayed exponential moment.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Quantitative Group Estimates}\label{sec:c4-8}
\subsubsection{Carrier, Source and Physical Weights}\label{sec:c4-8-1}
All group comparisons and flat-subtraction identities are made on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$. There the source rows have their free inputs in $I$, so Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} gives $U_{\xi}(0)(r)= U_1(r)$ for every contour bond $r$, and the free vector $B= a+\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ equals $a$ on $I$ ($\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$ vanishes on $I$, proof of that lemma), so neither $A_{\mathrm e}$ nor $\Psi_{\xi}$ enters the fluctuating source rows; Lemma~\ref{lem:collar} and \eqref{eq:c-collar-identity} give $K_{\xi;1}$, and $K_{\xi;0}$ is the $s=0$ member of the interpolation \eqref{eq:c4-11-1}, with $H= H_{\xi,II}$, $P_{\xi,0}(a)=\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near}}\mathfrak p(a)$ and the chosen $r$-box, every primitive argument having zero retained input. The boundary Jacobian, the far primitives and the retained quadratic term are in $c_{\xi}$, and every fixed-kernel operation, probe measure and vacuum activity is built from the centred objects. Hence the local background data of a coefficient are $U_1$, the carrier geometry and the fixed coupling/cutoff/mean prescription; $V_0$ enters these local coefficients only through $U_1$.

The local-data comparison of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11} applies on a box containing all source and coefficient stencils and lying in $\Lambda_1$ outside $S_1$. The fixed-kernel support statements (Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-2}) place every surviving walk coefficient, seed inverse and primitive stencil there, and the regional $I$ and $\Omega_1$ are kept on both sides of the interpolation. At the flat endpoint these local formulas are the reference formulas for $a_W$, since their arguments contain no retained field, boundary map or additional $V_0$. The force--constraint and relative soft-gauge terms are those of the regional Hessian \eqref{eq:c-regional-hessian} and are included throughout.

Under a simultaneous site gauge each Hessian entry, restricted inverse and fixed walk coefficient is conjugated by the free-field adjoint action (Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}, Lemma~\ref{lem:walk-series}), the protected cutoffs are invariant, and the row solution is covariant; orthogonal changes of the integration variables leave the closed selected integrals unchanged, including their spatial Cauchy integrals, and their Laplace transforms give the covariance of each probe measure; the vacuum activities and Ursell products are scalar invariants; finally $T_WP_W^{-1}$ and $h$ are simultaneously conjugated at the interval base. This is the gauge law of the group closed contraction factor by factor (Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-2}).

$\mathcal O$ is the positive outer operation \eqref{eq:native-source-explicit-outer-operation}: the Haar and constraint factors are measures and the displayed cutoffs and exponentials are nonnegative, and $0<\mathcal Z_0<\infty$ (finite by the measurability paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}; $\mathcal Z_0=\int\mathcal O[\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]]\,\dd V=\int\mathcal O[\mathsf w_{\xi}]\,\dd V$ is the normaliser of \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}, the integral of a positive function, since $\nu_{\xi;1}$ is a probability measure and so $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]=\mathsf w_{\xi}$ by \eqref{eq:c-collar-identity}), so $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ is a positive normalised functional.

In \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity}, multiplied by $\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}$ and with $\mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]=\mathsf w_{\xi} F_{\xi}(1)$ on $A^c_{\mathrm{cov}}$, every term is integrable against the finite positive measure $\mathcal O[\mathsf w_{\xi}\,\bigcdot \,]\,\dd V$, because $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)|=| F_{\xi}(0)-\mathscr R_{\xi}|\leqslant 3$ by \eqref{eq:part1-scalar-extraction}, $| F_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant 1$ and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}, $| F_{\xi}(1)|\leqslant 1$, and $|\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{resp},\chi}g_0r| I_C|$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ (Section~\ref{sec:c3-6}). With $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-6-2}, the full identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-1}
    \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C)]=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}f_{\xi}(0)\bigr]+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\;,
\end{equation}
by \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity} and \eqref{eq:native-source-physical-ratio}.

The far uncovered event is empty: if coverage fails, either a contour bond $r$ is not a bond of $\Omega_1\supseteq\Lambda_1$, so that $r$ has an endpoint in $\Lambda_1^c= B_{\xi}$, or a bond of a stencil $\mathcal F_r\not\subseteq I$ is a free bond with no endpoint in $\Lambda_1$ ($I=\Lambda_1^*$, Section~\ref{sec:branch-data}); in both cases an element of $\Gamma_C$ (a contour bond or a bond of a free-input stencil) lies in $E(B_{\xi})$, so $\operatorname{dist}(\Gamma_C,E(B_{\xi}))=0$ and $A_{\mathrm{cov}}^c\subseteq\mathsf N_0\subseteq\mathsf N_b$ (\eqref{eq:c4-2-1}; the events $\mathsf N_b$ increase with $b$).

The exterior response is $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-6-2}, bounded in Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard}.

\subsubsection{Two Quantitative Pins}\label{sec:c4-8-2}
\begin{definition}[Components, Classes, and Their Weights]\label{def:components}
A component $\gamma$ consists of a nonempty unordered root family $\mathcal A(\gamma)$ of marked domains and an ordered list $(\mathfrak c_1,\ldots,\mathfrak c_k)$ of cluster occurrences with connected incidence graph as in Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}. Its cube count $n_{\gamma}$ counts every constituent cube with its occurrence multiplicity; $\mathsf T_{\gamma}$ is the union of the contact sets of its roots, $H_{\gamma}$ the hull of $\mathsf T_{\gamma}$, $X_{\gamma}$ the union of its domains (roots and cluster constituents), and $F(\gamma)$ its footprint, defined by \eqref{eq:c4-6-footprint} with the domains of $X_{\gamma}$ and the traversals of $H_{\gamma}$. The weight of a component is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-2}
    t_{\gamma}\coloneqq\frac{\rho^{|\mathcal A(\gamma)|}}{k!}\prod_{D\in\mathcal A(\gamma)}m(D)\prod_{j=1}^kM_v(\mathfrak c_j)\;.
\end{equation}
A class $K$ is an unordered family of components with connected hull-overlap graph, with weight $t_K\coloneqq\prod_{\gamma\in K}t_{\gamma}$. A class is long when the union of the hulls of its members has at least $n_C/2$ positions.
\end{definition}

Every component has at least one marked root, so $\mathsf T_{\gamma}\neq\varnothing$ (only families of marked domains contribute, Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}), and its hull is a cyclic interval of fewer than $n_C/2$ traversals or the whole contour (Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}). For a long class all components merge into the whole-contour group (Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}).

Summing unordered distinct roots is overcounted by ordered root tuples divided by their factorial; for the positive recursion the sum over classes is overcounted by ordered tuples divided by the tuple factorial, dropping the disjointness restrictions. The exponent $\varpi$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-3}
    0<\varpi\leqslant \min\Bigl(\frac1{16},\frac{\lambda_*}{64C_{\mathrm g}}\Bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
with $C_{\mathrm g}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}.

\begin{lemma}[Hull and Spread Constants]\label{lem:c4-8-hull}
There are constants $A_{\mathrm h}$, $A_{\mathrm x}$, fixed before the coupling, such that for every component $\gamma$, $| H_{\gamma}|\leqslant A_{\mathrm h}LMn_{\gamma}$, and the distance from a source contact of $\gamma$ to any cube of $X_{\gamma}$, halos included, is at most $A_{\mathrm x}LMn_{\gamma}$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Both bounds follow from the square geometry and the wall connectivity of a component's domains (the geometry paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:c4-6}).
\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[Pin Rates]\label{def:pin-rates}
With $A_{\mathrm h}$, $A_{\mathrm x}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-hull}, let
\begin{equation*}
    \theta_{\mathrm h}\coloneqq\frac{\varpi}{4A_{\mathrm h}LM},\qquad \theta_{\mathrm x}\coloneqq\frac{\varpi}{4A_{\mathrm x}LM},\qquad A_{\mathrm s}\coloneqq 1+A_{\mathrm h},\qquad \mathfrak s(\gamma)\coloneqq n_{\gamma}+\frac{| H_{\gamma}|}{LM}\;,
\end{equation*}
and fix $\eta>0$ with $1000\eta A_{\mathrm s}<\varpi/8$. Further, $d_C$ is the contour distance and $d_T(a',\Delta)$ the periodic fine distance (Section~\ref{sec:c4-2}) from the bond of the traversal $a'$ to the cube $\Delta$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Component Pins]\label{lem:c4-8-2}
There are constants $C_{\mathrm{pin}}$ and $C$, fixed before the coupling, such that, for $\rho$ below a threshold depending on them and with the rates of Definition~\ref{def:pin-rates}:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] for every root $D_0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-4}
    \sum_{\gamma\, | \,D_0\in\mathcal A(\gamma)}t_{\gamma} e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}}\leqslant \rho\,m(D_0)e^{(\varpi+1/4)N_1(D_0)},\qquad
    \sup_{a\in\mathcal I_C}\sum_{\gamma\, | \,a\in\mathsf T_{\gamma}}t_{\gamma} e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}}\leqslant C_{\mathrm{pin}}\rho\;;
\end{equation}
\item[(b)] for every traversal $a$ and every cube $\Delta$,
\begin{gather}
    \sum_{\gamma\, | \,a\in H_{\gamma}}t_{\gamma} e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/4}\leqslant \sum_{a'\in\mathcal I_C}e^{-\theta_{\mathrm h}d_C(a,a')}\sum_{\gamma\, | \,a'\in\mathsf T_{\gamma}}t_{\gamma} e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/2}\leqslant C_{\mathrm{pin}}\rho\Bigl(1+\frac{2}{e^{\theta_{\mathrm h}}-1}\Bigr)\;,\label{eq:c4-8-5}\\
    \sum_{\gamma\, | \,\Delta\subset X_{\gamma}}t_{\gamma} e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/4}\leqslant C_{\mathrm{pin}}\rho\sum_{a'\in\mathcal I_C}e^{-\theta_{\mathrm x}d_T(a',\Delta)}\leqslant C\rho\;,\label{eq:c4-8-6}
\end{gather}
and the footprint pin $\sum_{\gamma\, | \,\Delta\in F(\gamma)}t_{\gamma} e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/4}\leqslant C\rho$ holds, with $C$ enlarged by the stencil factor $CLM$;
\item[(c)] the three pins of (b) hold with the weight $e^{100\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}$, leaving a fixed exponential margin.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The sum is a two-species positive tree recursion, the recursion of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:vacuum-clusters} (Appendix~\ref{app:kp}) with two kinds of nodes: the roots $D$, with weight $\rho\,m(D)e^{\varpi N_1(D)}$ and cost $N_1(D)/4$, and the cluster occurrences $\mathfrak c$, with weight $M_v(\mathfrak c)e^{\varpi n(\mathfrak c)}$ and cost $n(\mathfrak c)/4$; a connected incidence graph is bounded by the sum of its spanning trees, the factorials are the exponential-generating factorials of the unordered roots and the ordered occurrence list, and the iterates $T^{(k+1)}_v= t_v\exp(\sum_{v'\sim v}T^{(k)}_{v'})$ satisfy $T^{(k)}_v\leqslant t_ve^{a_v}$ once $\sum_{v'\sim v}t_{v'}e^{a_{v'}}\leqslant a_v$ for every node $v$ (weights $t_v$, costs $a_v$).

The criterion holds. The occurrences hitting a node have weighted mass at most one half of its cost, by \eqref{eq:c4-7-9} applied to the node's constituents, since $e^{\varpi n}e^{n/4}\leqslant e^{n/2}$ ($\varpi+1/4<1/2$). A root hitting a node is incompatible with one of its constituents, so it contains one of the at most $9N_1$ cubes meeting a constituent cube or sharing a wall with it ($N_1$ the node's cube count); for a fixed cube $Q$,
\begin{equation*}
    \sum_{D\ni Q}m(D)e^{(\varpi+1/4)N_1(D)}\leqslant \varepsilon_*\sum_{D\ni Q}e^{-(\lambda_*-(\varpi+1/4)C_{\mathrm g})\ell_1(D)}\leqslant \varepsilon_*B(\lambda_*/2)\eqqcolon C_{\mathrm a}\;,
\end{equation*}
by $N_1(D)\leqslant C_{\mathrm g}\ell_1(D)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-domain-geometry}(1); the final domains are localisation domains) and the animal bound \eqref{eq:native-source-animal-sum}, applicable because $\lambda_*-(\varpi+1/4)C_{\mathrm g}\geqslant \lambda_*-\tfrac5{16}C_{\mathrm g}\geqslant \lambda_*/2> C_{\mathrm g}\log64$ by $\varpi\leqslant 1/16$ and $\lambda_*\geqslant 2C_{\mathrm g}\log128$ (\eqref{eq:c2-kappa-choice}). So the roots hitting a node have weighted mass at most $9\rho C_{\mathrm a}N_1\leqslant N_1/32$, one eighth of the cost, once $9\rho C_{\mathrm a}\leqslant 1/32$, a condition on $\rho$ alone, that is on $g_0$. The rooted sum at $D_0$ is therefore at most $\rho\,m(D_0)e^{\varpi N_1(D_0)}e^{N_1(D_0)/4}$, the first bound of \eqref{eq:c4-8-4}. A root $D_0$ with source contact $a$ has a bond of $\mathsf L_{D_0}$ in the stencil $\mathcal F_{r_a}$ (\eqref{eq:part1-contact-set}), so it contains one of the at most $C_{\mathrm{st}}$ cubes meeting that stencil ($C_{\mathrm{st}}$ a constant of $L$ and $M$); summing the first bound over these roots by the display gives the second bound with $C_{\mathrm{pin}}\coloneqq C_{\mathrm{st}}C_{\mathrm a}$.

(b) By Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-hull}, if a traversal $a$ lies in $H_{\gamma}$ and $a'$ is a contact of $\gamma$, then $d_C(a,a')\leqslant A_{\mathrm h}LMn_{\gamma}$, so $e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/4}\leqslant e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/2}e^{-\theta_{\mathrm h}d_C(a,a')}$, and the contour sum $\sum_{a'}e^{-\theta_{\mathrm h}d_C(a,a')}\leqslant 1+2/(e^{\theta_{\mathrm h}}-1)$ is uniform in $n_C$. For a cube $\Delta\subset X_{\gamma}$ the analogous inequality holds with $\theta_{\mathrm x}$ and the torus distance; for each of the four straight sides the sum over $a'$ is at most $1+2/(e^{\theta_{\mathrm x}}-1)$ up to the fixed cube/halo offset, bounded by the full one-dimensional periodic lattice sum independently of $n$ and the periods. A cube $\Delta\in F(\gamma)$ either meets a domain of $X_{\gamma}$ or its stencil halo (a fixed offset, absorbed as above) or meets the stencil of a traversal of $H_{\gamma}$, and at most $CLM$ traversals have stencils meeting a given cube; so the footprint pin is at most \eqref{eq:c4-8-6} plus $CLM$ times the hull pin \eqref{eq:c4-8-5}, which is the stated bound with the enlarged constant.

(c) $100\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)\leqslant 100\eta A_{\mathrm s}n_{\gamma}<\varpi n_{\gamma}/8$, so the enhanced weights are dominated by the $e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/4}$ of (b) with a margin $e^{\varpi n_{\gamma}/8}$.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Short Classes and the Exceptional Whole-Contour Merge}\label{sec:c4-8-3}
\begin{lemma}[Class Pins]\label{lem:c4-8-3}
Let $C$ be the constant of the pins (b)--(c) of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2} and assume $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$. Let $\sigma_K\coloneqq\sum_{\gamma\in K}\mathfrak s(\gamma)$ for a class $K$. Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] for every overlap-connected class $K$, before the promotion of a long class to the whole contour, the hull and footprint pin sums $\sup_{a\in\mathcal I_C}\sum_{K\, | \,a\in\bigcup_{\gamma\in K}H_{\gamma}}t_Ke^{64\eta\sigma_K}$ and $\sup_{\Delta}\sum_{K\, | \,\Delta\in\bigcup_{\gamma\in K}F(\gamma)}t_Ke^{64\eta\sigma_K}$ are at most $C\rho$;
\item[(b)] a long class satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-7}
    \sigma_K\geqslant \frac{1}{LM}\sum_{\gamma\in K}| H_{\gamma}|\geqslant \frac{n_C}{2LM},\qquad
    \sum_{K\ \mathrm{long}}t_Ke^{4\eta\sigma_K}\leqslant C\rho n_Ce^{-30\eta n_C/(LM)}\;;
\end{equation}
\item[(c)] the whole-contour groups created by the exceptional merge have total weighted mass $\sum_{W\ \mathrm{whole}}M(W)e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}$ at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-8}
    C\rho n_Ce^{-30\eta n_C/(LM)}e^{4\eta n_C/(LM)}e^{C\rho n_C}\leqslant C\rho n_Ce^{-25\eta n_C/(LM)}\leqslant C'\rho\;,
\end{equation}
uniformly in $n_C$;
\item[(d)] the two weighted group pins \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} hold.
\end{itemize}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
(a) The positive overlap-tree recursion runs on the decorated components with the weights enhanced by $e^{64\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}$. The pin of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2}(c) controls the overlap sum of a hull: the components whose hulls meet $H_{\gamma}$ have weighted mass at most $C\rho| H_{\gamma}|\leqslant \eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)/8$ by the hypothesis $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$, so the rooted recursion over components (node weight $t_{\gamma} e^{64\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}$, node cost $\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)/8$; the pins of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2}(c) carry the weight $e^{100\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}\geqslant e^{64\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)}e^{\eta\mathfrak s(\gamma)/8}$, which covers the node cost) gives the hull and footprint pins for every class before promotion: the sum over the classes containing a component pinned by the hull pin at $a$, or by the footprint pin at $\Delta$, is the rooted sum with that component as root. No property of the union interval enters, so the class pins hold for long classes as well; for a short class the interval $\mathcal H(K)$ is the union of its hull intervals (Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}), so its size is bounded by the additive class cost $\sigma_K$.

(b) The first inequality is the definition of $\mathfrak s$; the second is the definition of a long class (the union of its hulls has at least $n_C/2$ positions, Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}). A class is anchored at a traversal of its union interval; there are at most $n_C$ anchors, and the class pin (a) with the weight $e^{64\eta\sigma_K}$ gives the second bound of \eqref{eq:c4-8-7}, the remaining exponent $60\eta\sigma_K$ being at least $30\eta n_C/(LM)$.

(c) Once a long class occurs, every other component is merged into the whole-contour group; the other components with their $4\eta$ weights sum to at most $e^{C\rho n_C}$ (each has a contact on the contour and is pinned there by Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2}(c), so the sum over the families of further components is at most $\prod_{a\in\mathcal I_C}\exp(C\rho)$), and the whole-contour interval weight costs $e^{4\eta n_C/(LM)}$. The middle inequality of \eqref{eq:c4-8-8} uses $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta$, implied by the hypothesis, and the final maximum is finite uniformly in $n_C$ because $LM$ and $\eta$ are fixed.

If a spatial pin lies in an additional component, that component is rooted by its footprint pin at a further cost $C\rho$, the anchored long-class factor and remaining exponential being paid by \eqref{eq:c4-8-8}; if it lies in the long class, the footprint pin replaces the hull pin; pins on the whole contour are covered by the total whole-group bound. Polynomial moments use a smaller part of the same enhanced-weight margin.

(d) A group $W$ with a short interval determines a class $K$ (Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}), and the groups with class $K$ are the interleavings of the cluster lists of its components: by the interleaving count of Lemma~\ref{lem:grouped-source} there are at most $k(W)!/\prod_{\gamma\in K}k_{\gamma}!$ of them, $k(W)=\sum_{\gamma\in K}k_{\gamma}$, and by \eqref{eq:c4-6-MW} each has
\[
    M(W)=\prod_{\gamma\in K}\bigl(\rho^{|\mathcal A(\gamma)|}\prod_{D\in\mathcal A(\gamma)}m(D)\prod_jM_v(\mathfrak c_j)\bigr)/k(W)!\;,
\]
so the sum of $M(W)$ over the groups with class $K$ is at most $t_K$. Every such $W$ has $\mathfrak s(W)\leqslant \sigma_K$, since $n(W)=\sum_{\gamma\in K}n_{\gamma}$ and $\mathcal H(W)$, the union of the overlapping hulls $H_{\gamma}$, has at most $\sum_{\gamma\in K}| H_{\gamma}|$ traversals, and $F(W)\subset\bigcup_{\gamma\in K}F(\gamma)$. Hence the sums of \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} over short groups are bounded by the pin sums of (a), and those over whole-contour groups by (c).
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Interior Boxes, Endpoints and the Differentiated Group Weight}\label{sec:c4-8-4}
Let $C_{\mathrm{box}}$ be a fixed geometric constant for the group footprint and the row/contour halos such that a liftable enclosing comparison rectangle has diameter at most $C_{\mathrm{box}}LMn(W)$, increased so that a group with
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-9}
    n(W)<\frac{b}{4C_{\mathrm{box}}LM}
\end{equation}
has its entire rectangle and stencils within $b/2$ of a source contact and an injective lift (Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-4}). On a far history this box lies in $\Lambda_1$, hence in $\Omega_1$, and outside $S_1=(\Omega_1\setminus\Omega_1^{\sim-1})\cup R_1$; its plaquettes satisfy $\delta_{Q_W}(U_1)\leqslant C\varepsilon_1$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation} and the distance check of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-5}, and, for a group passing the phase test of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-1} (the groups failing it are treated in Section~\ref{sec:c4-12-2}), the Hessian bounds \eqref{eq:c4-7-7} of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3} hold on the globally small extension used for its comparison.

All other groups keep their undifferentiated difference, $| c_W|+| a_W\chi|\leqslant 2M(W)$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-6-2}); their cube count $n(W)$ is at least $b/(4C_{\mathrm{box}}LM)$, and if a rectangle fails to lift the same lower bound holds, since $N_{\min}=\min_iN_i\geqslant 2LMR_1>32b$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-2}) and a wrapping connected network has length at least a fixed fraction of $N_{\min}$.

For a good box, by the coefficient locality and covariance of Sections~\ref{sec:c4-8-1} and~\ref{sec:c4-11}, with the tree gauge rooted at the initial interval base and $h$ fixed, $c_W(U_1;h)$ is compared with $c_W(\id;h)= a_W\chi(h)$ by the small-phase extension and the fundamental theorem of calculus (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-1}, for a group passing the phase test). By the product rule,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-8-10}
    \mathscr D_{\omega} w_{\xi}(W)=\frac{(-1)^{k(W)}}{k(W)!}\sum_{j=1}^{k(W)}\mathscr D_{\omega}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c_j)\prod_{l\ne j}\Phi^{\mathrm v}_{\xi}(\mathfrak c_l)\;,
\end{equation}
bounded by Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-4} by $C_M\|\omega\|_{\infty}\sum_jn(\mathfrak c_j)$ times the positive product majorant.
