With the joint source derivative of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-3}, whose factor $L_f+\sum_DN_1(D)$ is at most $C(|\mathcal H(W)|+n(W))$ because the number $L_f$ of varying background occurrences in the relative word is at most $2|\mathcal H(W)|$ times the fixed reconstruction-row overlap constant (Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-1}) and $\sum_DN_1(D)\leqslant n(W)$, this gives $|\mathscr D_{\omega} c_W|\leqslant C\|\omega\|_{\infty}(n(W)+|\mathcal H(W)|)M(W)$ uniformly in $h$ (\eqref{eq:c4-12-2}); the curvature phase bound contributes $C\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)^2\delta_{Q_W}$, and with $|\mathcal H(W)|\leqslant CLMn(W)$ all these losses are a fixed constant times $\varepsilon_1$ times a fixed polynomial in $\mathfrak s(W)$, absorbed by the enhanced pin ($x^ke^{-\eta x}\leqslant k!\eta^{-k}$).

For a large group the factor $e^{-\eta b/(8C_{\mathrm{box}}LM)}$ is extracted from its reserved weight $e^{\eta\mathfrak s(W)/2}$. Combining the two classes and summing over a contour pin gives \eqref{eq:c4-6-8} (Section~\ref{sec:c4-12-2}).

\subsection{The Coefficient Extension and the Countable-Gas Limit}\label{sec:c4-9}
\subsubsection{The Small-Phase Extension}\label{sec:c4-9-1}
Sections~\ref{sec:c4-4} and~\ref{sec:c4-7} give the joint source and one-derivative bounds at the physical centred background and on every globally small real extension described here, for each closed character $\chi(T_WP_W^{-1}h)$ uniformly in $h$.

Let $W$ be a good interior group of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}, with enclosing fine rectangle $Q_W$, which contains all coefficient, reconstruction, averaging and interval/closing stencils. By the support statements of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-2}, for the fixed selection indices and the fixed spatial Cauchy coefficient defining the group only the background links on $Q_W$ are used: the restricted seed inverse uses entries on $E_0$, every walk coefficient has its domains in the final component, and the potential and source rows have their finite stencils. The regional $I$, $\Omega_1$ and every auxiliary parameter are held fixed.

$g_W$ is the rooted tree gauge of $U_1$ on $Q_W$, with $g_W(\mathrm{base})=\id$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-10-5}). If $C_{\mathrm{tg}}\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)^2\delta_{Q_W}\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2$ (the phase test; since $\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)$ is at least the largest side $R$ of $Q_W$, it implies the hypothesis $C_{\mathrm{tg}}R^2\delta_{Q_W}\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-10-5}), the principal phases $B_W(b)=\frac1i\log U_1^{g_W}(b)$ on the rectangle, extended by $B_W=0$ on every other bond, define the coefficient argument and its direction:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-9-1}
    U_{W,t}(b)= e^{itB_W(b)},\qquad\omega_W(b)= B_W(b),\qquad\|\omega_W\|_{\infty}=\max_bh(B_W(b)),\qquad0\leqslant t\leqslant 1\;;
\end{equation}
the norm is the invariant norm $h$, the comparison with the cutoff norm being absorbed in $C$. $L_f$ is the number of occurrences of background links in the relative word $T_WP_W^{-1}$ on which this argument varies, and $L_f\leqslant 2|\mathcal H(W)|$ times the fixed reconstruction-row overlap constant. The complementary $h$ is held fixed at the root base.

At each $t$ the operator $H_t=\iota_I^*\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{U_{W,t}}\iota_I$, the row reconstruction $q_{U_{W,t}}$ and the near primitives at $U_{W,t}$ are formed with zero retained input and the same protected $r$-box. For a generic noncritical $U_{W,t}$ the energy primitive is defined by subtracting its constant, linear and quadratic Taylor terms as in \eqref{eq:native-source-energy-residual}, the Hessian keeping the force--constraint term; the Haar and constraint-Jacobian primitives use their analytic row formulas. These definitions specify an analytic coefficient extension.

For $t\in(0,1)$ the extension is an auxiliary analytic kernel without the fixed-$V$ constraint. At the physical endpoint each compensated primitive agrees with its Taylor-subtracted formula by locality, criticality entering only through the primitive-sum identity \eqref{eq:native-source-primitive-sum}; at the flat endpoint the formulas agree with the reference formulas.

Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3} gives $\gamma_L/2\leqslant H_t\leqslant m_L$; the designated inverses, reconstruction and means use the fixed smaller row charts since $\| B_W\|_{\infty}\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2$ and $\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \tau_L/4$; the host norms and their derivatives are bounded by $C^{\partial}_0g_0(1+r)^3$ on these charts; so the Gaussian payment, the positive forest budget and the source estimates hold uniformly in $t$. The force term is one of the local entries off the minimum.

\begin{lemma}[The Coefficient Path]\label{lem:c4-9-1}
For a small interior group (\eqref{eq:c4-8-9}, a good box of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}) passing the phase test of Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-1}, and for each $h\in G$ in the closed character $\chi(T_WP_W^{-1}h)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-9-2}
    d_W(U_1;h)=\int_0^1\mathscr D_{\omega_W}c_W(U_{W,t};h)\,\dd t\;,
\end{equation}
and $|\mathscr D_{\omega_W}c_W(U_{W,t};h)|\leqslant C\|\omega_W\|_{\infty}(L_f+n(W))M(W)$ uniformly in $t$ and $h$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
At $t=1$ the group coefficient agrees with the original one by coefficient locality on $Q_W$ and simultaneous gauge covariance (Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-3}): the values outside $Q_W$ can be replaced in the argument because no term of the spatial Cauchy coefficient consults them, and the root gauge $g_W(\mathrm{base})=\id$ leaves $h$ unchanged. At $t=0$ the coefficient is exactly the regional reference one, with the same $I$ and the same group index $W$, so $c_W(U_{W,0};h)= a_W\chi(h)$.

The fundamental theorem of calculus applies: by the dominated-convergence majorants of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-3} and the termwise differentiation statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}, $t\mapsto c_W(U_{W,t};h)$ is continuously differentiable on $[0,1]$ with derivative $\mathscr D_{\omega_W}c_W(U_{W,t};h)$. The derivative of $c_W$ differentiates $\prod_j\Phi^{\mathrm v}(\mathfrak c_j)$, giving the occurrence sum \eqref{eq:c4-8-10} with majorant $C\|\omega\|_{\infty}(\sum_jn(\mathfrak c_j))M(W)$, and the root integral, giving $C\|\omega\|_{\infty}(L_f+\sum_{D}N_1(D))M(W)$ by Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-4-3} and~\ref{lem:c4-7-1}; the sum is the displayed bound.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Parameter and Period Conventions}\label{sec:c4-9-2}
All results inherit the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} and the compatible even fine periods of Section~\ref{sec:c3-7}: every fine period $N_i$ is an even integer multiple of $\ell= LMR_1$, and $\ell$ is odd ($L$ odd, $M$ and $R_1$ powers of $L$). If $N_i= q_i\ell$ then $q_i$ is even and positive, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-9-3}
    N_{\min}=\min_iN_i\geqslant 2LMR_1>32\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor=32b\;,
\end{equation}
the strict middle inequality because $\ell$ is odd. The square-fit condition $K_i\geqslant 3(n+2)$ and the source-row and coarse-grid conditions of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} are also in force. Thus the good comparison box and every fixed stencil have a unique lift under the small-group criterion \eqref{eq:c4-8-9}, and the periodic failure lies in the large-group class.

$\Gamma_C$ consists of the individual positive contour bonds and all their fixed input templates, $C_L$ including the number and size of the templates, and the radius-$b$ ball of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1} is around each individual bond, so the count $4(2b+3)^4$ has no $n_C$-dependent factor.

The input of Appendix~\ref{app:exterior-chessboard} is the one-point probability $p_z\leqslant q\leqslant e^{-c_*\pi_*^2}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c3-7-4} and Proposition~\ref{prop:c3-7-5} (this $q$ is the $q_{\mathrm{pt}}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}) with $p_0(g)= A_0(\log g^{-2})^{p_0}$, $p_0\geqslant 5\mathfrak r\geqslant 10$.

\subsubsection{Countably Many Group Species and Differentiation}\label{sec:c4-9-3}
\begin{lemma}[Countable Species]\label{lem:c4-9-2}
At a fixed finite torus let $\mathcal W_N\coloneqq\{ W\, | \,n(W)\leqslant N\}$, a finite set, with partition sum $S_N$ and connected-cluster logarithm $\mathscr L_N$, $S_N= e^{\mathscr L_N}$. Under the hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-3} ($C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$ and $g_0$ small),
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-9-4}
    \sum_W| a_W| e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\leqslant C\rho n_C<\infty,\qquad \mathscr L_N\to\mathscr L,\qquad S_N\to S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}= e^{\mathscr L}\ne0\;,
\end{equation}
the restricted identity $S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}= e^{\mathscr L^{[\mathfrak B]}}$ ($\mathscr L^{[\mathfrak B]}$ the connected-cluster logarithm of the species compatible with $\mathfrak B$) and the ratio bound \eqref{eq:c4-6-7} hold for the countable index set, and the background derivatives of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-4-3}, \ref{lem:c4-7-1} and~\ref{lem:c4-7-4} may be taken termwise and integrated in $t$ before the countable limit.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
$\mathcal W_N$ is finite: the domain set is finite, and $n(W)$ bounds the number of roots, occurrences and members of every occurrence. Its gas satisfies the same Kotecký--Preiss inequality, deleting species only decreasing the positive sums. Every group has a nonempty contour interval, $| a_W|\leqslant M(W)$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-6-2}) and $e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}= e^{\eta\mathfrak s(W)/8}\leqslant e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}$, so the pin \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} summed over the $n_C$ traversals gives the first bound of \eqref{eq:c4-9-4}; the rooted-tree estimate bounds the total absolute connected-cluster series by this finite sum up to a fixed constant; each finite cluster tuple is present for all large $N$, so absolute domination gives $\mathscr L_N\to\mathscr L$; independently the full gas sum over finite compatible families is absolutely bounded by $\exp(\sum_W| a_W|)$, and dominated convergence gives $S_N\to S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$.

The same argument after excluding every species incompatible with a fixed compatible family $\mathfrak B$ gives the restricted identity; the logarithmic difference is the connected-cluster sum of tuples hitting $\mathfrak B$, counted once, with absolute sum at most $\sum_{W\in\mathfrak B}\mathfrak a_W/8$ by the pinned estimate.

For the derivatives, Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-7-1} and~\ref{lem:c4-7-4} give summable positive majorants independent of $t$ on the extension; on each finite truncation the product and integral derivatives are justified by the uniform Gaussian coercivity (Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-3}) and the fixed protected box, and the walk derivative series converges on its unchanged contours (Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-2}); the cluster majorant $n(\mathfrak c)M_v(\mathfrak c)$ is paid by its exponential moment and the group majorant has only the polynomial in $\mathfrak s(W)$, paid by the reserved weight. Uniform absolute convergence permits termwise differentiation and $t$-integration before the countable limit.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Integrability of the Far-History Sum}\label{sec:c4-9-4}
The near-history contribution is bounded after forming $\mathscr R_{\xi}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}). On covered far histories the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-5} bounds $\sum_{\mathfrak B\ne\varnothing}| S^{\circ,[\mathfrak B]}_{\xi,C}R_{\xi}(\mathfrak B)|$ by $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|$ times the exponential of the one-group sum \eqref{eq:c4-6-9} minus one; since $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant 1$ ($S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$ is the normalised integral \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas} of $f^{\circ}_{\xi}$, a normalised character of modulus at most one, against the positive reference kernel $K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}$) and the exponential is uniform in the branch fields and retained variables, it is integrable against the normalised positive history law at each fixed loop and cutoff, which justifies the far-history sum/integral exchanges.

\subsection{Analytic Inputs for the Coefficient Extension}\label{sec:c4-10}
\subsubsection{Joint Background/Phase Analyticity and Primitive Derivatives}\label{sec:c4-10-1}
For each of the finitely many row/primitive stencil types, in its translated fine-lattice frame, the background on the stencil is $U_Z(b)= e^{iZ_b}$; background directions use the maximum $h$-norm on this finite label set. The radii $\tau_{\mathrm b}$ and $\theta_0>0$ are such that $\| Z\|<2\tau_{\mathrm b}$ and $\| A\|<2\theta_0$ keep every finite path product and relative product entering the bond average and the mean of \cite[(0.4), (0.11)]{BalabanRG1} (\eqref{eq:nonlinear-average}) inside the matrix-logarithm neighbourhood $\| W-\id\|_{\mathrm{op}}<1/2$; this is possible uniformly over the finite types, every word having bounded length and $e^{iA}e^{iZ}$ being analytic in both variables.

The radii $\tau_{\mathrm b}$, $\theta_0$ used below are those of the final joint domain, after the reductions of this section and of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-5}; in particular $2\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \tau_L/2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3}) and $2\theta_0\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-5}), so that Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii)--(iii) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means} apply at each real $Z$ with $\| Z\|<2\tau_{\mathrm b}$ and each $A$ with $\| A\|<2\theta_0$.

The mean of \cite[(0.11)]{BalabanRG1} solves $\sum_j\log(W_jM^{-1})=0$. At $W_j=\id$, $M=\id$ its derivative in the Lie-algebra parameter of $M$ is $-n\,\id$, so the parametric analytic implicit function theorem gives a jointly analytic local mean in the background and fluctuating phases; it agrees with the mean of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-means}, both taking the value $\id$ at zero and solving that equation in the same smaller neighbourhood. The joint radii are shrunk so that the mean stays in that neighbourhood.

The bond constraint on a row $c$ is the jointly analytic function
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-1}
    \mathcal Q_Z(A)=\frac1i\log\bigl(\mathsf M(e^{iA}U_Z,c)\mathsf M(U_Z,c)^{-1}\bigr),\quad LQ_Z= D_A\mathcal Q_Z(0),\quad N_Z(A)=\mathcal Q_Z(A)-LQ_ZA\;,
\end{equation}
$\mathsf M$ the bond average of \cite[(0.4)]{BalabanRG1}, with $N_Z(0)= D_AN_Z(0)=0$ for every $Z$.

The coefficient of the designated phase in $LQ_Z$ is uniformly invertible on a smaller background polydisc, by the identity-background designated inverse (Lemma~\ref{lem:two-block}) and continuity, so the designated inverse $h_Z$ with $LQ_Zh_Z=\id$ and $\mathsf C_Z=\iota_{\mathrm{free}}-h_ZLQ_Z\iota_{\mathrm{free}}$ are analytic in $Z$ with uniformly bounded first background derivatives; these are the maps of Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}. The row solution is defined by
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-2}
    \widetilde D_Z(A)= N_Z\bigl(A-h_Z\widetilde D_Z(A)\bigr)\;.
\end{equation}
On smaller joint balls the derivative of the right side in $\widetilde D$ has norm at most $1/2$ uniformly in $Z$, since $D_AN_Z(A)= O(\| A\|)$; uniform analytic contraction (the parametric implicit function theorem) gives joint analyticity and $\|\widetilde D_Z(A)\|\leqslant C\| A\|^2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii) at each real $Z$). Cauchy estimates on the larger joint balls, followed by the order-two zero in $A$, give for $l=0,1$ and each fixed $k$ needed below
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-3}
    \| D_Z^lD_A^k\widetilde D_Z(A)\|\leqslant C_{l,k}\| A\|^{\max(2-k,0)}\;.
\end{equation}
All constants are maxima over finitely many types, independent of the volume, the history and $g_0$; the dimensions of the types depend on $L$ and $G$ only.

The protected free input satisfies $g_0\|\mathsf C_Za\|<\theta_0/2$ after reducing the coupling, and the phase $q_Z(a)= g_0\mathsf C_Za-h_Z\widetilde D_Z(g_0\mathsf C_Za)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-4}
    \| D_Zq_Z(a)\|\leqslant Cg_0(1+r),\qquad\| D_Z^lD_a^kq_Z(a)\|\leqslant C_{l,k}g_0^k
\end{equation}
for $l=0,1$ and $1\leqslant k\leqslant 2K+1$, $K$ the fixed row input count of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-4}.

Analytic traces of $X$ and $X^{-1}$ extend $\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{tr}X$ from unitary fields, where it equals $\operatorname{tr}(X+X^{-1})/2$; the energy and relative gauge expressions are therefore jointly analytic finite word functions. For the local energy function $E_Z(s)$ in the dimensionless free phase $s$ (the action and gauge-fixing functional of \eqref{eq:action-primitive} at the background $U_Z$), the compensated primitive has the Taylor-remainder form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-5}
    p^{\mathrm E}_Z(a)=-\frac{g_0}{2}\int_0^1(1-t)^2D_s^3E_Z(tg_0a)[a,a,a]\,\dd t\;.
\end{equation}
Its first background derivative has the same factor $g_0$, since $D_ZD_s^3E_Z$ is uniformly bounded on the smaller joint domain; hence $| p^{\mathrm E}|+\| D_Zp^{\mathrm E}\|\leqslant Cg_0(1+r)^3$, the relative means and the soft-gauge term being included in $E_Z$.

The Haar function $\log(\sigma(q)/\sigma(0))$ is analytic in $q$ with an order-two zero, so composed with $q_Z$ it and its $Z$-derivative are at most $Cg_0^2(1+r)^2$. The constraint-Jacobian logarithm is $\log\det(\id-h_ZD_A\widetilde D_Z)$ on a matrix ball of radius $<1/2$; its value and $Z$-derivative are at most $Cg_0(1+r)$, as $D_A\widetilde D_Z= O(g_0(1+r))$ and $D_ZD_A\widetilde D_Z$ has the same order, and the real determinant is positive on that ball, so the analytic logarithm restricts to the real logarithm of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(iii).

Summing the finite primitive types assigned to one host gives the host derivative bound with $C^{\partial}_0= N_{\mathrm h}\max(C_{\mathrm p},C^{\partial}_{\mathrm p})e^{\kappa(B_{\mathrm h}+4)}$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}; this constant and the finite source derivative constants are fixed after $M$ and $\tau_{\mathrm b}$ and before $g_0$, and no Mayer, walk or reserve constant depends on them.

\subsubsection{Differentiated Fixed Walks and Exact Locality}\label{sec:c4-10-2}
The series \eqref{eq:c-weighted-walk-series} has the parameters $s_H=2h_+$, $\mathsf A_H=\id-H/s_H$, $\mathsf P_H=\mathsf A_H^{n_*}$, $q_H=1-\gamma/s_H$, $\beta= V_*q_H^{n_*}$ ($V_*= V_{n_*}$), $a_*= e^{81\kappa_1}$ and $n_*$, fixed from the common input bounds for all backgrounds. Of the background these constructions use only the input bounds \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-inputs}, $\gamma\leqslant H\leqslant h_+$, and the $R$-locality of the entries; both hold along $U_{W,t}$, the two-sided bound by Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3} and the locality by the entry statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}, whose radius $R$ does not depend on the background.

The index set contains every geometrically allowed tuple of bond indices, including those whose coefficients vanish at a particular background, so it does not change under differentiation. The weights $w_{\omega}(\sigma)$ and domains $D(\omega)$ depend only on the labels and the fixed geometry.

Let $c_H$ bound the Schur row and column norms of $\mathscr D_{\omega} H/\|\omega\|_{\infty}$, supplied by the finite analytic entries of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-1}. Then $\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathsf A_H=-\mathscr D_{\omega} H/s_H$ and $\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathsf A_H^j=\sum_{l=0}^{j-1}\mathsf A_H^l(\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathsf A_H)\mathsf A_H^{j-1-l}$, a block sum of which is bounded by $V_jjq_H^{j-1}c_H\|\omega\|_{\infty}/s_H$. Let $d_*\coloneqq V_*n_*q_H^{n_*-1}c_H/s_H$ and let $d_{\mathrm{ini}}$ be the maximum of the corresponding bounds for $j< n_*$. Differentiating the grouped walk products gives the absolute Schur bound
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-6}
    \|\mathscr D_{\omega} S_{Z_0}(\sigma)\|_{\mathrm{Schur}}\leqslant C^{\partial}_{\mathrm w}\|\omega\|_{\infty},\qquad
    C^{\partial}_{\mathrm w}= s_H^{-1/2}n_*\Bigl(\frac{a_*d_{\mathrm{ini}}}{1-a_*\beta}+\frac{a_*^2V_*d_*}{(1-a_*\beta)^2}\Bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
the denominators positive because $a_*\beta\leqslant 1/4$ (\eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-grouping}); the same bound holds on the spatial Cauchy circles.

The derivative of $C_{E_0}$ is $-C_{E_0}(\mathscr D_{\omega} H_{E_0})C_{E_0}$, with $H_{E_0}\coloneqq\iota_{E_0}^*H\iota_{E_0}$, and that of $\Gamma_{E_0}$ is the product rule on $\iota_{E_0}^*H\Pi_{I\setminus E_0}S_{Z_0}$ (\eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-C-Gamma}); their operator norms are fixed constants times $\|\omega\|_{\infty}$.

For a selected final domain $Z$ the spatial variables outside $Z$ are zero and the protected seed enlargement $Z_0'$ lies in $Z$; a walk with a coefficient domain meeting a cube outside $Z$ has a zero spatial factor, which remains zero after background differentiation. Every surviving walk, including every hidden fine step in its grouped powers, has its coefficient stencil inside its declared domains by the construction of $D_b$ (Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}).

The restricted inverse $C_{E_0}=H_{E_0}^{-1}$ consults only entries on the seed $E_0$, included in the comparison rectangle, and the normalised Gaussian determinant is $\det C_{E_0}$. All potential and source stencils and every constituent vacuum domain of $c_W$ lie in $Q_W$. Hence no surviving selected coefficient consults the background outside $Q_W$; this is the locality used at $t=1$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-1}.

The common full Gaussian prefactor $\mathfrak n_{\xi}$ (Section~\ref{sec:fixed-first-kernel}) cancels in the conditional ratio defining $F_{\xi}(0)$ (\eqref{eq:fixed-probe-centred-source}).

\subsubsection{The Complex-Gaussian Moment Payment}\label{sec:c4-10-3}
On a selected component, $E$ is its seed carrier $E_D$, $J_Z$ its auxiliary carrier $J_D$ (the block of $\bigsqcup_DJ_D$ belonging to this component, Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks}), $H_E=\iota_E^*H\iota_E$, $C_E= H_E^{-1}$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma_1+i\Gamma_2$ is the block of $\Gamma_{E_0}(\sigma)$, the pairings being complex bilinear. Before cutoffs and Mayer factors the joint density with respect to real Lebesgue measure $\dd B\,\dd X$ is the two centred Gaussian normalisations times
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-11}
    G_{\sigma}(B,X)=\exp\Bigl[-\frac12\langle B,H_EB\rangle-\langle B,\Gamma X\rangle-\frac12\langle\Gamma X,C_E\Gamma X\rangle-\frac12\| X\|^2\Bigr]\;.
\end{equation}
The columns of $\Gamma$ outside $J_Z$, and those of its derivative, vanish identically by Lemma~\ref{lem:component-blocks}, so the auxiliary standard Gaussians outside $J_Z$ integrate to one.

With $\alpha=\alpha_G$ and $C_{\alpha}=(H_E-\alpha\id)^{-1}$, the absolute density times $e^{\alpha\| B\|^2/2}$ is a positive real Gaussian with the original determinant prefactor; in the variables $y= B+C_{\alpha}\Gamma_1X$ its exponent is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-12}
    -\frac12\langle y,(H_E-\alpha)y\rangle-\frac12\langle X,(\id-T_{\alpha})X\rangle\;,\qquad T_{\alpha}\coloneqq\Gamma_1^{\mathsf T}(C_{\alpha}-C_E)\Gamma_1+\Gamma_2^{\mathsf T}C_E\Gamma_2\;,
\end{equation}
the reserve matrix of Appendix~\ref{app:fixed-kernel-payment}. With $H_E-\alpha\geqslant \gamma/2$ (from $H\geqslant \gamma$, \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-inputs}, and $\alpha_G\leqslant \gamma/2$, Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii)), $\| T_{\alpha}\|\leqslant 1/4$ (\eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-reserve-payment}) and $\|\Gamma_1\|\leqslant A_*$ (the norm paragraph of Appendix~\ref{app:fixed-kernel-payment}) and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-13}
    c_{\mathrm G}=\frac{\min(\gamma/2,3/4)}{2(1+2A_*/\gamma)^2}>0\;,
\end{equation}
the real quadratic form is at least $c_{\mathrm G}(\| B\|^2+\| X\|^2)$. Its total unnormalised mass is the determinant product bounded by $e^{N_1(Z)}$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:gaussian-payment}(ii), and its normalised covariance is at most $c_{\mathrm G}^{-1}\id$. With $d= d_G(| E|+| J_Z|)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-14}
    \int(1+\| B\|^2+\| X\|^2)e^{\alpha_G\| B\|^2/2}| G_{\sigma}(B,X)|\,\dd B\,\dd X\leqslant (1+d/c_{\mathrm G})e^{N_1(Z)}\;,
\end{equation}
and $d\leqslant 8d_G(LM+1)^4N_1(Z)$, so the loss is linear in the cube count $N_1(Z)$ with a fixed $M$-dependent constant, paid by the margin $3/4$ in $\id-T_{\alpha}$.

The logarithmic derivative of the Gaussian normalisation contributes $\operatorname{Tr}(C_E\mathscr D_{\omega} H_E)/2$; the exponent derivative contributes $-\langle B,(\mathscr D_{\omega} H_E)B\rangle/2$, $-\langle B,(\mathscr D_{\omega}\Gamma)X\rangle$ and $-\mathscr D_{\omega}\langle\Gamma X,C_E\Gamma X\rangle/2$ with $\mathscr D_{\omega} C_E=-C_E(\mathscr D_{\omega} H_E)C_E$; each is bounded by $C\|\omega\|_{\infty}(d+\| B\|^2+\| X\|^2)$ by Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-2}. Hence \eqref{eq:c4-10-14} proves the differentiated Gaussian payment $C_MN_1(Z)\|\omega\|_{\infty} e^{N_1(Z)}$ on the same Cauchy circles and carriers, all normalisers and the negative compensator $-\frac12\langle\Gamma X,C_E\Gamma X\rangle$ differentiated. The protected cutoff domain does not depend on the background, so the derivative has no surface term.

\subsubsection{Source Remainder Bounds}\label{sec:c4-10-4}
Let $\mathsf J\coloneqq(b_1,\ldots,b_q)$ be distinct selected labels and let $a'$ denote all other selected root variables. The mixed fundamental theorem of calculus gives the exact identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-7}
    \Delta_{\mathsf J}f(B,a')=\int_{[0,1]^q}D_{b_1}\cdots D_{b_q}f\Bigl(a'+\sum_{j=1}^qs_jB_{b_j}\Bigr)[B_{b_1},\ldots,B_{b_q}]\,\dd\mathbf s\;,
\end{equation}
the sum in the argument meaning the canonical embedding into the free carrier. Let $K$ be a fixed bound for the number of source rows affected by one free label and for the number of inputs of one row.

The source is $f_W(a;h)=\chi(T_W(a)P_W^{-1}h)$ or the original closed Wilson character, a normalised character, so $| f|\leqslant 1$; untouched factors are unitary in its representation. The derivative product rule has at most $K^q$ row assignments, and the derivatives within a row have order at most $2K+1$, whose constants \eqref{eq:c4-10-4} are fixed. Consequently, with a fixed $C_{\chi}$ enlarged once,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-8}
    \| D_{b_1}\cdots D_{b_q}f\|\leqslant (C_{\chi} g_0)^q,\qquad\sup|\Delta_{\mathsf J}f|\leqslant (C_{\chi} g_0r)^q\;.
\end{equation}
For root $j$ let $P_j$ be its homogeneous degree-$q_j$ projection after taking $\Delta_{\mathsf J_j}$. Subtracting the integrand of \eqref{eq:c4-10-7} at zero root input and integrating its first derivative along the segment $t(\mathbf sB)$ gives $q_j$ terms, each with one additional derivative and one additional selected $B$ factor. Thus, for any set $O$ of roots,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-9}
    \sup\Bigl|\prod_{j\in O}(1-P_j)\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f\Bigr|\leqslant u^{q+| O|},\qquad u= C_{\chi} g_0(1+r)\;,
\end{equation}
the choices of the extra increment, at most $\prod_{j\in O}q_j\leqslant 2^q$, being absorbed in $C_{\chi}$. The row-order bound $2K+1$ covers these remainders simultaneously because the roots have disjoint selected labels and a row has at most $K$ inputs.

A single background derivative hits either a row coefficient or one of the $L_f$ background occurrences of the closed word; \eqref{eq:c4-10-4} and the product rule give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-10}
    \sup\Bigl|\mathscr D_{\omega}\prod_{j\in O}(1-P_j)\Delta_{\boldsymbol{\mathsf J}}f\Bigr|\leqslant C_{\chi}\|\omega\|_{\infty}(L_f+q)\,u^{q+| O|}\;.
\end{equation}

\subsubsection{Tree Gauge on a Comparison Rectangle}\label{sec:c4-10-5}
\begin{lemma}[Tree Gauge]\label{lem:c4-10-5}
Let $Q$ be an injectively lifted fine rectangle of largest side $R\geqslant 1$ with a root $o\in Q$, let $U$ be a unitary field, and let $\delta_Q(U)$ be as in \eqref{eq:c4-6-deltaQ}. For $x\in Q$ let $P_x$ run from $o$ to $x$ in coordinate order, each coordinate run oriented by its displacement; these paths form a rooted tree. Let $g(o)\coloneqq\id$ and $g(x)\coloneqq U(P_x)$, so that $U^g(b)= U(P_x)U(b)U(P_{x'})^{-1}$ for $b=(x,x')$ is the based closed transport at $o$ of the fundamental loop of $b$. Then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-15}
    U^g(b)=\prod_{j=1}^{m_b}G_jU(\partial p_j)^{\epsilon_j}G_j^{-1},\qquad m_b\leqslant 3R,\qquad\epsilon_j\in\{1,-1\}\;,
\end{equation}
with every plaquette $p_j$ in $Q$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-16}
    | U^g(b)-\id|_{\sigma}\leqslant 3R\,\delta_Q(U)\;.
\end{equation}
There is a constant $C_{\mathrm{tg}}$, depending only on the fixed group chart and $\tau_{\mathrm b}$, such that $C_{\mathrm{tg}}R^2\delta_Q(U)\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2$ implies that every $U^g(b)$, $b\subset Q$, lies in the group chart, with principal phase $B_b$ satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-10-17}
    \max_{b\subset Q}h(B_b)\leqslant C_{\mathrm{tg}}R^2\delta_Q(U)\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2\;.
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For a bond of direction $\mu$, its last $\mu$-step is moved past the later coordinate runs of $P_x$. Each interchange with a perpendicular fine edge replaces the ordered word by one plaquette transport conjugated by the preceding word; all plaquettes stay in $Q$, and the number of interchanges is at most $\sum_{\nu>\mu}| x_{\nu}-o_{\nu}|\leqslant 3R$. Negative coordinate runs reverse a plaquette orientation without altering this count. Induction on the interchanges gives the exact nonabelian word \eqref{eq:c4-10-15}, the order being that of the step interchanges and $G_j$ the preceding transport to the plaquette, so every factor is a conjugated closed plaquette.

Unitary invariance of $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ and telescoping give \eqref{eq:c4-10-16}, with a constant independent of $R$. Norm conversion to the operator norm and the fixed local group logarithm give $h(\log U^g(b))\leqslant 3C_G\sqrt N\,R\,\delta_Q$ whenever that distance is inside the group chart; since $R\geqslant 1$, requiring $C_{\mathrm{tg}}\geqslant 3C_G\sqrt N$ and $C_{\mathrm{tg}}\geqslant 6\sqrt N\tau_{\mathrm b}/r_G$ makes $C_{\mathrm{tg}}R^2\delta_Q\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2$ sufficient for the chart condition and for \eqref{eq:c4-10-17}. The constants do not grow with $b$ or the scale $R_1$.

The root $g(o)=\id$ leaves the complementary $h$ fixed in every closed contraction.
\end{proof}

\subsection{Identification of the Centred Coefficient and Its Local Extension}\label{sec:c4-11}
This section concerns $c_W$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4-6-1}, with $W$ fixed on a covered branch, under the hypotheses of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} (its Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} included) and Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, with their fixed charts, carriers, cutoffs and parameters.

\subsubsection{The Exterior Dependence}\label{sec:c4-11-1}
The exterior-response parameter is $s$, and the background-path parameter is $t$. Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} defines
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-11-1}
    K_{\xi;s}(a)=\Theta_{\xi}(a)\exp\Bigl(-\frac12\langle a,H_{\xi,II}a\rangle-s\langle a,H_{\xi,IJ}A_{\mathrm e}\rangle+\sum_{\mathfrak p\ \mathrm{near}}\mathfrak p(a+sA_{\mathrm e})\Bigr)\;,
\end{equation}
with $U_1$ held fixed in the $s$-interpolation. The collar identity and the boundary-response identity give, with $F_{\xi}(s)$ defined with the same Wilson function $f_{\xi}$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-11-2}
    \mathcal J^{\mathrm a}_{\xi}[1]= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1},\qquad F_{\xi}(1)= F_{\xi}(0)+\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]\;.
\end{equation}
On a covered branch every contour row has its entire free-input set in $I$. Since $\Psi_{\xi}$ is the identity on $I$ and $A_{\mathrm e}$ vanishes there, row locality implies, for every $a$ in the integration box, that every contour link in $f_{\xi}(a)$ is its reconstruction from $a$ alone at background $U_1$: this is the argument of the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} with $a$ retained instead of set to zero, using Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}. Thus the source and $K_{\xi;0}$ have zero retained free input; $U_1$ itself still depends on the exterior determining data.

Every selected measure in $c_W$ is constructed from $K_{\xi;0}$: its potentials are the near primitives at $a$, its Hessian is $H_{\xi,II}$ and its cutoff is $\Theta_{\xi}$. The factors involving $\Psi_{\xi}(A_{\mathrm e})$, the far primitives and the boundary-map Jacobian are in $c_{\xi}$, and the interaction between $a$ and $A_{\mathrm e}$ is accounted for by $\mathcal B_{\xi}$. Consequently the physical comparison is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-11-3}
    \frac1{\mathcal Z_0}\int\mathcal O\bigl[e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}F_{\xi}(0)\bigr]\dd V+\frac1{\mathcal Z_0}\int\mathcal O\bigl[e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]\bigr]\dd V\;,
\end{equation}
with $I_{\xi;1}$; the term with $\mathcal B_{\xi}$ plays the role of the boundary separation in \cite[(1.26)--(1.30)]{BalabanCRE}.

\subsubsection{Covariance of the Selected Coefficient}\label{sec:c4-11-2}
For a site gauge $g$ let $R_ga(b)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ad}_{g(b_-)}a(b)$ on free bonds; $R_g$ is orthogonal for $h$, preserves each free bond subspace and commutes with geometric restrictions. The intertwinings in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality}, $Q_{U^g}R_g= R^{(1)}_gQ_U$, $\mathcal N_{U^g}\circ R_g= R^{(1)}_g\mathcal N_U$, $h_{U^g}= R_gh_U(R^{(1)}_g)^{-1}$ and $\mathsf C_{U^g}= R_g\mathsf C_UR_{g,*}^{-1}$ with $(R^{(1)}_gv)(c)\coloneqq\operatorname{Ad}_{g(c_-)}v(c)$ (the row covariance of Section~\ref{sec:regular-hessian-stencils}, used in the same way in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:schur}), give $q_{U^g}(R_ga)= R_gq_U(a)$, branch included: $R_gq_U(a)$ solves the transformed row equation and lies in the same invariant small ball, and the uniqueness of the small row solution there (Lemma~\ref{lem:row-locality}; the uniqueness ball of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}(ii)) identifies it with the selected solution.

The joint fixed point of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-1} is identified with this solution by choosing its phase radius so that its $O(\| A\|^2)$ bound lies inside the uniqueness ball of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} (Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-5}); the inverse and mean branches are those fixed in the row construction.

The action of each plaquette is invariant and each relative soft-gauge mean is conjugated at its base, so the constant, linear and quadratic Taylor coefficients of the energy primitives transform with their arguments, the force--constraint term included; subtracting them preserves the covariance of the compensated primitives even at noncritical backgrounds. The Haar density is conjugation invariant. The constraint-Jacobian endomorphism transforms by conjugation between the same free and designated spaces, so its determinant and its selected logarithm are unchanged, the logarithm branch being fixed by continuation from zero within the nonvanishing chart. Hence each primitive and each host sum $\mathbf V_{\xi}(Y)$ is invariant under the simultaneous transformation of background and free variables.

The Hessian, each restricted seed inverse and every fixed walk transform by $R_g$ on their indices, by the entry identities of Lemma~\ref{lem:hessian-gauge-locality} and the geometric walk formula; all geometric choices, Cauchy variables and Mayer parameters are unchanged. The change of variables $B\mapsto R_gB$, $X\mapsto R_gX$ in the selected integral preserves Lebesgue and standard Gaussian measures, the two allowed cutoff norms (\eqref{eq:marginal-cutoff-invariance}), the conditional Gaussian determinant and the cross and compensator terms, so each selected measure is pushed forward by $R_g$, and in the probe formula $\delta_B-\delta_0$ is pushed to $\delta_{R_gB}-\delta_0$. Summing selections,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-11-4}
    \widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{U^g,D}=(R_g)_*\widehat\nu^{\mathrm f}_{U,D}\;.
\end{equation}
The vacuum activities, their Ursell products and $w_{\xi}(W)$ are scalar invariants, the incompatibility graph and every numerical combinatorial factor being field independent. Both $T_WP_W^{-1}$ and the complementary $h$ transform at the initial interval vertex $o$, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-11-5}
    c_W(U^g;g(o)hg(o)^{-1})= c_W(U;h)\;.
\end{equation}
The rooted comparison gauge has $g(o)=\id$.

\subsubsection{Domain and Endpoint}\label{sec:c4-11-3}
Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4} defines the small interior groups by \eqref{eq:c4-8-9}. The support of such a group includes every root domain, each vacuum-cluster domain occurrence, their coefficient halos and the whole contour interval $\mathcal H(W)$ with its closing transport. Under \eqref{eq:c4-8-9} the enclosing rectangle has diameter at most $C_{\mathrm{box}}LMn(W)$, lies within $b/2$ of a source contact and is injectively liftable under the period convention of Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-2}; on the far-history event the box and its halos lie in the regular region. All other groups, including winding or boundary-reaching groups, are in the large-domain tail of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}, as in the small-domain/large-domain separation of \cite[(3.5)--(3.9)]{BalabanRG1} and the boundary separation of \cite{BalabanCRE}.

A small interior group is taken in its rooted tree gauge; if $C_{\mathrm{tg}}\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)^2\delta_{Q_W}(U_1)\leqslant \tau_{\mathrm b}/2$, then $B_W$ and $U_{W,t}$ are defined by \eqref{eq:c4-9-1}. With $\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \tau_L/4$ and $c_L\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \gamma_L/4$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3}) the entry Lipschitz estimate and the flat compression gap supply the two-sided Hessian bounds throughout the path.

For each selected coefficient Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-2} fixes all walk parameters and restricts every surviving walk and coefficient stencil to its final domain. Thus, on the supports included in $Q_W$, the $t=1$ recipe equals the gauge-transformed physical centred recipe, its values on bonds outside $Q_W$ cannot enter the coefficient, and \eqref{eq:c4-11-5} returns the coefficient to the original gauge. At $t=0$ the recipe is the regional reference recipe with exactly the same $I$, $\Omega_1$, $W$, cutoffs and constants. This yields the endpoint identities
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-11-6}
    c_W(U_{W,1};h)= c_W(U_1;h),\qquad c_W(U_{W,0};h)= a_W\chi(h)\;.
\end{equation}

For differentiation under the selected integrals, the norm of $X$ in Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-3} is the norm of $X$ restricted to $J_Z$; all other auxiliary columns integrate out with mass one and have zero derivative. The common strictly positive $c_{\mathrm G}$ of \eqref{eq:c4-10-13} supplies a background-independent Gaussian majorant for that finite-dimensional integral and its first derivative; the selected sums use the summable majorants of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1} and Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-4}, and the vacuum occurrence sums those of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-4} and Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}. These majorants give dominated convergence for the derivative of the group coefficient, that of $w_{\xi}(W)$ included.

\subsubsection{The Site-Gauge Extension and Lifting}\label{sec:c4-11-4}
The endpoint statement concerns covered far histories and the small interior groups of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}. The rooted site gauge is extended from $Q_W$ to the whole torus by the identity on sites outside $Q_W$. Every background bond consulted by the coefficient has both endpoints inside $Q_W$: in defining $Q_W$ the enclosing rectangle is enlarged to contain both endpoints of each Hessian stencil, row set, block-mean path, plaquette and interval or closing-path bond, an enlargement that is part of the fixed halo included in $C_{\mathrm{box}}$. Boundary bonds of the site-gauge extension are not consulted by the coefficient.

Along $U_{W,t}$ only the finite product $w_{\xi}(W)$, $(-1)^{k(W)}/k(W)!$ times the product of the specified vacuum cluster occurrences, varies; the global exclusion ratio $q_{\xi}(\mathcal A)$ is expanded at the original background before the group construction. Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-4} supplies the sum of the occurrence derivative majorants, and \eqref{eq:c4-8-10} applies the finite product rule.

The regional scalar $a_W$ is defined in Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} from $w^{\circ}_{\xi}(W)$ and the same root measures at the identity background (\eqref{eq:part1-reference-group}); its closed Schur identity \eqref{eq:part1-closed-schur} is the $t=0$ identity.

For the lifting, each constituent connected domain is represented by a tree of its constituent coarse cubes and adjoining faces, and the union is rooted at a source contact. Each root or cluster-domain tree has at most its number of cubes minus one edges; incompatibility joins have bounded range, and the finite reconstruction halos add a fixed range at their contacts. The contour-hull extent bound bounds the additional contour edges joining the components by $CLMn(W)$; the network contains the whole interval $\mathcal H(W)$ and its closing path. The resulting connected bond network has a spanning traversal of length at most $CLMn(W)$ with $C$ fixed.

If this is less than $N_{\min}/4$, the traversal is lifted from its root: every lifted vertex lies within that distance of the root, and two lifts of the same vertex could differ only by a nonzero period vector, of length at least $N_{\min}$, while the two paths giving them have total length less than $N_{\min}/2$, a contradiction. Every point of the enclosing coordinate rectangle and of its stipulated halos is within $\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)\leqslant C_{\mathrm{box}}LMn(W)$ of the root, and two lifts of such a point would differ by a nonzero period vector, of length at least $N_{\min}$, while being joined through the root by two segments of total length at most $2C_{\mathrm{box}}LMn(W)< b< N_{\min}$ (\eqref{eq:c4-8-9}, \eqref{eq:c4-9-3}); so the rectangle and its halos project injectively. $C_{\mathrm{box}}$ includes these constants, so by \eqref{eq:c4-8-9} and \eqref{eq:c4-9-3} every small group lifts.

In applying the entry estimates, $\tau_{\mathrm b}$ is taken small enough for both the $h$-maximum and the stated entry-chart norm, using $h\leqslant |\bigcdot |_{\sigma}\leqslant \sqrt Nh$, before $g_0$ is chosen. Geometrically allowed zero walks re-index the same series and do not change its value or support domains.

\subsubsection{Source and Radius Specifications}\label{sec:c4-11-5}
The imported mean covariance is \cite[(0.6)]{BalabanRG1}, $\mathsf M(\{ uU_jv\})= u\mathsf M(\{ U_j\})v$ for the specified mean on its small-diameter domain, which \cite[(0.10)]{BalabanRG1} asserts for the selected mean; it is used for unitary site gauges with no smallness restriction on the gauge values, the relative distances and the real chart domains being preserved. The cutoff invariance is \eqref{eq:marginal-cutoff-invariance}.

The curvature input of Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4} is Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-plaquette-deviation}. Every vertex $x$ of a plaquette of $Q_W$ lies in $\Lambda_1$, since $Q_W\subset\Lambda_1$, and the $L$-block containing $x$ contains a neighbouring vertex ($L\geqslant 3$). That internal fine bond is free, since designated bonds join distinct blocks, and belongs to $I$ because it has the endpoint $x\in\Lambda_1$; so the plaquette has a bond within two fine-bond metric units of $I$, within the $3R_{\mathrm c}$ the lemma requires. This yields the bound $\delta_{Q_W}(U_1)\leqslant C\varepsilon_1$, with the fixed conversion between the lemma's operator norm and the norm $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-10-5}.

For the branch identification of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-2} let $C_{\mathrm{D,joint}}$ be the constant in $\|\widetilde D_Z(A)\|\leqslant C_{\mathrm{D,joint}}\| A\|^2$ on the joint chart of Section~\ref{sec:c4-10-1}. After that chart is fixed, $\theta_0$ is reduced so that $2\theta_0\leqslant \vartheta_*/2$ and $4C_{\mathrm{D,joint}}\theta_0^2<\rho_{\mathrm d}$; the norms of $Z$ and $A$ are those of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart}, in which $\vartheta_*$, $\rho_{\mathrm d}$ and $\tau_L$ are measured, and the background radius satisfies $2\tau_{\mathrm b}\leqslant \tau_L/2$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-3}), so every real background with $\| Z\|<2\tau_{\mathrm b}$ lies in the chart of that lemma. At real backgrounds the joint solution for $\| A\|<2\theta_0$ then lies in the uniqueness ball of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-uniform-chart} and is its selected solution. The coupling threshold is fixed after these radii so that the phase inputs $g_0\mathsf C_UB$ of the enlarged free box remain in $\| A\|<\theta_0$.

\subsection{Quantitative Assembly}\label{sec:c4-12}
This section proves the first-step estimate for $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ of \eqref{eq:c4-1-1}. It uses the hypotheses of Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction} (its Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} included) and Appendix~\ref{app:background-estimates}, the compatible even-period and square-fit conventions of Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-2}, and the same irreducible normalised character. Constants may depend on the fixed group, the character, $L$, $M$ and the fixed expansion and chart choices, but not on the coupling, the square length, the compatible torus size or the history; the coupling is chosen last.

\subsubsection{The Joint Derivative Supplied to the Group Coefficient}\label{sec:c4-12-1}
The quantitative derivative is obtained from Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-7-1} and~\ref{lem:c4-7-2} and Section~\ref{sec:c4-10}. For each selected root the source is $\Delta_{\mathsf J}f$, a closed character difference; \eqref{eq:c4-10-9} bounds its mixed Taylor remainder by $u^q$ and supplies an extra $u$ for each odd leading term removed by reversal.

The root's Gaussian derivative is even in its joint $(B,X)$ variables, including its determinant and compensator derivatives, and a derivative of a selected ordinary potential carries a factor $\zeta$ and vanishes at $\zeta=0$; so the independent-root parity/Cauchy argument of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-2} applies after one background derivative.

Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-7-1}(b),(c) (\eqref{eq:c4-7-4}, \eqref{eq:c4-7-5}) bounds a differentiated potential; \eqref{eq:c4-10-6} sums the derivatives of all geometrically indexed walks on the same spatial contours; \eqref{eq:c4-10-14} pays each Gaussian derivative by $C_MN_1(D)$ times the same $e^{N_1(D)}$ determinant majorant, with $X$ restricted to $J_Z$, all other auxiliary variables integrating to one. Host and Gaussian derivatives therefore insert one factor $N_1(D)$. The source derivative inserts the number $L_f$ of varying contour/closing links plus the number of selected labels, which Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1} bounds by $C_M\sum_DN_1(D)$. The resulting joint estimate is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-1}
    |\mathscr D_{\omega}\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)|\leqslant C_{\chi}\|\omega\|_{\infty}\Bigl(L_f+\sum_{D\in\mathcal A}N_1(D)\Bigr)\prod_{D\in\mathcal A}\rho\,m(D)\;,
\end{equation}
with $\rho$ of \eqref{eq:c4-4-8} and $m(D)=\varepsilon_*e^{-\lambda_*\ell_1(D)}$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-1}; the pairing $\mathfrak Q_{\xi}(\mathcal A;f)$ and its source are evaluated at the background $U_{W,t}$ of the fixed coefficient path of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11} in place of $U_1$ (the subscript $\xi$ is kept for brevity).

For a vacuum occurrence $\mathfrak c$ the selected-integral derivative gives \eqref{eq:c4-7-8}; differentiating the finite product $w_{\xi}(W)$ by \eqref{eq:c4-8-10}, its occurrences $\Phi^{\mathrm v}(\mathfrak c_j)$ likewise evaluated at $U_{W,t}$, and adding the root-integral derivative yields, uniformly for $h\in G$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-2}
    | c_W(U;h)|\leqslant M(W),\qquad|\mathscr D_{\omega} c_W(U;h)|\leqslant C_{\chi}\|\omega\|_{\infty}\bigl(n(W)+|\mathcal H(W)|\bigr)M(W)\;.
\end{equation}
The undifferentiated estimate holds at the original physical background and at the regional flat reference. The factor from the relative interval's inverse word, at most a fixed multiple of $|\mathcal H(W)|$, is included in $C_{\chi}$.

\subsubsection{Payment of the Local and Tail Losses}\label{sec:c4-12-2}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-4}]
Let $s=\mathfrak s(W)\geqslant 1$, so that $\mathfrak a_W=\eta s$. The fixed hull and box bounds give $n(W)+|\mathcal H(W)|\leqslant CLMs$ and $\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)\leqslant C_{\mathrm{box}}LMn(W)\leqslant C_{\mathrm{box}}LMs$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-8-4}). The endpoint identities \eqref{eq:c4-11-6}, the path integral \eqref{eq:c4-9-2} with the derivative bound \eqref{eq:c4-12-2} along it, and the plaquette estimate $\delta_{Q_W}(U_1)\leqslant C\varepsilon_1$ of Section~\ref{sec:c4-11-5} with the phase bound \eqref{eq:c4-10-17} therefore give, for a small interior group passing the phase test,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-3}
    \mathfrak d_W(U_1)\leqslant C_{\chi}\varepsilon_1s^3M(W)\;.
\end{equation}
If the phase test of such a group fails, then $C_{\mathrm{tg}}\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)^2\delta_{Q_W}>\tau_{\mathrm b}/2$; with $\delta_{Q_W}\leqslant C\varepsilon_1$ and $\operatorname{diam}(Q_W)\leqslant CLMs$ this gives $1\leqslant C\varepsilon_1s^2$ with constants fixed before the coupling, so the two undifferentiated endpoint bounds \eqref{eq:c4-12-2} give \eqref{eq:c4-12-3} again, as $s\geqslant 1$. For a group outside the small interior class
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-4}
    \mathfrak d_W(U_1)\leqslant 2M(W),\qquad s\geqslant T_b\coloneqq \frac{b}{4C_{\mathrm{box}}LM}\;.
\end{equation}

For the local polynomial payment let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-5}
    C_{\eta,3}\coloneqq\sup_{s\geqslant 1}s^3e^{-(31\eta/8)s}<\infty\;,
\end{equation}
so that $s^3e^{\eta s/8}\leqslant C_{\eta,3}e^{4\eta s}$; for the tail, $s\geqslant T_b$ gives $e^{\eta s/8}\leqslant e^{-2\eta T_b}e^{4\eta s}$. Hence the two weighted pin estimates of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-8-2} and~\ref{lem:c4-8-3} imply
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-6}
    \begin{gathered}
    \sum_WK_{\chi}\mathfrak d_W(U_1)e^{\mathfrak a_W/8}\leqslant C_{\chi}\bigl(\varepsilon_1+e^{-2\eta T_b}\bigr)\sum_WM(W)e^{4\eta\mathfrak s(W)}\leqslant C_{\chi} n_C\rho\bigl(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)}\bigr),\\
    c=\frac{\eta}{2C_{\mathrm{box}}}\;.
    \end{gathered}
\end{equation}
The last summation uses that every $W$ has a nonempty contour interval, so summing the contour-pin estimate \eqref{eq:c4-6-5} over the $n_C$ traversals counts every group at least once; the whole-contour groups are included by Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-3}(d). This is \eqref{eq:c4-6-8}.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The Signed Family Sum and the Physical Expectation}\label{sec:c4-12-3}
\begin{proposition}[The Signed Defect Bound]\label{prop:c4-12-3}
Under the hypotheses stated at the start of this section, for $g_0$ below the thresholds of Lemmas~\ref{lem:c4-2-1}, \ref{lem:c4-6-2} and~\ref{lem:c4-6-3}, with $R_{\Upsilon}\geqslant 2$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-7-1}, Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-1}), $u\leqslant u_*$ and $v\leqslant 1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-4-2}) and the small-coupling conditions of Sections~\ref{sec:c4-10-1} and~\ref{sec:c4-11-5}, with $\rho$ of \eqref{eq:c4-4-8}, $\rho= O(g_0^2(1+r)^4)$, $\varepsilon_1= g_1p_0(g_1)$, $b=\lfloor LMR_1/16\rfloor$, $\pi_*=\min(p_0(g_0),p_0(g_1))$ and the constants $C'_L$, $c_*$ of \eqref{eq:c4-2-2} and $C_{\chi}$, $c$ of \eqref{eq:c4-6-8},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-7}
    | E_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}+\frac1{\mathcal Z_0}\int\mathcal O\Bigl[\mathsf w_{\xi}\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}\cap\mathsf N_b^c}| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\Bigl(e^{C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})}-1\Bigr)\Bigr](V)\,\dd V\;,
\end{equation}
and consequently
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4-12-8}
    | E_{\mathrm{def}}|\leqslant C'_Ln_Ce^{-(c_*/2)\pi_*^2}+e^{C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})}-1\;.
\end{equation}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-3} supplies the single joint ratio \eqref{eq:c4-6-7}. Combined with the closed-contraction product bound \eqref{eq:c4-6-4}, formed after each $d_W$, the nonempty compatible-family sum is bounded by the exponential series of the summable one-group weight \eqref{eq:c4-6-8}, which on covered far histories is \eqref{eq:c4-6-9} (Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-5}); the countable-group limit is the dominated finite-species limit of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-9-2}, with the same positive majorant and the nonzero reference partition function supplied by its convergent logarithm.

Combining the near-history estimate \eqref{eq:c4-2-2} with the positivity of the original history measure gives \eqref{eq:c4-12-7}.

Since $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}|\leqslant 1$ (Section~\ref{sec:c4-9-4}), the physical normalisation yields \eqref{eq:c4-12-8}.
\end{proof}

When $C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})\leqslant 1$, the exponential term of \eqref{eq:c4-12-8} is at most $2C_{\chi} n_C\rho(\varepsilon_1+e^{-cb/(LM)})$.

\subsubsection{Fixed Reserve Conventions}\label{sec:c4-12-4}
The exponential vacuum estimate used in Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-8-2} holds with $n(\mathfrak c)/2$ as well as with $n(\mathfrak c)/4$: the rooted-tree proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:activity-bounds} applied to the numerical activity $m(D)e^{N_1(D)/2}$ with node cost $N_1(D)/8$ has combined exponent $5/8$, below the $1+6\theta$ of the activity payment \eqref{eq:fixed-kernel-raw-activity-payment}, which gives the first bound of \eqref{eq:c4-7-9}.

In the footprint-contact sums of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-2} (\eqref{eq:c4-6-5}) and Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-3}, footprint contact includes adjacency of two $LM$-cubes (a shared face, edge or corner). A cube has at most $3^4-1$ such neighbours, so the spatial pin is summed over them as well, which inserts a fixed factor in the constant $C$ multiplying $\rho$; the smallness condition $C\rho LM\leqslant \eta/8$ of Lemma~\ref{lem:c4-6-2} is imposed with this factor.

\section{The Regional Scalar of the Covered Branch}\label{app:regional-scalar}
This appendix identifies the scalar $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C}$ of the branch identity \eqref{eq:c-one-step-branch-identity}, defined in Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction} as the reference-gas sum \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas}, with the regional square scalar \eqref{eq:regional-square-scalar} at the carrier $I$, and thereby with the perimeter/corner coefficient $\kappa_C$ of \eqref{eq:extracted-loop-scalar} up to the error of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}. The quantitative comparison of the regional square scalar with the bulk square is the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}, in particular \eqref{eq:regional-square-boundary-comparison} and \eqref{eq:regional-square-periodic-comparison}.

\subsection{Conventions}\label{sec:c4c-1}
The cutoff prescription $\sigma$, the bare coupling $g_0$, the irreducible normalised character $\chi$, the averaging and mean prescription of \cite{BalabanRG1} and the designated-bond convention are those of the rest of the paper, with the standing conditions \eqref{eq:c-standing-conditions} and the collar conditions \eqref{eq:regional-collar-sizes}. The fine periods are $N_{\mu}= LK_{\mu}$, and $C= C_n$ is a coarse translate of the counterclockwise square with vertices $0$, $nLe_1$, $nL(e_1+e_2)$, $nLe_2$, with $n$ coarse segments of length $L$ on each side and $K_{\mu}\geqslant 3(n+2)$ for every coarse period; its physical perimeter is $P(C_n)=4nL\varepsilon$.

Let $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ be the set of covered branches of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} and let $\xi\in A_{\mathrm{cov}}$. The carrier is $D= I=\Lambda_1^*$ (Section~\ref{sec:sourced-effective-interaction}), the set of free bonds with an endpoint in $\Lambda_1$, which is the carrier $D_+$ of Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} and contains its $D_-$; $D^c$ is its complement in the torus free carrier $E_{*,T}$; distances are those of the periodic fine-bond metric $d_T$ of \eqref{eq:marginal-covariance-input}.

For a coarse segment $j$ of the cyclic index set $J_C\coloneqq\{0,\ldots,4n-1\}$ let $K_j$ be the union of the fixed free-input stencils of its fine traversals, and with the fixed range $R_0=4(1+R_*+R_H+L)$ of Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} let
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4c-1-1}
    d_j\coloneqq\max\bigl(0,d_T(K_j,I^c)-R_0\bigr),\qquad\iota_T\coloneqq\max\bigl(0,N_{\min}/4-R_0\bigr),\qquad N_{\min}\coloneqq\min_{\mu} N_{\mu}\;,
\end{equation}
the distance to the empty set being infinite with $e^{-\infty}=0$. The constants below depend on the character, the group, $L$ and the forest parameters only, not on $n$, the compatible periods or the shape of $I$; $g_0$ is chosen after them, below the common flat and regional thresholds. $\tau$ is the marked-forest parameter of \eqref{eq:marginal-fixed-forest-bound}; enlarging a fixed majorant constant multiplies $\tau$ by a fixed factor, absorbed in the constants and the coupling threshold.

\subsection{Identification with the Regional Square Integral}\label{sec:c4c-2}
\begin{lemma}[The Reference-Gas Scalar at the Carrier $I$]\label{lem:c4c-2-1}
On $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$, under the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1} and the thresholds displayed in the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4c-2-1}
    S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}= S^{\circ}_{I,C_n,T}=\frac{\displaystyle\int\Theta^{\sigma}_I(B)e^{P_{I,T}(B)}\chi\bigl(\Hol_{U_{g_0,T}(i_{I,T}B)}C_n\bigr)\,\dd\mu_{C_{I,T}}(B)}{\displaystyle\int\Theta^{\sigma}_I(B)e^{P_{I,T}(B)}\,\dd\mu_{C_{I,T}}(B)}\;,
\end{equation}
the right side being \eqref{eq:regional-square-scalar} at $D= I$, with every original primitive label retained, including the labels crossing the boundary of $I$, and with the exterior link value the identity.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:part1-reference-gas}, $S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}=\int f^{\circ}_{\xi} K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}\,\dd a/I^{\circ}_{\xi;0}$, the normalised expectation of the full reference Wilson loop under the centred kernel at the identity background, whose precision is $H^{\circ}_{\xi}=\iota_I^*\mathsf H^{\Omega_1}_{\id}\iota_I$, whose potentials are the near primitives evaluated at zero retained input and whose cutoff is the bond cutoff on $I$. Both sides of \eqref{eq:c4c-2-1} are ratios of two integrals over $\mathfrak g^I$, so it suffices to identify the factors of the integrands.

Precision: by Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-regional-entry} at the identity background the entries of $H^{\circ}_{\xi}$ are $f_{bb'}(0)$, the entries of the flat Hessian \eqref{eq:flat-covariance} on the branch's torus (as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}), and the collar puts every precision and primitive stencil touching $I$ inside the regular region (the identification paragraph of Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} preceding \eqref{eq:regional-kernel-identification}), so $H^{\circ}_{\xi}= i_{I,T}^*H_Ti_{I,T}$, the diagonal contributions of the plaquettes crossing the boundary of $I$ included; the Gaussian normaliser of $\mu_{C_{I,T}}$ is common to numerator and denominator and cancels within the ratio. This is the full-square form of \eqref{eq:regional-kernel-identification}, which uses only that the source is a closed contraction with the given input stencils.

Reconstruction: the row solutions $\widetilde D_{U,c}$ of Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} (Lemma~\ref{lem:charts}) at the identity background and those of Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification} agree as analytic germs at zero by their defining equation and uniqueness; the Hilbert-ball domain of Lemma~\ref{lem:charts} (reference version) and the maximum-norm domain of the flat expansion have a convex common phase domain containing the closed cutoff box at the stated thresholds, and analytic continuation on that domain identifies the two solutions throughout the box.

Primitives: Section~\ref{sec:source-phase-primitives} groups the gauge primitives by their centre $y$ while \eqref{eq:regional-periodic-weight} indexes them by the pairs $(y,x)$; the sums coincide, the degree-two Taylor residual being linear in the local term, and every primitive whose free support misses $I$ vanishes at $i_{I,T}B$ while every primitive meeting $I$ is retained on both sides.

Cutoff: at zero exterior free field the conditional cutoff is $\Theta^{\sigma}_I$ at the threshold $r=\delta_0/g_0$ in the norm $|\bigcdot |_{\sigma}$, as in Section~\ref{sec:regional-identification}.

Wilson factor: on a covered branch every contour traversal has its free-input set in $I$, so the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:covered} applies verbatim with $a$ retained instead of set to zero and gives that each contour link of $f^{\circ}_{\xi}(a)$ is its reconstruction from $a$ alone, that is, $U_{g_0,T}(i_{I,T}B)$ at $B= a$; the boundary map is the identity by the reference-data convention $\Psi^{\circ}=\id$ of Section~\ref{sec:joint-extraction}.

Numerator and denominator agree factor by factor, so the ratios agree.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The Scalar of the Branch Identity}\label{sec:c4c-5}
\begin{proposition}[The Regional Scalar of the Covered Branch]\label{prop:c4c-5-1}
Under the conventions of Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1} and the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction}, on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$,
\begin{gather}
    S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}= e^{-\delta m^{\sigma}(g_0,\varepsilon)P(C_n)}\bigl(z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}(g_0,\pi/2)\bigr)^4e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}=\kappa_{C_n}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}\;,\label{eq:c4c-5-1}\\
    | E^{\circ}_{\xi}|\leqslant C\tau^2\Bigl[\sum_{j\in J_C}e^{-cd_j}+4ne^{-c\iota_T}+(n+1)e^{-cn}\Bigr]\;,\notag
\end{gather}
with $\kappa_{C_n}\coloneqq e^{-\delta m^{\sigma}(g_0,\varepsilon)P(C_n)}(z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}(g_0,\pi/2))^4$ the coefficient of \eqref{eq:extracted-loop-scalar}, built from the coefficients of \eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass} and \eqref{eq:corner-square-factor}, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4c-5-2}
    E^{\circ}_{\xi}= E^{\circ}_{I,C_n,T}=(F_{I,C,T}-F_{C,T})+(F_{C,T}-F_{C,\infty}(n))+E^{\sigma}_n\;,
\end{equation}
the error of Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} at $D= I$: as in its proof, $F_{I,C,T}=\log S^{\circ}_{I,C_n,T}$ on the connected source branch, $F_{C,T}=\log(N^{\sigma}_{C_n,T}/D^{\sigma}_T)$, $F_{C,\infty}(n)= F_{\square,\infty}(n)$ is the bulk logarithm \eqref{eq:corner-fixed-square-limit}, and $E^{\sigma}_n\coloneqq F_{\square,\infty}(n)-n\sum_{v\in\mathscr V_{\square}}\kappa_v-\sum_{(v,w)\in\mathscr C_{\square}}\zeta_{v,w}$ is the corner-extraction error, $| E^{\sigma}_n|\leqslant C\tau^2(n+1)e^{-cn}$ by \eqref{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound}, with $n\sum_v\kappa_v=-\delta m^{\sigma} P(C_n)$ (\eqref{eq:marginal-square-mass}) and $\sum_{(v,w)}\zeta_{v,w}=4\log z^{\sigma}_{\mathrm c}$ (\eqref{eq:corner-square-factor}), so that $F_{I,C,T}=\log\kappa_{C_n}+E^{\circ}_{\xi}$.

A segment with $d_j=0$ contributes a boundary term of size $C\tau^2$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Lemma~\ref{lem:c4c-2-1} and Proposition~\ref{prop:regional-square-extraction} at $D= I$, which is covered on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ and is the carrier $D_+$ itself (Section~\ref{sec:c4c-1}), so $D_-\subseteq D\subseteq D_+$ holds with the collar; the three terms of \eqref{eq:c4c-5-2} are \eqref{eq:regional-square-boundary-comparison}, \eqref{eq:regional-square-periodic-comparison} and the corner extraction \eqref{eq:corner-square-extraction-bound}, the first two retaining the changes of kernel and of summation range as errors before the translation-invariant coefficients are identified, as in \cite[(4.35)--(4.37)]{BalabanRG1}; the exterior operation and its boundary terms are those of Section~\ref{sec:remaining-physical-comparison}.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[The Physical Identity with the Scalar Substituted]\label{cor:c4c-5-2}
Under the hypotheses of Proposition~\ref{prop:c4c-5-1}, with $E_{\mathrm{def}}$ of \eqref{eq:c4-1-1} and $E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$ of \eqref{eq:c3-6-2},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:c4c-5-3}
    \mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]=\kappa_{C_n}\,\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}\bigl[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)\bigr]+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}\;,
\end{equation}
where $\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}$ uses the original outer operation, the weight $\mathsf w_{\xi}= e^{c_{\xi}}I_{\xi;1}$ and the physical $\mathcal Z_0$. Every term is integrable against the normalised history weight.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
By \eqref{eq:c4-8-1}, $\mathbb E_{\varepsilon}[W_{\chi}(C_n)]=\mathbb E_{\mathrm h}[\mathbf 1_{A_{\mathrm{cov}}}S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}f_{\xi}(0)]+E_{\mathrm{def}}+E_{\mathrm{bdry}}$, with $f_{\xi}(0)= W_{\chi}(C_n;U_1)$ on $A_{\mathrm{cov}}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:covered}), into which \eqref{eq:c4c-5-1} is substituted. $E^{\circ}_{\xi}$ is a function of the finite geometry at fixed torus and reference parameters, hence of the history labels through $I$ alone, and is independent of the field values at fixed labels, so the first term is measurable; its bound has at most $4n$ boundary terms, $| E^{\circ}_{\xi}|\leqslant C\tau^2(9n+1)$, so the factor $e^{E^{\circ}_{\xi}}$ is bounded and the term integrable.

For the other terms, $| S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}|\leqslant 1$ because it is the normalised integral of a character of modulus at most one against the positive reference kernel $K^{\circ}_{\xi;0}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:c2-reference}); $| F_{\xi}(s)|\leqslant 1$ since $F_{\xi}(s)=\int f_{\xi}\,\dd\nu_{\xi;s}$ (\eqref{eq:convex-response-operands}) with $\nu_{\xi;s}$ a probability measure, and $| f_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant 1$; hence $|\mathcal B_{\xi}[f_{\xi}]|=| F_{\xi}(1)-F_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant 2$ (\eqref{eq:c-exterior-response}) and the summed signed defect $| F_{\xi}(0)-S^{\circ}_{\xi,C_n}f_{\xi}(0)|\leqslant 2$, and both are integrable against the probability history weight.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Scope]\label{rem:c4c-8-1}
The identity \eqref{eq:c4c-5-3} concerns the reconstructed fine loop at the background $U_1$ after the first step; the bare coarse loop and the later scales are not covered.
\end{remark}
